title: Global solutions for continuous-time Burgers equations and infinite-volume polymer measures
text:
Title: Global solutions for continuous-time Burgers equations and infinite-volume polymer measures
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study the stochastic Burgers equation on the whole space, driven by space-homogeneous Gaussian noises that are white in time and colored in space, for both positive and zero viscosity. We show that in dimension one, for any fixed average velocity, there is a unique ergodic global solution to the Burgers equation for all nonnegative viscosities, and that the One Force---One Solution principle holds. We also describe the basin of attraction and show that these global solutions are one-point pullback attractors. Moreover, the viscous global solution converges to the inviscid global solution as the viscosity tends to zero. Our technique relies on the study of polymer measures; accordingly, we establish the existence and uniqueness of infinite-volume polymer measures in a given asymptotic direction, as well as their convergence to semi-infinite minimizers in the zero-temperature limit. We also establish the existence part of all these results in arbitrary dimension larger than one.

title: Do Benign-Trained Hidden-State Probes Detect Tool Errors Under Adversarial Conditions?
text:
Title: Do Benign-Trained Hidden-State Probes Detect Tool Errors Under Adversarial Conditions?
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Although hidden-state probes efficiently monitor model operation, it remains unclear whether probes trained on benign tool use remain useful for detecting incorrect actions under adversarial conditions. In this research, we assess this problem from the perspective of operational tool-action correct- ness. we use four AgentDojo suites, four conditions, and three models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, and GLM- 4.6V-Flash (9B). We perform a five-fold, task-grouped out-of-fold (OOF) evaluation for each model. We train step-specific logistic- regression probes only on benign and non-defended trajectories and evaluate them on held-out trajectories for benign, prompt- injection, system-override, and tool-poisoning conditions. We compare our hidden-state probe to mean tool-call-token entropy, negative mean tool-call-token log-probability, and self-consistency uncertainty. The paired tests highlight six significant differences after Holm correction. All of the tests involve Qwen2.5-14B- Instruct under the system-override condition, with all three scalar uncertainty metrics obtaining higher area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and average precision (AP) than the hidden-state probe. These results suggest that benign-trained hidden-state probes should not be assumed to reliably detect operational tool-action errors under adversarial conditions.

title: Adapting Boltz-2 with limited experimental activity data improves early enrichment in virtual screening
text:
Title: Adapting Boltz-2 with limited experimental activity data improves early enrichment in virtual screening
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Virtual screening aims to prioritize active compounds from large chemical libraries within a limited experimental budget. When applying Boltz-2 to virtual screening, a key challenge is how to use limited experimental data from the target assay to improve the prioritization of active compounds. We investigated whether fine-tuning the Boltz-2 affinity heads with a small number of binary activity labels could improve early enrichment of active compounds in hit discovery. We compared fine-tuning with 40-300 labels in a retrospective evaluation on eight MF-PCBA targets. With 300 activity measurements, fine-tuning increased the number of actives in the top 1% by a geometric mean of 1.77-fold across the eight targets and improved average precision (AP) by 2.14-fold relative to the control without fine-tuning. We also investigated whether rescoring a subset of candidates could retain the improvement in hit recovery by reranking only the top-ranked Boltz-2 candidates with the fine-tuned head. Restricting rescoring to approximately 10% of the evaluation set retained hit recovery comparable to full rescoring. These findings show that affinity-head fine-tuning with limited activity labels improves early enrichment with Boltz-2 and that this benefit can be retained when rescoring a restricted set of candidates.

title: Adaptive Output Regulation of Linear Systems with Unknown Harmonic Exosystems and Additive Noise
text:
Title: Adaptive Output Regulation of Linear Systems with Unknown Harmonic Exosystems and Additive Noise
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This paper addresses error-feedback output regulation for known multivariable linear plants subject to an unknown exosystem and additive Gaussian process and measurement noise. The exosystem generates constant and sinusoidal signals, but its dimension, frequencies, and coupling matrices are unavailable. An output-injection transformation represents the external action through known channels. A causal observer then produces a residual independent of the applied input, whose filtered output separates into a harmonic signal, stationary colored Gaussian noise, and a decaying transient. Using this observation model, a Fourier procedure consistently identifies the number and values of the active positive frequencies in the presence of noise. The identified frequencies determine a regulator through interpolation with stable residual filters. A contractive filter realization, nonexpansive state resizing, and bounded gain updates ensure closed-loop moment bounds uniformly over the selected filter orders. If the gain bound contains the ideal interpolation gain, the adaptive plant response and tracking error converge in mean square to those of the corresponding known-frequency regulator. The limiting mean-square tracking error is a linear function of the process- and measurement-noise covariances. In the absence of both noises, the tracking error converges to zero.

title: An Autonomous Spectral Representation for Fully Asymmetric Spherical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Dynamics
text:
Title: An Autonomous Spectral Representation for Fully Asymmetric Spherical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Dynamics
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study the large size dynamics of a fully asymmetric spherical Sherrington- Kirkpatrick model, allowing for a distinguished random signal that interacts with the evolving spin configuration. We first derive the large-N dynamical mean-field limit and characterize the law of a typical coordinate by an effective Gaussian process whose covariance must satisfy a self-consistency relation. The resulting formulation is intrinsically nonlocal in time and is not, in its usual form, a closed finite-dimensional dynamical system. Our main contribution is an autonomous spectral representation of this limiting dynamics. We introduce an auxiliary stationary chain of Gaussian replicas whose one-step marginal reproduces the effective field appearing in the dynamical mean- field equation. Applying a matrix-valued Herglotz representation, or equivalently Fourier analysis in the replica index, converts the covariance structure of the chain into a family of finite-dimensional matrix-valued evolution equations indexed by the unit circle. The macroscopic observables, including the signal overlap, are then recovered from explicit spectral integrals. This representation replaces the original two-time self-consistency problem by an autonomous spectral closure and provides a convenient framework for both analysis and numerical computation. We prove the validity of the representation and compare its predictions with direct simulations of the finite-dimensional system

title: Omni-JEV: Text and Dual-Stream Speech Decisions
text:
Title: Omni-JEV: Text and Dual-Stream Speech Decisions
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

A user utterance does not uniquely determine the next action in full-duplex dialogue: its consequences depend on the assistant's response state and interaction history. Speech activity, utterance completion, and interruption intent provide related evidence, whose implications for a response require an explicit action policy. We formulate this task at collected-segment endpoints and introduce Omni-JEV, which maps text or role-indexed user and assistant-reference speech to probabilities over five interaction actions. An aligned speech-to-speech understanding backbone encodes the acoustic roles separately and shares its candidate readout with text inputs. Bilingual weak supervision supports cross-entropy fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning for probability-sensitive decisions (RLCD). We compare Gaussian-logit and categorical Choice RLCD from the same supervised initialization under matched training exposure, observing different trade-offs between classification and probability quality. Gaussian Omni-JEV achieves test accuracies of 84.08% for audio and 96.55% for text. This common action interface supports decisions about when a full-duplex voice assistant should respond, preserve ongoing speech, interrupt, or resume an interrupted response.

title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
text:
Title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. Cross-target similarity analysis confirms that the optimized patterns remain target-specific. Source characterization yields a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio of approximately 585. Accuracy is limited by pump-phase transfer, parasitic nonlinear background, waveshaper constraints, amplitude-only filtering, and measurement noise. Joint spectral intensity contains no spectral-phase information. Therefore, the results demonstrate control of measured frequency-bin populations and correlations, not complete reconstruction of the two-photon state. Phase-sensitive characterization is required to verify inter-bin coherence and quantify the entanglement dimensionality of the output state. Our results establish direct measurement feedback as a practical approach to reconfigurable frequency-bin correlation engineering when an accurate end-to-end model is unavailable.

title: Predicting Endocrine Disruptors: A Deep Learning QSAR Model for Estrogen Receptor Activity
text:
Title: Predicting Endocrine Disruptors: A Deep Learning QSAR Model for Estrogen Receptor Activity
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) threaten human health, ecosystems, and biodiversity by interfering with hormonal signaling pathways conserved across vertebrates. Traditional in vivo assays are costly and time-consuming, limiting their capacity to screen the growing number of chemicals. To address this, we developed a deep learning-based QSAR model to predict estrogen receptor (ER) binding molecules. Using a curated dataset of 224 compounds and 2,944 molecular descriptors and fingerprints, a deep neural network (DNN) incorporating dropout and batch normalization was trained and validated. The model achieved training and test accuracies of 96.65% and 91.30%, respectively, with an ROC-AUC of 0.81, a precision of 0.82, and a recall of 0.88 for the active class. Molecular docking against estrogen receptor (PDB ID: 5TOA) confirmed that several predicted compounds exhibited binding comparable to Estradiol, sharing key interactions. This model enables rapid screening of potential EDCs, supporting efficient chemical risk assessment and contributing to biodiversity conservation by identifying compounds that may disrupt reproduction and population stability in humans and wildlife.

title: An Integrative Computational Approach to Predict Viral Epitopes by Targeting the MHC-TCR Complexation
text:
Title: An Integrative Computational Approach to Predict Viral Epitopes by Targeting the MHC-TCR Complexation
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

T-cell immunity acts as a major defense system against controlling viral infections in vertebrates. During viral entry, innate immune cells degrade the viral proteins (antigens) and present them on their surface via Major Histocompatibility (MHC) proteins. T-cell receptors (TCRs) recognize these antigens/peptides presented by MHC (pMHC), initiating a T-cell mediated immune response. Despite its significance, the mechanism by which pMHC-TCR binding triggers T-cell activation remains unclear. In this study, we employed an integrative computational approach combining Bioinformatics, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations, and Machine Learning (ML) to identify viral epitopes as potential vaccine candidates. We performed large-scale all-atom and coarse-grained MD simulations on MHC-peptide-TCR complexes embedded into dendritic and T-cells, for which experimental immunogenicity data is available. One hundred fifty such systems are simulated for 1 μs each to capture the conformational and dynamical changes that underlie T-cell activation. Our ML model (DynamiT), trained on simulation-derived structural and dynamical features extracted from 2500 time points, revealed key determinants responsible for T-cell activation with an accuracy of 73.3%. Notably, we have identified the bending of the TCR transmembrane region, major dynamic motions of the TCRα constant region and the buried surface area at the pMHC and TCR interface as critical factors influencing immune response initiation. Our approach unravels the mechanism of T-cell mediated immune response and helps ML-guided screening of viral epitopes for vaccine development.

title: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of BC8 carbon near terapascal pressures
text:
Title: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of BC8 carbon near terapascal pressures
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Whether carbon forms crystalline structures beyond diamond at terapascal pressures remains unresolved. Predicted for nearly four decades, the denser BC8 phase has lacked direct crystallographic evidence. Here we report the first direct crystallographic identification of BC8 carbon, formed as a single crystal from molten carbon during laser-driven decaying-shock compression of [100]-oriented diamond following loading above 1.1 TPa. Using in situ orientation-resolved single-crystal X-ray diffraction, we observe discrete Bragg spots whose spacings and angular relationships are reproduced by a common orientation matrix within each indexed BC8 reflection group, providing constraints beyond powder peak matching. Our single-crystal formation strategy and direct diffraction evidence resolve the decades-long quest for a post-diamond carbon structure, demonstrating how dynamic loading pathways can make predicted high-pressure phases experimentally accessible.

title: Ionic gradients shape the spatial organization and dynamics of supramolecular polymers
text:
Title: Ionic gradients shape the spatial organization and dynamics of supramolecular polymers
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Living supramolecular materials such as microtubules and actin filaments assemble and function in dynamic, heterogeneous environments, subject to chemical concentration gradients. Their rapid and precise response to such gradients---via aggregation, disassembly, or autonomous motion---underlies the fine spatiotemporal control typical of living systems. Reproducing such responsiveness in synthetic materials is a central challenge in materials science and requires a molecular-level understanding of how gradients couple to supramolecular structure and dynamics, which remains difficult to access experimentally. To this end, we combine implicit-solvent coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) with the constant chemical potential MD (C$μ$MD) technique to investigate, at molecular resolution, the coupling of two prototypical supramolecular polymer models with externally imposed ionic concentration gradients. Despite their contrasting responses to homogeneous ionic conditions, both systems undergo pronounced spatial reorganization under the gradient, generating regions of locally enhanced supramolecular activity that are inaccessible to homogeneous systems with the same overall content of self-assembling species. Crucially, the local supramolecular dynamics is largely determined by the local concentrations, consistent with the formation of local quasi-equilibria: this direct connection between spatial composition and supramolecular activity emerges as a common governing principle across the two models. These findings shed light on the spatially complex supramolecular response that can be triggered by chemical gradients, and show how a single gradient simulation can encode this response across a continuous range of local chemical environments, thus providing a general strategy to investigate and design materials operating under spatially heterogeneous conditions.

title: Optimistic Gradient Algorithms with Randomized Coordinate and Variance Reduction Strategies for Composite Inclusions
text:
Title: Optimistic Gradient Algorithms with Randomized Coordinate and Variance Reduction Strategies for Composite Inclusions
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

In this paper, we consider a class of possibly nonmonotone finite-sum composite inclusions in which evaluating all components or updating all coordinates at every iteration can be computationally expensive. We develop two optimistic gradient frameworks that combine variance reduction with randomized block-coordinate updates. The first framework applies under a blockwise average Lipschitz continuity condition and the existence of a weak-Minty solution. It achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1/k)$ convergence rate for the expected squared residual, and its iterates converge almost surely under mild additional conditions. The second framework relies on a backward-forward reformulation under average co-coercivity and co-hypomonotonicity. It achieves faster $\mathcal{O}(1/k^2)$ and $o(1/k^2)$ rates for the expected squared residual, as well as $o(1/k^2)$ almost-sure rates. For both frameworks, we provide a generic condition on the stochastic estimator that covers mini-batch, loopless SVRG, and a generalized JacSketch-type estimator, and we derive the corresponding oracle complexities under importance-based block sampling. In particular, in highly heterogeneous regimes, the L-SVRG and JacSketch variants attain $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}ε^{-2}\big)$ and $\mathcal{O}\big(n + n^{2/3}ε^{-1}\big)$ oracle complexities for the nonaccelerated and accelerated methods, respectively. Numerical experiments illustrate the effects of variance reduction and block-coordinate sampling, and compare the proposed methods with existing baselines.

title: Clever Hans in Chemistry: Chemist Style Signals Confound Activity Prediction on Public Benchmarks
text:
Title: Clever Hans in Chemistry: Chemist Style Signals Confound Activity Prediction on Public Benchmarks
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Can machine learning models identify which chemist made a molecule from structure alone? If so, models trained on literature data may exploit chemist intent rather than learning causal structure-activity relationships. We test this by linking CHEMBL assays to publication authors and training a 1,815-class classifier to predict authors from molecular fingerprints, achieving 60% top-5 accuracy under scaffold-based splitting. We then train an activity model that receives only a protein identifier and an author-probability vector derived from structure, with no direct access to molecular descriptors. This author-only model achieves predictive power comparable to a simple baseline that has access to structure. This reveals a "Clever Hans" failure mode: models can predict bioactivity largely by inferring chemist goals and favorite targets without requiring a lab-independent understanding of chemistry. We analyze the sources of this leakage, propose author-disjoint splits, and recommend dataset practices to decouple chemist intent from biological outcomes.

title: Invariance principle for long-memory linear processes under sublinear expectations
text:
Title: Invariance principle for long-memory linear processes under sublinear expectations
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We establish an invariance principle for long-memory linear processes with power-law coefficients under sublinear expectations. Under truncated-moment and capacity-tail conditions, we construct these processes on a canonical space and prove weak convergence in continuous path space of their linearly interpolated, normalized partial sums. The limiting sublinear law is represented as an upper expectation over stochastic integrals with a fractional Brownian moving-average kernel and predictable volatility controls, driven by a two-sided classical Brownian motion. When variance uncertainty vanishes, the limit reduces to the classical fractional Brownian limit. The proof combines a multidimensional Rosenthal inequality, coefficient approximation, and the invariance principle for independent and identically distributed random variables to establish finite-dimensional convergence. Tightness follows from second-moment increment bounds. Uniform approximation on compact sets then extends the convergence from bounded Lipschitz to bounded continuous test functions.

title: Universal Approximation by Equivariant Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks with a Bilinear Readout
text:
Title: Universal Approximation by Equivariant Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks with a Bilinear Readout
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We prove universal approximation for the bilinear-readout equivariant message-passing network (BREMP), a reference architecture for equivariant graph neural network interatomic potentials. Its layers combine equivariant convolutions with affine maps, and its readout forms invariants from products of the equivariant features. We construct a one-layer feature that determines the local environment up to permutations of atoms of the same type. The construction uses spherical harmonic filters of degree no larger than the largest number of neighbors at a common distance from the center. Iterating the construction recovers the environment reachable in as many hops as there are layers, using the same bound on filter degrees at the layer cutoff. The readout approximates every continuous invariant function of the features uniformly on compact sets. Together these give universal approximation of atomic energies at a prescribed physical range using a shorter layer cutoff. We assume that, throughout the admissible class, message passing reaches all neighbors in each physical environment within a common number of layers. Finally, DPA4, an interatomic potential architecture in production use, inherits this result by approximating the BREMP layers constructed in the proof and realizing the bilinear readout.

title: Attractivity Implies Lyapunov Stability for Multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini Systems
text:
Title: Attractivity Implies Lyapunov Stability for Multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini Systems
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study the linear multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini recurrence with uniformly bounded boundary data prescribed on the open coordinate faces. Attractivity is understood in the sense of Pringsheim convergence, in which all discrete indices tend to infinity. We establish that attractivity alone implies Lyapunov stability, and consequently is equivalent to asymptotic stability, for an arbitrary number of discrete directions. Our proof combines inheritance of attractivity by lower-dimensional subsystems, a Baire-category uniform boundedness argument, and word-sum estimates to control coordinate slabs outside the Pringsheim tail. We use a generalized spectral stability criterion proved in a separate companion preprint, without reproving that criterion here. We also obtain a uniform exponential interior estimate and contrast our boundary/convergence convention with an earlier two-dimensional attractivity theorem.

title: State-specific perturbation theory for configuration interaction singles: Theoretical analysis, benchmarks, and improvement with size-intensive level shifts
text:
Title: State-specific perturbation theory for configuration interaction singles: Theoretical analysis, benchmarks, and improvement with size-intensive level shifts
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We recently proposed a state-specific second-order perturbation theory based on the configuration interaction singles (CIS) state, termed CIS(2). Here, we clarify its theoretical connections, assess the accuracy of its excitation energies in greater detail, and develop size-intensive level shifts to improve both accuracy and convergence of its amplitude equations. We first derive the MP2 structure of its working equations and show that our previously introduced Hybrid partition recovers CIS(D) when the ground-state Fock operator is used and the residual Fock action on the CIS reference is neglected. For this partition, an expanded benchmark shows that using the CIS-state Fock operator improves Rydberg and especially charge-transfer accuracy relative to CIS(D), while slightly worsening valence accuracy. We analyze how the hole and particle densities contribute to these changes in excitation energy, which differ among the classes. We then introduce size-intensive level shifts that preserve the ground-state correlation contribution of noninteracting fragments while leaving the ground-state MP2 energy unchanged. With appropriately calibrated parameters, these shifts improve overall accuracy and substantially accelerate convergence without increasing the formal scaling of the amplitude solve. Different optimal parameters for valence and Rydberg states reveal the limitations of a common parameter. The analysis further shows that shifting the contracted-triples block contributes markedly to the excitation-energy correction in addition to accelerating convergence.

title: Different Corpora, Different Skills? A Paired Study of Small Language Models
text:
Title: Different Corpora, Different Skills? A Paired Study of Small Language Models
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Small language models are often trained under tight data budgets, where the choice of pretraining corpus may matter as much as model size or training recipe. We compare two contrasting corpora at matched 10-million- and 37-million-word budgets: the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica and the BabyLM 2026 strict pretraining corpus. For each corpus, we train teacher models, distilled 58-million-parameter Baby-Llama students, and no-distillation student ablations, using the same model families, training recipes, and evaluation protocol across corpora. Across BLiMP, BLiMP Supplement, EWoK, Entity Tracking, and COMPS, the corpora produce different skill profiles rather than a single quality ranking. BabyLM 2026 is consistently stronger on linguistic acceptability benchmarks, while Britannica is often stronger on Entity Tracking, a synthetic state-tracking task. The contrast appears across teacher and student models and at both budgets, with the cleanest cross-seed replication in the distilled student comparison. Targeted controls show that the central contrast persists after matching training exposure and at a longer diagnostic context; direct teacher ensembling also does not reproduce the 10M Britannica student's Entity Tracking behavior. Entity Tracking magnitudes nevertheless remain sensitive to training dynamics. For this corpus pair, corpus choice can therefore produce different relative skill profiles at small scale, motivating multi-benchmark evaluation when comparing pretraining data.

title: Neutron Scattering studies of the density dependence of One-dimensional Quantum Fluids
text:
Title: Neutron Scattering studies of the density dependence of One-dimensional Quantum Fluids
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

In previous work, we demonstrated that $^4$He confined within a templated porous material preplated with a noble gas to enhance dimensional reduction exhibits one-dimensional behavior. Neutron scattering revealed that the excitations in confined $^4$He are qualitatively distinct from those in two- and three-dimensional superfluid helium, aligning with quantum Monte Carlo calculations. These simulations suggest that three solid layers form, with a one-dimensional liquid located at the center of the pore. Here, we present neutron scattering results as the filling fraction of the one-dimensional core is varied. We observe that the one-dimensional liquid always forms with a fixed density, even as the pore filling increases. We posit that this is due to the growth of the one dimensional extent of the liquid as the filling is increased, but its density remains unchanged.

title: Torsion, valley holonomy, and Berry phases of quasiparticles encircling dislocations and defect complexes in graphene
text:
Title: Torsion, valley holonomy, and Berry phases of quasiparticles encircling dislocations and defect complexes in graphene
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We investigate the geometric phase acquired by low-energy quasiparticles encircling defects in graphene. Following Anandan, this phase is the holonomy of the Poincare connection; its translational part couples momentum to torsion, giving $P_a\int T^a$. In the Katanaev-Volovich theory, dislocation torsion is confined to the defect core. For graphene, the relevant momentum is $\hbar(τ_3\KK+\mathbf q)$. We show that an isolated dislocation yields a topological valley factor $e^{\mp2πi/3}$ when its Burgers vector $\bb$ lies outside the $\sqrt3\times\sqrt3$ superlattice, together with a dispersive factor $e^{-i\mathbf q\cdot\bb}$ for every nonzero $\bb$. The topological factor recovers the lattice result of Mesaros et al. as a torsion-flux phase; 4-8 dislocations retain only the dispersive contribution. Composing Volterra elements gives the holonomy of defect complexes. At zero net Frank angle, it depends only on the net Burgers vector. The valley flux obeys a three-coloring rule: pentagons and heptagons contribute according to their Kekule site color, whereas squares and octagons do not. Atomic models confirm that ring content alone does not fix the phase: a 5-8-5 core is invisible as a divacancy or as a dislocation with $|\bb|=\sqrt3a$, but carries flux $\pm1/3$ for $\bb=2\mathbf a_1$. The torsion trace produces no geometric phase: its vector coupling violates time-reversal symmetry, while the allowed axial coupling causes only anisotropic short-range scattering.

title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
text:
Title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

title: PCR-ALERA: A PCR-ELISA analogue but antibody-free DNA detection system
text:
Title: PCR-ALERA: A PCR-ELISA analogue but antibody-free DNA detection system
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

PCR-ALERA is a new concept for DNA detection that combines DNA amplification by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with an activator-linked enzyme reactivation assay (ALERA). PCR-ALERA resembles the commercial, semi-quantitative PCR-ELISA assay that offers high sensitivity and high-throughput screening in microplates. PCR-ALERA overcomes a major drawback of PCR-ELISA since it does not require the time-consuming handling of expensive antibodies. In the first step of the assay, commercially available modified nucleotides were incorporated during PCR amplification of the target DNA. A selenocysteine containing peptide (the activator) was linked to the amplified DNA by click chemistry. This peptide has been optimized for the highly efficient activation of the latent protease papain by selenolate-triggered disulfide cleavage. The DNA-peptide hybrid was then immoblized in microplate wells and incubated with latent papain. The latter was readily activated and converted a fluorogenic substrate to a fluorescent product with high catalytic turnover. Overall assay time is about 4 hours including PCR.

title: A Time-Resolved Framework for Quantifying Neuronal Network State Transitions
text:
Title: A Time-Resolved Framework for Quantifying Neuronal Network State Transitions
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Electrophysiological recordings provide powerful tools for characterizing the dynamics of neuronal networks. In vitro neuronal cultures offer a controlled setting for investigating network responses to diverse interventions, including pharmacological and optogenetic stimulation. However, conventional analyses often reduce electrophysiological activity to aggregate measures calculated over fixed temporal windows, providing only a static representation of the network state. Here, we introduce a comprehensive, multiparametric analytical framework designed to characterize both the temporal evolution of network activity and the transitional states induced by external interventions. The framework combines multiple network discriminators with a compositional analysis that resolves electrode-level responses into excited, inhibited, and unchanged states over successive temporal segments. We apply the framework to electrophysiological recordings obtained under pharmacological interventions with 4-aminopyridine (4-AP), optogenetic stimulation, and additional benchmark conditions. The results demonstrate that the proposed analysis can reveal subtle and transient responses that may be difficult to detect using conventional aggregate measures, including responses to low-dose pharmacological interventions. These findings highlight the value of temporally resolved and compositional analyses for characterizing heterogeneous neuronal network responses in vitro.

title: Efficient Plane-to-Point Energy Transfer from Supramolecular Excitonic Systems to Molecular Acceptors
text:
Title: Efficient Plane-to-Point Energy Transfer from Supramolecular Excitonic Systems to Molecular Acceptors
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Collective excitonic interactions in supramolecular assemblies offer opportunities for efficient light harvesting and directed energy transport. Here, we demonstrate efficient energy transfer from two-dimensional silica-encapsulated TDBC J-aggregate sheets to covalently attached ATTO 590 molecular acceptors. Silica encapsulation preserves the J-aggregate excitonic properties while enabling acceptor functionalization at a defined separation from the donor plane. Steady-state donor quenching and acceptor sensitization yield energy-transfer efficiencies of 75-81% in solution, while time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal donor lifetime shortening. We develop a generalized Forster resonance energy-transfer model for an extended planar donor coupled to localized molecular acceptors, predicting an inverse fourth-power dependence of the transfer rate on donor-acceptor separation. Using experimental spectroscopic data and estimated structural parameters, the model predicts an energy-transfer rate of 4.77 x 10^10 s^-1, approximately ten times faster than the intrinsic donor decay rate, corresponding to a theoretical energy-transfer efficiency of approximately 91%. These findings provide a framework for developing hybrid excitonic architectures for light harvesting.

title: Which data samples matter when training a quantum model?
text:
Title: Which data samples matter when training a quantum model?
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The expressivity, loss landscapes, and generalization behavior of quantum machine learning models have been studied extensively, yet mainly from a model-centric point of view. Little is known about the compatibility of particular quantum models with specific datasets. In this work, we study quantum machine learning models with a data-dependent focus by establishing a quantum-compatible form of the V-usable information. This metric quantifies the information a model can extract from a dataset, enabling a direct, data-centric comparison of different models. We employ this metric to study which data points contribute most significantly to a model's learning process. This enables us to develop an informed preselection strategy for data subsets that can significantly improve the data efficiency of the training pipeline. This work establishes the V-usable information as a powerful diagnostic tool for learning dynamics and a practical route to data-efficient quantum machine learning.

title: Dynamic heart rate variability for classification of arrhythmia burden
text:
Title: Dynamic heart rate variability for classification of arrhythmia burden
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Purpose: Heart rate variability (HRV) may provide information beyond heart rate (HR) for identifying arrhythmia burden, but the value of temporal HRV variation remains unclear. This study developed a dynamic HRV measure quantifying the interquartile range of window-level root mean square of successive RR-interval differences (IQRRMSSD) and evaluated its utility in classifying total abnormal-beat and premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden compared with the conventional RR-based HRV measure, RMSSD. Methods: Manually annotated 30-minute ECG recordings from 43 individuals were analyzed using overlapping windows. A linear support vector classifier was used to classify individuals as having high or low arrhythmia burden, defined using 1% and 10% burden thresholds. Four feature sets were evaluated: HR alone, HR with RMSSD, HR with IQRRMSSD, and all three measures. Performance was assessed using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation. Results: HRV-containing feature sets generally outperformed HR alone, depending on outcome and threshold. At the 1% threshold, IQRRMSSD showed particularly high sensitivity for total abnormal-beat and PVC burden ($0.970 \pm 0.064$ and $0.882 \pm 0.193$, respectively). At the 10% threshold, conventional RMSSD showed the strongest overall discrimination, achieving a ROC-AUC of 0.947 for PVC burden. Combined features sometimes improved the sensitivity-specificity balance but not overall discrimination. Conclusion: These findings suggest that a conventional RR-based HRV measure is informative for elevated ectopic burden, while a dynamic HRV measure may provide complementary information for lower-burden abnormalities.

title: Frequency-Space Mechanics: A Sequence and Coordinate-Free Representation for Protein Function Prediction
text:
Title: Frequency-Space Mechanics: A Sequence and Coordinate-Free Representation for Protein Function Prediction
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Protein function prediction is dominated by representations grounded in sequence and static structure, neither of which captures the collective vibrational dynamics through which proteins act. Here we introduce frequency-space mechanics, a representational framework in which a protein is encoded as a mechanical harmonics graph (MHG): nodes are vibrational modes derived from molecular dynamics, and edges are harmonic couplings weighted by octave alignment between mode frequencies. The representation is coordinate-free, sequence-independent, scale-invariant, and inhabits a latent mechanical space in which the original atomic coordinates have been projected out. The same construction applies to any system with a tractable eigendecomposition. Trained on 5,238 SwissProt proteins under a strict 30% sequence-identity split and using no sequence information, a graph neural network over static MHGs predicts GO molecular function terms across the ontology, demonstrating that vibrational physics alone encodes broad functional class. Kuramoto entrainment of the harmonic coupling graph, formally a Hamiltonian operation over mode frequencies and directly compatible with quantum annealing hardware, improves prediction for proteins whose function depends on collective conformational dynamics. On CLIC1, a fold- and function-switching chloride channel excluded from training, entrainment amplifies channel-activity signal 7.5-fold and antioxidant signal 2.4-fold, recovering both functional states from dynamics alone.

title: Multiphysics Simulation Framework for Continuous Ion Transport and Energetics in Atmospheric Pressure Interfaces
text:
Title: Multiphysics Simulation Framework for Continuous Ion Transport and Energetics in Atmospheric Pressure Interfaces
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Optimizing atmospheric pressure interfaces requires balancing efficient ion transport with unwanted collision activation. The complex environment at the inlet region, including rapid pressure drops, RF/DC electric fields, ion-gas collisions, and space charge effects, makes simulation of this system challenging. In this work, we introduce MuCITE (Multiphysics simulation for Continuous Ion Transport and Energetics), which combines continuous ion injection, precomputed electric and gas flow fields, and particle-in-cell space charge updates. Furthermore, by employing improved impulsive collision theory, it can not only predict transport but also analyze the loss position of ions and the evolution of their kinetic energy, internal energy, and dissociation probability during transport. Transport predictions with ion currents and activation trends of in-source fragmentation were compared with experimental measurements using a custom-built source and a Q-Exactive HF source. The results show that the simulation predictions agree well with the experimental results and can serve as a reference before experiments. MuCITE allows users to derive ion transport, output beam characteristics, and ion energy through the configurable interface geometry and operating conditions. It supports simulation-guided design and tunable parameters to achieve predicted efficient ion transport or in source activation.

title: Modular Bayesian Inference for Partially Misspecified Mixtures with Uncertain Class Labels
text:
Title: Modular Bayesian Inference for Partially Misspecified Mixtures with Uncertain Class Labels
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Scientific inference often involves observations from multiple latent populations whose class memberships are uncertain and must be inferred from available data. While full Bayesian mixture modelling provides a principled approach to joint uncertainty quantification in this setting, often the model is misspecified or less trustworthy for populations that are not the target of the inference, which can distort posterior inference for the parameters of interest. We propose a modular Bayesian framework that safeguards against such biases. We decouple classification from downstream inference using fixed class probabilities, for example from a classifier trained on a subset of labelled data. We then protect inference on the parameters of interest by preventing the likelihood contributions of less trustworthy populations from influencing them. A key benefit of this principled modularization is that it greatly simplifies inference, reducing a fully joint mixture analysis to sampling label allocations, fitting the protected downstream model for each sample, and averaging the resulting posteriors. We establish calibration conditions on these class probabilities under which the proposed procedure preserves the inferential target of the analysis with known labels, and demonstrate the method in synthetic experiments and in cosmological analysis of photometric supernova samples.

title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
text:
Title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on one of the most abundant chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. We describe three directions to combine and extend these effects and overcome their limitations. Pore hierarchy resolves the classical trade-off between interface area and transport speed by combining large and small pores and thereby allows functions to be scaled from thin planar films to three-dimensional components. Surface modification becomes a design variable that tunes the interaction between water and the pore wall. It can be set locally and, with switchable coatings, on demand. Finally, pores only a few molecules wide alter the properties of water itself. In the absence of a bulk-like volume, water can become dielectrically anisotropic and highly conductive. Altogether, these steps turn porous silicon from a responsive material into an adaptive, water-driven material.

title: Feeling Easier, Working Harder: Cognitive Load in AI-Assisted Code Comprehension
text:
Title: Feeling Easier, Working Harder: Cognitive Load in AI-Assisted Code Comprehension
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Software developers spend significant time reading and understanding code, increasingly supplemented by generative AI. While these tools aim to reduce the difficulty of reading code, interacting with them introduces a dual-task environment that may impose extraneous cognitive load that is challenging to capture. This study investigates how access to generative AI affects developers' real-time cognitive workload, code comprehension performance, and self-perceived code comprehension strategies. We conducted a 3x2 within-subjects study with 20 novice CS students reviewing Java code snippets of varying lengths with or without AI assistance, followed by an AI-unassisted comprehension quiz. Cognitive workload was continuously captured using a Detection-Response Task (tDRT) during both reading and quiz phases, and compared to post-quiz NASA-TLX and SEQ scores. AI assistance significantly increased objective cognitive workload, raising tDRT reaction times by 11.2%, yet participants' perceived workload remained unchanged. Code comprehension scores were high under both conditions, with no evidence that AI assistance improved comprehension at the difficulty levels evaluated; a ceiling effect limited power to detect benefits on harder tasks. Qualitatively, participants reported trusting the AI conditionally -verifying its output against their own reading for more complex snippets, but directly trusting it for simpler code- and, while many felt their reading process was unchanged, a notable subset shifted toward skimming or reading the AI's explanations in place of the code itself. These findings reveal that developers do not accurately perceive the cognitive resources they expend when managing AI tools. This study provides evidence of added cognitive effort associated with using generative AI, pointing towards a need to account for this dual-task penalty in software engineering tools and education.

title: Uniform Dimension Theorem for SLE in Natural Time
text:
Title: Uniform Dimension Theorem for SLE in Natural Time
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

For $0<κ<8$, we prove a uniform dimension transformation theorem for SLE in natural time: on a single probability-one event, Hausdorff and packing dimensions of every time set are multiplied by $d=1+κ/8$, and the same holds for lower and upper box dimensions of every bounded time set. The result applies to self-similar SLE with stationary increments, chordal SLE in the half-plane, and chordal SLE in bounded piecewise $C^1$ Jordan domains. In the last case, the box-dimension conclusion holds under a positive-angle endpoint hypothesis. We also establish boundary-inclusive local Hölder continuity of every order below $1/d$ for chordal SLE in natural time and identify the exact local dimension $d$ of the natural occupation measure on compact time intervals.

title: Detecting Nonbilocal Correlations via Parameterized Elegant Joint Measurement
text:
Title: Detecting Nonbilocal Correlations via Parameterized Elegant Joint Measurement
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum networks constitute a defining resource for quantum information processing; however, their nonclassical behavior is jointly governed by the choice of measurement basis and the independence of the distributed sources. We study a bilocal entanglement-swapping network in which the central node performs a three-parameter elegant joint measurement (EJM). For two independent Bell-state sources, we construct two binary edge observables and then derive a quantum prediction involving three parameters, which surpasses the classical constraints. In particular, the parameter θ controls both the degree of entanglement of the EJM basis states and the maximum value of the quantum prediction. These results provide an analytic and directly reproducible route for tuning nonbilocal correlations in an experimentally relevant two-source network.

title: Residual Carleman lift for nonlinear lattice Boltzmann simulations
text:
Title: Residual Carleman lift for nonlinear lattice Boltzmann simulations
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Low-order Carleman embeddings replace nonlinear dynamics by a larger linear system, but truncation errors can accumulate even when the underlying nonlinear model is accurately approximated by a quadratic equation. We construct a residual Carleman lift (RC2) of lattice Boltzmann dynamics in which an independently evolved spectral background supplies the coefficients and forcing of a second-order residual lift. In a double-shear-layer test, conventional fixed-rest Carleman reaches $87.3\%$ final error, whereas prepared RC2 achieves $0.136\%$ through vortex roll-up, without restarting the lift or using fine-reference feedback. The results demonstrate control of the finite-time accuracy of a fixed-order linear embedding through nonlinear preparation.

title: In vitro binding energies capture Klf4 occupancy across the human genome
text:
Title: In vitro binding energies capture Klf4 occupancy across the human genome
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Transcription factors (TFs) regulate gene expression by binding to specific genomic loci determined by DNA sequence. Their sequence specificity is commonly summarized by a consensus binding motif. However, eukaryotic genomes contain billions of low-affinity DNA sequences to which TFs associate with a sequence-dependent binding energy. We currently lack insight into how the genomic sequence defines this spectrum of binding energies and the resulting pattern of TF localization. Here, we set out to obtain a quantitative understanding of sequence-dependent TF binding to both motif and non-motif sequences. We achieve this by first pursuing accurate measurements of physical binding energies of the human TF Klf4 to a library of short DNA sequences in a fluorescence-anisotropy-based bulk competitive binding assay. Second, we show that the highly non-linear sequence dependence of Klf4 binding energies can be captured by combining a linear model of binding energies with an Ising model of the coupled recognition of nucleotides by a TF. We find that this statistical mechanics model parametrized by our in vitro measurements captures Klf4 binding patterns on individual long DNA molecules stretched in the optical tweezer, and is predictive for Klf4 occupancy across the entire human genome without additional fit parameters.

title: Multimodal Road Closure Mapping via Cross-Modal Graph Attention
text:
Title: Multimodal Road Closure Mapping via Cross-Modal Graph Attention
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Accurate and timely identification of road closures is critical for large-scale navigation and logistics systems, yet remains challenging due to the need to jointly reason over visual evidence, spatial context, and road network topology. Existing approaches either rely on manual map updates or focus on detecting closure-related objects without resolving which road segment is affected. In this work, we introduce a unified multimodal and multitask framework that jointly performs road closure classification (no, partial, complete) and road segment association within a single learning architecture. Our model integrates graph-structured map data, satellite imagery augmented with projected street-level detections, and street-view images using modality-specific encoders and cross-modal transformer attention, enabling explicit reasoning over visual cues and network topology. Evaluated on nearly 20K real-world scenarios collected from a large-scale commercial vehicle fleet, our approach achieves 72.7% closure classification accuracy and 60% road segment association accuracy, outperforming frontier vision-language models by over 28 percentage points on closure classification while being over 4,000x smaller and 100x faster at inference. Extensive ablations demonstrate the importance of cross-modal attention, edge-aware pooling, and graph message passing for accurate geospatial reasoning. This work establishes the first benchmark for joint road closure classification and segment-level attribution, and shows that task-specific architectural inductive biases substantially outperform general-purpose multimodal models for structured geospatial understanding.

title: Distinguishing life from non-life via molecular frontier orbital energy gaps
text:
Title: Distinguishing life from non-life via molecular frontier orbital energy gaps
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Amino acids (AAs) are a key target in the search for life beyond Earth due to their extensive role in the machinery of all known life, persistence over geologic timescales, and analytical detectability. However, AAs can also arise from abiotic processes on planets and in space. For example, material from asteroid Bennu contained 33 AAs, including 15 of the 20 proteinogenic AAs that are fundamental to life's functions. Distinguishing life from non-life based on AAs in a sample remains an unsolved problem, particularly when their isotopic and structural signatures (e.g., chirality) could be altered via physicochemical processes. Here we introduce LUMOS (Life Unveiled via Molecular Orbital Signatures), a statistical framework that distinguishes life from non-life by analyzing the distribution of abundance-weighted HOMO-LUMO gap (HLG) values of AAs within a sample. Compilation of AAs datasets from diverse environments and provenances revealed that abiotic samples display highly uniform distributions of AAs HLGs. In contrast, biotic samples show greater variance and preference towards AAs with lower HLG, likely reflecting the need for life to control when, where, and how chemical reactions occur. LUMOS achieves >95% accuracy in distinguishing biotic versus abiotic provenance across diverse environmental and extraterrestrial conditions. These results suggest that varied molecular reactivity within biochemical systems may be a universal feature of life, representing an agnostic biosignature unlinked to the specific set of AAs used by life as we know it. LUMOS is compatible with existing analytical instrumentation, applicable to returned samples or in situ analyses. Broader characterization of abiotic and biotic environments will further refine the chemical boundaries separating biotic from abiotic chemical systems.

title: When Does Context Help? A Systematic Study of Target-Conditional Molecular Property Prediction
text:
Title: When Does Context Help? A Systematic Study of Target-Conditional Molecular Property Prediction
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

We present the first systematic study of when target context helps molecular property prediction, evaluating context conditioning across 10 diverse protein families, 4 fusion architectures, data regimes spanning 67-9,409 training compounds, and both temporal and random evaluation splits. Using NestDrug, a FiLM-based architecture that conditions molecular representations on target identity, we characterize both success and failure modes with three principal findings. First, fusion architecture dominates: FiLM outperforms concatenation by 24.2 percentage points and additive conditioning by 8.6 pp; how you incorporate context matters more than whether you include it. Second, context enables otherwise impossible predictions: on data-scarce CYP3A4 (67 training compounds), multi-task transfer achieves 0.686 AUC where per-target Random Forest collapses to 0.238. Third, context can systematically hurt: distribution mismatch causes 10.2 pp degradation on BACE1; few-shot adaptation consistently underperforms zero-shot. Beyond methodology, we expose fundamental flaws in standard benchmarking: 1-nearest-neighbor Tanimoto achieves 0.991 AUC on DUD-E without any learning, and 50% of actives leak from training data, rendering absolute performance metrics meaningless. Our temporal split evaluation (train up to 2020, test 2021-2024) achieves stable 0.843 AUC with no degradation, providing the first rigorous evidence that context-conditional molecular representations generalize to future chemical space.

title: A Modular Perspective for Modeling MARL Systems
text:
Title: A Modular Perspective for Modeling MARL Systems
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

The growing complexity of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has fragmented the literature, obscuring underlying architectural choices behind diverse implementations. This fragmentation makes it difficult to evaluate critical modeling dimensions in isolation, identify how components affect the resulting system dynamics, and compare, reuse, or combine contributions across the literature. This paper proposes a modular perspective for modeling, analyzing, and implementing MARL systems. We decompose them into eight functional modules: agents, environments, learning, reward modeling, training and execution modes, communication, modeling of other agents, and evaluation criteria. For each module, we clarify its role and review representative approaches. We instantiate this decomposition in MARLKIT, a framework whose modules are explicit and interchangeable. MARLKIT demonstrates how the proposed perspective supports transparent experimental assumptions and the controlled variation and combination of MARL mechanisms. Experiments illustrate its ability to prototype, compare, reuse and combine modules while making differences between configurations explicit. Overall, the paper provides a structured perspective on MARL modeling and implementation, offering a common language for making modeling choices explicit, supporting clearer descriptions of MARL approaches, and supporting more controlled experimentation through the systematic isolation and combination of MARL mechanisms.

title: Meet biform singletons in your area! Topological actions for edge modes
text:
Title: Meet biform singletons in your area! Topological actions for edge modes
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We present topological field theories propagating biform singleton fields as edge modes. In even spacetime dimensions $D=2p$, these are irreducible representations of the conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,2p)$ with two-column Young diagrams of height $p$. Their duality properties depend on the parity of $p$: They propagate chiral degrees of freedom for odd $p$, and exhibit electric--magnetic duality for even $p$. We are able to construct the topological actions by realising the hidden conformal symmetry inherent to singletons geometrically in terms of an auxiliary bulk $\text{AdS}_{2p+1}$ geometry. Using these as a starting point, we are able to apply a recently established covariant boundary reduction procedure to yield novel action formulations with manifest Lorentz covariance. We also show how, breaking manifest Lorentz covariance, we recover known formulations of biform singletons.

title: GeONet: Geometry-Encoded Operator Network for Predicting Flow in Heterogeneous Porous Media
text:
Title: GeONet: Geometry-Encoded Operator Network for Predicting Flow in Heterogeneous Porous Media
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Rapid prediction of pressure-driven flow in microfluidic porous media is important for experimental design, tracer-test interpretation, and digital-twin development for subsurface energy and critical mineral applications. High-fidelity simulations resolve geometry-controlled flow but are computationally expensive across large geometry ensembles. Here, we introduce GeONet, a Geometry-Encoded Operator Network that predicts steady-state pressure fields by jointly representing material properties, spatial coordinates, and solid--void geometry. GeONet extends the Branch--Trunk architecture with a dedicated Leaf Network encoding the binary domain mask through multiscale features. The Branch Network represents porosity and permeability, the Trunk Network combines coordinates with local geometric descriptors and random Fourier features, and a gated DeepMixer integrates these representations to predict pressure. GeONet was trained and evaluated using 5,000 PFLOTRAN simulations of heterogeneous Reduced Complexity Platform domains, comprising nearly 30 TB of data. Comparisons with pore-scale Stokes solutions across three geometries yielded Pearson correlations of 0.987--0.991 and $R^2$ values of 0.974--0.982, supporting PFLOTRAN as reference data. Under matched partitions and two-stage hyperparameter optimization, GeONet substantially outperformed a boundary-condition-aware DeepONet baseline. Across three held-out domains, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0381--0.0500, MAPE of 1.76--2.59%, and $R^2$ of 0.9673--0.9822, versus 0.1483--0.2040, 7.81--10.45%, and 0.5658--0.7126 for DeepONet, respectively. On three additional unseen geometries, GeONet achieved NRMSE of 0.0448--0.0676 and $R^2$ of 0.9511--0.9770. These results demonstrate improved accuracy, pressure-range preservation, and cross-geometry generalization through explicit geometry encoding.

title: Parametrize Integer Programming by Packing Imbalanced Circuits
text:
Title: Parametrize Integer Programming by Packing Imbalanced Circuits
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study the standard form Integer Programming problem (IP) parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number. This number is $0$ if and only if $A$ can be transformed to a totally unimodular matrix by row operations, in which case (IP) is solvable in polynomial time. We show that if the constraint matrix represents a graphic matroid, (IP) is fixed-parameter tractable when parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number of the matrix. The proof combines an Erdős-Pósa property for edge-colored non-monochromatic cycles with a reduction to mixed-integer programming using few integer variables. In contrast, by a reduction from the parity potential problem, we show NP-completeness of feasibility of (IP) when the constraint matrix represents a cographic matroid, even if kernel of the constraint matrix is $2$-regular and imbalanced circuits pairwise intersect.

title: Hermes: Large DEL Datasets Train Generalizable Protein-Ligand Binding Prediction Models
text:
Title: Hermes: Large DEL Datasets Train Generalizable Protein-Ligand Binding Prediction Models
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The quality and consistency of training data remain critical bottlenecks for protein-ligand binding prediction. Public affinity datasets, aggregated from thousands of labs and assay formats, introduce biases that limit model generalization and complicate evaluation. DNA-encoded chemical libraries (DELs) offer a potential solution: unified experimental protocols generating massive binding datasets across diverse chemical and protein target space. We present Hermes, a lightweight transformer trained exclusively on DEL data from screens against hundreds of protein targets, representing one of the largest and most protein-diverse DEL training sets applied to protein-ligand interaction (PLI) modeling to date. Despite never seeing traditional affinity measurements during training, Hermes generalizes to held-out targets, novel chemical scaffolds, and external benchmarks derived from public binding data and high-throughput screens. Our results demonstrate that DEL data alone captures transferable protein-ligand interaction representations, while Hermes' minimal architecture enables inference speeds suitable for large-scale virtual screening.

title: Optimal Last-Iterate Bounds for Nonexpansive Stochastic Approximation
text:
Title: Optimal Last-Iterate Bounds for Nonexpansive Stochastic Approximation
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

We establish last-iterate mean-square residual bounds for nonexpansive stochastic approximation (SA), or stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann (KM) iterations. In particular, we consider fixed-point mappings that are nonexpansive with respect to the Euclidean norm, and focus on polynomially decaying stepsizes. We study three conditions on the conditional second moment of the noise, and obtain bounds that are optimal up to logarithmic factors in each case. When it scales linearly with the squared residual, the best rate is $O(1/k^{1-ε})$ for any $ε>0$. In this case, for all considered stepsizes, our bounds match those of the noiseless KM iteration. When it is bounded by a constant, the best rate is $O(\log^2 k/\sqrt{k})$. When it scales affinely with the squared norm of the iterate, the best rate is $O(1/k^{1/2-ε})$, and the mean-square residual can diverge if the stepsizes are not square-summable. Thus, unlike for contractive SA, square-summable stepsizes are necessary for nonexpansive SA. We demonstrate how various algorithms with cocoercive maps, such as stochastic gradient descent, linear SA, and learning in cocoercive games, fit into our framework, and how the different noise conditions arise in each of them.

title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
text:
Title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicted. To support exploration of many mutants, we developed a fast, physics-constrained all-atom predictor that utilizes explicit geometric constraint enforcement to achieve >10 fold increase in speed than AlphaFold3 with guaranteed physical validity. Lastly, ProTEUS refines its prediction and understanding of protein activity through closed loop experimental feedback to guide evolution toward a desired phenotype. ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type. ProTEUS provides a world-model framework that connects virtual evaluation of mutational outcomes with experimental learning for efficient protein evolution.

title: Exact thermal correlators at vanishing momenta and the black hole singularity
text:
Title: Exact thermal correlators at vanishing momenta and the black hole singularity
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We study thermal two- and three-point functions of scalar primaries in holographic CFTs dual to AdS black branes. The three-point function arises from a cubic scalar interaction in the bulk. At vanishing external momenta, the tree-level results can be written in closed form and are exact in the operator dimensions. We reproduce them through direct CFT calculations in two dimensions. Their large-dimension expansions contain subleading exponential terms encoding the radial proper time from the horizon to the black hole singularity. These results provide an exact test of earlier WKB and saddle-point predictions for higher-point thermal correlators, confirming the proper-time signature while correcting the predicted asymptotic form.

title: Thirty years of primordial deuterium abundances: A provenance-aware statistical reanalysis
text:
Title: Thirty years of primordial deuterium abundances: A provenance-aware statistical reanalysis
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

(ABRIDGED:) Primordial deuterium provides one of the most precise observational tests of Big Bang nucleosynthesis, yet the published literature is built on a comparatively small number of high-redshift absorption systems. We construct a provenance-aware database of 957 published primordial-D/H values from 247 publications spanning 1994--2026 and trace observational entries, wherever possible, to their underlying physical absorbers. Of the 795 observational entries, 80.1 percent represent reused individual or compilation values; only 11.4 percent correspond to new determinations of individual absorption systems. Although 52 distinct absorbers are identified overall, the eight most frequently represented systems account for 62.0 percent of all identifiable absorber mentions. An inverse Herfindahl--Hirschman measure applied to our full database gives an effective representation equivalent to only 16.28 equally represented absorbers, demonstrating that the published literature is strongly concentrated around a much smaller effective subset. Despite this strong internal dependence, the modern consensus value of $10^5({\rm D/H})\simeq2.5$ is robust to alternative absorber-level treatments and survives removal of the eight dominant systems. However, the apparent precision of literature-level compilations is more sensitive to repeated representation than a simple count of published values implies. We also identify a synchronised transition in the compilation literature around 2013--2014, associated with increasingly selective and homogeneous analyses while older individual values continued to circulate. The modern D/H consensus is therefore robust in central value, but the underlying literature is less statistically independent than its publication density suggests. This thus highlights the importance of provenance-aware analysis in precision cosmology.

title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
text:
Title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.

title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Quasi-Newton SQCQP Method for Nonlinear Programming Problems
text:
Title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Quasi-Newton SQCQP Method for Nonlinear Programming Problems
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

In this paper, we propose a variance-reduced stochastic quasi-Newton sequential quadratic constrained quadratic programming method (VR-QN-SQCQP) for finite-sum nonlinear optimization with equality and inequality constraints. Exact nonlinear-constraint Hessians are replaced entirely by safeguarded symmetric rank-one (SR1) curvature models built from first-order constraint gradients, while PAGE estimates the objective gradient and an exact \(L_1\) merit function provides globalization. Under explicit regularity, boundedness, relative QCQP-accuracy, and step-length assumptions, the analysis establishes almost-sure subsequential convergence to Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) points and, under stronger uniform step-length and error-control conditions, an expected \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer-iteration bound for the squared KKT residual. A conditional local stability result also compares learned-curvature directions with their exact-Hessian counterparts. Numerical experiments compare VR-QN-SQCQP against Exact-SQCQP-PAGE on Sparse PCA using 253,680 CDC BRFSS 2015 observations and on a dense nonlinear benchmark. Over ten seeds, both methods converge in all Sparse PCA runs, while on the dense benchmark the proposed method converges in 10/10 runs versus 9/10 for the exact-Hessian variant. The proposed method performs zero exact constraint-Hessian evaluations and reduces median curvature-construction time on the dense benchmark from 0.1230 s to 0.0111 s. Overall runtime benefits remain problem-dependent.

title: PDFP: GPU-Accelerated Feasibility Pump via PDHG
text:
Title: PDFP: GPU-Accelerated Feasibility Pump via PDHG
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

The feasibility pump (FP) is among the most widely used primal heuristics for mixed-integer linear programming. It alternates between rounding an LP-feasible point and projecting the rounded point back onto the feasible region of the LP relaxation. Recent pump-based heuristics compute the projection with the primal--dual hybrid gradient method (PDHG), which is scalable on modern GPUs. They pose it as a linear program, which needs auxiliary variables and constraints for general integers. Once the projection runs on the GPU, the constraint-propagation rounding (CPR) of FP~2.0 takes a large share of each iteration. For the projection, we propose PDFP, a custom first-order method that solves the pump's projection problem directly, without auxiliary primal variables or constraints. We prove that it keeps the accelerated linear rate of restarted Halpern PDHG. For the rounding, we propose a new procedure that is more efficient than CPR and, under certain assumptions, still returns a CPR rounding. It also chooses rounded values by constraint violation, which can produce feasible roundings where nearest rounding cannot. Finally, our pump runs two independent trajectories concurrently on one GPU through CPU--GPU synchronization. This exploits the variance in trajectory length and lets the pump terminate sooner on average. Computational experiments on MIPLIB~2017 instances show early, promising results: these contributions speed up the discovery of the first incumbent solution. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/MIT-Lu-Lab/PDFP.

title: Large-D approach to nearly critical holographic matter and Yang-Mills deconfinement
text:
Title: Large-D approach to nearly critical holographic matter and Yang-Mills deconfinement
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We study a systematic expansion of dynamical black hole solutions in a class of five-dimensional Einstein-dilaton theories that are holographically dual to nearly critical, strongly coupled four-dimensional field theories. The expansion is motivated, through dimensional reduction, by the large-D limit of pure gravity, where D is the number of spacetime dimensions. At leading nontrivial order, the Einstein equations reduce to a closed set of non-relativistic hydrodynamic equations in four dimensions, as first shown in our previous letter; these equations generalize the large-D effective theory of black branes. We derive the thermodynamics and hydrodynamics of the system from black hole thermodynamics and the holographic dictionary, and show that the energy-momentum tensor extracted from the near-boundary geometry is conserved precisely when the effective equations hold. We analyze planar, cylindrical, and spherical domain walls between coexisting phases, as well as non-equilibrium steady-state walls with nonzero momentum flux. We also show how the near-horizon geometry can be completed by a holographic flow to an asymptotically AdS5 region. Finally, as an application to the confinement-deconfinement transition of Yang-Mills theory, we construct the domain wall between the confined and deconfined phases in improved holographic QCD, compute its surface tension, and compare it with recent lattice results.

title: Spacetime Evolution Induced by a Massive Cosmic String in Numerical Relativity
text:
Title: Spacetime Evolution Induced by a Massive Cosmic String in Numerical Relativity
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Cosmic strings are one-dimensional topological defects formed during phase transitions in the early universe. ''Massive'' cosmic strings possess a sufficiently large tension to close their transverse space, forming a conical singularity outside the string, as a static gravitational effect. In a dynamical context, such strings are expected to drive topological inflation.
