It evaluates ten-million-variable dense binary matrices at approximately 307~Gb/s, consuming a 12.5-TB logical matrix through a 64-MiB packet buffer. Ground-state recovery on planted instances and agreement with reference executions verify the computation. Together, the two modes scale dSB to concurrent requests and dense models beyond GPU memory.

title: Data Center Power Flexibility Characterization: A DeepSets Reinforcement Learning Approach
text:
Title: Data Center Power Flexibility Characterization: A DeepSets Reinforcement Learning Approach
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Data centers can provide power flexibility through the scheduling of computing workloads, cooling systems, and batteries. Characterizing this flexibility online is useful but challenging because of the complex coupling among these resources. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a role-conditioned cross-head DeepSets reinforcement learning approach to characterize the power flexibility interval of a data center at each time step. First, we formulate the flexibility characterization problem as a Markov decision process that jointly models the three resources under a carbon budget, with actions specifying the upper and lower endpoints of the power flexibility interval. We then design DeepSets actor and critic that represent delay-tolerant workloads as an unordered set, enabling the proposed approach to accommodate varying numbers of workloads with a fixed number of trainable parameters. Finally, because maximizing the width of the flexibility interval requires moving its endpoints in opposite directions, we develop a role-conditioned cross-head decoder that distinguishes their respective roles while keeping them coordinated. Case studies on the Google Cluster Data show that the proposed approach provides more than twice the daily flexibility of the standard soft actor-critic method with nearly zero carbon overshoot while using 87.7% fewer trainable parameters.

title: Neural topology optimization of ship structures under propulsion machinery vibrations
text:
Title: Neural topology optimization of ship structures under propulsion machinery vibrations
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Ship structural vibrations contribute to noise, fatigue, and equipment damage, while dynamic-compliance topology optimization can produce pathological designs near resonance. This study extends neural-reparameterized topology optimization using a convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KATO) to forced-vibration design with active input power (AIP) as the objective. Applications include a 100 Hz engine-supporting deck panel and an 18 Hz thruster foundation frame. Helmholtz PDE filtering and Heaviside projection control feature sizes and manufacturing tolerance. Across both deck families, all eight optimized layouts reduce AIP relative to size-optimized references and, after finite-depth extrusion, also achieve lower static compliance. For unrestricted, manufacturing-aware, and stress-aware frame variants, KATO matches GCMMA in AIP within 0.5 dB while yielding 22-36x lower static compliance after matched-volume binary re-analysis. In a near-resonant 300 Hz case, both methods reduce initial AIP by more than 32 dB; KATO maintains a connected design, achieves 59x lower binary static compliance, and reduces maximum AIP over 1-500 Hz by 2.7 dB. KATO runs 6.4-10.4x faster than GCMMA for the implemented stress-aware formulations. The results demonstrate neural AIP-driven topology optimization as an efficient approach for designing connected, feature-size-controlled ship structures with improved forced-vibration performance.

title: The Complexity of KKT Points of Quadratic Programs with Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
text:
Title: The Complexity of KKT Points of Quadratic Programs with Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Computing a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point of a quadratic polynomial over the unit hypercube is known to be $CLS$-complete, when the coefficients of the polynomial are encoded in binary. We prove that the problem remains $CLS$-complete even when the coefficients are encoded in unary. This is the first problem proven to remain $CLS$-hard when the input is given in unary.

title: Motion-Induced Polaron Resonance beyond the Orthogonality Catastrophe
text:
Title: Motion-Induced Polaron Resonance beyond the Orthogonality Catastrophe
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We investigate the spectroscopic response of a repulsively interacting, infinitely heavy impurity moving at constant velocity $v$ through a one-dimensional ideal Fermi gas. Using an exact functional-determinant approach, we calculate the Ramsey response and spectral function, fully accounting for many-body particle-hole excitations. We uncover a strongly nonmonotonic dependence on impurity velocity: decoherence is enhanced around the Fermi velocity, whereas sufficiently rapid motion restores a narrow, long-lived polaron resonance. A long-time wave-packet analysis yields analytical expressions for the polaron energy and decay rate over the full velocity range and quantitatively captures the numerical results. At high velocity, the polaron energy approaches the mean-field value, the decay rate vanishes as $1/v$, and the spectral weight approaches unity. Thus, rapid prescribed motion provides a dynamical route to suppressing the orthogonality catastrophe and restoring polaron coherence even for an infinitely heavy impurity, where recoil is entirely absent.

title: DNA geometry around highly transcribed bacterial genes
text:
Title: DNA geometry around highly transcribed bacterial genes
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Recent high-resolution (500 bp) Hi-C experiments reported contact maps with unusual patterns around highly expressed bacterial DNA loci. These patterns, described as arched stripes and bundled domains, extend over nearly 100 kbp. We performed Brownian Dynamics simulations with a specially designed coarse-grained model to rationalize these findings. The main feature of the model is that it takes explicitly into account the waves of positive (respectively, negative) supercoiling generated by the translocating polymerase downstream (respectively, upstream) of its position. Contact maps computed from the simulations also display the arched stripe and bundled domain patterns for above-threshold values of the rate of twist injection. Computed DNA conformations indicate that these patterns reflect an extraordinarily entangled DNA geometry, which involves both plectonemic and toroidal supercoiling, with some DNA segments experiencing both of them simultaneously. Moreover, DNA segments located on each side of the polymerase systematically wind around tracts located on the other side, which is a purely out-of-equilibrium effect driven by the continuous injection of twist. The present work therefore reveals that repeated transcription of a DNA locus systematically brings into contact DNA segments separated by several tens of kbp, which may eventually contribute to allosteric modulation and long-range communication.

title: Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales
text:
Title: Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

For one-dimensional strict local martingales of the form $\mathrm{d} X_t=σ(X_t) \mathrm{d} W_t$ starting from $X_{0}=x_{0}>0$, we prove the strong rate $\mathbb{E}\left[|X^h_N-X_T|\right] \lesssim h^{\min\{θα,\frac{1}{2}\}}$ for a discrete scheme~$X^h$ truncated at a level $h^{-α}$, with time step~$h$, as $h\downarrow 0$, where~$θ$ depends on the truncation property. For the CEV model $σ(x)\equiv x^{1+γ}$ in particular, the rate is~$\frac{1}{2}$ for any $γ\in (0,1)$ (up to a logarithmic pre-factor at $γ=\frac{1}{2}$).

title: Surrogate Losses for Fairness-Aware Classification: Fisher Consistency and Calibration
text:
Title: Surrogate Losses for Fairness-Aware Classification: Fisher Consistency and Calibration
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Fairness-aware classification seeks to balance predictive accuracy and fairness across demographic groups. Although surrogate losses facilitate the optimization of fairness-aware objectives, it remains unclear when minimizing these losses yields optimal decisions under the original fairness-aware risk. This paper investigates the statistical validity of surrogate-based fairness-aware classification under demographic parity and equal opportunity, considering both attribute-blind and attribute-aware settings. We introduce fairness-aware Fisher consistency and characterize it through conditions on the derivatives of the surrogate losses. The characterization shows that consistency depends not only on the individual loss functions but also on their interaction within the fairness-regularized objective. We further establish a calibration inequality that relates the excess fairness-aware risk to the excess surrogate risk, providing a quantitative connection between surrogate optimization and the original classification objective. Numerical experiments illustrate how deviations from the consistency conditions affect fairness-aware excess risk and how the regularization parameter influences the well-posedness of surrogate optimization. An application to consumer credit default prediction demonstrates that appropriately calibrated fairness regularization can substantially reduce demographic disparities while maintaining predictive performance.

title: Euclid. Predicting scaling relations for emission-line galaxies using simulated data
text:
Title: Euclid. Predicting scaling relations for emission-line galaxies using simulated data
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The Euclid spectroscopic surveys will substantially increase the number of observed emission-line galaxies. We assess the ability of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS) and Euclid Deep Survey (EDS), at the final DR3 depth, to recover the star-forming main sequence (MS), dust-mass relation (DMR), and mass-metallicity relation (MZR) from emission-line measurements. We use MAMBO (mocks with abundance matching in Bologna) spectroscopic simulations processed with the official Euclid pipelines. The MS is traced over $0\leq z\leq 4$ using Pa$β$, H$α$, and [OII] as SFR tracers. The shallow EWS flux limit biases the MS towards higher normalisation and a flatter slope by selecting the brightest, most strongly star-forming galaxies. The deeper EDS enables almost complete sampling with Pa$β$ and H$α$ at log$_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)\geq10.3$ over $0\leq z\leq 1.88$, with mild biases at both redshift limits. The [OII]-based MS is increasingly biased towards higher SFRs at the highest redshifts. The DMR is traced through the Balmer decrement over $1.45\leq z\leq 1.88$ and $0.9\leq z\leq 1.88$ in the EWS and EDS, respectively. The derived colour excess agree well with the input values, although detecting the faint H$β$ line restricts the sample to less obscured galaxies at fixed $M_*$, particularly in the EWS; the DMR is better sampled in the EDS. Finally, a golden sample detected in multiple optical rest-frame emission lines at $1.49\leq z\leq 1.88$ recovers gas-phase metallicities with typical accuracy of 0.1 dex at log$_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)\geq10$, while lower-mass galaxies show biases up to 0.15 dex. Relative to H-band limited sample, this sample preferentially traces the upper MS and lower MZR. Despite the simplified simulations lacking effects such as mutual spectral contamination and detector persistence, these forecasts provide a benchmark for future Euclid spectroscopic analyses.

title: Effect of Correlation on the Pressure-Induced Insulator to Metal Transition in Complex Spin-Orbit Coupled Double Perovskite La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$
text:
Title: Effect of Correlation on the Pressure-Induced Insulator to Metal Transition in Complex Spin-Orbit Coupled Double Perovskite La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We study the effect of electron correlation ($U$) and hydrostatic pressure on the electronic properties of double perovskites La$_2$CoIr$_{1-x}$Ti$_x$O$_6$ for $x$ = 0, 0.5, and 1, using first-principles electronic structure calculations within density functional theory (DFT). At ambient pressure, we systematically vary the electron correlation, i.e., on-site Coulomb interaction to study its effect on band gap and structural parameters. Increasing the value of $U$ enhances the band gap of all three compositions while producing only a slight variation in structural parameters. The effect of hydrostatic pressure is also studied for the same compositions. The estimated band gap values at ambient pressure closes at approximately 39, 42, and 53 GPa for $x$ = 0 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 5 eV and $U_\mathrm{Ir}$ = 2 eV), 0.5 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 5 eV and $U_\mathrm{Ir}$ = 2 eV), and 1 (for $U_\mathrm{Co}$ = 4 eV), respectively, indicating pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transitions. These results show that electron correlation stabilises the insulating state, whereas hydrostatic pressure favours the metallic state by closing the band gap. These findings highlight the tunability of correlated oxides through electron correlations and pressure, offering insights for materials design.

title: Digital nanophotonic biosensing empowered by silicon Mie voids
text:
Title: Digital nanophotonic biosensing empowered by silicon Mie voids
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Optical biosensors are indispensable in medical and environmental diagnostics, yet existing approaches are fundamentally limited in their sensitivity due to ensemble-averaged measurements. Digital biosensing has emerged as a promising solution for resolving individual binding events, thereby providing signals at very low analyte concentrations down to the single-molecule level. Here, we present a novel concept for digital optical biosensing empowered by dielectric Mie voids, combining nanoparticle-based contrast enhancement and deep learning for ultrasensitive biomarker detection. The resonantly trapped light in the air cavities of the periodic Mie void arrays ensures strong overlap between the near-fields and the single gold nanoparticles that are captured on the surface in the presence of the protein biomarker. Remarkably, this strong interaction creates high-contrast digital signals for the precise counting of single nanoparticles located both within and outside the voids, yielding efficient use of the entire sensor area for high sensitivity. We employ deep-ultraviolet (DUV) lithography for the scalable and low-cost production of Mie voids in silicon wafers and automated image analysis with a convolutional neural network for robust nanoparticle counting. As a proof of our concept, we demonstrate the detection of an important disease biomarker, interleukin-6 (IL-6), from small sample volumes at concentrations as low as 1.84 pg/ml, within the physiological range of healthy individuals. Owing to its scalability, precision, and adaptability, our digital nanophotonic biosensing approach based on silicon Mie voids establishes a versatile route for applications ranging from bioanalytics to health and environmental monitoring.

title: Benchmarking Vendor-Guided Optimizations on Edge NPUs: From NPU Only to End-to-End Performance. Extended technical report
text:
Title: Benchmarking Vendor-Guided Optimizations on Edge NPUs: From NPU Only to End-to-End Performance. Extended technical report
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Edge NPU performance depends not only on hardware capabilities, but also on model transformation and the overall deployment pipeline. We propose a benchmarking methodology that separates these effects by comparing three configurations: Baseline, Vendor Guided NPU Only (VG-NPU), and Vendor Guided End-to-End (VG-E2E), where VG-NPU preserves common model I/O and host-side processing while VG-E2E follows the vendor-native deployment pipeline. We apply this methodology to four edge NPUs and three vision workloads. VG-NPU improves both accuracy and Runtime-call latency in 10 of 12 NPU--workload combinations, whereas VG-E2E reduces System-level latency in all combinations but improves accuracy in only four. Moreover, NPU-level performance rankings do not always match End-to-End rankings, and VG-E2E provides an additional 10.4--70.7\% reduction in System-level latency over VG-NPU. These results demonstrate the importance of evaluating vendor-guided optimization separately at the controlled model-transformation and full deployment levels when comparing heterogeneous commercial Edge NPU platforms in practice.

title: Physics-Aligned Electronic Ground-State Learning Improves Generalization
text:
Title: Physics-Aligned Electronic Ground-State Learning Improves Generalization
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) excel at in-distribution tasks, accelerating drug and material development, yet they struggle to generalize out-of-distribution. We propose to push the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier by designing observable-agnostic electronic ground-state descriptor models (GSMs) with computational costs situated between MLIPs and Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT). We align the learning objectives and architectures of GSMs with the governing equations of KS-DFT by enforcing physical constraints and removing optimization pressure on unphysical or irrelevant degrees of freedom. In our size-extrapolation experiments from QM9 to QM40, our combined contributions OrthoNormal-Loss (ON-Loss) and Grassmann Restricted Occupied-Orbital Training (GROOT) reach a 79.1% energy and 83.4% force mean absolute error (MAE) reduction over previous state-of-the-art density GSMs. For Hamiltonian GSMs, ON-Loss and Residual Optimal-gauge Conditioning-aware KS-Eq. Training (ROCKET) together reduce the energy and force MAEs of the strongest baseline by 99.8% and 95.9%, respectively. Using a self-consistency rejection criterion, we filter out extrapolation errors on QMugs, rejecting fewer than 0.4% of predictions while reaching an energy MAE of 0.07 mHa. Finally, we demonstrate the efficiency of label-free self-consistency fine-tuning, and transfer GSMs to reactive chemistry in Transition1x, reaching energy errors below chemical accuracy.

title: Reconstructing Boundary Layer Wind Profiles with Machine Learning: A Comparative Study on IGRA Radiosonde Data
text:
Title: Reconstructing Boundary Layer Wind Profiles with Machine Learning: A Comparative Study on IGRA Radiosonde Data
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Wind profiles in the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) drive short-range forecasting and wind-energy siting, yet sparse radiosonde coverage forces practitioners to interpolate them from a handful of physical predictors. We benchmark modern tabular learners against analytical parameterizations on 158,097 IGRA soundings. CatBoost, TabM, and FT-Transformer reduce RMSE to 1.3-1.6 m/s, against approximately 3 m/s for power-law and Monin-Obukhov fits; once the predictor set is fixed the three architectures differ by less than 0.05 m/s, so accuracy is driven by predictors rather than architecture. A cohort analysis of within-bin profile dispersion places an empirical floor of approximately 1.77 m/s on any point-wise predictor that uses standard radiosonde features, consistent with prior eddy-viscosity inversions. A one-dimensional Fourier Neural Operator applied as a post-hoc corrector to frozen tabular predictions reduces near-surface RMSE on U.S. stations from 1.5 to 1.2 m/s, while leaving upper-layer error unchanged. Further gains should come from new predictors rather than larger models.

title: Cubic Curvature Corrections to Taub-NUT-AdS Black Holes and Their Thermodynamics
text:
Title: Cubic Curvature Corrections to Taub-NUT-AdS Black Holes and Their Thermodynamics
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We investigate cubic curvature corrections to four-dimensional Taub-NUT-AdS black holes and their thermodynamics. We construct the complete analytic solution to the first order in the higher-derivative couplings, and derive the corrected Hawking temperature and Wald entropy. The NUT potential remains unchanged, while reconstructing the NUT charge and Gibbs free energy through the Maxwell relation leaves just one undetermined function of the NUT parameter. We then independently evaluate the Gibbs free energy using two improved Reall-Santos methods, based on either the field redefinition or the background subtraction. After matching the thermodynamic variables, both methods yield identical results and fix the undetermined function, providing a consistent determination of the mass and NUT charge. Our work therefore establishes that the thermodynamics of Taub-NUT-AdS black hole withstands the higher-derivative corrections.

title: Polarization controlled second harmonic generation imaging of stretched collagen fibrils reveals collagen deformation pathway in situ
text:
Title: Polarization controlled second harmonic generation imaging of stretched collagen fibrils reveals collagen deformation pathway in situ
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

The tensile properties of single collagen fibrils, the building block of load-bearing tissues, have been studied extensively by nanomechanical techniques and molecular dynamics simulation. However, the deformation pathway of collagen molecules within fibrils has not yet been observed experimentally. In addition, the role played by divalent and trivalent enzymatic crosslinks in modulating this deformation pathway is poorly understood. Here we used polarization controlled second harmonic generation (SHG) imaging combined with atomic force microscopy (AFM) to characterize the molecular state of collagen triple helices within stretched single collagen fibrils. The fibrils were extracted from a pair of bovine leg tendons from the same animal in order to compare fibrils with a high amount of immature divalent crosslinks to fibrils with a high amount of mature trivalent crosslinks. By selecting fibrils with a large SHG intensity gradient along their length and then imaging the same fibrils by AFM we were able to link the observed intensity gradient with a gradient in D-band strain and a gradient in molecular strain as estimated from the SHG anisotropy parameter rho. In contrast to previous studies at the tendon scale, we observed that the SHG molecular strain is always larger than the D-band strain for all fibrils with this difference being largest for fibrils rich in divalent crosslinks. By analyzing the behavior of the relative density of SHG emitters as a function of molecular strain, we observe a two-state transition from an SHG producing to a non SHG producing state with a free energy barrier between 6 and 10 kBT that we propose corresponds to the local untwisting of the collagen triple helix superhelical twist which likely preceded bond rupture and loss of the SHG signal. We also show that trivalent crosslinks tend to delay the transition onset compared to divalent crosslinks.

title: CPathOGen: Spatially and Morphologically Controlled H&E Counterfactuals for Probing Pathology Models
text:
Title: CPathOGen: Spatially and Morphologically Controlled H&E Counterfactuals for Probing Pathology Models
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Computational pathology models infer biologically and clinically meaningful outcomes from histology, but their predictions are shaped by complex, intertwined tissue signals whose roles are important to understand. Common pixel- and feature-space perturbations can produce implausible tissue, making model responses difficult to interpret. We introduce CPathOGen, a conditional latent-diffusion framework for generating paired H\&E counterfactuals with explicit controls over cellular spatial organization, nuclear morphology, and stain appearance. Cellular maps condition spatial structure through a spatial encoder, while a morphology/appearance vector modulates denoising through blockwise feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM). On held-out H\&E tiles, CPathOGen generates visually plausible tissue with improved distributional agreement after spatially guided selection, as reflected by lower Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Kernel Inception Distance (KID); generated cells track requested abundance and position, and measured morphology and color vary monotonically with their controls. We use these verified interventions to probe pathology encoders with endpoint heads, task-specific classifiers, and survival models. Responses are quantified using total variation distance and prediction-flip rate. We further introduce the Biology-Nuisance Sensitivity Ratio, a metric that contrasts model sensitivity to biologically motivated morphology and spatial factors with sensitivity to non-biological, stain-related nuisance variation. CPathOGen provides a practical, fidelity-audited framework for evaluating robustness and controlled feature sensitivity in computational pathology model. \href{https://github.com/a12dongithub/PathOGen}{GitHub} and \href{https://huggingface.co/a12donhf/CPathOGen}{Hugging~Face}.

title: GEAR: A GPU-Accelerated Global Solver for Bounded Continuous Nonlinear Programs via Linear Bound Propagation
text:
Title: GEAR: A GPU-Accelerated Global Solver for Bounded Continuous Nonlinear Programs via Linear Bound Propagation
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We present a novel GPU-accelerated global solver for constrained nonlinear programming (NLP) inspired by the efficient linear bound propagation framework in neural network (NN) verification. Existing work on NN verification, a problem that can be cast as feasibility detection for a nonlinear objective, demonstrated orders-of-magnitude speedups with the linear bound propagation-based framework when compared to traditional solvers. Extending this paradigm to global nonlinear programming requires addressing many challenges: a global constrained NLP solver must effectively exploit all, possibly unstructured, nonlinear constraints to improve the objective, whereas NN verification typically handles simple input box constraints over a well-structured NN and does not directly optimize an objective function. We address these challenges by fully exploiting the linear bounds produced by bound propagation: these linear bounds can be viewed as relaxations of nonlinear constraints and used to provide lower bounds, check infeasibility, and guide the search for a primal solution. In addition, we propose tighter linear relaxations for bilinear, quotient, and other commonly used nonlinear functions in NLP problems, and a projected augmented Lagrangian method tightly coupled to our dual solving procedure to produce primal solutions. Our method solves 421 of 505 bounded and continuous NLP problems in the GAMS and MINLPLib benchmarks under a 180-second limit, more than each of the six global solvers we compare with, including Gurobi and BARON (commercial), and SCIP (open-source). Sixteen of these problems are certified by none of the six global solvers; all of them contain exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric terms, which are often challenging for traditional approaches. Project webpage is at https://verified-intelligence.github.io/GEAR.

title: Generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics from gravitational perturbations of near-extremal Kerr
text:
Title: Generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics from gravitational perturbations of near-extremal Kerr
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We derive the generalized Schwarzian thermodynamics of near-extremal Kerr directly from four-dimensional gravitational perturbations of the near-horizon geometry. We construct two families of exact linear perturbations of the near-NHEK background: a non-normalizable mode that deforms the asymptotic boundary, and a normalizable mode supported near the horizon. Both perturbations are smooth solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations reduced to the Jackiw--Teitelboim equation for the dual scalar, without conical singularities. We study their asymptotic symmetries and show that they generate an algebra of time reparametrizations; requiring the gauge parameters to depend on the Schwarzian mode, the isometry condition selects the stationary KdV hierarchy. The same hierarchy is independently enforced by the vacuum Einstein equations on the perturbation coefficient. In the Euclidean regime, we evaluate the Hamiltonian action and show that each mode independently generates a tower of odd-power corrections to the near-extremal entropy.

title: Semi-Analytic Predictions for Strong-Lensing Perturbers in Cold and Self-Interacting Dark Matter
text:
Title: Semi-Analytic Predictions for Strong-Lensing Perturbers in Cold and Self-Interacting Dark Matter
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Strong gravitational lensing is sensitive to the abundance and internal structure of dark matter halos, providing a probe of gravothermal evolution in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM). We combine semi-analytic cold dark matter (CDM) subhalo histories with a model for gravothermal evolution in SIDM to generate CDM and SIDM subhalo populations across SIDM parameter space. We predict their projected enclosed masses and deflection-based projected density slopes and compare them with three perturbers inferred through gravitational imaging in PJ011646, SDSS J0946+1006, and JVAS B1938+666. For SIDM model parameters $σ_0/m_χ=147.1$ cm$^2$/g and $w=120$ km/s, SIDM subhalos reproduce all three perturbers more often than CDM subhalos. For PJ011646, we find ~0.6 cored SIDM subhalos per host matching the perturber, compared with ~0.002 in CDM, while core-collapsed subhalos are too steep. For SDSS J0946+1006, we find ~3 core-collapsed and ~0.004 cored SIDM subhalos per host, compared with none in 900 CDM realizations, although baryons, neglected here, may matter for such massive subhalos. For "detection V" in JVAS B1938+666, we find ~220 core-collapsed and ~20 cored SIDM subhalos per host within the $2σ$ posterior region, compared with ~0.2 in CDM; the CDM candidates require exceptionally early accretion, at median redshift $z\sim13$. Simultaneously reproducing all three perturbers requires $w\gtrsim10^2$ km/s, so that the massive (~$5.6\times10^{10}M_\odot$) progenitors of SDSS J0946+1006 candidates can collapse, and is achieved for $σ_0/m_χ\gtrsim10^2$ cm$^2$/g in the parameter sets studied. Our results show how semi-analytic models can quantify how often subhalos reproduce individual perturbers in different dark matter models, and our modular framework can be readily updated as models of tidal stripping and late-stage gravothermal evolution in SIDM improve. (abridged)

title: An internal mode shifts the depinning threshold of dissociated dislocations without changing universality
text:
Title: An internal mode shifts the depinning threshold of dissociated dislocations without changing universality
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Driven elastic manifolds exhibit a depinning transition whose large-scale behavior is governed by a nonequilibrium critical fixed point. Real interfaces, however, often possess internal degrees of freedom, raising the question of whether such modes alter depinning universality or only nonuniversal properties of the transition. We address this question for a dissociated dislocation, whose two Shockley partials define a fluctuating stacking-fault width driven by correlated random-alloy stresses. Comparing exact thresholds on identical disorder realizations with the width either free or frozen, we find that width fluctuations leave the depinning universality class unchanged: the roughness exponent $ζ$ and correlation-length exponent $ν$ remain the same even when the width becomes strongly fluctuating and locally multistable. The threshold, however, shifts. The shift is governed by the elastic crossover length of the internal mode rather than by multistability, and can have either sign. An infinite-range mean-field treatment misses this mechanism. With the physical two-partial elastic kernel and disorder calibrated against measured strengths, width fluctuations raise the athermal critical resolved shear stress by 10-35% over that of a rigid dissociated dislocation. An internal mode can thus be irrelevant at the depinning fixed point while remaining quantitatively important for where the transition occurs.

title: Thermal Stability and Structural Relaxation Kinetics of Commercially Pure Titanium
text:
Title: Thermal Stability and Structural Relaxation Kinetics of Commercially Pure Titanium
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

This work explores the structural relaxation of cryorolled commercially pure titanium subjected to subsequent annealing.Nanostructured specimens with an average grain size of ~50 nm were produced by plastic deformation via cryogenic rolling at 100 K to a true strain of 1.20, followed by annealing at 425 K, 525 K, 725 K, and 945 K. Microstructural evolution was examined using electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction. Cryogenic rolling was found to induce pronounced grain fragmentation, with coherent scattering regions (CSRs) of 30-50 nm dominating the substructure. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that annealing drives crystallite growth: a slight increase at 525 K, accelerated coarsening at 725 K, and complete recrystallization at 945 K. The kinetics of grain growth follow the classical Lifshitz-Slyozov-Wagner model, with a growth exponent of ~4, reflecting the role of triple junctions and defect-controlled boundary diffusion. The activation energy, estimated at ~97 kJ/mol, corresponds to typical values for grain boundary diffusion in α-Ti, confirming that cryogenic deformation produces a highly non-equilibrium microstructure whose relaxation is strongly temperature dependent.

title: CliffRank: A Dual-Branch Framework for Activity-Cliff Ranking Prediction
text:
Title: CliffRank: A Dual-Branch Framework for Activity-Cliff Ranking Prediction
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Activity-cliff ranking remains difficult because local structural changes can cause large activity differences, while high-quality data that resolve the underlying mechanisms remain limited. To use available activity labels more effectively, we combine absolute-activity regression with ranking-consistency learning. CliffRank trains two parallel predictors with mean squared error, a thresholded listwise loss, and Pairwise Preference Consistency (PPC), which aligns relative ordering in the preference-probability space. On three antimicrobial peptide datasets, CliffRank with ESM2-t12 achieved the highest mean Spearman correlation of 0.5393 and mean Recall@50 of 21.4, although the leading method varied across individual datasets. On three small-molecule datasets, CliffRank with PNA, where PPC was activated after 120 epochs, achieved the highest mean Spearman correlation of 0.6890, while its mean Recall@50 of 30.4 matched that of ACANet-PNA. The PPC results also define its practical limits. Asymmetric initialization improved the MolCLR-GIN averages but did not improve every target. For PNA without pretrained weights, delayed PPC improved selected metrics, but no schedule was best for both mean Spearman correlation and mean Recall@50. Future work should evaluate more targets and antimicrobial peptide systems, develop adaptive PPC schedules, and incorporate protein or membrane context when available.

title: Enhancing Gravitational Waves from Global Strings via a First-Order Phase Transition
text:
Title: Enhancing Gravitational Waves from Global Strings via a First-Order Phase Transition
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We perform the first (3+1)-dimensional lattice simulations of a cosmological first-order phase transition (PT) in which true-vacuum bubbles with random phases nucleate, expand, and collide, producing a network of global strings. We find that the string network enters the scaling regime, and the coefficient of the logarithmic growth is smaller than the value obtained for a second-order PT. From the axion spectrum, we derive the dark-matter relic abundance and the dark-radiation bound from big bang nucleosynthesis on the axion decay constant $f_a$ and mass $m_a$. The ratio of the gravitational wave emission rate to the axion emission rate is found to be about two orders of magnitude larger than in the second-order case, and the resulting gravitational wave spectrum can be probed by pulsar timing arrays as well as by space- and ground-based interferometers.

title: Two-Loop $n$-Point Identical Helicity Amplitude for Gravity Minimally Coupled to a Chiral Fermion
text:
Title: Two-Loop $n$-Point Identical Helicity Amplitude for Gravity Minimally Coupled to a Chiral Fermion
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Motivated by recent developments in the two-loop identical-helicity sector of gauge theory when the one-loop self-dual integrability anomaly of Bardeen and Cangemi, or the equivalent twistor-space version of Costello and Paquette, vanishes, we compute the two-loop four-point identical-helicity amplitude in gravity coupled to a single chiral fermion, for which the corresponding self-dual anomaly also vanishes. We show that the infrared-subtracted amplitude is purely rational and proportional to the identical-helicity tree amplitude of pure gravity with a single insertion of the operator $R^3$. Using this connection, we obtain a closed-form expression for the two-loop $n$-point identical-helicity amplitude in gravity minimally coupled to a fermion. We do so by first obtaining the corresponding identical-helicity gauge-theory tree amplitude with a single $F^3$ insertion using a chiral bootstrap. We then convert these $n$-point gauge theory amplitudes using Kawai-Lewellen-Tye to obtain gravity amplitudes with an $R^3$ insertion, which are necessarily equal to the desired two-loop identical helicity amplitudes of gravity coupled to a chiral fermion. As a nontrivial check, we explicitly verify crossing symmetry and the expected soft limits of our expressions through 13 points.

title: Predicted state-to-state collisional rate coefficients from neural networks
text:
Title: Predicted state-to-state collisional rate coefficients from neural networks
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Molecular spectra observed in the interstellar medium are commonly analyzed using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium models, which requires accurate state-to-state collisional rate coefficients. Close-coupling calculations become prohibitively expensive for transitions from highly excited rotational states, therefore available datasets are often truncated at low initial states and temperatures; and since each new system also requires an accurate ab initio potential energy surface, many detected molecules have no collisional data. We employ two machine learning strategies to predict rotational state-to-state rate coefficients of molecules included in the train set beyond the range of initial states and temperatures computed so far, and predicting those of a molecule absent from training and validation sets. Feed-forward neural networks are trained on state-to-state de-excitation rate coefficients of 24 linear molecules colliding with para-H2. Scheme 1 includes all systems in the train+validation set, with 70%, 80%, and 90% initial-state boundaries and a 90% temperature boundary. Scheme 2 is trained on 22 systems described only by transition and molecular properties, and predicts two excluded systems, CS and CF+, whose astrophysical impact is explored with non-LTE calculations. For the 90% boundary, Scheme 1 predicts 99.4% of the test transitions within a factor of 2, and no prediction deviates from the reference value by more than a factor of 4.7. This model was used to complete 18 datasets. Scheme 2 reproduces the rate coefficients of two excluded systems within a factor of 3 for more than 92% of their transitions. Both schemes provide near-instantaneous complements to close-coupling calculations: Scheme 1 extends the range of a molecule already included in the training set with high accuracy, while Scheme 2 gives a reasonable first estimate for a molecule that has not been studied.

title: Shotgun Assembly of the Non-Uniform Labeled Lattice Model
text:
Title: Shotgun Assembly of the Non-Uniform Labeled Lattice Model
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

In this paper, we study the graph shotgun assembly problem in the labeled lattice model, as introduced by Mossel and Ross (2019). We start with a $d$-dimensional lattice of length $n$, where the color of each vertex is sampled i.i.d. from a distribution $π$. Then, we ask whether it is possible to reconstruct the coloring of the lattice given the coloring of each subgrid of length $k$. While previous work by Ding and Liu (2023) and Demidovich, Panichkin, and Zhukovskii (2023) identified the reconstruction threshold when $π$ is uniform, we examine the non-uniform case. This paper establishes a sufficient condition for the impossibility of reconstruction for $d \geq 2$ using information-theoretic arguments. Our negative result matches the known threshold in the uniform case.

title: Thermal damping of spectator scalar dark matter: Relaxing the overclosure and isocurvature bounds
text:
Title: Thermal damping of spectator scalar dark matter: Relaxing the overclosure and isocurvature bounds
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

A light scalar present during inflation generically acquires a misalignment and can later constitute the dark matter. Since it fluctuates independently of the inflaton, however, it carries isocurvature perturbations. Isocurvature and overclosure bounds together rule out the simplest version of this scenario at high inflationary scales. We show that a weak coupling to the primordial plasma can relax both bounds simultaneously. The plasma depletes the scalar abundance through thermal damping, a dissipative effect arising from the plasma's finite equilibration time, thereby relaxing the overclosure bound. If the damping grows with the oscillation amplitude, it can also drive different initial amplitudes onto a common attractor that depends only on the local radiation temperature. This synchronizes the scalar with the adiabatic clock, thus suppressing its isocurvature. The resulting isocurvature bound on the inflationary scale relaxes by exactly the factor by which damping reduces the abundance, in addition to the relaxation from the larger initial misalignment now allowed. This result holds for any damping rate quadratic in the amplitude, regardless of its temperature dependence.

title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
text:
Title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients. Given an initial time and state of a process, KC-Maps models its distribution integrated to any given time, corresponding to the weak solution of the SDE. To recover the correct dynamics, KC-Maps satisfies two key properties: (i) it satisfies the boundary conditions, which we incorporate directly into the neural network architecture, and (ii) it respects the Kolmogorov--Chapman equation, which provides an efficient training objective. We empirically demonstrate that KC-Maps learns to integrate the dynamics of peptide molecular systems and outperforms classical molecular dynamics in terms of GPU-hours.

title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
text:
Title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We introduce NEOPIC, a framework for learning the field operator in particle-based methods applied to kinetic plasma simulations. Its key novelty is a neural operator that acts directly on the empirical measure of the particles, rather than on a grid, and is evaluated at the particle positions. No mesh or tree is needed and, unlike grid-based neural operators, no deposition onto a mesh takes place, so the particle noise that dominates the inputs of particle simulations is not aliased. Since it replaces only the field solve, it serves as a plug-and-play field solver for particle-based methods: it can be trained on data from particle-in-cell, particle-in-Fourier or tree codes, and combined with any time integrator, including implicit schemes. We prove that the discrete evaluation coincides with the continuous operator at any number of particles (representation equivalence) and derive an error analysis that separates sampling, learning and time-stepping errors: up to the learning error, NEOPIC has the error structure of standard Monte Carlo particle methods. We show that the particle noise in the training data acts as an implicit regularizer, which gives guidance on the number of training particles in relation to the particle numbers used at inference. A complexity analysis shows that NEOPIC is an $O(N_p)$ method whose constants are set by the architecture alone, independently of any mesh or tree. Numerical experiments on electrostatic benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including Landau damping, two-stream and bump-on-tail instabilities, a cyclotron mini-app and a Penning trap, confirm the theoretical findings. A single model trained on several mini-apps generated by different reference methods captures all of them and remains stable up to twice the training time window, which points towards foundation models for fields in particle-based methods.

title: The 2d Ising Model on Hyperbolic Lattices and the Role of Boundary Conditions
text:
Title: The 2d Ising Model on Hyperbolic Lattices and the Role of Boundary Conditions
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We investigate the role of boundary conditions in the critical behaviour of the ferromagnetic Ising model on regular hyperbolic tessellations. Using worm and Metropolis simulations, we compare open boundaries with wired boundaries implemented through a common auxiliary spin. For open boundaries, the susceptibility exhibits volume-based finite-size scaling with non-mean-field scaling exponents that are approximately stable across four tessellations, supporting the possibility of a common universality class. Comparisons with Binder crossings and susceptibility peaks reveal substantial finite-size effects. For wired boundaries, the central-to-auxiliary spin correlator exhibits radial scaling consistent with a mean-field magnetization exponent. The central-spin response to a uniform magnetic field provides a further consistency test of $δ=3$. Layer-resolved responses to a weak boundary field also reveal an enhancement of the induced magnetization towards the interior. Our results highlight the importance of boundary conditions and the distinction between interior and whole-system observables in characterizing critical phenomena on non-amenable lattices.

title: Reduced magnetohydrodynamics with electron inertia in pseudodipole coordinates
text:
Title: Reduced magnetohydrodynamics with electron inertia in pseudodipole coordinates
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We study the altitude-dependent structuring of field-aligned currents by driven Alfvén waves in an expanding auroral flux tube. The model uses the reduced magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) long-thin ordering assumptions along with electron inertia. We derive a magnetic tension operator consistent with energy conservation in the expanding geometry. We compare uniform density with a prescribed profile containing a dense ionospheric end and a low-density upper region. The simulations produce localized current concentrations near the lower boundary and filamentary structures at greater heights. Broad structures remain visible in the magnetic and velocity stream functions while their perpendicular derivatives reveal finer magnetic field, velocity, and current structure. With the nonuniform density profile, the run with additional upper boundary reflection shows finer current structure and greater numerical dissipation. Spectral diagnostics show forward nonlinear energy transfer and altitude-dependent power-law-like intervals without a broad constant-flux range. The narrowest current concentrations span only a few grid cells, so their physical widths remain unresolved.

title: Pathway-resolved analysis of internal conversion enabled by Gaussian boson sampling
text:
Title: Pathway-resolved analysis of internal conversion enabled by Gaussian boson sampling
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) has provided strong evidence of quantum advantage, motivating the search for real-world applications. Such applications rely on mapping physical problems to the native GBS output: photon-number patterns sampled from a highly non-trivial probability distribution. Here we derive a GBS-compatible mapping for the rate constant $k_\mathrm{IC}$ of internal conversion (IC), incorporating two important physical effects -- Duschinsky rotations and Herzberg--Teller contribution. We validate this framework using sampling \textit{simulations} of dibenzoterrylene, reproducing reported values of $k_\mathrm{IC}$. Beyond $k_\mathrm{IC}$ reconstruction, we show that the photon-number patterns of GBS encode the vibrational mode combinations responsible for the IC process, which we refer to as non-radiative pathways. This pathway-resolved data can then be grouped in different ways to extract multiple physically motivated observables. In particular, it enables $k_\mathrm{IC}$ analysis at several levels, from individual modes and mode family contributions to recurring vibrational configurations shared by multiple pathways. We find that Duschinsky rotations increase the fraction of $k_\mathrm{IC}$ associated with correlated vibrational pathways from 46% to 86%, and identify the mode combinations with the largest rate contributions. These pathway-resolved insights can guide targeted molecular modifications, including selective deuteration and bond substitution, to control non-radiative decay.

title: LongTails: Automated Research in Optimization
text:
Title: LongTails: Automated Research in Optimization
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We introduce LongTails, a framework for discovering and improving oracle-complexity bounds with formal verification in Lean 4. Using LongTails, we have already obtained more than 100 new results across a broad range of optimization problems, including generalized smoothness, heavy-tailed noise, finite-sum and composite optimization, and higher-order and zeroth-order methods. Our goal is to scale discovery and continually develop new methods with non-trivial and valuable theoretical guarantees using modern agentic systems. The framework is specialized for optimization, where we separate a Setup, specifying the problem class, assumptions, available information, and success criterion, from a Complexity, specifying a sufficient oracle-call budget. Once a Setup is fixed (e.g., $L$-smooth convex optimization with the goal of finding $x_{\mathrm{out}}$ such that $f(x_{\mathrm{out}}) - f(x^\star) \leq \varepsilon$), agents search for better Complexities (e.g., $O(\sqrt{L R^2 / \varepsilon})$, where $R \geq \|x_0 - x^\star\|$) by designing algorithms and proving their convergence. The framework then checks the proofs and guarantees that every accepted Complexity can indeed be attained under the given Setup. This turns the search for new methods into an ongoing effort to improve their theoretical guarantees. To the best of our knowledge, LongTails is the first framework to scale automated research in optimization across such a broad range of problems with formally verified theoretical guarantees.

title: Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution
text:
Title: Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Parton multiplicity entropy, proposed by Kharzeev and Levin as entanglement between the region probed in deep inelastic scattering and the proton's remainder, was compared with hadron multiplicity data. It is computed from parton densities, which do not fix the partons' quantum state. We show that a one-parton density matrix from Lipatov's wave functions determines two entropies for resolved modes with finite mean number and entropy. Its trace is the mean parton number, and normalization gives a sampled parton's entropy. A compatible thermal state, if it exists, maximizes entropy at fixed one-parton matrix. This maximum equals the actual entropy only for that thermal state and measures entanglement only for a specified subsystem of a pure state. The geometric multiplicity entropy follows if all emitted partons share one mode. An entropy computed from densities becomes such a maximum, an upper bound on the actual entropy, only for specified resolved modes. We also show that the state averaged over unrecorded emissions, assumed incoherent across scales, obeys probability-preserving Lindblad evolution on finitely many regulated modes with the resolution scale if emission and no-emission terms match. The occupations reproduce leading-order DGLAP, with virtual terms, at leading logarithmic accuracy as the cutoffs on momentum fractions are removed. The reduction holds for strongly ordered transverse momenta in light-cone gauge and dilute occupations, including those of newly resolved modes. Approximating momentum and helicity modes by independent thermal populations closes the occupation equation and gives this bound's evolution, with Bose and Pauli factors from the operator algebra. We propose testing this approximation at HERA or the LHC. The test compares the mode number inferred from normalized hadron factorial moments in a rapidity window with the window's transverse mode count.

title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
text:
Title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We study the global $V$-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential $u$ (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time $V$-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.

title: On the Generalization Gap of Streaming Federated Learning with Markovian Data
text:
Title: On the Generalization Gap of Streaming Federated Learning with Markovian Data
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Streaming federated learning (SFL) allows clients to train a shared model from continuously arriving data without retaining large local datasets. Such streams often exhibit temporal dependence, yet its effect on generalization remains poorly understood. In this paper we study the expected generalization gap of the aggregated model when client data follow Markov processes, using information-theoretic and rate-distortion techniques. Our framework accommodates heterogeneous Markovian dynamics across clients and distinguishes temporal dependence from information acquired during local learning. We establish bounds under cross-entropy loss, specializing them to Linear Next-Token Prediction (LNTP) and Self-Attention Next-Token Prediction (SANTP). These results quantify the effects of client count, communication rounds, sample size, data dimension, mixing time, and context length. In particular, they reveal a communication--generalization tradeoff: although frequent aggregation may help optimization, it can weaken generalization guarantees. They also suggest a potential advantage of distributed over centralized streaming learning under a fixed total data budget. Temporal dependence enters through the square root of the mixing time. By analyzing the history-state process, we obtain refined bounds with improved context-length dependence under suitable mixing conditions. Experiments on GPT-style language-model pretraining with TinyStories and real-world time-series forecasting illustrate how collaboration and communication frequency influence generalization under temporal dependence

title: PHL: Persistent Hyperdigraph Learning for Protein-Protein Binding Affinity Prediction
text:
Title: PHL: Persistent Hyperdigraph Learning for Protein-Protein Binding Affinity Prediction
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Persistent homology and persistent Laplacians have become effective descriptors of large molecular binding interactions, the latter encoding multiscale geometry and spectral information beyond the harmonic subspace. Both, however, are built on undirected graphs and pairwise contracts, while the interactions that determine binding are often directional and involve more than two atoms at once. We introduce persistent hyperdigraph learning (PHL), which represents these directed, many-body interactions directly. Because hyperdigraph Laplacian spectra become costly to compute at higher topological orders, we further use stochastic trace estimation to develop a matrix-free formulation(MFPHL) that estimates Laplacian trace statistics from probe-based quadratic forms evaluated through sparse boundary operators, without assembling or diagonalizing. The number of probes required for a target relative accuracy of the trace estimate is independent of matrix dimension, and per-probe cost scales with operator sparsity. On protein-protein binding affinity benchmarks, MFPHL reduces feature-generation time by roughly two orders of magnitude relative to the eigenvalue-based pipeline. Its predictive accuracy matches that of spectral PHL on the P2P wild-type set within training-seed variability but is lower on the two larger datasets. This dataset-dependent trade-off brings higher-order hyperdigraph features within practical reach.

title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films
text:
Title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

The thermal conductivities of (001) $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films deposited on $c$-plane sapphire substrates were measured with frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). The thermal conductivity increases from 1.83 $^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$ W/m$\cdot$K to 2.26 $^{+0.35}_{-0.40}$ W/m$\cdot$K as the thicknesses increase from 159 nm to 689 nm. This weak thickness dependence indicates that the majority of the intrinsic phonon mean free paths are smaller than the range of investigated film thicknesses. First-principles-based calculations that include phonon-phonon and phonon-boundary scattering capture this size-dependent behavior and support our experimental observation. Temperature-dependent measurements of a 689 nm film from 293 to 400 K show a decrease in thermal conductivity with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon-phonon scattering. A weaker temperature dependence is observed in a 159 nm film where phonon-boundary scattering becomes more prominent. At comparable film thicknesses, our measured $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ films exhibit lower values of cross-plane thermal conductivity than the other experimentally measured Ga$_2$O$_3$ polymorphs. Our experimental observations are supported by prior predictions, which suggest that the low thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ results from its complex crystal structure, which leads to increased anharmonicity and lower phonon group velocities relative to other polymorphs. Thermal management strategies, such as integration with high-thermal-conductivity substrates, may thus be required to mitigate self-heating for $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$-based electronic devices.

title: Second-Order Homogenization of Particulate Elastomeric Composites for Structural-Scale Damage Analysis
text:
Title: Second-Order Homogenization of Particulate Elastomeric Composites for Structural-Scale Damage Analysis
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Damage prediction in particulate elastomeric composites is challenging due to the strong material heterogeneity, nearly incompressible behavior of the matrix, and the presence of localized stress concentrations arising from matrix-inclusion interactions. In the present work, a computational framework is developed for damage propagation analysis of particulate elastomeric composite structures. The effective constitutive response of the heterogeneous material is first determined using the second-order homogenization method. The resulting homogenized response is subsequently used to identify equivalent hyperelastic material parameters for structural simulations. A three-parameter isotropic damage model is incorporated to capture damage-induced softening. A mixed displacement-pressure finite element formulation, is used to alleviate volumetric locking associated with nearly incompressible property of elastomers. The proposed framework is validated through full-scale simulations and homogenized response involving composites with varying inclusion volume fractions. Numerical investigations demonstrate that the homogenized models is able to reproduce the global force-displacement response within 2% error and damage evolution characteristics of the heterogeneous composites while significantly reducing the computational cost.

title: Bolek: A Multimodal Language Model for Molecular Reasoning
text:
Title: Bolek: A Multimodal Language Model for Molecular Reasoning
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Molecular property models increasingly support high-stakes drug-discovery decisions, but their outputs are often difficult to audit: classical predictors return scores without rationale, while language models can produce fluent explanations weakly grounded in the input molecule. We introduce Bolek, a compact multimodal language model that grounds natural-language reasoning in molecular structure by injecting a Morgan fingerprint embedding into an instruction-tuned text decoder. Bolek is fine-tuned on molecular alignment tasks, including molecule description, RDKit descriptor prediction, and substructure detection, and on downstream reasoning over 15 TDC binary classification tasks using synthetic chains-of-thought anchored in concrete molecular features. Across these tasks, Bolek outperforms its Qwen3-4B-Instruct base on all endpoints in yes/no mode and on 13 of 15 in chain-of-thought mode, raising mean ROC/PR AUC from 0.55 to 0.76. It also outperforms TxGemma-9B-Chat on 13 of 15 binary classification tasks despite being less than half its size. Bolek's explanations are more grounded than those of the baseline LLMs: it cites numerical descriptors 10-100x more often per chain-of-thought, and the cited values agree strongly with RDKit for key descriptors such as TPSA, MolLogP, and MolWt (Spearman rho = 0.87-0.91). Generalisation extends beyond the training panel: on 15 unseen TDC classification endpoints, Bolek matches TxGemma on five, and it produces non-trivial rank correlations on three held-out regression endpoints despite never seeing downstream regression during training. These results suggest that targeted modality injection and reasoning supervision tied to verifiable molecular features can yield compact, auditable molecular reasoning models.

title: Joint Quantization and Dynamic Partitioning for Context-Aware Edge Vision Transformers
text:
Title: Joint Quantization and Dynamic Partitioning for Context-Aware Edge Vision Transformers
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Deploying vision transformer models across connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) requires joint management of computation and Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication. Static split-inference methods use fixed partition points and cannot adapt to time-varying link bandwidth, processing load, and concurrent multi-stream traffic. This paper proposes an edge orchestration framework that jointly selects model partition points, per-layer quantization bitwidths, and execution placement across heterogeneous vehicular compute nodes. The joint partitioning and mixed-precision allocation problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) that minimizes compute and communication energy subject to end-to-end latency and task-quality constraints. The framework is evaluated on Jetson Orin Nano (8~GB), Jetson Orin NX (16~GB), and Jetson AGX Orin (32~GB) nodes using OPV2V-driven multi-stream workloads with $K \in \{2,4,6,8\}$. Across the evaluated configurations, the proposed formulation reduces V2V communication energy by $33.3$--$36.0\%$ relative to a Uniform INT8 split. At $K=8$, end-to-end task completion latency is reduced by $34.0\%$ on the Orin Nano and $33.1\%$ on the Orin NX relative to the same baseline, while limiting the reduction in 3D detection accuracy to $3.1$--$4.1$ percentage points in $\mathrm{mAP}_{50}$ relative to FP16 execution.

title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
text:
Title: Davenport Constants of High-Dimensional Integer Sets
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.

title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle
text:
Title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Matrix factorization provides a simple model for studying the training dynamics of neural networks. Recent studies of gradient flow under small initialization have analyzed how trajectories escape from a neighborhood of the origin and approach their first nonzero stationary point. In this paper, we study continuous-time dynamics that applies a finite number of Newton-Schulz iterations to the normalized matrix gradient (Muon). We show that the number of Newton-Schulz steps can change the rank selected during the early stages of training and allow the resulting trajectory to bypass the first nonzero stationary point approached by gradient flow. Under an additional residual-inertia condition, we prove that bypass occurs for all sufficiently large finite Newton-Schulz depths and provide an explicit sufficient threshold. We also construct an example in which the bypass threshold is four.

title: Consistent Mapping for Fluid Structure Interaction with Geometrically Nonlinear Isogeometric Beams
text:
Title: Consistent Mapping for Fluid Structure Interaction with Geometrically Nonlinear Isogeometric Beams
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Isogeometric beam formulations provide an efficient reduced-dimensional representation of slender structures, combining accurate geometry and high-order continuity with few structural degrees of freedom. Their application to fluid--structure interaction (FSI) requires transferring motion and loads between the one-dimensional beam centerline and the surrounding fluid interface. While mapping strategies exist for conventional finite element beams, geometrically nonlinear isogeometric formulations require operators consistent with their spline-based kinematics and distinct descriptions of cross-sectional rotation. This work develops consistent beam-to-surface mappings for geometrically nonlinear isogeometric Bernoulli and Timoshenko beams in partitioned FSI. Fluid-interface points are attached to the beam in the reference configuration and reconstructed using the nonlinear kinematics of each formulation. Consistent linearization yields a configuration-dependent mapping operator whose transpose ensures work-conjugate load transfer. The formulations are verified through analytical deformation tests, convergence studies, and virtual-work checks, and evaluated in beam-based adaptations of the Mok and Turek--Hron benchmarks and the Goland wing flutter benchmark. The results confirm accurate interface reconstruction and work-conjugate load transfer under large deformations, while demonstrating the applicability of both beam formulations to coupled FSI problems.

title: Preference-Based Constraint Handling for Multi-Objective Design-Decision Optimisation: Acceptability Relaxation and Feasibility Guidance
text:
Title: Preference-Based Constraint Handling for Multi-Objective Design-Decision Optimisation: Acceptability Relaxation and Feasibility Guidance
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Multi-objective design-decision optimisation (MODO) problems contain negotiable acceptability limits and non-negotiable feasibility constraints. Hard constraints define the feasible design space, whereas actors may reconsider acceptability limits through deliberation and compromise. Relaxing such limits is a preference judgement: penalties or violation measures do not necessarily represent how actors value departures from initial requirements. This paper introduces a preference-based constraint-handling framework. For negotiable limits, preference functions model how actor preference changes with relaxation, allowing the preferred design and acceptable degree of relaxation to be determined through the same aggregation process. Approach 1 represents relaxation as an additional objective and search variable; Approach 2 incorporates it into the preference function of the affected criterion. When constructed consistently, both yield the same best-fit-for-common-purpose solution but differ in complexity and computational effort. The framework addresses stalemate problems, where relaxation is required to recover an acceptable solution, and non-stalemate problems, where modest relaxation may reveal a better design. Hard feasibility constraints remain fixed, and infeasible designs remain inadmissible. A feasibility-guidance function supplies IMAP-IGS with graded information on scaled violations, guiding the search towards difficult-to-reach feasible regions. Every feasible design takes precedence over every infeasible design, and the final recommendation is selected exclusively from the feasible set through A-FINE preference aggregation. The framework integrates acceptability negotiation, feasibility guidance, and design optimisation without conflating their meanings, while preserving preference consistency and decision validity.

title: pbhalo: computing primordial black hole and minihalo populations from a single primordial perturbation spectrum
text:
Title: pbhalo: computing primordial black hole and minihalo populations from a single primordial perturbation spectrum
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

An enhancement of the primordial curvature power spectrum on small scales can give rise to two populations of compact objects: primordial black holes (PBHs), which form during radiation domination, and dark matter minihalos, including ultracompact minihalos (UCMHs), which form from the same modes during matter domination. We present pbhalo, an open-source Python package that computes the PBH mass function, the halo mass function and the UCMH abundance from a single spectrum in a given cosmology and applies observational constraints on the PBH abundance and on the spectrum jointly. The package components are validated against colossus (a code for halo mass functions and cosmological quantities), pbhstat (a code for the PBH mass function from a given spectrum) and published results; joint constraints are illustrated for lognormal peaks. The code is distributed under the MIT license.

title: On the Relative Security of Prompt Injection: Mechanised Definitions, Defences and Verdicts for LLM Agents
text:
Title: On the Relative Security of Prompt Injection: Mechanised Definitions, Defences and Verdicts for LLM Agents
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

An LLM agent that reads untrusted content, such as an email or a web page, may follow instructions hidden in it. Noninterference is too strong for such agents, since a useful agent lets untrusted content influence what it does and may disclose the user's data by design, and declassification needs a release policy written for each task. We instead state security relative to a reference agent, which runs the same plan under the same runtime monitor with a model that never obeys untrusted content. An agent is relatively secure if every leak it has is a leak the reference already has. Our framework, PlanTERS, instantiates relative security, a notion from speculative execution, with a small agent language in which the attacker chooses how the model follows instructions, a composition with runtime monitors, and attacker models that differ in what they observe. A fence theorem shows that revoking injectable tools at the first untrusted read, and never granting them back, makes every plan relatively secure at the event level on finite runs, for every model behaviour in which each injection is a single call and the model obeys on a schedule fixed in advance; with a fairness condition, this extends to possibly infinite runs. We prove or refute relative security for agents with fences, budgets, approvals, loops and dual LLMs, in Isabelle/HOL.

title: Integrating Action Prefix Prediction and Alignment Across Modalities for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
text:
Title: Integrating Action Prefix Prediction and Alignment Across Modalities for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Learning representations from multimodal observations is difficult in reinforcement learning with limited interaction data. Multimodal Joint Predictive Representation combines multimodal latent prediction with contrastive learning across modalities, but its recursive rollout depends on earlier predictions and its pairwise alignment focuses on correspondence between modalities. We propose Improved Predictive Representation, which combines prediction from action prefixes with alignment at the observed anchor based on Contrastive Multimodal learning. At each horizon, it predicts future representations directly from the observed anchor and the corresponding sequence of actions. We evaluate two crop configurations: IPR-S with a minimum retained crop area of 10%, and IPR-H with 50%. Across five DeepMind Control Suite tasks, IPR-H achieves an average return across tasks that is 10.0% higher than the baseline with visual and depth images and 3.4% higher with visual images and position vectors. The relative performance of the two configurations varies across tasks. In Webots, both IPR configurations achieve higher mean final returns than the baseline without LiDAR, but not when LiDAR is available.

title: A Triangular Log-Det PDHG for Semidefinite Programming: Complementarity Selection and Global Linear Convergence
text:
Title: A Triangular Log-Det PDHG for Semidefinite Programming: Complementarity Selection and Global Linear Convergence
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Semidefinite programming (SDP) is an important class of convex optimization problems with wide applications in practice. In this paper, we study a solution-selection question for first-order methods for solving SDPs: Can a first-order method provably select a strictly complementary solution when one exists, and a maximally complementary solution otherwise? We propose Triangular Log-Det PDHG (TriLog-PDHG), a primal-dual hybrid gradient method equipped with a triangular log-determinant Bregman kernel. We show that TriLog-PDHG converges to a KKT point for any fixed positive shift and to a maximally complementary solution for every sufficiently small positive shift. When a strictly complementary solution exists, the unshifted method provably selects a strictly complementary KKT point and enjoys a global linear convergence rate. Under the same condition, we further develop an averaged and adaptively restarted variant that accelerates convergence. Numerical experiments on classical examples and SDPLIB instances illustrate the complementarity-selection and convergence properties predicted by the theory.

title: PepLLM: ESM-Guided Llama for Structured Protein-Peptide Binding Interface Analysis
text:
Title: PepLLM: ESM-Guided Llama for Structured Protein-Peptide Binding Interface Analysis
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Protein-peptide interactions are central to cellular regulation and peptide-based drug discovery, yet existing computational methods mainly focus on interaction classification, binding-site prediction, or peptide binder generation. These formulations provide limited insight into the physicochemical mechanisms that determine how a peptide binds to a protein.
