Electrostatics are evaluated analytically in an atom-centered Gaussian basis, while an equivariant network learns the kinetic and exchange-correlation energy from energies and gradients of non-ground-state densities. Minimizing the functional from a superposition of atomic densities recovers the Kohn-Sham ground state: on held-out crystals, the density error falls from 6.7% to 0.4% of the electron count and the energy error reaches 0.25 mHa per atom, half that of a same-architecture interatomic potential. A single functional can be trained for both isolated molecules and periodic systems, and the model generalizes to larger unit cells. It largely preserves relative-energy rankings and reproduces convex-hull vertices on the tested H-N composition slice. Together, these results demonstrate the viability of machine-learned all-electron orbital-free DFT for variational density optimization and energy evaluation in fixed-geometry solids.

title: Quasinormal Modes Criticality across Black Hole Extremality
text:
Title: Quasinormal Modes Criticality across Black Hole Extremality
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We investigate the extremal solution branch to nonextremal branch transition in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg anti-de Sitter black holes, where the nonlinear electromagnetic parameter $λ$ governs the existence of the extremal branch solution. At fixed pressure and charge, extremal black hole only exist for $λ\leqλ_c$. For $λ>λ_c$, the lowest Hawking temperature keeps nonzero. Near this threshold, the lowest temperature follows a linear critical scaling, $T_{\min}\propto(λ-λ_c)^{α_T}$. We investigate the corresponding dynamical behavior by computing the quasinormal modes of a massless scalar perturbation along the lowest-temperature black hole branch. As the critical threshold is approached, two complex-frequency quasinormal modes branches collide on the imaginary axis and reorganize into distinct purely imaginary branches. Then the imaginary parts of these modes, together with higher overtones, reach zero at the critical threshold, described by $Γ_n\propto(λ-λ_c)^{α_n}$, with $α_n\simeqα_T$. The resulting zero-damped modes become increasingly localized near the event horizon, and their relative damping rates closely follow the overtone spacing predicted by the near-horizon AdS$_2$ spectrum. Our results show that the thermodynamic and dynamical critical behavior remain closely connected even when extremal black hole solutions cease to exist, providing further evidence for the relevance of near-extremal spectral behavior in this distinct critical regime.

title: Anchor Behavior, Not Parameters: Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning with a Single Shared Prompt
text:
Title: Anchor Behavior, Not Parameters: Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning with a Single Shared Prompt
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Prompt-based continual learning adapts a frozen pre-trained vision transformer by tuning a small set of prompt tokens. Recently, one-prompt methods which share one single prompt across all tasks make this paradigm maximally parameter efficient. The open question is how a shared prompt can keep the knowledge of old classes while being updated for new ones. Existing methods protect old knowledge in parameter space, where they freeze task-specific prompts, expand new components, or sparsely gate which tokens receive gradients. However, this method sacrifices plasticity, yet the drift it still permits in shared tokens can corrupt the prompt's function on past classes. What must be preserved is the prompt's behavior. We propose TEA-Prompt, which couples (i) a token evaluation module that assigns each prompt token a continuous, input-conditional relevance score injected into the attention logits, softly specializing tokens across tasks without discarding any of them, and (ii) an attention-behavior anchoring loss that constrains each token's attention output around class-specific query regions using only compact Gaussian query statistics without stored old images, weighted by the token's past relevance. Anchoring the attention value allows the parameters to continue updating freely, as long as their interaction remains unchanged. TEA-Prompt achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with markedly lower forgetting on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, and CUB-200 with only 0.38M parameters. Code is publicy available at https://github.com/cuonga1cvp/TEA-Prompt.git

title: Kernelised covariance matrices, dimension reduction and imbalanced spectral clustering
text:
Title: Kernelised covariance matrices, dimension reduction and imbalanced spectral clustering
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

The Gaussian Mixture Model (abbrv. GMM) is a classic generative model for clustered data, for which spectral clustering based on dimension reduction via PCA has been an effective framework. In this work, we investigate kernelised covariance matrices as an alternative mechanism for dimension reduction and spectral clustering, focusing on truncation kernels that select pairs of data points with suitable separation constraints. The structure of these matrices is motivated by considerations from statistical mechanics of repulsive particle systems. Our approach is particularly relevant for the setting of imbalanced clusters, where the sizes of the largest and smallest clusters have a diverging ratio with the problem size, and existing PCA-based methods turn out to be of limited effectiveness. We demonstrate efficient dimension reduction and clustering performance of these modified covariance matrices, substantiated by quantitative bounds. In particular, they achieve superior dimension reduction guarantees compared to PCA for a wide range of parameters in the regime of imbalanced clusters. For spectral clustering, our approach exhibits improvements over PCA in the imbalanced setting, in particular guaranteeing accurate clustering in a much larger regime of intra-cluster separations. Our theoretical guarantees reflected in a range of simulation experiments that exhibit these improvements for unbalanced clustering problems. Our analytical approach, based on kernel Laplacians, provide a toolbox as well as a relevant conceptual ingredient for clustering problems at large. We believe that our work will motivate the application of such kernelised covariance matrices for related classes of statistical problems, as well as spur new investigations in the theory of random matrices.

title: Algebraic classification of single-field inflationary dynamics
text:
Title: Algebraic classification of single-field inflationary dynamics
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We develop an algebraic classification of canonical single-field inflationary dynamics using an exact depressed cubic equation for the inflaton velocity. Its root structure identifies a branch-swap boundary distinct from the limiting boundary of downhill motion, where ultra-slow-roll inflation naturally emerges. Independently, the conservation of momentum conjugate to the comoving curvature perturbation in the long-wavelength limit provides a criterion for the growth or decay of the gauge-invariant difference between comoving and uniform-density curvature perturbations. Combining these criteria, we construct a unified dynamical chart in terms of the Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, illustrating its applicability to constant-roll inflation and simple toy models. Our classification shifts the emphasis from assigning models to fixed categories toward understanding the dynamical regimes traversed by inflationary trajectories and their implications for primordial perturbations.

title: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing
text:
Title: The simulability frontiers of photonic quantum computing
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Estimates of when photonic devices outgrow classical simulation are hard to compare: even for single-photon boson sampling, quoted thresholds range from 50 to 98 photons, as they rest on different tasks and assumptions. We propose as a common unit the time a classical computer needs to draw one sample from the device's exact output distribution, up to floating-point rounding. Only exactness applies equally to every kind of light, since the cost of approximate sampling depends on the accuracy required. The simulability frontier is the device size at which our fastest exact sampler produces one sample per second on a fixed machine; this device size increases with better hardware and algorithms. As the time per sample grows exponentially with the number of detected photons, doubling the machine speed moves the frontier by about one photon, whereas a better algorithm changes the growth rate. We measure the frontier with photonic-engines, an open-source GPU library of exact samplers for single photons, entangled photons from quantum emitters, vacuum-single-photon superpositions and squeezed light. Each sampler is validated against a simulator sharing no code with it. On one NVIDIA H100 GPU, with Haar-random interferometers, twice as many modes as photonic inputs and photon-number-resolving detectors, the frontier lies at 38.3 single photons and at 31.0 entangled photons from one emitter. For squeezed light, a timing model fitted to measurements places it at 41.5 squeezed photonic inputs of mean photon number 0.5. For our samplers, coherence alone makes simulation harder: sources that emit a photon with probability one half reach 64.2 when vacuum and photon are mixed incoherently, as for lossy single photons, but only 50.0 when they are in coherent superposition. Feed-forward from mid-circuit measurement of up to three modes lowers the single-photon frontier only from 38.3 to 38.1.

title: Lattice Hamiltonians for Chiral Gauge Theories
text:
Title: Lattice Hamiltonians for Chiral Gauge Theories
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We present a lattice Hamiltonian for chiral gauge theories on the boundary of a slab. The formulation is gauge-fixed, so the gauge variables are the physical modes of the boundary field, and Gauss's law holds exactly. The bulk gauge field is determined by the boundary field and an integer label, which is the topological charge that the boundary generates and the bulk stores as a localized instanton. The bulk enters as a dielectric, and both gauge anomaly conditions become the question of whether the boundary satisfies Gauss's law on its own. For background gauge fields, we show that sectors that differ by a unit of bulk charge are degenerate after Pauli-Villars subtraction and the mirror fermions decouple. The boundary theory has no vacuum angle. Every term in the Hamiltonian is defined in terms of the boundary gauge variables, the integer label and the fermion modes, a starting point for quantum circuit construction.

title: Kagome Flat Bands from Self-Assembled Water on Non-van der Waals 2D Materials
text:
Title: Kagome Flat Bands from Self-Assembled Water on Non-van der Waals 2D Materials
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

The properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials are governed not only by their intrinsic electronic structure but also in particular by their surface chemistry and interactions with the environment. The surfaces of non-van der Waals (non-vdW) 2D materials are intrinsically reactive and may require chemical stabilization under realistic experimental conditions. Here, we perform a systematic first-principles study of water passivation of non-vdW 2D materials and demonstrate that molecular water adsorption is energetically and dynamically favored for a wide range of systems. Rather than dissociating, water molecules frequently remain intact and form adsorbed ordered surface overlayers. These overlayers can adopt a kagome lattice geometry, leading to the emergence of flat electronic bands directly at the valence-band edge. Analysis of the electronic structure reveals a strong intermolecular coupling between neighboring water lone pairs within this kagome topology, while the locked molecular orientations simultaneously produce an electrostatically frustrated surface potential. These findings establish water not only as a stabilizing agent but also as an active element for electronic structure engineering of non-vdW 2D surfaces.

title: Restrained Diffusion Bridges: Targeted Denoiser Training and Refinement
text:
Title: Restrained Diffusion Bridges: Targeted Denoiser Training and Refinement
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Diffusion models are often inaccurate in critical, data-sparse regions of the target distribution. Sampling from restrained distributions, biased distributions used in classical enhanced sampling to concentrate data near chosen configurations, can control where training data are collected but biases the learned distribution. We establish that this bias cancels exactly when forward noising from restrained data is conditioned on the restrained configuration at an appropriately chosen intermediate time. This allows a pretrained model fine-tuned on restrained data to achieve high accuracy in any chosen region of the target distribution, regardless of its probability, using standard denoising or flow matching objectives without importance weights. When no target data are available, Gibbs sampling enables inference from a model trained exclusively on restrained data.

title: An entropic barrier to equilibration in the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation: Rigorous bounds for the microcanonical Brownian motion
text:
Title: An entropic barrier to equilibration in the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation: Rigorous bounds for the microcanonical Brownian motion
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

The relaxation of the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation is known to slow down dramatically when the energy density $\varepsilon$ exceeds a critical value $\varepsilon_c$, where the system enters a condensed phase. Replacing the Hamiltonian dynamics by Brownian motion on the microcanonical surface of $N$ sites at fixed mass and energy, we prove rigorous upper and lower bounds on the equilibration time $τ_{\mathrm{eq}}$, which is governed by the first non-zero eigenvalue $λ_1$ of the Laplacian on this surface. In the condensed phase the equilibration time is stretched exponential, not exponential, in the system size. The upper bounds on $λ_1$ come from trial functions: of one occupation for $\varepsilon \varepsilon_c$, where they cross the bottleneck through which the condensate moves between sites. The lower bounds on $λ_1$ come from a Bochner-Reilly argument, with a vector field that compensates the concavity of the boundary. As a result, $τ_{\mathrm{eq}}=O(1)$ for $\varepsilon \varepsilon_c$, asymptotically in $N$, $(\sqrt{2}-1)\sqrt{\varepsilon-\varepsilon_c}\leq\lnτ_{\mathrm{eq}}/\sqrt{N}\leq\sqrt{\varepsilon-\varepsilon_c}$. We conjecture that the left-hand bound is sharp and the right-hand one is not.

title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
text:
Title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,α}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,α}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.

title: Smoothed Least-Absolute Conditional Multidimensional Scaling via Iteratively Reweighted Majorization
text:
Title: Smoothed Least-Absolute Conditional Multidimensional Scaling via Iteratively Reweighted Majorization
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Conditional multidimensional scaling combines latent coordinates with observed covariates to fit pairwise dissimilarities. We develop a smoothed l1 formulation using the shifted Charbonnier loss. We prove residualwise sharpness of the quadratic loss majorizer, monotonicity, compact containment, and stationarity of noncollapsed accumulation points. A uniform additive bound quantifies approximation to exact least-absolute conditional stress. The experiments use paired contamination, separately calibrated loss parameters, combined-configuration recovery, and direct checks of the theorem's inequalities.

title: Recurrence in Sequence Space: How Epistasis Mimics Shared Ancestry
text:
Title: Recurrence in Sequence Space: How Epistasis Mimics Shared Ancestry
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Sequences in a protein family do not explore the sequence space freely: folding, packing, and binding couple residues, so the set of viable sequences is irreducibly correlated, a phenomenon referred to as epistasis. We show that such correlations lower the \emph{intrinsic dimension} $d_{\rm IN}$ of sequence space, counteracting the concentration of measure and broadening the distribution of pairwise distances. Consequentially, they make it likely that independently evolving lineages \emph{recur}, approaching one another by chance long after they last shared an ancestor. Using Kac's lemma we show that the logarithmic mean recurrence time grows linearly with the intrinsic dimension, $\log τ_{\rm rec} \propto {d_{\rm IN}}$ for typical sequences, so strongly constrained (low-dimensional) families recur often and generate sequence similarity that carries no genealogical signal. We establish this first in a solvable Ising-like model with tunable correlation, then in a real protein family using Potts models and Markov chain Monte Carlo, where $d_{\rm IN}$ remains predictive of recurrence even in multi-basins landscapes. Because recurrence is a property of the evolutionary process rather than of any estimator, it bounds the recoverability of deep history for distance-based and likelihood methods alike.

title: Reformulation Techniques for PDLP with Applications to QUBO and Joint Replenishment
text:
Title: Reformulation Techniques for PDLP with Applications to QUBO and Joint Replenishment
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Practitioners of linear programming widely believe that reformulating a linear program (LP) offers little benefit to interior-point methods: their iteration counts are famously insensitive to the formulation, so the payoff of reformulation beyond automatic presolve and customized linear solve is modest. This paper presents evidence that the same is not true of first-order solvers built on the primal-dual hybrid gradient method (PDHG), such as PDLP. Unlike interior-point methods, PDHG-type methods have per-iteration costs governed by the matrix representation of the formulation and iteration counts governed by its geometry, and both change under equivalent reformulations. We describe a general reformulation recipe: constraints drawn from a catalogue of projection-friendly polyhedra can be absorbed into the projection step of PDHG. We analyze what absorption does to the four constants that govern restarted PDHG: the coupling norm, the termination certificate, the distance scale, and the sharpness modulus. We perform the reformulation on two case studies. On the LP relaxation of quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO), absorption makes any step size below $1$ admissible on every instance, and yields a fully explicit linear rate. On the LP relaxation of the joint replenishment problem (JRP), whose optimum certifies a $2$-approximation for an NP-hard inventory problem, absorption improves the coupling norm and eliminates every matrix-vector product. Both reformulations run on GPUs with custom kernels in place of sparse matrix-vector products. We benchmark both against the GPU LP solver cuPDLPx applied to the original formulations. By solve time, the reformulated solvers are $6.4$-$9.6\times$ faster on QUBO and $6.1$-$28.9\times$ faster on the JRP. They take $1.7$-$4.3\times$ and $13.6$-$52.3\times$ fewer iterations respectively.

title: Unbounded advantage of adaptivity in entanglement-assisted communication
text:
Title: Unbounded advantage of adaptivity in entanglement-assisted communication
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Shared entanglement can reduce the amount of classical communication needed to perform distributed computation. This can be achieved either by first measuring the entanglement and then communicating classically, or by adapting the quantum measurement to the received message. Here, we introduce tasks that adaptive protocols can solve using just three entanglement-assisted messages, while the communication cost grows without bound when the quantum receiver is not adaptive. Consequently, no bounded amount of classical communication can reproduce all correlations generated by an entanglement-assisted ternary classical channel. We establish two complementary limitations on the relation between adaptive and non-adaptive quantum protocols. First, every adaptive protocol using a finite entanglement dimension admits a non-adaptive simulation at finite communication cost. Second, every adaptive protocol sending $d$ messages can be simulated to within error $\varepsilon$ using $O(d\log(1/\varepsilon))$ non-adaptive messages. Our results reveal the fundamentally unbounded advantage of adaptivity in quantum communication, but also that observing very large advantages requires both high-dimensional entanglement and very precise observations.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
text:
Title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Offline Reinforcement Learning with Online Action Selection Enabled by Sparse Gaussian-Process Critics
text:
Title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Offline Reinforcement Learning with Online Action Selection Enabled by Sparse Gaussian-Process Critics
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Start-ups and grade changes remain largely operator-driven, while developing and maintaining dynamic models for model-based control requires substantial engineering effort. Hybrid Offline Learning and Online Optimisation (HOFLON) uses one-step offline reinforcement learning to select actions from historical transition data. In its original implementation, the online objective combines the predicted return from a tree-ensemble critic with an adversarial-autoencoder (AAE) penalty for unfamiliar state-action pairs. We examine the effect of this penalty and replace the critic and AAE with a sparse variational Gaussian-process (sGP) critic. Actions maximise $μ- κσ$, an uncertainty-adjusted estimate of the return from one action followed by the historical operating practice. On the HOFLON polymerisation-reactor benchmark, removing the AAE from HOFLON led to 4 failed start-ups in 15 runs over five critics. At its published weight, the variation in the AAE penalty is four orders of magnitude smaller than the variation in the tree-ensemble critic. Nevertheless, it changes actions when the predicted returns of competing candidates are nearly equal, and paired runs with and without the penalty diverged from the first move. With a Matérn-5/2 sGP critic, $κ= 0$ led to failure in 13 of 15 runs, whereas with $κ= 3$ none of 15 runs (five critics, three noise realisations) failed. The median and lowest returns were 13,464 and 13,398 (HOFLON: 13,393 and 12,411). A squared-exponential sGP critic with learned inducing inputs needed $κ\geq 3$ to remain within the empirical data support in steady state, and then settled with a temperature offset of 2.0 K.

title: Linear Fitness Subspace in Protein Language Models Enables Sample-Efficient Directed Evolution
text:
Title: Linear Fitness Subspace in Protein Language Models Enables Sample-Efficient Directed Evolution
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Model-guided directed evolution seeks to identify high-fitness protein variants under limited oracle budgets. Protein language models (PLMs) provide rich representations for this task, but task-agnostic zero-shot scores can be misaligned with a target assay, while supervised search in high-dimensional embedding spaces can make surrogate modeling and uncertainty estimation sample-inefficient. We propose the Linear Fitness Subspace (LFS) hypothesis: within mutation-induced residue-level representation changes, a compact, assay-specific set of directions makes fitness variation linearly accessible from few labeled variants. This is a local, supervision-recoverable statement rather than a claim that protein fitness landscapes or global PLM geometry are universally linear. Building on this observation, we introduce Subspace-Guided Evolutionary Search (SGES), which estimates an LFS from a small initial sample and performs surrogate modeling, uncertainty estimation, and acquisition in the learned subspace. Across 10 core ProteinGym assays, 87 extended static-validation assays, and an 18-assay budgeted-search evaluation, SGES improves fitness prediction and search efficiency over zero-shot PLMs and recent ML-guided protein optimization baselines. Controlled comparisons with PCA, random projections, label-shuffled PLS, classical mutation features, and acquisition ablations further isolate the benefit of a fitness-aligned site-delta coordinate.

title: Conditional independence and graphical models for rankings
text:
Title: Conditional independence and graphical models for rankings
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Ranking models define probability distributions over rankings and are fundamental in applications such as preference learning and decision-making. Without structural assumptions, these models are intractable due to their factorial complexity. Although independence assumptions are key to reducing complexity and enabling interpretability, standard notions of conditional independence must account for the mutual exclusivity constraints inherent to rankings. We introduce relative rank models, a probabilistic framework based on structured coarsenings of the ranking space that relax these constraints while preserving relative order information. This representation enables a well-defined notion of conditional independence for rankings and allows rankings to be modeled using Bayesian networks. As a result, standard methods for learning and probabilistic inference can be applied to rankings, with interpretable representations based on conditional independence. We further show that two prominent ranking models based on independence assumptions tailored to rankings arise as special cases, providing a unifying framework for independence in ranking models.

title: Primordial non-Gaussianity in warm $k$-inflation with nonminimal derivative coupling
text:
Title: Primordial non-Gaussianity in warm $k$-inflation with nonminimal derivative coupling
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

This paper derives the finite-inertia intrinsic thermal bispectrum in potential-free warm $k$-inflation with nonminimal derivative coupling (NMDC). On a fixed Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker geometry, the complete cubic inflaton action determines the nonlinear stochastic source, encompassing temporal, spatial-gradient, and field-dependent kinetic interactions. The retarded solution captures the full momentum-triangle dependence while retaining unequal-time correlations, whereas its equilateral limit yields the intrinsic nonlinearity parameter. The power spectrum is computed with the same response and Gaussian initial state, thereby fixing the statistical normalization. A complementary local freeze-out reduction makes the interaction coefficients and two geometric shape contributions explicit. Comparison along an evolving near-attractor trajectory indicates that unequal-time finite-inertia propagation is crucial for quantitatively predicting the intrinsic bispectrum. The analysis also derives the slow-roll-suppressed nonlinear $δN$ conversion, together with the Arnowitt--Deser--Misner constraints and cubic vertices that characterize the direct gravitational effects of NMDC. These results clarify the respective roles of local freeze-out estimates and finite-inertia stochastic evolution in the nonlinear prediction.

title: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
text:
Title: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). We then conduct scenario analyses in which the acceptance rate of reused parts varies, and we quantify the joint implications for expected monetary outlays and CO 2 -equivalent emissions. Results show that higher PIEC acceptance can simultaneously reduce expected emissions and average claim cost, and the magnitude of the joint benefit depends on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process. The proposed framework provides a transparent, reproducible tool for insurers to evaluate repair-policy levers and to align claims operations with decarbonisation targets while retaining an explicit stochastic risk perspective.

title: The Ghost and Its Secret Partner
text:
Title: The Ghost and Its Secret Partner
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

The propagator of a ghost field acquires a pair of first-sheet complex conjugate poles above the multi-particle threshold. We show that this pole structure reveals the existence of a hidden asymptotic composite field -- the ghost's secret partner -- that remains coupled to the ghost asymptotically. This coupling induces persistent interference between the negative-norm one-particle state and the positive-norm composite-particle state. We analyze this phenomenon in four-derivative theories, in particular quadratic gravity, where the quantum dynamics prevents the spin-two ghost from appearing as an isolated asymptotic excitation. Although our results do not yet rule out observable negative probabilities, they may provide a dynamical basis for alternative amplitude prescriptions or superselection rules usually chosen or imposed ad hoc in theories with indefinite-norm vector spaces.

title: Proof of the conjecture about inequality of $1/H$-variations of fractional Brownian motion along the equidistant and the Lebesgue partitions
text:
Title: Proof of the conjecture about inequality of $1/H$-variations of fractional Brownian motion along the equidistant and the Lebesgue partitions
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We give an analytic proof of the comparison conjectured by Das, Łochowski, Matsuda and Perkowski for the fractional Brownian level-crossing constant: for standard fractional Brownian motion, $c_H>\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $0<H<1/2$ and $c_H<\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $1/2<H<1$, where $Z\sim N(0,1)$. At $H=1/2$, both constants equal one. The main tool is Gaussian comparison under ordering of increment variances. It applies because truncated variation is translation invariant and lattice-submodular, as follows from its minimum-total-variation characterization. A tangent variogram produces Brownian motion with an independent Gaussian drift on the upper side, and a periodic Brownian bridge on the lower side. The former has an explicit stationary reflection rate. For the latter we calculate an integrated cyclic crossing count by first-passage Laplace transforms. Elementary hyperbolic, theta-series, and Gamma inequalities then give strict comparisons on both full parameter ranges. No numerical integration, simulation, interval certificate, or quantitative local expansion at $H=1/2$ is used.

title: Pulsatile Endocrine Regulation with a Releasable Hormone Pool: Impulsive Feedback Model
text:
Title: Pulsatile Endocrine Regulation with a Releasable Hormone Pool: Impulsive Feedback Model
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

An impulsive model of endocrine regulation equipped with frequency- and amplitude-modulated pulsatile feedback is extended to study the dynamical effects pertaining to limitations due to the releasable hormone pool. The model describes a three-hormone regulatory loop and is applicable to endocrine systems such as the reproductive, stress, and growth hormone axes. Conditions guaranteeing the existence and uniqueness of a periodic solution with a single feedback-triggered impulse per period (a 1-cycle) are derived, together with monotonicity properties of its characteristics. An explicit Jacobian formula is obtained to assess local orbital stability. Model analysis demonstrates that a reduced hormone-pool replenishment rate produces a lower-amplitude, higher-frequency 1-cycle. This behavior is consistent with experimentally observed alterations in testosterone regulation in aging human males.

title: Towards coevolution-aware ancestral sequence reconstruction
text:
Title: Towards coevolution-aware ancestral sequence reconstruction
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) is a powerful approach for studying molecular evolution and the emergence of protein function. Yet most ASR methods assume that sites evolve independently, neglecting the epistatic constraints that shape protein structure, stability, and function. This simplification affects both ancestral inference and its evaluation: maximum-a-posteriori reconstructions may over-concentrate probability into a single over-idealized sequence, whereas independent posterior sampling can generate implausible or poorly functional ancestors. Here, we introduce a coevolution-aware ASR framework that combines standard phylogenetic inference with Direct Coupling Analysis (DCA), thereby preserving site-wise ancestral uncertainty while enforcing residue-residue constraints learned from extant protein families. To benchmark the method, we develop a controlled forward-evolution framework based on a DCA evolutionary sampler, allowing reconstructed ancestors to be compared with known ground-truth sequences generated under realistic epistatic constraints. Applied to beta-lactamases and DNA-binding domains, the approach improves reconstruction when ancestral states are epistatically constrained, and yields ensembles of candidate ancestors that are both phylogenetically consistent and statistically compatible with natural protein families. This framework bridges the gap between single-sequence MAP reconstruction and unconstrained posterior sampling, providing a practical route toward ancestral reconstructions that better reflect the coupled nature of protein evolution.

title: AutoNovo: Agentic Program Search Discovers Transferable Nucleic Acid Design Algorithms
text:
Title: AutoNovo: Agentic Program Search Discovers Transferable Nucleic Acid Design Algorithms
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

In-silico optimization of nucleic acids relies on predictive oracles that imperfectly capture biological function, so sequences optimized against one model may exploit model-specific artifacts and fail to generalize to independent models. Recent studies have shown that not all designers generalize equally well to independent models. In this work, we use agentic program search to iteratively propose, execute, evaluate, and revise code for nucleic-acid designers. We describe the successful strategies used to prompt the search. AutoNovo designers achieved the best observed mean among the evaluated methods on 3/3 DNA-design tasks in terms of in-silico performance, and 6/6 transfer tasks in terms of independent models. The designers come from a family of discovered nucleic acid designers rather than a single universal best designer. We plan to release the resulting designers. These results are the first steps in creating nucleic acid designers that maximize cross-model generalization, and thus improving the odds that in-silico designed sequences reflect real biology.

title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
text:
Title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. In this work, we develop a non-parametric reconstruction of this anomalous friction from dark standard sirens. We reconstruct its redshift dependence, encoded in the friction function $α_M(z)$, with a Gaussian process (GP) and derive the corresponding GW-to-EM luminosity-distance ratio $Ξ(z)$ by integration, explicitly retaining the relation between the local friction modification and its accumulated effect on the observed distance, while enforcing a monotonic and invertible GW luminosity distance. We apply the method to the GWTC-5.0 catalog, jointly inferring the source population, modified propagation, and background cosmological parameters. We find no evidence for departures from GR, with $α_M=0$ and $Ξ=1$ consistent with the posterior over the redshift range probed by the catalog. The result is stable under variations of the GP kernel, smoothness and amplitude priors, resolution prescription, and likelihood treatment. We further introduce function-space diagnostics for comparing flexible and parametric reconstructions, including prior calibration, prior-to-posterior contraction, common summaries of propagation-population degeneracies, and principal-component analysis. These tools make explicit which features are informed by the data and which are imposed by the function-space prior, providing a framework for interpretable non-parametric tests of gravitational-wave propagation.

title: MultiPASE: Shape-Aware Comparative 3D Genome Analysis
text:
Title: MultiPASE: Shape-Aware Comparative 3D Genome Analysis
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

3D genome structures reconstructed from Hi-C data provide valuable insights into chromatin organization, but comparing them across conditions and time points remains challenging because of noise, variability, and arbitrary orientation. State-of-the-art comparison approaches often rely on contact-matrix-based summaries, which do not preserve the spatial geometry of the reconstructed structures and make integration with gene expression and chromatin accessibility difficult. There is therefore a need for robust structural alignment and spatial abstraction methods that support integrated analysis across conditions and time points. We present MultiPASE, a computational pipeline for comparative analysis of reconstructed 3D genome structures represented as gene-level spatial point clouds. MultiPASE aligns point clouds into a shared coordinate frame using coarse-to-fine rigid registration with PCA-based axis disambiguation and robust ICP refinement, then summarizes spatial organization using two complementary shape abstraction methods that produce stable, nested, multi-scale representations from dense core regions to broader structural extent. Using Hi-C-derived reconstructions from viral infection experiments, we show how the approach reveals condition-dependent structural changes that are difficult to interpret from raw 3D structures alone. By integrating spatial structure with gene expression and chromatin accessibility, MultiPASE supports interactive analysis of spatial organization and gene relocation patterns. A quantitative validation, reported in the Supplementary Materials, shows that the proposed shape abstractions preserve non-convex features, remain stable across samples, and that the alignment pipeline is necessary for meaningful comparison. A usage case and a usability evaluation with eight participants demonstrate the pipeline's effectiveness for comparative structural analysis.

title: Local Limit Theorems for Heavy-Tailed Lévy Processes with Negative Drift
text:
Title: Local Limit Theorems for Heavy-Tailed Lévy Processes with Negative Drift
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

This paper establishes uniform local asymptotics for the first-passage time below zero and the stopped maximum of a Lévy process with negative drift and a locally regularly varying Lévy measure. We show that their probabilities of lying in distant intervals are asymptotic to the expected first-passage time multiplied by the corresponding Lévy masses, uniformly over interval widths bounded away from zero, including unbounded intervals. Although the two local events have asymptotically equivalent probabilities, their conditional overlap vanishes for fixed-width intervals. Nevertheless, we establish conditional concentration of the first-passage time and stopped maximum around their deterministic linear relation on scales dominating the fluctuations of the centered process. We further prove conditional functional limit theorems yielding a single-step process with random jump time on the original time scale and a deterministic linear descent on the accelerated scale. Finally, we identify the joint limiting distribution of the unscaled pre-passage position and terminal overshoot, distinguishing continuous passage from passage by a downward jump.

title: State-constrained optimal control with the theory of functional connections: squared slacks and junction exponents
text:
Title: State-constrained optimal control with the theory of functional connections: squared slacks and junction exponents
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

For optimal control problems with an affine state constraint, we combine the theory of functional connections (TFC), which writes every function satisfying prescribed linear conditions as an explicit expression in terms of a free function, with the squared-slack substitution $b - a^\top x(t) = s(t)^2$. Every trial trajectory then satisfies the endpoint conditions and the path constraint identically. The accuracy depends on the regularity of the slack function at the junctions with a boundary arc. Along an optimal trajectory, the constraint residual vanishes like $(t_1 - t)^m$, where the junction exponent $m$ is equal to the order $p$ of the constraint if and only if the $p$-th derivative of the constraint jumps at the junction, and thus a single polynomial slack converges algebraically. The \emph{multiple-arc TFC method} that we introduce, with unknown junction times and with residuals $(t_1 - t)^m σ(t)^2$ on the free arcs, represents the optimal trajectory exactly and converges geometrically when the arcs are analytic. In a linear-quadratic class, an exact cost identity shows that the cost of every trial trajectory is an upper bound of the optimal cost. We compare both approaches with direct collocation and indirect shooting on the Bryson-Denham problem, on a rendezvous problem with an approach corridor and on the six-dimensional atmospheric reentry of a space shuttle with three state constraints.

title: A State-Variable Theory of Evolving Material Symmetry
text:
Title: A State-Variable Theory of Evolving Material Symmetry
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Material architecture can evolve during loading, yet its mechanically expressed symmetry depends on both the structural state and the constitutive coupling. We connect these quantities through one parent-invariant free energy with a symmetric traceless internal tensor $\mathbf Q$. Its stabilizer distinguishes isotropic, uniaxial, and biaxial states, and projected gradient kinetics satisfies the structural dissipation inequality. Parent invariance generally guarantees only symmetry inheritance. For an explicit two-coupling elastic potential, we derive a stiffness-contraction reconstruction of $\mathbf Q$ and prove equality of the structural and tangent rotational symmetries for every nonzero coupling pair. The associated acoustic tensor links residual symmetry to protected transverse degeneracies. For a small uniaxial state, the leading squared-speed gap is $|γ_2s|\sin^2\vartheta/(2ρ_0)$; coupling selectivity and residual protection can suppress this term. We also derive a directional acoustic-trace reconstruction and state calibrated and nuisance-aware inverse conditions. Dimensionless structural-field, acoustic, transient finite-element, and synthetic inverse examples illustrate the predictions. The framework connects state evolution, mechanically expressed symmetry, and conditional observability without assigning independent dynamics to a group label.

title: How timing and mode of selection shape ancestral genetic contributions
text:
Title: How timing and mode of selection shape ancestral genetic contributions
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We examine a population that evolves according to a biparental Moran model with two distinct types of individuals. Each individual's type is determined by the allele they carry at one biallelic locus, which is transmitted in a Mendelian way. This type influences the individual's mating preferences. We investigate two specific mating patterns: (i) where the type determines the level of attractiveness, and (ii) where the type dictates the level of homogamous choosiness. In both scenarios, one type has an advantage over the other. Assuming an initial proportion b of individuals are of the advantaged type, we give an explicit formula for the asymptotic proportion of the population's genome that originates from these advantaged ancestors under an infinite population size approximation. Our results enable a comparison of the relative strengths of homogamous choosiness, attractiveness, and viability selection in terms of genome transmission, and prove notably that viability selection is always more efficient than both forms of reproductive selection.

title: Towards protein folding pathways by reconstructing protein residue networks with a policy-driven model
text:
Title: Towards protein folding pathways by reconstructing protein residue networks with a policy-driven model
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

A method that reconstructs protein residue networks using suitable node selection and edge recovery policies produced numerical observations that correlate strongly (Pearson's correlation coefficient < -0.83) with published folding rates for 52 two-state folders and 21 multi-state folders; correlations are also strong at the fold-family level. These results were obtained serendipitously with the ND model, which was introduced previously, but is here extended with policies that dictate actions according to feature states. This result points to the importance of both the starting search point and the prevailing condition (random seed) for the quick success of policy search by a simple hill-climber. The two conditions, suitable policies and random seed, which (evidenced by the strong correlation statistic) setup a conducive environment for modelling protein folding within ND, could be compared to appropriate physiological conditions required by proteins to fold naturally. Of interest is an examination of the sequence of restored edges for potential as plausible protein folding pathways. Towards this end, trajectory data is collected for analysis and further model evaluation and development.

title: Bagel: A Fast Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection Algorithm for Linear Models via Posterior Merging
text:
Title: Bagel: A Fast Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection Algorithm for Linear Models via Posterior Merging
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Bayesian online changepoint detection provides a natural framework for quantifying uncertainty about whether and when a change has occurred. It also enables the use of prior information which can increase detection power. Exact Bayesian inference sequentially updates the posterior of whether and when a change has occurred. We present a unified approach to calculating and updating this posterior for a class of regression models covering standard changepoint scenarios, such as changes in mean and slope, whilst also allowing common structure such as seasonal effects. However, naive implementation has a computational cost that increases linearly over time. We, further, introduce approximate updates that keep this cost constant. These are based on novel ideas of merging changepoint times, and are an alternative to existing pruning approaches. We show that merging enables better approximations of the posterior of when a change occurs. Furthermore, we introduce a novel condition for merging that accounts for both the posterior probability of the changepoint times and the similarity of their corresponding post-change parameters. We show that this is more accurate than conditions that only consider the former. We demonstrate the advantage of our approach on simulated data, and the Azure LLM inference traces.

title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
text:
Title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns. We optimize these mediators for correctness, informativeness, and linguistic quality through preference optimization, and evaluate the resulting explanations with human-calibrated metrics derived from separate human-labeled datasets. On the MovieLens-1M dataset, across multiple counterfactual generators and language models, the resulting summaries achieve high overall linguistic quality, while the strongest semantic results are obtained with high-success CFX methods such as ACCENT and SPINRec. Direct Preference Optimization improves the semantic metrics in almost all evaluated settings.

title: Einstein--Yang--Mills Plane Waves: Uniqueness and an Exact Curvature Double Copy
text:
Title: Einstein--Yang--Mills Plane Waves: Uniqueness and an Exact Curvature Double Copy
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Coleman found plane waves of Yang--Mills theory that are genuinely non-abelian in four dimensions and yet obey linear field equations, and Güven showed that they remain exact when gravity is included. We study these waves in $D$ dimensions. Coleman's profile, which is linear in the transverse coordinates, is singled out twice: up to gauge, it is the only profile with bounded energy density, and the only one for which the full Riemann tensor equals the color-contracted square of the Yang--Mills field strength that sources it. In anti-de Sitter space, we construct a closed-form family for every $D\geq4$; there, the full Riemann tensor cannot equal this color square. Waves whose transverse space is a sphere are always singular. In quadratic and Gauss--Bonnet gravity, a hyperbolic transverse space avoids this only if the waves defocus light or the higher-curvature terms become comparable to the Einstein term. All solutions extend, with changed coefficients, to generic gravity and gauge theories.

title: Retracing the Process of Translation: Proteome-wide mapping of stable transcriptomic predictors of protein abundance in cancer cell lines
text:
Title: Retracing the Process of Translation: Proteome-wide mapping of stable transcriptomic predictors of protein abundance in cancer cell lines
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Understanding the relationship between gene expression and protein abundance is central to molecular and systems biology. While gene expression reflects transcriptional activity, proteins are the functional molecules that determine cellular phenotypes. However, numerous post-transcriptional and translational regulatory layers complicate this relationship, and prior studies have reported only weak to moderate correlations between RNA and protein levels. Predicting protein abundance from transcriptomic data remains challenging, but it is a valuable goal for biological insight, especially when proteomic data is limited or unavailable. In this study, we applied a large-scale, Ridge regression-based feature selection strategy to identify predictive gene expression features for each of 8,423 proteins across 940 cancer cell lines. To our knowledge, this is the first work to perform such comprehensive protein-wise feature selection at this scale. Our analysis revealed both globally predictive and context-specific gene features. These included biologically meaningful modules such as immune-related genes, HOX transcription factor targets, and cytoskeletal components. The models identified stable candidate gene-protein associations that remained interpretable at the level of individual proteins and recurrent transcriptomic predictor patterns. Our approach enables interpretable modeling of protein expression from transcriptomic data and provides insight into transcriptomic features associated with protein abundance. This framework may support hypothesis generation, protein imputation in incomplete datasets, and deeper understanding of post-transcriptional regulation in cancer biology.

title: A globally convergent stochastic semismooth Newton method for strongly convex problems in Hilbert spaces
text:
Title: A globally convergent stochastic semismooth Newton method for strongly convex problems in Hilbert spaces
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We propose and analyze a globalized stochastic semismooth Newton method for stochastic optimization problems in Hilbert spaces where the objective is strongly convex with Lipschitz continuous, Newton differentiable gradient. Gradient and generalized Hessian information are only available through mini-batching. In each iteration, a full semismooth Newton trial step is accepted or rejected based on a stochastic residual test and rejected steps are replaced by damped steps in the same Newton direction. Throughout, we admit gradient estimators with affinely growing variance, as arises in optimization problems with random partial differential equations as constraints. We prove non-asymptotic global R-linear convergence in expectation as well as almost sure convergence. For sufficiently fast-growing batch sizes, the method transitions almost surely into a regime of pure Newton steps and converges R-superlinearly almost surely. The method is applied to the optimal control of a random elliptic equation featuring a Huber tracking term as well as a random parabolic equation with a Moreau--Yosida penalization of an almost sure state constraint.

title: INLA for Adaptive UAV Sampling of Radio Environment Maps in IoT Networks: Prior Width Governs Accuracy and Calibration
text:
Title: INLA for Adaptive UAV Sampling of Radio Environment Maps in IoT Networks: Prior Width Governs Accuracy and Calibration
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We study adaptive UAV sampling for radio environment map (REM) construction from non-Gaussian IoT observations. Integrated nested Laplace approximation(INLA) updates a Matérn GMRF posterior, with waypoints selected by entropy pre-screening and Sherman--Morrison lookahead over the reachable set. We show that the likelihood-induced Skew-Normal correction has a sextic entropy effect, explaining its limited influence on waypoint selection. Across 19 retained ray-traced windows,Random and lawnmower sampling cost a median 18.0\% and 14.0\% more residual NMSE than posterior-informed sampling, equivalently reductions of 15.3\% and 12.3\% when referred to those baselines, while differences among informative rules remain unresolved. Widening the prior shadowing standard deviation from 6.0 to 10.025\,dB improves NMSE and credible-interval coverage, with monotone improvement over a 4--16\,dB sweep on this corpus and no observed turning point, although overconfidence persists. Online width estimation from the UAV's own counts yields about 6.5\,dB without recovering the gain. Across 30 measured LoRaWAN propagation windows paired with simulated counts and scored only on received cells, the margin over non-adaptive sampling reproduces, the training-derived width minimizes the tested interval score, and GP-UCB has nominally $3$--$5\%$ lower NMSE. The results show substantial, corpus-dependent sensitivity to prior specification, while fine differences among acquisition rules have limited or unresolved effects, the preferred width depends on the corpus, scored cells and model mismatch.

title: Bayesian Sampling of Structural Ensembles: The Role of Ensemble-Counting Measures
text:
Title: Bayesian Sampling of Structural Ensembles: The Role of Ensemble-Counting Measures
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Structural ensemble refinement is widely used to integrate molecular simulations with experimental measurements. While most applications focus on the maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) ensemble, Bayesian sampling of the posterior distribution can provide uncertainty estimates and posterior averages for arbitrary observables. A notable step in this direction was introduced by the Bayesian Energy Landscape Tilting (BELT) framework, where sampling is performed on a family of maximum-entropy ensembles parametrized by Lagrange multipliers. Here, we show that Bayesian sampling in this setting requires an explicit choice of ensemble-counting measure. In particular, the flat measure in Lagrange-multiplier space used in the original BELT formulation leads to a posterior distribution that is formally non-normalizable for finite reference trajectories. We propose the Jeffreys measure as an invariant ensemble-counting prescription, restoring normalizability in the finite-sample situations considered here, and providing a consistent definition of posterior averages. Using both an analytically tractable Gaussian model and maximum-entropy refinement of RNA oligomer simulations, we compare different ensemble-counting measures and show that they can significantly affect Bayesian estimates. The resulting methodology has been implemented in the \texttt{MDRefine} software package.

title: PHASE: encoding global protein ensembles with local Hamiltonians and all-atom backmapping
text:
Title: PHASE: encoding global protein ensembles with local Hamiltonians and all-atom backmapping
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Protein function is governed by conformational ensembles, which can be viewed as high-dimensional probability distributions over molecular conformations. Yet the statistical organization of these distributions is often represented only implicitly, either through collections of simulation trajectories or within high-capacity generative models. Here, we introduce PHASE (Protein Hamiltonians for Sampling of Ensembles), a system-specific framework that converts atomistic conformational ensembles into an explicit and interpretable statistical model. Applied to ten conformational ensembles derived from approximately 37$μ$s of atomistic simulations of the adenosine A2A receptor, Hamiltonians containing only local residue couplings within 6$\mathring{A}$ reproduce residue-wise and pairwise microstate statistics, including correlations between residues that are not directly coupled in the model. Moreover, independently fitted inactive and active reference Hamiltonians define an endpoint preference coordinate that organizes newly sampled ligand-, effector- and conformation-dependent ensembles along the A2A activation landscape without receiving these biochemical labels as model inputs. Finally, a cluster-conditioned all-atom reconstruction model preserves the prescribed residue microstate patterns of newly sampled configurations, closing the coarse-graining-sampling-backmapping cycle. The resulting discrete representation additionally admits direct QUBO encoding, enabling classical annealing and providing a route toward future quantum-annealing implementations. PHASE therefore provides a protein-general procedure for constructing compact, interpretable and atomistically realizable statistical models of protein conformational ensembles.

title: LabAgent: Customize Any Research Hubs for Scientific Discoveries Using AI Agents
text:
Title: LabAgent: Customize Any Research Hubs for Scientific Discoveries Using AI Agents
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Scientific research is a continuous process that emphasizes inheritance. Methods developed by predecessors are often expanded upon by new researchers to explore more novel and in-depth scientific questions. However, the change of lab staff, such as student graduation, leads to a lack of personnel capable of replicating methods. Methods that have been developed with significant effort and resources cannot be continued. To address these limitations, we propose LabAgent, a reproduce and discovery harness tailored for a lab's continuous work. LabAgent employs two mechanisms to guarantee that all skills can be executed and verified and to record the corrective methods and experiences, allowing for direct correction or avoidance of similar errors. We applied LabAgent to drug property prediction, biomedical problem analysis, protein variant effect prediction, and statistical genetics in life science domains. LabAgent ranks first over commercial generalist agents in every domain, and demonstrates accurate reproduction of a published figure. Overall, these results demonstrate that LabAgent can effectively integrate and reasonably expand laboratory knowledge.

title: Spectral analysis of protein backbone geometry reveals abrupt helix--coil boundaries
text:
Title: Spectral analysis of protein backbone geometry reveals abrupt helix--coil boundaries
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The boundaries of cooperative helix--coil transitions influence protein allostery and conformational dynamics, yet the persistent one-to-two-residue ambiguity in their assignment remains poorly characterized. We apply the discrete Hasimoto map to translate three-dimensional C$_α$ backbone geometry into a one-dimensional discrete nonlinear Schrödinger effective potential and analyze its spatial-frequency structure. Helical segments appear as near-integrable, low-entropy states whose spectral power concentrates at the zero-frequency mode, whereas coil regions show broadband fluctuations. A pointwise integrability residual and a windowed spectral entropy separate the two phases with ROC AUC values of 0.783 and 0.715, and their combination reaches 0.803, while combining the residual instead with a low-frequency energy ratio reaches 0.815. Across 1\,986 proteins and 19\,148 of 21\,107 fitted helix--coil boundaries the transition is abrupt, with a median sigmoid width of 0.145 residues that measures the steepness of a single-step discrete jump rather than a literal sub-residue distance; the transition is directionally asymmetric, with helix exits sharper than entries. Across the full dataset every C$_α$ geometry-based assignment, including DSSP-calibrated P-SEA and both spectral probes, loses agreement with the DSSP hydrogen-bond reference most acutely at these boundaries, indicating that the assignment ambiguity is a general feature of C$_α$ geometry rather than any single algorithm. The windowed spectral probe is subject to a Gabor resolution limit and is therefore outperformed by the pointwise probe, which attains the lattice-limited resolution.

title: Are UFOs Real? Introducing Unified Factored Organizers
text:
Title: Are UFOs Real? Introducing Unified Factored Organizers
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Implicit in much research in deep learning is the assumption that if a network achieves low loss, then it must have learned a good representation of its training data. Recent work by Kumar et al. (2025, arXiv:2505.11581) questions this assumption, arguing that networks trained with conventional gradient descent achieve low loss despite learning fractured entangled representations (FER), leaving related concepts disconnected and unrelated concepts entangled inappropriately. Kumar et al. further show that dramatically better representations are possible: a network evolved through an open-ended, human-in-the-loop process learned unified factored representations (UFR) that capture the regularities of the domain far better than a counterpart with nearly identical outputs trained with conventional gradient descent. Inspired by UFR, this paper introduces unified factored organizers (UFOs), networks trained to model regularities in the representations of other networks. A network can then be trained both to achieve low loss on its task objective and to align its representations with the model learned by the UFO. Networks trained with UFOs are shown to learn qualitatively superior representations in an image-regression domain where representations are easily interpretable. To provide quantitative evidence for the impact of UFOs on representation learning, a transformer is trained with and without UFO regularization to grok a modular arithmetic problem set. When combined with weight decay, UFOs can reduce the number of transformer training steps needed to grok by more than 10x relative to weight decay alone. Without weight decay, UFOs can reduce the number of transformer training steps needed to grok by more than 100x relative to an unregularized baseline. If UFOs are real, they suggest a new paradigm where loss functions themselves are trained to learn an effective model of good representation.

title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
text:
Title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local properties, whereas the applied potential energy is a prescribed input. In this work, we propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently. Benchmarks on polar GaN systems and crystalline-Si/amorphous-SiO$_2$ interfaces demonstrate improved Hamiltonian accuracy and reproduction of thickness-dependent electrostatic variations, as well as spatially nonuniform field-induced screening that models without polarization fail to capture. Our model also allows us to study nanoscale electronic devices. By iteratively solving the Hamiltonian eigenproblem and self-consistently updating free-carrier occupations and the electrostatic potential, we simulate an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.

title: Semi-Device-Independent Certification of multi-qubit Entangled Basis Measurement
text:
Title: Semi-Device-Independent Certification of multi-qubit Entangled Basis Measurement
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The entangled basis measurement plays a pivotal role in fundamental information-processing tasks, such as dense coding, quantum teleportation, and entanglement swapping. Consequently, certifying such measurements in a device-independent manner remains an important task. In this work, we present a semi-device-independent (SDI) protocol in a prepare-and-measure (PM) scenario for certifying a class of m-qubit entangled basis measurements. Specifically, we consider a tripartite PM scenario featuring two senders and one receiver, where each sender sends an arbitrary number of 2^m inputs and the receiver performs a measurement with 2^m outcomes. We adopt a classical causal model framework to demonstrate the non-classicality of quantum measurements. We introduce nonlinear witnesses in classical causal models and demonstrate that the optimal quantum value exceeds the classical bounds. Further, we demonstrate that the optimal quantum value of the witness SDI certify the entangled basis measurement and the prepared states of the two senders.

title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic Rényi defects
text:
Title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic Rényi defects
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

The Rényi entropies of a ball are computed by the Rényi defect (the twist operator viewed as a conformal defect), which in holography is dual to a hyperbolic black hole. We identify hyperbolic black holes with homogeneous charged scalar hair as conformal defects that break the U(1) symmetry. At large $N$ and for repulsive self-interactions, conformality loss of the Rényi defect turns explicit symmetry breaking into spontaneous breaking: below a critical index $n_*$ the symmetry-breaking defect is reached only with an explicit source on the entangling surface; at $n_*$ the dimension of a defect operator from a light charged scalar turns complex; beyond $n_*$ the Rényi defect flows to the symmetry-breaking defect with no source. The condensate, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, instead preserves them outside a layer at the entangling surface, whose width diverges at $n_*$ with Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless scaling. The universal term of the Rényi entropy therefore jumps at $n_*$ to that of the symmetry-breaking defect. We demonstrate this mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, with closed-form saddles and defect data, and numerical flows. For a ball we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the radius is large enough, and that it ends at the symmetry-breaking defect as the radius grows.

title: Predicting unstable planar fault energies in multicomponent alloys from pure elemental components
text:
Title: Predicting unstable planar fault energies in multicomponent alloys from pure elemental components
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

The unstable planar fault energies (UPFEs) govern slip and twinning but are not experimentally measurable. Using EAM potentials complemented by DFT, we investigate their temperature and compositional dependence and their relationship with the shear modulus. For pure \textit{fcc} elements with low stacking fault energies (SFEs), UPFEs are substantially less temperature-sensitive than SFEs. The reported linear relationship between UPFEs and the product of shear modulus and Burgers vector ($μb_{\mathrm{p}}$) holds for close-packed elements and solid solutions, but deviates for intermetallics and non-close-packed elements. In the Co-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ni system, binary alloys show composition-dependent deviations, while the correlation strengthens with increasing chemical complexity. Furthermore, $μb_{\mathrm{p}}$ of multicomponent alloys linearly correlates with the composition-weighted elemental $μb_{\mathrm{p}}$ ($R^2=0.95$), despite a systematic negative deviation. This provides a simple, computationally inexpensive route for estimating $μb_{\mathrm{p}}$ and screening UPFEs directly from pure elemental constituents.

title: Multifractality in sputtered crystalline and amorphous transition metal nitride thin films
text:
Title: Multifractality in sputtered crystalline and amorphous transition metal nitride thin films
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

In this work, we present evidence for multifractal growth in Titanium and Niobium nitride thin films on different substrates. Self-similar multifractal structures such as dendrites and multi-branched snowflake-like structures are reported. The fractal dimensions are controlled by a combination of processing parameters and conditions at the film-substrate interface. Significantly, fractal growth is observed not only in crystalline films on crystalline and amorphous substrates but also on amorphous films on crystalline substrates. The 2D Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (2D MFDFA) carried out on the scanning electron micrographs, clearly reveals the multifractal nature of the nitride thin films. The statistical moments were varied between -5 to +5. The Hausdorff dimensions for the TiN films are in the range of 1.65 to 1.79 while it is 1.64 to 1.74 for the NbN thin films. It is proposed that the observed multifractality is due to a competition between morphological instabilities and Diffusion-Limited Aggregation

title: Local distinguishability of five five-partite orthogonal product states
text:
Title: Local distinguishability of five five-partite orthogonal product states
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The local distinguishability of five orthogonal product states (OPSs) has been studied in several multipartite settings, but the five-partite case still requires a systematic characterization. In this paper, we consider five five-partite OPSs, where any two states are orthogonal on exactly one subsystem. By analyzing the distribution of ten pairwise orthogonality relations over five subsystems, we classify the corresponding orthogonality structures by colored orthogonality graphs. After eliminating identical graphs under relabeling of states and permutation of subsystems, we obtain 443 different graphs in seven genuinely five-partite categories. We prove that the OPSs corresponding to 434 of these graphs can be perfectly distinguished by local operations and classical communication (LOCC), while the remaining 9 exceptional cases fall into two types and require separate analysis. Our results give a characterization of the local distinguishability of five OPSs in five-partite OPSs.

title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
text:
Title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Spatially resolved modeling of optically pumped alkali-metal vapors requires the solution of a high-dimensional nonlinear diffusive quantum master equation (DQME) coupled to state-dependent light propagation. We develop a structure-preserving computational framework for this coupled three-dimensional system in the high-pressure limit. The high-fidelity solver combines second-order finite differences, explicit pseudo-time marching, and an exponential-integrator discretization of the light-propagation equation. The scheme preserves the density-matrix trace, while a derived global pseudo-time-step restriction guarantees nonnegative, bound-preserving population updates and frozen-coefficient $1$-norm stability. In the absence of a closed-form solution for the general coupled problem, the solver is verified against complementary analytical reductions, pumping-rate asymptotics, and a light-propagation invariant, all of which are accurately recovered. Tensorized GPU implementation reduces the per-iteration cost by more than two orders of magnitude relative to a single-core CPU. For repeated parameter queries, we further construct an intrusive POD--Galerkin reduced-order model. The quadratic spin-exchange term is treated by an exact nonlinear quadratic expansion, whereas the nonpolynomial and nonlocal optical-pumping term is hyper-reduced using the discrete empirical interpolation method. At out-of-sample parameter points, the reduced model closely reproduces the full-order population and polarization fields while achieving speedup of more than \(7\times10^3\) relative to the single-core CPU full-order solver. The resulting hierarchy connects verified high-fidelity simulation with efficient reduced-order prediction for spatially resolved alkali-metal spin dynamics.
