title: Modular Hamiltonian and Typicality of Degenerate States
text:
Title: Modular Hamiltonian and Typicality of Degenerate States
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Free fermions exhibit Eigenstate Typicality (ET) meaning that the reduced density matrix, $ρ$, of a small spatial subsystem of a {\sl single}, typical, excited energy eigenstate is gaussian with a modular hamiltonian, $h \equiv -\log ρ$, asymptotically proportional to the free fermion hamiltonian. In effect, the ET may be thought of as providing an independent route to establishing the Fermi-Dirac (FD) distribution for free fermions. We revisit this argument for fermions belonging to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates. Specifically, we show that the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a superposition of degenerate eigenstates in a 1-d free fermion lattice system is interacting, and therefore the reduced density matrix for the subsystem is not gaussian. Measurements of the single particle distribution of a small subsystem would then exhibit non-thermal deviations from the FD distribution. These features may be traced to a violation of Wick's theorem for the chosen excited state. We develop a perturbation theory for the modular hamiltonian corresponding to a weak mixture of degenerate states and study the modular hamiltonian (exactly) computationally. Finally, we speculate that initial conditions in a realistic fermi system evolving towards equilibrium might be encoded in the interaction terms of the modular hamiltonian and consequent correlations of fermions.

title: A Density-Matrix Formulation of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra for Møller-Plesset and Configuration Interaction Methods
text:
Title: A Density-Matrix Formulation of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra for Møller-Plesset and Configuration Interaction Methods
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We reformulate the overlap of wave-function derivatives that defines the atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors (VG-APTs) used to compute vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) rotatory strengths. In place of our earlier determinant-level derivatives, the new approach expresses these tensors as contractions involving molecular-orbital derivative integrals, perturbed and unperturbed one- and two-electron density matrices, and dot products of the perturbed correlated wave-function amplitudes. Following the elegant treatment of the diagonal Born-Oppenheimer correction by Gauss and co-workers, the formulation holds for any real, normalized CI-like wave function. The two-electron density contribution vanishes exactly, because one perturbation is real (nuclear) and the other imaginary (magnetic field or momentum); this removes multiple terms from our earlier AAT and VG-APT expressions for second-order Møller-Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) and configuration interaction singles and doubles (CISD). We also present a simplified form of the origin-independent length-gauge [LG(OI)] rotatory strength that avoids the singular-value decomposition of the outer product of the length-gauge APT and VG-APT vectors for each mode, and that clarifies how the LG(OI) and velocity-gauge rotatory strengths are related. Applying the density-based AATs and VG-APTs to ($P$)-hydrogen peroxide, (\textit{S})-methyloxirane, and (\textit{S})-3-chloro-1-butyne, we find that discrepancies among the gauges arise chiefly from basis-set incompleteness in the VG-APT. The charge-sum rule serves as a useful measure of that incompleteness, independent of the correlation method.

title: Calmness Modulus of Parameterized Convex Constraint Systems: Exact Closed-Form Formulas via Second-Order Admissibility
text:
Title: Calmness Modulus of Parameterized Convex Constraint Systems: Exact Closed-Form Formulas via Second-Order Admissibility
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We resolve the open problem of deriving an exact, closed-form algebraic formula for the calmness modulus of $\mathcal{C}^2$ convex constrained feasible set mappings $\mathcal{F}(b) := \{ x \in \mathbb{R}^n \colon f_t(x) \le b_t, \, \forall t \in T \}$ under right-hand side perturbations at a given pair of the graph $(\bar{b}, \bar{x})$. First, under the condition $0_n \in \mathrm{int}\left(\mathrm{conv}\left\{ \nabla f_t(\bar{x}) ,\; t \in T(\bar{x}) \right\}\right)$, we prove that the calmness modulus coincides with the inverse distance from the origin to the boundary of the nominal subdifferential. Second, for general $\mathcal{C}^2$ convex systems where the previously mentioned interior condition does not hold, we introduce a second-order admissibility filtering over the active indexes. We show that this filtered family, $\mathcal{D}^0_2(\bar{x})$, yields an exact characterization of the calmness modulus relying solely on nominal data.

title: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data
text:
Title: Scaling Laws for SAE Training Data
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Activation storage is often a bottleneck in sparse autoencoder (SAE) training. We study how many unique activations an SAE needs when its total training budget is fixed. Quality improves rapidly as the buffer grows, then reaches a plateau where replaying the buffer is nearly as effective as using fresh activations throughout training. Beyond this point, additional unique activations bring little benefit to reconstruction or interpretability, so the buffer need not grow with the training budget. We describe this tradeoff between diversity and repetition with a scaling law for limited data. We validate it across dictionary sizes and token budgets, early, middle, and late layers of Llama-3.1, Qwen3 model sizes, and BatchTopK, TopK, and JumpReLU SAEs. Sweeps using mathematical text and Python code test the effect of changing the activation source. Evaluation covers explained variance (EV), reconstruction MSE, feature absorption, automated interpretability, and sparse probing. These results give a practical training rule: choose the smallest buffer that reaches the quality plateau and replay it for the remaining budget. In our experiments, this reduces activation storage by $8\text{--}64\times$ with negligible quality loss.

title: Blind Random Search with Noisy Measurements: Almost Sure Convergence and Convergence Rates
text:
Title: Blind Random Search with Noisy Measurements: Almost Sure Convergence and Convergence Rates
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Blind random search is a simple global optimization method that only requires the value of the loss function, without needing gradient information or an explicit loss model. However, its classical formulation assumes that the loss evaluation is noise-free, which limits its direct application to practical problems with noisy measurements. We extend blind random search by combining a vanishing acceptance threshold with the running average of noisy loss measurements. Under the stated assumptions, we prove that the proposed algorithm converges almost surely to the global minimizer. We further analyze the rate at which the loss at the current estimate approaches the minimum loss. For low-dimensional cases, we obtain an almost sure asymptotic upper bound on the difference between the two, and for high-dimensional cases, we prove that this difference, suitably scaled, has an exact Weibull limiting distribution.

title: Absorption Probabilities for Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension
text:
Title: Absorption Probabilities for Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

For every dimension $d\ge1$, we determine the probability that a prescribed point in $\mathbb R^d$ belongs to the convex hull over $[0,1]$ of a standard Brownian motion starting at the origin or of a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$. We obtain explicit one-dimensional integral formulas involving only standard special functions. For example, in dimension three the Brownian-motion absorption probability $p_3^B(r)$ for a prescribed point at distance $r>0$ from the origin is \[ p_3^B(r) =\frac{r}{\sqrt2\,π^{3/2}} \int_0^\infty \left(\fracπ{2\sqrt{1+v^2}}-1\right) \mathrm{e}^{-r^2(1+v^2)/4} (K_1-K_0)\!\left(\frac{r^2(1+v^2)}4\right)\,\mathrm{d} v, \] where $K_ν$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind. For each fixed dimension $d\ge1$ and each prescribed nonzero point in $\mathbb R^d$, we derive precise asymptotics of the non-absorption probabilities for the convex hulls of Brownian motion on $[0,T]$ and a Brownian bridge from $0$ to $0$ over the same interval, as $T\to\infty$. The corresponding probabilities are asymptotic to explicit positive constants times $T^{-1/2}(\log T)^{d-1}$ and $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$, respectively. We also consider the first time $τ_d$ at which the growing convex hull of a standard Brownian motion in $\mathbb R^d$ absorbs a prescribed point at distance one from the origin. We determine the Mellin and Laplace transforms of $τ_d$ explicitly. Although $\mathbb E[τ_d]=\infty$ in every dimension, we prove \[ \frac{\logτ_d-2d}{2\sqrt d} \xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1), \qquad d\to\infty. \] In particular, $τ_d^{1/d}\to\mathrm{e}^2$ in probability, as $d\to\infty$. Surprisingly, the same limit holds for $S_d^{1/d}$, where $S_d$ is the first time at which the Brownian convex hull contains the entire unit ball.

title: Going off the (momentum) grid: A simple implementation of noncold relics in linear Boltzmann solvers
text:
Title: Going off the (momentum) grid: A simple implementation of noncold relics in linear Boltzmann solvers
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Linear Boltzmann solvers typically evolve the perturbations of noncold relics, such as massive neutrinos or hot subcomponents of the dark matter, on a momentum grid, often switching to a fluid approximation on small scales for efficiency. We implement in CLASS the Dispersive Fluid Approximation (DFA), a fluid scheme that captures the scale-dependent sound speed of these species. Within the standard ncdm module, the DFA significantly outperforms the default CLASS fluid approximation in the cross and neutrino power spectra, and reduces errors in the cold dark matter power spectrum by up to an order of magnitude, while adding only 1-4% to the total runtime. We also present the first open-source implementation of the Generalized Boltzmann Hierarchy (GBH), which simplifies the implementation of noncold relics by integrating out the momentum dependence of their perturbations altogether. Combined with the DFA and tested on massive neutrinos, the GBH reproduces the matter power spectrum to better than permille accuracy and cosmological parameter constraints to better than 0.05 sigma, at a computational cost comparable to that of the standard implementation. We argue that the GBH is particularly well suited to non-thermal relics whose distribution function varies with time or across parameter space. Our implementation of both the DFA and the GBH in CLASS is publicly available at https://github.com/aradn97/class_GBH.

title: Relativistic Kohn--Sham Theory of Paramagnetic Magnetic-Resonance Properties
text:
Title: Relativistic Kohn--Sham Theory of Paramagnetic Magnetic-Resonance Properties
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

A general density functional theory based relativistic theory for paramagnetic NMR (pNMR) shifts, EPR g-tensors and hyperfine coupling tensors as well as magnetizabilities is derived. The formulation uses spin--orbit exact two-component (X2C) theory, gauge-including atomic orbitals, and generalized complex Kohn--Sham response equations with all ingredients being implemented analytically with the help of Goldstone modes and an orientation-constrained shielding. Additionally, we describe a two-component augmented Roothaan--Hall (ARH) solver for robust and stable convergence, which ensures that both a stationary point and a minimum are found. This is crucial for the convergence of the response equations for properties of paramagnetic systems. The extension of common population analyses for the two-component theory to aid in the interpretation of the spectra is further described. Using these new techniques, we are able to analyze the success and failure of density functional theory for relativistic open-shell systems including actinide complexes.

title: Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN for Efficient Multipath Parameter Estimation in MIMO Systems
text:
Title: Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN for Efficient Multipath Parameter Estimation in MIMO Systems
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

High-resolution multipath estimation in wideband multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels requires repeated searches over angle of arrival, angle of departure, and propagation distance. This paper presents neural network-assisted CLEAN (NN-CLEAN), which replaces the multidimensional search at each extraction step with a multi-head classifier while retaining least-squares (LS) estimation of the complex path gain, parametric reconstruction, and residual cancellation. The same classifier is applied to successive residuals, allowing the extraction depth to vary without changing its output structure. With the number of iterations prescribed by the reference multipath-component (MPC) count, off-grid synthetic tests show that NN-CLEAN slightly exceeds grid-search CLEAN (GS-CLEAN) in path accuracy for one and two MPCs, although its accuracy declines more rapidly at larger path counts. For complete three-MPC extraction at a batch size of eight, NN-CLEAN achieves an approximately $27\times$ speedup and a $52$-fold reduction in peak GPU memory relative to GS-CLEAN. Applied without retraining to two-MPC line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) Sionna ray-tracing channels within a coded MIMO link, NN-CLEAN substantially reduces channel-reconstruction mean-squared error (MSE) and bit error rate (BER) relative to interpolated LS channel estimation. GS-CLEAN retains an accuracy advantage on these channels, indicating the estimation cost associated with the computational savings.

title: A liquid vapor phase transition in quantum statistical mechanics
text:
Title: A liquid vapor phase transition in quantum statistical mechanics
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We prove a liquid vapor phase transition for a quantum system of particles in the continuum. The system is the quantum version with Boltzmann statistics of the point particles model introduced in by Lebowitz, Mazel and Presutti.

title: Origin of bias-voltage-dependent transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains
text:
Title: Origin of bias-voltage-dependent transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We investigated how the bias-voltage-dependent variation in the ferroelectric domain switching pathways affects the transient negative capacitance in multidomain PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains having, primarily, 90$^\circ$ walls. Using the vector piezoresponse force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, we show that, together with strain, local variation in composition results in the formation of labyrinthine domains in epitaxial films of thickness $\sim$1 $μ$m. Clear signature of emergence of bias-voltage-dependent pathways could be observed in the Raman modes exhibiting splitting due to an intermediate state - different from the initial and final states - at the ``intermediate state of switching". The polarization relaxation patterns also show different states emerging depending on the bias voltage characteristics. The phase-field simulation of relaxation of ``intermediate state of switching" corroborates the experimental results and also exhibits dependence of the domain-wall area on the bias voltage and damping parameter. Combining the results of experiments and theoretical calculation, we show, therefore, that the variation of bias voltage leads to a change in the domain switching pathways and each pathway is associated with specific domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching". Since, the net domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching" governs the magnitude of transient negative capacitance, this work thus traces the origin of tunability of transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor.

title: When Does Physics Beat Data? Data-Efficient Traffic State Estimation with Amortized PINNs
text:
Title: When Does Physics Beat Data? Data-Efficient Traffic State Estimation with Amortized PINNs
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Traffic state estimation (TSE) reconstructs traffic density at unmonitored locations from a sparse set of sensors. Data-driven models work well when sensors are dense but degrade sharply as coverage thins. We show that imposing the Lighthill-Whitham-Richards conservation law as a physics-informed prior makes TSE more data-efficient. On four real corridors (NGSIM, I-80, PeMS04, PeMS08), physics-informed estimators generalise to held-out sensors where data-driven models, including classical and deep kriging, overfit the observed ones. On the two shock-rich corridors the effect is a clear crossover: as more sensors are held out, data-driven models collapse while the physics-informed estimator degrades gracefully, leading the no-physics network by about 26-38% at 85-90% held out and the strongest classical kriging by about 10-21% at 90%. A matched smoothness prior does not reproduce the gain, and an extended Kalman filter on the same LWR model is outperformed on the shock corridors, so the advantage comes from how the conservation law is imposed. Finally, one loss-conditional PINN removes the per-corridor loss-weight search, matching a 20-point search at about 5x lower cost.

title: Soliton-Lattice Origin of Incommensurability in High-Pressure Antimony
text:
Title: Soliton-Lattice Origin of Incommensurability in High-Pressure Antimony
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

The microscopic origin of incommensurability in host-guest crystals remains unresolved. Here we show that the high-pressure antimony host-guest phase Sb-II is a soliton lattice, where localized guest-host misregistries decorate a commensurate 4/3 reference structure. First-principles calculations reveal a corrugated and hysteretic registry landscape, motivating a Frenkel-Kontorova description that accounts for soliton-lattice approximants of the form $(4n+1)/(3n+1)$. Machine-learning-potential calculations of these approximants show an energetically preferred soliton spacing, and their localized misregistry cores are also verified by first-principles relaxations. At finite temperature, the thermally broadened soliton lattice appears as an atomic density wave along the guest chains, consistent with experimental diffraction. This soliton-registry picture provides a microscopic mechanism for host-guest incommensurability in Sb-II.

title: CroCoMAE: Cross-modal self-supervised collaborative representation learning for SAR-optical remote sensing data
text:
Title: CroCoMAE: Cross-modal self-supervised collaborative representation learning for SAR-optical remote sensing data
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Remote sensing increasingly captures the Earth's surface through complementary sensors such as SAR and optical, yet ground-truth annotations remain scarce, limiting supervised approaches. Self-supervised learning (SSL) addresses the label scarcity, and cross-modal SSL further exploits the complementarity between co-located sensors, but existing cross-modal frameworks align modalities mostly through global image-level representations or treat them as largely redundant, leaving their fine-grained complementary structure underexploited. We propose CroCoMAE, a cross-modal SSL framework for SAR-optical remote sensing that unifies contrastive learning and masked image modeling within a ViT-based architecture, operating at two complementary levels. At the image level, an intra-modality contrastive loss on the class token yields globally discriminative, augmentation-invariant representations. At the patch level, masked image modeling drives fine-grained per-modality representations, while a cross-modal contrastive objective aligns a shared subspace across SAR and optical patch tokens, leaving the complementary subspace unconstrained to retain modality-specific information. On two SAR-optical benchmarks covering scene classification and semantic segmentation, CroCoMAE improves over uni-modal SSL baselines and outperforms state-of-the-art cross-modal frameworks in most configurations, with gains in both single-modality and multi-modal evaluation across varying label regimes and the largest improvements on semantic segmentation.

title: Classification of strongly non-hyperbolic critical points of planar second-order chemical reaction systems
text:
Title: Classification of strongly non-hyperbolic critical points of planar second-order chemical reaction systems
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

The dynamics of chemical reaction systems with two chemical species can be described (under mass-action kinetics) by planar autonomous systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with right-hand sides containing polynomials. While their behaviour close to hyperbolic critical points is well understood, their dynamics has not been fully characterized for strongly non-hyperbolic critical points, where the linearization close to the equilibrium is given by the zero matrix. In this paper, the behaviour of such chemical reaction systems is investigated. Considering second-order chemical reaction networks with a positive equilibrium point, we show that only nine geometric equivalence classes are possible out of the sixteen classes for general ODE systems. Examples of chemical reaction networks in each class are presented. All sixteen geometric equivalence classes can be realized by chemical systems if the non-hyperbolic equilibrium point is located at the origin.

title: Time-Reversal Selection Rule for Twist Disorder
text:
Title: Time-Reversal Selection Rule for Twist Disorder
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Random layer rotations are ubiquitous in layered matter, from turbostratic films to rotationally disordered crystals, and strongly suppress transport across the layers. Generated by a symmetry operation, this disorder is absent on the rotation axis, so the thickness laws of conduction are set by how fast backscattering vanishes there. We show that a time-reversal selection rule decides this: each twist harmonic of the interlayer bond is either a frame rotation, whose backscattering cancels, or a coupling change, which scatters. A zero-set theorem turns the rule into universal thickness laws for electrons and phonons, fixed by band-edge symmetry; random twist increments rescale the backscattering but keep its order. Where the axis is unprotected, band nodes provide a second route: a transparent energy with heavy-tailed disorder and an $N^{-3}$ law. A first-principles forward-channel model of black phosphorus shows both routes; its random-twist films act as a symmetry filter that, relative to aligned stacks, retains a hundred times more of the electron than of the hole conductance at 64 layers. The symmetry of band edges and phonon branches thus decides what crosses a disordered stack, making stacking disorder a design element.

title: Perceived Agency During Agent-Avatar Control Transitions in Virtual Reality
text:
Title: Perceived Agency During Agent-Avatar Control Transitions in Virtual Reality
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Prior beliefs about whether a virtual human (VH) is controlled by a human or a computer can shape how users interpret and respond to its behaviour. As emerging hybrid VH systems allow control to transfer between human operators and computer programs during an ongoing interaction, it remains unclear whether perceived agency updates with the actual controller or continues to reflect users' prior beliefs and first impressions. We investigated this question in a within-subject VR study with 24 participants across four conditions: always computer-controlled, computer-to-human, human-to-computer, and always human-controlled. We designed an interaction task in which participants acted as interviewers, asking the VHs a fixed set of questions. Before each interaction, participants were informed whether the VH was human- or computer-controlled, matching the actual controller at the beginning, but were unaware of possible control transitions. We found that perceived agency was strongly influenced by the controller presented at the beginning of the interaction, with no evidence of updating following the control transitions. Social evaluations including likeability and co-presence were generally higher in conditions where human control occurred later and covered a greater proportion of the interaction. The results suggest that prior beliefs and first impressions continued to shape perceived agency, whereas social evaluations were more sensitive to the VH's actual behaviour over the interaction.

title: Strain control of magneto-optical properties of ultra-thin Ni-Mn-Ga films grown by magnetron sputtering
text:
Title: Strain control of magneto-optical properties of ultra-thin Ni-Mn-Ga films grown by magnetron sputtering
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Ultra-thin epitaxial Ni-Mn-Ga films, 10-15 nm thick, were grown by magnetron sputtering on MgO(001), either directly on the substrate or on a Cr buffer, and studied by X-ray diffraction, magnetometry, and magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) spectroscopy. The films were austenitic, with the cubic cell tetragonally distorted in opposite directions. The film on bare MgO was stretched in-plane ($c/a=0.989$) and the film on Cr was compressed in-plane ($c/a=1.021$), while their unit-cell volumes differed by less than $0.3\%$. As the thermal expansion mismatch was expected to stretch the films in-plane in both cases, the opposite distortions were attributed to the lattice misfit. The room-temperature magnetization loops of the two films did not show significant differences, but their polar and longitudinal MOKE spectra differed in the amplitude, sign, and energy of the spectral structures over the whole 0.76-5 eV range. Magneto-optical simulations showed that the absence of the Cr buffer accounted only for the stronger low-energy polar MOKE rotation extremum of the film on MgO. We attributed the other changes to the strain-induced change of the electronic structure, consistent with theoretical predictions in which the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ sub-bands of the minority-spin Ni $e_g$ states exchange their order when the distortion changes sign. In parts of the spectrum, the two films showed Kerr rotation or ellipticity of opposite sign, so the choice of the growth template or a dynamically induced distortion can switch the sign of the magneto-optical response at a given photon energy.

title: Estimating Implicit Expected Log Density Ratios
text:
Title: Estimating Implicit Expected Log Density Ratios
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

When exact probabilities cannot be computed, \emph{density ratio estimation (DRE)} is a key subroutine in the wide range of applications where density ratios appear, from experimental design to generative modelling and reinforcement learning. In this paper, we introduce the concept of an \emph{expected log density ratio (ELDR)}: log density ratios that are integrated under some third, possibly distinct measure. We show many problems with implicit densities where DRE is naïvely used are actually ELDR estimation tasks, and prove fundamental limitations on finite-sample ELDR estimation. Based on these results, we argue that the typical DRE-based approaches are unsuitable for ELDR estimation, and provide some foundational motivation towards bespoke ELDR estimators. To demonstrate, we propose a simple modification to some DRE methods that allows samples convergent to the integral distribution to appear in training data. We show through benchmarks that this can improve ELDR estimation error.

title: Ultralight scalar field domain walls and Galileo GNSS atomic clocks
text:
Title: Ultralight scalar field domain walls and Galileo GNSS atomic clocks
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

In this article, we study the impact of an Earth-sized ultralight scalar field domain wall (DW) on the European Galileo Global Navigation Satellite System constellation and the feasibility of a related detection. In particular, a set of statistical procedures is developed and implemented to characterize the statistical properties of the background noise for a subnetwork of $N$ Galileo satellite clocks, including a false-alarm rate estimation and a detection efficiency analysis. These methods allow to implement a coincidence analysis and establish a preliminary statistical framework for a robust and controlled search for domain-wall crossings in clock data, and for deriving constraints on the associated fundamental particle physics parameters. The activity is addressed from the point of view of the scientific objectives of the Galileo for Science (G4S$\_2.0$) project.

title: CuAD: Source-to-Source Automatic Differentiation of CUDA Kernels for Discrete Adjoints in Computational Fluid Dynamics
text:
Title: CuAD: Source-to-Source Automatic Differentiation of CUDA Kernels for Discrete Adjoints in Computational Fluid Dynamics
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Discrete adjoint methods give the sensitivities that aerodynamic design and data assimilation require, but they remain hard to obtain for flow solvers that run on graphics processors. This paper presents CuAD, a source-to-source automatic differentiation tool that reads CUDA kernels and writes their tangent and adjoint versions as ordinary CUDA source. Its reverse mode is organised around the GPU thread. It adopts the convention of CUDA kernels that inputs and outputs do not alias, recomputes intermediate values instead of storing them, differentiates pure accumulations without a tape and keeps any remaining tape in a fixed thread-local array. We evaluate CuAD on four kernels from simple flow models and on a two-dimensional Euler solver. All generated derivatives pass dot-product tests to round-off, and the adjoint kernels cost two to six times the primal kernels. On a Biot-Savart summation compiled by one compiler, the CuAD adjoint costs about four times the primal at every size, as does Enzyme when the source declares the absence of aliasing with __restrict__. On the unchanged source Enzyme caches the loop in the device heap and costs 9 to 240 times the primal, while the heap tape of Clad costs 60 to 4400 times the primal and fails beyond 8192 vortices. Exact Jacobians assembled from the generated tangents also matter for accuracy. In single precision, the adjoint gradient of a finite-difference Jacobian reaches errors of 45 to 75 per cent on a stiff Burgers problem and of $5\times10^{-4}$ to $4\times10^{-2}$ on a transonic airfoil, whereas the generated Jacobian keeps them below $5\times10^{-5}$ and $3\times10^{-6}$. The applications include the shape sensitivities of lift and drag of a transonic NACA 0012, for which the residual, the boundary conditions and the wall force are differentiated by CuAD and the adjoint agrees with the tangent to $10^{-13}$.

title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
text:
Title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

title: Obscured Wildfire Flame Detection by Spatio-temporal Analysis of Smoke Patterns Using Frame-wise Transformers
text:
Title: Obscured Wildfire Flame Detection by Spatio-temporal Analysis of Smoke Patterns Using Frame-wise Transformers
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

In this paper, we propose a new paradigm in wildfire management for detecting both visible and obscured fire using Deep Learning (DL). The essence of our method is the joint spatial and temporal analysis of RGB videos, embracing the fact that temporal patterns of smoke motions in consecutive video frames can indicate obscured fire flames. This perspective contrasts the traditional approach of independently analyzing images and individual video frames. To this end, we propose a frame-wise transformer architecture that applies an attention mechanism between the consecutive frames while preserving spatial information within frames as opposed to regular attention mechanisms like the non-local block, which combines spatial and temporal information into a single vector. We also optimize the temporal pattern lengths under different spatial resolutions to achieve the highest performance while reducing the computational cost. To investigate the applicability of our method in aerial image processing, we applied it to a curated version of the FLAME2 dataset that includes dual-mode RGB/IR videos. The IR video feed is used to extract ground truth, while the model is trained only on RGB videos to maintain applicability to lowcost commercial drones (which are equipped only with regular cameras) and facilitate processing existing RGB-only datasets. Our proposed method achieves a Segmentation Foreground Dice score of 92.61%, an Object Detection Precision and Recall rate of 93.21% and 91.73%, and clip-level classification accuracy of 98.02%, respectively. We also investigated the efficacy and generalizability of our method through ablation study

title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
text:
Title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.

title: MuCO: Generative Peptide Cyclization Empowered by Multi-stage Conformation Optimization
text:
Title: MuCO: Generative Peptide Cyclization Empowered by Multi-stage Conformation Optimization
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Modeling peptide cyclization is critical for the virtual screening of candidate peptides with desirable physical and pharmaceutical properties. This task is challenging because a cyclic peptide often exhibits diverse, ring-shaped conformations, which cannot be well captured by deterministic prediction models derived from linear peptide folding. In this study, we propose MuCO (Multi-stage Conformation Optimization), a generative peptide cyclization method that models the distribution of cyclic peptide conformations conditioned on the corresponding linear peptide. In principle, MuCO decouples the peptide cyclization task into three stages: topology-aware backbone design, generative side-chain packing, and physics-aware all-atom optimization, thereby generating and optimizing conformations of cyclic peptides in a coarse-to-fine manner. This multi-stage framework enables an efficient parallel sampling strategy for conformation generation and allows for rapid exploration of diverse, low-energy conformations. Experiments on the large-scale CPSea dataset demonstrate that MuCO significantly and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in physical stability, structural diversity, secondary structure recovery, and computational efficiency, making it a promising computational tool for exploring and designing cyclic peptides. The demo of the proposed method can be found at https://github.com/mianqiu00/MuCO.

title: Curriculum proof repair with learned counterexamples
text:
Title: Curriculum proof repair with learned counterexamples
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Language models (LMs) have substantially lowered the barrier to applying formal verification for building reliable and secure software. Existing approaches commonly follow the verifier-in-the-loop paradigm, but the verifier often provides only coarse, binary pass/fail feedback, which offers little actionable signal on how the proof should be repaired. Recent work shows that counterexamples provide more actionable feedback by grounding proof failures in concrete program states, but generating useful ones at inference time requires costly iterative refinement. We present TopoVerus, an LM-based framework for Verus proof repair that internalizes counterexample-guided diagnosis as a model capability, producing useful counterexamples in a single pass. Our key insight is to train counterexample generation not as a standalone validation task, but as a data-driven diagnostic objective: a counterexample is useful when conditioning on it helps the model produce a safe, verifier-passing proof. Given a failed Verus proof and verifier error, TopoVerus generates a structured source-level counterexample, repair rationale, and repaired proof in one trajectory, optimized with reinforcement learning from Verus feedback and a proof-code safety gate. To guide the order of invariant repairs, TopoVerus introduces a curriculum with a topological graph reward based on invariant dependencies derived from inductiveness tests, which encourages counterexample generation to follow the same topological order. Across seven Verus benchmarks with 471 problems, TopoVerus achieves 61.6%/72.2% weighted-average Safe-Pass@1/Safe-Pass@3, outperforming the strongest baseline, Claude Sonnet 4.5, by 5.7/6.3 points. We also show that TopoVerus's learned counterexamples can directly augment the reasoning of existing LM-based proof repair approaches, improving their success rate by 64.3% compared to chain-of-thought diagnostics.

title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
text:
Title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to propose DNA sequences and edits. But successful design requires capabilities that current benchmarks do not measure. Here we introduce BEND 2.0 (BENchmark for DNA language models), which tests how well models predict the effects of DNA changes and whether these predictions can guide sequence design. Across eight tasks built on five experimental datasets, we find that model choice and how representations are accessed both affect performance. Linear readouts fitted to frozen representations can match or exceed models' native outputs, and functional post-training substantially improves the models' capabilities. Linear readouts transfer well across experimental assays and genes, suggesting that models capture functional patterns beyond the data used to fit individual predictors. At the same time, strong prediction of average effects can conceal weaker prediction of context-specific effects, and accurate prediction of combined mutation effects does not imply accurate prediction of their interactions. In design tasks, model predictions can reduce the number of candidates needed to find a desired response, but still leave substantial room for better design choices, particularly for context-specific and multi-cell objectives. Our benchmark reveals that genomic models now display signs of general utility but have yet to saturate on performance in even simple tasks.

title: Representational Alignment between Deep Neural Networks and Human Brain in Speech Processing under Audiovisual Noise
text:
Title: Representational Alignment between Deep Neural Networks and Human Brain in Speech Processing under Audiovisual Noise
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Speech comprehension in the human brain is an incremental process that begins with acoustic processing and advances to linguistic processing. While recent studies have revealed that the hierarchy of deep neural networks (DNNs) correlates with the ascending auditory pathway, the exact nature of this DNN-brain alignment remains underexplored. In this study, we investigate how DNN representations align with the brain's acoustic-to-linguistic processing. Specifically, we employed neural encoding models to simulate neural responses to acoustic (i.e., speech and noise envelope) and linguistic features (i.e., word onset and surprisal). By applying representational similarity analysis (RSA), we quantified the similarity between these neural responses and the DNN embeddings generated by a pre-trained automatic speech recognition (ASR) model, both before and after fine-tuning on audiovisual noisy data. Our results demonstrate significant DNN-brain alignment: embeddings from shallow layers exhibit higher similarity to neural responses associated with acoustic features, while those from deeper layers align more closely with neural responses related to linguistic features. Importantly, the fine-tuning process enhances this alignment by improving noise processing in shallower layers and refining linguistic representations in deeper layers. These results suggest that fine-tuned DNN models can naturally develop human-like processing patterns in noisy environments, highlighting a functional alignment between the human brain and DNNs in speech representation.

title: Localizing binary neutron stars with the Einstein Telescope: a full Bayesian comparison of the triangular and 2L configurations
text:
Title: Localizing binary neutron stars with the Einstein Telescope: a full Bayesian comparison of the triangular and 2L configurations
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The Einstein Telescope (ET), the European next-generation gravitational-wave observatory, is at a decisive stage: the choice of its detector configuration is still open, with profound implications for its scientific output. We provide a quantitative basis for this choice by comparing two candidate configurations at their proposed sites: the triangular design ($Δ$) at the Euregio Meuse-Rhine site, and the 2L design, with interferometers in Sardinia, Italy, and Lusatia, Germany. We present the first realistic estimates of sky-localization uncertainties for binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, moving beyond Fisher-matrix forecasts to full Bayesian parameter estimation that captures the multimodal structure of the sky posterior. We focus mainly on the high-frequency interferometers alone, providing an expected scenario for the first years of ET operations, as the more challenging low-frequency instruments will come online later. BNS injections span different sky positions and luminosity distances between 40 and 2000 Mpc, corresponding to signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) from 12 to 720. Our analysis relaxes the long-wavelength approximation and includes Earth's rotation and higher-order modes, all of which improve sky localization. We find that the $Δ$ configuration localizes low- and moderate-SNR sources in eight degenerate sky modes spread across both hemispheres and over the day and night sides of the Earth, with 90% credible areas reaching $\sim 2 \times 10^4 \, \mathrm{deg}^2$. In contrast, the 2L configuration recovers a single dominant mode that contains at least 50% of the posterior probability and is one to two orders of magnitude smaller in area. This represents a substantial advantage for multimessenger follow-up campaigns.

title: CORAL: A Modality Invariant Framework for Robust Vital Sign Rate Estimation Using Correloform Analysis
text:
Title: CORAL: A Modality Invariant Framework for Robust Vital Sign Rate Estimation Using Correloform Analysis
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Heart rate and respiration rate are crucial vital signs. We present CORAL to address challenges in automating continuous vital sign monitoring 1) in-hospital across broader populations (age, disease states), 2) at-home in telehealth and wellbeing applications (noise, placement), and 3) across data modalities (ECG, PPG, SCG, BioZ, etc.). We re-introduce Short-Time Autocorrelation Functions (STACFs) to introduce the correloform - a highly interpretable 2D signal transformation for tracking periodicity over time - and define CORAL as a generic analytical framework for robust rate estimation of quasi-periodic signals. We rigorously benchmark CORAL to show ubiquitous application in biosignals via capabilities arising by mathematical construction rather than domain-specific engineering, including rate estimation, resilient noise handling, automatic channel selection, and signal quality indication. CORAL achieves excellent instantaneous noninvasive fetal HR agreement in FECGSYNDB (F1 = 0.999) and ADFECGDB (F1 = 1.000). With difficult NICU neonates, CORAL estimates RR from wearable BioZ at r = 0.858 against breath-interval RR from simultaneous wired Philips impedance. CORAL SCG HR on CEBS achieves r = 0.990 and in free-living activity r = 0.970 when compared against commercial ECG. Without QRS detection, CORAL's instantaneous HR agrees with Pan-Tompkins and NeuroKit2 detectors as closely as they agree with each other (MIMIC-IV ICU ECG r = 0.87 to each vs. 0.88 between them). CORAL's HR standard deviation correlates strongly with interval-based HRV SDNN, even from mechanical SCG (CEBS r = 0.733) and across an ICU ECG cohort (r = 0.768).

title: Measurement-angle control of a continuously monitored quantum oscillator: purification limits and optimal protocols
text:
Title: Measurement-angle control of a continuously monitored quantum oscillator: purification limits and optimal protocols
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study the dynamic purification of a continuously monitored quantum harmonic oscillator coupled to a thermal bath, where the control is the quadrature measurement angle of up to two detectors with prescribed strengths and efficiencies. Within the Gaussian regime, the conditional state covariance obeys a deterministic Riccati equation, and we ask what purity can be reached and sustained by manipulating the angle in time, in analogy with rapid-purification protocols for qubits. We propose, analyze, and compare constant-rate, greedy, vibrational, and variational monitoring strategies on the basis of sustained purity starting from the thermal bath state, and quantify to what extent they are able to maintain higher purity levels compared to lab-fixed or phase-locked detectors. We highlight structural features, operational limits, and optimal protocols from each strategy and study how model parameters shape control performance. We observe that in the absence of measurement-frame anisotropy, the time-dependent strategies achieve higher but similar performance. Once this symmetry is broken, their performances diverge, either improving or worsening depending on the relative timescales of oscillator dynamics, thermalization, and measurement.

title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence
text:
Title: Deterministic, Reproducible Inference in Exact Integer Arithmetic, and Verifiable Distributed Inference as Its Consequence
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Optimized floating-point inference is not reproducible across environments: the same model on different hardware, compilers or thread counts can produce different bits. We present tritify, an open-source runtime that executes the forward pass of real models -- decoder-only language models, Mixture-of-Experts decoders, and the Segment Anything 2.1 image/video stack -- with the entire run-time path in exact integer arithmetic; floating point is confined to offline quantization and the float reference used for verification. We make three separate claims and verify each. (1) Cross-hardware reproducibility: the integer path produces bit-identical output run to run, across CPU instruction-set architectures, and across CPU/GPU, carried by a reproducing SHA-256 of the output. (2) Decision fidelity: the integer path reproduces the float reference's decision on the models and inputs tested, with the numeric exceptions measured; per-layer fidelity through sixteen layers of OLMoE-1B-7B and of a 106-billion-parameter MoE shows no fidelity cliff. (3) Location independence: a model's computation can be split across instruction sets, CPU and GPU, and networked machines with zero effect on the output bits. GLM-4.5-Air (106,852,251,264 parameters, 427 GB of integer codes) generated its answer across three machines, none of which can hold its integer codes in RAM, bit-identically to a single-host reference. The consequence is verifiable distributed inference: an untrusted server or a fleet of devices runs the model while an open scalar oracle re-derives the exact bytes; a guarantee against a dishonest server is future work. We do not claim a per-device speed-up, bit-equality of floating-valued intermediates, or confidentiality. Code: https://github.com/pelloran-inc/tritify

title: Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation
text:
Title: Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

On-policy distillation (OPD) reduces train-inference distribution mismatch by supervising a student on its own trajectories. For multi-turn tool-use agents, conditioning the teacher on a validated same-task successful trajectory as a reference can provide useful hindsight, but different successes may reach incompatible interaction states and offer misleading supervision. We cast successful-reference selection as a free-target optimal transport problem, which reduces to assigning each failed trajectory its most compatible successful reference. Because latent state paths are hidden, we use action-sequence alignment as an observable proxy for compatibility and instantiate it with longest common subsequence (LCS), which identifies a shared ordered backbone of actions while allowing recoverable detours. This perspective makes trajectory compatibility the central criterion for reference selection in multi-turn OPD. Experiments on ALFWorld and the airline domain of $τ^3$-bench show that LCS is the only evaluated reference selector to improve over reference-free OPD on both ALFWorld overall scores and all three airline metrics. Without further optimization, the airline-trained models also transfer to the retail domain, where LCS improves all three metrics.

title: Chaos on the mass shell
text:
Title: Chaos on the mass shell
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We study particle production in high-energy states for theories given by an RG flow between an asymptotically free or conformal theory in the UV and a massive theory in the IR. Using the framework of detector matching, we argue that distributions of produced particles satisfy universal evolution equations with energy, determined by the spectrum of light-ray operators of the UV theory. In particular, we interpret the UV Chew-Frautschi plot as a wave equation for particle densities on the mass shell, evolving with energy. (When the UV theory is a CFT, this wave equation is the same one that controls the spread of chaos in hyperbolic space at a particular temperature.) We test these ideas for integrable flows in 2d CFTs, finding an independent derivation of the evolution equations in terms of the thermodynamics of a Feynman gas. We also discuss consequences for 4d gauge theories, including the presence of a BFKL contrail produced by an outgoing wave of hadron number density.

title: Conditional stopping guarantees for a folded parametrization of reduced Stokes vectors
text:
Title: Conditional stopping guarantees for a folded parametrization of reduced Stokes vectors
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Stopping decisions made in parametrization coordinates need not certify physically accurate estimates. We establish conditional stopping guarantees for a folded parametrization of reduced Stokes vectors, including partial linear polarization. For strongly convex physical objectives on the bounded-intensity inner sheet, normalized first derivatives and one radial lower-curvature test give an explicit objective-gap bound with sharp tolerance orders $\varepsilon^{4/3}+ν^2$. The guarantee requires neither prior localization near an optimum nor a positive-semidefinite head Hessian. Its information basis is an exact recovery identity: one signed radial curvature restores the physical-gradient component lost at the fully linearly polarized fold, without stationarity or knowledge of the physical Hessian. For a nominal quadratic model, an outward-rounded implementation certifies a gap of at most $10^{-6}$ for 8,861 of 9,284 stored endpoints; it rejects all 295 historical false successes and 128 accurate endpoints. The full 128-fractional-bit pass takes 7.32 seconds and includes 52 scalar curvature evaluations. Controlled fits and released observations distinguish stopping certification from local fold diagnosis and subsequent coordinate repair. Twenty shared-network fits contain no saved near-fold negative-curvature candidates, and direct physical solvers are cheaper on the tested quadratics.

title: Out of Parameters, Saved by Syntax: UD-PrMPT for Parser Augmented Low Resource Machine Translation
text:
Title: Out of Parameters, Saved by Syntax: UD-PrMPT for Parser Augmented Low Resource Machine Translation
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Recent work advancing machine translation quality using LLMs for very low resource languages has relied on the injection of lexicon-based prompt components to expose vocabulary to models. However, these approaches run into a ceiling when models must guess sentence meaning purely from plausible combinations of possible word senses mapped to strings. In this paper we test UD-PrMPT, an approach using syntactic analyses in the Universal Dependencies formalism as prompt components to improve MT in five diverse low resource languages: Beja, Chintang, Chukchi, Coptic, and Xibe. Our results show additive improvements which stack on top of the lexicon based approach which are stronger for higher quality manual analyses but consistent for predicted parses as well.

title: When precise inference is wrong: Diagnosing model misspecification with applications to cosmic dawn and reionisation
text:
Title: When precise inference is wrong: Diagnosing model misspecification with applications to cosmic dawn and reionisation
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

As observations of the cosmic dawn (CD) and epoch of reionisation (EoR) rapidly improve in precision, the approximate forward models used to interpret them might struggle to keep pace. Bayesian inference with a misspecified model, one that cannot represent the processes generating the observations, can yield tightly constrained, yet misleading and biased astrophysics, with different parts of the observations favouring incompatible parameter values. Model misspecification can evade a $χ^2$ goodness-of-fit test, and Bayesian model selection requires a better model, which is not always available. We therefore apply the suspiciousness, a statistic developed to quantify tensions between datasets, to CD/EoR inference as a model criticism tool that tests whether these parts can be explained by the same parameters. We first apply it to HERA 21-cm power spectrum (PS) upper limits, which are too weak to reveal misspecification, as expected, and to HST and JWST UV luminosity functions (LFs). Under our galaxy model, the UV LFs at $z\leq10$ and $z>10$ are in tension at $5.0σ$ in the Gaussian limit, a failure visible in the fits, although doubling the uncertainties of the $z>10$ observations reduces it to $2.1σ$. Finally, we analyse a mock SKA-Low AA$^\ast$ 1080 h 21-cm PS with the model that generated it and with a simpler, misspecified model. We find that the misspecified model silently fails: it fits the PS well, passing visual inspection and, for most noise realisations, a $χ^2$ test, yet its inferred astrophysics is wrong. The Bayesian evidence disfavours it, but only relative to the true model, which is unavailable for real observations. The suspiciousness finds no tension for the well-specified model, but a $\sim3.4σ$ tension for the misspecified one, strongly ruling it out without requiring a more adequate candidate model.

title: Learning qBIC Resonances across Metasurface Families in Dielectric Fourier Space
text:
Title: Learning qBIC Resonances across Metasurface Families in Dielectric Fourier Space
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Bound states in the continuum (BIC) metasurfaces are typically described by geometry-specific parameters, hindering cross-geometry comparison, while ultranarrow quasi-BIC (qBIC) features are easily diluted in full-spectrum learning. Here, we map 2,015 samples from seven dielectric metasurface families onto a shared reciprocal-lattice grid. Two fixed low-order Fourier descriptors capture within-branch resonance shifts, with mean $R^2$ values of 0.871-0.999. Field-level analysis of two representative branches shows that these shifts are consistent with the Maxwell-Fourier perturbation picture. A five-channel Fourier-space backbone models the broadband spectrum. A local resonance expert uses complex Fourier coefficients to parameterize the qBIC resonance through a differentiable Fano layer. The expert reduces resonance-position mean absolute error (MAE) from 3.2 to 0.95 nm and reduces the minimum-transmission MAE by a factor of 14 on a geometry-blocked test set. The same coordinate supports spectrum-to-structure reconstruction.

title: Specializing Meta Multi-Objectivization as Baseline for Software Engineering Optimization
text:
Title: Specializing Meta Multi-Objectivization as Baseline for Software Engineering Optimization
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Given the discrete nature of many software engineering (SE) optimization problems, trapping at local optima remains a crucial issue in the optimizer designs. Meta Multi-Objectivization (MMO) is an optimization model for overcoming local optima by introducing an extra, auxiliary objective. Yet, MMO is originally designed only for configuration tuning, leaving its suitability for other SE problems in doubt, particularly regarding the choice of the auxiliary objective. In this paper, we study the possibility and resolution for specializing MMO as a general baseline across a range of SE optimization problems, making it a fundamental counterpart for future SE optimizers that seek to mitigate the issue of local optima. We do so by providing both theoretical remit and empirical evidence: we analytically show how the choice of the auxiliary objective is crucial while demonstrating the effectiveness of MMO under nine SE optimization problems comprising 212 cases when the right one can be chosen, i.e., MMO is able to outperform the other state-of-the-art and general-purpose optimizers in 79% and 94% of the cases, respectively. Drawing on the theoretical understanding and empirical findings, we then propose L2RAC, a tool that automatically recommends the best auxiliary objective choice for a given SE problem/case, hence helping to specialize MMO therein. Through extensive experiments, we reveal that, in general, L2RAC can more accurately rank the choice of auxiliary objective for MMO under a case than other guesses by up to 60%, saving as much as 99% of the cost that would otherwise be required to conduct trial-and-error when using MMO.

title: Quantum Noise Engineering in Advanced LIGO
text:
Title: Quantum Noise Engineering in Advanced LIGO
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Advanced LIGO is a gravitational-wave detector with extreme sensitivity, operating close to the quantum limits of optical measurement. The quantum noise in this system arises from vacuum fluctuations entering the interferometer readout port: phase-like fluctuations produce measurement imprecision, while amplitude-like fluctuations drive radiation-pressure back-action. In this review, we present an intuitive description in terms of complex fields and quadratures, and follow squeezed vacuum from its generation, through its interaction with the filter cavity and propagation through the interferometer, to the readout. We discuss how frequency-independent and frequency-dependent squeezing engineer quantum noise, and how correlations between optical quadratures map onto correlations between measurement imprecision and back-action. We conclude that LIGO is both a gravitational-wave observatory and a kilometre-scale platform for quantum measurement science.

title: Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning
text:
Title: Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization estimates descent directions from function values alone, which removes the activation storage required by backpropagation and makes it attractive for memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). Existing low-rank ZO methods either parameterize the additive update through Euclidean factors with a non-unique representation, or restrict each finite-difference direction to be low-rank. In this work, we propose to constrain each additive update block to a fixed-rank matrix manifold while keeping the pretrained weights frozen, so the learned update remains rank-constrained throughout fine-tuning. On this geometry, we build a Riemannian ZO gradient estimator that projects a random matrix onto the tangent space, normalizes it to correct the scale mismatch induced by projection, and further propose Zeroth-order Riemannian Gradient Descent (ZO-RGD) and its smoothed variant, ZO-RGD-S. We show that the ambient finite difference matches its retracted counterpart, the normalized estimator recovers the Riemannian gradient in expectation, and ZO-RGD converges under trajectory-regularity conditions. Experiments on LLM fine-tuning tasks show that the proposed algorithms are competitive with strong forward-only baselines across model families and tasks, with gains in several settings.

title: Exact (Non-)Accelerations of Heavy-Ball Discretizations
text:
Title: Exact (Non-)Accelerations of Heavy-Ball Discretizations
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Momentum methods with the same slow dynamics can have different worst-case rates on smooth strongly convex functions. We identify a half-step phase barrier in the gradient query that governs this difference. For momentum with extrapolation $τ_κ\toτ$, $β=1-θ/\sqrtκ+o(κ^{-1/2})$ and $hL\to y$, where $κ=L/μ$ and $θ,y>0$, the exact uniform distance factor is $1-c/\sqrtκ+o(κ^{-1/2})$, with $c=\min\{θ/3,c_Q(θ,y)\}$, when $τ>1/2$ and $y(1+2τ)<4$; $c_Q$ is the slowest quadratic decay exponent. Quadratically accelerated families with $\limsupτ_κ<1/2$ have divergent trajectories on the full function class. Upper bounds use finite-lag certificates: nonnegative combinations of inequalities for values and gradients at finitely separated query points, together with comparisons to the minimizer. For any prescribed accuracy, spiral mixtures or quadratic trajectories of one finite-dimensional objective give matching lower bounds at all iteration horizons. We resolve the parameter layer near $τ=1/2$ and classify all tunings of this family attaining the optimal leading constant 1. The flow also bounds the leading constant of every second-order stationary linear family with the same slow parameters $(θ,y)$ and fixed finite memory.

title: Direct calculation of dipole moment surfaces through second-order symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for properties
text:
Title: Direct calculation of dipole moment surfaces through second-order symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for properties
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Interaction-induced dipole moment surfaces are vital for calculating line intensities and collision-induced absorption coefficients for van der Waals complexes. We introduce the perturbative corrections, of second order with respect to the interaction operator, to the dipole moment (or, in general, any one-electron property) change due to noncovalent interactions. These are obtained in the spirit of the symmetry-adapted perturbation theory for properties (propSAPT) method, developed recently by some of us [B. Tyrcha et al., JCTC 21(9), 4562--4578 (2025)]. When orbital relaxation effects due to the external property field are properly introduced, these can be understood as analytical derivatives of the second-order SAPT interaction energies. We apply the newly introduced formalism to calculations of dipole moment surfaces for three light van der Waals complexes: He...Ar, He...H$_2$ and the H$_2$ dimer. The propSAPT method is compared against finite-field SAPT calculations and finite-field supermolecular CCSD(T) as the reference.

title: HyFlash: A Prefix-Memory Prior for On-Device Speculative Decoding
text:
Title: HyFlash: A Prefix-Memory Prior for On-Device Speculative Decoding
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Parallel block drafting accelerates speculative decoding by predicting multiple future positions in a single backbone pass, but on-device deployment constrains both drafter capacity and context storage. Under tight memory budgets, drafters must model long-range dependencies and fine-grained draft-position interactions without the growing KV-cache overhead of full-context attention. We propose HyFlash, a compact parallel drafter that introduces a prefix-memory prior to separate long-range context modeling from fine-grained draft-position interactions with limited capacity. Local attention captures recent context and draft-position interactions, while recurrent memory compresses historical target features into fixed-size states. This inductive bias enables effective local and long-range modeling with bounded draft-side memory. Experiments show that HyFlash achieves higher acceptance than full-context attention with substantially less KV storage and with larger gains for shallow drafters and long contexts.

title: General Time-Dependent Surface Flux for Multiple Ionization and Fragmentation of Molecules. I: General Theory
text:
Title: General Time-Dependent Surface Flux for Multiple Ionization and Fragmentation of Molecules. I: General Theory
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We introduce a method for efficiently computing multiple photofragmentation of atoms and molecules into photoelectrons and nuclear fragments. The method is a generalization of the time-dependent surface flux originally introduced for single and double photoionization.

title: Minimal Reflected BSDEs and Superhedging of Irregular American Claims
text:
Title: Minimal Reflected BSDEs and Superhedging of Irregular American Claims
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study the superhedging of American claims with an irregular optional payoff process $ξ$ over the full set $\mathcal{M}(X)$ of equivalent local martingale measures of a locally bounded market. We show that a process which is a strong optional supermartingale of class (D) under every $Q\in\mathcal{M}(X)$, with no bound from either side, decomposes as $S=S_0+\int H\,dX-A-C_-$, with a common integrand $H$, a right-continuous increasing process $A$ and a purely discontinuous increasing process $C$ given explicitly by the right jumps of $S$. For the robust Snell envelope this yields the superhedging duality $p_0(ξ)=\sup_{Q}\sup_τE^Q[ξ_τ]$ with an explicit optimal strategy and no regularity of $ξ$ in time. Unbounded payoffs are covered when $\{ξ_τ\}$ is uniformly integrable jointly over measures and stopping times, or when $|ξ|$ is dominated by a traded uniformly integrable martingale. For payoffs bounded below, the price is attained by wealth bounded below by a constant. For payoffs unbounded below this can fail, already in a complete market, and the price is attained once the constant bound is replaced by $-M$, with $M$ a traded martingale dominating $|ξ|$. In an incomplete Brownian market we study the associated reflected BSDE with an optional obstacle and a Lipschitz driver depending on the value. We prove existence and uniqueness of the minimal supersolution, a representation at stopping times, comparison and an equivalent dynamic minimality condition, for bounded data and for data dominated by a traded martingale. For a European-type obstacle, the Skorokhod conditions on the total regulator hold for some supersolution if and only if the terminal claim is attainable by a bounded wealth process; so in an incomplete market some data admit no supersolution satisfying them, while the right-jump regulator always satisfies its contact condition.

title: A concentration-independent paradigm rendering weak interactions inherently quantifiable
text:
Title: A concentration-independent paradigm rendering weak interactions inherently quantifiable
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

A vast class of weak, millimolar-affinity molecular interactions governs cellular function, yet their quantitative characterization has remained largely beyond conventional methods. For over a century, biochemistry has worked within a concentration-based framework where molarity scales with molecular number per volume (N/V), and experiments have usually, often implicitly, changed concentration by moving N while holding V fixed. The weak-interaction measurement bottleneck arises from this paradigm: reading weak binding through bulk concentration requires concentrations beyond practical limits, a framework constraint rather than one of instrumental sensitivity. Here we show that shifting experimental control from N to accessible volume V overcomes this bottleneck and opens previously intractable affinity ranges through nanoscale spatial confinement. Controlling V means controlling what biochemists have called "local concentration" and "proximity effects," recasting these long-ambiguous notions as quantitative variables grounded in first principles. Implemented in DNA nanocavities, the approach showed that geometric arrangement alone can override solution-phase binding hierarchies. The same spatial control quantified a protein-peptide interaction of order 10 mM from femtomoles per well, totalling under a picomole per titration. Even so, a standard plate reader gave a signal-to-noise ratio near 10^3, leaving headroom for still weaker interactions. The affinity-and-geometry readout also enabled rational screening for protein-protein-interaction modulators, identifying compounds that enhance weak associations by reweighting local encounters rather than binding tightly on their own or forming a stable ternary complex. Together, this volume-based paradigm and its implementation provide a general strategy for probing and modulating previously inaccessible biochemical phenomena.

title: A Quantum Reservoir for Neurodynamical Forecasting
text:
Title: A Quantum Reservoir for Neurodynamical Forecasting
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Forecasting neural activity from short recordings remains a fundamental challenge. Reservoir computing may offer an efficient paradigm for temporal prediction, however classical reservoirs typically underperform in small-data regimes. Here we investigate whether quantum reservoir computing (QRC) can help overcome this limitation. Building on recent advances, we introduce a quantum reservoir based on a transverse-field Ising model, combined with heterogeneous quantum measurements and polynomial ridge regression. On a standard benchmark task, results show that the quantum reservoir outperforms a classical counterpart overall, with prediction accuracy strongly dependent on reservoir parameters. We further demonstrate feasibility by running the same task on quantum hardware. To assess performance on biological signals, we evaluate QRC on simulated human electroencephalography (EEG) data with a parallel reservoir architecture. On this challenging task, the tested quantum reservoir did not match the performance of the classical one, but it produced stable, convergent predictions. This is a meaningful first step toward forecasting of biologically realistic neural data using a quantum reservoir. Overall, our findings indicate that although current quantum hardware and parallel reservoir architectures do not yet surpass classical methods on complex neural signals, QRC can be executed on near-term devices and does converge with realistic EEG-like data. This work establishes a practical baseline for future algorithmic and hardware developments aimed at clinical time-series forecasting with quantum systems.

title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks
text:
Title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Simulation-based Bayesian inference for Chemical Reaction Networks (CRNs) must simultaneously solve two computationally demanding problems: discriminating between overlapping reaction pathways and estimating reaction rate constants. Classical approaches, such as Sequential Monte Carlo ABC, rely on handcrafted summary statistics and scale poorly across large parameter spaces. To overcome this, we introduce a neural inference architecture. Our pipeline utilizes shared 1D-CNNs and a permutation-invariant Set Attention mechanism to learn low-dimensional summary statistics from variable-length, multi-experiment time-series data. These statistics simultaneously condition a model selection network to compute posterior model probabilities and model-specific conditional Invertible Neural Networks (cINNs) that estimate parameter posterior distributions. We demonstrate the practical utility of our approach on a real protodeboronation example, illustrating how it handles structural ambiguity and extracts kinetic parameters from competing catalyst deactivation pathways.

title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
text:
Title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Sampling from the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model is a fundamental problem in statistical physics and approximate counting. Although computationally hard in the worst case, sampling is expected to be efficient throughout the high-temperature uniqueness regime of the model using the natural single-site Glauber dynamics. We establish fast mixing bounds for every $q$, in the full high-temperature regimes in the two central graph families on $n$ vertices. (1) For every $Δ\ge 3$, the Potts Glauber dynamics mixes in $n\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps with high probability on a uniformly random $Δ$-regular graph for all $β<β_u(q,\mathbb T_Δ)$ where $β_u(q,\mathbb T_Δ)$ is the uniqueness threshold on the $Δ$-regular tree; (2) For every $d\ge 2$, the Potts Glauber dynamics has inverse spectral gap $n^{1+o(1)}$ on cubes or tori in $\mathbb Z^d$ for all $β<β_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ where $β_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ is the critical point on $\mathbb Z^d$. Both temperature thresholds are sharp as the Glauber dynamics slows down exponentially above them. These results overcome the challenge of bounding mixing times without access to correlation decay bounds in the presence of pinnings (i.e., without spectral independence or strong spatial mixing). For this purpose, our proof introduces a new dichotomy principle: throughout the high-temperature regime, any initial spin distribution is either such that its pinnings ensure good correlation decay, or Glauber dynamics escapes from that distribution quickly. We expect this kind of dichotomy to have further applications. As a demonstration, we also develop its analog for random-cluster dynamics and use it to prove that Swendsen-Wang dynamics on random $Δ$-regular graphs mixes in $O(\log n)$ time throughout uniqueness. The results in this paper were arrived at with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 and 6.

title: Pharmacology Knowledge Graphs: Do We Need Chemical Structure for Drug Repurposing?
text:
Title: Pharmacology Knowledge Graphs: Do We Need Chemical Structure for Drug Repurposing?
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The contributions of model complexity, data volume, and feature modalities to knowledge graph-based drug repurposing remain poorly quantified under rigorous temporal validation. We constructed a pharmacology knowledge graph from ChEMBL 36 comprising 5,348 entities including 3,127 drugs, 1,156 proteins, and 1,065 indications. A strict temporal split was enforced with training data up to 2022 and testing data from 2023 to 2025, together with biologically verified hard negatives mined from failed assays and clinical trials. We benchmarked five knowledge graph embedding models and a standard graph neural network with 3.44 million parameters that incorporates drug chemical structure using a graph attention encoder and ESM-2 protein embeddings. Scaling experiments ranging from 0.78 to 9.75 million parameters and from 25 to 100 percent of the data, together with feature ablation studies, were used to isolate the contributions of model capacity, graph density, and node feature modalities. Removing the graph attention based drug structure encoder and retaining only topological embeddings combined with ESM-2 protein features improved drug protein PR-AUC from 0.5631 to 0.5785 while reducing VRAM usage from 5.30 GB to 353 MB. Replacing the drug encoder with Morgan fingerprints further degraded performance, indicating that explicit chemical structure representations can be detrimental for predicting pharmacological network interactions. Increasing model size beyond 2.44 million parameters yielded diminishing returns, whereas increasing training data consistently improved performance. External validation confirmed 6 of the top 14 novel predictions as established therapeutic indications. These results show that drug pharmacological behavior can be accurately predicted using target-centric information and drug network topology alone, without requiring explicit chemical structure representations.

title: Modular and Looping Quantum Photonic Processing Unit for Quantum Computing
text:
