With nonlinear mass-action kinetics, and conservation laws in place of a normalization, chemical reaction networks seem to defy mutual linearity since species concentrations obey no such relation. We show that it was there all along, in the complexes' activities (mass-action monomials) rather than in the concentrations of species. For zero-deficiency networks with a single linkage class, controlling one reaction makes any three stationary activities obey a linear relation whose coefficients are independent of the controlled rate constants, the conserved quantities (hence the initial state), and even of the stoichiometry of complexes. This predicts hidden activities and bounds the activity ratios the control can reach, while a violation signals nonzero deficiency or multiple linkage classes.

title: Machine Learning-Enabled Time-Skipping Method: Theory and Perturbation-Based Verification
text:
Title: Machine Learning-Enabled Time-Skipping Method: Theory and Perturbation-Based Verification
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Simulating the time evolution of practical mechanics problems requires many time steps. This cost is further compounded by the iterative nature of implicit solvers. We present a cycle-based Machine Learning-enabled Time-skipping (MLT) method. In each cycle, several time steps are skipped, a machine learning (ML) prediction bridges the gap to initialize one solver step, and the physics-based solver then runs for several steps to correct any accumulated errors. Using the Implicit Function Theorem, we derive first-order estimates that characterize how ML prediction errors propagate. These estimates identify when errors remain bounded across cycles and guide the choice of cycle parameters, independent of model architecture. We verify these estimates on the Allen-Cahn equation and a forced variant using controlled synthetic perturbations that emulate ML errors. Wall-clock measurements confirm the theoretical speedup is realizable in practice. The MLT method provides a robust framework for accelerating time-marching in dynamic simulations.

title: Multi-Alignment Contrastive Learning for Enzyme--Reaction Retrieval
text:
Title: Multi-Alignment Contrastive Learning for Enzyme--Reaction Retrieval
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Identifying enzymes that catalyze target biochemical reactions is a key step in computational enzyme discovery and biocatalyst design. Recent representation-learning methods formulate this problem as enzyme--reaction matching, where paired enzymes and reactions are embedded into a shared space. However, most existing approaches primarily rely on pairwise enzyme--reaction supervision and make limited use of the relationships within reaction sets or enzyme families. This work introduces a multi-alignment contrastive learning framework for biochemical retrieval. The framework jointly models cross-domain compatibility between enzymes and reactions and within-domain relationships induced by functional annotations. In addition, a Gromov--Wasserstein-inspired regularization objective encourages geometric consistency between the learned enzyme and reaction representation spaces. By combining pairwise catalytic supervision with higher-order relational alignment, the model captures both direct enzyme--reaction associations and broader functional organization. We evaluate the approach on enzyme virtual screening and bidirectional enzyme--reaction retrieval tasks. Experiments on EnzymeMap show improved early-recognition performance under BEDROC and enrichment-factor metrics compared with strong contrastive baselines. On ReactZyme, the method achieves consistent gains across time-based, enzyme-similarity, and reaction-similarity splits, demonstrating robustness to unseen enzymes and unseen reactions. Ablation studies further indicate that within-domain alignment, functional supervision, and the geometric regularization term each contribute to the observed improvements. These results suggest that modeling multiple forms of alignment can improve contrastive retrieval models for enzyme discovery, reaction annotation, and related computational biology applications.

title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
text:
Title: Probing Non-Abelian Topology through Quench Dynamics
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quench dynamics offer valuable insights to topological matter, wherein the emergent topological phenomena serve as a dynamic probe to the topology of static Hamiltonians. While such a practice has been widely applied to detect the Abelian band topology or the Euler-class topology of band nodes, little is known regarding the quench dynamics of non-Abelian topological insulators in multiband systems, where the intertwining geometry of all eigenstates necessitates the description of noncommutative topological charges. Here we propose a quench protocol for non-Abelian topological insulators, so that the underlying topology can be systematically probed using dynamic signatures. Specifically, we develop a band-projection scheme to extract the gap-resolved topology from dynamic skyrmions in the emergent quasimomentum--time manifolds of the quench processes. These skyrmions are characterized by a series of gap-resolved dynamic Chern numbers, which enable us to reconstruct the full non-Abelian topology of the post-quench Hamiltonian, including the global non-Abelian topological charge and edge-state patterns under the open-boundary condition. Our proposal offers dynamical access to non-Abelian topology in multiband systems, and can be readily implemented using photons or cold atoms.

title: stMIND: Learning multiscale interaction dynamics from spatial-temporal transcriptomics
text:
Title: stMIND: Learning multiscale interaction dynamics from spatial-temporal transcriptomics
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Interactions within local cellular neighborhoods and across broader tissue scales jointly govern molecular state transitions and morphogenesis during development and regeneration. While time-resolved spatial transcriptomics simultaneously profiles gene expression and spatial coordinates, destructive sequencing samples distinct cells at each time point, leaving intermediate trajectories and multiscale intercellular interactions unobserved. Building upon our interacting mean-field neural stochastic differential equation framework, we present stMIND (Spatiotemporal Multiscale Interaction Neural Dynamics), a continuous-time generative framework that infers coupled molecular, spatial, and proliferation dynamics from unmatched spatiotemporal snapshots. stMIND decomposes cellular expression velocity vector/drift into three interpretable operators: a cell-intrinsic program, a local graph-difference attention operator that aggregates relative expression differences and spatial geometry within a co-evolving physical radius, and a nonlocal mean-field attention operator that captures long-range population context beyond the immediate neighborhood. By evolving dynamic spatial neighborhoods alongside cellular migration and enforcing orthogonality between intrinsic and interaction-driven drifts, stMIND resolves scale-specific intercellular influences through optimal transport in joint expression-position space. In axolotl and zebrafish benchmarks, stMIND leads in expression prediction, anatomical consistency and spatial coherence. Ablations confirm the need to combine disjoint local and nonlocal operators. It reveals a regenerative transition in axolotl telencephalon 10 to 15 days after injury, with a drift energy surge followed by nonlocal dominance and local counterbalance varying by cell type in reactive ependymoglial niches. It tracks developmental vector fields across zebrafish stages.

title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
text:
Title: Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Tin-based perovskites are promising candidates for lead-free photovoltaics but suffer from labile Sn$^{2+}$ coordination, rapid crystallization, and severe interfacial defects. Here, we develop a dynamic molecular transformation using 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) to regulate crystallization and interface chemistry simultaneously. During nucleation and growth, the carbonyl group coordinates with Sn$^{2+}$ to stabilize precursor complexes, moderate supersaturation, and enable controlled crystal growth. Upon annealing, PX undergoes in situ molecular transformation, suggested to form amidinium-functionalized species that preferentially occupy surface A-site vacancies, forming a passivation layer and suppressing nonradiative recombination. This coupled bulk-to-interface evolution yields compact, highly crystalline films with improved optoelectronic quality. Devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.18% and retain 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 h of continuous illumination. This work demonstrates a dynamic molecular engineering approach integrating crystallization control and interface passivation, providing a pathway toward efficient and stable lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Enhanced Coulomb pseudopotentials in high-pressure hydrides from first principles
text:
Title: Enhanced Coulomb pseudopotentials in high-pressure hydrides from first principles
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

In the Eliashberg theory of superconductivity, Coulomb interactions oppose the phonon-mediated attraction and suppress the superconducting critical temperature $T_{\mathrm{c}}$. However, most first-principles predictions continue to treat this repulsion with an empirical Coulomb pseudopotential $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ in the range 0.1-0.15. Here we present first-principles calculations of the Coulomb parameter $μ$ and pseudopotential $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ in superconducting hydrides across a range of pressures. The screened Coulomb interaction is evaluated at the random phase approximation level with the Mantel code. We demonstrate that several hydride systems, including H$_3$S, YSbH$_6$ and Mg$_2$IrH$_6$, have strong Coulomb repulsions driven by a large density of states at the Fermi energy, $N_{\mathrm{F}}$. For Mg$_2$IrH$_6$ we obtain $μ=0.62$ and $μ^*_{\text{ME}}\approx0.39$, leading to a 40 K suppression in $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ relative to a standard $μ^*_{\text{ME}}=0.16$. Our obtained $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ is far above the conventional range and, accounting for the energy dependence of the density of states, resolves the factor-of-two discrepancy between $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ estimates of previous studies. Across all systems and pressures studied, we find that $μ$ closely tracks $N_{\mathrm{F}}$, suggesting that commonly used $μ^*_{\text{ME}}$ values lead to overestimated $T_{\mathrm{c}}$ in materials where the density of states at the Fermi energy is large.

title: Probing Transformer Representations Layer by Layer, Module by Module
text:
Title: Probing Transformer Representations Layer by Layer, Module by Module
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Which representation should be probed in a transformer-based foundation model? Recent work shows that the standard practice of probing the final layer is often suboptimal, as intermediate layers can provide better features. Yet, representations are still largely studied along depth alone, treating each transformer block as an atomic unit. In this work, we analyze transformer representations layer by layer, module by module. Through more than 144,000 linear probing evaluations of vision foundation models (VFMs) and large language models (LLMs), we show that layer and module choices should be considered jointly: the best layer-module pair yields substantially larger gains over the final-layer residual stream than the best layer with the residual stream fixed. Moreover, module performance can vary substantially across layers, showing that useful representations cannot be characterized by depth alone. Building on these findings, we evaluate simple fixed probing strategies: the final-layer feedforward activation (Act@100) for vision and the second normalization layer at 60% depth (LN2@60) for language. These strategies improve over the probing baseline in a majority of evaluations and recover, on average, 42% and 86% of the gains from probing the best layer-module pair for vision and language, respectively. For VFMs, these gains increase with the transfer difficulty between pretraining and downstream data.

title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure
text:
Title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Let $γ$ be a Gaussian measure on the sequence space $\ell_2$ whose mean is zero and whose correlation operator $C_γ$ is a diagonal operator on $\ell_2$. Exact values of the $q$-average linear $n$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q<\infty$ are obtained. We also obtain asymptotic orders of the average linear $n$-width in $\ell_\infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$, and of the probabilistic linear $(n,δ)$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q\le 2$, and for $2<q\le \infty$ under some condition on $C_γ$.

title: Hessian-Similar Optimization with Capped Participation: Lower Bounds and Virtual Masters
text:
Title: Hessian-Similar Optimization with Capped Participation: Lower Bounds and Virtual Masters
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

What is the round complexity of Hessian-similar optimization when each round can contact at most $s$ of $m$ clients? Prior rates permit a free master or full participation and do not characterize strict caps. We count every one-vector query and reply. A hidden-client chain gives a lower bound for zero-respecting local algorithms with adaptive cohorts and random stopping: on strongly convex quadratics, the required rounds are $Ω((m/s)\sqrt{\min\{δ_a,\barδ/\sqrt m\}/μ}\,\log(1/ε))$ for $s\leq(m-2)/2$ in the high-accuracy, high-dissimilarity regime. Here $μ$ is strong convexity, while $δ_a$ and $\barδ$ bound anchor and average Hessian variation. To remove dependence on a poor anchor, virtual-master SVRS uses independent estimator and proximal cohorts and averages the proximal replies. With Catalyst, it reaches relative gap $ε$ in $\tilde O(m/s+(\sqrt{m/s}+m^{3/4}/s)\sqrt{\barδ/μ})$ expected rounds on quadratics with strongly convex clients, independent of $δ_a$. Combining this method with charged analyses of existing algorithms matches the lower bound's polynomial dependence for $s\leq\sqrt m$ and $s=Ω(m)$; the worst gap is $O(m^{1/8})$. A held-out 12-seed synthetic study finds fewer rounds than tuned SVRP in nine of ten dip-family incomplete-cohort cells, versus two of 30 other cells. The lower bounds concern zero-respecting algorithms and do not cover unrestricted messages.

title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
text:
Title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.

title: Interpretability Is Not Model-Specific
text:
Title: Interpretability Is Not Model-Specific
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Interpretability tools are usually built for one model at a time: a refusal direction, a truthfulness probe, or a steering vector is found with labeled data inside the model it explains. We ask whether such tools can be carried to other models through a map between residual streams fit only on unlabeled prompts. We transfer a refusal direction, tested causally by addition and ablation, and two read-out tools, a correctness direction and a sentiment probe, across 110 pairs of models from five families and 1B to 72B parameters and between base and instruction-tuned models, with controls for specificity and five seeds. How much transfers depends on what the map was fit on. A map fit on ordinary questions recovers 54\% of the target's own refusal steering and 16\% to 77\% of its correctness gain; adding unlabeled prompts from the region where the tool operates raises these to 102\% and 88\% to 98\%, while control directions recover at most 1\%. We prove that a linear map behaves this way whenever two models correspond linearly on the data it covers, and a label-free coverage score derived from this result tracks recovery across more than 16,000 runs and explains earlier reports that maps between models fail across domains. Carried read-out tools outperform anything the target's unlabeled representations yield. Interpretability results, once found, can be reused across models at the cost of a few unlabeled prompts.

title: Optimizing Multi-Tier Intermediation in Programmatic Advertising: A DAG-Based Mechanism for Supply Path Optimization
text:
Title: Optimizing Multi-Tier Intermediation in Programmatic Advertising: A DAG-Based Mechanism for Supply Path Optimization
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Digital programmatic advertising operates through complex, multi-hop supply chains. The opacity of these intermediary networks leads to significant efficiency losses, often referred to as the ``ad-tech tax.'' While current industry practices utilize heuristic Supply Path Optimization (SPO) to trim inefficient routes, they fail to optimize the equilibrium of the entire network. This paper extends previous work on Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) intermediation models by applying them to traceable programmatic supply chains mapped via the OpenRTB SupplyChain object. We introduce multi-attribute utility functions and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) to account for substitutable routing (OR nodes) and percentage-based fee structures. Furthermore, we outline a computational methodology and experimental framework using public \texttt{schain} and \texttt{sellers.json} data to benchmark optimal Nash social welfare against current uncoordinated market outcomes.

title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
text:
Title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Hybrid models combine softmax attention with linear attention, which compresses history into fixed-size recurrent states to balance model quality and inference efficiency. However, linear attention has not pushed this compression to its limit: we find that the queries, keys, and values of linear layers concentrate in a stable, low-dimensional subspace, a phenomenon we call the linear attention sink, so each state is effectively low-rank, with a rank that varies across states. Yet existing serving systems keep these redundant states dense, reading and rewriting them in full at every decoding step, so their memory traffic grows with the batch size and dominates the decoding cost. Thus SinkState stores each recurrent state in an adaptive low-rank form throughout inference with buffered updates and a local SVD restricted to the top subspace. SinkState further consolidates the remaining components asynchronously on the CPU. On four hybrid models with Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers, from 4B to 120B parameters, SinkState reduces the peak memory of recurrent states by up to 2.6x (1.9x on average) and speeds up decoding by up to 1.58x (1.25x on average) over Mamba-SSM and FLA, while maintaining accuracy.

title: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design
text:
Title: HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Designing microbial strains for growth-coupled production, in which cellular growth is linked to the synthesis of a target compound through genetic interventions, is a fundamental goal in metabolic engineering. Constraint-based methods can identify growth-coupled deletion strategies, but design for each target typically requires a separate search across a large number of possible gene-deletion combinations. This motivates a reusable approach that learns from previously evaluated strain designs to prioritize candidate interventions before downstream constraint-based evaluation. We present a reproducible protocol for growth-coupled gene deletion design that learns and ranks gene-deletion priorities for each target metabolite. Using computationally curated deletion strategies as learning resources, the protocol generates continuous deletion-priority rankings, constructs candidate strategies at adjustable search-space budgets, and evaluates these candidates through constraint-based metabolic analysis. Its learning component, HGPRGDel, explicitly represents gene-protein-reaction (GPR) logic, capturing how multiple genes can jointly support a reaction or alternative genes can maintain its activity, while integrating molecular and reaction-level information. Across e_coli_core, iMM904, and iML1515, the protocol achieves the highest macro-F1 and AUC among the evaluated learning configurations. HGPRGDel's rankings recovered an average of 90% of the reference deletion genes from MetNetComp by examining fewer genes than the evaluated baseline methods. By separating learned intervention prioritization from downstream constraint-based assessment, the protocol provides a reproducible framework for reusing strain-design knowledge while controlling the size of the candidate space and retaining mechanistic evaluation of growth-coupled production.

title: Symanzik Effective Hamiltonian for Lattice Quantum Field Theories
text:
Title: Symanzik Effective Hamiltonian for Lattice Quantum Field Theories
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We propose a framework to construct the Symanzik effective Hamiltonian for lattice quantum field theories directly based on dimensional analysis and symmetries in the Hamiltonian formulation. This allows to classify all operators which can contribute at a given order in the spatial lattice spacing. This list can be reduced using the equations of motion and other identities. We exemplify the framework for $φ^4$ and pure gauge theory, obtaining results consistent with earlier publications for the case of classical improvement. It provides the means to develop a non-perturbative improvement programme in the Hamiltonian formulation of lattice quantum field theories in the future.

title: A Compact High-Repetition-Rate Intense THz Source for Atomic-Scale Materials Characterization
text:
Title: A Compact High-Repetition-Rate Intense THz Source for Atomic-Scale Materials Characterization
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

High-intensity terahertz (THz) sources combining high repetition rates, strong field amplitudes, and long-term stability are key enabling technologies for next-generation ultrafast photonics. However, simultaneously achieving these characteristics in a compact and practical architecture remains a major challenge. Here, we report a high-performance tabletop THz source delivering intense single-cycle pulses at 100 kHz, generated by optical rectification in lithium niobate using an optimized echelon-based tilted-pulse-front scheme and driven by an industrial-grade ytterbium laser. The source achieves optical-to-THz conversion efficiencies exceeding 0.13% at room temperature, peak electric fields of several hundred kV/cm, and excellent long-term stability, establishing a robust platform for high-average-power strong-field THz applications. As a proof of concept, the source was integrated into an atom probe tomography (APT) instrument. APT reconstructs the three-dimensional chemical composition of materials through field-induced ion emission from a sharp nanotip. While THz-assisted ion emission has been shown to improve analytical performance by reducing thermal effects, previous demonstrations were limited to low-repetition-rate THz sources, restricting throughput and accessible analysis volumes. Using an aluminum nanotip, we demonstrate efficient THz-assisted APT at 100 kHz and benchmark its performance against conventional voltage- and laser-assisted operation. The high repetition rate enables rapid large-volume acquisition while improving mass resolving power, reducing thermal tailing, and preserving high-quality three-dimensional reconstructions. Beyond APT, this work establishes a compact and scalable high-repetition-rate THz platform for strong-field physics, nonlinear THz photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and material characterization at the nanoscale.

title: MicroFuse: Protein-to-Genome Expert Fusion for Microbial Operon Reasoning
text:
Title: MicroFuse: Protein-to-Genome Expert Fusion for Microbial Operon Reasoning
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Predicting microbial operon co-membership requires integrating two complementary biological signals: protein-scale molecular identity and genome-context organization. While recent biological foundation models provide powerful representations of each view independently, naive concatenation of these modalities ignores a key biological property -- protein identity and genomic context may agree when adjacent genes form a coherent functional module, or conflict when sequence similarity is misleading but genomic layout indicates independent regulation. We present MicroFuse, a protein-to-genome expert fusion framework that integrates structure-aware protein representations from ProstT5 with genome-context representations from Bacformer through a four-expert Mixture-of-Experts module (protein, genome-context, agreement, and conflict experts) with a learned soft router. Training combines binary cross-entropy with symmetric cross-modal InfoNCE alignment and disagreement-weighted supervised contrastive shaping. We further construct OG-Operon100K, a 100,000-pair scaffold-level benchmark from the OMG metagenomic corpus with biologically grounded positive and negative criteria. On OG-Operon100K, MicroFuse achieves the strongest AUROC, AUPRC, mAP, and mAR among ProstT5-only, Bacformer-only, and Concat MLP baselines. Ablations identify cross-modal contrastive alignment as the dominant component, and a hard sequence-conflict subset reveals MicroFuse's largest gains precisely in biologically ambiguous cases where protein identity alone is misleading.

title: XAI-Driven Confidence Estimation for OOD-Resilient Runtime Prediction
text:
Title: XAI-Driven Confidence Estimation for OOD-Resilient Runtime Prediction
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Machine learning-based resource management (RM) models degrade under out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs at runtime, yet existing approaches in the literature rely on a single global error margin that is overly conservative and fails to distinguish reliablepredictions from catastrophic failures. We propose Lightweight Runtime EXplainability (LEX), the first post-hoc XAI framework for input-specific runtime confidence estimation in ML-based RM. LEX clusters the embeddings of the training input space using a Gaussian Mixture Model and associates per-cluster prediction error bounds to input samples, enabling fine-grained runtime confidence signals without retraining. Evaluated on a state-of-the-art LSTM-based IPS forecasting model on Intel Alder Lake, across 34 benchmark applications, LEX achieves ~94% containment on unseen workloads and produces ~17% tighter per-input confidence bounds than global baselines. With its negligible runtime overhead, LEX advances the field by providing explainable and reliable input-specific confidence signals of ML predictions, thereby making ML-based resource management resilient to OOD at runtime.

title: Asymptotic safety is not generic
text:
Title: Asymptotic safety is not generic
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Asymptotically safe quantum gravity proposes a non-perturbative ultraviolet completion of gravity in which the high-energy behavior is controlled by an ultraviolet fixed point---the Reuter fixed point---for which there is robust evidence from a wide range of settings and truncations. The existence of asymptotic safety requires non-trivial zeros of beta functions, raising the question of how generic such fixed-point solutions are. In this work, we tackle this issue by investigating chiral perturbation theories. We focus on SU(2) and SU(3) chiral models, which share key features with gravity such as perturbative non-renormalizability or nonlinear interactions, but which are known to admit a different ultraviolet completion via new degrees of freedom. Using the functional renormalization group, we study these theories within a quartic-derivative truncation and find no evidence for an interacting fixed point. This result suggests that asymptotic safety is not generic, but rather a feature pertaining to certain special systems.

title: Analytic Bounds on Conformal Defect Spectra
text:
Title: Analytic Bounds on Conformal Defect Spectra
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Conformal defects describe impurities and boundaries at criticality. Their stability depends on the scaling dimensions of operators localized on the defects, but these dimensions are often difficult to determine. We derive analytic upper bounds on the lowest nonvacuum scaling dimension using only two defect entropies and the dimension of a defect-changing operator. The bounds identify when relevant operators must appear on the defect with larger defect entropy. They follow from the conformal bootstrap of four-point functions of defect-changing operators and apply to unitary conformal line defects and to conformal boundaries in two-dimensional CFTs. The Ising and Potts models provide exact checks. In three-dimensional $O(N)$ models, we apply the bounds to direct sums of pinning field defects with symmetry-related orientations. Data from a single such defect exclude stable impurity order with three or more orientations in $O(2)$ and $O(3)$, or four or more in $O(4)$, for any geometry of the orientations, and require a relevant domain-wall operator between individually stable pinning field defects at every nonzero relative angle up to $120^\circ$ in $O(3)$ and up to $109.47^\circ$ in $O(4)$. A direct fuzzy-sphere computation of the lowest domain-wall dimension at different relative angles for $N=2,3,4$ is consistent with these bounds and indicates that, within this class of impurities, only two-state order remains a candidate for stable order in $O(3)$ and $O(4)$, while none survives in $O(2)$. A separate application to AdS/BCFT shows that, at fixed unequal brane tensions, a light boundary-condition-changing operator requires additional light primaries on the boundary with larger boundary entropy.

title: Data-driven representation of continuous-time linear time-invariant behaviors via Hankel integral operators
text:
Title: Data-driven representation of continuous-time linear time-invariant behaviors via Hankel integral operators
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We present a data-driven representation of the finite-horizon behavior of deterministic controllable continuous-time LTI systems. We first introduce a notion of persistency of excitation for continuous-time signals that does not require the signal to be differentiable. We then show that, when the input is persistently exciting in this sense, the closure of the range of a Hankel integral operator built from a single input-output trajectory equals the behavior of the system over a finite time horizon. This result provides a nonparametric representation of system trajectories directly in terms of measured data, without requiring an explicit parametric model of the system.

title: Comonotonic and moment matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables II
text:
Title: Comonotonic and moment matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables II
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

In this paper, based on the concept of step-weighted distribution, we introduce a minimum-deformation approach to constructing comonotonic and moment-matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables. The proposed approach aims to minimize the Pearson deformation of a starting comonotonic approximation subject to moment-matching constraints. We establish several results concerning the existence and uniqueness of minimum-deformation comonotonic approximations and propose a method for determining the step quantiles and weights. In particular, when the number of steps is one greater than the moment-matching order, we show that the joint optimization problem can be reduced to an optimization problem involving only the partition points. The proposed framework accommodates moment matching of any prescribed finite order, and numerical experiments demonstrate its application to approximations matching the first five moments of the original sum. The numerical results also show that minimizing the Pearson deformation does not necessarily improve the approximation accuracy of risk measures, which depends on both the starting comonotonic approximation and the choice of partition points and correction weights.

title: Antisymmetric thermopower without magnetism in three-phase composites
text:
Title: Antisymmetric thermopower without magnetism in three-phase composites
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

A thermopower that turns a temperature gradient into a perpendicular electric field in every in-plane direction has relied on magnetism. Reciprocity permits it without magnetism, yet under a three-fold or higher axis it vanishes both in reciprocal elastic band transport and in composites of two isotropic phases with ideal interfaces. Here we show that composites of three isotropic phases carry it, and that under such an axis three is the minimum. A third, linearly independent transport matrix escapes the exact two-phase reduction; at weak contrast the first allowed axial term is cubic, proportional to a determinant of the three matrices times material-weighted, handed three-point correlations. Treating the phases as colours identifies the arrangements that allow the response, and crystal nets from reticular chemistry supply printable three-dimensional ones. Certified two-sided bounds give axial Seebeck coefficients of 49.5-50.2 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ in a planar cell and 76-84 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ in a printable woodpile; reflections in planes containing the axis reverse the response, and recolouring 24 nets to restore their parent symmetry switches it off. Around a line heat source the axial driving field has the $1/r$ azimuthal form of the magnetic field of a straight wire and drives circulating currents.

title: ECOS: Environment-Calibrated On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Agents
text:
Title: ECOS: Environment-Calibrated On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Agents
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

On-policy self-distillation lets a language agent act as its own Teacher by conditioning on privileged context such as skills written from its own trajectories. Its guidance, however, is weighted by how much this context shifts token likelihoods rather than by whether it improves behavior, so errors in self-written skills return through later updates. We propose environment-calibrated on-policy self-distillation, which uses environmental outcomes to decide how much to trust the Teacher's current guidance and which self-written skills to reinforce. Command-level advantages, estimated by comparing commands executed at similar observations, scale each Teacher preference and reward reflections and skills whose induced preferences favor higher-advantage commands. Without skills at inference, 3B and 7B agents reach 90.5% and 93.3% macro success on seen ALFWorld tasks and 75.5% and 80.5% success on WebShop. On unseen ALFWorld tasks, they outperform GRPO under the same protocol by 11.0 and 7.6 percentage points, respectively. In an ablation study, supervising only executable commands rather than the Actor's full response raises 3B WebShop success from 52.3% to 75.0%.

title: Evolutionary and Structural Constraints Define a Mutation-Resistant Catalytic Core in E. coli Serine Hydroxy methyltransferase (SHMT)
text:
Title: Evolutionary and Structural Constraints Define a Mutation-Resistant Catalytic Core in E. coli Serine Hydroxy methyltransferase (SHMT)
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Serine hydroxymethyltransferase is an essential enzyme in the Escherichia coli folate pathway, yet it has not been adopted as an antibacterial target, unlike DHFR, DHPS, or thymidylate synthase. To investigate this discrepancy, we applied a multi-scale computational framework that integrates large-scale sequence analysis of 1000 homologs, coevolutionary interaction mapping, structural community analysis, intrinsic disorder profiling, and adaptive fitness modelling. These analyses converge on a single conclusion: the catalytic core of SHMT forms an exceptionally conserved and tightly coupled structural unit. This region exhibits dense coevolution, strong intramolecular connectivity, minimal disorder, and extremely low mutational tolerance. Peripheral loops and termini, in contrast, are far more flexible. Relative to established folate-pathway antibiotic targets, SHMT active site is even more rigid and evolutionarily constrained. This extreme constraint may limit the emergence of resistance-compatible mutations, providing a plausible explanation for the absence of natural-product inhibitors. Fitness trajectory modelling supports this interpretation, showing that nearly all active-site residues tolerate only rare or neutral substitutions. Together, these findings identify SHMT as a structurally stable and evolutionarily restricted enzyme whose catalytic architecture is unusually protected. This makes SHMT an underexplored yet promising target for the rational design of next-generation antibacterial agents.

title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites
text:
Title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Chiral spacer cations crystallize two-dimensional hybrid perovskites in the polar Sohncke group $P2_1$, which places the polar axis in the inorganic layer. We analyze the spin-orbit field that this geometry allows and test it against first-principles spin textures of ten polar chiral lead-halide perovskites, their mirror enantiomers and four halide-substituted analogues. The point group $C_2$ with the twofold axis in the layer forbids the helical Rashba field and allows a linear term $γ_1 k_x σ_z$, the Rashba interaction of the in-plane polar axis, together with chirality-related Dresselhaus and radial terms. Thirty-four two-band $k \cdot p$ models were fitted to each band pair and ranked by the agreement of their spin directions with the calculation rather than by the band energies, which cannot distinguish them. In all strongly polar compounds, the conduction band is described by the persistent term alone, with $γ_1 = 1.09$-$1.98$ eV Å and a spin agreement of at least 0.98, whereas the best Rashba or Dresselhaus model reaches 0.20. The $R$ and $S$ enantiomers of each compound have opposite polarizations, and therefore opposite $γ_1$ and opposite persistent spin textures of equal magnitude, as required by the mirror that relates them; this holds in all ten compounds, so the choice of the enantiomer selects the spin direction. The magnitude of $γ_1$ correlates with the disparity of the in-plane Pb-X-Pb angles ($r = 0.95$). With electron masses of $0.26$-$0.43\,m_e$ along the spin-splitting directions, the associated persistent spin helices have wavelengths of 3.4-8.2 nm.

title: SurfSpec: Enhancing Off-Target-Agnostic Specificity by Bounding Pocket-Ligand Geometric Mismatch
text:
Title: SurfSpec: Enhancing Off-Target-Agnostic Specificity by Bounding Pocket-Ligand Geometric Mismatch
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Lead optimization in structure-based drug design aims to improve target binding while avoiding unintended interactions with off-target pockets. However, existing affinity-driven methods do not explicitly control specificity, whereas current specificity-aware approaches commonly require prior knowledge of off-target structures. We address off-target-agnostic specificity-aware lead optimization by analyzing the geometric mismatch between a ligand and the target pocket. We provide a conservative specificity lower bound for geometrically separated off-targets without requiring access to off-target structures. By metricizing pocket--ligand mismatch, the triangle inequality shows that reducing target--ligand mismatch improves a conservative lower bound on mismatch to a separated off-target class, which can be translated into a specificity lower bound through an empirical geometry--affinity calibration. Motivated by this analysis, we introduce SurfSpec, an off-target-agnostic lead optimization framework that iteratively grows ligands toward under-occupied regions of the target pocket surface. SurfSpec alternates between linker generation toward selected target-surface patches, which provides geometric pseudo-labels, and refinement under a pocket-conditioned ligand prior, which restores these pseudo-labels into valid ligands. On the CrossDocked2020 test set, SurfSpec reduces geometric mismatch and outperforms evaluated off-target-agnostic lead optimization baselines in empirical specificity, while maintaining competitive target-affinity improvement.

title: Bridging the Simulation-to-Experiment Gap with Generative Models using Adversarial Distribution Alignment
text:
Title: Bridging the Simulation-to-Experiment Gap with Generative Models using Adversarial Distribution Alignment
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

A fundamental challenge in science and engineering is the simulation-to-experiment gap. While we often possess prior knowledge of physical laws, these physical laws can be too difficult to solve exactly for complex systems. Such systems are commonly modeled using simulators, which impose computational approximations. Meanwhile, experimental measurements more faithfully represent the real world, but experimental data typically consists of observations that only partially reflect the system's full underlying state. We propose a data-driven distribution alignment framework that bridges this simulation-to-experiment gap by pre-training a generative model on fully observed (but imperfect) simulation data, then aligning it with partial (but real) observations of experimental data. While our method is domain-agnostic, we ground our approach in the physical sciences by introducing Adversarial Distribution Alignment (ADA). This method aligns a generative model of atomic positions -- initially trained on a simulated Boltzmann distribution -- with the distribution of experimental observations. We prove that our method recovers the target observable distribution, even with multiple, potentially correlated observables. We also empirically validate our framework on synthetic, molecular, and experimental protein data, demonstrating that it can align generative models with diverse observables. Our code is available at https://kaityrusnelson.com/ada/.

title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
text:
Title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Reward models used for off-policy evaluation (OPE) are commonly selected using held-out data. When sample size and context dimension grow proportionally, the difference in test risk between models fitted on the full sample and on a fixed fraction of it need not vanish. Held-out evaluation can therefore consistently estimate the test risk of the model trained on the smaller sample, but because the relative ranking of candidate reward models can change after full-data refitting, held-out selection can be suboptimal. We develop an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk under the target policy using only its training observations. This enables early stopping along the full-data gradient-descent trajectory without sample splitting. For neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, context-dependent multi-index target policies, and known context-independent logging, we prove uniform consistency of our criterion over a fixed finite set of gradient-descent iterates and a near-oracle guarantee for the selected reward model. The same correction yields a doubly robust estimator that consistently estimates the true policy value without sample splitting, even when reward-model prediction error does not vanish. Experiments show decreasing risk-estimation error as dimension grows at a fixed sample-to-dimension ratio, and improved reward-model selection relative to held-out baselines. Empirically, our correction also reduces the root mean squared error of doubly robust value estimates computed from the same data used to fit and select the reward models.

title: GPU-Accelerated Non-Interactive Encrypted Neural Network Training with Batched Diagonal Packing
text:
Title: GPU-Accelerated Non-Interactive Encrypted Neural Network Training with Batched Diagonal Packing
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Training a neural network under homomorphic encryption requires transposes, batch reductions, optimizer updates, and repeated refreshes in addition to forward matrix products. We combine rectangular diagonal packing, feature-major SIMD mini-batch lanes, baby-step giant-step evaluation, and compact optimizer state in an MIT-licensed Rust CKKS implementation. Its CUDA path keeps training and bootstrap ciphertext arithmetic on the GPU, while retaining host key generation and client operations. In a matched 100-update experiment on the main non-interactive MNIST model, device-resident bootstrapping reduces training time from 14,268.295 to 293.075 seconds, a $48.68\times$ ratio against our CPU implementation, with exactly equal decoded parameters and predictions. Including setup and final evaluation gives a $40.67\times$ ratio. A separate GPU run completes ten passes over 4,800 images in 2,967.095 seconds and achieves 90.35% test accuracy versus 90.41% for its plaintext twin. These are single-initialization results; exact CPU/GPU parameter agreement is verified at 100 updates, not for the full 1,000-update run. Earlier completed CPU runs support a larger-batch key-switch advantage and baseline-batch accuracy within the registered tolerance, but the baseline-batch normalized key-switch target is missed. The released ReBoot baseline does not meet the common security-estimator threshold, and its full-setting CPU time is unmeasured. We therefore distinguish measured acceleration of our implementation from conditional layout comparisons and do not claim unconditional superiority over ReBoot.

title: Pool-free, residual-triggered ansatz growth for variational imaginary-time evolution: when a fixed operator order beats adaptive screening
text:
Title: Pool-free, residual-triggered ansatz growth for variational imaginary-time evolution: when a fixed operator order beats adaptive screening
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Adaptive variational algorithms such as ADAPT-VQE and AVQITE screen an operator pool at every growth step, and ADAPT-VQE also re-optimizes all parameters. We study a pool-free alternative for variational imaginary-time evolution (VITE). The layers are fixed in advance by nested commutators of the Hamiltonian, grouped by symmetry and particle number, and the next layer is appended when the relative McLachlan residual exceeds a threshold. On five non-integrable systems (the mixed-field Ising chain and tori, and stretched H$_4$), this dynamic VITE reaches a relative error of $10^{-4}$ with 1.6-5.4 times fewer circuits than the cheapest of six to eight adaptive variants, including single-Pauli-string and qubit-excitation pools and batched ADAPT-VQE. On the chain the advantage persists from 8 to 16 sites. Screening and re-optimization account for most of the adaptive methods' cost. On the spin models, a longitudinal-field scan shows that the advantage requires broken integrability, which makes adaptive screening expensive. The advantage is lost on transverse-field Ising models, at tight targets (relative error $10^{-6}$) and where the schedule front-loads weak layers.

title: The Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the Cramér--Lundberg model with Erlang $E_2(μ)$ claims: spectrum, exact moments and matrix reduction
text:
Title: The Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the Cramér--Lundberg model with Erlang $E_2(μ)$ claims: spectrum, exact moments and matrix reduction
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study the Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the classical Cramér--Lundberg model with claims having an Erlang distribution of shape parameter 2. We derive an integro-differential equation with two boundary conditions. For every positive discount rate, we show that its characteristic polynomial has one negative root and two distinct positive roots. Boundedness excludes the growing exponential term and yields a representation of the transform as a sum of two decaying exponentials. We construct a finite-dimensional matrix reduction of the convolution chain. For a model parameter set, we obtain exact expressions for the ruin probability, the mean time of ruin, and higher moments, including the third moment at zero initial surplus. We prove analyticity in the discount rate and justify the resulting moment series. We consider the analytic continuation of the representation to negative discount rates separately. For Erlang claims with an arbitrary positive integer shape parameter, we establish a closed linear system and the asymptotics of the root continuing the zero root at zero discount.

title: More physics at the entangling surface: boundary conditions and entanglement in 2d TQFT
text:
Title: More physics at the entangling surface: boundary conditions and entanglement in 2d TQFT
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We present a systematic treatment of entanglement in two-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). Our approach clarifies the sensitivity of entanglement measures to the cutting maps that implement Hilbert space factorization. Such maps embed the TQFT Hilbert space into a description with potentially more degrees of freedom, and for entanglement to be well defined they must be isometric, i.e., they must preserve the norms of all states. We show that the naïve cutting map based solely upon path integration subject to boundary conditions is not isometric for generic TQFTs. For any 2d TQFT, we give a prescription to construct isometric cutting maps by dressing path integration with suitable edge operators. This allows us to compute entanglement for any state, any bipartition, and any boundary condition. As a consequence, we find a non-integer "ground-state degeneracy" à la Affleck-Ludwig, despite all boundary conditions being gapped. We further show how to reconstruct the partition function of the TQFT at arbitrary genus from the multi-interval Rényi entropies of a single state. For theories with (possibly non-invertible) symmetries, we show that the entanglement entropy of the symmetric ground state can distinguish gapped phases with the same symmetry, without any further knowledge of their vacua, while the entanglement asymmetry of the vacua entropically detects symmetry breaking. We illustrate our formalism with a range of applications, from finite gauge theories to Haagerup gapped phases and infrared phases of adjoint QCD$_2$.

title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction
text:
Title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Graph forecasters for sensor networks are trained in one regime and deployed in others, where sensor coupling and signal frequency content both change. We split this spectral shift into an operator channel and a frequency channel, each with a dimensionless measure. ST-GFM (Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting Model) filters every input step with Chebyshev and bidirectional diffusion filters on one learned, non-symmetric operator and alternates them with per-node temporal attention. For the operator channel we prove Frobenius-norm perturbation bounds for both graph branches, show that the Chebyshev bound is attained to first order, and compute its constant from the trained weights and the measured operator norm: 17.9 on METR-LA and 21.5 on PEMS-BAY. Under random edge dropout the trained layer moves by 2.0% to 3.1% of this bound. Masked Spectral Reconstruction (MSR), a self-supervised loss active in the first 40 epochs, matches the log power spectrum of the encoder output to that of the input. For small log-spectral residuals on unclamped bins it is proportional to an Itakura-Saito divergence to leading order. Removing it raises the 60-minute MAE by 0.30 on METR-LA, close to the 0.33 lost when all three self-supervised losses go. Under one shared evaluation pipeline, the 60-minute MAE of ST-GFM is 3.5% below a retrained STAEformer on METR-LA and 13.0% below it on PEMS-BAY. Its 60-minute MAE is 3.0980.017 on METR-LA (five seeds) and 1.5760.006 on PEMS-BAY (three seeds), the lowest PEMS-BAY MAE among twelve published baselines.

title: MedGSSR: Generalizable Medical Image Super-Resolution 3D Reconstruction via Hierarchical Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting
text:
Title: MedGSSR: Generalizable Medical Image Super-Resolution 3D Reconstruction via Hierarchical Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

High-resolution volumetric medical imaging is critical for clinical diagnosis, yet acquisition is often limited by scanner hardware, scan time, and for CT, radiation dose. Medical 3D Super-Resolution (Med3DSR) offers a computational alternative, but existing methods commonly rely on per-subject optimization, pretrained priors, or coordinate-based implicit representations, which compromise anatomical fidelity and limit efficiency. To address these limitations, we present MedGSSR, a fully end-to-end feed-forward framework that represents volumes as an explicit 3D Gaussian field for Med3DSR. Unlike coordinate-based implicit functions, our explicit 3D Gaussian representation naturally enhances signal continuity and local high-frequency fidelity. Specifically, MedGSSR explicitly decouples the reconstruction process into coarse-grained structural preservation and fine-grained textural refinement through the proposed Pyramid Anatomical Encoder and a Hierarchical Gaussian Projector. To support arbitrary-scale super-resolution, we introduce sub-voxel Gaussian decomposition and a Differentiable Gaussian Voxelizer that directly queries the continuous 3D intensity field, reducing discretization artifacts. Extensive experiments on MRI and CT benchmarks demonstrate that MedGSSR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Notably, our framework exhibits robust generalizability across unseen datasets without requiring per-subject optimization, enabling fast inference and high-fidelity volumetric super-resolution in practical clinical settings. Our project webpage, including code, is at https://william2ai.github.io/medgssr

title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
text:
Title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Padé resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

title: Self-Energy Construction for Chain Representations of Open Quantum Systems
text:
Title: Self-Energy Construction for Chain Representations of Open Quantum Systems
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We identify the self-energy as the environmental response to the system, which transforms covariantly under shifts of the system--environment cut. For a semi-infinite chain with asymptotically uniform parameters, this transformation admits a fixed point that defines the asymptotic boundary self-energy (BSE), whose spectral density is the Wigner semicircle. A chain-extended BSE exploits the trend of the retained chain, offering improved accuracy in representing the environment. The transformation introduces a pseudo-hyperbolic self-energy distance that is invariant under shifts of the cut, providing a natural geometry for comparing environmental responses. As a demonstration, this geometry enables cut-independent error measure of finite damped-oscillator closures of the chain, distinguishing the closure error from the chain depth error, and offers a more accurate fitting scheme than fitting the time-domain correlation function.

title: Cold Hypersonic Gas Jets for Precision Laser Spectroscopy of Radioactive Molecules
text:
Title: Cold Hypersonic Gas Jets for Precision Laser Spectroscopy of Radioactive Molecules
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

The sensitivity to possible beyond standard model physics via a study of the nuclear Schiff moment (NSM) has since recently been driving laser spectroscopy of short-lived radioactive molecules. These experiments have in part been hindered by inefficient cooling of the molecular degrees of freedom, resulting in complex, difficult to interpret molecular spectra. Hypersonic (de Laval) nozzles have been shown to provide ideal environments to study cold short-lived actinides by means of in-gas-jet laser ionization spectroscopy. We present here the first application of this technique on molecules using $^{229,230,232}$ThO laser ablation targets. Translational and rotational temperatures were characterized via laser spectroscopy and found to be $12.5(25)\,\mathrm{K}$ and $7.2(6)\,\mathrm{K}$, respectively, along the nozzle-collimated $60\,\mathrm{mm}$-long, $5\,\mathrm{mm}$-diameter gas jet. An upper bound of the vibrational temperature was estimated as no transitions from $v''=1$ were observed. Molecular King-plot analysis shows a large field shift of $-4.0(13)\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}/\mathrm{fm}^2$, indicating enhanced sensitivity to the differential nuclear charge radii. Relativistic FSCCSD calculations reproduce the measured molecular field-shift factor, providing a benchmark between state-of-the-art molecular and atomic calculations.

title: Yang-Mills theories with scalar matter: a first foray using the Curci-Ferrari model
text:
Title: Yang-Mills theories with scalar matter: a first foray using the Curci-Ferrari model
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

The Curci-Ferrari (CF) model provides an efficient perturbative framework for describing several aspects of the infrared (IR) dynamics of Yang-Mills (YM) theories. We extend this framework to YM theories coupled with scalar matter and investigate its main properties, with particular emphasis on the one-loop two-point correlation functions of scalars, gluons, and ghosts. We analyze the renormalization group (RG) structure of the model, computing its beta functions and studying the corresponding RG flows for different scalar masses. We establish the existence of IR-safe trajectories along which perturbation theory remains under control and identify a novel fixed-point, while recovering the standard CF results in an appropriate limit. We then confront our results with lattice data through a simultaneous fit of the scalar, gluon, and ghost propagators, finding excellent agreement. Our results indicate that, within the approximations considered here, the CF framework gives a successful perturbative description of the IR regime of YM theories coupled with scalar matter.

title: AcupunctureBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Generative Models in the Acupuncture Domain
text:
Title: AcupunctureBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Generative Models in the Acupuncture Domain
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in the field of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), standardized benchmark evaluations for TCM have gradually emerged. Acupuncture is a crucial component of TCM. However, existing evaluation benchmarks are lacking in this domain. To address this gap, this paper proposes AcupunctureBench, the first independently constructed large-scale multimodal benchmark for the acupuncture domain, covering text, image, and video modalities. The AcupunctureBench spans multidimen sional knowledge in acupuncture, including acupuncture theory, meridians and acupoints, clinical reasoning, TCM syndromes, and practical acupoint operation. To achieve large-scale construction while ensuring medical professionalism, this work designs a human-machine collaborative data construction pipeline and proposes efficient deduplication strategies to reduce redundant samples, while extensively adopting data synthesis to mitigate data leak age risks. AcupunctureBench contains a total of 58,526 question samples and 1,216 video samples, covering multiple task types including objective questions, subjective question answering, case analysis, image understanding, image reasoning, and video understanding. Based on this benchmark, this paper evaluates 14 large language models, 14 large multimodal models, and 4 video foundation models, and further releases the first dedicated evaluation website for the acupuncture domain.

title: Pathwise-Budgeted LLM Routing: Online Allocation with K-Bit Tail-Cost Learning
text:
Title: Pathwise-Budgeted LLM Routing: Online Allocation with K-Bit Tail-Cost Learning
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Firms using large language models under fixed budgets must decide which model to call and whether to retry a failed task. Because a call's charge is revealed only after completion, one long response can exhaust the remaining budget and leave later tasks unserved. Our objective is to maximize the number of tasks solved before service stops. We develop a contextual bandit policy, ADP-HT, which learns each model's task-specific success probability and constructs conservative cost estimates from coarsened response-length labels on a quantile grid with $2^K$ intervals. The policy weighs predicted success against these costs, adjusting the cost penalty to realized spending and the budget available per remaining task. Under calibration, local regularity, and grid-coverage conditions, we bound the excess allowance in the policy's conservative cost estimates. At a fixed sample size, increasing $K$ reduces the discretization term but increases the estimation allowance. At the tightest tested budgets, ADP-HT solves more than twice as many MATH500 and GPQA tasks as the best implemented baseline. It achieves the highest mean cumulative score at ten of fourteen RouterBench budgets. On LiveCodeBench, it outperforms a deployed commercial router in both default and cost-saving modes at the three lowest test budgets.

title: Remote Sensing-Based Hybrid Statistical and Machine Learning Ensemble Modeling of Yellowfin Tuna Catch in the Western Equatorial Indian Ocean
text:
Title: Remote Sensing-Based Hybrid Statistical and Machine Learning Ensemble Modeling of Yellowfin Tuna Catch in the Western Equatorial Indian Ocean
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares) is an economically important pelagic species in the Indian Ocean, but its monthly catch variability is difficult to predict because reported catch is influenced by ocean productivity, thermal habitat, monsoon seasonality, fishing-ground characteristics, and fleet behavior. This study develops a remote sensing-based statistical and machine learning stacked ensemble for modeling monthly yellowfin tuna catch across five fishing grounds in the western equatorial Indian Ocean during 2003-2024. Monthly fishery records were integrated with satellite-derived chlorophyll-a concentration (CHL) and sea surface temperature (SST). Linear mixed models (LMMs) and a generalized additive mixed model (GAMM) were used to represent interpretable current and lagged environmental effects, while Random Forest models captured nonlinear interactions among lagged, rolling, seasonal, anomaly, and spatial predictors. Expanding-window validation over the pre-COVID evaluation period from 2008 to 2019 was used to reduce temporal leakage. Among the individual models, the GAMM achieved the best log-scale performance, with an R-squared value of 0.137 and an RMSE of 1.284, while RF-E6 achieved the lowest RMSE on the kilogram scale. The nonnegative Ridge stacked ensemble improved the log-scale R-squared value to 0.177, with an RMSE of 1.254 and an MAE of 1.000. These results show that satellite-derived CHL and SST contain useful but incomplete predictive information for monthly catch modeling.

title: Efficient and Accurate Zero Shot Generation of Symmetric Protein Complexes
text:
Title: Efficient and Accurate Zero Shot Generation of Symmetric Protein Complexes
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Symmetric organization is a fundamental principle of biomolecular complex assembly. The same principle underlies engineered applications, from vaccine platforms to nanomaterials, making symmetric de novo generation a core capability for computational protein design. We establish a theoretical foundation equating generation of an assembly with underlying symmetry group $G$ to generation within a quotient space over $G$. This directly allows $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant models to generate symmetric structures with minimal distribution shift. With this insight we introduce ZeUS ($\textbf{Ze}$ro-shot $\textbf{U}$nified $\textbf{S}$ymmetrization), a framework that converts any pretrained $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant backbone generative model into an efficient generator of symmetric assemblies with no retraining. ZeUS operates on a single $\textit{canonical subunit}$ and utilizes $\textit{phantom subunits}$ to preserve internal model operations, reducing memory and runtime cost by $\mathcal{O}(|G|)$ for finite groups $G$, compared to a full-complex forward pass. We implement ZeUS for IPA-based models (FrameDiff, FoldFlow) and axial-attention-based RFdiffusion, showing high generation efficiency with minimal degradation to generation quality. We then apply ZeUS to generate symmetric complexes of over $10{,}000$ residues with exact, untruncated attention, a scale previously intractable with any model.

title: Extending SOMPZ beyond Spectroscopic Coverage for Roman Weak Lensing
text:
Title: Extending SOMPZ beyond Spectroscopic Coverage for Roman Weak Lensing
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Precision weak lensing cosmology requires accurate galaxy redshift distributions. However, the spectroscopic samples used to characterize these distributions do not fully span the magnitude--color--redshift space of weak lensing source galaxies, necessitating extrapolation. This challenge will be critical at the depth of the Roman Space Telescope's High Latitude Imaging Survey (Roman HLIS). Using simulated LSST Year 4 and Roman HLIS photometry from the Cardinal simulations, we quantify how spectroscopic incompleteness biases photometric-redshift (photo-z) calibration and cosmological constraints. We find that the standard Self-Organizing Map p(z) (SOMPZ) method produces substantial tomographic bin overlaps and biased source redshift distributions. To address these limitations, we develop Roman-SOMPZ, which uses dedicated individual-galaxy photo-z estimators to supply redshift references for tomographic binning and redshift estimation. For the latter, we introduce UMAP-flow-z, an estimator that uses a UMAP embedding of deep-field galaxy colors to infer redshifts for phenotypes lacking spectroscopic representation. Compared with the standard pipeline, Roman-SOMPZ produces better-separated tomographic bins and lower absolute mean-redshift biases in eight of nine bins. Propagating the estimated redshift distributions into cosmological inference, we find that existing spectroscopy is adequate for early-stage weak lensing analyses in the Roman deep fields. Conversely, full medium-tier cosmology will require further improvements in redshift characterization.

title: MOOD: Benchmarking Post-Hoc OOD Detection for Materials Property Prediction
text:
Title: MOOD: Benchmarking Post-Hoc OOD Detection for Materials Property Prediction
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is essential for deploying machine learning models in high stakes scientific applications, yet methods that flag OOD inputs without retraining the model have been validated almost exclusively on image classification. We introduce MOOD (Materials Out-of-Distribution Detection), a benchmark for evaluating whether these post-hoc OOD detectors transfer to graph neural networks (GNNs) on materials property prediction. MOOD evaluates 15 post-hoc detectors and 2 supervised diagnostic probes across 4 GNN architectures, 5 MatBench tasks, and 15 physically motivated compositional and structural shifts, yielding 264 evaluation settings and over 13,000 AUROC measurements across three encoder training seeds. Our evaluation reveals three key findings. First, current post-hoc detectors perform near chance; all 15 detectors achieve an AUROC around 0.5. Second, detector failures decompose into two regimes: method bottlenecks and encoder bottlenecks. Method bottlenecks arise when supervised probes can separate in-distribution (ID) from OOD samples but unsupervised detectors fail, meaning that the embeddings contain OOD signal that current detectors do not extract. Encoder bottlenecks arise when even supervised probes fail to separate ID from OOD samples, indicating that the relevant shift is not accessible in the frozen GNN representation. Third, when OOD prediction error exceeds ID error, the AUROC of distance-based and density-based detectors correlates with the size of that gap. Collectively, these findings indicate that reliable OOD detection in scientific domains requires representation learning strategies that explicitly preserve OOD relevant signal, particularly for tasks where current GNN architectures encode no extractable signal at all.

title: Random semigroups á la Gromov
text:
Title: Random semigroups á la Gromov
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We introduce a model of random semigroups analogous to Gromov's density model for random groups. For a fixed number $n\ge 2$ of generators and a density parameter $δ\in (0,1)$, we impose a uniformly chosen set of $\lfloor n^{2δl}\rfloor$ relations of the form $u=v$, where $u,v$ are distinct words of length at most $l$, and study the resulting semigroup as $l\to\infty$. We prove that, with overwhelming probability, above density $1/2$ the semigroup is trivial, while below density $1/2$ it contains a free subsemigroup of rank two, has a Golod-Shafarevich semigroup algebra over every field, and has a homomorphic image which generates a non-elementary hyperbolic group. We also show that the small cancellation condition $C(m)$ holds with overwhelming probability whenever $δ<1/2m$. Finally, for $n\ge 3$, at critical density $1/2$ we obtain a subsequential limiting distribution on finite semigroups, with positive mass at the trivial semigroup and unbounded support in size. This contrasts with random groups, which have order at most two with overwhelming probability at critical density.

title: Load-Balanced Neural-Network-Aided Adaptive Tabulation of Phase Equilibria for Transcritical Multiphase Flows
text:
Title: Load-Balanced Neural-Network-Aided Adaptive Tabulation of Phase Equilibria for Transcritical Multiphase Flows
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Simulating high-pressure transcritical flows with phase change is critical for advanced propulsion, yet traditional first-principles approaches, vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) calculations, consume most of the runtime and frequently fail to converge. Standalone machine learning models introduce heavy evaluation overhead across large grids, while dynamic tabulation still relies on fragile iterative solvers. To resolve these limitations, this study introduces a hybrid In-Situ Adaptive Tabulation and Artificial Neural Network (ISAT-ANN) framework. A pre-trained ANN replaces the iterative solver during table expansion to guarantee crash-free operation, while ISAT enables rapid data retrieval via local linear interpolation. To eliminate parallel load imbalances, an O(N) greedy load-balancing algorithm redistributes computational tasks across cores. Coupled with Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR), the framework was validated on a Mach 5 shock-droplet interaction benchmark. It accurately captured shock-interface dynamics without instability, achieving a 2.30 times speedup in thermodynamic calculations on a single core and 2.62 times in parallel over standalone ANNs, with AMR providing an additional 2.92 times overall efficiency boost. This plug-and-play framework offers a stable, scalable path for high-fidelity multiphase flow simulations.

title: Proper generalized decomposition with synthetic preconditioning for multiscale parametric phonon transport
text:
Title: Proper generalized decomposition with synthetic preconditioning for multiscale parametric phonon transport
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Deterministic solution of the phonon Boltzmann transport equation is costly for two reasons: the distribution depends on high-dimensional phase space, and source iteration converges slowly when scattering is frequent. We address both for the steady linearized gray Callaway model in two dimensions by combining proper generalized decomposition (PGD) with the general synthetic iterative scheme (GSIS). The distribution is a sum of products of a space--azimuth factor and a polar factor. This splitting is intrinsically low-rank: along each characteristic the polar angle only stretches the in-plane optical depth, so the rank is bounded, uniformly in the Knudsen numbers, by the numerical rank of the kernel $\exp(-τ/\sinφ)$. PGD--GSIS updates the factors against a macroscopic source frozen within each alternating step and refreshed by the GSIS moment equations. A Fourier analysis shows that pure PGD, although implicit in the polar factor, moves macroscopic information only through lagged spatial sweeps and stalls like source iteration, whereas the synthetic refresh sees only third-order moments of the representation error. On an isothermal cavity, cross-plane conduction and phonon Poiseuille flow, PGD--GSIS reproduces full-order solutions at ranks 3--14, with heat-flux errors below $6\times10^{-3}$ from the diffusive to the ballistic regime and memory independent of the polar resolution. Treating the inverse Knudsen numbers as coordinates of the polar factor yields one spatial basis over four decades of both; a joint update of all polar factors, which costs only small nodal linear systems, is required for accuracy at large Knudsen numbers.

title: PhoPunct: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Transformer Architectures for Vietnamese Punctuation Restoration
text:
Title: PhoPunct: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Transformer Architectures for Vietnamese Punctuation Restoration
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Vietnamese punctuation restoration is often evaluated on relatively small benchmarks, limiting conclusions about how architectural choices scale with data volume. We present a controlled benchmark on News and Novels corpora containing 22.1 million labeled tokens (19.9M News and 2.2M Novels). We evaluate 17 architectures formed from four pretrained Transformer backbones and optional bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and conditional random field (CRF) layers, together with a PhoBERT-large-Bi-LSTM-CRF model, PhoPunct.
