In interviews, patients told a severity are rated as having nearly every symptom, so an assessment agent's recognition of absent symptoms goes untested, and scored against the stated severity the agent places a quarter of them in their band, against about half of patients given a real symptom profile. Having the model word such a profile restores half to two thirds of the variation.

title: Chiral Response of QCD Topology across the Thermal Crossover
text:
Title: Chiral Response of QCD Topology across the Thermal Crossover
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We introduce a novel relation connecting the light-quark-mass derivative of the topological susceptibility in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) to the connected correlation between the squared topological charge and the integrated light-quark scalar density. This relation gives direct access to the chiral response of QCD topology---the local logarithmic light-quark-mass derivative of the susceptibility---from a single ensemble at fixed quark masses for each temperature, without additional simulations at shifted masses. Applying this relation to $(2+1)$-flavor lattice QCD at $m_π\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$ over temperatures ranging from well below to well above the chiral crossover, we find that the response rises rapidly through the crossover from approximately unity toward two. This evolution corresponds to a change from nearly linear to nearly quadratic dependence of the topological susceptibility on the light-quark mass. Using the chiral response as the exponent of a local power law in the light-quark mass, we determine its effective amplitude from the topological susceptibility. This amplitude exhibits a maximum near the crossover temperature, reflecting the competition between the decreasing topological susceptibility and the increasing chiral response. These results reveal a thermal reorganization of the quark-mass dependence of QCD topology beyond the suppression of topological fluctuations alone.

title: Mudskippers use tail thrusting to help crutching to move on mud of various wetness
text:
Title: Mudskippers use tail thrusting to help crutching to move on mud of various wetness
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

At the water-land interface, amphibious fishes encounter wet flowable substrates made of granular solid-water mixtures, which can stay solid or flow like a fluid. As these substrates become wetter or drier, their yield strength (at which solid-fluid transition occurs) and cohesion (how sticky they are) both change, challenging locomotion. Despite substantial understanding of tetrapod locomotion on flowable substrates (mostly dry sand), we know little about how amphibious fishes cope with wet flowable substrates of various wetness. Here, we studied mudskippers on clay mud of controlled, variable wetness over the range where solid-fluid transition occurs. As mud became wetter, its strength decreased by 100-fold, leading the animal to sink deeper, with larger areas of body and fins contacting mud. By contrast, mud stuck most easily at intermediate wetness. The increased sinkage and contact and stickiness change caused more mud to stick to and pull against the animal on wetter mud. We also tested dry mud, which stuck to animal fins as its mucus dried. Despite these challenges, the mudskipper predominately used a conserved crutching gait on all except the wettest mud tested, with a modest performance reduction. When normal crutching became less effective, the animal assisted it with tail thrusting, by bending and straightening it to push downward and backward to generate additional thrust and lift, or even thrusting the tail to jump. These observations suggest that mudskipper's crutching motor program is well adapted to its native muddy substrates but inflexible, with most novelty in tail use.

title: Where Did the Evidence Go? Diagnosing Proof-Set Loss in Long-Term Conversational Memory
text:
Title: Where Did the Evidence Go? Diagnosing Proof-Set Loss in Long-Term Conversational Memory
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Long-term conversational question answering can require several separated dialogue turns that support an answer only together. We introduce EviCover, a retrieval approach designed to retain this complementary evidence. It converts questions into observable evidence requirements, checks requirement coverage using retrieved source identifiers, and selects turns jointly. We track annotated support sets - the benchmark-labeled dialogue turns associated with each question - through retrieval, reranking, and final answer-generation context. We evaluate the baseline memory pipeline on generated, human-verified LoCoMo conversations and human-written REALTALK conversations, and examine EviCover on REALTALK's 108 multi-hop questions. Compared with the hybrid lexical/dense baseline, support-turn recall among 60 candidate turns rises from 0.526 to 0.575, and recall in the final ten-turn context rises from 0.349 to 0.379. The evidence funnel identifies separate discovery and selection failures, while paired answer evaluation shows that greater evidence recall does not yet establish a correctness gain. This analysis locates where complementary evidence is lost and distinguishes evidence retrieval from its use in answer generation.

title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
text:
Title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. This generates a direct dark matter-dark energy interaction. We show that generic models with a significant dark matter-dark energy coupling suffer from a naturalness problem: the Coleman-Weinberg potential induced by the interaction is typically much larger than the dark energy scale. In our model, the corrections arise from a monodromy tower of dyon states, allowing them to be exponentially suppressed. In the minimal setup, the interaction strength is predicted to be $\sim 0.1\%$, below the sensitivity of current observations. We discuss scenarios in which cosmological population of higher-charge dyons can enhance the interaction to the percent level, producing an apparent phantom dark energy equation of state. We further show that the parameter space of the axion-monopole model preferred by fitting the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) results can also naturally explain the cosmic birefringence with a small anomaly coefficient.

title: Distributed Zeroth-Order Composite Finite-Sum Optimization via Incremental Variance Reduction
text:
Title: Distributed Zeroth-Order Composite Finite-Sum Optimization via Incremental Variance Reduction
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study decentralized composite finite-sum optimization over a fixed connected undirected network, where agents access local component functions through function evaluations and share a possibly nonsmooth convex regularizer. In this setting, standard two-point gradient estimators can retain nonvanishing variance at a solution, complicating their integration with gradient tracking. We propose Distributed Zeroth-Order Incremental Variance Reduction (Distributed ZIVR), which combines incrementally updated component-gradient estimates with a proximal gradient-tracking scheme. The method admits an implementation using a constant number of function evaluations per agent at every iteration, without intermittent full-component or full-coordinate refreshes. For convex smooth component functions and strongly convex local averages, we establish linear convergence up to a controllable finite-difference error. With the finite-difference radius chosen for the target accuracy, Chebyshev-accelerated mixing yields a per-agent oracle complexity of $\widetilde{O}(d(m+κ)\log(1/ε))$ for expected squared solution error $ε$, where $d$ is the dimension, $m$ is the number of components per agent, and $κ$ is the condition number. This matches the centralized ZIVR oracle bound, while the communication bound has only an inverse square-root dependence on the network spectral gap. Experiments on logistic and robust regression demonstrate rapid reduction of solution and consensus errors.

title: RootQuantV2: Adapting a Vision Foundation Model for Root-Trait Regression from Minirhizotron Imagery
text:
Title: RootQuantV2: Adapting a Vision Foundation Model for Root-Trait Regression from Minirhizotron Imagery
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

A lack of high-throughput phenotyping solutions for root traits in field-grown crops has severely constrained understanding and improvement of below-ground traits and processes. Minirhizotrons are the standard non-destructive root-phenotyping method in field environments. Computer vision solutions are needed to allow automated trait estimation at scale, but training data is scarce and human annotations are often inaccessible because they reside in proprietary software that only exports per-image scalar totals of root length and surface area. Nevertheless, large numeric archives of these root traits already exist. RootQuant showed that the traits can be predicted directly from the whole image by regression, thus removing manually traced masks from the pipeline; RootQuantV2 takes that idea further by replacing RootQuant's CNN backbone with a self-supervised ViT. We adapt a frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 with a hybrid parameter-efficient scheme. Training only 11.9M parameters (3.78% of the model), RootQuantV2 achieves length and area $R^2$ of 0.950 and 0.930, respectively, while lowering length/area RMSE by 24.3%/20.7% over RootQuant. RootQuantV2 thus repurposes legacy numeric archives for high-throughput, automated root trait estimation.

title: Dual-Corrected Stochastic Block Model ($\text{DC}^2\text{SBM}$): A Generalized Structure Detection Method for Attributed Networks
text:
Title: Dual-Corrected Stochastic Block Model ($\text{DC}^2\text{SBM}$): A Generalized Structure Detection Method for Attributed Networks
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Community detection in attributed networks is one of the core tasks of complex network analysis. The stochastic block model (SBM) and its variants are able to detect generalized network structures such as assortative, disassortative and mixed structures. However, existing generative methods either ignore node heterogeneity, or characterize node activity in the topological and attribute dimensions by one and the same factor, making it difficult to correctly model node activity when the two kinds of activity are decoupled. In this paper, we propose the Dual-Corrected Stochastic Block Model ($\text{DC}^2\text{SBM}$), which introduces independent correction factors---a topological degree factor and an attribute abundance factor---into the link-generation and attribute-generation channels, respectively, thereby effectively decoupling node activity from membership inference, and which further introduces a global scaling parameter to resolve the mismatch between the normalization constraints and the network scale. The model is inferred by the expectation--maximization (EM) algorithm, and the newly introduced factors cancel out completely in the posterior computation, so that no additional computational cost is incurred. Experiments on synthetic and real attributed networks show that DC^2SBM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in community detection accuracy, with an especially pronounced advantage when the topological signal is weak. The two correction factors can be recovered independently from their respective channels without cross-talk. Analytical as well as controlled experiments further demonstrate that modeling with a single shared factor fails when the two kinds of activity are decoupled---a regime that is prevalent in real networks---thereby validating the necessity of dual independent correction.

title: Asymmetric Reheating of a Dark Sector
text:
Title: Asymmetric Reheating of a Dark Sector
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We study asymmetric post-inflationary reheating in a framework with two sequestered MSSM-like sectors (the ``visible'' and ``dark'' sectors) with different supersymmetry-breaking scales, with dark matter corresponding to the lightest dark baryons. In this setup, independent Affleck-Dine dynamics in the two sectors offers a natural explanation for the comparable abundances of visible and dark matter. We relate the resulting temperature hierarchy to the inflaton's partial decay widths in different kinematical regimes, where it may decay into dark sector particles via 2-, 3- or 4-body processes. The latter case yields the most asymmetric reheating scenario, and we discuss the implications of this regime for the dark sector's thermal history, namely regarding the corresponding strong and weak interactions. While in this kinematical regime the contribution of light dark sector degrees of freedom to $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ is negligible, we show that it increases significantly in the regime where 3-body decays are possible, particularly near the threshold for dark Higgs pair-production where $ΔN_{\rm eff}^{\max} \simeq 0.078$. The current combined BBN+CMB+BAO bound leaves only a narrow allowed interval of the 2-body decay regime immediately above threshold, while next-generation CMB experiments could probe slightly below it.

title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
text:
Title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Bone scaffolds must reconcile a macroscale mechanical response with microscale geometric feasibility, yet conventional approaches to their design restrict attainable constitutive properties. This work presents a concurrent two-scale topology optimization framework; a conditional rectified flow generates periodic lattice microstructures, which are then refined in latent space by exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities. The resulting unit-cell geometries and their spatial assignments are jointly optimized under mechanical and feature-size constraints. In a distal rabbit femur benchmark, all eight flow-started refinements produce printable cells with maximum relative errors under 1\% across six prescribed engineering moduli. Constructing the implant from a single tiled cell reproduces intact whole-femur compliance within 0.1\% and regional strain energy within 0.35\% under four loading conditions. In human femoral reconstruction, multiscale concurrent optimization produces a cortical mid-shaft scaffold with porosity 63\% while satisfying the compliance constraint within 2\% under walking and stair-climbing loads. It achieves an 84\% porosity on a proximal cancellous scaffold with strain-energy deviations below 0.25\% under the same loads. Analysis of the learned representations reveals distinct architectural families in latent space. Further, the attention heads of the rectified-flow transformer specialize for spatial shifts -- learning the analogue of a finite-difference stencil -- and coordinate symmetries, with ablations showing their influence on generated topologies. These results establish a route to printable, mechanically constrained scaffold designs. The framework is general enough for extending to many other multiscale structural design applications including topology-microstructure co-design in metal additive manufacturing.

title: Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime
text:
Title: Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We establish quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximations for edge-count fluctuations in dense exponential random graphs at single-phase criticality of any fixed even order $2m_*\ge 4$. The Hamiltonians use injective homomorphism counts of fixed simple graphs, with nonnegative leading coefficients for the higher-order terms. In bounded calibrated windows, edge-density fluctuations on the scale $n^{-1/m_*}$ admit an explicit non-Gaussian approximation with error $O(n^{-1/m_*})$. For parameter perturbations by fixed multiples of $n^{-1}$ with a nonzero first-order drift correction at the critical density, the deterministically centered edge count admits a Gaussian approximation on the scale $n^{(3m_*-2)/(2m_*-1)}$, with error $O(n^{-1/(2m_*-1)})$. Both rates hold in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. The key step is to construct auxiliary kernels for exterior graphs outside an event of exponentially small probability. These kernels contract uniformly on the full row state space and agree with the conditional Gibbs updates on typical row configurations, yielding the conditional cumulant estimates used in Stein's method.

title: An Adaptive Short-Step Variant of BroxGD with Linear Convergence under Quadratic Growth
text:
Title: An Adaptive Short-Step Variant of BroxGD with Linear Convergence under Quadratic Growth
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Broximal Gradient Descent (BroxGD), recently analyzed by Richtárik et al. (arXiv:2605.08850v1), is a projection-free sister method to Projected Gradient Descent (ProjGD) for solving $\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)$, where $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ and $\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ is nonempty, closed and convex. The method performs local linear minimization over the feasible set intersected with a Euclidean ball and carefully prescribed radius. Like ProjGD, BroxGD enjoys linear convergence in the smooth strongly convex setting, with the same condition-number dependence. However, the known radius rule leading to linear convergence requires unavailable information and is therefore impractical. We develop an adaptive short-step variant of BroxGD which converges linearly for smooth convex functions under quadratic growth (generalizing strong convexity), without requiring unavailable information. We use $$z_k\in\arg\min_{z\in\mathcal X\cap\mathbb B(x_k,t_k)}\langle\nabla f(x_k),z\rangle,\quad x_{k+1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{S_k}(x_k-\nabla f(x_k)/L),$$ where $L$ is the smoothness constant of $f$, $\mathbb B(x,t)$ is the Euclidean ball centered at $x$ of radius $t$, and $S_k$ is the line segment connecting $x_k$ and $z_k$. The radius is updated by $t_{k+1}=\max\{\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|,t_k/2\}$. Projection onto $S_k$ requires only scalar clipping. Assuming an exact local linear minimization oracle, each update uses one oracle call. For any positive initial radius, we bound all oracle calls to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ and obtain $O((L/α)\log(1/\varepsilon))$ for fixed initialization, where $α=\min\{α_0,L\}$ and $α_0>0$ is the quadratic-growth constant.

title: Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification of Breast-Cancer Pathology AI Agreement under Reader- and Annotation-Condition-Dependent Reference Labels
text:
Title: Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification of Breast-Cancer Pathology AI Agreement under Reader- and Annotation-Condition-Dependent Reference Labels
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Human reference labels used to evaluate medical AI can vary across readers and annotation workflows. We quantified agreement of a fixed pathology AI system with a future qualified reader without treating inferred consensus as error-free biological truth. Linked Evaluation and Unbiased NuCLS multirater data were analyzed using a fixed external HoVer-Net decision vector. The selected frame contained 1,144 anchors, 52 fields of view, five slides/patients, and five primary readers. The target was fixed-AI agreement with a future reader, with descriptive contrast $Δ=θ_E-θ_U$. Analyses included raw agreement and iMRMC benchmarks, reader-only and shared-detectability Bayesian models, structural sensitivities, adversarial simulations, and predictive assessment. Among 5,188 reader-anchor pairs observed in both conditions, 19.62% changed AI-agreement state, while raw agreement was 0.5466 in Unbiased and 0.5473 in Evaluation. The reader-only model gave $Δ=-0.0008$ (95% CrI, $-0.0033$ to $0.0008$), and the shared-detectability model gave $Δ\approx0$ ($-0.0140$ to $0.0127$). Across structural perturbations, absolute agreement ranged from 0.420 to 0.646 in Unbiased and 0.409 to 0.640 in Evaluation. Frozen adversarial simulations met the comparative-stability criterion (median $R=0.295$; 14/16 model-scenario cells had $R<1$). Held-out-AI prediction supported shared predictive information, but varied by slide composition. The Evaluation-minus-Unbiased contrast was comparatively stable, whereas absolute agreement was structurally sensitive. These findings do not establish equivalence, causal assistance effects, biological accuracy, or new-patient transportability. Evaluations using variable human references should report reader population, selected frame, observation mechanism, and structural sensitivity.

title: Point defects and primary radiation damage in Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys from molecular dynamics
text:
Title: Point defects and primary radiation damage in Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys from molecular dynamics
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Co-free Fe-Ni-Cr-Mn high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are candidates for nuclear structural applications. We used molecular dynamics with the EAM-21 potential, stiffened at short range, to study five HEAs that have been irradiated experimentally: Fe37Ni34Cr16Mn13 (ES1), Fe35Ni35Cr15Mn15 (P35), Fe46Ni22Cr15Mn17 (Y3), Fe27Ni28Cr18Mn27 (Kumar) and Fe30Ni30Cr10Mn30 (C30). They were compared with pure Ni, Fe60Ni40, the Fe70Ni10Cr20 model alloy of 316L, and Fe50Ni34Cr16, which is ES1 with Mn replaced by Fe. We calculated stacking fault energies, threshold displacement energies, point-defect formation and migration energies, and 1015 displacement cascades from 5 to 40 keV at 300 and 823 K. The stacking fault energy follows the Ni content: 19-44 mJ/m^2 in the alloys and 113 mJ/m^2 in Ni. Compared with the Mn-free alloys, the HEAs have lower threshold displacement energies (48-56 against 64-74 eV) and lower dumbbell formation energies, and Mn is the element most transported by interstitials. All the concentrated alloys leave about the same number of Frenkel pairs, 56-72 at 40 keV, half the number in Ni. At 40 keV, 54-58% of the interstitials are in clusters in the HEAs, against 67-71% in Fe60Ni40, Fe70Ni10Cr20 and Fe50Ni34Cr16 and 82% in Ni. At the same cluster size, clusters of 4-12 interstitials are faulted about half as often in the HEAs, and this does not follow the stacking fault energy. The surviving interstitials are enriched in Mn in the HEAs and in Ni in the Mn-free alloys, and depleted in Cr. The results support direct loop formation in cascades in Fe60Ni40 and Fe70Ni10Cr20 and less of it in ES1.

title: Cosmic String Networks with Time-Varying Tension: Field-Theory Simulations and an Analytic Model
text:
Title: Cosmic String Networks with Time-Varying Tension: Field-Theory Simulations and an Analytic Model
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Cosmic string networks are predicted in some early-Universe scenarios, and in certain models, the string tension becomes a function of time. Here, for the first time, we perform numerical field-theory simulations of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension in an expanding Universe. We use a modified Abelian-Higgs model in which the tension varies as a power law of the scale factor $a$, that is, $μ\propto a^{-2m}$. We perform simulations on grids containing $8192^3$ grid points, with $m\in[-0.5,0.5]$, during radiation- and matter-dominated epochs. We find that, in our model, a string network forms only when the potential decreases more slowly than the amplitude of field oscillations redshifts due to the expansion of the Universe. Once formed, the network evolves according to the standard scaling behavior predicted by the velocity-dependent one-scale (VOS) model. To interpret these results, we compare the predictions of the VOS model with time-dependent tension to the asymptotic values obtained from the numerical simulations. Overall, we find good agreement between the numerical field-theory simulations and the calibrated VOS model. These results shed light on the evolution of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension and have potential implications for their observational signatures.

title: Thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich Effect in the circumgalactic medium - III: does richness matter?
text:
Title: Thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich Effect in the circumgalactic medium - III: does richness matter?
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We measure the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich Effect in the circumgalactic/intragroup medium (CGM/IGrM) of 7 million $\rm M_{200c} = 10^{12-14}$M$_\odot$ $z \leqslant 1$ DESI Legacy Survey galaxies/groups using ACT+Planck observations, and investigate for the first time how the thermal pressure depends on richness. We detect the one-halo term down to 10$^{12.2}$M$_\odot$ at $5.8σ$. While several mass-richness bins are well described by the standard GNFW thermal-pressure profile ($β=5.49,r_o=0$), others favor a flatter and/or miscentered profile ($β=1.3-4.0,r_o>0.1 \rm R_{200c}$), with the mass dependence of this pattern varying with richness. The wide variety of thermal pressure profiles across mass and richness indicates a range of physical regimes, from dominant thermal feedback to efficient cooling with subdominant thermal feedback, and even substantial cooling. In some mass bins, the super-virial ($\approx2-7 \rm T_{200c}$) temperature floor (the lowest temperature allowed by the data for baryon-sufficient halos) points to significant heating. However, dominant kinetic-mode feedback is not essential anywhere, challenging a universal (ejective)feedback-vs-gravity picture. The slope of the thermal energy-mass relation in IGrM is consistent with self-similarity, but in the CGM it falls below self-similarity by $7.3σ$. This makes halos of relatively low mass and richness the dominant contributors to the universe's thermal energy budget at $z\leqslant1$. We therefore argue that calibrations of thermal energy scaling relations must move beyond the convention of using mass as the sole demarcator and instead incorporate additional intrinsic and environmental properties of galaxies.

title: Molecular conical intersections with odd electron number are realizations of the topological Yang monopole
text:
Title: Molecular conical intersections with odd electron number are realizations of the topological Yang monopole
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

The two-level conical intersection of a molecule with odd electron number in the absence of magnetic field obeys time-reversal symmetry $T^{2}=-1$ (referred to as the $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection), and has a five-dimensional branching space due to the Kramer degeneracy. Similar to how the conical intersection of a molecule in a magnetic field ($T^{2}=0$) behaves as the Dirac monopole, the $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection behaves as the Yang monopole, an mathematical generalization of Dirac monopole with SU(2) gauge field and SO(5) symmetry. This implies that we can study topological properties of $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersections in chemistry based on what is known about Yang monopole in high energy physics. In this work, we present a few mathematical tools to study this connection. First, we show that geometric algebra and quaternion numbers together provides a natural way to utilize the $T^{2}=-1$ time reversal symmetry and the SO(5) symmetry in scaled coordinates, making it simple to derive eigenfunctions, Berry connection and Berry curvature of $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection. In particular, this approach provides a simple proof that when viewed from the upper or lower states, the $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection behaves as the self-dual or self-antidual Yang monopole with second Chern number $C_{2}=+\frac{1}{4}$ or $-\frac{1}{4}$ respectively. In addition, we propose a visualization method for the SU(2) Berry connection of $T^{2}=-1$ conical intersection. This is achieved by showing that the nonzero part of the Berry connection induces Hopf-fibration on the $S^{3}$ longitude space, and is further visualized through stereographic projection.

title: Continuous modeling of manipulative participation for stance analysis: Online discourse on the 2024 Street Animal Law in Türkiye
text:
Title: Continuous modeling of manipulative participation for stance analysis: Online discourse on the 2024 Street Animal Law in Türkiye
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Studies of online political discourse commonly infer public opinion through stance analysis while implicitly assuming that observed user participation is authentic. Meanwhile, studies focusing on detecting manipulative participation are typically modeling it as a binary phenomenon, overlooking the varying degrees to which users may engage in coordinated or inauthentic behavior. This study proposes a continuous modeling approach for manipulative participation and examines its integration with stance analysis. Using online discourse on the 2024 Street Animal Law in Türkiye as a case study, we collected a dataset comprising 7,320,574 tweets from 537,994 users. From this corpus, 301 users were selected through a high-information sampling strategy and manually annotated by domain experts using a 10-criterion rubric that yields user-level continuous manipulative participation scores. Evaluation under a unified user-level cross-validation protocol showed that the proposed framework accurately estimates both manipulative participation and user stance, with gradient boosting methods providing the best manipulative participation estimates and BERTurk achieving the highest stance classification performance. External validation on an independently annotated user set demonstrated good generalization performance. The findings support modeling manipulative participation as a continuous construct rather than a binary label, providing a more informative basis for computational analyses of the relationship between manipulative participation and stance in online political discourse.

title: OCP-Based Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Quadrotor Trajectory Tracking
text:
Title: OCP-Based Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Quadrotor Trajectory Tracking
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Fast online optimization is essential for nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) on resource-limited aerial platforms. This paper presents an analytical-derivative NMPC solver for quadrotor trajectory tracking. For the state-affine translational model with held thrust and attitude commands, fourth-order Runge--Kutta integration yields an exact discrete-time prediction map. Forward--backward difference equations provide the gradient and exact Hessian of the finite-horizon cost condensed over the input sequence. These derivatives drive a nested optimal-control-based direction recursion, while a shifted warm start reuses the preceding solution. The resulting solver addresses the unconstrained tracking problem without a general-purpose nonlinear programming package. Gazebo experiments show comparable tracking accuracy to iLQR and two acados SQP configurations, with mean solver-time speedups of $1.97$--$2.30$. In onboard flight tests, the mean solver time is $0.3121$\,ms, corresponding to speedups of $3.37$--$5.77$ over the same baselines. The largest measured solver time is $3.7754$\,ms within a $20$-ms control period. These measurements cover the numerical solver and exclude estimation, communication, and command publication.

title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
text:
Title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Although safety can be improved through model fine-tuning, such approaches can be computationally expensive and may degrade previously acquired capabilities through catastrophic forgetting. Recent jailbreak defenses have therefore explored targeted interventions on specific model components associated with unsafe behavior. However, existing approaches typically decouple two inherently related decisions: where to intervene and how to modify the selected components. Such sequential optimization may be suboptimal because the optimal intervention location can depend on the intervention applied there, and vice versa. In this work, we introduce AttentionSwitch, the first jailbreak defense to jointly optimize intervention sites and strengths within a frozen LLM. Specifically, AttentionSwitch learns a sparse set of attention heads together with query-conditioned multiplicative scaling factors, allowing the outputs of the selected heads to be either attenuated or amplified without altering the directions of their representations. Across popular language models and jailbreak attacks, AttentionSwitch outperforms existing defenses, with particularly strong results when training data is scarce.

title: Task- and dataset-specific information in protein language models
text:
Title: Task- and dataset-specific information in protein language models
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Protein language models (PLMs) have transferred the latest advances from natural language processing to computational biology. These models, trained on large corpora of protein sequence data, are widely used to translate amino acid sequences into latent-space embeddings, ready for use in diverse downstream tasks (DTs). By consensus, embeddings from the models' last layers are used, while the models' internal behavior remains poorly understood. We analyzed 13 PLMs across 15 DTs and 9 datasets to assess the value of embeddings from intermediate PLM layers. We trained probe models on embeddings from each layer, compared their performance, and showed that the last layers of PLMs rarely produced embeddings that led to the best results on downstream tasks. Furthermore, we identified a connection between how models learn a certain DT and the similarity between that DT and the pre-training objective. For example, for residue-level downstream tasks, we observed a steady increase in performance across almost all PLM layers, which we attributed to their similarity to most PLMs' pre-training objectives. To allow the community to capitalize on our findings, we provide PLMSommelier, a Python package that automatically identifies the best PLM layer for a given DT with ~98% accuracy and creates a truncated model using only the early layers up to the best-performing layer. This will help users save time and memory during inference and yield better predictive performance.

title: Stability, discretization, and optimality of continuous-time causal optimal transport
text:
Title: Stability, discretization, and optimality of continuous-time causal optimal transport
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We prove stability of continuous-time causal and bicausal optimal transport problems when both marginals converge in adapted Wasserstein distance along common vanishing time shifts. The marginal laws, filtrations, and costs may all vary, while the limit remains the original causal or bicausal transport problem. This allows for time discretization and the approximation of transport problems between non-degenerate scalar fractional stochastic differential equations by their Wong--Zakai schemes. We further establish sufficient conditions so that the synchronous coupling is optimal for the bicausal transport problem between scalar fractional stochastic differential equations under continuous, nonnegative submodular costs of polynomial growth. This result covers all Hurst parameters \(H\in(0,1)\) up to an additional order-preserving commutator condition on the corresponding coefficients for the rough regime \(H\in(0,1/2)\).

title: reComposer: Editable Planning for Controllable Image Generation
text:
Title: reComposer: Editable Planning for Controllable Image Generation
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Prompt-based image generation makes it easy to produce visual assets, but offers little support for engaging with the creative process. Prompting collapses interdependent creative decisions into a monolithic instruction and returns a finished image, leaving control limited to revising the prompt or correcting the model's output. We present reComposer, a process-oriented image-generation interface built around editable planning, which decomposes users' evolving intent into meaningful creative decisions - such as subject, composition, or palette - and collaborates with users to explore underspecified goals and alternatives. reComposer supports conversational and direct manipulation of the plan, moving between concept-level intent and visual-level control. We evaluated reComposer with 8 design and non-design professionals. Compared to prompting, participants felt greater control and ownership while developing visual assets, exploring alternatives, and iterating on details. Our findings suggest how shifting generative AI interaction from specifying outputs to shaping process can support creative thinking alongside asset production.

title: Vector Lyapunov functions for nonconvex constrained optimization
text:
Title: Vector Lyapunov functions for nonconvex constrained optimization
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Nonconvex constrained optimization problems are commonly solved by a Newton method for necessary conditions (sequential linear/quadratic programming) or a barrier reformulation (interior-point methods). We present a vector Lyapunov analysis for Newton-type algorithms based on constraint violation and optimality of the primal solutions to a sequence of approximate optimization problems. We thus prove local stability and convergence by constructing a strict Lyapunov function for the primal solution.

title: Constrained Gradient Equilibrium: Approachability under Locally Constrained Adversaries
text:
Title: Constrained Gradient Equilibrium: Approachability under Locally Constrained Adversaries
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Gradient equilibrium (GEQ) is a recent framework in online learning that requires the time-averaged gradients along the learner's trajectory to vanish. We study GEQ when the learner is constrained and ask when such an equilibrium remains achievable in an adversarial environment. We first show that constrained GEQ (CGEQ) can be impossible even under simple and slowly varying constraints, motivating imposing local temporal structure on the adversary. We then develop an approachability framework for CGEQ under locally constrained adversaries, and obtain necessary and sufficient characterizations in the spirit of classical Blackwell approachability. Beyond these theoretical characterizations, we provide an algorithmic principle that converts window-wise no-regret learners into CGEQ algorithms under a local feasibility condition with margin. Experiments on synthetic and real data demonstrate that the resulting algorithms perform strongly in both achieving GEQ and respecting the constraints.

title: Structure Before Intelligence: Gating What Agentic Scientific Workflows Release
text:
Title: Structure Before Intelligence: Gating What Agentic Scientific Workflows Release
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

An agentic scientific workflow can run to completion and still release wrong results: a silent numerical error, a stale input, or a defect in a shared upstream step can contaminate several outputs while a sibling branch stays correct. We treat trust in such results as a release decision. A harness around the workflow's directed acyclic graph (DAG) decides which outputs may be used: it enforces mandatory checks, contains failures to the affected branch, recomputes from tracked versions, adds validators, and releases a result only if a risk model estimates its probability of being invalid as low. Language-model agents work inside the harness, choosing corrective actions and reviewing releases, but cannot override it. On 60 held-out paired instances of two workflows with injected faults, we switched components on and off. Each supplied a different property. Containment and recovery raised the number of correct results. Validation supplied safety: fixed rules without validation released 37 invalid results, while validating every candidate released none. Risk estimation supplied efficiency, matching that safety with 31% fewer validators at somewhat lower yield, although better targeting than random validation was not shown. Lineage evidence helped on one workflow. The language model added no measurable benefit: whether invalid results escaped depended on the harness, not the model. This proof of concept points to a practical path: placing agents inside explicit release-control structure can keep released scientific results trustworthy, and it gives more capable agents a measurable baseline to improve on.

title: When Answer Decodability Is Not a Decision: Separating Final-Answer and Imminent-Emission Signals in Chain-of-Thought
text:
Title: When Answer Decodability Is Not a Decision: Separating Final-Answer and Imminent-Emission Signals in Chain-of-Thought
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Answer probes applied to chain-of-thought hidden states are often read as evidence that a language model has already decided its final response. This reading overlooks a competing signal, the candidate the model is about to mention. We introduce emission-controlled dual-target probing (ECDP), which fits the same low-rank reader family separately to the imminent mention and to the final answer at identical positions, with target-specific nulls and thresholds fixed before any fit. On correct DecisionDepth (DD) rollouts in which a distractor is mentioned before the final answer, Qwen3.5-4B decodes the next mention at .966 (null .234) but the final answer only at .221 (null .186), an emission gap of .696 [.648, .744]; Llama-3.1-8B gives .575 [.514, .632]. This pattern is not universal. In a pre-specified evaluation of Qwen3-8B with thinking enabled on held-out MMLU questions, using a full-prefix attention reader over every thinking position, both targets are decodable and the final answer is read far more strongly (mention-minus-answer lift -.398 [-.459, -.336] at layer 22 over 467 questions). Model, task, positions, and reader change together between these settings, and an attempted matched comparison on DD produced no valid statistics because the imminent-mention probe did not train reliably, so we do not identify what reverses the order. On DD, planted-signal controls show that the reader recovers an injected final-answer signal at one tenth of full dose. Answer-candidate decodability is therefore target-relative and protocol-dependent: a strong answer readout does not by itself establish when a model commits, and a probe that fails to train is not evidence that the information is absent. ECDP is a practical control for distinguishing imminent text emission from evidence of a settled decision.

title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
text:
Title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Uncertainty quantification is crucial in scientific machine learning, where models inform safety-critical tasks such as flood forecasting, financial risk management, and thermal control in machines. Conformal prediction provides distribution-free coverage guarantees, but in time-dependent settings common to physics and engineering, these guarantees can break down, leading to systematic undercoverage. We study this problem in the context of surrogate models for time-dependent physical systems described by partial differential equations. We prove that in a function space setting, distributions at arbitrarily close times can be mutually singular, making exact coverage guarantees impossible. We further show that in discretized settings, the total variation distance between distributions often saturates exponentially fast with the grid resolution, mandating restrictions on the spatial discretization to ensure coverage. Finally, for certain settings, we show how to use principled weighted conformal prediction to obtain finite-sample coverage guarantees over growing time horizons.

title: Audiovisual diarization of overlapping click trains in sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) vocal sparring using a three-hydrophone array
text:
Title: Audiovisual diarization of overlapping click trains in sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) vocal sparring using a three-hydrophone array
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

The individual attribution of sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) vocalizations during surface interactions constitutes a methodological challenge due to acoustic overlaps, multipath propagation, body shadowing, and indistinguishable inter-pulse intervals among similar-sized individuals. A multimodal audio-visual workflow is presented to deinterleave and attribute uncharacterized click trains produced by immature males during ``vocal sparring'' using a portable three-hydrophone array coupled with synchronized video. The approach combines spectro-temporal tracking, based on inter-click interval dynamics and the Constant-Q Transform, with spatial time-difference-of-arrival modeling projected onto the image plane for optical validation. Analysis of 2,655 manually validated clicks shows that purely acoustic clustering diarization errors remain low, peaking at 25.79% only during extreme temporal superpositions. Integrating the optical modality resolves residual spatial indeterminacies; although near-planar array geometry induces vertical ambiguities, the system achieves up to 100% horizontal visual concordance for primary emitters. Crucially, this framework successfully reconstructed and assigned 11 distinct, intertwined click trains totaling 882 clicks to specific focal individuals despite near-field tactile constraints. Because ethological descriptions remain incomplete without identifying the emitter, explicitly correlating these emissions with physical kinematics provides the fine-scale resolution required to define this socio-acoustic behavior.

title: An Effective Spoken Language Understanding Approach Leveraging Query-Adaptive Intent Detection
text:
Title: An Effective Spoken Language Understanding Approach Leveraging Query-Adaptive Intent Detection
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Large language models enable fine-tuning-free spoken language understanding (SLU) through in-context learning, but direct query-based retrieval may select semantically similar yet intent irrelevant demonstrations. This paper presents Query-Adaptive Intent Detection via Prototype Extraction (APEX), a two-stage retrieval framework that first selects candidate intents using intent-level prototypes and then retrieves contextual exemplars within the selected intent space. Experiments on the SLURP dataset evaluate joint SLU performance using Exact Match Accuracy (EMA) under full-transcript and perplexity-stratified conditions, with additional retrieval analysis on ASR-generated transcripts. Compared with query-based retrieval, APEX improves EMA by 4.34 and 3.97 percentage points with Qwen3 4B and Gemma-3-4B, respectively, on full transcripts. Under high-perplexity inputs, APEX also yields EMA gains of 7.66 and 2.13 percentage points. Retrieval analysis further indicates that prototype-guided candidate selection achieves higher ground truth intent coverage across multiple input conditions.

title: Evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$
text:
Title: Evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Correlations and topology are central pillars in the study of emergent electronic phases. Topological flat bands near the Fermi level unite these concepts, providing a route towards correlated topological phenomena and unconventional magnetism. Despite theoretical predictions, momentum-resolved observation of a topological flat band at the Fermi level has remained elusive. Using angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we observe a flat band at the Fermi level within the topologically non-trivial electronic structure of the magnetic kagome Weyl semimetal Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$. We further uncover a strong temperature dependence in which the flat band shifts across the Fermi level, accompanied by a reconstruction of the Fermi surface. Strikingly, this evolution occurs on the same temperature scale as previously reported anomalies in the magnetic response. Together, these results provide evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$, establishing a microscopic setting in which topology, electronic correlations, and magnetism become intertwined.

title: Quantum trajectory of a spin oscillator, continuous retrodiction beyond the Heisenberg uncertainty relation
text:
Title: Quantum trajectory of a spin oscillator, continuous retrodiction beyond the Heisenberg uncertainty relation
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The Heisenberg uncertainty relation in quantum mechanics limits the precision of predicting the outcome of measurements of any non-commuting observables. However, this restriction does not apply to retrodictive guessing of the outcomes of past measurements. Here, we experimentally demonstrate this using a spin oscillator consisting of $ 5.17 \times 10^{10}$ rubidium atoms. Through weak continuous measurements, we monitor canonical spin observables $\hat{x}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\hat{p}_{\mathrm{A}}$ with $[\hat{x}_{\mathrm{A}},\hat{p}_{\mathrm{A}}] = i\hbar$. By combining information obtained before and after time $t$, we retrodict the outcomes of measurements of $\hat{x}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\hat{p}_{\mathrm{A}}$ at time $t$ with variances that remain, concurrently over 1.4 hours, $\sim$ 1.01 dB below the bound set by the Heisenberg uncertainty relation. We also infer and demonstrate the ability to retrodict, with the same precision, the measurement outcomes for arbitrary quadratures of the spin oscillator. This brings interesting prospects for further research on quantum measurements, and for quantum-enhanced sensing that combines trajectory and entanglement strategies.

title: A general-purpose multi-path stacked coupling for stochastic reaction networks
text:
Title: A general-purpose multi-path stacked coupling for stochastic reaction networks
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Stochastic reaction networks are continuous-time Markov chain models for interacting populations, with applications in biochemistry, epidemiology, ecology, and related areas. Coupling multiple stochastic reaction networks effectively is a fundamental challenge in stochastic simulation. Existing variance-reducing coupling methods are typically designed for pairs of processes, though specialized multi-path constructions have been developed for particular applications. To fill this gap, we introduce the multi-path stacked coupling (MSC), a space-time Poisson construction that jointly simulates a finite collection of stochastic reaction networks with common reaction channels and reaction vectors, but possibly different intensity functions and initial conditions. Each pairwise marginal of MSC has the same law as the corresponding split-coupled pair, allowing existing variance bounds to transfer directly; in finite-state settings, we also obtain first-order expansions for the mean and second moment of finite-difference numerators. We demonstrate the framework through three sensitivity estimation tasks requiring several nearby parameterized paths: estimating many first derivatives simultaneously, estimating a single first derivative using a wider finite-difference stencil, and estimating higher-order derivatives. Numerical experiments on a processive phosphorylation network demonstrate strong performance in each of the three application areas considered, consistent with the theoretical advantages of MSC: across all three applications, MSC achieves the smallest root mean square error (RMSE) among the methods considered over the tested computational budgets.

title: Representational Atoms in Neural Networks
text:
Title: Representational Atoms in Neural Networks
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Understanding the internal representations of neural networks and characterizing their relationship with human conceptual structure are two critical questions for elucidating model mechanisms. The former reveals how learned knowledge is organized in internal representations, whereas the latter provides a basis for interpreting these representations through human conceptual structure. Here, we formally define fundamental representational units (FRUs) and establish two evaluation criteria: fidelity and stability. We further prove that threshold-activated sparse autoencoders (TSAEs) can identify FRUs with high fidelity and stability under appropriate conditions, and validate this result through large-scale experiments. Further analyses reveal that FRUs with higher stability exhibit greater monosemanticity and can be composed across layers to recover semantic organization corresponding to human conceptual structure. These results provide a unified framework for defining, evaluating and identifying FRUs in neural networks, and establish a foundation for characterizing the relationship between neural network representations and human conceptual structure.

title: Trail systems self-organize through individual route optimization
text:
Title: Trail systems self-organize through individual route optimization
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

As animals, including humans, walk, they compact the vegetation and ground beneath them, reducing the cost of movement for subsequent travelers. From this positive feedback emerge networks of trails which allow for efficient movement and store generational-scale information about the environment. Models simulating this process show how individuals following local cues produce trail systems with many of the features of real-world networks. However, little has been done to investigate walkers with more complete knowledge of their environment and the abilities to plan their behavior intelligently. Here we introduce a simple general model for trail formation, based on minimizing cost of movement by individuals. As in real environments, our simulations produce a striking variety of complex trail networks. We show that these trail systems optimally connect space according to the spatial needs of the walkers, that the geometry of those trail systems matches theoretical predictions and that the systems they generate may fall into multiple attracting states. As technological advances allow us to quantify trail systems across diverse habitats and species, our model provides a theoretical foundation for empirical research on animal trails and for understanding the emergence of human transportation networks, with implications for urban design.

title: Transformer-Based Characterization of Criticality in Directed Percolation
text:
Title: Transformer-Based Characterization of Criticality in Directed Percolation
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Directed percolation (DP) provides a canonical framework for studying nonequilibrium phase transitions into absorbing states, yet extracting critical behavior directly from high-dimensional spatiotemporal configurations remains challenging. Here, we investigate (1 + 1)- and (2 + 1)-dimensional bond DP using a supervised Transformer encoder. Supervised learning results demonstrate that the Transformer can distinguish between the active and absorbing phases of directed percolation with high accuracy. The critical point and critical exponents estimated from the model's classification probabilities align closely with reference values from existing literature, indicating that the model not only achieves phase classification but also yields outputs containing information related to critical scaling behavior. To probe the model's internal representation, we employ attention rollout and define an attention center that quantifies the temporal centroid of the cumulative attention distribution. The attention patterns and the attention center reorganize systematically near the critical region and exhibit pronounced finite-size dependence. Finally, we examined the model's transferability between configurations generated from fully occupied initial states and those from single-seed initial states. The results indicate the presence of transferable information between the two types of data, though the transfer performance exhibits directional asymmetry. Furthermore, when using an equal amount of target-domain data, fine-tuning yielded only a marginal improvement in accuracy compared to training from scratch.

title: Winding-Pack Quench Simulation of Stellarator Coils: Hydraulic Field-Network Coupling and Transverse Heat Conduction in OPENSC$^2$
text:
Title: Winding-Pack Quench Simulation of Stellarator Coils: Hydraulic Field-Network Coupling and Transverse Heat Conduction in OPENSC$^2$
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Quench propagation in cable-in-conduit conductors is thermo-hydraulically driven, yet existing 1D models treat a conductor as one straight adiabatic cable with prescribed pressure and mass-flow boundaries, so secondary quenches and flow redistribution between windings cannot be resolved. We extend the open-source code OPENSC$^2$ with transverse heat conduction between turns, a 3D field resolving the current-sharing temperature, induced losses, and a lumped hydraulic network coupled to the conductors by a mass-flow formulation. Validated against the 2006 W7-X coil tests, it predicts the quench site, cuts the outlet-temperature error from 55 K to 12 K, and reproduces the neighboring windings' heating as flow reversal through the coil inlet.

title: Odd Elasticity in Strain-Gradient Continua: Anisotropy Classification and Non-Hermitian Elastodynamics
text:
Title: Odd Elasticity in Strain-Gradient Continua: Anisotropy Classification and Non-Hermitian Elastodynamics
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Odd elasticity extends continuum mechanics to active nonconservative systems containing internal energy sources, such as robotic active metamaterials with nonreciprocal feedback. Modeling these systems as effective continua requires relaxing Maxwell-Betti reciprocity, which results in stiffness tensors lacking major symmetry. In this contribution, we extend this framework to 3D strain-gradient odd elasticity to incorporate the length scales inherent in these heterogeneous systems. By applying the full hierarchy of 3D point-group symmetries along chiral and achiral branches, we derive the exhaustive set of fourth-, fifth-, and sixth-order odd elastic stiffness tensors. Further, utilizing the dynamic principle of virtual work, we formulate the equilibrium equations, higher-order boundary conditions, and the generalized acoustic tensor for elastodynamic analysis. The results demonstrate that nonreciprocal moduli survive even under full isotropy in the sixth-order stiffness, under hemitropy in the fifth-order stiffness, and under cubic symmetry in fourth-order stiffness. In contrast, the elastodynamic analysis reveals that under isotropic and hemitropic limits, despite the underlying odd stiffness moduli, the acoustic tensor remains unconditionally Hermitian. Non-Hermitian elastodynamics is shown to require anisotropy. By numerically analyzing a transversely hemitropic odd elastic continuum, we demonstrate that this symmetry reduction results in non-Hermitian elastodynamic phenomena including exceptional points in the dispersion spectra and active energy exchange through simultaneous amplification and attenuation of the elastic wave components. These results provide the necessary theoretical foundation for future multiscale homogenization frameworks for anisotropic strain-gradient active microstructures, and for the design of nonreciprocal strain-gradient metamaterials.

title: Towards large-scale ab initio Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Efficient Sampling-based Quantum Computing Algorithms
text:
Title: Towards large-scale ab initio Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Efficient Sampling-based Quantum Computing Algorithms
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) requires the calculation of highly accurate electronic-structure energies and nuclear forces at every time step, which can quickly become computationally expensive. Sample-based quantum diagonalization offers a route to such calculations on quantum hardware, but its use in AIMD simulations has so far been limited to active spaces of about 20 qubits. In these spaces, exact diagonalization is tractable, and the quantum circuits are typically built from standard coupled-cluster amplitudes. Here, we introduce SqDRIFT-AIMD, which combines randomized sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SqDRIFT) with analytical nuclear gradients. With SqDRIFT-AIMD, we obtain more accurate ground-state energies than the conventional coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) driven AIMD simulation for the $40$-qubit active space. We apply SqDRIFT-AIMD to study the dynamics of proton transfer in the Zundel cation, using circuits executed on IBM Heron r3 quantum processors. SqDRIFT energies fall below CCSD across the $40$-qubit double-well PES and stay within a few m$E_\text{h}$ of CCSD at 52 qubits. The $40$-qubit SqDRIFT-AIMD trajectory tracks the SHCI-driven proton transfer to within $1.33$ mÅ and exhibits excellent total energy conservation, with a standard deviation of only $0.245$ m$E_\text{h}$. These results extend quantum-centric AIMD to active spaces beyond the reach of exact diagonalization.

title: Integrating Low-Thrust Transfer Dynamics into POMDP Planning for On-Orbit Servicing
text:
Title: Integrating Low-Thrust Transfer Dynamics into POMDP Planning for On-Orbit Servicing
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Recent developments in both high-thrust (HT) and low-thrust (LT) propulsion technologies broaden design options for on-orbit servicing (OOS) missions. However, incorporating LT transfers into OOS mission planning requires accounting for the trade-off between prescribed transfer duration and propellant consumption. Multi-servicing, multi-transfer OOS mission planning is inherently sequential and requires adaptive planning tools that account for propulsion-dependent transfer durations and mass-dependent propellant consumption. Thus, transfer dynamics must be integrated into mission planning and scheduling to increase flexibility and adaptability. In addition, the planning is often done with imperfect information about the system's state and stochastic service demands. This paper focuses on modeling orbital transfers, particularly LT transfers, within a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework for OOS mission planning. To enable offline policy computation, the transfer model must provide explicit state transitions and rewards for all admissible actions. The state space is therefore augmented with the servicing vehicle's remaining propellant to enable consistent mass updates. HT transfers are modeled using a precomputed transfer matrix that maps each transfer to the time of flight and propellant consumed. LT transfers are represented using an analytical GEO phasing model with prescribed transfer-duration alternatives. For each alternative, the model calculates propellant consumption and maneuver feasibility as functions of the required phase change and the current servicing-vehicle mass. The proposed modeling approach is evaluated on simplified OOS planning scenarios using circular phasing with HT and LT propulsion. The resulting POMDPs are solved using the Successive Approximations of the Reachable Space under Optimal Policies (SARSOP) algorithm, and the policies obtained under HT and LT are compared. This comparison provides a quantitative assessment of the feasibility and operational impact of LT options, particularly regarding the potential role of advanced electric propulsion in future servicing architectures.

title: Discrete quality-factor control in a side-coupled photonic crystal microcavity: evanescent Bloch tunnelling and the finite-cell correction
text:
Title: Discrete quality-factor control in a side-coupled photonic crystal microcavity: evanescent Bloch tunnelling and the finite-cell correction
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

A point-defect cavity side-coupled to a line-defect waveguide in a two-dimensional photonic crystal of silicon rods in water is studied with plane-wave expansion and finite-difference time-domain computations. The defect-rod radius tunes the resonance continuously within the band gap, as first-order perturbation theory predicts, whereas the quality factor changes in discrete steps set by the number of lattice rows between cavity and guide; displacing the defect rod by up to a tenth of a period changes it by less than 7 percent. Each added row multiplies the quality factor by a factor that follows, without an adjustable parameter, from the decay of the evanescent Bloch channel of the bulk crystal that is phase-matched to the guided mode; the channel at zero wavevector along the guide predicts little more than half that factor. Two biases of a finite computational domain, leakage across the cladding and a standing wave set up by reflections at the ends of the truncated guide, lower the per-row factor and change the quality factor by up to a factor of two if left uncorrected. Scaled to 1550 nm the design gives a sensitivity of 634 nm per refractive index unit, which perturbation theory reproduces, and the linewidth agrees with that of a transmission spectrum normalized to a cavity-free reference. Absorption by water caps the quality factor near 9200 and limits the useful number of barrier rows. The guided mode lies inside the light cone, so a slab of finite height needs a different guide.

title: Self-Indexing Latent Memories for Access-Aware Continual Instruction Tuning of LLMs
text:
Title: Self-Indexing Latent Memories for Access-Aware Continual Instruction Tuning of LLMs
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Continual instruction tuning often preserves old skills with task-private modules. Inference still requires selecting the right module from the prompt alone. We introduce Task-Isolated Latent Adapter Continual Training (TILA-CT), a replay-free method that makes each task module self-indexing. Each task receives a latent memory and adapter bank in a frozen LLM. During adaptation, the memory gathers causal-prefix information and injects task-conditioned context. For access, its persistent state provides the routing prototype used by a shared prompt-only router. On the 8-task CT-Pipeline stream, TILA-CT achieves 65.19 acquisition and 63.98 final macro score, with 1.38 points of average forgetting. A middle-reversed order gives 65.38 acquisition and 64.17 final macro score. Across 6 backbones, final scores remain within 1.5 points of acquisition. Ablations support memory-derived routing keys and causal gathering. Final macro routing accuracy is 93.9\%, and oracle routing recovers 1.21 final macro points. These results separate preserved task computation from learned access to it.

title: Multimodal risk trajectories reveal heterogeneous paths to dementia
text:
Title: Multimodal risk trajectories reveal heterogeneous paths to dementia
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Dementia comprises biologically heterogeneous disorders, yet current risk assessment provides limited insight into how subtype-specific risk emerges and diverges before clinical diagnosis. We developed NetMoint, a multimodal framework integrating partially observed plasma proteomic, structural magnetic resonance imaging and cerebral haemodynamic phenotypes to predict individualized risks of Alzheimer's disease (AD), vascular dementia (VD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) across 1-, 5-, 10- and 20-year horizons. Among 104,120 UK Biobank participants free of dementia at baseline, NetMoint achieved mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.937, 0.930 and 0.932 for AD, VD and FTD, respectively. The biological determinants of prediction shifted with time, from structural brain vulnerability at shorter horizons towards circulating molecular signatures at longer horizons, with distinct subtype-specific biological profiles. Multi-horizon risk profiling identified distinct temporal trajectories of dementia susceptibility. Among participants who subsequently developed AD, 0.7% followed a persistently very-high-risk trajectory, with predicted risk reaching 53.50% at 20 years, whereas 8.3% of those who developed FTD followed an increasing very-high-risk trajectory, reaching 67.17%. These high-risk trajectories were marked by distinct molecular signatures, with lower TGFB1 characterizing the AD group and higher NDRG1 the FTD group. In an independent ADNI-to-UK Biobank analysis, AD risk prediction remained informative after harmonization to 138 shared features, with an AUC of 0.741 at 20 years. Together, these findings establish a multimodal framework for trajectory-resolved dementia risk stratification, identifying small but high-risk populations within dementia subtypes and linking their divergent risk trajectories to distinct molecular signatures.

title: Inverse optimization for divisor methods of apportionment
text:
Title: Inverse optimization for divisor methods of apportionment
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

The apportionment problem is to allocate a fixed number of seats among regions in proportion to their populations. In this paper, we propose an inverse optimization approach to evaluate how fairly an observed apportionment treats each region. It is well known that every divisor method can be formulated as a separable discrete convex minimization problem. We introduce a weighted divisor method, in which a nonnegative weight is assigned to each region, as the forward problem. Then we formulate an inverse optimization problem that finds the weight vector closest to the all-one vector in the $\ell_1$-norm such that the observed apportionment is optimal for the forward problem. We show that the optimal weight vector is always unique and has a closed-form expression as the median of three values that depend on a single parameter. Based on this result, the inverse optimization problem is reduced to a one-dimensional monotone equation, and it can be solved in $O(n \log n)$ time, where $n$ is the number of regions. We also apply the proposed approach to the apportionment of the single-member districts of the House of Representatives of Japan.

title: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents
text:
Title: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Goal interpretation is to translate a natural language instruction into a formal symbolic goal that a planner can execute. It is critical for embodied agents because any error here propagates to every downstream planning and action step. Doing it well requires both generating suitable candidates and reliably selecting among them. We present a two-stage generate-then-rank approach to Goal Interpretation in the Embodied Agent Interface (EAI). First, supervised fine-tuning adapts a Large Language Model (LLM) to EAI's output convention. Second, Candidate-Output Ranking from Errors (CORE) learns preferences over complete outputs from the model's own generated alternatives. We conducted experiments on the household scenes of the Embodied Agent Interface Benchmark. Multiple open source LLMs including DeepSeek-V3 chat, DeepSeek-Reasoner, and Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-72B were evaluated. The proposed method outperformed the baseline models including LLMs with simple prompting, chain-of-thought, and knowledge graph based approaches.

title: Deterministic Quantum Search for NP Problems Through Verifier-Based Oracle Construction
text:
Title: Deterministic Quantum Search for NP Problems Through Verifier-Based Oracle Construction
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Problems in the class NP are important in computational science, where a given candidate solution can be verified in polynomial time, while finding a solution may require evaluating the entire search space in the worst case. Classical exhaustive approaches generally solve such problems by evaluating the verifier function over all possible inputs, resulting in a worst-case query complexity of O(N), where N = d^n represents the size of the search space, d is the number of possible values for each variable, and n is the number of variables. Quantum search algorithms can solve unstructured search problems more efficiently by reducing the query complexity to O(sqrt (N)), providing a quadratic speedup over classical exhaustive search. However, conventional quantum search formulations typically assume access to an oracle that identifies valid solutions, while standard implementations generally yield probabilistic success. In this work, we propose a generalised quantum oracle construction method for NP problems, together with a deterministic quantum search framework that identifies satisfying assignments using their corresponding classical verifier functions. The proposed framework retains the quadratic query speedup of quantum search over classical exhaustive search. We further establish that constructed oracle can be implemented using a number of gates polynomial in the size (L) of the binary encoding of verification function, consistent with the polynomial-time evaluation of the corresponding classical verifier, while the total qubit requirement remains O(poly(L)). The construction is demonstrated on multiple N-SAT instances, with circuit-level simulations confirming deterministic identification of satisfying assignments. These results establish the applicability of deterministic quantum search to NP problems while retaining the quadratic query advantage over classical exhaustive search.

title: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
text:
Title: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Bañados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.

title: How Risky Is Your Data-Driven Policy?
text:
Title: How Risky Is Your Data-Driven Policy?
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Data-driven algorithms are ubiquitous across industries, and there is an extensive literature on analyzing their \emph{average} performance. The risk profile of such algorithms, while critical, is much less understood. This paper quantifies the risk of data-driven policies and isolates its sources. We evaluate a policy through the conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of its loss over the training sample, any policy randomization, and the future outcome, at a fixed unknown distribution. Regret against an oracle that knows the distribution decomposes into expected post-sample regret (PS), the average outcome-only CVaR gap of the selected action, and a sample-risk premium (SR), the additional tail risk omitted by averaging those evaluations. The analogous premium vanishes under expected loss. We characterize when the premium vanishes and how large it is relative to post-sample regret. For losses with a continuous density near the tail cutoff, we identify conditions under which both components decay at the same rate, yet the limiting ratio of the premium to post-sample regret can reach the thousands. When a probability mass at the cutoff moves with the action, the premium can decay more slowly and dominate post-sample regret. We establish conditions under which sample average approximation learns the oracle action at rate $n^{-1/2}$ in both settings, but its combined-risk regret is of order $n^{-1}$ in the first and $n^{-1/2}$ in the second. In finite-sample numerical examples of SAA in both settings, the premium accounts for approximately $74\%$--$97\%$ of regret.

title: Coexisting Kondo and Weyl-like transport in kagome heavy-fermion metal, Yb$_y$Co$_3$G$e_{3-x}$Sn$_x$
text:
Title: Coexisting Kondo and Weyl-like transport in kagome heavy-fermion metal, Yb$_y$Co$_3$G$e_{3-x}$Sn$_x$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Strong electron correlations and topology offer complementary routes to controlling electrical conduction, as correlations can make electrons heavy (e.g. Kondo lattices) whereas topology can make them behave as massless particles (e.g. Dirac or Weyl systems), and having both in one material is rare. In Kondo lattice systems, Kondo hybridization between localized 4$f$ and conduction electrons strongly enhances the quasiparticle mass, where in Weyl-Kondo systems these Kondo-renormalized bands form Weyl states, and simultaneous signs of both Kondo and Weyl states in one material have not been observed in transport. Here we report signs of both in the kagome metal \ce{Yb_yCo3Ge_{3-x}Sn_x} by combining magnetotransport, heat capacity, magnetization, angle-resolved and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, and DFT+U calculations to reveal Yb-dependent Kondo scattering developing into lattice coherence, with extrapolated Sommerfeld coefficient of approximately 2 ~Jmol$_{\mathrm{Yb}}^{-1}$K$^{-2}$. Transverse magnetoresistance (MR) follows single-ion Kondo scaling, whereas longitudinal transport contains an additional negative response proportional to B$^2$ and remains unsaturated up to 32 T, consistent with a chiral anomaly. These findings support a picture of Kondo and Weyl-like conduction arising from distinct electronic states without external Fermi-level tuning, suggesting a possible route to combining correlated and topological functionality in a bulk material.

title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
text:
Title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)
