Here, we extend the methodology to learn aSSM-reduced models from data collected from hardware soft robotic platforms. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot. We then use this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks, ranging from 2D to 3D trajectories with static and dynamic constraints. We find that our methodology enhances accuracy and precision across all control tasks compared to available data-driven linear methods and model-free reinforcement learning. While we focus here on a soft-helicoid trunk robot, our methodology relies solely on hardware data and is therefore applicable to a broader class of soft robotic systems.

title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
text:
Title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. Representative calculations spanning continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, trajectory simulation, and magnetometry closely reproduced corresponding EasySpin results. In matched benchmarks, TorchSpin CPU execution was faster than EasySpin for six of nine workloads although performance depended strongly on the calculation. We therefore focused on the capabilities enabled by automatic differentiation in PyTorch. In a Cu(II) powder-spectrum demonstration, feedback propagated through TorchSpin improved the quality of a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) without using parameter labels during refinement. Models trained from randomly initialized CNNs using only noisy spectra and TorchSpin reconstruction loss achieved median similarities of $\geq$ 0.99. CNNs trained on TorchSpin-generated libraries also transferred without adaptation to independently generated EasySpin spectra with performance comparable to EasySpin-trained controls. Once trained, the CNN produced initial parameter estimates in approximately 1 ms per spectrum while a batch of 512 was processed in approximately 1.3 ms with GPU acceleration. TorchSpin therefore provides both a tested Python implementation of established EPR calculations and a differentiable physical layer for rapid learned inference, spectral refinement, and parameter-label-free training.

title: Crosstalk-Induced Row Hammer Attacks on Quantum Random Access Codes
text:
Title: Crosstalk-Induced Row Hammer Attacks on Quantum Random Access Codes
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum processors remain susceptible to crosstalk-induced effects despite the continuous evolution of their underlying hardware architectures. In this work, we experimentally investigate the effectiveness of crosstalk-induced attacks across six IBM superconducting quantum processors and one IQM processor. Our results demonstrate that such attacks can be launched across all the platforms, due to persistance of crosstalk, although their effectiveness varies significantly between devices. The probability of a measurement outcome flip in the victim qubits reaches a maximum value of $60\%$. Also, it is seen that processors sharing identical coupling graphs exhibit different vulnerability profiles, indicating that connectivity alone is insufficient to predict attack efficiency. Finally, to demonstrate the practical relevance of these attacks, we study their impact on quantum random access codes (QRACs), observing a degradation in their average success probabilities.

title: ChemInsight: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating and Diagnosing Chemistry Understanding and Reasoning in Large Language Models
text:
Title: ChemInsight: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating and Diagnosing Chemistry Understanding and Reasoning in Large Language Models
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

We introduce ChemInsight, a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on chemistry tasks that require multi-step reasoning and structured chemical understanding. We propose a two-dimensional scoring system (scope and depth) to assess both task coverage and reasoning completeness. ChemInsight consists of 203 challenging chemistry questions organized into 50 bundles, which support the two-dimensional scoring evaluation scheme. We evaluate ten representative LLMs using ChemInsight and observe consistently low performance across models, with scope scores below 30% and depth scores below 11%, substantially lower than human expert performance. We then proceed to ask (1) What factor limits the advancement of current LLMs in chemistry? (2) To what extent are statistically driven language-model training methods effective at modeling chemistry symbolic language such as SMILES? And (3) Can LLM performance in chemistry be improved through intensive training on large, domain-specific corpora?

title: Integral Compensation for Discrete-time Bearing-only Target Localization and Circumnavigation
text:
Title: Integral Compensation for Discrete-time Bearing-only Target Localization and Circumnavigation
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This paper investigates the discrete-time control problem of driving an agent to localize and circumnavigate an unknown target at a prescribed radius using bearing measurements. Discretizing existing continuous-time circumnavigation controllers can introduce steady-state orbit bias, even at sampling rates that preserve stability. To eliminate the sampling-induced orbit bias, we propose an adaptive compensator for a circumnavigation controller formulated directly in discrete time. Driven by the estimated agent-to-target distance, the proposed compensator dynamically learns the geometric correction required to achieve the desired circumnavigation radius. Unlike existing static correction methods, neither the proposed controller nor the compensator update explicitly uses the sampling interval. Exponential convergence is rigorously established using Lyapunov-based analysis. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms.

title: ConvLUT: Rethinking Convolutional Architectures for Ultra-Low-Latency LUT-Based Inference
text:
Title: ConvLUT: Rethinking Convolutional Architectures for Ultra-Low-Latency LUT-Based Inference
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Lookup-table (LUT)-based neural networks (NNs) offer a compelling path to ultra-low-latency inference on FPGAs. However, existing LUT-based neural networks have largely been restricted to MLP-style topologies, leaving structured vision and audio tasks underexplored. We present ConvLUT, a family of fully unrolled LUT-mappable convolutional architectures targeting the MLPerf Tiny benchmarks. It is comprised of a standard convolutional model built around a hierarchical tree of LUTs and a depthwise separable model following the MobileNet design philosophy. These architectures are enabled by four key contributions: a unified LUT-based convolutional framework supporting standard, depthwise, and pointwise convolutions under explicit fan-in constraints; a LUT-tree that addresses the $k^2c$ receptive field dimensionality bottleneck; a channel-partitioned LUT pooling layer that replaces conventional spatial pooling; and a hardware-aware iterative pruning strategy for stable convergence at scale. Evaluated on CIFAR-10, Visual Wake Words, and Keyword Spotting, ConvLUT achieves competitive accuracy with fully unrolled inference latencies below $\sim 50$ ns. On CIFAR-10 it reaches at least a $8844\times$ latency reduction over non-logic-based prior implementations, and outperforms existing MLP-style LUT-based models on the same task by at least $20$ pp in test accuracy.

title: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated Finite-Element Formulation in JAX for Large-Deformation Shells with Contact: Application to Patient-Specific Aortic Valve Simulation
text:
Title: A Differentiable, GPU-Accelerated Finite-Element Formulation in JAX for Large-Deformation Shells with Contact: Application to Patient-Specific Aortic Valve Simulation
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Patient-specific aortic-valve models can help assess how tissue properties and geometry influence leaflet deformation and coaptation, with potential to inform intervention planning. Large deformations, near-incompressibility, and evolving contact make these simulations computationally demanding and can challenge nonlinear convergence. Differentiable, GPU-accelerated methods offer efficient derivative evaluation and parallel computation, but their matrix-free application to soft-tissue shells with contact remains less established. We developed a forward solver using tatva's energy-based finite-element framework in JAX. The solver combines finite-strain extensible-director shells, hyperelastic constitutive models, and a finite-range repulsive contact energy. Nonlinear equilibrium is solved using a regularized, matrix-free Newton-Krylov method with two-level preconditioning. Automatic differentiation evaluates tangent-vector products without forming or storing the primary tangent matrix, while GPU execution parallelizes element and quadrature-point computations. Constitutive, shell, contact, and self-contact responses were assessed against analytical, semi-analytical, and published benchmarks. At a contact-free plate equilibrium, implicit sensitivities of the converged apex displacement to constitutive parameters, thickness, and pressure agreed with finite differences from independent nonlinear simulations. Simulations of three patient-specific aortic-valve models (two tricuspid and one bicuspid) achieved final relative equilibrium residuals below 10^-4. Median GPU runtimes were approximately 15-25 minutes, with 5.3-6.5-fold speedups relative to corresponding CPU runs on the tested hardware. These results provide component-level verification and demonstrate GPU-accelerated forward valve simulation in the tested cases, supporting future gradient-based inverse studies.

title: Second-order Bethe-Salpeter kernels: the interplay of vertex-corrected quasiparticle energies and the screened interaction
text:
Title: Second-order Bethe-Salpeter kernels: the interplay of vertex-corrected quasiparticle energies and the screened interaction
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We study second-order Bethe-Salpeter kernels generated by truncating an iterative formulation of Hedin's equations after the second cycle. Starting from the Hartree-Fock or the $GW$ self-energy, whose first cycles correspond to TDHF and $GW$+BSE, we obtain the second-cycle kernel by differentiating the first-cycle correlation self-energy with the interacting correlation function replaced by the non-interacting one, and evaluate it in the static limit of the effective kernel. Using fixed restricted Hartree-Fock orbitals, we benchmark 30 singlet and 28 triplet excitation energies for seven small molecules (six for the triplets) against the theoretical best estimates from QUEST v1.2. The second cycle lowers the mean absolute error (MAE) in both sequences. For the $GW$ sequence, the MAE decreases from 0.63 to 0.29 eV (singlets), on par with ADC(2) (0.30 eV), and from 0.43 to 0.38 eV (triplets). BSE$^{(2)}$@HF removes the triplet instabilities of TDHF and yields MAEs of 0.43 and 0.38 eV, or 0.31 and 0.30 eV when the Tamm-Dancoff approximation is applied in all cycles. Assigning the statically screened interaction $W_0$ to the exchange part of the $GW$ self-energy counts second-order screening twice in the second-cycle kernel and strongly blueshifts valence excitations. Without this double counting, dressing the exchange-type terms with $W_0$ lowers the singlet MAE from 0.37 to 0.29 eV but leaves the triplets nearly unchanged. Replacing second-order Green's function (GF2) quasiparticle energies by vertex-corrected ones in the same kernel raises excitation energies by about 0.7 eV, improving Rydberg but degrading valence excitations. A perturbative dynamical correction of the kernel blueshifts valence excitations by 0.3-0.4 eV and increases the errors of all full-matrix BSE$^{(2)}$ variants. The consistent improvement over the first cycle suggests that higher cycles are worth pursuing.

title: Solvating machine-learning interatomic potentials for solution-phase chemistry
text:
Title: Solvating machine-learning interatomic potentials for solution-phase chemistry
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Most machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on gas-phase data, which limits their use for chemistry in solution. Here, we introduce AnySolv, a transferable implicit solvation potential that provides solvent-dependent energy and force corrections to existing gas-phase potentials without retraining them. It is trained on 1.4 million solvation energies and forces computed with density functional theory (DFT) and SMD in 36 solvents, spanning charged, open-shell, and transition-state structures. Because solvents are represented by continuous physical descriptors, AnySolv supports 179 solvents, including those absent from training. On external benchmarks, AnySolv reproduces DFT-SMD solvation energies to 2-4 meV mean absolute error at more than three orders of magnitude lower cost, and it matches the accuracy of DFT-SMD against experimental solvation free energies. This enables screening of the mechanisms of 120 nucleophilic aromatic substitution reactions in six phases as well as molecular dynamics simulations that reproduce the experimentally observed solvent-dependent conformational preferences of alanine dipeptide. By providing transferable solvation corrections to existing MLIPs, AnySolv enables scalable simulations of solvent-dependent chemical reactivity and molecular dynamics.

title: Transferable Implicit Solvent Machine Learning Potential for Drugs and Proteins Approaching Ab Initio Accuracy
text:
Title: Transferable Implicit Solvent Machine Learning Potential for Drugs and Proteins Approaching Ab Initio Accuracy
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLPs) have revolutionized atomistic modeling, offering the potential to replace traditional methods like Density Functional Theory (DFT). However, inference time of MLPs is orders of magnitude slower than that of classical force fields, hindering real-world applications for biomolecular systems that require timescales of microseconds and beyond. Implicit solvent MLPs can address this issue, but are faced with data challenges associated with coarse-grained modeling. Consequently, previous approaches relied on empirical force field data, thereby inherently limiting the MLP's accuracy. Here, we introduce the Transferable Water Implicit Network (TWIN), an implicit water MLP parametrized entirely by an Equivariant Graph Neural Network and trained solely on ab initio and experimental labels. We demonstrate TWIN's transferability across drug-like molecules, peptides, and proteins, achieving excellent results on ab initio and experimental crystallographic and NMR benchmarks, consistently outperforming previous machine-learning-based implicit solvent or coarse-grained models. Furthermore, TWIN closely matches DFT-based explicit solvent MLPs while providing a two-order-of-magnitude faster timestep evaluation, paving the way for efficient ab initio-level modeling of biomolecular systems in aqueous environments.

title: Low-Rank Kolmogorov-Arnold Generator Flows for Interpretable Operator Learning
text:
Title: Low-Rank Kolmogorov-Arnold Generator Flows for Interpretable Operator Learning
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Neural operators that learn physical laws from data should generalize beyond their training distribution and expose the learned law in closed form. The Kolmogorov-Arnold neural operator achieves both for position-dependent dynamics by learning a dense pseudo-differential symbol over all positions and frequencies, at a cost that grows with the square of the resolution and with closed forms that must be read out by hand. This dense symbol is unnecessary: a finite-order variable-coefficient differential operator has a symbol whose separation rank is bounded by the number of its coefficient functions, independently of the resolution, and the symbols that this network learns on its own benchmarks have rank two. We introduce the Kolmogorov-Arnold flow (KAFlow), which learns the generator of a physical operator as a low-rank symbol built from univariate Kolmogorov-Arnold functions, fixes the gauge of these functions so that every term has a unique place, integrates the dynamics with exact exponential integrators, and distills its closed form automatically. On the synthetic benchmarks of the Kolmogorov-Arnold neural operator, KAFlow lowers the out-of-distribution loss by 3.4 to 11 times and recovers every coefficient to within 10^-4 without symbolic templates, reaching the precision floor of the data. On long-horizon quantum dynamics, it lowers the state infidelity by up to 6 orders of magnitude, and by 30 times when trained only on position and momentum measurements. KAFlow also learns a variable-order fractional operator 15 times more accurately than existing operator networks and discovers nonlocal, fractional and non-polynomial dispersion relations on which sparse regression fails.

title: Weak solutions to granular medium equations via stochastic particle approximations
text:
Title: Weak solutions to granular medium equations via stochastic particle approximations
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We establish weak existence for McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations associated with granular medium equations with porous medium diffusion, for m>1 in arbitrary dimension. The result covers a class of nonconvex potentials with locally Lipschitz gradients of polynomial growth. Our particle approximation generates nonlinear diffusion through density-dependent noise and allows initial densities with finite Boltzmann entropy but infinite internal energy.

title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for the Regime-Switching Consumption-Investment Problem
text:
Title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for the Regime-Switching Consumption-Investment Problem
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This paper establishes an entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) framework for the continuous-time consumption-investment problem under a regime-switching market model with general utility functions. By incorporating randomized exploratory policies and Shannon entropy regularization into the stochastic optimal control formulation, we derive closed-form representations for the optimal exploratory consumption and investment strategies. Specifically, the optimal investment strategy follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution, whereas the optimal consumption strategy takes the form of a Gibbs measure---which specializes to a Gamma distribution under logarithmic utility and a non-standard exponential distribution under power utility. Crucially, our theoretical analysis reveals that the classical deterministic optimal decisions correspond to the mode---rather than the mean---of these exploratory distributions. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of the exploratory value function to its classical unregularized counterpart as the temperature parameter vanishes. For algorithmic design, we develop a continuous-time q-learning framework grounded in a novel continuous-time q-function, prove the policy improvement theorem, and establish martingale characterizations for both on-policy and off-policy learning. We find that parameterizing the actor network based on theoretical distribution families can help accelerate convergence and enhance numerical stability. Furthermore, numerical experiments across regime-switching environments provide empirical support for our theoretical findings, demonstrating stable loss convergence as well as the monotonicity and concavity of the learned value functions.

title: Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
text:
Title: Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We give a framework for transporting vectors along Markov processes that may have jumps, without assuming a manifold or other specific geometric structure. We prove existence and uniqueness of the resulting transport. In doing so, we develop a theory of vector bundles defined quasi-everywhere, in which the vectors live, and an axiomatic framework for energy forms that determine the bundle and the transport.

title: Geometric-Chemical Distance Between Protein Surfaces
text:
Title: Geometric-Chemical Distance Between Protein Surfaces
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Proteins recognize, bind, and catalyze through molecular surfaces, where geometry and chemical patterning determine interaction. Comparing these surfaces requires both a geometric--chemical distance and a correspondence that relates one complete surface to another. Here we introduce IFACE (Intrinsic Field--Aligned Coupled Embedding). IFACE derives a symmetric geometric--chemical distance by optimizing a probabilistic coupling over intrinsic geometry, mean curvature, electrostatics, hydrophobicity, and hydrogen-bond propensity. The same coupling provides an explicit surface map. For molecular-dynamics conformers, IFACE distinguishes the same protein from distinct proteins more accurately than TM-distance and a Laplace--Beltrami spectral distance. A Jensen--Shannon distribution distance performs best in this binary identity test, because aggregate surface-feature distributions already identify each protein. A distance must also satisfy a global requirement: its pairwise values must place many distinct protein surfaces consistently in one space. We therefore tested IFACE across six protein families. It produces the strongest family classification and clustering among the distributional, spectral, MaSIF, and SurfaceID comparisons. The inferred maps preserve geodesic neighborhoods and transfer heme-centered pocket regions across cytochrome P450 proteins. IFACE therefore provides, from one construction, both a distance between complete protein surfaces and the local map that explains that distance.

title: Hydra: Towards Transferable Multi-Task Learning on Temporal Graphs
text:
Title: Hydra: Towards Transferable Multi-Task Learning on Temporal Graphs
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Real-world evolving networks are naturally modeled as temporal graphs (TGs), where capturing temporal dynamics is essential for predicting future graph properties that support downstream decision-making. Existing temporal graph methods have been developed primarily for single-task prediction, and little is known about their generalization across tasks or transfer to unseen networks. This leaves the challenge of multi-task graph property prediction in TGs largely open. We address this challenge by introducing Hydra, a novel architecture that integrates local connectivity features from temporal GNNs with a spectral learning module that captures global connectivity patterns. This design enables joint learning of local and global information under a multi-task objective. In multi-task classification, Hydra achieves an 8.9% relative gain in AUC over the strongest competitor. In multi-task regression, Hydra achieves competitive results in all three tasks, while obtaining the best results in two tasks with a 8.2% relative gain in MAE compared to the strongest baseline. Moreover, Hydra delivers these gains with a 22% reduction in training time compared to temporal transfer models. These results provide the first systematic evidence that multi-task transferable learning on temporal graphs is effective. By delivering consistent top-ranked performance, Hydra highlights multi-task training on temporal graphs as a promising direction toward adaptable foundation models for temporal graphs.

title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
text:
Title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

High-resolution weather prediction is important for resolving local atmospheric patterns missed by coarse global forecasts. Large pretrained weather backbones have improved global forecasting, but adapting them to produce future high-resolution fields from recent coarse states remains challenging and costly. We formulate this setting as Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), a task that jointly refines spatial and temporal resolution while predicting future high-resolution trajectories. To this end, we propose a framework that decomposes prediction into spatial and temporal stages using a shared pretrained backbone, fixed numerical scaffolds, and lightweight residual heads. For backbone adaptation, we introduce PROLA (PRincipal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation), which allocates a fixed low-rank budget between pretrained weights' principal directions and their orthogonal complement. PROLA further rescales rank-1 optimizer updates using gradient signals, improving adaptation without increasing trainable rank. Experiments in the PSWD setting show that PROLA outperforms representative low-rank adaptation baselines. Further experiments across diverse datasets and tasks support the broader applicability of PROLA, showing that its benefits extend beyond the primary weather downscaling setting.

title: Weak Values in Postselected Quantum Trajectories
text:
Title: Weak Values in Postselected Quantum Trajectories
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Weak value (WV) describes the amplified response of a meter when the measured system undergoes postselection. While conventional WV theory mainly rests on a single system-meter interaction setting, it remains unexplored whether WV can act as an effective pointer for sequential quantum measurements under postselection. Here we introduce the concept of WVs to the setting of sequential quantum measurements and quantum trajectories. We find that WV naturally emerges in postselected quantum trajectories of sequential weak measurements, by establishing a connection between the WV of the measured observable and the postselected statistics of quantum trajectories. Using sequential weak measurements on a qubit or an oscillator implemented by Ramsey interferometry with an ancilla qubit, we show that postselection shifts the collective record polarization away from the unconditioned ones, with an effective bias described by the WV. Our predictions are feasible to test in various platforms.

title: A single LU~factorization approach to model reduction for linear system families with a quadratic matrix pencil
text:
Title: A single LU~factorization approach to model reduction for linear system families with a quadratic matrix pencil
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

To solve a family of large linear systems where the system matrix depends on the family parameter quadratically, we propose a new solution approach. Our method employs the derivatives of solutions with respect to the parameter. It turns out that the accumulated solution derivatives of increasing order, evaluated at a single specially chosen parameter value, provide successively better approximations to solution subspaces for the whole linear system family. We show that the derivatives can be computed by a recurrence, involving, at each step, solving a linear system with the same matrix. Constructing an orthonormal basis for the subspace spanned by the derivatives then leads to an efficient solver where just a single (sparse) LU factorization (or a single preconditioner setup in an iterative scheme) suffices to solve the whole linear system family. We call the new method ODB (orthonormal derivative basis method). As shown in numerical tests, compared to conventional solution methods, the ODB method allows to drastically reduce computational costs.

title: Mass-Varying Dark Matter, Naturally
text:
Title: Mass-Varying Dark Matter, Naturally
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Ultralight scalars that vary dark-matter masses require protection from quantum corrections. Cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries provide this protection but also suppress variation of the mean mass of equally populated partners. Unsuppressed variation typically requires asymmetric reheating through symmetry-breaking couplings that threaten radiative control. We show that scalar-induced mass splittings built into these constructions can instead bias relic abundances through symmetric interactions. The mechanism applies to thermal and nonthermal relics that reach internal equilibrium after production, and permits mass variation over a broad range of timescales.

title: Critical Slowing Down and the Crossover to Quantum Scrambling in Holographic CFTs
text:
Title: Critical Slowing Down and the Crossover to Quantum Scrambling in Holographic CFTs
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We investigate critical relaxation dynamics and their connection to quantum information scrambling in the conformal field theory dual to a Reissner-Nordström anti-de Sitter (RN-AdS) black hole. Employing the holographic dictionary, we formulate the thermodynamics in terms of boundary CFT variables and study the stochastic evolution of the reduced horizon radius using Langevin and Fokker-Planck formalisms. We demonstrate pronounced critical slowing down in the dual CFT, characterized by an enhancement of the autocorrelation time and stochastic fluctuations, accompanied by a suppression of the lowest nonzero Fokker-Planck eigenvalue. The autocorrelation time exhibits a universal power-law divergence, $τ\sim|ε|^{-Δ}$, with $Δ\simeq 2/3$, consistent with the analytical prediction and previous bulk gravitational results. Going beyond the conventional single-parameter analysis, we incorporate variations of the CFT central charge and identify a combined scaling variable involving temperature and central charge, demonstrating that the leading relaxation dynamics retain the same critical exponent along different trajectories in the two-dimensional parameter space. Finally, we explore the interplay between thermodynamic relaxation and quantum information scrambling by comparing the relaxation timescale with the fast-scrambling timescale. The comparison reveals a crossover between thermodynamic relaxation and quantum scrambling for which we derive the corresponding crossover scale analytically and find that, in the large-central-charge limit, it behaves as $\hatε\sim(C\ln C)^{-3/2}$. We also verify this numerically using the full nonlinear free-energy landscape. Our results connect critical dynamical scaling, finite-central-charge effects, and quantum scrambling within the holographic CFT framework.

title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
text:
Title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Generative models can support both state estimation and control in robotics. For control, a common approach is to use the model as a policy that directly samples actions conditioned on observation histories. However, models that jointly represent states, actions, and observations can also predict how the robot state and its environment evolve. We investigate whether these predictions can improve state estimation and control through a change in inference procedure, without modifying the pretrained model. To this end, we use particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories. A single pretrained diffusion model generates these hypotheses along with their predicted observations and associated action proposals. As new measurements arrive, particles are reweighted according to how well their predicted observations match the measurements. While particle filtering conventionally uses these weights only for state estimation, we also use them to guide action selection, favoring proposals associated with hypotheses that better explain the observations. Simulation experiments in partially observed navigation and vision-based manipulation demonstrate improvements in both state estimation and task performance compared to action generation without filtering, using the same pretrained model and no additional test-time information.

title: Identifying Neural Dynamics Using Nonlinear Interventional State Space Models
text:
Title: Identifying Neural Dynamics Using Nonlinear Interventional State Space Models
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

State-space models (SSMs) recover low-dimensional latent dynamics from high-dimensional observations, but latents are generally not identifiable from observational data alone. Interventional state-space models (iSSMs) use perturbations to break observational symmetries and identify parameters up to permutation, scaling, and shift. However, prior work restricts identifiability to linear latent dynamics and piecewise-linear emissions, excluding many behaviors characteristic of neural circuits. We extend iSSMs to a substantially broader model class: we prove that (i) affine identifiability holds under general injective emission functions and Gaussian latent transitions, and (ii) with interventions, identifiability up to permutation, scaling, and shift is preserved under general nonlinear latent dynamics. We validate our theory on simulated FitzHugh-Nagumo dynamics, and then demonstrate two applications: adjudicating between competing models of decision-making; and predicting responses to unseen micro-stimulation in macaque and human neural recordings, with proof-of-concept generalization to a held-out stimulation site in the latter. Finally, simulations yield practical guidance for designing stimulation protocols that improve identifiability.

title: Computational modeling of RNA-protein binding interactions under an external force
text:
Title: Computational modeling of RNA-protein binding interactions under an external force
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

RNA binding proteins play a crucial role in post-transcriptional gene regulation by controlling the transport, processing, and translation of their target RNAs. Post-transcriptional gene regulation leads to the differential expression of genetic material and loss of regulation or over-regulation relates to a large range of cancers and diseases - many of which have directly been associated with RNA binding proteins and their target RNAs. To understand RNA, RNA binding proteins, and how they function in gene expression, it is essential to characterize how RNA binding proteins interact with their target RNAs. Here, we aim to assess the potential for single molecule force spectroscopy experiments to be used in the characterization of RNA-protein binding by investigating to what extent a change of extension due to RNA-protein binding is experimentally measurable and what aspects of the interaction can be deduced from such measurements. We predict the effect of protein binding on RNA force extension measurements via the open-source ViennaRNA package, which we have modified to simultaneously consider an external force, protein binding, and RNA secondary structure. From this work, we see protein concentration-dependent responses to external forces with discernable differences in predicted extensions around biologically relevant concentrations and a connection to protein binding domain geometry for several RNA binding proteins.

title: Where Position Matters: Profiling-Guided Layer-Wise RoPE Allocation in Transformers
text:
Title: Where Position Matters: Profiling-Guided Layer-Wise RoPE Allocation in Transformers
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) typically uses uniform coverage across Transformer layers despite heterogeneous positional requirements. Phase-off interventions reveal non-uniform, model-specific rotary-phase dependence, while coverage interventions relate it to coverage-upgrade benefits. We propose profiling-guided layer-wise RoPE allocation, assigning high/low coverage under a fixed budget using early coverage-benefit profiles. The framework supports fixed-width query/key representations and physical rotary-dimension allocation in Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA). Normalized-depth mapping transfers profiles within model families, enabling small-model measurements to guide larger-model allocations before pretraining. A brief analysis relates selection and transfer to score calibration and inter-layer interactions. From-scratch experiments demonstrate validation-loss improvements over available budget-matched baselines, while analytical resource accounting identifies favorable quality--storage--compute trade-offs for physical MLA. These results connect positional demand to transferable, efficient architecture design.

title: Equivariant Deep Learning in Direct-Product Space for Electronic-Structure Hamiltonian Prediction
text:
Title: Equivariant Deep Learning in Direct-Product Space for Electronic-Structure Hamiltonian Prediction
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Most existing equivariant architectures for Hamiltonian prediction propagate features in direct-sum spaces of irreducible spherical tensors, whereas the target Hamiltonian is naturally an operator block in a direct-product representation over local orbital and spin bases. This representation mismatch fragments contiguous Hamiltonian blocks, obscures direct manipulation of orbital couplings, and organizes features into irregular angular-momentum components that require numerous transformations and are poorly aligned with efficient hardware execution and memory management. To address both the representation mismatch and computational bottleneck, we propose DP-Learner, an equivariant learning framework that performs message passing directly on Hamiltonian-like operator blocks in the direct-product space. Theoretically, we propose Lie-generator-based directional embedding and invariantly weighted left--right products and contractions that preserve equivariance to SO(3), SU(2), and spatial inversions, without explicit Clebsch--Gordan decomposition or inverse reconstruction. Methodologically, we instantiate this principle as a Transformer architecture, in which Hamiltonian-like feature matrices or tensors evolve through equivariant operators in the direct-product space, while non-linear invariant scalar routing controls structured gating over matrix units, directional propagation, attention, and environment-embedded context interactions. We further construct MP-HAM-110K, a large-scale Hamiltonian dataset comprising more than 110,000 material structures covering 68 elements with both Hamiltonian and wavefunction data. Experiments on MP-HAM-110K and Materials-HAM-SOC demonstrate that DP-Learner dramatically improves Hamiltonian prediction accuracy and inference efficiency over the state-of-the-art method.

title: ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning
text:
Title: ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning but can suffer from redundant basis directions. Constraining the basis factor to the Stiefel manifold addresses this redundancy through orthonormality. Landing methods allow temporarily infeasible iterates to explore a neighborhood of the manifold while progressively restoring orthogonality without per-step retractions. To improve optimization efficiency while retaining this flexibility, we introduce ProLand (Product-space Landing), a retraction-free optimizer that combines coordinated factor updates with Muon-style spectral directions. By designing the updates in the space of the represented weight increment, ProLand separates objective optimization from orthogonality restoration, supporting efficient feasibility recovery. This coordinated construction also enables Muon-style directions to guide objective optimization while preserving that separation. Experiments cover four GLUE validation tasks on DeBERTa-v3-base and seven language benchmarks on Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Moonlight-16B-A3B across multiple adapter ranks. Across these 11 tasks, ProLand achieves the highest average score among the compared methods in every tested encoder and decoder model-rank configuration.

title: greenWTE: Frequency-domain solver for the phonon Wigner Transport Equation with arbitrary heating using Green's functions
text:
Title: greenWTE: Frequency-domain solver for the phonon Wigner Transport Equation with arbitrary heating using Green's functions
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Heat transport in solids is usually described in a phenomenological way via Fourier's law. However, at small time and length scales in low thermal conductivity materials, a microscopic description is needed. This is traditionally done by invoking the phonon Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE), which has been successful in describing transport in high thermal conductivity materials. Recently, a generalization of the BTE, the Wigner Transport Equation, was developed to be able to microscopically describe transport in low thermal conductivity materials by taking into account not only phonon scattering processes but also phonon tunneling processes, so-called coherences. We present a Python package that solves the Wigner Transport Equation (WTE) in spatial and temporal Fourier space for arbitrary source terms, thereby enabling the study of heat transport at small space and time scales. This allows one to compute both static and dynamic thermal conductivities from bulk to nanoscale. Beyond that, it can be used to study the response of phonon systems in materials to arbitrary heat sources.

title: Spontaneous brain-wide rotational dynamics constrain cue-evoked behavior
text:
Title: Spontaneous brain-wide rotational dynamics constrain cue-evoked behavior
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Uncovering low-dimensional representations of brain-wide neural dynamics and their relationship to behavior remains a central challenge. Here, we show that spontaneous brain-wide rotational dynamics constrain cue-evoked behavior and learning. To systematically establish these findings, we developed a dimensionality-reduction technique called Rotational Component Analysis (RCA) that optimizes the detection of low-variance rotational modes even within individual trials. We applied RCA to motor-cortical spike-train data from monkeys and humans, mouse cortex-wide calcium imaging, and human functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). In mice, a rotational mode identified from activity recorded at rest predicts cue-evoked behavior: the phase of rotation when a randomly timed cue arrives predicts whether the animal subsequently pulls the lever. We explain this surprisingly strong correlation using both a recurrent neural network (RNN) and a minimal two-dimensional model of response learning, in which the intrinsic rotational mode serves as a dynamical constraint on response and learning. We further identify double-rotation modes containing two centers of rotation that separate preparatory from task dynamics in both mouse and human data. Remarkably, corresponding modes also organize neural dynamics during a non-motor human task, and rotational irreversibility captures early psychosis even when principal component analysis shows no group difference. Our work establishes rotational dynamics as low-dimensional coordinates that constrain how ongoing brain states are converted into behavior. More broadly, RCA provides a versatile tool for detecting hidden nonreciprocal dynamics in biological and physical datasets.

title: How large an effect would we have seen? Positive controls, detection floors and dataset pitfalls in scalp-EEG speech decoding
text:
Title: How large an effect would we have seen? Positive controls, detection floors and dataset pitfalls in scalp-EEG speech decoding
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Objective. Studies that decode imagined speech from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) commonly validate their pipelines with a positive control, usually overt speech, and report null results without stating what effect size the pipeline could have detected. Approach. Using ds003626 ("Thinking out loud"), KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, we audited decoding of overt speech, articulator preparation and imagined speech with artifact-channel subsets, band-limited decoding and trial selection, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion. We injected class-dependent effects of known amplitude into the real recordings to measure the detection floor of five decoder families, and we checked the ds003626 labels against the dataset's acquisition protocol. Main results. On ds003626, two lip electrodes decoded overt speech at 0.7430 and the eight external channels at 0.7068, against 0.4231 for the 128-channel scalp montage, and no decodable signal survived in the 8-30 Hz band. On the other two corpora, within-subject accuracy rose monotonically with frequency into the range dominated by muscle activity. Band-power logistic regression detected an injected 8-30 Hz desynchronization of 0.54 uV under a criterion fixed in advance, whereas a compact convolutional network (EEGNet) detected nothing within subject up to 4.31 uV. In ds003626, the condition codes are the reverse of the intuitive reading, the class encoding changed between public releases, and condition is a deterministic function of time within each session. Significance. In these corpora the overt-speech positive control is dominated by myogenic signal and cannot validate a decoding pipeline. We recommend that speech-decoding studies report band-limited and artifact-channel accuracy, the direction of accuracy across frequency, and a measured detection floor.

title: D3Tree: Learning to Prune Block-Diffusion Draft Trees for Efficient Verification
text:
Title: D3Tree: Learning to Prune Block-Diffusion Draft Trees for Efficient Verification
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Block-diffusion drafters propose a whole block of tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees built from their position-wise marginals increase the expected accepted length of speculative decoding. Every tree node occupies a query row in target verification, so under concurrent serving low-yield branches compete with other requests for verification capacity. Existing tree methods select verified nodes by draft probability under a fixed or cost-selected per-request budget, and thus always retain a prefix of the drafter's ranking. We present D3Tree, which learns which nodes of a block-diffusion draft tree are worth verifying. A tree-size head with 2H+2 parameters predicts each candidate's conditional survival from the draft state, the candidate embedding, and its draft log-probability. Thresholding the product of these scores along parent chains yields an ancestor-closed subtree whose size adapts to each request and decoding round. The head is trained on a frozen drafter with conditional labels on the full candidate tree; an optional joint mode also steers the drafter toward the retained reference path. At serving time, D3Tree verifies whole trees under light load and, under heavy load, allocates one batch-wide node budget by predicted survival, sized to the target's matrix-multiplication tiles. Retained trees share one ancestor-masked target pass, while construction, pruning, and scheduling run on the GPU and overlap with the host. Across six vision-language verifiers and 17 text and multimodal benchmarks, D3Tree is fastest in 70 of 72 load settings, with 3.2-4.0x speedup over autoregressive decoding for one request and 1.3-1.8x at 64 concurrent requests, where fixed-budget trees fall below autoregressive speed. Under a time-varying arrival trace, it has the lowest mean end-to-end latency in every arrival phase.

title: Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the random velocity model with controlled sweeping
text:
Title: Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the random velocity model with controlled sweeping
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

The present paper establishes the Richardson dispersion law, predicting the particle separation with time according to $\E R_t^2 \sim t^3$, as well as anomalous dissipation for the associated tracer, for a random Hölder continuous velocity vectorfield with controlled sweeping.

title: Functional Dimensional Regularization for the Lee-Yang Model
text:
Title: Functional Dimensional Regularization for the Lee-Yang Model
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We apply functional dimensional regularization (FDR) to the Lee-Yang universality class, a paradigmatic non-unitary theory, and compute its main critical exponents across the dimension range $3\leq d\leq 6$. By combining a second-order derivative expansion with polynomial field expansions, we obtain results that are compatible with resummed $\varepsilon$-expansion as well as with state-of-the-art estimates from Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy Sphere techniques. This demonstrates that, in the context of non-unitary theories, FDR retains the efficiency and rapid convergence to accurate critical exponents already observed in the Ising and O(N) cases.

title: Changepoint localization via nested exchangeability tests: from point estimates to confidence intervals
text:
Title: Changepoint localization via nested exchangeability tests: from point estimates to confidence intervals
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We study distribution-free uncertainty quantification for a changepoint estimate in an offline setting. We observe a sequence with a single changepoint and are given an estimate of its location. The pre- and post-change segments are independent and each consists of i.i.d. (or, more generally, exchangeable) observations from arbitrary and unknown distributions. We introduce Changepoint LOcalization via Nested Exchangeability testing (CLONE), a novel method for constructing distribution-free confidence intervals around that estimate by testing exchangeability in nested windows centered at the reference estimate. Under these assumptions, CLONE provides finite-sample coverage for any black-box reference estimator. Using a geometrically shrinking radius grid, CLONE requires only $O(log n)$ permutation tests. We characterize optimal scores for the framework and provide practical recommendations that result in sharp confidence intervals. Under mild assumptions, CLONE confidence intervals have asymptotically vanishing normalized length. Simulations and experiments on image and text data support our theoretical findings.

title: CosmoVerse Data Challenge: How Tip of the Red Giant Branch Analysis Choices Shape the Inferred Hubble Constant
text:
Title: CosmoVerse Data Challenge: How Tip of the Red Giant Branch Analysis Choices Shape the Inferred Hubble Constant
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Tip of the red giant branch (TRGB)-based determinations of the Hubble constant ($H_0$), the current expansion rate of the Universe, depend on choices made in selecting and analyzing stellar photometry and in assembling the sample of calibrator galaxies hosting Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia). The CosmoVerse Data Challenge invites participants to analyze public photometric catalogs within a shared distance-ladder framework, opening each step of the measurement to the community and testing how these choices propagate into $H_0$. Participants independently selected photometric catalogs, galaxies, and TRGB measurement settings, while using a common SN Ia compilation and fitting procedure to convert distances into $H_0$. Supported by public notebooks and a training school, the challenge received 26 submissions from 22 participants. All submissions used the same analysis notebook, many participants were trainees at the school, and the true galaxy distances are unknown; the results therefore characterize the sensitivity of the submissions to analysis and sample-selection choices and are not a combined determination of $H_0$ or an estimate of the systematic uncertainty in published TRGB measurements. The inferred $H_0$ values have a median of $77.10\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and a standard deviation of $7.38\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ $(5.11\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for the scaled median absolute deviation), $\sim 3.4$ $(\sim 2.4)$ times the typical quoted uncertainty of a submission. Differences in the measured tip of the anchor galaxy NGC 4258 add a coherent shift in the distance scale. The challenge shows how different choices within a common framework can produce substantially different values of $H_0$, and provides an open basis for tracing these differences and for making datasets and tools more transparent and accessible.

title: Flow Matching Meets 3D Curvilinear Structure Segmentation in Medical Imaging
text:
Title: Flow Matching Meets 3D Curvilinear Structure Segmentation in Medical Imaging
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Segmentation of curvilinear anatomical structures in 3D medical images remains challenging due to complex topology, severe class imbalance, weak contrast, and large variations in structure morphology. While deep learning approaches for 3D curvilinear segmentation have been proposed, they are often tailored to specific anatomies or modalities, limiting generalization across clinical settings and leaving room for improvement. Recent generative models have shown the benefits of iterative prediction for structured segmentation tasks, yet diffusion-based methods suffer from computationally expensive sampling, hindering their use on high-resolution 3D volumes. We present 3D-CurvSegFlow, a flow matching-based model for 3D curvilinear structure segmentation. The model learns a continuous transformation from a simple source distribution to the target vascular representation, enabling progressive refinement of complex curvilinear geometries with efficient inference. We evaluate our method on Three public challenging datasets covering distinct anatomies and modalities: portal vein, cerebral vessel, and coronary arteries. Using a common architecture and training strategy across all tasks, our method outperforms general-purpose and vessel-specific approaches, with strong preservation of thin branches and vascular continuity. This work not only advances the state-of-the-art in 3D curvilinear segmentation but also opens new avenues for efficient, generalizable, and clinically applicable methods in medical image analysis.

title: Fade to... Red? Scheduling Coloured Noise Exploration Supports Efficient Robot Learning with Reduced Movement Jerk
text:
Title: Fade to... Red? Scheduling Coloured Noise Exploration Supports Efficient Robot Learning with Reduced Movement Jerk
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Exploration in deep reinforcement learning (RL) for continuous control is commonly driven by temporally uncorrelated Gaussian (white) action noise, which leads to jerky motions with locally constrained exploration. In contrast, temporally correlated coloured noise, particularly pink noise, has been shown to support more efficient exploration in RL. Motivated by these findings, we inquire whether scheduling changes to the noise colour over the course of training can outperform white noise for continuous control robotics. We perform a systematic study of 49 linear schedules between white and red noise, together with generalised state-dependent exploration (gSDE), on four sparse-reward manipulation tasks with a Fetch arm and a Shadow Dexterous Hand. We find that the noise colour at the end of training does not affect learning efficiency or end performance, whereas fading towards red noise halves the jerk of exploration in every task. Balancing learning efficiency, end performance and smoothness, red noise emerges as the preferred strategy: it learns as efficiently as pink noise with almost 2-fold less movement jerk. We therefore recommend exploration schedulers that fade towards red noise as the default for off-policy robot learning.

title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
text:
Title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Vanishing-error recovery of a fusion qubit from a fixed-sector ground doublet of four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain requires at least the shorter three-defect span of physical spins to leading order. Across arbitrary preselected spin sets and unrestricted joint decoding, this bound holds when the thermodynamic limit precedes large spacings at fixed positive ratios. An exact interval decoder attains it. Collective records of both logical axes in the complement force successful near-minimal supports to concentrate in density on a leading-order shortest interval.

title: Pepti-Agent: An AI Agent for Peptide Design and Optimization
text:
Title: Pepti-Agent: An AI Agent for Peptide Design and Optimization
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Therapeutic peptides occupy a valuable design space between small molecules and biologics, but their development requires satisfying several competing constraints at once: solubility, hemolytic activity, and nonspecific surface fouling are governed by overlapping sequence features, so improving one property often degrades another. Computational design addresses this by pairing generative models with sequence-based property predictors, iteratively proposing and refining candidates. However, these components are typically wired together as monolithic scripts that are difficult to inspect, extend, or reuse, and they often refine sequences by natural-language reasoning rather than by tracking the evolving multi-property state of each candidate. We present Pepti-Agent, a closed-loop, peptide-specific framework that exposes generation, property prediction, and single-residue mutation as independently inspectable Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools. A large language model controller invokes these tools and consults live predictor output between calls, so refinement is guided by each sequence's current property profile rather than by language reasoning alone. Task-specific PeptideGPT models generate candidates, ProtBERT-based classifiers score solubility, hemolysis, and non-fouling, and two interchangeable mutation operators propose sequence edits. By recording a per-step trace of controller decisions, predictor outputs, and accepted mutations, Pepti-Agent offers a reproducible substrate for benchmarking multi-objective design strategies and for prioritizing candidates for experimental validation.

title: Vapor phase growth and characterization of van der Waals BiSbTeSe platelets on semiconducting MoS2
text:
Title: Vapor phase growth and characterization of van der Waals BiSbTeSe platelets on semiconducting MoS2
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Three dimensional topological insulators of the tetradymite family, such as BiSbTeSe (BSTS), are attractive for spintronic and quantum device applications because of their compensated, bulk-insulating character. Nanostructured BSTS platelets are promising for practical TI based devices. However, their growth often requires complex equipment, organometallic precursors, or electrically insulating substrates. Simple growth on technologically relevant semiconducting substrates remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the vapor phase growth of van der Waals BSTS platelets directly on semiconducting MoS2 using a presynthesized BiSbTe1.5Se1.5 crystal as the source material. The grown BSTS platelets exhibit thicknesses ranging from 4 nm to 246 nm, with an average lateral size of 1.4 mkm for individual platelets. Raman spectra of platelets, acquired in correlation with AFM thickness measurements, reveal contributions from both BSTS and the underlying MoS2 substrate. Among the characteristic BSTS modes, A21g mode shows the highest sensitivity to platelet thickness and local composition. EDS analysis reveals a systematic thickness dependence of the platelet composition, with an apparent crossover around 49 nm that coincides with a change in the thickness dependence of the low-wavenumber component of the E2g Raman band. This correlation suggests a composition-related origin of the Raman behavior, with the compositional variations tentatively attributed to the differential volatility of the constituent elements during growth. These results demonstrate that MoS2 is a promising van der Waals platform for BSTS deposition and provide a structural and compositional baseline for future studies of BSTS-MoS2 heterostructures.

title: FinEvolveKG: Controlled and Attributable Prompt Evolution for Financial Knowledge Graph Construction
text:
Title: FinEvolveKG: Controlled and Attributable Prompt Evolution for Financial Knowledge Graph Construction
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Financial institutions construct knowledge graphs (KGs) from shared SEC 10-Ks to serve risk analysis, portfolio management, and investment research, whose analytical needs differ. Extraction must adapt without fragmenting shared grounding, typing, and temporal rules. Hand-authored persona prompts and fine-tuning add cost. Weight-free prompt optimization offers an alternative, but unconstrained evolution of a monolithic prompt can rewrite shared rules alongside persona guidance, obscuring changes and complicating review. We introduce FinEvolveKG, a KG-construction harness separating reusable general and persona-policy blocks and mechanically confining GEPA, a reflective prompt optimizer, to the designated block. During persona adaptation, the approved general block remains byte-stable and every optimizer edit is localized to a separately versioned persona policy. A dual objective balances generic temporal-KG quality with persona-relevant facts, motifs, and multi-hop connectivity. We evaluate five mutation scopes on ticker-disjoint 10-K splits, with three seeds for the persona-conditioned arms (v3-v5) across three personas. On the three-seed mean, the complete two-stage block-constrained workflow (v4) improves over the frozen prompt baseline (v1) by 19.4-30.9% and over the tested unconstrained full-prompt workflow (v5) by 2.2-6.4%, leading v5 on both objective components and winning all nine paired-seed comparisons with the lowest seed variance in every persona. Without further optimization, v4 also exceeds v5 across all evaluated out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts. An SME audit supports using the generated triplets as ground truth; a blinded two-SME audit favors v4 over v5 in 70.1% of contrast-enriched judgments. These results show that mechanically attributable evolution can coexist with strong empirical performance, without attributing the gains causally to the boundary.

title: Transient PULSE: Code for the Transient Propagation of UltraLight (pseudo)Scalars to Earth
text:
Title: Transient PULSE: Code for the Transient Propagation of UltraLight (pseudo)Scalars to Earth
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We present Transient PULSE, a software package that numerically implements a previously developed source-to-detector framework for transient ultralight bosonic signals from astrophysical bursts. Predicting these signals relies on connecting the source emission spectrum to its evolution during propagation and the resulting observables at a terrestrial detector. The package discretizes a user supplied energy spectrum into momentum modes, propagates them through a specified matter density profile and constructs the time-frequency energy density distribution at Earth, accounting for dispersion and in-medium screening effects. This treatment accommodates non-Gaussian source spectra and provides inputs for detector specific analyses. A complementary analytical module estimates coupling sensitivities, arrival time delays and screening thresholds from parameterized source and detector properties.

title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev-Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
text:
Title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev-Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum-inspired numerical methods for partial differential equations represent discretized fields and operators as quantics tensor trains (QTT), so that their cost depends on how compressible the problem is rather than on the number of unknowns. Global spectral formulations in this setting have so far relied on Fourier bases, restricted to periodic problems, or on collocation, which does not preserve the variational structure exploited by tensor-network solvers. We introduce a QTT Chebyshev-Galerkin method that assembles and solves global spectral systems directly in compressed form, without forming the underlying arrays. Starting from the weak formulation, the method handles coupled elliptic systems with variable coefficients, smoothly mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet-Robin boundary conditions, and yields symmetric positive-definite systems suited to variational tensor-network solvers. Parameters and random inputs enter as additional coordinates, so the same construction returns the solution over an entire parameter space in a single solve. In linear elasticity, the method retains spectral convergence and reaches errors below $10^{-8}$ on a three-dimensional benchmark, beyond those attained by QTT finite differences and Q2/Q4 FEniCSx finite elements over the tested range. A six-parameter cantilever design study covering $1.7\times10^{7}$ designs is solved in a single 92s run, and a stochastic problem with ten random coordinates is represented with $2.4\times10^{6}$ times less memory than its full coefficient array.

title: Physiology as Topology: Intervenable Organ Graphs for Longitudinal Patient Forecasting
text:
Title: Physiology as Topology: Intervenable Organ Graphs for Longitudinal Patient Forecasting
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Do language models forecast patient trajectories by reasoning through physiology, or by fitting surface statistics? We introduce PhysioCircuit, a multi-agent agent system that represents each organ as an agent and each physiological relation as an editable mechanism card with direction, lag, and evidence. Its expert-defined graph is frozen at inference, enabling controlled edge interventions. We also introduce PhysioCircuit-Bench, a mechanism-controlled benchmark spanning three organ systems, treatment events, and real ICU admissions. We evaluate intervention-direction agreement (IDAR), which requires the affected organ to change in the expected direction within the expected lag window. The expert graph substantially outperforms all topology controls on edge-IDAR, including fully connected, random, and reversed graphs. Independent clinician adjudication supports the counterfactual results. PhysioCircuit transfers to new organ systems by configuration alone, without retraining, while preserving inspectable and editable relations.

title: Development of time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy using heralded emission spectroscopy for organic light-emitting materials
text:
Title: Development of time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy using heralded emission spectroscopy for organic light-emitting materials
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Organic light-emitting materials are widely used in optoelectronics and bioimaging, but sometimes conventional fluorescence spectroscopy techniques can be limited by scattering, background fluorescence, photon pile-up and photobleaching. We report a quantum-spectroscopic approach using frequency-entangled, nondegenerate photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion with heralded detection, to perform photoluminescence lifetime measurements at low excitation intensities. We demonstrate this approach across three organic light-emitting material classes: the fluorescent dye Rhodamine 6G, an organic semiconducting conjugated polymer poly[2-methoxy-5-(2-ethylhexyloxy)-1,4-phenylenevinylene] (MEH-PPV), and a fluorescent protein mOrange. The intrinsic timing correlation between signal and idler photons enables coincidence gating that suppresses uncorrelated background counts. Across all materials and integration times of 500, 1000 and 3600 seconds, heralded detection yields signal-to-noise ratios 1.6-3.0 times higher than classical pulsed-laser excitation attenuated to match heralded photon counts in the fitting range. For MEH-PPV, this roughly halves the noise amplitude. Our measured lifetimes closely match long-integration classical pulsed-laser reference values.

title: Near linear mixing of random-cluster Glauber dynamics on random regular graphs
text:
Title: Near linear mixing of random-cluster Glauber dynamics on random regular graphs
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study the random-cluster model on locally treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p \in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q \in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, at parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf u}(q,d)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all graphs with degree bounded by $d$. On typical graphs, the same is predicted at $p>p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$, where $p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $d$-regular wired tree. Our result confirms this prediction for random regular graphs, showing that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix in time $O(n^{1+o(1)})$ on a random $d$-regular graph for all fixed $q>2$ and $p>p_{\mathsf s}$. For comparison, the best prior sampling results for these models that held for all $p>p_{\mathsf s}$ required $q\gtrsim \log d$ \cite{BGPZ26}. The key difficulty is that simply utilizing the contraction of cavity messages on $d$-regular trees does not suffice to cover the entire regime $q>2$. To address this issue, motivated by \cite{LS26}, we develop a careful bootstrap argument to show the shrinkage of disagreement under grand coupling. The core ideas of the proof were generated using GPT-6 and the Pharos system; the proof was then refined and simplified by the author.

title: Planting neutrino SE-EdS: A < 3% accurate clustering approximation for neutrinos and other hot dark matter
text:
Title: Planting neutrino SE-EdS: A < 3% accurate clustering approximation for neutrinos and other hot dark matter
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The age of the cosmic neutrino is upon us. Aside from their fundamental importance to particle physics and the recent tensions in their mass scale $M_ν= \sum m_ν$, neutrinos' degeneracies with other cosmological parameters in analyses of scale-dependent cosmic clustering will significantly affect the estimates of these parameters, making accurate, inexpensive, easily-implemented approximations essential tools for theoretical cosmology. We present a new linear approximation, SE-EdS, applicable to non-relativistic neutrinos and other hot dark matter, which is exact in the linear Einstein-de Sitter case, and < 3% accurate for a broad range of flat and non-flat cosmologies characterized by parameters $0.2 \leq Ω_{m,0} \leq 1$, $0 \leq Ω_{ν,0} \leq 0.018$, $-0.1 \leq Ω_{K,0} \leq 0.1$, and $w_0 \leq -0.6$, at all length scales. This broad coverage in $Ω_{m,0}$ makes SE-EdS ideal for N-body simulations, whose redshift range $z \lesssim 100$ demands accuracy for time-dependent $Ω_m$ between unity and the preferred late-time values $\sim 0.3$. SE-EdS may be used to paint neutrinos into simulations in Fourier space, where its < 3% error and neutrinos' $\leq$ 3% matter fraction guarantees < 0.1% errors in the total matter density contrast, thereby including neutrino effects upon clustering at negligible computational cost. We quantify the approximation's accuracy; extend it to a broad range of cosmologies; and explore its correspondence with higher-order corrections to existing linear response schemes. A simple implementation is available online at https://codeberg.org/upadhye/SE-EdS .

title: Homogeneous to multi-scale inhomogeneous complex magnetism in Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho), Revealed by muSR and Machine-Learned Muon-Site Calculations
text:
Title: Homogeneous to multi-scale inhomogeneous complex magnetism in Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho), Revealed by muSR and Machine-Learned Muon-Site Calculations
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We report a comprehensive muon spin rotation and relaxation (muSR) study of the hexagonal 6H-perovskites Ba3LnRu2O9 (Ln = Gd, Ho) to investigate the role of rare-earth anisotropy in the magnetic ground state of 4d-4f coupled systems. Ba3HoRu2O9 exhibits two successive magnetic orderings at TN1 = 46 K and TN2 = 10 K, leading to a complex magnetic ground state, whereas Ba3GdRu2O9, with Gd3+ (L = 0) S-state ions, shows primarily single magnetic ordering at TN = 14.5 K. Zero-field (ZF) and longitudinal-field (LF) muSR measurements reveal markedly different magnetic behavior despite their structural similarity. Ba3HoRu2O9 displays a multi-scale inhomogeneous magnetic state characterized by two-component exponential relaxation, broad local-field distributions, incomplete LF decoupling, and persistent spin dynamics. The muSR results identify two characteristic magnetic energy scales near 46 and 10 K, associated with correlated Ru-Ho interactions and quasistatic magnetic ordering, respectively. Redfield analysis further demonstrates strong local magnetic fields and distributed spin fluctuation timescales, confirming magnetic inhomogeneity. Machine-learning-assisted muon-site and dipolar-field calculations show that the broad field distribution naturally arises from muons sensing distinct coexisting magnetic domains at different structural sites. In contrast, Ba3GdRu2O9 exhibits a comparatively homogeneous antiferromagnetic ground state below 14.5 K, with Gaussian relaxation consistent with a narrow static field distribution. These results establish that the rare-earth ion in Ba3LnRu2O9 is a powerful tuning parameter, driving the ground state from homogeneous to complex, multi-scale inhomogeneous behavior through competing 4d-4f magnetic interactions.

title: Online Matching with Arbitrary Stochastic Rewards
text:
Title: Online Matching with Arbitrary Stochastic Rewards
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Online matching with stochastic rewards is a generalization of online bipartite matching in which an attempt to match an online arrival to an offline resource may fail with some probability. Each arrival allows at most one attempt and the success probabilities of its edges are revealed when it arrives. Greedy is 0.5-competitive, which is the best possible for deterministic algorithms. While better competitive ratios are known in several special cases, beating 0.5 for arbitrary probabilities has remained open. We show that, against the adaptive offline benchmark and for arbitrary probabilities, a randomized Perturbed Greedy algorithm is at least 0.591-competitive in the unweighted setting and at least 0.531-competitive with vertex weights. The perturbation functions combine Greedy with scaled versions of the classic exponential function.

title: Multiplicity of elastic wave propagation in random polycrystals
text:
Title: Multiplicity of elastic wave propagation in random polycrystals
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

The coherent elastic wave in untextured polycrystals, central to ultrasonic and seismic characterization, was recently observed to have two modes per polarization at short wavelengths. However, their physical origin and amplitude partition have remained open. We address both by theory, grain-scale numerical simulations and a grain velocity estimate. The first-order smoothing approximation, simplified by the far-field approximation, predicts three waves, which are the classical effective wave and one for each type of scattered wave (longitudinal and transverse). At long wavelengths, only the effective wave is weakly attenuated. At short wavelengths, one of the other two waves joins it with comparable attenuation, whereas the third stays far more attenuated. A new residue method, which needs no fitting, gives the same pattern for the amplitude partition, with the two waves sharing the coherent field and the third carrying little. The simulations reveal exactly these two modes, for transverse waves in iron and longitudinal waves in strongly anisotropic SrMgSn, and never the third. The wavefields reveal the mechanism, in which the incident wave is extinguished within one grain correlation length and the coherent field is rebuilt by forward multiple scattering. Strikingly, a grain velocity estimate from single-crystal constants provides independent evidence, tracing the two modes to plane waves of the individual grains and closely reproducing their velocities. Observability of multiple waves is thus set by attenuation and amplitude partition together, and short-wavelength measurements in random media must allow for more than one coherent mode.

title: On self-similar random quotients of the line
text:
Title: On self-similar random quotients of the line
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

A surprisingly wide variety of important random fractal metric spaces in modern probability theory can be viewed as self-similar random quotients of the real line, including the continuum random tree, Liouville quantum gravity surfaces, the trace of Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and self-similar ($s=2d$) long-range percolation on $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that the metric and resistance growth dimensions are well-defined in a certain sense for every random metric space in a class containing all of the above examples. Our results are new for the trace of Brownian motion.

title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
text:
Title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms can only be evaluated by classical computers on restricted or small instances. Here we demonstrate automated discovery of quantum programs beyond these regimes including order-of-magnitude improvements on scientific applications.
