Exploratory analysis suggests why direction matters: a charge's potential differs at the three vacancy nitrogens and moves the spin of the two $e'$ holes among them, more when the charge faces one nitrogen than the gap between two. $E$ follows this spin imbalance through one constant, $c\approx8$ GHz per $μ_{\mathrm{B}}$, across donors and applied fields, whereas in PBE $D$ is nearly insensitive to it. A three-site model with one fitted screening constant reproduces the frozen-lattice $E$ to 83 MHz rms. Results are for one charge state in a free-standing monolayer; absolute $|E|$ varies by tens of percent across approximations.

title: Standardized Planck-Mean Absorption Coefficients for High-Temperature Gases
text:
Title: Standardized Planck-Mean Absorption Coefficients for High-Temperature Gases
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Planck-mean absorption coefficients of pure gases are calculated from line-by-line integrations of HITEMP and ExoMol spectra up to 5000 K for use in high-enthalpy radiative heat transfer simulations. The dataset extends beyond conventional combustion products, including high-temperature radicals, nitrogen-bearing species, soot precursors, metal oxides, metal hydrides, and halides: AlF, AlH, AlO, BH, C2, C2H2, CH, CH4, CN, CO, CO2, H2O, HBO, HCN, HF, MgH, MgO, N2O, NO, NO2, OH, SiO, TiH, TiO. New calculations are validated against historical correlations for overlapping species, demonstrating good agreement over their applicable temperature ranges. Strong visible opacities result in large Planck-mean absorption coefficients for many of the considered species, highlighting the need to account for their radiative contribution in extreme environments. A brute-force search over several candidate functional forms is performed to provide a common set of coefficients, establishing a standardized framework that can be easily integrated into production solvers and extended as additional high-temperature line lists become available.

title: A Note on the NP-Hardness on Quadratic Optimization over Doubly Stochastic Matrices and the Gromov-Wasserstein Problem
text:
Title: A Note on the NP-Hardness on Quadratic Optimization over Doubly Stochastic Matrices and the Gromov-Wasserstein Problem
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

The Gromov-Wasserstein problem is an extension of the regular optimal transport problem that is adapted for pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. Broadly speaking, given a pair of metric measure spaces, the Gromov-Wasserstein problem seeks couplings between these spaces that minimize the distortion between the metric evaluations. In this note we record the fact that the Gromov-Wasserstein distance between finite metric spaces is NP-Hard to compute. Our argument relies on a reduction from the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem, and it builds on ideas in Vayer's thesis and Ryner et. al's work that draw connections between the 2-Gromov-Wasserstein and the Quadratic Assignment Problem. During the preparation of this manuscript we learned of the appearance of Breitung et. al's work, whose result essentially supersedes ours. We hope this note serves as a useful companion whose proof is, hopefully, more elementary and easier to understand.

title: Continuized Quasar-Convex Acceleration via an Unbiased Finite-Mixing Network Oracle
text:
Title: Continuized Quasar-Convex Acceleration via an Unbiased Finite-Mixing Network Oracle
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study decentralized minimization of a smooth network average that is globally quasar-convex with respect to a fixed minimizer; the node functions may be nonconvex and need not share a minimizer. A unit-rate Poisson clock drives an exactly simulable continuized process: between events the state follows a closed-form accelerated flow, and each event uses one oracle vector. One master theorem covers oracles with a predictable bias and a state-dependent variance and keeps the inverse-quadratic term $\mathcal{O}(LR_0^2/(γ^2T^2))$; one selected-row lemma supplies the oracle moments of three network implementations. CQA-Net keeps a common state, mixes local rows for finitely many rounds, and disseminates one uniformly selected row; its oracle is unbiased at every mixing depth, so incomplete averaging affects only the variance. A walking token removes dissemination, the shared clock, and the shared root, and an importance weight keeps it unbiased on fixed graphs. D-CQA keeps local states and mixes them; under bounded heterogeneity it needs $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrtχ\sqrt{L}R_0/(γθ\sqrt{\varepsilon}))$ communication rounds and no dissemination. Changing graphs enter through certified operator norms. Experiments on a certified nonconvex regression on static and changing graphs compare the three implementations.

title: A Fast Proximal-Gradient Algorithm for Decentralised Optimisation
text:
Title: A Fast Proximal-Gradient Algorithm for Decentralised Optimisation
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We consider a connected multi-agent network where agents coordinate to minimise a finite sum of convex functions. Each function in the sum can be further expressed as the sum of a smooth and nonsmooth component and is known only to a single agent in the network. We propose a decentralised proximal-gradient-type algorithm for solving this problem, which we term Fast PG-EXTRA. In each iteration, agents evaluate the gradient of the smooth component of their local objective functions and the proximal operator of the nonsmooth component, followed by communicating the results with neighbouring agents in the network. Fast PG-EXTRA can be viewed as an accelerated variant of PG-EXTRA, in the sense that it enjoys non-ergodic $o(1/k^2)$ convergence rates in terms of the first-order optimality residual, successive iterates, and consensus error, compared to PG-EXTRA's ergodic $O(1/k)$ convergence rates. Our analysis of Fast PG-EXTRA is based on an accelerated variant of the Condat--Vũ algorithm for non-distributed convex minimisation, which has similarly improved convergence rates compared to the Condat--Vũ algorithm. We validate our convergence results for Fast PG-EXTRA and demonstrate its potential advantages compared to PG-EXTRA with numerical experiments for power state system estimation and $l_1$-regularised logistic regression.

title: Recurrent Modular Structure in Spiking Neural Network Reinforcement Learning
text:
Title: Recurrent Modular Structure in Spiking Neural Network Reinforcement Learning
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Biological neural circuits are both modular and recurrent, with dense communities sparsely linked to one another. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) for reinforcement learning are usually feed-forward, and it is unclear how to obtain functional modules in a recurrent SNN or what they buy. In this work, we introduce a class of spiking networks, called Community Recurrent SNNs (CoRe SNNs): recurrent networks partitioned into communities with fixed roles. A controller community receives the stimulus, each action has its own community, and latent communities carry internal state. Spiking activity is then a walk between communities, and the action is the community the walk reaches. All learning is local and three-factor, and the recurrent communities are closer to cortical microcircuits than a feed-forward actor. We compare three regimes for obtaining the communities: dynamic modularity, in which a new learning rule we introduce, Map-STDP, encourages modular structure during learning; partial modularity, in which a stochastic block model (SBM) initialization enforces it partly; and full modularity, in which sealing enforces it fully. On CartPole, across three spiking neuron models, Map-STDP improves learning over the same network without it matches full modularity (sealed communities) on two of the three models, and makes the observed spike walk more compressible. Replacing the feed-forward actor of a TD-STDP actor-critic with recurrent action communities improves on the feed-forward network on CartPole and LunarLander, and matches it on Acrobot. How strongly to enforce modularity depends on the task: full modularity helps most on Acrobot, while on LunarLander the dynamic, partial and full regimes perform alike. Overall, these recurrent modular networks can match or even improve upon feed-forward approaches, with improvements in bio-plausibility and energy efficiency.

title: Local and itinerant orbital contributions to the gyromagnetic response of paramagnetic metals
text:
Title: Local and itinerant orbital contributions to the gyromagnetic response of paramagnetic metals
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Orbitronics exploits orbital angular momentum to generate and manipulate angular-momentum currents for controlling magnetisation, offering new approaches to magnetic memory and logic. A quantitative description of this process requires establishing how orbital angular momentum contributes to magnetic moments and, consequently, to the gyromagnetic response that governs magnetisation dynamics. Here, we present a first-principles framework for calculating the effective gyromagnetic tensor (g') of paramagnetic metals, consistently incorporating local and itinerant orbital contributions, spin-orbit coupling, and both state- and occupation-change effects. Applying the framework to V and Pt, we find that orbital paramagnetic responses are comparable to or larger than spin contributions and substantially modify g' from the free-electron value. The atom-centered approximation can underestimate the orbital response by approximately a factor of two, while neglecting occupation changes produces significant errors in the calculated g'. Our calculated g' values for V and Pt agree with experiment, while their pronounced dependence on band filling reveals a route to engineering angular-momentum responses through electronic-structure control. The results establish the modern theory of orbital magnetism as an essential ingredient for describing gyromagnetic response and provide a framework for identifying materials with enhanced orbital functionalities.

title: TACTUS: A Robotic Palpation System for Spatially Heterogeneous Hardness Mapping of Woody Breast Myopathy
text:
Title: TACTUS: A Robotic Palpation System for Spatially Heterogeneous Hardness Mapping of Woody Breast Myopathy
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Woody breast (WB) myopathy is a spatially heterogeneous fibro-degenerative condition of the broiler Pectoralis major muscle. Existing mechanical reference methods rely on single-point or sequential compression measurements, limiting characterization of spatial hardness variability. This study presents TACTUS (Tactile Adaptive Conformal 3D Uniform Sensing), an automated tactile array that generates thickness-normalized, three-dimensional hardness maps at 20 anatomically distributed locations within approximately 30 s. TACTUS integrates 20 independently motorized tactuators with force-sensing resistors and encoder-driven linear actuators, alongside a LiDAR depth camera for surface profiling and adaptive compression. The system was evaluated using 100 broiler breast fillets across four WB severity classes (Normal, Mild, Moderate, Severe). TACTUS identified significant force differences among severity classes (ANOVA, p < 0.001), with the strongest differentiation in the cranial region and a significant caudal effect not detected by texture-analyzer measurements. Fillet-level TACTUS force showed moderate but significant correlation with texture-analyzer measurements (Pearson r = 0.441, p < 0.001). Semivariogram, local change entropy, and heterogeneity analyses revealed increasing and anatomically structured hardness variability with WB severity. These findings demonstrate TACTUS as an automated, operator-independent platform for spatially resolved mechanical characterization and ground-truth generation to support hyperspectral and near-infrared spectroscopy-based WB classification systems.

title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
text:
Title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

title: An adaptive time-tree transition kernel for Bayesian phylogenetic inference
text:
Title: An adaptive time-tree transition kernel for Bayesian phylogenetic inference
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Bayesian phylogenetic and phylodynamic analyses can be very time-consuming, owing to the combination of complex models that are used to estimate key parameters from increasingly large genomic data sets and their associated metadata. The use of high-performance computer hardware can -- to a certain extent -- alleviate the computational burden and markedly decrease the time to results. Still, even converging to the posterior can be a lengthy endeavour, with the burn-in aspect of such analyses potentially taking days or even weeks for large data sets. One of the key aspects that hampers performance in Bayesian phylogenetic inference is the efficiency with which tree topology proposals explore tree space. We here propose a novel adaptive tree transition kernel, which we call `subTreeLeap' (STL), which involves modifying the phylogeny by walking along patristic distance paths in the tree according to an adaptable radius parameter. STL is a general proposal, which can be used with contemporaneous or time-calibrated sequence data, being particularly suited to the latter due to respecting temporal precedence constraints. We carefully assess its impact on convergence and statistical mixing of the exploration of posterior tree space, by comparison to replicate ``golden runs'' obtained from lengthy analyses of empirical data under standard tree transition kernels. We find that STL successfully explores the same posterior tree space as standard kernels, but often does so in a more efficient manner. We discuss limitations as well as future potential improvements to STL that could substantially increase the speed at which Bayesian phylogenetic inferences are obtained.

title: Graph-Guided Bayesian Factor Analysis: A Fast Integrated EFA-CFA Approach for High-Dimensional Data
text:
Title: Graph-Guided Bayesian Factor Analysis: A Fast Integrated EFA-CFA Approach for High-Dimensional Data
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Factor analysis has been central to the analysis of high-dimensional biomedical data. However, existing exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis methods face several limitations: less interpretable factor findings, difficulty in identifying which variables can and cannot be represented by low-dimensional factors, challenges in estimating the covariance among factors, and maximum-likelihood fits that break down when variables outnumber subjects. We propose graph-guided Bayesian factor analysis (gg-BFA) to address these gaps. We first use a Bayesian model to explore and learn the latent graph structure, identifying which variables can and cannot be represented by low-dimensional factors and how many factors are needed. A dense-subgraph search proposes partitions of the variables into communities, each defining one factor, and a forward stepwise search compares their fractional variational posteriors and stops when the evidence lower bound first decreases. We show that this search recovers the true communities even when the number of variables grows much faster than the sample size. We then develop a confirmatory Bayesian model whose variational posterior of the covariance contracts at the parametric rate up to a logarithmic factor, yielding posterior inference for the factors and their covariance, as well as predictions of missing values. Its four members range from a community mask to several cross-loadings per variable. In five biomedical panels, the complete analysis took under ten minutes each on one GPU, and cross-loadings improved held-out covariance and the prediction of masked measurements. In TCGA Kidney, six of the first eight factors were enriched for known pathways, and 190 of the 210 factor correlations had 95% credible intervals excluding zero. Overall, gg-BFA is computationally fast and provides interpretable factor analysis findings and reliable inference results.

title: Radio view of the Peanut cluster: merger-induced stripping and a radio halo shortly after pericentric passage
text:
Title: Radio view of the Peanut cluster: merger-induced stripping and a radio halo shortly after pericentric passage
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The Peanut galaxy cluster (SRGe CL0238.3+2005) offers a rare opportunity to investigate thermal and nonthermal processes only $\sim0.1$\,Gyr after pericentric passage. We present a multi-frequency radio study of this system at $z=0.42$ using new MeerKAT and uGMRT observations, complemented by Chandra and MUSTANG-2 data. We identify two morphologically and spectrally distinct radio components: a double-lobed source in the northern subcluster and extended diffuse emission across the cluster center. The double-lobed source has a strongly curved, ultra-steep spectrum and is offset by $\sim22$\,kpc from the nearest brightest cluster galaxy. Its spectral curvature and positional offset are consistent with remnant AGN plasma that may have been displaced during the merger or reshaped by a shock. The diffuse emission extends over $\sim1$~Mpc and is classified as an ultra-steep spectrum ($α=-1.77\pm0.11$ between 400\,MHz and 1.28\,GHz) radio halo. Its volume-averaged radio emissivity, $(1.1\pm0.1)\times10^{-41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-3}$ Hz$^{-1}$ at 1.4\,GHz, is an order of magnitude higher than the characteristic value for other halos. The radial profile of the halo is well described by a single exponential fit and its radio emission correlates tightly with the X-ray, with a best-fit slope of $1.11\pm0.05$. Chandra and MUSTANG-2 observations reveal candidate surface brightness discontinuities, with the most prominent inner feature coinciding with a region of flatter spectral index, potentially tracing localized particle (re)-acceleration. The coexistence of an extended ultra-steep spectrum radio halo, high radio emissivity, remnant AGN plasma, and candidate X-ray/SZ discontinuities makes the Peanut cluster an important test case for understanding the evolution of diffuse radio emission and its connection to the dynamical state of the intracluster medium in early-stage mergers.

title: Can Blue UV-Bright Galaxies Drive Reionization at Cosmic Dawn? An $M_{\rm UV}=-19.6$ Galaxy with $f_{\rm esc}\approx0.85$ at $z=9.244$
text:
Title: Can Blue UV-Bright Galaxies Drive Reionization at Cosmic Dawn? An $M_{\rm UV}=-19.6$ Galaxy with $f_{\rm esc}\approx0.85$ at $z=9.244$
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We revisit EBG-1, a gravitationally lensed galaxy at $z = 9.244$, using newly obtained deep (14 hr) JWST/NIRSpec G235M ($R \sim 1000$) spectroscopy. EBG-1 is one of the bluest galaxies observed at $z > 9$. Along with its remarkably blue continuum of $β= -2.99 \pm 0.15$, we find very weak nebular emission from EBG-1. We obtain a $3σ$ upper limit of EW $< 8.4$ Angstrom for C III], a marginal H$β$ measurement (EW $= 256.2 \pm 122.2$ Angstrom), and a $5σ$ detection of [O III] $λ5007$ (EW $= 882.8 \pm 180.6$ Angstrom). These lines suggest an oxygen abundance of $12 + \log(\mathrm{O/H}) = 7.16 \pm 0.25$ ($\simeq 3\% Z_{\odot}$) and $\log(\mathrm{C/O}) < -0.88$ ($3σ$), placing EBG-1 on the C/O-metallicity sequence traced by lower-redshift galaxies. To constrain the escape fraction ($f_{\rm esc}$), we compare the observed UV slope and emission-line equivalent widths with synthetic spectra generated using BEAGLE. The models favor $f_{\rm esc} \gtrsim 0.75$, with $f_{\rm esc} \approx 0.85$ providing the best overall agreement with the observations. These results suggest that relatively UV-bright galaxies like EBG-1 can achieve the exceptionally high ionizing efficiencies supported by late reionization scenarios.

title: Site4Drug: Predicting Drug-Binding Target Sites with an AI Agent
text:
Title: Site4Drug: Predicting Drug-Binding Target Sites with an AI Agent
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Selecting where to intervene on a protein (i.e., choosing a targetable site) is often a more ambiguous and failure-prone bottleneck than selecting what binds, especially for membrane proteins where accessibility, topology, and post-translational modifications (PTMs) constrain actionable regions. We present Site4Drug, a modality-aware site-finding agent that outputs a ranked list of targetable regions with explicit constraints, evidence summaries, risk flags, and a traceable decision log. Rather than requiring users to specify the drug modality upfront, Site4Drug can recommend a binding modality (e.g., antibody/peptide-like vs small-molecule) from the same evidence used for site discovery, including topology, hydropathy, PTM propensity, disulfides, domain context, and sequence. Importantly, this evidence is applied consistently across modalities, including small-molecule pocket discovery, to avoid selecting chemically plausible but biologically occluded sites.

title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
text:
Title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The Hubble tension motivates direct tests of the internal consistency of the local distance ladder. We perform forward and backward consistency checks between Type Ia supernovae in Cepheid host galaxies and the Hubble-flow supernova sample using Pantheon+ data. Within flat $Λ$CDM, we impose Planck-CMB priors on one sample, infer the supernova absolute-magnitude calibration, and propagate it to the other sample to recover the Hubble constant, which should match the input value if the second and third rungs of the distance ladder align perfectly. We examine the impact of host-galaxy peculiar velocities using redshift corrections based on the Manticore-Local reconstruction. These corrections shift the recovered $H_0$ from $74.30^{+1.18}_{-1.20}$ to $71.37^{+1.23}_{-1.18}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the forward analysis and from $60.83^{+0.98}_{-0.97}$ to $63.25^{+0.95}_{-0.93}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the backward analysis, bringing both results closer to the input CMB constraint. Comparing the cosmological intercepts of the magnitude-redshift relation inferred from two rungs of the distance ladder before and after peculiar-velocity corrections, we find that the significance of the discrepancy decreases from $6.8σ$ to $3.9σ$ in the forward check and from $7.3σ$ to $4.3σ$ in the backward check. Peculiar-velocity corrections therefore partially alleviate the intercept tension, while the residual discrepancy is further cut in half by volumetric bias down to $\sim1.7σ$. Our results highlight the importance of local velocity modeling and motivate further tests of sample selection and calibration systematics in assessing distance-ladder consistency.

title: IRIS: an agentic eye on symmetry-derived paths and energy landscapes of structural phase transitions
text:
Title: IRIS: an agentic eye on symmetry-derived paths and energy landscapes of structural phase transitions
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Structural phase transitions underpin ferroelectric and multiferroic functionality, but constructing interpretable energy landscapes remains dependent on specialist expertise. Predicting this behaviour rests on Landau free energies expanded in symmetry-adapted order parameters: their coefficients classify a transition, expose the couplings between distortions, set switching paths and barriers, and parametrize phase-field and effective-Hamiltonian models at larger scales. Obtaining these coefficients from first principles means sampling the Born--Oppenheimer energy surface along symmetry-derived structural paths, which requires crystallographic analysis, reliable structure generation and extensive computation, especially for coupled multidimensional order parameters. Here we introduce IRIS, an agentic workflow that converts plain-language requests and crystal structures into symmetry-adapted energy landscapes and fitted Landau energy models. Deterministic gates govern acceptance of structures, calculations and fits, while language models interpret requests and select constrained recovery actions. Applications across six compounds include a six-dimensional BiFeO$_3$ landscape that separates competition between polar and tilt amplitudes from directional locking and ranks homogeneous switching pathways. Controlled replays detected all 53 injected faults; disabling gates allowed 14 silent errors. Four prospective BaTiO$_3$ runs produced fitted landscapes from 96 density-functional calculations in 34 minutes total without intervening human decisions. IRIS makes physical model construction a reusable computational capability and provides a framework for scientific automation grounded in explicit verification.

title: Hidden Sector Relic Abundances from an Effective Planck Mass
text:
Title: Hidden Sector Relic Abundances from an Effective Planck Mass
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Hidden sectors are generic in beyond the Standard Model constructions and string compactifications. We consider models featuring hidden sectors that have dark matter candidates. The relic density is set in part by the energy-injecting inflaton branching ratio $B$ to the sector. We develop a general framework to determine the dependence on $B$ for thermalized hidden sectors by defining an effective Planck mass for the Boltzmann equations for the hidden sector degrees of freedom. We apply this framework to several representative examples, including freeze-out/freeze-in WIMPs and multi-component dark matter. We find that the fractional energy density carried by freeze-out relics (in both single and multi-component models) and monopoles produced from second order phase transitions scale as $B^{1/4}$ and thus may lead to an overclosure problem, even with $B \ll 1$. On the other hand, the energy density of freeze-in relics scales as $B^{5/4}$ and is thus cosmologically irrelevant for sufficiently small $B$. Finally, we discuss the cumulative implications of a large number of hidden sectors.

title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
text:
Title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Unplanned 30-day intensive care unit (ICU) readmission is a critical benchmark for evaluating healthcare quality. Most predictive models assume readmission risk depends solely on a patient's individual pathophysiological state, ignoring hospital operational context and resource capacity. In practice, discharge decisions are dynamic trade-offs between patient stability and bed turnover pressures. To address this gap, we develop an Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for ICU discharge risk assessment. The system combines multi-agent collaborative extraction with self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to eliminate template noise from progress notes, while constructing departmental workload indicators alongside admission flow features, continuous vital signs, and sparse medical codes (ICD/DRG). Addressing severe class imbalance (about 10.5% readmissions) and alarm fatigue, we implement data normalization, class reweighting, and decision-threshold calibration. In 20 independent runs across 20,000 ICU stays from MIMIC-III, empirical findings demonstrate that: vital signs alone have limited predictive capacity under real-world class imbalance (PR-AUC of 0.1387 +/- 0.0086); directly concatenating raw text embeddings degrades decision tree performance (XGBoost and LightGBM PR-AUC drop to 0.3893 and 0.4030); whereas an end-to-end multimodal fine-tuning architecture (Transformer E2E FineTune) utilizing layer-wise parameter freezing and differential learning rates reverses text negative transfer, achieving the highest AUROC of 0.8288 +/- 0.0110, PR-AUC of 0.4373 +/- 0.0310, and F1-Score of 0.4757 +/- 0.0196. Operational indicators supply independent risk signals, laying an engineering foundation for high-utility clinical decision support tools.

title: Tribocharging of Granular Materials Dictated by Geometric and Thermoelectric Effects
text:
Title: Tribocharging of Granular Materials Dictated by Geometric and Thermoelectric Effects
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Tribocharging of granular materials is a widespread phenomenon ranging from volcanic eruptions and dust storms to pharmaceutical processing, yet its underlying mechanism remains elusive. Recent thermoelectric models have provided a quantitative framework for triboelectric charge transfer, but they have difficulty accounting for charging between identical materials. In this Letter, we propose a theory of granular tribocharging based on the interplay between particle geometry and thermoelectric response. Collision-induced frictional heating produces a size-dependent temperature asymmetry between particles, generating a thermoelectric voltage that drives charge transfer. The sign of the Seebeck coefficient determines the charging polarity, while particle size and thermal properties set its magnitude. Our multi-collision theory explains the experimentally observed size- and material-dependent reversal of charging polarity, as in quartz and nylon.

title: Looking for gravitational waves with orbital dynamics: GUEST mission and the $μ$Hz band of Gravitational Waves
text:
Title: Looking for gravitational waves with orbital dynamics: GUEST mission and the $μ$Hz band of Gravitational Waves
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

`Adding colour'' to the gravitational-wave sky by probing unexplored frequency bands has the potential to unveil new and unexpected phenomena in the Universe. The microhertz band, between pulsar timing arrays and LISA, is a particularly attractive target: it should host the extension of the signal recently found by pulsar timing arrays (if it is generated by a family of sources of gravitational waves), and it may harbour signals from the early Universe, primordial black holes or dark matter. In these proceedings, we review how the orbits of gravitationally bound systems act as resonant detectors of microhertz gravitational waves and ultra-light dark matter. We then describe GUEST (Gravitational Universe Exploration with Satellite Tracking), a mission concept recently proposed to the ESA F-class call, consisting of two dense passive spheres covered with retroreflectors, placed in highly eccentric Earth orbits and tracked by a global laser-ranging network.

title: Nepali-English Code-Mixed Speech Recognition: Data Preparation and Adaptation of a Speech Foundation Model
text:
Title: Nepali-English Code-Mixed Speech Recognition: Data Preparation and Adaptation of a Speech Foundation Model
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Nepali speakers regularly mix English words into conversation, but multilingual speech recognisers often struggle with language switches and the writing script used for English words. We study how to adapt SraVaani, a 449M-parameter hybrid TDT-CTC model, using a 172.8-hour corpus covering six Nepali speech domains. Its pretrained tokenizer does not support digits and several common symbols. Rather than replace it or discard these recordings, we generate Nepali and English readings for numbers and use zero-shot ASR output to select a plausible form. Full fine-tuning reduces test word error rate (WER) from 48.6% to 17.1%; a 12-epoch run reaches 16.3%, compared with 16.4% for fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo. Freezing the encoder increases WER to 25.5%, while excluding numeric clips raises WER on numeric test speech from 14.3% to 21.3%. We also evaluate on FLEURS using both its original references and mixed-script alternatives. The comparison shows that transcription conventions explain part, but not all, of the out-of-domain performance loss.

title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
text:
Title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Speculative decoding speeds up language models by letting a lightweight drafter propose several future tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Block diffusion drafters such as DFlash draft a whole block in one forward pass, and DDTree builds a draft tree from their per-position distributions. Each of these distributions assumes that the drafter's own most likely continuation is correct. A tree, however, gains over a chain only on branches that leave this continuation, where the drafter's top-1 accuracy drops from 89% to 18% and its candidate lists miss the right token far more often. When re-run from the fork token, the same drafter is usually correct, so the errors come from the prefix that the distributions condition on rather than from what the drafter knows. We introduce DForkTree, a training-free method that re-anchors each branch on its own tokens. DForkTree adds n-gram statistics from the target model's own outputs to the drafter's scores as pointwise mutual information, weights them more after the fork, and builds the optimal tree under these scores exactly on the GPU. On Qwen3.5-4B and 9B, with all tree methods sharing one drafter, tree pipeline and verifier, DForkTree is the fastest tree method on every benchmark. It is up to 41.5% faster than DFlash and 15.1% faster than DDTree in the same setting, with average speedups of up to 4.75x over autoregressive decoding.

title: Cotunneling-Assisted Redistribution of Nonpassivity in a Photosynthetic Junction
text:
Title: Cotunneling-Assisted Redistribution of Nonpassivity in a Photosynthetic Junction
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We investigate how cotunneling affects passive-state ordering in a Photosystem II reaction center modelled as a nonequilibrium molecular junction. We use a full pigment excitation manifold, with excitonic and charge-transfer rates computed within a Nakajima-Zwanzig formalism using realistic spectral densities. Cotunneling is introduced through a microscopically constructed doubly reduced acceptor state obtained from relevant quinone-side two-electron configurations, while photoexcitation is allowed into the full excitonic manifold. Passive-state permutations are quantified through ergotropy and energetic capacitance. We find that thermodynamic smoothness in ergotropy and energetic capacitance can conceal microscopic state rearrangements. Cotunneling redistributes the extractable nonequilibrium energy among the quinone acceptor, the donor-pheophytin radical pair, and excitonic states with strong contributions from pigments on the inactive branch. At high Coulomb interaction, cotunneling produces no passive-state reordering. Piecewise-linear relations among ergotropy, energetic capacitance, and mean energy further reveal the population reorderings generated by cotunneling.

title: Efficient Searches for Low-Energy Structures in Clusters with Thousands of Particles: Application to the Thomson Problem
text:
Title: Efficient Searches for Low-Energy Structures in Clusters with Thousands of Particles: Application to the Thomson Problem
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We propose an algorithm for identifying low-energy minima in systems containing thousands of particles, at moderate computational cost. We focus on spherical crystals, in which particles form ordered structures on the surface of a sphere. Our method uses symmetric seed configurations, or known structures, to initialize searches across contiguous ranges of system sizes. Newly identified minima are then used to guide searches at neighbouring sizes, allowing information to propagate efficiently through configuration space. We have tested this approach on the Thomson problem, one of the few interacting-particle systems for which global optimization has been considered for systems of this size. We substantially improve on many previous solutions, particularly at larger system sizes, where systematic global optimization is computationally expensive. Since favourable packings for the Thomson problem are reflected in systems spanning atomistic to mesoscopic length scales, the newly characterized defect patterns may inform structure prediction for a broad range of problems with spherical topology.

title: The running of Weyl gauged gravity: asymptotic freedom, its obstruction, and a way out
text:
Title: The running of Weyl gauged gravity: asymptotic freedom, its obstruction, and a way out
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We compute the one-loop beta functions of quadratic gravity in Weyl conformal geometry, the gauge theory of diffeomorphisms and dilatations with a dynamical Weyl gauge boson. The divergences are extracted diagrammatically in the background field method, with a gauge fixing procedure adapted to the semidirect product structure of the gauge group. The Weyl-tensor coupling and the Weyl gauge coupling are asymptotically free, and the running of the latter is special, being independent of the other couplings and of any two-derivative matter content. The obstruction to an ultraviolet completion comes from the square of a Weyl-covariant curvature scalar, denoted $\widehat{R}{}^2$: the flow of the corresponding coupling has no fixed point in the physically interesting region and becomes trivial, the only real fixed points require a decoupled Weyl boson and a tachyonic scalar mode. This also holds when including the Standard Model with any nonminimal Higgs coupling and, more generally, for any matter with two-derivative kinetic terms. Weyl-invariant four-derivative scalars with a sufficiently large coupling to $\widehat{R}{}^2$ can remove the obstruction, producing a fixed point in the physical region that is ultraviolet attractive in all directions and has a nonvanishing Weyl gauge coupling.

title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
text:
Title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We prove that the centered height function of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble converges for each $β>0$, under rescaling of space and time variables, towards the Gaussian free field in the half-plane. The conformal structure for GFF involves the spatial change of coordinate $x\mapsto \sqrt{-x}$. The $β$--dependence is isolated in the field rescaling by $\sqrtβ$. For the proofs we study the asymptotic expansions of the moments of Laplace transforms of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble developed in our previous work with Xu.

title: Task-Calibrated Random Features via Influence-Based Error Cancellation
text:
Title: Task-Calibrated Random Features via Influence-Based Error Cancellation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Random features approximate kernel integrals by Monte Carlo, yet only selected frequency-sampling errors affect a downstream task. We propose Task-Calibrated Random Features (TCRF), which balance frequency moments constructed from task-specific influence using weights shared across kernel entries. Closed-form weights coincide with classical minimum-distance calibration; the contribution is a reusable, task-derived calibration space. We show that first-order variance equals the residual variance after projection onto this space. For kernel ridge regression, complete cancellation yields a non-Gaussian second-order limit. For kernel Stein discrepancy, a subset identity and disjoint-block variance decomposition eliminate the linear component of pilot noise. Positive exponential-tilting weights preserve the positive-semidefinite feature representation and support higher feasible calibration ranks. Paired experiments show improved approximation to exact kernel ridge regression at larger frequency budgets and to the exact empirical Stein discrepancy under a fixed alternative, even after accounting for a frequency-equivalent pilot budget. Gains are smaller with cross-validated ridge, landmark pilots require conservative rank selection, and near the Stein null allocating the pilot budget to additional ordinary frequencies is preferable.

title: Pore-scale mechanisms of capillary imbibition in cement-based materials revealed by direct numerical simulations in a realistic FIB-SEM microstructure
text:
Title: Pore-scale mechanisms of capillary imbibition in cement-based materials revealed by direct numerical simulations in a realistic FIB-SEM microstructure
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Moisture transport in cement-based materials involves transient multiphase flow through highly irregular pore networks, where evolving air--water interfaces strongly influence liquid invasion and gas displacement. Here, pore-resolved, image-based direct numerical simulations (DNS) are used to investigate spontaneous imbibition in a FIB--SEM-reconstructed cementitious microstructure, resolving air--water interface dynamics at nanometre-to-micrometre spatial scales and nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales. As these dynamics remain inaccessible to direct experimental observation at such scales, the simulations provide, to the best of our knowledge, the first direct view of transient imbibition within the capillary porosity of a realistic cementitious microstructure. The three-dimensional simulations reveal highly heterogeneous wetting-front propagation, continuous interface reconfiguration, and progressive air entrapment, showing that local dynamics depend on evolving interface curvature and capillary-pressure fields rather than on characteristic pore size alone. Significant air entrapment develops even within the capillary pores and under perfectly water-wetting conditions, progressively reducing the saturation rate, while the capillary pressure of trapped-air clusters depends strongly on local interface geometry rather than gas volume alone. Controlled two-dimensional analyses show that the balance between capillary, viscous, inertial, and gravitational effects is strongly scale-dependent. Comparison with the three-dimensional simulations highlights the importance of out-of-plane interface curvature and pore-network connectivity. The framework also resolves moisture conditions at the steel--concrete interface, illustrating its potential for corrosion-relevant pore-scale analysis.

title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
text:
Title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Existing multimodal attribution methods typically rely on paired modalities as proxy supervision, implicitly assuming that image-text pairs are semantically aligned. Information bottleneck (IB)-based attribution methods follow this general paradigm and instantiate it through a global sufficiency-compression objective. In realistic multimodal datasets, however, this assumption is frequently violated due to partial semantic misalignment and unreliable cross-modal correspondences. Through theoretical analysis, we show that, under such misalignment, information-bottleneck-based attribution objectives exhibit a structural limitation: by assuming equal reliability across all proxy supervision signals, they induce posterior over-contraction and forced explanations. To address this issue, we propose TIB, a sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck framework that adaptively modulates attribution strength according to cross-modal reliability, without assuming semantic alignment. Extensive experiments on controlled benchmarks and large-scale datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed approach, while also validating the identified failure mode.

title: Defect Anomalies at a Distance
text:
Title: Defect Anomalies at a Distance
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Surface defects carry Weyl and gravitational anomalies that generalize the central charges of two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) and characterize the anomalous response of gapless surface modes to background geometry. These anomalies usually appear as contact terms on the defect. We explain how they are encoded at a distance, in scheme-independent integrated bulk stress-tensor correlators. We derive sum rules for them in terms of defect operator data, establish a lower bound on the boundary Weyl anomaly in three-dimensional CFTs, and illustrate our results with explicit examples.

title: When Are Nesterov Trajectories Eventually Locally Minimizing?
text:
Title: When Are Nesterov Trajectories Eventually Locally Minimizing?
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We revisit the variational characterization of Nesterov's celebrated method and study when Nesterov trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, a notion that we define precisely. We show that this question is equivalent to the nonnegativity of an associated Schrödinger operator acting on variations of the trajectory. For power objectives of the form \[ f(x)=\frac{1}{p}\|x\|^p \] (where $\| \cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm), we give a complete characterization: Among all exponents $p\ge 2$, the Nesterov trajectory with non-zero initial position is eventually locally minimizing if and only if $p=4$. We further interpret this exceptional exponent through the stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.

title: Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians
text:
Title: Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Simulation of molecular vibrations is emerging as a promising application of quantum computing in quantum chemistry. In this work, we develop new strategies for block-encoding the second-quantized $n$-mode representation of the vibrational Hamiltonian, whose algebraic structure closely parallels that of the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. We derive linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) representations of this Hamiltonian based on Pauli decomposition and tensor hypercontraction (THC) and construct efficient circuits for the corresponding block encodings. We also extend the Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) technique to vibrational Hamiltonians, yielding a lower LCU 1-norm and, consequently, a lower overall circuit cost. For the molecules considered here, BLISS-THC reduces the Toffoli cost of quantum phase estimation by more than two orders of magnitude relative to existing block-encoding approaches. In comparison with recent Trotter-based methods, it shows up to a ninefold reduction in the T-gate count, with the relative savings tending to increase with system size. Asymptotically, and up to polylogarithmic factors, both the Pauli and THC LCUs trade additional ancillas for a quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modes, while THC provides an additional quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modals. These results highlight the importance of Hamiltonian factorizations and Toffoli-qubit tradeoffs for reducing the computational cost of quantum simulations of molecular vibrations.

title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
text:
Title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^\natural$ and formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own.

title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs
text:
Title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Production deployments often use different models to balance cost and quality through cascading, routing, and switching models during long conversations. Context accumulates across turns. Each switch requires the target to repeat prefill over this context. Existing methods transfer full-attention (FA) K/V caches across models. Hybrid linear-attention models also retain recurrent states (REC) and convolution histories (Conv). The interaction between Conv and REC complicates cross-model state transfer. Conv perturbations can change keys and values in recurrent layers and alter REC updates. Conv histories are overwritten, but changes in REC can still affect later outputs. More accurate REC reconstruction need not improve continuation. Building on this, we propose Hybrid State Transfer (HST) for all three state types. It uses structured REC maps and preserves history order during Conv alignment. We calibrate the adapters using the frozen target's outputs during continuation. FA cache map updates are merged offline. Across five benchmarks, Qwen3.5 4B$\rightarrow$27B and 9B$\rightarrow$27B achieve mean task retentions of 89.88% and 94.11%, respectively. With source caches already available, separate timing on synthetic 16K inputs yields handoff body speedups of $21.66\times$ and $21.91\times$.

title: RATSIFT: Resolution-Adaptive Transformer for Solar Irradiance Forecasting and Temporal Downscaling
text:
Title: RATSIFT: Resolution-Adaptive Transformer for Solar Irradiance Forecasting and Temporal Downscaling
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Accurate forecasting and temporal downscaling of solar irradiance is critical for reliable renewable energy integration and grid management. Traditional methods often struggle to capture rapid irradiance variability. In this work, we develop a Transformer-based architecture for simultaneous forecasting and temporal downscaling. The model takes input data at arbitrary resolutions and generates outputs at any resolutions represented within the training data, leveraging both global and local contextual information. To improve training efficiency, a genetic algorithm-based optimization framework is implemented to identify suitable model hyperparameters, while reducing the computational cost of exhaustive grid search. The effectiveness of the proposed model is shown by analyzing real data in Dallas, Texas. The proposed model achieved root mean square error (RMSE) values of 28.785, 29.544, 30.157, 32.132~W/m\(^2\) for 15-, 30-, 60-minute, and irregularly spaced global input and producing forecast at 5-minutes resolution, respectively. Furthermore, this model produced reliable uncertainty estimates, exhibiting wider prediction intervals for high-resolution inputs during volatile solar conditions, whereas coarser-resolution inputs result in narrower intervals and significantly lower training time and computational cost. Our approach provides a scalable and efficient framework for multi-resolution solar irradiance forecasting and temporal downscaling, suitable for practical energy forecasting and grid management applications.

title: LongCap: Hour-Scale Timestamped Audio Captioning via Chunk-wise Processing
text:
Title: LongCap: Hour-Scale Timestamped Audio Captioning via Chunk-wise Processing
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Describing hours of audio requires accurate event timing and sustained descriptive detail throughout the recording. We present LongCap, a framework for timestamped audio captioning (TAC), with the human-annotated LongCapBench and three diarization-inspired metrics: Timeline Error Rate (TER), Granularity Error Rate (GER), and Caption Similarity (tcpCapSim). LongCap interleaves audio chunks with structured event captions, using relative timestamps and retained context to support length extrapolation within a 1M-token inference context window. Event-level reannotation restores caption detail, while systematic studies examine model scaling, dependency supervision, and self-distillation. LongCap-Diar achieves strong benchmark results and extrapolates to 16 hours of concatenated audio despite training on recordings no longer than 40 minutes. Our TAC models are competitive with Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus on short clips, outperform evaluated baselines in caption similarity and timeline accuracy in segment-level comparisons on LongCapBench-TAC-Long, and caption full recordings approaching two hours. On LongCapBench-TAC, 9B and 35B-A3B offer favorable size-performance tradeoffs, while 122B-A10B substantially improves event-dependency recovery. These findings support long-horizon general audio understanding and provide a foundation for always-on voice agents.

title: Homeostatic Noise Buffering in Biomolecular Condensates Hinges on Phase Multiplicity Modulated by Interfacial and Droplet Size Effects
text:
Title: Homeostatic Noise Buffering in Biomolecular Condensates Hinges on Phase Multiplicity Modulated by Interfacial and Droplet Size Effects
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Specific mixing or demixing of molecular species is a characteristic feature of condensed intracellular membraneless compartments. How sequence patterns of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) fundamentally impact subcompartmentalization of biomolecular condensates and their role in buffering against concentration fluctuations are hereby addressed by modeling liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of polyampholytic sequence pairs using random phase approximation (RPA) polymer theory and molecular dynamics (MD). RPA theory predicts both binary and ternary LLPS in a temperature-sensitive manner. We observe demixing underpinned by ternary LLPS for pairs with dissimilar sequence charge patterns but not for pairs with similar sequence charge patterns. Notably, the predicted behaviors are corroborated by MD when RPA is augmented with interfacial tension and/or a finite-size formalism commensurating with the typical small sizes of MD model systems, supporting our stipulation that RPA theory is a useful sequence-specific modeling tool for biomolecular condensates with larger, more realistic sizes when finite-size effects are much less significant. In principle, when the condensate size is sufficiently large, ternary LLPS is superior to binary LLPS in noise buffering because the IDP compositions of the three coexisting phases in ternary LLPS remain unchanged over an extended two-dimensional concentration regime, whereas the two coexisting phases in binary LLPS are fixed only along a tieline. However, when condensate sizes are sufficiently small, the buffering capacities of ternary versus binary LLPSs are more complex as they are modulated differently by finite-size effects. Biophysical ramifications of this interplay are discussed in view of the size diversity of natural biomolecular condensates.

title: A Trust Region Approach for Learning Schrödinger Bridges
text:
Title: A Trust Region Approach for Learning Schrödinger Bridges
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

We study the numerical approximation of Schrödinger Bridges in the setting where samples from the target distribution are unavailable and only an unnormalized target density is given. In this regime, the widely used iterative proportional fitting (IPF) procedure (and its variants) often exhibits severe numerical instabilities, stemming from ill-conditioned underlying control problems and from the fact that the optimal solution may lie far from the initialization. To address these issues, we propose a trust region variant of IPF that constrains successive updates to remain at a fixed Kullback-Leibler divergence from the current iterate. This restriction significantly improves numerical stability. Moreover, we show that the resulting method admits an interpretation as a mirror descent scheme with an adaptively chosen step size. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on several challenging sampling tasks.

title: Semantically Aligned KV Cache Compression for Efficient Agentic Autoregressive Video Generation
text:
Title: Semantically Aligned KV Cache Compression for Efficient Agentic Autoregressive Video Generation
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Agentic autoregressive video generation combines semantic planning, sequential generation, and visual verification for controllable synthesis. Growing visual histories enlarge the key-value (KV) cache, increasing memory use and attention costs across candidate rollouts. Existing compression methods primarily optimize individual generators without the planner's semantic constraints, risking low priority for states supporting requested attributes or actions. We introduce SemanticKV, a training-free method for semantically aligned KV cache compression. To our knowledge, SemanticKV is the first KV cache compression method for agentic autoregressive video generation that explicitly uses planner-extracted semantic constraints to guide retention. Text cross-attention identifies constraint-related video positions, whose self-attention queries are collected into separate groups. Attention weights are averaged within each group and maximized across groups, giving each cached entry a high score when strongly used by any represented constraint. A single top-k selection retains high-scoring entries under the memory budget, leaving their keys, values, and positions unchanged. For fixed query groups and equal entry costs, this selection minimizes an additive upper bound on worst-group discarded attention. The method operates independently within each candidate without retraining or additional video generations. We evaluate four AR video backbones on three benchmarks for 5-, 30-, and 60-second generation. On Causal Forcing at a compression ratio of 0.7, SemanticKV obtains a VBench Total Score of 84.10, compared with 84.05 for the strongest compressed baseline and 83.99 for Full KV. It achieves a 1.22x speedup over Full KV and reduces KV-cache memory from 6.04 GB to 1.81 GB, a 3.35x reduction.

title: Language, Not Code Abstraction: Natural-language Training Shapes Brain-aligned Geometry
text:
Title: Language, Not Code Abstraction: Natural-language Training Shapes Brain-aligned Geometry
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Code-trained language models produce positive brain scores, which raises the question of whether abstract structure learned from programming languages can substitute for natural-language training. We trained 25 GPT-2-small models on TinyStories, Python, C functions, x86-64 assembly, and the corresponding machine code, and scored them using a shared tokenizer and encoding procedure against matched random-weight models. On Pereira-243 and Tuckute2024, TinyStories exceeds the mean of the four code models by $Δr = 0.053$ and $0.059$ (Holm-corrected $p<0.001$), while code training leaves alignment near the random-weight level. The language advantage is benchmark-specific: Blank2014 shows no corrected language-code difference, and Fedorenko2016 shows no language benefit. Geometry tracks the encoding result on Pereira-243: TinyStories seeds converge on the most similar representations, and its fit-free correspondence with neural dissimilarity peaks at $ρ= 0.14$, twice the code and random-weight levels. Binary-trained models have about three effective dimensions, so seed agreement alone does not imply neural correspondence. Updating only the embedding matrix on English improves mean-over-depth alignment for every code model more than an equal update on its own corpus. Within this architecture and training setup, natural-language training produces a distinct representational geometry with closer neural correspondence on Pereira-243

title: A constraint dissolving method for generally constrained optimization over a nonconvex set
text:
Title: A constraint dissolving method for generally constrained optimization over a nonconvex set
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This manuscript studies a constraint dissolving method for solving optimization problems with general constraints, comprising an abstract constraint G(x) \in C and a potentially nonconvex geometric constraint x \in D, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first constraint dissolving type method applicable to this general setting. More specifically, we introduce an auxiliary variable s to decouple G(x) \in C into G(x) = s and s \in C, and construct the constraint dissolving mapping acting jointly on both variables. We then propose a penalty-based constraint dissolving method, in which the penalty parameter is updated adaptively according to the feasibility error. Under mild conditions, every accumulation point is Mordukhovich-stationary. By a specific choice of the constraint dissolving mapping, every accumulation point is guaranteed to be feasible, which stands in contrast to standard penalty-type methods in nonconvex settings. Numerical experiments on Rosenbrock, portfolio, and MAXCUT problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method against the augmented Lagrangian and the penalty decomposition methods.

title: A Luminescent Organic Triradical as an Optically Addressable Qudit
text:
Title: A Luminescent Organic Triradical as an Optically Addressable Qudit
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Luminescent molecular trityl radicals provide options for optically-addressable electron spins and are promising for quantum sensing. Here, we present a luminescent triradical comprising three trityl groups covalently attached to a central phenyl ring. We find two distinct photoluminescence bands at 633 nm and 690 nm with different temporal evolutions, which we attribute to excited quartet and doublet states respectively. The ground state quartet is 1 meV (11.5K) lower in energy than the doublet, resulting in near-equal population of doublets and quartets at room temperature. We demonstrate optically initialized spin polarization, coherent control of the ground state quartet, and optical readout. Potential for optical quantum sensing is shown via optically detected magnetic resonance at room temperature and magneto-photoluminescence up to 3% at 5 mT. This material is a candidate optically addressable molecular qudit, providing opportunities to leverage larger state spaces than qubit systems.

title: Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap: Persistent Homology Enables Cross-Species Ion Channel Classification via Multimodal Graph Neural Networks
text:
Title: Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap: Persistent Homology Enables Cross-Species Ion Channel Classification via Multimodal Graph Neural Networks
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Protein classifiers are highly sensitive to evaluation protocol: random train/test splits induce phylogenetic leakage, allowing models to exploit taxon-specific correlations and substantially overestimate out-of-distribution performance. This issue is particularly acute for venom compound classification by ion-channel target (Ca2+, K+, Na+), where reported accuracies of 80-90% do not reflect generalization to unseen taxa. We formulate cross-species prediction as a structured distribution shift in which taxonomic identity acts as a confounder, requiring representations that capture structural features invariant across phylogeny. Using a shared multimodal backbone that fuses ESM-2 sequence embeddings with a disulfide-aware graph attention network, we systematically compare five structural inductive biases (spectral, Riemannian, SE(3)-invariant, statistical-manifold, and persistent-homology representations) under a leave-one-taxon-out evaluation protocol on a benchmark of 1,373 ColabFold-predicted venom compounds spanning five taxa. The persistent-homology representation summarizes backbone geometry through topological descriptors that are robust to local structural perturbations, providing an inductive bias toward phylogenetically invariant learning. Under conventional i.i.d. splits, all models achieve similar accuracy (81-86%), masking differences in inductive bias. Under taxonomic shift, this parity collapses: a sequence-only baseline drops to approximately 30%, the remaining geometric priors cluster at 54-55%, while our persistent-homology model (PH-GNN) achieves 63.4%, outperforming the next-best method by over 8 percentage points. These results demonstrate that random-split evaluation obscures meaningful differences in representation quality and identify topological representations as an effective inductive bias for learning under structured biological distribution shift.

title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn
text:
Title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) has been proposed as a physiological cue for deepfake detection, based on the premise that synthesized faces lack a genuine cardiac signal. We examine what rPPG-style detectors learn on Celeb-DF++ (22 forgery methods) and FaceForensics++ (FF++), using one identically sampled window per real and fake video. On talking-face forgeries, simple chrominance traces reach an AUC of 0.998, exceeding a dedicated rPPG extractor (0.87). Controlled experiments indicate that this signal is not physiological in origin. On fully synthesized forgeries, it is equally discriminative when extracted from background regions or from full frames without face detection, and it is concentrated above the 0.7 to 4 Hz heart-rate band. It is largely removed by shuffling frame order but persists after normalizing resolution, frame rate and encoding, and an independent reimplementation reproduces these findings. Removing high-frequency content makes most synthesized videos appear real, adding it makes real videos appear fake, and injecting a synthetic pulse has little effect. In controlled self-reenactment experiments with two generators, animating a face from a single frame introduces the same high-frequency signal, whereas reconstructing each frame from its own source does not. Face-based chrominance detectors trained on Celeb-DF++ classify over 99% of real FF++ videos as fake, indicating that they largely encode video source rather than manipulation, and a CLIP-based detector exhibits the same behavior. A frozen CLIP backbone matches or exceeds fusions of CLIP with rPPG and frequency features. Finally, we show that the official Celeb-DF and Celeb-DF++ splits share identities and source-video content between training and test, and that custom protocols reusing test videos and identities in training inflate weaker detectors by up to 0.30 AUC.

title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements
text:
Title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

With single-copy measurements, every mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes, pure modes included, is learned to trace distance $ε$ from $Θ(m^3/ε^2)$ copies, with no logarithmic factor, against the known $Θ(m^2/ε^2)$ for collective measurements. We prove the upper bound, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189 (lower bound for $ε\le1/3600$), and fill most open entries of the sample-complexity table of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states, for single-copy, $k$-copy and collective measurements. The single-copy measurement's noise is matched to the metric at every occupation scale. With blocks of $k$ copies, the covariant highest-weight measurement of arXiv:2611.07271, read out through the Weyl-shift estimator, is exactly unbiased for every state; it gives $Θ(\max\{m^3/k,m^2\}/ε^2)$ in Frobenius norm on all states and in trace distance on every class at a fixed distance from the pure boundary. The gain $1/k$ ($k\le m$) away from the pure boundary, against $1/\sqrt k$ on cold number-conserving states, is therefore attained. For bosonic Gaussian states with bounded covariance, any displacement and squeezing, and occupations $n_1\le\dots\le n_m$, $O((m^2+r^3+\sum_{i,j>r}1/(n_i+n_j))/ε^2)$ single-copy measurements suffice, $r$ the largest index with $r\,n_r\le2$; this is the minimax rate on dyadic-interval classes, with no spectral gap or cold-mode count assumed, and holds with no covariance bound for displaced passive states. With no bound on energy or squeezing, non-Gaussian measurements learn centred one-mode states, mixed included, from $O(ε^{-2})$ and centred pure $m$-mode states from $O(m^2/ε^2)$ single copies, free of the $\log\log E$ term of Gaussian measurements, and $m$-mode states from $O(m^3/ε^2)$ copies, entangled only in a first round on blocks of $4m+6$.

title: Bounds on Attainable Rate Modulation in Fermi's Golden Rule
text:
Title: Bounds on Attainable Rate Modulation in Fermi's Golden Rule
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Controlling transition rates is a central objective across quantum optics, condensed-matter physics, and chemical physics, encompassing processes such as spontaneous emission, energy and charge transfer, spin relaxation, and chemical reactions. Although Fermi's golden rule provides a powerful framework for calculating such rates of weakly coupled transitions, conventional calculations require the interaction to be specified in advance; the range of rate responses attainable over a broader interaction space remains unknown. We formulate spectral-overlap golden-rule rates as quadratic forms of the interaction and derive rigorous bounds on rate modulation over a specified interaction space. As an example, application to energy transfer from a donor to a molecular vibration coupled to an optical cavity reveals that enhancement and suppression depend jointly on the interaction and cavity detuning, including continuous reversal of the rate response for a fixed interaction. The same approach may elucidate rate control for other golden-rule processes, including excitation-energy transfer, nonadiabatic electron transfer, nonradiative electronic transitions, vibrational and spin relaxation, and spontaneous emission.

title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
text:
Title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum algorithms for machine learning, chemistry, and cryptanalysis often assume coherent access to classical data at negligible physical cost. We instead treat data loading as a hardware process and quantify the dynamic energetic cost of a quantum random access memory (QRAM) query on a superconducting processor. Using the metric-noise-resource framework, we relate query fidelity and power to gate duration, relative two-qubit drive strength, and the distribution of attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, while accounting for thermal photons and gate errors. We analyze the linear-depth multiplexer and the noise-resilient bucket-brigade architectures, adapting the latter to a native superconducting gate set and refining its fidelity analysis using the fully decomposed gate schedule. For a representative bucket-brigade QRAM query with a $12$-qubit address register we obtain a query fidelity of $0.969$. The query consumes $3.51\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{J}$ of dynamic energy, corresponding to an average dynamic power of $4.38\,\mathrm{W}$ and a peak of $64.4\,\mathrm{W}$. Our optimization shows that, at fixed target fidelity, the operating point and attenuation profile can change the average power by a factor of two or more.

title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
text:
Title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. Numerical experiments for a semiconductor inverse problem confirm that the proposed Bayesian all-at-once approach yields a speedup of approximately a factor of two, while having a comparable reconstruction quality as the conventional reduced-based setting.

title: Two examples in amplituhedron tilings
text:
Title: Two examples in amplituhedron tilings
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We give an example of a tiling of the $m=4$ amplituhedron that has fewer cells than that of the magic number conjecture. The tiling uses an injective degree two cell.

title: QLoRA Fine-Tuning of Ministral LLM for Sequence-to-Function Protein Annotation
text:
Title: QLoRA Fine-Tuning of Ministral LLM for Sequence-to-Function Protein Annotation
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Functional annotation of newly sequenced proteins remains a bottleneck in molecular biology: the number of sequences in public repositories grows far faster than the capacity for manual curation. Most computational approaches consider annotation as multi-label classification over a fixed ontology, which constrains predictions to a predefined label set. In this work we study the the protein annotation as a sequence-to-text generation problem. We fine-tune the 3B-parameter Ministral 3 base model with QLoRA (4-bit NF4 quantization with low-rank adapters) on sequence annotation pairs. We assess predictions with an LLM-as-expert protocol: a GPT model prompted as a senior molecular-biology curator scores organism identification as binary and function annotation quality. We conclude that QLoRA-fine-tuned compact LLMs can generate curator-style annotations with genuine biological value for a substantial subset of proteins. We also discuss future directions in data quality, model scaling, and evidence grounding that are needed to make the approach sufficiently reliable for practical use.

title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
text:
Title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

The prediction of transition remains challenging because the receptivity amplitude is usually prescribed rather than measured. This work uses Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) to study an unforced Mach 6 nitrogen boundary layer over a 120 mm flat plate, with no imposed inlet wave, wall signal, modal shape, or disturbance spectrum. The retained unsteady field is the intrinsic finite-particle stochastic fluctuation field carried by the DSMC representation. Changing the DSMC particle count provides an independent numerical control parameter that sets a predictable finite-particle noise floor while preserving the time-averaged boundary-layer flow. Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is then applied to unforced DSMC snapshots. The DMD eigenvalues and spatial modes estimate the quantities that appear in the LST normal-mode description, including frequency, temporal growth or decay, wavenumber, wavelength, phase speed, mode location, and amplification envelope. LST is used after extraction to test whether the data-derived structures occupy the expected second-mode band. The results show that DSMC data can connect a measured finite-particle stochastic disturbance level to second-mode instability dynamics without imposed disturbance spectra.

title: Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation
text:
Title: Quadratic Bendixson criterion for delay systems: a numerical implementation
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We present a software implementation (as a Python package) of approximation schemes for verifying frequency inequalities arising from the quadratic Bendixson criterion for systems of delay equations (with a single delay in the linear part). In applications to dissipative nonlinear autonomous systems, such inequalities ensure global stability. The theoretical foundations of this approach were developed in our related work. In particular, it was shown that the transfer operators involved into the frequency inequalities can be represented as integral operators with bounded kernels of the Hardy--Volterra type. Here, we use this representation to construct approximation schemes based on finite-dimensional truncations of the transfer operators. Examples of using the package are provided.

title: Synthetic Stochastic Time Series from Generative Models
text:
Title: Synthetic Stochastic Time Series from Generative Models
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Obtaining statistically converged time-series data represents a fundamental challenge in computational chemistry, where sampling is constrained by the prohibitive computational cost of high-fidelity simulations. The accuracy attainable from a finite simulation budget is governed by the standard-error scaling $1/\sqrt{n}$, rendering exhaustive sampling challenging for systems of realistic complexity. Here we show that generative models trained on high-quality stochastic trajectories can reproduce key statistical properties of the underlying process and generate additional synthetic trajectories at substantially lower computational cost, thereby enhancing the sampling accessible from a finite set of simulations. We present a systematic comparison of four generative architectures across two complementary data sources: an analytically tractable Ornstein-Uhlenbeck reference and donor-acceptor energy-gap trajectories from all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Among the four architectures tested, the denoising diffusion probabilistic model reproduces the target statistics most consistently, across both data sources and across the range of correlation times examined, and generates far faster than the sequential Transformer.
