First, we implement the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ action by identifying pairs of points on the original curve, thereby mapping them to a single point on the S-folded curve. Second, motivated by arXiv:2112.14550, we tune mass parameters to special values, corresponding to the insertion of $D_4$ 7-branes. As a nontrivial consistency check, we show that the two Seiberg--Witten curves agree with each other when expressed in the Weierstrass normal form.

title: Do AI Agents need Preventive Care? An Epidemiologic Cohort Design for Agentic AI
text:
Title: Do AI Agents need Preventive Care? An Epidemiologic Cohort Design for Agentic AI
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

As AI agents increasingly perform tasks autonomously across sectors, including healthcare and biomedical research, understanding how their behaviors develop and influence outcomes over time becomes increasingly important. Existing evaluations largely focus on model capabilities and performance on predefined tasks. Here, we propose an epidemiologic cohort design for studying agentic AI, drawing on principles established in human population studies. The framework treats individual agents as members of a cohort, their underlying model as genetic makeup, accumulated work as their time scale, and naturally occurring behaviors as exposures that may influence subsequent outcomes. By following agents longitudinally, this approach enables investigation of behavioral determinants of adverse events, estimation of their potential preventable burden under causal assumptions, and characterization of behavioral changes over an agent's work life. We illustrate the design through two prospective observational cohorts examining curiosity and probing as a safety question, and data checking and analytical accuracy as a reliability question. Together, the framework and illustrative studies provide a generalizable blueprint for designing epidemiologic cohorts of AI agents.

title: Efficient One-Shot Simulation of Network Instruments and Multi-party Purity Distillation
text:
Title: Efficient One-Shot Simulation of Network Instruments and Multi-party Purity Distillation
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We undertake an information theoretic study of instrument compression problems (ICPs) in {multiple network} configurations, wherein the goal is to design and analyze protocols that simulate specific quantum classical (QC) correlation amidst distributed parties - some holding components of the quantum state and the rest holding classical registers - with minimum communication. We present a \textit{unified framework} of protocols based on likelihood instruments whose analysis yields new inner bounds in the one-shot and asymptotic regimes for the different network configurations we study. Our framework comprises of a common template for designing the instrument simulation protocol and analyzing its information theoretic performance. We also address a related problem of multi-party purity distillation wherein three distributed parties have to distil pure states efficiently via local operations and minimal communication. In regards to the tools, in addition to one-shot purity concentration protocol of \cite{202203arXiv_ChaPadSen} and one-shot quantum simultaneous decoder of Sen \cite{202102SAD_Sen}, we leverage Sen's fully smooth multi-partite covering \cite{202504arXiv_Sen} for all of our covering bounds.

title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation
text:
Title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

LLM-based recommender systems increasingly generate chain-of-thought (CoT) text before each item prediction to activate the LLM's reasoning capacity, costing tens to hundreds of extra tokens per recommendation at inference. We ask whether inference-time reasoning artifacts (textual or latent) can be replaced by training-time supervision alone, without loss of accuracy. We propose LatentRec, a framework for LLM-based generative recommendation that replaces inference-time reasoning artifacts with training-time per-step head supervision. LatentRec has three components. A 2.5M-parameter Continuous Thought Module iterates K latent reasoning steps over the LLM's hidden state during training. Soft Token Selection bridges the ~14x norm gap between hidden states and input embeddings. A Per-step Reasoning Loss (PRL) supervises every intermediate state through the LLM's prediction head against the first token of the target Semantic ID. The trained LLM retains this accuracy without the module at inference, so the module can be discarded at deployment. On three Amazon benchmarks, LatentRec improves HR@10 by 4.0-5.0% (relative) over a CoT-distilled baseline at 18.3x lower latency (batch=1). Per-step training supervision consistently improves accuracy across three datasets, paid once at training rather than at every recommendation.

title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
text:
Title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

title: Occupation Measures in the ODE Method: Wasserstein Convergence and Rates
text:
Title: Occupation Measures in the ODE Method: Wasserstein Convergence and Rates
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study occupation measures associated with stochastic approximation recursions within the ordinary differential equation (ODE) method. Under Lyapunov conditions ensuring that the limiting ODE has a globally exponentially stable equilibrium, we establish that the continuous-time occupation measures associated with the piecewise linear interpolation of the iterates converge almost surely in the $2$-Wasserstein topology to the Dirac mass at the equilibrium, the unique invariant probability measure of the limiting semiflow. The choice of the $2$-Wasserstein distance is naturally aligned with our continuous- and discrete-time Lyapunov drift analysis. We also consider two discrete-time sequences of occupation measures, induced by the algorithmic time scale and the iteration count, respectively, and we establish their almost sure convergence to the same invariant measure in the $2$-Wasserstein distance. We then derive corresponding convergence rates in expectation, providing a nonasymptotic complement to the almost sure results. These expectation bounds also imply some tail probability estimates. Finally, we verify that our results apply to a canonical class of linear recursions.

title: QuDPy-FDGF: A Python-Based Tool for Computing Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Responses Using Frequency Domain Green's Functions
text:
Title: QuDPy-FDGF: A Python-Based Tool for Computing Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Responses Using Frequency Domain Green's Functions
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We present QuDPy-FDGF, an open-source Python framework that evaluates Liouville-space pathways as hybrid chains of time propagators and frequency-domain Green's functions. Frequency-resolved intervals are computed directly through shifted linear systems, without time propagation followed by a Fourier transform, while other intervals may remain in the time domain. A model-agnostic block interface separates the physical model from pathway construction, numerical propagation, and detection. The released implementation provides an explicit dense Liouville-space backend for reference calculations and a sector-resolved sparse backend using matrix-free generator actions, Krylov time propagation, and generalized minimal residual (GMRES) resolvent solves. Its observable layer reuses propagated pathway responses to evaluate operator expectation values, action-detected readout interactions, instantaneous jump rates, and integrated mean jump counts. The framework is assessed on an analytically solvable open two-level system and on two examples of increasing complexity: the complete third-order rephasing response, with its eight sequences, of a thermally initialized anisotropic Heisenberg (XXZ) spin chain with unequal excitation sectors, and two coupled dissipative anharmonic modes whose spectra depend on the detected observable, with the fifth-order double-quantum response of their closed limit. The calculations reproduce the analytical two-level response, check the matrix-free sparse evaluation against the dense assembly of the generator, and recover the harmonic-limit cancellation of the fifth-order signal when the required three-excitation manifold is retained. QuDPy-FDGF therefore provides a unified framework for pathway- and observable-resolved nonlinear spectroscopy in finite or truncated Hilbert spaces with unitary or Markovian Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) dynamics.

title: Toward Long-Range Correlation Energies from Charge Fluctuations: Incorporating Exact Exchange into ACKS2$ω$
text:
Title: Toward Long-Range Correlation Energies from Charge Fluctuations: Incorporating Exact Exchange into ACKS2$ω$
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Long-range electronic correlation can be represented in terms of coupled fluctuations of atomic charges and higher multipoles, motivating a density-response description beyond local dipolar polarization, particularly in low-dimensional, conducting, and small-gap systems where collective electronic fluctuations become important. We extend the frequency-dependent polarizable force field ACKS2$ω$ to electronic-structure references containing exact exchange by deriving both the static and additional frequency-dependent exchange contributions, with particular attention to HFsrPBE, which combines long-range Hartree--Fock exchange with short-range PBE exchange and correlation. Numerical validation of ACKS2$ω$ using dipole polarizabilities and $C_6$ dispersion coefficients for the 27 molecules of the TS27 set, with HF, PBE, B3LYP, and HFsrPBE as the underlying electronic-structure references, shows that including the exchange contributions and enriching the response basis improve agreement with the corresponding orbital-space linear-response calculations, although finite-response-basis errors remain molecule dependent. Long-range correlation energies evaluated through the adiabatic-connection fluctuation-dissipation theorem using the ACKS2$ω$ parameters reproduce the corresponding HFsrPBE orbital-space results for small test molecules when the response basis is made complete within the chosen orbital basis, while a local multipole decomposition resolves the finite-basis energies into monopole--monopole, mixed, dipole--dipole, and remaining higher-multipole contributions, providing a route to evaluating long-range correlation energies in terms of charge fluctuations within atom-condensed models.

title: RxnOptBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Reaction-Condition Optimization in Organic Methodology
text:
Title: RxnOptBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Reaction-Condition Optimization in Organic Methodology
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Chemical reaction-condition optimization -- choosing the catalyst, ligand, solvent, reagent, temperature, time, and atmosphere that jointly maximize yield and stereoselectivity -- is a central, judgement-laden subtask of organic methodology research that large language models are increasingly expected to support. Yet existing chemistry benchmarks evaluate reaction-class labelling, retrosynthesis, or SMILES manipulation, and do not ask models to read a real condition-screening table and pick the best set. We introduce RxnOptBench, a benchmark whose every option and precedent is a real wet-lab entry mined from the optimization tables of organic-methodology papers published in 2025, graded by a continuous relative score derived from a declared headline utility that combines reported yield with enantiomeric excess (ee), diastereomeric ratio (dr), and regioisomeric ratio (rr), and equipped with a paired precedents-vs-no-precedents design that isolates in-context use of literature evidence from parametric memorization. Across nine frontier LLMs and three Chemistry LLMs, even the best models leave substantial headroom: chemistry-specialized models fall to the random-baseline floor on multi-axis selection, while open-weight models have closed most of the gap to proprietary frontier models. We release the final human-reviewed benchmark test set and evaluation code.

title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
text:
Title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= 1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.

title: Analytic and numerical study of dark matter halos in the Horndeski theory
text:
Title: Analytic and numerical study of dark matter halos in the Horndeski theory
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The models of modified gravity that can explain the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe must pass the local tests of gravity, introducing a screening mechanism so that any additional fifth force in gravity is suppressed at stellar scales. Dark matter halos, in contrast, by their extendedness in scale, may exhibit a transition of screening to small scales, providing a probe of modified gravity and the origin of the late-time acceleration. We perform comprehensive studies of dark matter halos with Vainshtein screening in the Horndeski theory. Given that dark matter is cold and a dark matter halo is spherically symmetric, we analytically clarify the conditions for the halo profile under which the Vainshtein screening works effectively. We find that the Vainshtein screening is less effective even within the Vainshtein radius as the profile approaches a core-like structure around the center of a halo, which motivates us to postulate that some features owing to the fifth force can survive during the dynamical evolution of a halo. We numerically examine our postulate by a $N$-body simulation for an isolated halo with the assumption of Newtonian two-body interactions with the spherical external fifth force. We make use of three proxies of the mass through hydrostatic dynamics, the Jeans equation, and gravitational lensing, all of which must be identical in the case of Newtonian gravity as a weak-field approximation to General Relativity. We find that these proxies can be biased relative to each other at a (quasi) equilibrium, quantitatively indicating that the fiducial model of gravity is not Newtonian. Our result affirmatively suggests that multiple mass proxies from observations are capable of testing gravity on halo scales.

title: Singular Tracking of Fractional Brownian Motion under Proportional Costs
text:
Title: Singular Tracking of Fractional Brownian Motion under Proportional Costs
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study adapted finite-variation tracking of fractional Brownian motion under quadratic loss and proportional adjustment costs. For $H\in(0,1)$, \[ V_λ(T;a,b,σ)\underset{λ\downarrow0}{\sim}κ_HT a^{(1-H)/(1+H)}(λb)^{2H/(1+H)}σ^{2/(1+H)}. \] The positive long-run cell value $κ_H$ is unchanged by full past information. A bounded full-past reset correction yields finite-horizon bounds and continuity in $H$. The Brownian value is $κ_{1/2}=\frac12(\frac32)^{2/3}$. Coupling local paths with their filtrations gives a local limit, which we verify for Gaussian Volterra targets. Every asymptotically optimal control has the same leading tracking--variation cost split. Primal and dual bounds quantify the cell value. For $H<1/2$, we construct a positive-factor approximation and relate factor resolution to horizon length.

title: WarBias: A Bilingual LLM Benchmark of Stereotypes About Internally Displaced People and Veterans
text:
Title: WarBias: A Bilingual LLM Benchmark of Stereotypes About Internally Displaced People and Veterans
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

This paper contains examples of stereotypes about veterans and displaced people that may be offensive or distressing. Social bias benchmarks for language models commonly examine categories such as gender, race, and religion, often drawn from lists of legally protected characteristics. Veterans and internally displaced people (IDPs) fall outside these lists, and stereotypes about them, which can undermine access to employment, housing, and social participation, remain largely absent from language model evaluation. We introduce WarBias, a Ukrainian-English benchmark of stereotypes about these two groups. Built from a taxonomy of 120 stereotype claims grounded in research and monitoring reports, WarBias contains 1,007 stereotype-counter-stereotype-unrelated sentence triplets and 240 multiple-choice questions per language. A Ukrainian language model selected in a blinded human pilot generated the Ukrainian triplets. At least two independent annotators reviewed each triplet in the annotation cohort. The authors revised items in response to the reviews, and the final release was machine-translated into English. Each claim carries a human severity rating. In a baseline evaluation of six models, four prefer stereotypical Ukrainian sentences about at least one group, most strongly about IDPs, while English scores are mostly balanced. WarBias supports complementary evaluations of stereotypical preferences and context-sensitive judgments, and provides paired forget/retain material for unlearning-based bias mitigation. We document the benchmark's construction, intended uses, and limitations, and offer its construction method as a template for analogous benchmarks in other conflict-affected societies.

title: Broad-Persistent Advising in Interactive Reinforcement Learning via Latent State Encoding
text:
Title: Broad-Persistent Advising in Interactive Reinforcement Learning via Latent State Encoding
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Deep Interactive Reinforcement Learning (Deep IntRL) accelerates reinforcement learning training by incorporating external advice. However, conventional Deep IntRL uses each piece of advice only in the current step and discards it after a single interaction. Persistent Advising and Broad-Persistent Advising (BPA) extend this process by storing advice in persistent memory and reusing it in similar states through state generalisation based on K-means clustering. This research proposes Encoder BPA, which employs a latent encoder to retrieve and reuse advice. In this framework, a trained encoder is used to map a state sequence into a latent representation at every time step. Advice can be retrieved through latent comparison, together with a top-(k) aggregation and a consistency condition to improve reuse stability. Experimental results show that Encoder BPA improves learning efficiency and advice utilisation at an early stage of training compared with different Deep IntRL approaches, especially in complex and partially observable environments.

title: The Reference Set Is Not the Answer Set: GEOM-DRUGS Is Missing Low-Energy Conformers on Its Own Energy Surface
text:
Title: The Reference Set Is Not the Answer Set: GEOM-DRUGS Is Missing Low-Energy Conformers on Its Own Energy Surface
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Machine-learned conformer generators are scored on GEOM-DRUGS by proximity to a reference ensemble that standard benchmark metrics implicitly treat as ground truth. We test whether that finite set is complete on the GFN2-xTB surface used to construct it. Across five public generators, settled, low-energy structures remain outside the $0.75$\,Å reference radius after removing reflections, incorrect stereochemistry, and post-relaxation connectivity changes ($2.3$--$7.0\%$ of submitted conformers, depending on architecture). In a targeted DFT audit, $107$ of $113$ chemically screened novel/reference pairs remain outside that radius after full $ω$B97X-D3BJ re-optimization. A threshold-free complementary test needs no radius and no energy window at all: on $15.0\%$ $[8.0, 22.0]$ of molecules some generator has already found a chemically intact structure lying below the \emph{entire} released ensemble. A complementary CREST search reproduces the minimum released in $65$ of $69$ molecules, and in $11$ of them it reaches more than $0.5$\,kcal/mol below the complete released ensemble. Augmenting the references with conformers proposed by held-out architectures raises absolute coverage-precision for every generator tested, by $1.48$--$2.99$ points. Together, these results show that GEOM-DRUGS precision is sensitive not only to generator quality but also to incomplete reference support.

title: One-Sided Expert-Parallel All-to-All for Mixture-of-Experts Inference over NVLink
text:
Title: One-Sided Expert-Parallel All-to-All for Mixture-of-Experts Inference over NVLink
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Expert parallelism (EP) shards the experts of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layer across GPUs, so every MoE layer requires two all-to-all communications, namely dispatch and combine. Compared with training, inference processes relatively few tokens per GPU at a time, and at small batch sizes fixed costs that do not grow with the number of tokens, rather than data movement, dominate the latency. We present NVLinkOneSided, a one-sided EP all-to-all for GPUs within a single NVLink domain. Each source rank pushes its tokens, without first exchanging metadata, into rank-major buffers on the target GPUs, and the grouped GEMMs read them in place instead of from a per-expert copy. We provide two protocols for the synchronization that the communication requires, namely Fence and Sentinel, for high-throughput and low-latency scenarios respectively. On Blackwell GPUs, NVLinkOneSided completes dispatch and combine 1.2-3.0$\times$ faster than DeepEP, with the largest speedups at small batch sizes. The resulting MoE layer is up to 2.4$\times$ faster than DeepEP with DeepGEMM. It even outperforms the fused DeepGEMM MegaMoE at up to 128 tokens per GPU, making it still competitive for decoding. We expose NVLinkOneSided through a modular interface, so that it is agnostic to the activation quantization format, decoupled from the MoE compute backend and easy to integrate into inference frameworks.

title: A Differentiable Framework for Inverse Identification of Heterogeneous Cohesive Laws
text:
Title: A Differentiable Framework for Inverse Identification of Heterogeneous Cohesive Laws
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

This work develops a differentiable finite element framework based on an intrinsic cohesive-zone formulation for identifying traction-separation laws from global force-displacement histories and spatially sparse strain measurements. The framework employs physics-constrained neural networks to represent flexible, thermodynamically structured cohesive laws, with sensitivities computed through automatic differentiation and a discrete adjoint that accounts for the history-dependent evolution of interfacial damage. To enable identification of spatially heterogeneous cohesive behavior, we extend learned constitutive priors to irreversible interfacial damage by constructing a shared, low-dimensional family of cohesive laws from representative traction-separation histories. This representation exploits common constitutive structure and parameter sharing to reduce the number of unknowns and regularize the inverse problem, while allowing local cohesive behavior to vary spatially through latent coordinates. Numerical investigations involving double-cantilever beams and fiber-matrix composites demonstrate that accurate reproduction of global force-displacement responses does not necessarily imply accurate recovery of the underlying cohesive laws. Incorporating spatially resolved strain measurements substantially improves constitutive identification, even when the admissible responses are constrained by a learned prior. Comparisons with conventional bilinear cohesive models and Bayesian optimization further illustrate the benefits of the learned constitutive representation and adjoint-based identification for high-dimensional inverse problems.

title: Adaptive Quantum Metrology of Gravitational Waves
text:
Title: Adaptive Quantum Metrology of Gravitational Waves
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We develop a feedback-controlled quantum metrology scheme to probe weak gravitational waves (GWs) through their direct energy exchange with light. Adaptive SU(2) direction control, based on current estimates of the GW frequency and phase, allows the frequency shifts acquired in successive interaction intervals to add rather than cancel. The resulting persistent frequency difference is converted into an optical phase difference for interferometric readout. We further extend the scheme to elliptically polarized GWs using two transverse sensing channels separated by $45^\circ$ to probe the $+$ and $\times$ components independently. After the GW interaction, the two signals are mapped onto orthogonal polarization modes, enabling phase accumulation along a common path. We derive the corresponding quantum Fisher information matrix and find a $T_{\rm int}^2T_{\rm ph}^2$ scaling in the ideal coherent regime. For a fixed-photon-number probe, the sensitivity shows Heisenberg-like $1/n$ scaling in the ideal case.

title: Non-compact Kogut-Susskind gauge theories: 1D lattice models with exact ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge invariance
text:
Title: Non-compact Kogut-Susskind gauge theories: 1D lattice models with exact ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge invariance
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The Kogut-Susskind (KS) formulation of gauge theories constructs quantum many-body Hamiltonians with gauge invariance under a compact Lie group exactly implemented on a spatial lattice. Here, we revisit this construction for a non-compact gauge group. Although motivated in part by theories like general relativity whose first-order formulation involves the non-compact Lorentz group as a local symmetry, we focus on simpler cases in one spatial dimension akin to the Schwinger model. In a bottom-up approach, we show how exact gauge invariance under the simplest non-compact Lie group ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ can be retained exactly on a 1D lattice, and highlight the differences that arise with respect to compact gauge groups, including a continuous spectrum of the Casimir operators of the gauge fields and the emergence of infinite-dimensional representations of the matter fields. For the pure gauge theory, we discuss how a consistent restriction to the positive semigroup ${\rm SL}^{+}(2,\mathbb{R})$ reproduces well-known results from the quantization of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Motivated by the constraint structure of general dilaton gravity, we introduce static charges coupled to the non-compact gauge field, which can be realised by single-fermion degrees of freedom living in an additional, synthetic dimension. With static charges our lattice model remains exactly integrable, but when extending to dynamical fermionic matter, we arrive at an interacting 1D ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ KS gauge theory. We give an interpretation of this model as a chain of charges sequentially connected by strings whose tension pulls matter left or right depending on the sign of the relative continuous ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ fluxes. This picture becomes exact when the involved ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ charges are strongly self-interacting, where we solve the reduced two-body problem analytically.

title: Hints of self-interacting dark matter from strong gravitational lensing
text:
Title: Hints of self-interacting dark matter from strong gravitational lensing
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

An analysis of 29 quadruply imaged quasars hints at dark matter halo densities consistent with gravothermal core collapse, a key prediction of self-interacting dark matter. We interpret this evidence through elastic Yukawa scattering, combining lensing with upper limits on the cross-section strength from galaxy clusters and Milky Way satellite evaporation. Favored models have dark matter masses of $20$-$80\,{\rm GeV}$, MeV-scale mediators, and Yukawa-potential strengths near $10^{-3}$, yielding cross-sections of $10^2$--$10^4 \, {\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$ at $10\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$. Cosmological, direct and indirect detection bounds on MeV-scale mediators motivate a neutrinophilic scalar dilepton that decays invisibly without Higgs mixing. These results demonstrate how inferences on core collapse constrain dark sector physics.

title: QAOA Inside ADMM: Subproblem Wins Do Not Become Decomposition Wins at Matched Budgets
text:
Title: QAOA Inside ADMM: Subproblem Wins Do Not Become Decomposition Wins at Matched Budgets
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We benchmark the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) as the binary subproblem solver in a two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for mixed-binary problems against classical solvers under matched budgets. With 23 optimizer evaluations per subproblem, scoring determines the comparison: on its final readout, the optimized QAOA loses to random search at $n=12$ and 16 binary variables (inconclusive at 20; exploratory and post hoc tests). When credited with its best sample, it wins. In a noiseless 12-qubit simulation, transferred-angle depth-2 QAOA finds the exact optimum of 97.3\% of planted-family subproblems, against 50.6\%--67.4\% for the four strongest local heuristics (100\% against 90.4\%--94.4\% crediting the four best bitstrings) and a not significantly different 96.5\% for semidefinite rounding with local search (SDP+LS). Under our evaluation-counting convention, its time to solution there is a factor of three to five below the local heuristics' but grows with a larger exponent; it is ten times that of SDP+LS and, in seconds, 54 times that of tabu search with restarts. For the benchmark class, an unconstrained binary quadratic problem in disguise, ADMM's binary step is a proximal step on the reduced problem: at unit penalty ADMM re-solves it, and for larger penalties exact solutions increasingly stall. On two families that do not reduce to one, less accurate solvers found the problem optimum more often at unit and larger penalties. No family gave QAOA a better ADMM outcome than the best classical solver and penalty. The benchmark includes a correctness gate and a log of its hypothesis tests.

title: JUBILEE: A Benchmark Environment for Off-Policy Evaluation in Debt Collections
text:
Title: JUBILEE: A Benchmark Environment for Off-Policy Evaluation in Debt Collections
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Off-policy evaluation (OPE) estimates the value a candidate decision policy would achieve, using only data logged by the policy already in production. In debt collections, unrecorded factors can influence both actions and outcomes. This paper presents JUBILEE, a benchmark environment built around a debt-collections simulator that generates million-loan panels with competing risks, rare recovery events, and hidden factors driving both outcomes and assignment. The evaluation includes an 80-run comparison of tabular and gradient-boosted estimators under two synthetic outcome mechanisms and a 190-run parameter grid. Independent policy simulations provide reference values with estimated Monte Carlo uncertainty for a synthetic reward score and for simulated cash. With hidden factors influencing action assignment, several tabular methods agree closely while underestimating the field-visit policy's score, an error that also appears with boosted models. Intervals from tabular doubly robust estimation usually contain the reference without hidden assignment dependence but mostly miss it when that dependence is present. Estimates from randomized decisions do not show the same large error, although their limited precision leaves policy choice uncertain. The decision consequences depend on how policy value is defined. The field-visit policy ranks last under the score and first under simulated cash, which excludes channel costs. Under cash, log-based estimators miss this best candidate in nearly every run with hidden assignment dependence in the paired study. JUBILEE supports reproducible study of these failure modes under specified collections mechanisms.

title: Recursive Pricing and Incumbent Subtree Column Generation for Solving Optimal Classification Trees
text:
Title: Recursive Pricing and Incumbent Subtree Column Generation for Solving Optimal Classification Trees
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Solving optimal classification tree (OCT) problems is computationally challenging because branching, routing, and leaf-assignment decisions must be optimized jointly. We develop an incumbent subtree column generation algorithm (ISCG-OCT) that exploits the recursive structure of classification trees. We first introduce a mixed set-packing and set-partitioning formulation (MSSF). We then construct a restricted master problem whose columns represent feasible subtree patterns. Unlike conventional dual-based column generation, our incumbent-centered pricing evaluates objective improvements relative to the current solution. We establish a recursive decomposition in which fixing a branching decision separates the remaining pricing problem into independent subtree subproblems, enabling exact dynamic programming. We also develop threshold-based variants that trade optimality guarantees for computational efficiency. Computational experiments on 27 benchmark datasets demonstrate competitive training and testing accuracy and substantial reductions in solution time on many instances. When initialized with a CART solution, ISCG-OCT can certify global optimality faster than warm-started mixed-integer programming solvers on selected instances. These results demonstrate how recursive pricing and structured subtree optimization can improve the computational efficiency of exact classification tree methods.

title: Privacy for Free in Efficient Agnostic Halfspace Learning
text:
Title: Privacy for Free in Efficient Agnostic Halfspace Learning
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We provide the first computationally efficient, differentially private algorithms for agnostically learning halfspaces. In particular, we study three different settings of agnostic learning: improper learning under Gaussian and log-concave marginals; proper learning under Gaussian marginals; and semi-agnostic learning under Gaussian marginals. In all three aforementioned settings, the added cost in the sample complexity due to privacy matches the respective non-private sample complexity, implying that we get privacy for free.

title: Geometric Causal Models
text:
Title: Geometric Causal Models
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Scientists often seek to draw causal inferences from structured data that is not independently and identically distributed, such as spatial data, network data, or molecular data. We develop geometric causal models (GCMs), a framework for causal inference from dependent data that exploits underlying symmetries of the data generating process. For example, in spatial data, we consider processes that are symmetric under translations, or in graph data, symmetric under permutations of the nodes. We show how symmetries, formalized with group theory, can enable causal identification and estimation. We deploy ergodic theory for amenable groups to establish identification, and combine geometric deep learning with scalable Bayesian inference for estimation. We recover i.i.d. causal models and do-calculus when the data is a sequence and the symmetry is permutation equivariance, and find novel types of causal models when we use alternate structures and symmetries. As an example, we construct a causal model that satisfies the symmetries of DNA. This GCM enables new estimators for the effects of genetic variation, combining deep functional genomics models to describe outcomes and DNA language models to describe propensities. We illustrate on semisynthetic data.

title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
text:
Title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Foundation models (FMs) learn reusable representations from large collections of unlabeled data. In chemistry the corresponding data mainly consists of molecular structures, which are abundant, whereas experimental measurements are scarce. Chemical FMs such as ChemBERTa and MoLFormer were therefore trained on diverse molecular structures to enable fine-tuning on small experimental datasets (less than 100 datapoints in most realistic scenarios) and subsequent property prediction. At the same time, general-purpose FMs such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were trained on virtually all publicly available data, including knowledge of the humankind on molecular properties and laws governing them. Here we compare accuracies of chemical and general-purpose FMs on tasks from various areas of chemistry. Strikingly, general-purpose GPT-6 Astra outperforms the currently eligible chemical FMs on five physicochemical and quantum-chemical regression tasks when only 60 experimental datapoints are available. Only when provided 10x datapoints do the best chemical FMs reach performance of GPT-6 Astra: on 1,000 and 10,000 points they show performance on par with Astra on 60 and 1,000 points, respectively. Thus, counterintuitively, frontier general-purpose FMs are better suited for guiding chemical research in data-scarce areas than specialized chemical FMs, suggesting that learning relevant primitives (e.g. chemical structures) does not substitute training on relevant humankind knowledge.

title: Structured Quantum Hardness from Unstructured Assumptions
text:
Title: Structured Quantum Hardness from Unstructured Assumptions
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Whether useful structured hardness can arise from unstructured assumptions is a fundamental question in complexity and cryptography. The longstanding Bennett-Gill question asks whether $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ remains hard relative to a random oracle; [GIKKLS, STOC 2023] recently gave a conditional affirmative answer in the classical setting. We establish the quantum analogue: if $\mathsf{UP}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}$, then $\mathsf{NP}^{O}\cap\mathsf{coNP}^{O}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}^{O}$ with probability $1$ over a random oracle $O$. Beyond extending the classical result, this separation has a distinctly quantum significance: Shor's algorithms defeat canonical number-theoretic hardness candidates, while lattice assumptions and other leading post-quantum cryptographic assumptions do not directly supply hard languages with two-sided classical certification on every input. Our conditional oracle separation provides evidence that such structured quantum hardness can nevertheless arise from unstructured sources. Complementing this result, we rule out fully black-box quantum reductions of worst-case quantum hardness in $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ to post-quantum injective one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation. This barrier excludes a broad class of black-box approaches to deriving structured quantum hardness from generic cryptographic primitives, providing partial evidence that the non-black-box techniques in our first result are essential.

title: Does the inverse distance ladder rule out late-time solutions to the Hubble tension? A model-independent test using DES-Dovekie supernovae and DESI DR2 BAO
text:
Title: Does the inverse distance ladder rule out late-time solutions to the Hubble tension? A model-independent test using DES-Dovekie supernovae and DESI DR2 BAO
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

It has been argued that the inverse distance ladder disfavours late-time solutions to the Hubble tension. We test this with a cosmographic expansion where $H$ is a fourth-order polynomial in $1 - a$. We combine the uncalibrated DES-Dovekie SNIa with DESI~DR2 BAO, assuming a standard sound horizon $r_{\rm d} = 147.05 \pm 0.30$~Mpc. Using only DES SNIa yields $H_0 = 76.25 \pm 2.87$ km/s/Mpc, which is $3.1σ$ above the CMB-calibrated $Λ$CDM prediction but consistent with SH0ES ($1.0σ$). Adding the legacy SNIa decreases $H_0$ to $67.98 \pm 0.69$ km/s/Mpc, $4.7σ$ below SH0ES. The $8.27$ km/s/Mpc drop in $H_0$ upon including the legacy SNIa cannot be attributed to expected sample variance: under a fiducial $Λ\text{CDM}$ model, only $1.24\%$ of $10^4$ mock realisations exhibit such a large $H_0$ shift due to the changed redshift sampling. This points to a systematic tension between DES and legacy SNIa datasets. We next add local $H_0$ anchors (the bright siren, SNII, TRGB + SBF) and test a parametrisation where the $Λ$CDM $H(z)$ is enhanced by $ΔH(z) = A \exp (-z/z_1)$. We recover $H_0 = 70.00^{+4.78}_{-0.98}$ km/s/Mpc and $z_1 < 0.086$ at $1σ$ confidence using DES SNIa, but $H_0 = 67.66 \pm 1.01$ km/s/Mpc and $z_1$ is unconstrained using DES + legacy. Late-time solutions are thus viable with the homogeneous DES catalogue, but not with the legacy SNIa as published. Allowing them to be arbitrarily recalibrated relative to the main DES sample yields an inferred offset of $ΔM_\rm{legacy} = 0.0646 \pm 0.0391$~mag, raising the predicted $H_0$ to $71.03 \pm 1.99$ km/s/Mpc. Ongoing SNIa surveys like DEBASS will provide a homogeneous sample of SNIa down to redshifts accessible via the distance ladder, assessing the validity of the current legacy samples and hence the feasibility of late-time solutions to the Hubble tension.

title: Unitary implementability of Darboux transformations
text:
Title: Unitary implementability of Darboux transformations
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We investigate the unitary implementability of the canonical transformations corresponding to Darboux transformations in the Hamiltonian formalism recently developed for gauge invariant perturbations of nonrotating black holes. Starting from the formalism in the black hole interior, we demonstrate that these canonical transformations are unitarily implementable under general conditions on the effective potentials appearing in the master equations of the perturbations. We also show that the privileged massless Fock representation of the perturbative variables selected by admitting (Heisenberg) unitary dynamics, employed in our quantization, is not unitarily equivalent to the simple massless representation of the master variables satisfying the effective Regge-Wheeler equation. This highlights the importance of the choice of master variables in which the quantum representation is initially defined. Furthermore, we show that not all such choices of variables possessing unitarily implementable dynamics can be reached through Darboux transformations, but rather through more general canonical transformations. These results advance our understanding of the relationship between well-established classical relations in black hole perturbation theory and their quantum representations, explaining how isospectral Darboux transformations can be extended to include all the infinitely many possible values of the angular momentum such that they are unitarily implementable in a quantum field theory context.

title: Demystifying Graviton Detection
text:
Title: Demystifying Graviton Detection
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Detecting single gravitons is possible through the extraction of discrete energy quanta from passing gravitational waves. For decades, this was considered hopeless, with estimates suggesting a detector the size of Jupiter. Here, I explain how these earlier estimates relied on the highly inefficient electron ionization process, while the absorption through the full mass quadrupole of a macroscopic system can bring graviton detection within experimental reach. Operating in the LIGO frequency band solves the challenges of graviton sources and noise suppression, allowing gravitons to be extracted from known passing gravitational waves and detection events to be heralded by classical gravitational-wave observations. Combined with the ability to resolve single energy quanta in macroscopic systems, such as in quantum acoustics, this opens a realistic path toward graviton detection. I also discuss the general limitations of particle detection in establishing an underlying quantum theory, illustrated by an energy-nonconserving semiclassical alternative. Nevertheless, the semiclassical alternative is not standard classical wave physics, and extracting $E=\hbarω$ from a passing wave constitutes bona fide particle detection. This opens the way not only to the first detection of individual gravitons, but also to experimentally probing linearized quantum gravity and the graviton counting statistics of gravitational waves.

title: Doubly-robust causal inference for multi-valued treatment regimes with recurrent neural networks
text:
Title: Doubly-robust causal inference for multi-valued treatment regimes with recurrent neural networks
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We propose a doubly-robust method to estimate the causal effects of multi-valued treatment regimes on patient outcomes. A multi-valued treatment regime assigns personalized treatments from a set of competing options based on a patient's history. Existing methods for optimal treatment regimes are largely limited to binary or continuous treatments. We extend the longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimator (LTMLE) to accommodate multi-valued treatments by modeling treatment assignments with a multinomial model. We further integrate recurrent neural networks (RNNs) into the LTMLE framework as learners for the outcome, treatment, and censoring models, and compare this approach to ensemble machine learning. Simulation studies show that LTMLE with either ensemble machine learning or RNNs is approximately unbiased, with close to nominal coverage, whereas sequential g-computation with ensemble machine learning is substantially biased under a dynamic rule. A multinomial treatment model performs similarly to a series of binomial regressions with ensemble machine learning, but yields more stable inference when the treatment model is an RNN.

title: Maximum of the Two-Dimensional Directed Polymer in the Critical Window
text:
Title: Maximum of the Two-Dimensional Directed Polymer in the Critical Window
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Let $Z_N^{β_N}(x)$ denote the partition function of the two-dimensional directed polymer started at $x\in \mathbb{Z}^2$, in Gaussian environemnt, in the critical window, with parameter $β_N=\sqrt{(1-\vartheta/\log N)/R_N}$. Here $R_N\sim (\log N)/π$ is the truncated collision Green function at the origin for the simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. Let $\mathfrak M_N$ denote the maximum of $\log Z_N(x)$ over $|x|_\infty\leq \sqrt{N}$. We prove that, for any $\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}$, in probability, $$\mathfrak M_N/\sqrt{\log N}\to 2\sqrt{2}\text{ as }N\to\infty.$$

title: Deep learning enables large-scale inverse design of free-form metasurfaces
text:
Title: Deep learning enables large-scale inverse design of free-form metasurfaces
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Metasurfaces are ultrathin optical elements that control light through carefully engineered structures smaller than the wavelength of light, enabling compact devices with functionalities that are difficult to achieve with conventional optics. However, exploiting their full design freedom over large areas has been prohibited by the large computational cost of repeated electromagnetic simulations required for inverse design. Here we introduce a physics-tailored deep-learning surrogate model that exploits the locality and symmetries of electromagnetic interactions to generalize from small-scale simulations to metasurfaces orders of magnitude larger. The model captures nonlocal interactions while predicting optical fields more than four orders of magnitude faster than the conventional electromagnetic solver it is trained on, enabling gradient-based topology optimization under arbitrary illumination. We validate the approach through the inverse design and experimental realization of free-form metagratings with diffraction angles up to 75 degrees, as well as a millimeter-scale free-form holographic metasurface more than 1,000 wavelengths across and comprising 1.6 billion degrees of freedom. By decoupling the scale of electromagnetic simulation from the scale of inverse design, our approach enables system-scale free-form photonic devices that retain nanoscale design freedom.

title: Frustrated shapes of solid domains in fluid membrane vesicles: From rolls and folds to crumples and wrinkles
text:
Title: Frustrated shapes of solid domains in fluid membrane vesicles: From rolls and folds to crumples and wrinkles
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Fluid-solid composite vesicles, comprising 2D solid domains integrated into a topologically-closed fluid bilayer membrane, exhibit complex morphologies arising from the geometric frustration between spherical closure of the membrane and 2D solid elasticity. This scenario is distinct from the better studied case of multi-fluid domain vesicles. Here, we study the elastic energies and shape equilibria of a closed vesicle membrane containing a single, flexible circular solid domain using discrete finite-element (Surface Evolver) simulations, determining the key physical and mechanical parameters to govern shape selection. While we find that the 2D solid (shear) elasticity has minimal impact on the highly-under inflated morphologies, the geometrically non-linear resistance of the solid to Gaussian curvature substantially impacts the shape and elastic patterns form for inflated vesicles, by an amount that it grows with ratio of vesicle size to the elastic thickness of solid. For sufficiently large (thin) vesicles we characterize a generic sequence of ground state patterns of solid shape with increasing inflation: from cylindrical rolls and isometric folds to spatially complex patterns of crumples and wrinkles and ultimately to smooth caps. This sequence of non-isometric patterns at high-inflation is shown to be governed by the same far-from-threshold mechanics used to describe similar shape transitions in microscopic sheets on curved liquid interfaces, establishing that inflated shapes are governed by two basic mechanical scales of membrane tension. We find our predictions for highly-anisotropic shape equilibria of fluid-solid composite vesicles closely match experimentally observed shapes of giant unilamellar vesicles of phase-separated DPPC and DOPC.

title: Correlations carried and controlled by coupled non-Markovian environments
text:
Title: Correlations carried and controlled by coupled non-Markovian environments
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

An environment can retain quantum information and carry it between spatially separated systems. Describing the combined influence of these processes requires a treatment of both environmental memory and spatial correlations. Here, we formulate a local hierarchy of pure states for quantum systems coupled to spatially correlated, non-Markovian environments whose modes themselves exchange excitations. We use this method to describe the reduced spin dynamics of a chain of locally coupled Rabi spin--cavity pairs motivated by cavity-QED implementations, where photon hopping in the eliminated cavity environment generates correlations and entanglement between otherwise isolated spins. Monitoring intermediate cavities and feeding their measurement records back onto the corresponding spins further enhances correlations between endpoint spins that receive no direct feedback. The delayed response when feedback starts, and continued entanglement growth after it stops, support a mechanism in which coherent environmental dynamics carry the effects of earlier feedback to the endpoint spins. Finally, tensor-network simulations of XXZ and Heisenberg chains show how environmental transport changes many-body correlation patterns. These results show how coupled environments and local feedback can control correlations between distant spins. We provide a numerically exact stochastic pure-state framework for simulating these processes, opening up avenues to explore the coherent and dissipative control of interacting non-Markovian many-body systems.

title: ZeroFold: Protein-RNA Binding Affinity Predictions from Pre-Structural Embeddings
text:
Title: ZeroFold: Protein-RNA Binding Affinity Predictions from Pre-Structural Embeddings
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The accurate prediction of protein-RNA binding affinity remains an unsolved problem in structural biology, limiting opportunities in understanding gene regulation and designing RNA-targeting therapeutics. A central obstacle is the structural flexibility of RNA, as, unlike proteins, RNA molecules exist as dynamic conformational ensembles. Thus, committing to a single predicted structure discards information relevant to binding. Here, we show that this obstacle can be addressed by extracting pre-structural embeddings, which are intermediate representations from a biomolecular foundation model captured before the structure decoding step. Pre-structural embeddings implicitly encode conformational ensemble information without requiring predicted structures. We build ZeroFold, a transformer-based model that combines pre-structural embeddings from Boltz-2 for both protein and RNA molecules through a cross-modal attention mechanism to predict binding affinity directly from sequence. To support training and evaluation, we construct PRADB, a curated dataset of 2,621 unique protein-RNA pairs with experimentally measured affinities drawn from four complementary databases. On a held-out test set constructed with 40% sequence identity thresholds, ZeroFold achieves a Spearman correlation of 0.65, a value approaching the ceiling imposed by experimental measurement noise. Under progressively fairer evaluation conditions that control for training-set overlap, ZeroFold compares favourably with respect to leading structure-based and leading sequence-based predictors, with the performance gap widening as sequence similarity to competitor training data is reduced. These results illustrate how pre-structural embeddings offer a representation strategy for flexible biomolecules, opening a route to affinity prediction for protein-RNA pairs for which no structural data exist.

title: Does Pretraining Teach Chemical Language Models Chemistry?
text:
Title: Does Pretraining Teach Chemical Language Models Chemistry?
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Chemical language models (CLMs) are pretrained on large corpora of molecules with the aim of learning representations that transfer to diverse downstream tasks. Here, we systematically study the effects of pretraining using a series of such CLMs across 64 molecular property prediction datasets. We find that the downstream gains of pretraining in CLMs do not scale and performance saturates below gradient-boosting baselines. Across the regimes evaluated, only supervised pretraining on traditional physico-chemical descriptors consistently improves downstream performance for the CLMs tested whereas some forms of pretraining result in models worse than a randomly initialized encoder. While models can resolve molecular structure well, they do so no better than a randomly initialized model, suggesting that, at best, CLMs learn descriptor-like properties in addition to low-level token statistics during pretraining, but surprisingly little chemistry beyond what classical molecular features already capture.

title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
text:
Title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We determine the sharp order of discrepancy in Tusnády's problem in every fixed dimension $d\ge 2$. The largest combinatorial discrepancy of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$, extending Wei's planar result and matching Nikolov's upper bound. More strongly, with high probability, this lower bound holds simultaneously for every subset obtained by deleting at most a sufficiently small fixed fraction of a uniform $N$-point sample. We apply this geometric estimate to online thinning of two independent samples of size $n$ from an unknown common distribution, where observations must be kept or discarded upon arrival. For every fixed dimension $k\ge 1$ and expected deletion budget $ρn$, with $0<ρ<2$, we prove that the minimax expected prefix discrepancy over lower orthants is $Θ_{k,ρ}((\log n)^{k+1/2})$. In dimension one, the optimal terminal discrepancy is instead $Θ_ρ((\log\log n)^{3/2})$, giving a sharp separation between the prefix and terminal objectives. For $k\ge 2$, we obtain terminal bounds differing by a factor of $\log n$. The lower bounds are based on Gaussian small-ball estimates for box-incidence matrices, while the upper bounds use stationary Metropolis thinning and, in one dimension, a terminal cancellation procedure.

title: Certified Scalable Enclosures for Uncertain Underdetermined Systems
text:
Title: Certified Scalable Enclosures for Uncertain Underdetermined Systems
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

The central challenge in underdetermined models with bounded uncertainty, such as in nonlinear design and estimation, is certifying the solution sets. Conventional solution methodologies, such as those based on Newton's method or on sampling-based uncertainty quantification, are either not applicable due to the underdetermined nature or do not give guarantees that all solutions have been found, assuming they converge. We addressed this issue for a problem that arises in nonlinear design, where a target steady-state box is prescribed and the parameters have to be found. We developed a trapezoidal linearisation method that rigorously encloses all solutions and combined it with a tractable linear programming method to compute the component-wise bounds. We showed that the resulting families of linear programs can iteratively contract an initial parameter region. A subdivision of the target state and the initial parameter region can improve the contraction and provide tighter enclosures. The trapezoidal relaxation gives a family of linear programs that can also be used for finding solutions for interval linear systems via the Oettli-Prager characterisation. We demonstrate the generality of the method through different applications, including nonlinear design in biomolecular circuits, a sensitivity analysis method, and in a compressed sensing context, and discuss the trade-off between enclosure tightness and computational cost.

title: Principles of Client Enrichment in Multicomponent Biomolecular Condensates
text:
Title: Principles of Client Enrichment in Multicomponent Biomolecular Condensates
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Biomolecular condensates are commonly organized by a small number of scaffold molecules that drive phase separation together with client molecules that do not condense on their own but become selectively recruited into the dense phase. A central open question is how client recruitment feeds back on scaffold interactions to determine condensate composition. Here we address this problem in a reconstituted focal adhesion system composed of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) and phosphorylated p130Cas (Cas) as scaffolds and the adaptor protein paxillin (PXN) as a client. We show that both FAK phosphorylation and PXN recruitment produce a common compositional response in which FAK becomes enriched while Cas is depleted within the condensate. To interpret these observations, we develop two complementary theoretical descriptions. First, within a two-component Flory-Huggins framework, we show that phosphorylation can be captured by either strengthening heterotypic FAK-Cas interactions or increasing the effective number of interaction-relevant segments on FAK, both of which bias partitioning toward FAK-rich condensates. Second, we introduce a minimal three-component Flory-Huggins theory without an explicit solvent and map it onto an effective two-component description, demonstrating that client recruitment renormalizes homotypic and heterotypic scaffold interactions. Analytical predictions for the location of the critical point are tested in reconstituted multicomponent systems through PXN addition, showing that client recruitment alone tunes proximity to criticality and reshapes condensate composition. Together, our results reveal distinct yet convergent physical routes by which post-translational modification and client recruitment control scaffold composition in multicomponent condensates.

title: Leviathan: a very massive, extended sub-millimetre galaxy spectroscopically confirmed at $\rm z = 4.05$
text:
Title: Leviathan: a very massive, extended sub-millimetre galaxy spectroscopically confirmed at $\rm z = 4.05$
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We present Leviathan, a sub-millimetre galaxy (SMG) spectroscopically confirmed at $z=4.051$ with JWST/NIRSpec. Modelling 31 bands of photometry from the rest-frame ultraviolet to the millimetre, we find a stellar mass of $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=11.34^{+0.15}_{-0.22}$, making Leviathan one of the most massive spectroscopically confirmed galaxies at $z>4$, yet consistent with $Λ$CDM for a star-formation efficiency of approximately 20%. Although SMGs are often thought to be building the dense cores of compact quiescent galaxies, Leviathan is extended, with a rest-frame $0.9\,μ\mathrm{m}$ half-light radius of 4.3 kpc. Spatially resolved SED fitting gives a half-mass radius of $3.1\pm0.4$ kpc, consistent with its size in rest-frame $1.5\,μ\mathrm{m}$ imaging. This is three times larger than quiescent galaxies of the same mass, but consistent with the size-mass relation of star-forming galaxies at $4<z<5$ extrapolated to $M_\star=10^{11.3}M_\odot$. Leviathan forms stars on the main sequence (approximately $400\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$) with dust spread across its disc. Both its stellar mass and dust are more extended than those of $z\approx3$ SMGs. Alongside GN20.2b, which has a similar mass and star-formation rate but is three times smaller, these show that massive dusty galaxies at $z\approx4$ can have very different stellar structures, and that not all have their stellar mass concentrated in a compact core.

title: Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control: Exact Guarantees, Limits, and Overlapping Extensions
text:
Title: Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control: Exact Guarantees, Limits, and Overlapping Extensions
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We study group-conditional conformal risk control (CRC) for disjoint and overlapping groups under bounded monotone losses. For disjoint groups, we establish exact finite-sample conditional risk control, two-sided bounds on the group-restricted risk, and fundamental limitations arising from local support and calibration-rank granularity. For overlapping groups, we study two exactly valid approaches: group-restricted calibration followed by union deployment, and direct calibration of the deployed prediction-set family. We characterize the union's limiting reconciliation gap, identify conditions for its disappearance, and establish sharp lower bounds for structured losses in specified product-form models. We also demonstrate a strict size advantage for direct calibration in an ordinal model. Experiments show that direct calibration can reduce prediction-set size, but its efficiency depends on group structure, loss type, and shape fitting. Results on historical diabetic-retinopathy scores further illustrate these tradeoffs. Overall, local support, reconciliation slack, and threshold heterogeneity determine efficiency, with neither approach uniformly dominating.

title: Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps
text:
Title: Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

HI intensity mapping is a promising probe of the large-scale structure of the Universe, but is limited by foregrounds and instrumental systematics. For the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) L-band data, it is found that emission line stacking measurement reveals a type of systematics related to the instrument beam. Using simulations with a full-sky electromagnetic beam model, we show that the chromaticity and sidelobes of the MeerKAT beam modulate the frequency-smooth foreground emission and introduce oscillating structures that persist after foreground removal. The beam rotates with respect to the sky between two types of scans, and combining datasets with different beam orientations before foreground cleaning makes the residuals stronger. In MeerKLASS L-band data, processing these two types of scans separately significantly suppresses the oscillating residuals while preserving the stacked HI signal. The ratio of the HI signal amplitude to the systematic fluctuation amplitude increases by 81%. We find an oscillating structure in PCA mode 11 in our previous data processing, but simply removing this mode does not improve the stacked spectrum due to the signal loss. Our strategy can help mitigate spectral ripples that are induced by the beam in future MeerKAT and SKA-Mid surveys.

title: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
text:
Title: Untangling flow-harmonic correlations in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC using event-shape engineering
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Symmetric cumulants $\mathrm{SC}(m,n)$ measure the correlation between the event-by-event fluctuations of the flow harmonics $v_m$ and $v_n$, which, for higher harmonics, is influenced by the nonlinear response to the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) flow. Event-shape engineering, which selects events by the reduced flow vector $q_n$, is expected to control this contribution. However, its power is limited by the small forward multiplicity in light-ion collisions. In this work, we study the effect of the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections on the symmetric cumulants in OO and Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV using EPOS4 with an ATLAS-like acceptance. Using the law of total covariance, the symmetric cumulant is separated into a selected part, which follows the differences between the $q_n$ classes, and a residual part within them. It is observed that in OO collisions the correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$ remain almost entirely within the $q_2$ classes, unlike in Pb--Pb collisions. Nevertheless, events with the smallest $q_2$ in central OO collisions show weaker correlations of $v_2$ with $v_3$ and $v_4$, which is attributed to $v_4$ approaching its linear response. In Pb--Pb collisions, the $q_2$ and $q_3$ selections act separately on the two factors of the nonlinear coupling of $v_5$, which establishes a way to isolate them experimentally.

title: Multimodal Alignment and Preference Optimization for Zero-Shot Conditional RNA Generation
text:
Title: Multimodal Alignment and Preference Optimization for Zero-Shot Conditional RNA Generation
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The design of RNA molecules that interact with specific proteins is a critical challenge in experimental and computational biology. Despite recent progress in natural language modeling and deep learning-based protein design, there remains significant room to improve the frequency of successful interactions and the authenticity of generated sequences for functional applications. In this work, we frame conditional RNA sequence generation as a multi-stage alignment problem, introducing Moirain: a suite of models optimized via multimodal supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Our approach begins with large-scale pretraining on diverse RNA corpora to capture the fundamental grammars of sequence plausibility. To achieve target-specific generation, we employ a multimodal SFT architecture that conditions RNA synthesis on protein structural and sequential features. Finally, we leverage DPO to refine the model using synthetic interaction data: taking advantage of DPO's unique ability to navigate non-aligned preference spaces, we improve functional fitness without collapsing the learned natural distribution. Extensive evaluation of the Moirain series (Moirain-Base, -Multi, and -DPO) demonstrates that our framework consistently produces novel, diverse, and biologically plausible RNA sequences with superior binding affinities compared to existing baselines.

title: Elementary-Symmetric Ricci Gravity: Metric Formulation
text:
Title: Elementary-Symmetric Ricci Gravity: Metric Formulation
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We investigate a four-dimensional metric theory of gravity whose Lagrangian is a linear combination of the elementary symmetric polynomials of the Ricci tensor. We derive the field equations and characterize Einstein vacua and a real, diagonalizable class of parallel-Ricci vacua. The latter includes direct products of two constant-curvature surfaces and can exhibit a hierarchy of curvature radii. The Einstein vacua possess multiple branches associated with the distinct roots of a polynomial, whose multiple roots define boundaries in parameter space. We derive the linearized equations on maximally symmetric backgrounds, distinguish the scalar and spin-2 degrees of freedom, and then analyze their classical linear stability. We also obtain the generalized Friedmann constraint and the associated homogeneous evolution equations. An illustrative spatially flat solution evolves from the neighborhood of an unstable de Sitter solution toward a stable de Sitter solution. This behavior may motivate further investigation into early- and late-time accelerated expansion and provide a gravity-driven mechanism for automatic end of inflation.

title: Conditional Neural SDEs for Financial Time-Series Generation
text:
Title: Conditional Neural SDEs for Financial Time-Series Generation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Conditional generation of time-series paths is a central problem in probabilistic modeling, where the goal is to simulate future trajectories that are both realistic and responsive to external context. It has direct applications in finance and economics. Neural stochastic differential equations provide a natural framework for this task by combining continuous-time stochastic dynamics with learnable drift and diffusion functions. However, directly modeling the target state can be unstable in conditional settings, especially when the target and conditioning variables have strong level dependence, limited training data, or different dimensions.We propose a residualanchor Neural SDE architecture that decomposes the target into a learned conditional anchor and a stochastic residual. The anchor captures the context-dependent baseline, while the Neural SDE (Stochastic Differential Equation) models the residual dynamics around this baseline. This separation reduces the burden on the stochastic dynamics and generalizes spread-based representations to more general conditioning settings.We evaluate the approach on real-world financial time series, including conditional interest-rate scenarios and a comparison with a time-series foundation model. The results show that the proposed model can generate plausible conditional paths, maintain competitive point accuracy, and provide calibrated uncertainty estimates.

title: A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding
text:
Title: A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study a fundamental problem in machine learning: partial recovery of a planted signal $\boldsymbol{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ from a spiked tensor $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}} = λ\, \boldsymbol{v}^{\otimes p} + \boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$, where $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ has symmetric Gaussian entries of variance $\asymp n^{-1}$. While previous works replace $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ by an i.i.d. standard Gaussian tensor to circumvent technical difficulties caused by dependencies, this paper directly analyzes the symmetric model via random matrix theory. We show that the square unfolding algorithm is subject to a sharp phase transition for partial recovery at $λ\asymp n^{(p-2) / 4}$, validating an open conjecture from Montanari and Richard (2014). We get precise expressions for the limiting spectral distribution, deterministic equivalent, phase transition threshold and overlap. The main message is that unfolded symmetric tensors spectrally behave like standard Wigner matrices, up to simple transformations accounting for high-order symmetries. We consider extensions to multiple orthogonal spikes, recursive unfolding and non-square unfolding via disproportionate random matrix theory, leading to an interesting conjectured statistical-computational tradeoff regarding the choice of unfolding: square versus long.

title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Prékopa--Leindler inequality
text:
Title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Prékopa--Leindler inequality
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We give a new, simpler proof of sharp stability for the Prékopa--Leindler inequality. In contrast to the main arguments from Figalli, van Hintum and Tiba~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}, our proof hinges mostly on the sharp stability theory for the Brunn--Minkowski problem, developed by the same authors \cite{figalli2024BM}, and on the idea of using a height transportation approach in order to match level sets. As a by-product of our techniques, we are able to prove the sharp dependency on $τ= \min\{λ,1-λ\}$ in the Prékopa--Leindler stability constant whenever one of the inputs is logarithmically concave, producing a new, simplified proof of two of the main results from~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}. Finally, in the same fashion as Kristály and Pîrvuceanu \cite{kristaly2026quantitative}, we are able to obtain new stability results for the Bakry-Emery log-Sobolev inequality and for the Talagrand inequality. Due to the sharpness of the inputs, these results are optimal in terms of exponents. We moreover show that the $L^1$ nature of the distance in such results \emph{cannot} in general be improved to any other $L^p$ distance, where $p>1.$

title: Testing non-classical gravitational phase dynamics under strong dephasing
text:
Title: Testing non-classical gravitational phase dynamics under strong dephasing
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Whether gravity must be quantum is often approached by asking whether two masses can become entangled through their mutual gravitational interaction. In practice, the weak interaction competes with environmental decoherence, so the final state may contain no entanglement even when the underlying gravitational phase remains coherent. We investigate what can still be learned from the dynamics in a dephased Bose--Marletto--Vedral setup. The dominant Newtonian effect for well-separated paths is an accumulated phase rather than transfer between interferometer arms, a regime motivated by matter-wave gravitational phase experiments and quantified here by wavepacket-overlap and deflection estimates. Keeping independently characterized local which-path dephasing fixed, we prove an exact finite-time distinction between the gravitational conditional-phase evolution and every passive stochastic local-phase model (induced by a classical mediator), including regimes where the chosen input remains separable at all times. The distinction survives, with a modified sensitivity, when the comparison is enlarged to population-preserving classical measurement and feedback through a diagonal PPT relaxation. These results identify an operational test of gravitational phase dynamics in the strong-dephasing regimes, conditional on explicit and physically motivated classical mediator models.

title: Dynamics and pseudospectra around quantum exceptional points
text:
Title: Dynamics and pseudospectra around quantum exceptional points
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Exceptional points (EPs) are a hallmark of non-Hermitian physics, giving rise to extreme sensitivity and enhanced dynamic response. Such unique spectral singularities have been extensively studied in classical photonics, both at theoretical and experimental levels, where the relevant observables are evident. That is not necessarily the case in the quantum regime, where this kind of behavior around EPs, to a large extent, remains elusive. In fact, the interplay between dissipation and quantum fluctuations makes the complete Lindbladian evolution quite different from effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian descriptions. In this context, we investigate the signatures of the Liouvillian EPs on spectral and dynamic response by considering properly normalized long-time averages and imbalances. Even though our approach is generic, we focus on two paradigmatic models-a lossy Bose-Hubbard lattice and a dissipative two-spin system, where we investigate the role of quantum jumps and interactions in the Liouvillian spectrum, in terms of complex and structured pseudospectra. Our results demonstrate how non-Hermitian phenomena emerge in realistic quantum lattices, providing a bridge between classical EP physics and experimentally accessible open quantum systems.

title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
text:
Title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. We investigate these differences using the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) as an exemplary problem setting. We first establish the relationships between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. Since B&B and $A^*$ admit numerous algorithmic enhancements, we focus on relatively basic implementations. This allows us to examine the fundamental differences between the methods rather than compare the performance of state-of-the-art solvers.
