Numerical examples illustrate drone navigation and arm pick-and-place through KKT-residual histories and MuJoCo simulations, together with preliminary initialization results for the full-horizon optimal-control problems.

title: The PAU Survey: Self-supervised image denoising for flux-preserving photometry
text:
Title: The PAU Survey: Self-supervised image denoising for flux-preserving photometry
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Context. Deep photometric surveys increasingly rely on low signal-to-noise imaging, where noise affects source detection, flux measurements, photometric redshifts, and sample selection. Self-supervised denoising methods are attractive because they do not require ground-truth images, but applying them to quantitative photometry requires controlling the flux biases they may introduce. Aims. We evaluate and improve Noise2Void (N2V) for denoising real astronomical images, focusing on preserving fluxes, reducing photometric scatter, and retaining the main source features across a wide magnitude range. Methods. We use real observations from the Physics of the Accelerating Universe Survey (PAUS) together with PAUS-like simulated images. We show that standard N2V systematically underestimates galaxy fluxes, especially for faint galaxies. To mitigate this bias, we add a bounded-output layer that limits large negative outputs, and fine-tune the model with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and two flux-aware loss terms that preserve the flux scale and improve repeated-exposure flux consistency. Results. For PAUS galaxies with 22 <= i_AB < 23 in the NB645 band, the standard N2V flux-ratio distribution peaks far below unity, while the bounded-output model restores it close to the original PAUS flux scale. The flux-aware LoRA fine-tuning reduces the width of the repeated-exposure flux-difference distribution to sigma_68 = 0.529 in NB645, an effective 47% reduction in random flux scatter relative to the original PAUS uncertainty scale, while keeping the median flux ratio close to unity. Conclusions. Denoising methods for astronomical surveys must be evaluated with photometric diagnostics, not image-quality metrics alone. With flux-aware modifications, self-supervised denoising can be adapted to low-SNR survey images while preserving the flux information needed for quantitative analysis.

title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
text:
Title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black-hole X-ray binaries show nonlinear coupling with broadband variability, producing characteristic ridge, hypotenuse, and web-like structures in the bicoherence. However, the origin of these structures remains unclear. We develop a mathematical model in which a modulator phase-locked to the QPO acts multiplicatively on the underlying variability. The resulting frequency mixing naturally produces both the ridge and hypotenuse associated with the fundamental QPO, as two parts of the same modulation-induced bispectral structure, and the same mechanism extends to the second harmonic. The model further predicts opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. We test these predictions using NICER observations of Swift~J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI~J1820$+$070. The bispectral maps show QPO-related ridge--hypotenuse structures broadly consistent with the model, with qualitatively opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. In particular, the biphase map provides a complementary diagnostic that reveals weak coupling structures that are difficult to identify from the bicoherence alone. We also compare the measured bispectral modulus with the predictions for isolated ridges and hypotenuses. These predictions broadly reproduce the observed frequency dependence, while localized deviations remain near the fundamental-QPO and second-harmonic frequencies, where different bispectral structures overlap. Our results provide a simple mathematical framework in which the web-like pattern in the bispectrum could arise naturally from multiplicative coupling between a QPO-phase-locked modulator and the underlying variability.

title: Methods for Inferring Interaction Potentials from Cross-Linking Mass Spectrometry Data
text:
Title: Methods for Inferring Interaction Potentials from Cross-Linking Mass Spectrometry Data
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) has emerged as a powerful quantitative technique for probing intra-protein structural information as well as protein-protein interactions at an unprecedented scale. XL-MS data yield information on the pairwise spatial proximity of proteins through inter-molecular linkers. However, systematic methods for adapting such data for coarse-grained interacting particle models remain limited. Predominant focus is put on directly fitting radial distribution functions (RDFs), while numerous observables, e.g. coordination numbers, which are functionals of the RDF, cannot be uniquely inverted. In this work, we develop a framework for parameterizing interaction potentials from such observables in potentially phase-separated mixtures, as encountered in XL-MS results. We establish a connection between this problem and the inverse Henderson problem and adapt algorithms such as Iterative Boltzmann Inversion and Iterative Monte Carlo to its numerical solution. We derive exact and low-density limit gradient approximations and propose two new algorithms based on an adaptation of the predictor-corrector~framework. In total, we evaluate several optimization algorithms on biologically realistic ten-component test systems. We demonstrate that for homogeneous fluids, all methods achieve exceptional efficiency and accuracy. Critically, we further demonstrate successful parametrization in a challenging three-phase system. Here, three algorithms, namely Adam and gradient descent employing the low-density derivative as well as Newton's method with the exact gradient, reliably recover the correct parameters. These results establish a clear pathway from XL-MS experiments to coarse-grained protein models for systems where phase separation governs biological function, potentially enabling new investigations of biomolecular condensates and protein aggregation.

title: A Hierarchical Variational Inequality Approach to Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking with Nonlinear Shared Constraints
text:
Title: A Hierarchical Variational Inequality Approach to Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking with Nonlinear Shared Constraints
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study the computation of variational generalized Nash equilibria (v-GNE) in games with strongly monotone pseudo-gradients and nonlinear convex shared constraints. We show that the v-GNE problem is exactly equivalent to a hierarchical variational inequality, whose lower level is given by the gradient of a smooth convex penalty of the constraint violation over the local action sets. Building on this reformulation, we propose a hierarchical regularization scheme that operates entirely in the primal space and requires only projections onto the local action sets. In the centralized setting, we prove last-iterate squared distance convergence to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t^{\scriptscriptstyle 2/3})$ under a local error bound condition, which holds, e.g., under Slater's condition, improved to $O(1/t)$ under a global error bound condition. We then extend the scheme to the partial-decision information setting, where the agents communicate over a network and maintain local estimates of the joint action. We derive a distributed algorithm with a constant stepsize operating in the primal space and converging to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t)$.

title: Understanding When and Where Self-Supervised Speech Models Learn Phonemes and Prosodic Cues through Layer-Wise and Time-Resolved Probing
text:
Title: Understanding When and Where Self-Supervised Speech Models Learn Phonemes and Prosodic Cues through Layer-Wise and Time-Resolved Probing
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) encode a rich hierarchy of acoustic, prosodic, and phonetic information, yet when and where it emerges during pretraining remains unclear. We train frozen-encoder probes on every Transformer layer across pretraining checkpoints of two matched models: HuBERT-Base, whose stage 2 is a separately initialized model trained on new pseudo-label targets, and single-objective wav2vec 2.0-Base. Our five tasks span an acoustic-to-abstract gradient: absolute pitch (F0), speaker-relative pitch, lexical stress, phoneme boundaries, and 38-way phoneme identity. Acoustic-prosodic cues and phone boundaries are decodable from the earliest checkpoints and barely shift across layers, whereas phoneme identity is constructed during pretraining, re-localizing to upper-middle layers under HuBERT's stage-2 targets at a matched update count. Acquisition order therefore tracks abstraction from the acoustic surface, not the segmental/suprasegmental distinction, extending to prosody an account established for phonetic, lexical and syntactic structure; the no-switch wav2vec 2.0 shows no comparable re-localization.

title: Reciprocal mirror map derivatives, euler-twisted Gromov-Witten invariants, and instanton counts via quantum Serre duality
text:
Title: Reciprocal mirror map derivatives, euler-twisted Gromov-Witten invariants, and instanton counts via quantum Serre duality
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We study mirror map derivatives as a means of relating the genus zero Gromov-Witten theories of an anticanonical Calabi-Yau hypersurface in a smooth, almost minimal Fano variety and the local Calabi-Yau formed from the total space of the Fano's canonical bundle with the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano. A precise relationship between reciprocal mirror map derivatives is obtained from the non-equivariant limit of quantum Serre duality for the euler-twisted theory of the ambient Fano as formulated by Iritani, Mann, & Mignon. This allows us to express the generating series of 3-point euler-twisted invariants as the derivative of the local mirror map with respect to the closed one. In low dimensions, this series is shown to be a modular form of Eisenstein type which has arisen before in this area. We prove integrality of the twisted invariants from this identification. The regularized small quantum $D$-module of the Fano is reducible, and we show it is equivalent to an inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs equation governed by this generating series. The reciprocal mirror map derivative is then shown to be a generating function of local 3-point invariants, which recovers some known results for local Calabi-Yau threefolds and proves a conjecture of the second named author and A. Malmendier in previous work on local fourfolds. Explicit calculations for $\mathbb{P}^2,\mathbb{P}^3$ and $\mathbb{P}^4$ illustrate these relationships, which includes the vanishing of positive-degree ordinary genus-zero invariants for anticanonical elliptic curves and K3 surfaces, the recovery of the quintic threefold's instanton numbers, and finally some formulas for genus-zero invariants of local projective spaces.

title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
text:
Title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $μ$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-Élie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.

title: Existence, Uniqueness, Feller Property and Diricihlet form of the Keller-Segel particle system up to blow up
text:
Title: Existence, Uniqueness, Feller Property and Diricihlet form of the Keller-Segel particle system up to blow up
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

The Keller-Segel particle system as defined in \cite{ft} through the Dirichlet form theory (see \cite{f}) consists of $N$ planar Brownian motions interacting through the kernel $x\in \rr^2 \mapsto θK(x) = -θx/\|x\|^2$, where $θ>0$. One particularity of this model is that collisions (i.e. overlapping of particles) occur depending on the value of $θ$, making the well-posedness of the particle system delicate. In this work, we propose a new notion of solution of this SDE without relying on the Dirichlet form theory and prove uniqueness in law of such solutions. The proof relies on an excursion decomposition of the particle system based on the "barycenter-radius-angle" decomposition in \cite{ft}. As additional results, we prove that the solution is strong Markov, has the Feller property and fits in the definition of solutions in the Dirichlet form sense. Finally we prove that the law of the particle system starting from a configuration where all the particles overlap is explicit.

title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
text:
Title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(δt)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $κ(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.

title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
text:
Title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $ρ_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/ρ_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_βN^{-β}$ for every $0 0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Structural domains associated with permeation, gating and selectivity of Aquaporin ion channels found across phyla
text:
Title: Structural domains associated with permeation, gating and selectivity of Aquaporin ion channels found across phyla
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Aquaporins (AQPs) are an ancient group of channels that arose early in phylogeny and radiated throughout the kingdoms of life. Classified as members of the broad Membrane Intrinsic Protein family, AQPs originally were envisioned as strictly water pores that were constitutively open. International research interest is driving new views of AQPs as multi-functional channels with complex control mechanisms that enable adaptive responses to physiological challenges. Expanding numbers of AQP classes are being discovered to allow permeation of diverse solutes in parallel to the archetypal substrate water, with channel activities that show subtype-specific regulation by intracellular and extracellular signals. To date, at least fifteen classes of AQPs from mammals, plants, insects and algae have been proposed to carry ions, enabling amino acid sequence comparisons that suggest ion channel functional domains arise from conserved transmembrane, loop and teminal regions of the tetrameric AQP protein, serving as selectivity filters, gates, and sites for modulation. More AQP ion channel classes likely await discovery, pending identification of relevant activators. Subtype-specific control of dual water-and-ion AQP classes orchestrate diverse roles for AQPs across the domains of life, promoting homeostasis, cell motility, nutrient acquisition, redox protection, sensory detection, and intercellular signaling in cells and tissues.

title: Optimal Configurations for Mordell's Problem
text:
Title: Optimal Configurations for Mordell's Problem
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Mordell's problem asks for the largest product of squared pairwise distances among $n$ points in the complex plane with a prescribed sum of squared distances from the origin. When this sum equals $n$, the maximum for $2\le n\le5$ is known to be $n^n$, attained precisely by the $n$th roots of unity up to rotation and relabeling. For $n\ge6$, Chalk showed that a regular polygon together with its center gives a larger product than the regular $n$-gon. We prove that for $6\le n\le9$ the maximum is $(n-1)^{n-1}r_n^{n(n-1)}$, where $r_n=\sqrt{n/(n-1)}$. Up to the same symmetries, the unique maximizer consists of the origin and the vertices of a regular $(n-1)$-gon of radius $r_n$. For six points, algebraic elimination reduces the proof to an exact comparison of stationary values. For seven points, we compare all twelve classes in a published classification of equilibria. For eight and nine points, rigorous interval arithmetic establishes an inequality for every admissible pair. Summing over pairs gives the sharp global bound, and the equality conditions determine the configuration. An explicit ten-point comparison and a known instability result together exclude Chalk's configuration for every $n\ge10$. For each $n$ from two through eight, Mordell's problem and the minimum-diameter problem studied by Bateman and Erdős have a common optimal configuration.

title: Almost sure bounds and tail phases for critical non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
text:
Title: Almost sure bounds and tail phases for critical non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Gu and Zhang asked for almost sure upper and lower bounds on the Taylor coefficients $a_n$ of $\exp(\sum_{k\ge1}X_kz^k/\sqrt{k})$ in the unit disc, and for the dependence of these bounds on the input tail. For independent, identically distributed, rotationally invariant complex inputs with $\mathbb E|X_1|^2=1$, we prove the universal almost sure bound $|a_n|=O((\log n)^{1/4})$. Almost surely, $\limsup_{n\to\infty}|a_n|/(\log n)^{1/4}$ is positive and finite exactly when $\mathbb E[|X_1|^2\log^+|X_1|^2]<\infty$, and is zero otherwise. For each input law, we define a deterministic scale such that, almost surely, the coefficients are bounded exactly when the scale is bounded, and tend to zero exactly when it vanishes. We also determine the almost sure logarithmic growth exponent as the maximum of contributions from collective fluctuations and individual large inputs. Explicit tails exhibit distinct thresholds for boundedness and for upper bounds at the scale in the phase criteria. Examples show that neither the leading tail nor the set of finite logarithmic moments determines the almost sure phase.

title: CIS(2): a state-specific, size-intensive perturbative correction to configuration interaction singles
text:
Title: CIS(2): a state-specific, size-intensive perturbative correction to configuration interaction singles
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We present a state-specific second-order perturbation theory based on a configuration interaction singles (CIS) reference and its generalized Fock operator. Starting from a fully internally contracted construction, we retain the complete doubles space and internally contracted triples in the first-order wave function. We consider two partitions, Canonical and Block-diagonal, with reference excitation energies given by the Fock excitation gap $ω^{(0)}$ and the CIS excitation energy $ω_{\rm CIS}$, respectively. Our analysis establishes that strict size-intensivity is preserved when the contracted-triples denominators use bare Fock gaps and the occupied--virtual Fock block is projected to remove residual spectator coupling. Based on this observation, combining Canonical triples with Block-diagonal doubles yields a size-intensive Hybrid partition. These properties are verified for water with non-interacting helium atoms. Our formulation enables $O(o^3v^2)$ cost per matrix--vector product in a semicanonical basis. On the QUEST\#1 benchmark, Canonical and Block-diagonal show opposite systematic biases, whereas Hybrid gives the best overall accuracy among the three partitions. Its mean absolute errors for singlets and triplets are 0.24 and 0.15~eV, compared with 0.28 and 0.22~eV for CIS(D). The improvement is largest for Rydberg excitations, although CIS(D) remains more accurate for valence singlets.

title: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight
text:
Title: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Quantum algorithms for linear algebra that access a matrix $A$ through quantum random access memory (QRAM) prepare quantum states proportional to the solutions of linear systems and related problems. Dequantized classical algorithms, when given sampling and query access to $A$, return sampling and query access to an approximate solution. Both kinds of algorithms use a number of queries that is polynomial in the normalized Frobenius norm $ρ=\|A\|_F/\|A\|$ and does not directly depend on the dimension. For linear systems at fixed condition number and accuracy, quantum algorithms use $\widetilde O(ρ)$ queries, whereas the best dequantized algorithms use $\widetilde O(ρ^4)$. We prove that this quartic gap is tight in the worst case, up to a logarithmic factor. For every constant $κ_0>1$, we construct dense linear systems with condition number at most $κ_0$ for which sampling from the solution within a sufficiently small constant total variation distance requires $Ω(ρ^4/\logρ)$ classical queries but only $Θ(ρ)$ quantum queries. The same separation holds, for errors below smaller thresholds, for positive-definite systems, least squares, ridge regression, matrix powers and square roots, imaginary-time and real-time Hamiltonian evolution, and sampling from the top principal component. Our results therefore show that many quantum algorithms for linear algebra, achieve a near-quartic speedup in the worst case, over classical algorithms with sampling and query access. All of these classical lower bounds follow from the same framework, which is based on a lower bound for sampling from distributions that depend on a fixed set of Fourier coefficients of an unknown Boolean function.

title: The wave equation and two-electron atomic wavefunctions
text:
Title: The wave equation and two-electron atomic wavefunctions
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Axisymmetric solutions of the classical wave equation in three spatial dimensions are shown to be in one-to-one correspondence to functions which annihilate the two-electron kinetic energy operator expressed in coordinates relative to a fixed nucleus.

title: NeuroInspector: A Local-First Environment for Inspecting and Annotating Hierarchical Neuroscience Datasets
text:
Title: NeuroInspector: A Local-First Environment for Inspecting and Annotating Hierarchical Neuroscience Datasets
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

The growing scale and structural complexity of neuroscience datasets have made dataset inspection an increasingly distinct stage of the research workflow. Existing inspection workflows, however, remain fragmented, often relying on exploratory scripts, manual documentation, and repeated navigation of unfamiliar file structures before meaningful scientific analysis can begin. Here we present NeuroInspector, a lightweight, browser-based environment for inspecting HDF5 and NWB files. Using WebAssembly-based HDF5 parsing (h5wasm), NeuroInspector runs entirely client-side: files are opened directly from local disk, and the application implements no file-upload endpoint, including in its hosted deployment. The tool combines structural navigation, metadata inspection, sampled data previews, and path-level annotation into portable, fingerprinted "project packs" that preserve inspection decisions without modifying the original file. Rather than functioning as an analysis or validation platform, NeuroInspector provides a dedicated, traceable environment for the inspection stage that precedes formal analysis.

title: The Stellar-Mass Dependence of Feedback-Driven Outflows in DESI DR1 Star-Forming Galaxies
text:
Title: The Stellar-Mass Dependence of Feedback-Driven Outflows in DESI DR1 Star-Forming Galaxies
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Stellar feedback plays a key role in regulating star formation and shaping the evolution of star-forming galaxies. Low-mass galaxies provide one of the most powerful laboratories for testing stellar feedback and its impact on galaxy evolution. Numerical simulations predict that repeated feedback-driven gas inflows and outflows generate a "breathing mode," producing a positive correlation between mass-normalized gas velocity dispersion and recent star formation in dwarf galaxies. Whether this kinematic signature persists at higher stellar masses has remained untested. We investigate this question using $\sim1200$ star-forming galaxies with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy and COSMOS2020 photometry spanning $7.9<\log M_\star/M_\odot<11.5$ within $z<0.25$. Ionized-gas kinematics are measured with pPXF, and recent star formation histories are reconstructed through joint spectrophotometric fitting with Prospector. We confirm the predicted positive correlation throughout the low-mass regime with $\log M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 9.8$, quantitatively consistent with previous observations and FIRE-2 simulations. Above $\log M_\star/M_\odot \sim 9.8$, the correlation weakens rapidly and becomes consistent with zero, providing the first empirical constraint on the stellar mass scale above which the kinematic signature of feedback-driven outflow cycles becomes negligible. Our results establish a characteristic stellar mass above which stellar feedback no longer dominates galaxy-scale gas kinematics, providing a new observational benchmark for models of feedback-regulated galaxy evolution. Future joint analyses of gas kinematics and stellar structure will test whether this transition is accompanied by the broader galaxy response predicted by the breathing mode scenario.

title: Mixed modified-gravity--modified-inertia MOND theories
text:
Title: Mixed modified-gravity--modified-inertia MOND theories
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

It is plausible that in a more fundamental theory of MOND both gravity and inertia will differ from their Newtonian versions. Such theories, if they embody the basic tenets of MOND, will share its primary predictions with existing theories, which modify either gravity or inertia. But they are expected to differ in their structure and in their secondary predictions. Here, I discuss families of nonrelativistic MOND theories that modify both the kinetic and the gravitational actions of Newtonian dynamics. Each family is spanned by one parameter $0\leη\le 1$, which is the scaling dimension of the deep-MOND limit of all terms in the action. Pure modified gravity ($η=0$) and pure modified inertia ($η=1$) are the end cases in each family. I speak of families, since the modified action terms themselves are not strictly specified, but are treated in rather general terms. These theories are artificial in that they are not based on a single unifying idea that dictates the modification of the two components. But they are still useful in pinpointing some idiosyncracies of such theories. For example, neither of the two modified terms, by itself, leads to MOND phenomenology; only their combined effect does. I show how the two combine to make some of the primary MOND predictions, such as asymptotic flatness of rotation curves, the mass-asymptotic-speed relation, and the deep-MOND, virial, mass-velocity-dispersion ($M-σ$) relation. Another idiosyncracy of such theories is the emergence of different interpolating functions in the kinetic equations of motion and in the gravitational field equations, each relevant under different circumstances, and neither of which have the standard deep-MOND limit. Such examples alert us to the wide range of theories that can lead to MOND phenomenology.

title: MERCE: Method-Space Correlation Energy Extrapolation toward High-Rank Coupled Cluster Accuracy
text:
Title: MERCE: Method-Space Correlation Energy Extrapolation toward High-Rank Coupled Cluster Accuracy
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Energy extrapolation is a well-established strategy for approaching quantum-chemical limits without performing prohibitively expensive calculations. Complete basis set extrapolation is widely used, whereas extrapolation across electronic structure methods remains much less developed. Method-Space Effective-Rank Correlation Energy Extrapolation (MERCE) is introduced as an adaptive effective-rank framework for estimating high-rank finite-basis correlation energies from second-order Moller-Plesset perturbation theory (MP2), coupled cluster with single and double excitations (CCSD), and CCSD with perturbative triples [CCSD(T)]. The method assigns adaptive effective ranks to MP2 and CCSD(T) from the local MP2-CCSD-CCSD(T) correlation energy pattern and fits a compact three-point extrapolation form for each system. A hierarchical model-selection protocol balances cross-dataset transferability, maximum dataset-level mean absolute error (MAE) ratios, robustness on developmental sets referenced to full configuration interaction (FCI), size-consistency defects, and performance for A24 noncovalent interaction energies. Across the chemically diverse benchmarks used during model development, the selected MERCE model substantially reduces CCSD(T) errors and frequently improves upon the tested higher-rank coupled cluster baselines. Transferability is further assessed using calculations performed only after the functional form and parameters were frozen. Formal nonadditivity is quantified using artificial noninteracting pairs and the actual A24 and selected S66 component calculations.

title: Certifying quantum code and circuit distances at scale
text:
Title: Certifying quantum code and circuit distances at scale
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Code and circuit distances characterize how strongly quantum error correction suppresses logical errors and guide code comparisons, schedule choices and resource estimates. Yet many published distances are only upper bounds from heuristic searches. Here, we express both distances as tropical partition functions and evaluate them with rank-based dynamic programming and weight-bounded search. Circuit reductions and relaxations shrink the problems, and proved lower bounds with explicit logical errors of matching weight certify exact values. On two benchmarks, our method certifies more instances than all other tested exact solvers combined. We certify distances for codes with up to 31,200 qubits, such as Google's modular hyperbolic codes, and for memory circuits with up to $8\times10^5$ fault mechanisms, such as those of high-rate Cornucopia codes. Our audit of 26 recent papers identifies overestimated distances and non-tight upper bounds in 10 papers, with a maximum discrepancy of at least eight. Certified distances also guide circuit design and show which defective chips remain usable. In particular, we certify circuit distance 16 for IBM's two-gross memory circuits with the standard schedule, not the assumed 18, whereas redesigned schedules reach 18 at one noisy cycle, at the cost of one more timestep per cycle. At 99.98% junction yield, keeping gross-code memory blocks with dead checks that are certified at distance 10 or more raises the estimated usable share from 53% for perfect blocks alone to 94% with an improved schedule.

title: From Bellissard's gap labeling to atomistic quasiperiodic bilayers
text:
Title: From Bellissard's gap labeling to atomistic quasiperiodic bilayers
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Bellissard's framework uses covariant observables to describe aperiodic solids. We examine how butterfly-like spectra in twisted bilayers can be related to bulk gap labels and topological response. A bulk gap permits a spectral projector and an integrated density of states. A topological response requires an additional pairing of that projector. In an illustrative finite honeycomb bilayer, an exact second-moment identity isolates the interlayer contribution to spectral variance. Angle-resolved spectra, finite state counts, an uncoupled reference, and size and broadening checks show how coupling redistributes spectral weight without assigning a bulk gap label. We then examine the requirements for atomistic electronic-structure calculations, including nonorthogonal orbitals, projected densities of states, and basis functions that move during relative sliding. The resulting framework specifies the steps needed to connect atomistic spectra with bulk state counting and topological response.

title: From Imperfect Information to Controlled Steps: Stochastic Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noise and Compression
text:
Title: From Imperfect Information to Controlled Steps: Stochastic Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noise and Compression
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Stochastic optimization relies on information whose statistical quality, availability, and computational cost can vary substantially. Heavy-tailed observations challenge concentration, compression distorts communicated vectors, and generalized smoothness changes how far an algorithm can move. This dissertation studies these difficulties through two linked design decisions: how to construct an informative search vector and how to convert it into a controlled step. We first develop high-probability methods under bounded central $p$-th moments, $p\in(1,2]$, allowing infinite variance when $p<2$. Clipped gradient, accelerated, extragradient, and gradient descent-ascent methods come with guarantees for stochastic minimization and variational inequalities, with smoothness and moment conditions needed only where the iterates lie with high probability. For composite and distributed problems, shifted and innovation clipping preserve the fixed point that direct clipping can disturb, while retaining linear speedup. We then characterize the value of richer stochastic information: lower complexity bounds quantify when same-sample gradient differences and stochastic Hessian information improve heavy-tailed nonconvex optimization, and normalized momentum variance reduction and Hessian-corrected momentum attain matching or near-matching in-expectation bounds. Separately clipping gradients and their correction terms yields batch-free high-probability methods. For compressed distributed optimization, we prove convergence of normalized error-feedback methods under generalized smoothness without a uniform gradient-dissimilarity assumption, and develop parameter-agnostic variants with five momentum estimators. Finally, we extend the estimator hierarchy to linear minimization oracles over arbitrary norm balls, recovering the Euclidean rates under estimator-specific generalized smoothness.

title: Conserved and relaxing modes enable polynomial-success coherent Carleman lattice Boltzmann evolution
text:
Title: Conserved and relaxing modes enable polynomial-success coherent Carleman lattice Boltzmann evolution
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Carleman linearization represents nonlinear lattice Boltzmann collision dynamics in a form amenable to quantum block encoding, but low postselection probabilities in existing population-space encodings make coherent multi-step evolution exponentially unlikely to succeed. We present a quantum Carleman lattice Boltzmann scheme based on the multi-relaxation-time collision operator in a weighted Hermite moment basis. In this basis, the lifted collision operator separates into small coupled blocks whose norm exceeds unity because of the coupling between conserved and relaxing modes. This block structure enables a norm-attaining block encoding with a single-step success probability close to unity. Crucially, scaling the pair sector for a prescribed evolution horizon makes the combined encoding and sector-selection overhead grow polynomially rather than exponentially with the number of steps. For a hundred-step evolution, the resulting complete-run success probability exceeds that of population-space encodings by orders of magnitude. Over horizons of several tens of steps, the truncated dynamics reproduces the nonlinearly generated modes of a benchmark flow to within a few percent. We verify the combined preparation, evolution and readout protocol as a single unitary circuit and give a complete gate-level resource estimate for extracting a nonlinear observable of the benchmark flow from a coherent Carleman evolution. The block structure of conserved and relaxing modes holds equally on three-dimensional lattices and provides a constructive route to norm-attaining encodings for lattice Boltzmann models with quadratic equilibria.

title: Operational Interpretation of Controllability Allocation Scores via Randomized Interventions
text:
Title: Operational Interpretation of Controllability Allocation Scores via Randomized Interventions
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Controllability allocation scores (CASs) assign weights to virtual input channels without specifying how interventions should be implemented. This paper provides an operational interpretation through randomized finite-duration interventions with prescribed, possibly candidate-dependent waveforms. Selection probabilities are fixed before a mean-output target is specified, while waveform amplitudes are optimized after the target is revealed. We derive the unique minimum expected-energy amplitude policy and formulate volumetric and weighted average-energy allocation criteria. We also establish a finite-trial mean-output error bound and show that waveform-based weighted AE-CAS minimizes an upper bound on the target-averaged mean-square error. We establish uniform convergence of normalized waveform-response Gramians and show that accumulation points of optimal allocations solve the limiting problem. With uniform timing, equal positive waveform efficiencies recover the original CAS in the short-duration limit, whereas unequal efficiencies yield waveform-weighted limits. Under the former conditions, the limiting error bound is proportional to the original weighted AE-CAS objective. For common waveforms, we further establish an exact finite-duration correspondence with the original full-state V-CAS under uniform timing.

title: McKean-Vlasov flights without moments: well-posedness, propagation of chaos and a critical threshold for law-dependent jumps
text:
Title: McKean-Vlasov flights without moments: well-posedness, propagation of chaos and a critical threshold for law-dependent jumps
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study McKean-Vlasov equations driven by an isotropic $2s$-stable L{é}vy noise, $s\in(0,1)$, whose solutions may have no finite mean, with coefficients that are Lipschitz with respect to a bounded Wasserstein-type distance. When the jump noise is additive, we prove strong well-posedness for every initial law and every $s$, without any moment assumption, and propagation of chaos at the rate $N^{-1/2}$ for kernel interactions. When the size of the jumps depends on the law, we prove the same results for $s>1/2$, and we show by an example that uniqueness fails for every $s<1/2$. The value $s=1/2$ thus separates well-posedness from non-uniqueness; the critical case itself remains open. These results answer, for stable noise, the question of uniqueness without moments raised by Jourdain, M{é}l{é}ard and Woyczy{ń}ski and by Cavallazzi.

title: ADE Quiver Duality Proposals: Graph Classification and Nodewise Realizations
text:
Title: ADE Quiver Duality Proposals: Graph Classification and Nodewise Realizations
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We use the large-$N$ index strategy to find new quiver dualities in four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ quiver gauge theories. We study gauge quivers with or without an adjoint field at each gauge node, and bifundamental matter between selected nodes with fixed $R$-charges. Imposing the finite-meson condition restricts the allowed gauge graphs to finite ADE diagrams and leads to a new simultaneous duality for ADE quivers. We present an explicit superpotential that produces a uniform classical meson spectrum consistent with the large-$N$ index approach's prediction. We then relate the simultaneous rank transformation to the longest element of the ADE Weyl group, whose reduced expressions organize nodewise duality sequences realizing the simultaneous ADE duality. Realizing the simultaneous ADE duality through such nodewise sequences offers a finite-$N$ consistency check beyond the large-$N$ index construction. Moreover, we realize the simultaneous ADE duality as a sequence of subquiver simultaneous dualities.

title: Comment on the recent claims of H0 measurements with the ZTF DR2 SN Ia sample (arXiv:2610.36051)
text:
Title: Comment on the recent claims of H0 measurements with the ZTF DR2 SN Ia sample (arXiv:2610.36051)
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Karchev et al. (2026) derived a value of H0 by combining the ZTF SN Ia DR2 sample with SH0ES calibrator Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia; Riess et al. 2022), used to anchor the SN Ia absolute luminosity. The ZTF SN Ia DR2 dataset (Rigault et al., 2025) is the largest (O(3000)) SN Ia sample to date obtained with a single telescope. However, as emphasized in the data release, the absolute photometric calibration of the survey has not yet been established to the precision required for cosmological inference. The relative photometric zeropoint offset between the SH0ES and ZTF SN Ia DR2 samples, which is fully degenerate with H0, is therefore unknown and cannot be determined from publicly available data. The photometric corrections introduced in Karchev et al. (2026) do not address this global calibration offset. Consequently, their reported H0 determination is not supported by the available calibration information. We nonetheless share the excitement of pursuing state-of-the-art cosmology with ZTF and are actively working toward the release of a fully calibrated dataset

title: Quantized memory of measurement records near the light cone of quantum circuits
text:
Title: Quantized memory of measurement records near the light cone of quantum circuits
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum processors now measure qubits in the middle of a circuit, and the stream of outcomes is the raw output of error correction, measurement-based state preparation and monitored dynamics. For a scrambling circuit, predicting the statistics of this stream is as hard as simulating the processor, so there is no exact reference to check it against once the device outgrows classical simulation. We show that near the light cone the problem becomes exactly solvable, for any two-qubit gate. In a brickwork circuit with one polarized qubit in a maximally mixed background, measurements along the edge of the light cone form a two-state Markov chain, and measurements $d$ sites inside the edge are generated by $\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1$ qubits that move with it, while the rest of the chain, however large, acts on them as a memoryless bath. The memory of the record is therefore quantized, one bit on the edge and at most one more for every site of displacement, a bound that generic gates attain. The same causal structure determines which hardware noise the record can see, removes that sensitivity at no gate cost, and yields a tomography-free witness of dual-unitarity. On a 156-qubit superconducting processor, a demonstration with its analysis specified in advance finds the predicted memory one and two sites inside the light cone, and none where the theory forbids it. This gives dynamic circuits an exact reference at any system size, and shows that the collision models of open-system theory arise exactly inside chaotic dynamics.

title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
text:
Title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Robotic additive manufacturing requires joint paths that reconcile robot feasibility with process-specific geometry. We develop an offline optimization-based path planner that combines joint-path regularity and self-collision penalties with process costs and constraints, so that a new process enters through its own reference, residuals, and tolerances. Full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization handle references of different lengths. Iterative Weight Tuning (IWT) determines the cost weights from the gaps between Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and their targets. In carbon-fiber winding and robotic 3D printing, the planned paths meet the geometric tolerances and all KPI targets, and both paths are executed on a UR10e, without extrusion for printing, with joint-level tracking recorded during execution.

title: No Exponential Quantum Advantage for Decoded Quantum Interferometry with Local Quantum Decoders
text:
Title: No Exponential Quantum Advantage for Decoded Quantum Interferometry with Local Quantum Decoders
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Decoded quantum interferometry (DQI) reduces optimization of sparse linear constraint problems, and sampling from their Gibbs measures, to decoding a linear code from a quantum state. We study DQI on random $D$-regular $k$-sparse instances with $k\ge3$, for which local decoders such as belief propagation with quantum messages (BPQM) are commonly used. Such decoders estimate a typical codeword symbol using only the qudits within logarithmic distance of it. Our main insight is that the thresholds of the decoding problem induced by DQI correspond to phase transitions of the Gibbs measure that are well studied in statistical physics: tree reconstruction for local decoders and, for Max-$k$-XORSAT, condensation for the optimal decoder. This insight allows us to prove two main results. First, we prove an information-theoretic obstruction: no local decoder can recover the codeword with high probability above the tree reconstruction threshold. Conversely, we show that a decoder based on BPQM reaches this threshold. Since the cavity method predicts that local Markov chains equilibrate rapidly up to the same threshold, we expect DQI with local decoders to give no exponential speedup for sampling and no advantage in approximate optimization with amplitude functions that depend only on the number of violated constraints. Second, we consider the optimal decoder (the pretty-good measurement, for which no efficient implementation is known) and show that it succeeds exactly below the condensation threshold. The condensation threshold thus provides a tight upper bound on the performance of DQI with these amplitude functions, providing a strict refinement of the limit that Jordan et al.\ derived from the Holevo bound. Our results point to efficient nonlocal decoders that succeed between the two thresholds as the only viable path to a quantum advantage with DQI on these instances.

title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
text:
Title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

As text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly positioned as world simulators, it is essential to evaluate whether their videos conform to physical commonsense. However, existing benchmarks rely on annotators who rate each video with a single score based on intuition, yielding ratings that are subjective and do not tell which physical principle is violated. We introduce PhyRubric, a rubric-grounded diagnostic framework for evaluating physical commonsense in T2V generation. For each caption, PhyRubric constructs a caption-specific rubric before any video is seen, decomposing the caption into semantic and physical items, and derives scores from item-level verdicts grounded in timestamped evidence. We instantiate this framework as PhyRubric-Bench, which spans 34 categories across five physical domains, and scale it up to PhyRubric-Train with 3,788 videos, on which we fine-tune the open-source PhyRubric-Judge. Empirical results across ten T2V models show that physical commonsense remains far from solved, and that PhyRubric-Judge correlates more closely with human judgments than existing open-source judges while matching the frontier proprietary Gemini 4 Argon. Further analysis provides actionable insights for T2V models.

title: Learning Biological Hierarchies in Single-Cell Foundation Models
text:
Title: Learning Biological Hierarchies in Single-Cell Foundation Models
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Cell types are organized by taxonomic relationships that define lineages in the so-called cell ontology. However, most existing foundation models typically ignore cell-type lineages encoded in this cell ontology. We introduce a biologically informed foundation model called scOntoFM, which embeds hierarchical cell ontology into representation learning. Using Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) distances from the ontology graph, our framework pairs efficient offline triplet sampling with hierarchical cell-ontology learning. This approach jointly preserves local neighborhoods and shapes the global embedding geometry to reflect the ontology structure. Across diverse cell- and gene-level benchmarks, the model consistently improves performance, with especially strong gains in zero-shot settings. Our model also balances batch integration with biological structure preservation, providing complementary perspectives to existing embedding evaluation frameworks and supporting scalable biological discovery.

title: Spin Migration in the Argon Dimer
text:
Title: Spin Migration in the Argon Dimer
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We introduce the concept of \emph{spin migration}, i.e. time-dependent spin density, and the absolute smallest example of molecular spintronics. We illustrate the concept by \emph{ab initio} calculations of the coupled vibronic motion of the electrons and the nuclei in the argon dimer cation, in which the vibrational level spacing is similar to the spin--orbit splitting of the atomic argon cations. We find that the spin density varies on multiple time scales, given by the natural time scales of the electronic and nuclear wavepackets.

title: Quantum-Informed Graph Decomposition
text:
Title: Quantum-Informed Graph Decomposition
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is a near-term quantum algorithm for solving combinatorial optimization problems, but its accuracy and resource requirements may scale poorly with problem size or structure, reducing its utility in practice. Approaches such as the Graph Decomposition for Optimization Algorithm (GDOA) seek to address this by iteratively reducing an input problem until it reaches a size where it can be solved using QAOA while maintaining the same optimal solution. This algorithm, however, requires solving integer programs that have exponentially many variables, and can result in suboptimal solutions, as the integer programs may contain slack terms. In this work, we propose a heuristic called the Quantum Enhanced Graph Decomposition (QEGD) algorithm. Its novelty lies in its use of QAOA as a subroutine for sparsifying a graph through local vertex-merging. The algorithm, when used to sparsify MaxCut problems that are then solved using QAOA, achieves higher approximation ratios across all tested graphs than GDOA for random 5-regular and 6-regular graphs. We then compare the time-to-solution and approximation ratio of QEGD to other QAOA variants a collection of Erdös-Rényi graphs. QEGD has higher approximation ratios on average than QAOA$^2$ and ParaQAOA on all tested graphs. It also results in higher average approximation ratios than DC-QAOA on sparse Erdös-Rényi graphs and comparable average approximation ratio on denser Erdös-Rényi graphs. However, its average wall-clock time is between 0.4\% and 5\% of the average DC-QAOA wall-clock time.

title: PARIS: A multi-agent LLM framework for end-to-end, PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews with pre-synthesis corpus quality assessment
text:
Title: PARIS: A multi-agent LLM framework for end-to-end, PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews with pre-synthesis corpus quality assessment
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Systematic literature reviews (SRs) remain slow and labor-intensive, and most automation tools address single stages of the workflow. We present PARIS (PRISMA Agentic Research Intelligence System), an open-source framework in which a conductor agent running in Claude Code orchestrates 15 specialized large language model (LLM) agents, from scoping a research question to exporting a manuscript draft. Agents are specified declaratively, coordinate exclusively through persisted artifacts that the conductor validates before every transition, and delegate retrieval, bibliometric analysis and scoring to deterministic Python utilities. Three human checkpoints gate study inclusion, corpus adequacy and the synthesis outline. We also introduce QualityScore, a pre-synthesis index that aggregates normalized network, bibliometric, semantic and process sub-scores into a 0-100 grade. Two case studies illustrate both: AI chatbots and university students' learning (388 records, 100 included) and AI-assisted SR methods (131 records, 123 included, QualityScore 69.1 recomputed with a proxy network sub-score). They show end-to-end feasibility across domains and the diagnostic use of QualityScore: in the first run, corpus improvements chosen at the corpus-adequacy checkpoint raised the score from 74.6 to 81.9 and the number of pre-2023 studies from 1 to 19. Audits of both runs exposed failure modes: incomplete retrieval, counts that drifted between agents, unrecorded or delegated checkpoint decisions and a grade that depends on how citation data are handled. PARIS fully supports 8 of the 27 PRISMA 2020 items and partially supports 11. Output quality has so far been judged only by an internal reviewer agent; independent validation against human reviews is the next step.

title: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory
text:
Title: Gabor Gabor: E-Gaborformer, a Strictly Causal Speech Recognizer with Gabor-Dictionary Convolutions and Delta-Rule Memory
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Real-time voice agents need a speech recognizer that never waits for future audio and whose memory per call does not grow with the length of the call. We present E-Gaborformer, a strictly causal encoder that combines Gated DeltaNet-2 recurrent layers with sliding-window attention in a 3:1 ratio, and builds every temporal convolution from a fixed dictionary of causal Gabor atoms. Its streaming state is constant, about 19 MB per call at production scale including the prediction network, where a causal-attention encoder of the same size accumulates over 1 GB after ten minutes. In a controlled causal study on LibriSpeech, E-Gaborformer leaves the initial plateau earlier, reaches a given accuracy up to 18% sooner, and matches or beats an E-Branchformer trained with the identical front end and recipe. At production scale, a 0.6B-parameter Hebrew and English streaming transducer built on E-Gaborformer has 28 to 31% lower word error rate (WER) than NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming, a model of the same size, on English voice-agent traffic, and up to 20% lower Hebrew WER than our previous production system. The same weights serve strictly causal and 480 ms-lookahead decoding with no loss in accuracy, and a two-class formulation of the RNN-T lattice trains the transducer 2.6x faster with exact loss and gradients.

title: Relating approaches to interacting quantum clocks and systems
text:
Title: Relating approaches to interacting quantum clocks and systems
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

The problem of describing the dynamics of quantum systems relative to quantum clocks with which they interact is relevant to the physics of quantum reference frames and quantum gravity alike. There have been different approaches that derive a relational time-dependent Schrödinger equation for the system relative to the clock from a time-independent Hamiltonian constraint. We show that some of these approaches, due to Smith and Ahmadi, Gemsheim and Rost, as well as the so-called Born-Oppenheimer approach, can be unified in a single framework for describing conditional quantum states. In particular, the Born-Oppenheimer approach to quantum cosmology is seen to correspond to a type of interacting Page-Wootters formalism. We discuss the issue of unitarity and linearity, or lack thereof, in the relational dynamics, and we conclude with a brief outlook to further developments.

title: From local learning to global electronic properties in large-scale systems
text:
Title: From local learning to global electronic properties in large-scale systems
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Machine learning from local atomic environments offers an efficient route to electronic structure, but evaluating global electronic properties in large systems remains computationally demanding. Here we combine real space charge density learning with stochastic propagation using Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians constructed from the predicted densities. The framework avoids target system self-consistent iterations and explicit diagonalization, while hierarchical blocking enables dense grid inference within limited GPU memory. We demonstrate density of states calculations for one million Si atoms and optical and transport calculations for over one hundred thousand atoms, without training separate models for each property. This framework extends the practical scale of electronic structure calculations within Kohn-Sham DFT, opening opportunities to investigate how atomic structure governs electronic, optical and transport properties at length scales relevant to real materials and devices.

title: Network Effect Decomposition for Causal Effect Estimation under Network Interference
text:
Title: Network Effect Decomposition for Causal Effect Estimation under Network Interference
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Estimating causal effects from observational network data requires accounting for both individual treatment and neighborhood exposure. Existing outcome models commonly incorporate these intervention variables into a joint predictor and estimate causal effects through prediction contrasts, leaving the corresponding response components implicit. We propose the $\underline{N}$etwork $\underline{E}$ffect $\underline{D}$ecomposition $\underline{Net}$work (NEDNet), which parameterizes the conditional outcome response as a query-invariant pre-treatment baseline plus separate treatment- and exposure-response pathways. Path-specific neighborhood contextualization supplies local pre-treatment information to the two pathways. We characterize the fitted response through a unique reference-normalized decomposition, which is equivalent to a zero mixed treatment--exposure contrast. Experiments on semi-synthetic benchmarks derived from BlogCatalog and Flickr show that NEDNet achieves the lowest PEHE among the compared methods for individual, peer, and total effects across homogeneous and covariate-heterogeneous response settings.

title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
text:
Title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. Whether this gas kinematic feature is common among cool-core clusters remains unclear. Here, we revisit XRISM observations of A1795 and A2029 to investigate the signatures of AGN feedback and their contribution to the gas velocity fields. In A1795, AGN feedback dominates the velocity dispersion in the core, similar to Perseus, and may provide turbulent heating at a rate comparable to radiative cooling. In contrast, we obtain only an upper limit on the AGN feedback contribution in A2029, where merger-driven motions dominate. Tailored simulations indicate that an off-axis minor merger $\simeq1.6$ Gyr ago displaced the central low-entropy gas in A2029, potentially suppressing AGN activity. This gas is now returning to the center, possibly facilitating the re-establishment of AGN feedback. We propose an evolutionary view of the double-cascade scenario, in which merger-driven motions dominate during and shortly after significant mergers, while feedback-driven turbulence re-emerges in cluster cores as systems relax. This framework provides a basis for interpreting XRISM kinematic measurements of (weak) cool-core clusters. Our findings highlight the importance of spatially resolved gas kinematics and detailed modeling for identifying double-cascade features and disentangling the contributions of AGN feedback and mergers.

title: Learning developmental dynamics from lineage context
text:
Title: Learning developmental dynamics from lineage context
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

A central goal of biology is to predict the dynamics of multicellular systems. Lineage context (the states of a cell's sisters, cousins, etc.) could inform these predictions, but how best to leverage it remains unclear. Here we introduce lineage inpainting, a generative modeling approach that uses lineage context with tree-structured transformers and stochastic interpolants to model cell state dynamics across lineage trees. Applied to a lineage-traced transcriptional atlas of mouse embryogenesis, it recovers dynamics not resolved by gene expression alone, including multiple transcriptional convergence events where distinct lineages are drawn to a common state. Despite being fit on unperturbed development, lineage inpainting can generate hypotheses about perturbation responses by simulating counterfactuals. These simulations agree in many cases with observed developmental phenotypes, including a single-cell measurement of the Tbx5 knockout response. Our results show that lineage information provides a rich source of context for learning multicellular dynamics.

title: The effect of local stacking fault fluctuations on dislocation glide and the interplay with solid solution strengthening in Al-Mg alloys
text:
Title: The effect of local stacking fault fluctuations on dislocation glide and the interplay with solid solution strengthening in Al-Mg alloys
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Concentrated alloys are characterized by a random arrangement of solute atoms of different sizes, which generates spatially fluctuating displacement and stress fields with non-trivial correlations. This chemical disorder also induces local fluctuations in stacking-fault (SF) energies, giving rise to fluctuating SF forces acting on the partial dislocations bounding the SF. In this work, we investigate the characteristics of the SF noise, including spatial correlations and the impact of such SF energy fluctuations on dislocation glide. Specifically, the gliding behavior of screw, edge, and mixed dislocations in a model concentrated Al-Mg random alloy with varying Mg content is analyzed. The interplay between SF energy fluctuations and solid-solution noise is also discussed. We show that SF forces are spatially correlated, in close analogy with long-range elastic stresses, and exhibit a robust negative correlation along the slip direction. We identify the physical origin of these correlations and demonstrate that they significantly contribute to the critical resolved shear stress for dislocations to glide. In contrast, correlations in other directions are weaker but can still be non-negligible, depending on the underlying interatomic interactions.

title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
text:
Title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Chiral gauge theories underlie the Standard Model, yet none has been simulated nonperturbatively. Lattice constructions that evade the Nielsen-Ninomiya obstruction entail complex fermion measures or infinite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces. Here we provide a gauge-invariant Hamiltonian lattice regularization of 1+1-dimensional abelian chiral gauge theories built from clock-and-shift qudits with $\mathbb{Z}_N$ gauge fields, in which the global chiral symmetry and its 't Hooft anomaly survive exactly mod $N$. Anomaly cancellation on the lattice lets the Gauss laws be imposed and solved exactly, reducing the theory to an unconstrained qudit chain. Using infinite matrix product states, we simulate the canonical 1+1-dimensional chiral gauge theory, the 34-50 model, and find excellent agreement with analytic predictions, showing that a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space at $N=6$ reproduces the expected infrared physics of the continuum 34-50 model. This provides an efficient and practical solution to the problem of simulating general abelian chiral gauge theories in 1+1 dimensions, both on classical and quantum computers.

title: De-lensing cosmic birefringence with joint reconstruction
text:
Title: De-lensing cosmic birefringence with joint reconstruction
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Reconstruction of anisotropic cosmic birefringence from the CMB is limited by lensing $B$-mode sample variance and partially degenerate with the lensing curl. We study the joint reconstruction of lensing (gradient and curl) and birefringence at the maximum-a-posteriori point, whose spectra are near-optimal statistics. We predict the joint response and noise analytically, validate them on simulations, and show unbiased inference of its amplitude. Errors will shrink $5$-fold relative to quadratic estimators at SPT-3G+ depths, promising much tighter constraints on parity-violating new physics, owing to the removal of the lensing $B$-polarization sample variance.

title: The Statistical Geometry of Latent Recovery in Hidden Markov Models
text:
Title: The Statistical Geometry of Latent Recovery in Hidden Markov Models
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) offer an important capability to interpret fitted latent states and transitions. When emission distributions nearly coincide, a small observation-density error does not ensure accurate estimation of the latent quantities needed for interpretation. This motivates us to characterize convergence rates for latent recovery that account for emission separation. Our main contribution lies in deriving deterministic inverse inequalities that convert Hellinger error between fitted and true densities into bounds on latent recovery errors. We develop these bounds for multivariate Gaussian HMMs with a common, known emission covariance matrix and combine them with a Hellinger estimation guarantee for the global maximum likelihood estimator to obtain latent recovery rates. Although the joint observation distribution is a Gaussian mixture with exponentially many path components, they share the same emission centers across time. Leveraging this shared structure, we show that the separation exponents are governed by the maximum number of simultaneously approaching centers rather than the number of path components. Under exact specification, the global bounds on state-sequence probability discrepancies and the 1-Wasserstein loss for latent location distributions exhibit sharp separation exponents that do not increase with the number of selected times. Moreover, sufficiently small observation-density error guarantees unique matching between fitted and true emission centers, which yields error bounds for individual emission centers and transition rows. Under over-specification, individual split-state transition rows are not necessarily identifiable, so we quantify aggregate latent recovery errors and show that state-sequence probability bounds incur larger separation exponents compared to exact specification. We conduct synthetic experiments to validate our theoretical results.

title: Strain-Induced BCC-to-FCC Transformation in Tungsten Uncovered by Molecular Dynamics Simulations with Machine Learning Potentials
text:
Title: Strain-Induced BCC-to-FCC Transformation in Tungsten Uncovered by Molecular Dynamics Simulations with Machine Learning Potentials
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Polymorphic transformations occur in a minority of metals. Tungsten is not one of them. This observation does not rule out its intrinsic phase transition possibility, but may be due to inaccessible thermodynamic and mechanical conditions in conventional experiments. Herein, we investigate the body centered cubic (BCC) to face centered cubic (FCC) transformation in tungsten via a rigorously validated machine learning potential (MLP) molecular dynamics (MD) approach. Our simulations demonstrate that strain induced BCC to FCC transformation indeed occurs in tungsten. The FCC phase exceeds 20 at.% at low temperature and in the presence of dislocations. In the perfect crystal moderate temperatures favor phase transformation kinetics. Structural analysis confirms the transformation following the Bain and Nishiyama Wassermann orientation relationship. These results establish the viability of strain induced polymorphic transformation in tungsten and provide a critical guideline for the experimental production of duplex tungsten with enhanced ductility addressing a longstanding challenge in tungsten material engineering for high-temperature structural applications.

title: Variational Splines and Generalized Gaussian Processes
text:
Title: Variational Splines and Generalized Gaussian Processes
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Tikhonov regularization, kriging, and Gaussian-process regression share the same algorithm because, for a linear inverse problem with a Gaussian prior and Gaussian noise, the minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) estimator is the solution of a regularized least-squares problem. We show that this equivalence survives the passage from vectors to generalized functions: the regularized least-squares estimators become generalized splines, and the Gaussian random vectors become generalized Gaussian processes (GGPs) on the dual of a nuclear space. A whitening operator $\mathrm{L}: \mathcal{S} \to L_2$ specifies both the native Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L} \subset \mathcal{S}'$ of the splines and a family of GGPs, which solve a stochastic differential equation subject to boundary conditions. We prove that the Gaussian spaces of these processes are congruent to the core $\mathrm{L}^\ast(L_2)$ of the native space, and that their MMSE estimators from finitely many linear measurements are generalized splines. Our framework extends the classical correspondences of Kimeldorf-Wahba, Parzen and Kailath in two respects: our estimators form a broader class that includes generalized functions, and we give a proper Bayesian treatment of the case where the null space of $\mathrm{L}$ is non-trivial. The framework gives a precise meaning to statements such as ``fractional splines are the optimal estimators of fractional Brownian motion,'' and it provides a rigorous Bayesian formulation of infinite-dimensional linear inverse problems.

title: All-Disorder Localization for the One-Dimensional Anderson Model with Power-Law Hopping
text:
Title: All-Disorder Localization for the One-Dimensional Anderson Model with Power-Law Hopping
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We consider the one-dimensional random operator \[ (H_{λ,ω}u)(n) = \sum_{m\ne n}\frac{u(m)}{|n-m|^r} +λω_nu(n), \] where the random variables $ω_n$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $[-1,1]$ (i.e., \mbox{$ω_n\stackrel{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[-1,1]$}). For every $λ>0$ and $r>3/2$, we prove that $H_{λ,ω}$ almost surely has pure point spectrum and admits an orthonormal eigenbasis $\{ψ_j\}$ satisfying \[ \sum_{n\in\bbZ}(1+|n|)^{2τ}|ψ_j(n)|^2<\infty \qquad \text{for every }j\text{ and }0\leτ<r-\frac32. \] These conclusions establish spectral localization, thereby rigorously confirming the prediction of earlier analytical and numerical studies in the physics literature, which identified $r=3/2$ as the marginal exponent.

title: What are local complementations, really?
text:
Title: What are local complementations, really?
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

A local complementation at a vertex $v$ of a graph $G$ replaces the induced neighborhood of $v$ with its complement. Local complementations are, at face value, peculiar operations. Yet they famously show up when describing the local Clifford equivalence among graph states, and, because of this, have become a fundamental notion in the study of graph states. Following Bouchet, we show here how local complementations on graphs are more naturally thought of in terms of switchings of (matroid) bases of stabilizer states. Bases and switchings reveal structural properties of stabilizer states that are harder to glean from the graph-theoretic description alone, such as vertex-minors and statistics of local Pauli measurements. Bases also simplify prior proofs about graphs up to local complementations, of which we give several examples. Bases are foundational in the study of (multi)matroids; as such this paper serves as a gentle introduction to the applications of multimatroids to quantum information theory.

title: Fitting Conventional and Neural Exchange-Correlation Functionals to Accurate Densities without Self-Consistent Fields
text:
Title: Fitting Conventional and Neural Exchange-Correlation Functionals to Accurate Densities without Self-Consistent Fields
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Exchange-correlation functionals are usually fitted with energy-only losses, so better energies often bring worse densities. We introduce a workflow that predicts in closed form, from one Fock build on inverse Kohn-Sham orbitals of any accurate density, a functional's self-consistent density, and fits it to that density with no self-consistent-field solution. Fitted convexly, a CF22D-form hybrid beats CF22D and MN15 on unseen energies, dipole moments, and unfitted densities (6.8- and 22-fold lower density error). A neural meta-GGA fitted to 6 energies and 11 densities beats SCAN in both.

title: Learning consistent molecular mechanics force fields from first principles
text:
Title: Learning consistent molecular mechanics force fields from first principles
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Classical force fields (FFs) remain the workhorse for large-scale simulations even as machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approach ab initio accuracy. They decompose total configuration energies into simple effective interactions whose parameters are traditionally assigned based on atom or bond types, enabling efficient simulations but also limiting their ability to adapt across configurations. Recent machine learning approaches have improved the accuracy and transferability of bonded parameters in these FFs by inferring them as functions of local atomic environments, but still rely on empirical nonbonded parameters for practical simulations. In this work, we introduce a unified approach, \texttt{grappa-fullFF}, which learns both bonded and nonbonded parameters \emph{consistently} and simultaneously from ab initio reference data. By incorporating physically inspired regularization via supervision of the electrostatic potential and an architecture that facilitates charge equilibration, our model recovers accurate electric response properties, achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on geometry optimization benchmarks, and reproduces the conformational sampling of both classical and existing machine-learned FFs, without relying on externally assigned nonbonded parameters.

title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
text:
Title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Conditional generative models are increasingly used for scientific prediction beyond the direct training support. Yet scientific questions often concern whether one intervention changes the effect of another. Such interactions can be of primary interest while explaining little of the total variation, allowing models to appear accurate overall without recovering the relevant scientific effect. It remains unclear how these models learn interactions and when these successfully extrapolate to unseen conditions. We therefore study interaction recovery in flow-matching models using a physiological time-series simulator, drug dose-response data, combinatorial cell perturbations, and molecular conformer generations, where we separate recovery from hallucinated interaction structure.
