LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

title: Polyformer: a generative framework for thermodynamic modeling of polymeric molecules
text:
Title: Polyformer: a generative framework for thermodynamic modeling of polymeric molecules
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The classic paradigm of structural biology is that the sequence of a biomolecule (protein, nucleic acid, lipid, etc) determines its conformation (shape) which determines its biological function. Protein folding programs like AlphaFold address this paradigm by predicting the single best conformation given a sequence that defines the molecule. However, biomolecules are not static structures, and their conformational ensemble determines their function. We present the Polyformer -- a generative framework for thermodynamic modeling of polymeric molecules. Given the sequence and temperature (or another thermodynamic variable), the Polyformer generates conformations faithful to the molecule's thermodynamic conformational ensemble. It is the first generative model that solves three problems simultaneously: how does a molecule fold, what is its conformational ensemble, and how does the conformational ensemble change as we change physical temperature. As a concrete test case, we apply Polyformer to protein domains with 50-111 residues and report good agreement of model predictions to Molecular Dynamics (MD) trajectories.

title: Learning to Rank Propagators in Constraint Programming
text:
Title: Learning to Rank Propagators in Constraint Programming
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

The order in which propagators are executed can substantially affect the performance of constraint programming solvers, yet propagator priorities are typically determined by fixed, manually designed heuristics. In this work, we explore learning instance-dependent propagator priorities from static problem features. We formulate the task as a learning-to-rank problem, addressing the challenge that the quality of a priority assignment can be measured through solver runtime, while the desired priorities of individual propagators are not directly observable. A self-attention-based model jointly scores the propagators present in an instance and is trained using pairwise preferences derived from solver runtimes measured under randomized propagator priority assignments, with a Plackett-Luce-based ranking objective. Predicted rankings are mapped to the discrete priority levels of the Choco solver before search begins, without modifying its propagation or search procedures. We evaluate the approach on XCSP3 instances and demonstrate that propagator ordering can have a substantial impact on solving time. On a test set of 698 instances, picked out as most difficult by problem class, the learned priorities increase the number of solved instances from 634 to 654, reduce median solver runtime by 27.93%, and reduce aggregate penalized runtime (PAR1) by 12.65% compared with Choco's default priorities. We further observe that improvements vary across problem classes and show that a simple policy selecting between learned and default priorities further increases the number of solved instances. These results demonstrate the potential of learning instance-dependent propagator priorities to improve constraint programming performance, particularly on difficult instances.

title: Gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rotating background: An eigenfunction approach
text:
Title: Gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rotating background: An eigenfunction approach
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We construct the free gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rigidly rotating cylindrical coordinates using an eigenfunction approach within the Feynman gauge. Starting from the quadratic gauge-fixed QCD action, we derive the corresponding kinetic operators and obtain their spectral representations. For the gluon field, a circular polarization basis diagonalizes the vector wave operator, leading to polarization-dependent shifts in the orders of the radial Bessel functions. In the absence of radial boundaries, we explicitly recover the standard Minkowski propagator in inertial Cartesian coordinates, showing that the off-diagonal tensor components in the cylindrical basis have a geometrical origin. We then extend the construction to a finite-radius cylinder satisfying the causality condition $|Ω|R<1$, imposing relative boundary conditions on the gluon field and Dirichlet conditions on the ghosts. The resulting discrete transverse spectra involve both Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues for the gluon modes, from which we obtain explicit spectral representations of the propagators. Our results provide a consistent framework for perturbative QCD calculations in rotating geometries, retaining the angular-momentum, polarization, and boundary effects relevant to future studies of correlation functions and radiative corrections.

title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making
text:
Title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

System-1 Decision Models directly make structured probabilistic decisions over query-specified options given a state in a single forward pass, without autoregressively generating reasoning trajectories or textual responses. Recent evaluations cover diverse tasks but often rely on existing benchmarks, where prior exposure to test material can obscure generalization. Moreover, real-world decision making often involves long contexts, large option spaces, and complex logical dependencies, challenges that existing benchmarks do not adequately capture together. Thus, we introduce MMDM (Massive Multitask Decision Making), a benchmark of 5,448 high-quality questions across 16 task categories, combining newly constructed tasks with source-grounded recompositions and rewrites for single-select, multi-select, and soft-label decision making in fresh contexts. It covers realistic scenarios such as agent state tracking, tool and skill selection, preference judgments, and rubric scoring, with option spaces ranging from 2 to 1,024 and inputs extending to 64,817 tokens. With MMDM, we conduct a comprehensive quantitative evaluation of 28 decision models, showing that many perform well on common knowledge yet struggle with interdependent options, constrained decisions, and multi-select tasks. For example, Perplexity Decider-V1.2 reaches 78.75% Hard Single-select Accuracy on world knowledge, but only 53.95% on option logic and 47.95% on constraint planning, while the best Hard Multi-select Accuracy across all models is 36.81%. These results highlight joint reasoning, constraint-aware selection, and complete multi-select recovery as key priorities for decision model development, with MMDM providing a testbed for measuring this progress.

title: Duration-Aware World Models for Sleep Staging with Dwell-Time Constraints
text:
Title: Duration-Aware World Models for Sleep Staging with Dwell-Time Constraints
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Closed-loop neuromodulation requires sleep staging that respects stage-specific minimum dwells: stimulation policies switch by sleep stage, and a policy change is permitted only after the current stage has persisted for its minimum duration. Discriminative classifiers fragment stage trajectories---for example, a 30 s Wake segment inside a 10 min N2 run---and even hidden semi-Markov smoothing leaves 11.3% of segments below the minimum dwell threshold. This paper presents a world model in which a recurrent state-space model (RSSM) learns dwell structure endogenously from EEG, via duration-aware latent sampling, a survival-curve dwell prior, and transition-matrix calibration, and a trajectory-level hard-constraint layer guarantees the minimum dwell at decoding. On SHHS-1 (200 subjects, 160/20/20, three repeated splits), the model reaches a test accuracy of 0.690 +/- 0.053 (95% CI over 3 folds) versus 0.641 +/- 0.042 for an identically split discriminative baseline, with macro-F1 +17.5 pp and better accuracy on all three folds. On Sleep-EDF the constraint layer cuts below-threshold segments from 71.8% to 0.1% with no accuracy loss (0.734 to 0.737), and an online locked scheduler reduces RL policy switches by 87% per night while keeping every policy run at least 90 s. To the best of the author's knowledge, this is the first system to couple learned dwell statistics with a decoding-time hard guarantee. Code and pretrained weights will be released.

title: Generative Replica-Exchange: A Flow-based Framework for Accelerating Replica Exchange Simulations
text:
Title: Generative Replica-Exchange: A Flow-based Framework for Accelerating Replica Exchange Simulations
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Replica exchange (REX) is one of the most widely used enhanced sampling methodologies, yet its efficiency is limited by the requirement for a large number of intermediate temperature replicas. Here we present Generative Replica Exchange (GREX), which integrates deep generative models into the REX framework to eliminate this temperature ladder. Drawing inspiration from reservoir replica exchange (res-REX), GREX utilizes trained normalizing flows to generate high-temperature configurations on demand and map them directly to the target distribution using the potential energy as a constraint, without requiring target-temperature training data. This approach reduces production simulations to a single replica at the target temperature while maintaining thermodynamic rigor through Metropolis exchange acceptance. We validate GREX on three benchmark systems of increasing complexity, highlighting its superior efficiency and practical applicability for molecular simulations.

title: Fast Nanophotonic Inverse Design using Precomputed Numerical Green Functions
text:
Title: Fast Nanophotonic Inverse Design using Precomputed Numerical Green Functions
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Inverse design has been transformative in nanophotonics, providing an automated means of realizing high-performance, non-intuitive devices. However, the primary bottleneck of existing inverse design approaches is their reliance on time-consuming and computationally expensive full-wave electromagnetic simulations. In this work, we extend the Precomputed Numerical Green Function (PNGF) method for the first time to nanophotonic inverse design, accelerating evaluation of the forward problem by multiple orders of magnitude with no loss in accuracy compared to the full-wave solution. After a single, fully parallelizable precomputation step, both the objective function and its gradient can be evaluated through simple calculations whose cost scales linearly with the size of the design region. A low-rank matrix update technique further reduces the cost of objective function evaluation, yielding sub-millisecond computation times per iteration. Design examples using both gradient-based level-set optimization and tile-flipping direct binary search often achieve more than three orders of magnitude speedup in design time, resulting in an ultrafast photonic inverse design platform that can design new devices from scratch in seconds.

title: Comment on "Is there a density-gradient expansion for the electronic exchange energy?"
text:
Title: Comment on "Is there a density-gradient expansion for the electronic exchange energy?"
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Perdew et al. [arXiv:2610.07201 (2026)] dispute our finding [Phys. Rev. B 113, 115136 (2026)] that the separate exchange ($b_x$) and correlation ($b_c$) contributions to the $q^2$ coefficient of the long-wavelength proper polarization function depend on the infrared regularization of the Coulomb interaction, although their sum $b_{xc}=b_x+b_c$ does not. We question their claim that the conventional exchange coefficient is uniquely determined. In Qian's [J. Math. Phys. 56, 111901 (2015)] derivation, which Perdew et al. cite in support of their claim of a unique exchange-gradient coefficient, an integral of the form $\int_{-a}^{b}dx/x$ crosses a singularity and does not exist as an ordinary improper integral. Its finite Cauchy principal value (which is a particular way of regularizing the integral) is obtained only by excluding equal intervals on the two sides of the singularity; unequal exclusions give different answers. Independently, Sham's calculation with the screened interaction $e^{-λ_0 r}/r$ gives an exchange-gradient coefficient different from the bare-Coulomb calculations of Svendsen--von Barth [Int. J. Quantum Chem. 56, 351 (1995)] and Engel--Vosko [Phys. Rev. B 42, 4940 (1990)]. The discrepancy remains when $λ_0>0$ is so small that $1/λ_0$ is comparable to the size of the observable universe, making the two interactions experimentally indistinguishable on laboratory scales. Why should the exactly unscreened result be preferred, even if its calculation is accepted as valid? Our calculation shows that the ambiguity of the separate contributions cancels in the combined, regulator-independent coefficient $b_{xc}$.

title: Generation and spectroscopic characterization of continuous-wave 148.4-nm light in strontium tetraborate
text:
Title: Generation and spectroscopic characterization of continuous-wave 148.4-nm light in strontium tetraborate
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Continuous-wave (CW) radiation at 148.4~nm is required to drive the $^{229}$Th isomeric transition of a solid-state nuclear clock, and frequency doubling of 296.8-nm light is its most direct source. We generate CW 148.4-nm light by random quasi-phase matching in strontium tetraborate and characterize it with a compact CaF$_2$ prism spectrometer, which reaches picowatt sensitivity without filters or a grating and reads the wavelength from the rotation angle of a solar-blind photomultiplier. The observed harmonic profile has an angular FWHM of 0.36$^{\circ}$, corresponding to a convolution-limited spectral width of about 0.6 nm rather than the intrinsic linewidth. The directly estimated output is 1.9 nW at room temperature; scaling the measured temperature dependence gives an inferred 4.8 nW at the best observed temperature. The conversion varies by an order of magnitude across the crystal and is strongly structured in temperature: between 30 $^{\circ}$C and 50 $^{\circ}$C it shows several maxima only a few degrees apart, so a small excursion moves the output from a maximum to a minimum. These measurements provide valuable information on the realization and characterization of a high-quality 148.4-nm light source, and pave the way for the future development of high-performance nuclear optical clocks.

title: Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
text:
Title: Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We reformulate two-dimensional conformal field theory (2d CFT) in the language of noncommutative geometry. To this end, we introduce automorphic forms for the von Neumann algebraic quantum group $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. A quantum measure space is a von Neumann algebra equipped with a weight. We study such spaces carrying a weight-preserving action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. We argue that every unitary bosonic 2d CFT with central charge $c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2>1$ is equivalent to a quantum measure space with an action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})\times\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. In this dictionary, Virasoro primary operators are quantum automorphic forms and their scaling dimensions correspond to the spectrum of a quantum Laplace operator. The Virasoro crossing equations express associativity of multiplication on the quantum measure space. For compact theories, the algebra is a type III$_1$ factor. Liouville CFT is realized as $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$ acting on itself by left and right translations. Virasoro boundary conditions correspond to quantum measure spaces with an action of a single copy of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. When the boundary spectrum is discrete, these are noncommutative counterparts of compact hyperbolic surfaces. The formulation accommodates models both with and without extended chiral algebras. It bridges the Virasoro conformal bootstrap with categorical and von Neumann algebraic approaches to 2d CFT.

title: Hydrogen Thermodiffusion in Tungsten: Trapped Hydrogen Distorts Heat of Transport Estimation from Total Concentration Profiles
text:
Title: Hydrogen Thermodiffusion in Tungsten: Trapped Hydrogen Distorts Heat of Transport Estimation from Total Concentration Profiles
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We investigate hydrogen diffusion in tungsten under thermal gradients in the presence of trapping sites using multiscale simulations. Using molecular dynamics simulations, we find that the heat of transport, which quantifies the coupling between temperature gradients and hydrogen transport, for hydrogen in tungsten is positive (thermophobic) at lower temperatures but changes sign near $1000$ K. We investigate the origin of the heat of transport and find that harmonic transition state theory with elastic thermal-expansion corrections is insufficient to explain the observed behaviour, consistent with either a breakdown of local thermodynamic equilibrium or non-negligible anharmonic contributions. We further extend previous studies of hydrogen thermodiffusion by including the effect of trapping sites in both simulations and analytical models. We show that when trapped hydrogen accounts for a significant fraction of the total hydrogen concentration, the heat of transport inferred from measurements of the total concentration is dominated by the temperature dependence of the trapped hydrogen population and no longer reflects the gradient in the mobile hydrogen concentration. Consequently, experimentally measured heats of transport cannot in general be used directly in continuum-scale models that explicitly account for trapping and detrapping. In such models, the heat of transport should be based on mobile hydrogen concentrations only to avoid incorporating trapping effects twice.

title: Can AI Agents Reliably Optimize Computational Chemistry Codes?
text:
Title: Can AI Agents Reliably Optimize Computational Chemistry Codes?
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches have opened new possibilities in computational and theoretical chemistry. AI agents can now execute computational workflows autonomously, and their use in scientific software development represents another promising direction. Herein, we present a general strategy for the controlled optimization of scientific software using a dual-agent harness. By using separate worker and controller agents for optimization and evaluation, respectively, we find that this approach can reduce computational costs while preserving numerical accuracy for the computational chemistry methods examined. We apply this strategy to TIP4P water simulations in LAMMPS, as well as to Coulomb and exchange matrix construction and linear-response time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations in PySCF. Among these applications, the largest speedups are obtained for TDDFT. We then extend this strategy from optimizing established packages to developing efficient parallel CPU- and GPU-accelerated implementations of an initially serial molecular dynamics code, resulting in speedups of two to three orders of magnitude. Finally, we apply the protocol to open-ended algorithm development by constructing an adaptive self-consistent field approach that coordinates the use of multiple solvers. We find that the resulting approach can converge some challenging systems and occasionally reach lower-energy solutions than those obtained with the standalone solvers tested. These applications demonstrate that a strategy developed for improving code efficiency may also support the systematic development of computational methods. Overall, our benchmark study provides an example of AI-assisted advances in computational chemistry.

title: CV-TF-QKD
text:
Title: CV-TF-QKD
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We introduce a continuous-variable version of twin-field quantum key distribution, using independent Gaussian-modulated coherent states and an untrusted single-photon relay. Full-record reconciliation and a binary phase-disclosure protocol achieve nearly equal asymptotic key rates against collective attacks. At fixed weak input-referred excess noise per arm, both rates per relay use scale as $\sqrtη$, where $η$ is the end-to-end transmissivity. For phase disclosure, we establish composable security against general coherent attacks using a bounded test of preparation intensities and sign-parity complementarity. For specified apparatus parameters, finite-key calculations incorporating detector inefficiency, dark counts, phase fluctuations, and reference overhead predict rates exceeding the pure-loss and matched thermal-loss repeaterless bounds. These results extend the twin-field advantage to Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum cryptography.

title: The Multi-trace Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
text:
Title: The Multi-trace Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We introduce a multi-trace eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, an extension of ETH that governs connected correlations of operator matrix elements with arbitrary index structures, including several disjoint index cycles. We derive multi-trace ETH from local rotational invariance, relate its independent data to higher-order free cumulants, and construct a cyclic matrix model that encodes the resulting multi-cycle data. We provide evidence for multi-trace ETH in chaotic quantum systems and compute multi-trace correlations in low-dimensional gravity. In few-body systems, multi-trace contributions arise from correlated periodic orbits, including a linear ramp contribution to the one-point spectral form factor. In two dimensions, we compute interaction-induced multi-trace correlations from a quartically coupled bulk scalar in JT gravity, relating winding matter diagrams to corrections of matter-channel weights and anomalous dimensions. In three dimensions, we show that multi-trace non-Gaussianities arise from both topology-changing saddles and light matter. Using Virasoro TQFT and conformal mean-field theory, we compute examples involving knot and link complements and torus wormholes with matter loops. Across these settings, multi-trace ETH provides a common framework for both connected correlators in chaotic quantum systems and multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes in gravity.

title: One Temperature to Rule Them All?
text:
Title: One Temperature to Rule Them All?
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Inference-time sampling is a central mechanism for improving large language models, with temperature controlling the tradeoff between reliability and diversity. While recent work suggests that varying temperature across samples can improve multi-sample inference, simple fixed-temperature schemes remain the standard in practice. We investigate this discrepancy in the canonical pass@K setting, asking when temperature diversity is useful, and when a single tuned temperature suffices. To this end, we analyze per-question success probabilities across multiple models and datasets, tracking how they vary with sampling temperature. We identify several consistent properties of these profiles, including that harder questions are less likely to share efficient sampling temperatures, although this trend is only logarithmic in hardness. We then derive an efficient method for evaluating the theoretically optimal multi-temperature allocation scheme, and show that although such a scheme improves performance, its gains over single-temperature baselines are typically modest when temperature is tuned as a function of the sampling budget K. We explain this phenomenon through mathematical mechanisms that we call dulling effects, and show how they ensure the robustness of temperature choices across different question distributions. Our results clarify when multi-temperature sampling is useful, and how temperatures should ideally be chosen.

title: A Telescopic Method with Guaranteed B-Stationarity for Partitioned Cardinality and Complementarity Constraints
text:
Title: A Telescopic Method with Guaranteed B-Stationarity for Partitioned Cardinality and Complementarity Constraints
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We consider the minimization of a smooth function subject to box constraints and partitioned cardinality constraints (PCC): the variables are divided into groups and, within each group, at most a prescribed number of variables may be non-zero. This class contains bound-constrained minimization, cardinality-constrained minimization and bound-constrained mathematical programs with complementarity constraints. We introduce the Telescopic Method, which alternates iterations of a bound-constrained method on the faces of the feasible set with inexpensive one-dimensional "escaping" tests that exchange a variable of the current face by a currently null one within the same group. We prove, without constraint qualifications and without requiring global solutions of subproblems, that every limit point of the generated sequence is B-stationary, i.e., it satisfies the first-order condition defined by the tangent cone of the feasible set. This guarantee is obtained with exchanges of a single variable, whatever the number of non-null entries of the limit point, because B-stationarity for this class of problems decomposes into conditions on single variables. On the 60 bound-constrained mathematical programs with complementarity constraints of the test set of Kirches, Larson, Leyffer and Manns, the method found approximately B-stationary points in all the problems. Applications to separable regression, sparse polynomial approximation and portfolio selection are described and tested numerically.

title: A Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Free-Energy Surface for the First Step of MIL-101(Cr) Secondary Building Unit Formation
text:
Title: A Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Free-Energy Surface for the First Step of MIL-101(Cr) Secondary Building Unit Formation
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Metal-organic framework (MOF) self-assembly mechanisms remain poorly characterized because ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) are accurate but too computationally expensive to converge the free-energy surfaces (FES) that govern secondary building unit (SBU) nucleation and growth. This work addresses that limitation for the first step of MIL-101(Cr) SBU formation. Using MACE-POLAR-M, a long-range-aware equivariant machine-learned interatomic potential fine-tuned on a compact DFT reference dataset built from exploratory metadynamics, this work obtains a converged 2D FES for this step at a level of theory (ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPP) at which AIMD would be prohibitively expensive. The pre-trained model samples relevant configurations but gets the thermodynamics wrong, predicting an endothermic reaction and a false global minimum. Fine-tuning corrects both, recovering the expected exothermic process and the correct product basin in agreement with proposed literature mechanisms. The resulting FES also refines the mechanism. It shows that water release from the chromium center proceeds stepwise, through two sequential energy barriers, rather than the single concerted step originally proposed. We find that model accuracy is specific to the reaction coordinate and does not extend to the dissociated fragment configurations excluded from fine-tuning, a direct consequence of the training-data choice that protects accuracy along the reaction path for the FES prediction task. Together, these results establish a validated, computationally tractable route to obtain free-energy surfaces for MOF formation chemistry, transferable to other reactions where AIMD remains prohibitive, and identify training-data composition as the key determinant of which reaction properties a fine-tuned checkpoint can reliably describe.

title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
text:
Title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. Region-aware reference selection improves masked PSNR by 3.60 dB over recency when candidate references can themselves be occluded. Reference-age analysis further defines the operating interval for the brief, repeated occlusions targeted by TransGHOST.

title: AuDiR: Diagnosing Audio Reasoning with Rule and Percept Interventions
text:
Title: AuDiR: Diagnosing Audio Reasoning with Rule and Percept Interventions
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Answer accuracy alone does not distinguish failures in acoustic perception, rule knowledge, and rule application. AuDiR (Audio Diagnostic Reasoning) examines these distinctions through controlled input interventions. Each item contains an audio clip, a multiple-choice question, a task-general rule, and a textual description of the acoustic observations needed to answer. Three conditions progressively supply the rule and observations; a fourth removes the audio while retaining the question and rule. The first correct diagnostic condition assigns an operational response label, without identifying a unique internal cause. The current benchmark contains 201 items in 18 families drawn from 9 sources, with answer references documented separately from percept extraction. In a preliminary evaluation of Gemini-3.8-flash, accuracy is 29.3% without supplied information, 31.3% with the rule, and 98.5% with the observations also supplied. No-audio accuracy is 23.9%, with a confidence interval containing the 25.0% chance rate. A family-level knowledge probe associates incomplete rule recall with larger gains from rule provision. These results show the benefit of supplying acoustic observations as text, while incomplete validation, possible recognition shortcuts, and non-monotonic responses limit stronger failure-attribution claims.

title: Pricing Today, Shaping Tomorrow: Contextual Dynamic Pricing in Purchase-Driven Evolving Systems
text:
Title: Pricing Today, Shaping Tomorrow: Contextual Dynamic Pricing in Purchase-Driven Evolving Systems
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Across diverse markets, it is important for firms to balance attracting customers with managing operational conditions, such as workloads and delivery times. Dynamic pricing plays a central role in this tradeoff, as the orders generated today can change the conditions faced by future customers. We develop a novel framework for contextual dynamic pricing with an observed shared state and unknown purchase-driven transitions. The valuation model allows unknown mean functions of customer covariates and state, unknown state-specific scales and a common unknown standardized noise distribution. We propose Shadow-Adjusted Pricing in Evolving Systems (SHAPE), which incorporates a purchase's future revenue consequences into current pricing. Purchase-shadow adjustment and scale standardization reveal a common one-dimensional oracle price map across states, allowing SHAPE to retain its pricing history across value updates without repeating coarse exploration. The same active sales records support price-map learning and joint updates of continuation values and purchase shadows, without fitting the noise distribution or full transition matrices. To support this reuse under purchase-driven feedback, we establish pricing guarantees for history-dependent inputs and stability bounds for the joint updates. Under regularity, coverage and design conditions, we obtain sublinear expected regret against a finite-horizon dynamic oracle for linear, Hölder and sparse linear mean models. For affine valuations at fixed state and feature dimensions, SHAPE matches the static semiparametric minimax time exponent up to logarithmic factors for every fixed noise-tail smoothness order $β\ge2$. Numerical experiments further demonstrate the appealing performance of SHAPE.

title: Shadow Molecular Dynamics for General Nonlinear Flexible-Charge Models
text:
Title: Shadow Molecular Dynamics for General Nonlinear Flexible-Charge Models
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Machine-learned interatomic potentials have greatly expanded the reach of molecular dynamics simulations, but complex chemical environments often require explicit treatment of long-range electronic response, including charge transfer and polarization. Physics-based flexible-charge models capture these effects but require global nonlinear charge equilibration at every time step to obtain Born-Oppenheimer energies and forces. This process is computationally expensive and can lead to instabilities unless tightly converged. Here, we introduce a shadow molecular dynamics framework for flexible-charge models with arbitrary local nonlinearities and long-range multipolar electrostatics. We replace the exact Born-Oppenheimer potential with a nearby shadow potential obtained by exactly equilibrating a partially linearized electronic energy functional. This provides conservative forces and reduces the global nonlinear equilibration to a quasi-diagonal linear problem that can be solved directly at low cost. Auxiliary dynamical electronic degrees of freedom, propagated through an extended-Lagrangian dynamics, capture the long-range electronic response and define the reference state for the linearization of the energy functional. GPU-accelerated simulations with over 100,000 atoms demonstrate that the shadow potential closely follows the tightly converged Born-Oppenheimer surface, while maintaining long-term stability at a computational cost approaching that of a fixed-charge model. These advances establish an efficient and broadly applicable framework for machine-learned interatomic potentials that explicitly incorporate long-range electrostatic interactions and environment-dependent electronic response.

title: A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration
text:
Title: A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Single precision (FP32) halves the memory and data movement of double precision (FP64), and on accelerators is often several times faster. Its rounding errors are harmless except in the stored state. A modified equation for Runge-Kutta methods in Shu-Osher form and linear multistep methods separates the rounding of the stored state, a forcing proportional to $1/Δt$, from truncation and from right-hand-side rounding, which sets a $Δt$-independent floor. We bound this forcing for strong-stability-preserving schemes and identify two mechanisms that keep its sign fixed, so it accumulates as a bias: past a turnaround step, refining the step increases the error, in FP64 as in FP32. For a model oscillator the analysis predicts the floor and the FP32-to-FP64 ratios of turnaround step and minimum error within 30%. Our remedy needs no FP64 arithmetic: each state variable is stored as the unevaluated sum of two FP32 numbers, updated with error-free transformations, while every right-hand-side evaluation stays in FP32. Unlike compensated summation, it needs no rewriting of the scheme. In model problems from geophysical flow, mechanical dynamics and celestial mechanics, with five Runge-Kutta and multistep schemes, it restores design-order convergence to the floor. In large-eddy simulations of a high-lift airplane wing on three refined grids, up to 544 million cells, with time steps $Δt$, $Δt/2$ and $Δt/4$, FP32 overpredicts the lift by 2.1, 4.5 and 7.7%, while the two-float lift agrees with FP64 within 0.3% on every grid, and on graphics processing units the production solver runs 1.6 to 2.7 times faster than FP64.

title: APO2CS: Advantage-Aware Preference Optimization for Two-Level Constructive Search in Combinatorial Optimization
text:
Title: APO2CS: Advantage-Aware Preference Optimization for Two-Level Constructive Search in Combinatorial Optimization
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Preference optimization has emerged as a promising alternative to reward-based training for neural combinatorial optimization. However, existing methods typically rely on binary pairwise labels, which discard the magnitude of solution-quality differences and provide supervision only at the complete-solution level. We propose Advantage-aware Preference Optimization for Two-level Constructive Search (APO2CS), a preference-based training objective for constructive neural solvers that integrates both macro-level and micro-level supervision. At the macro level, APO2CS enriches pairwise preferences with an advantage term derived from objective-value differences. At the micro level, it compares partial trajectories, thereby providing denser supervision throughout the sequential construction process. The resulting objective can be used either to train a policy from scratch or to fine-tune a pretrained one. Experimental results show that APO2CS improves the expressiveness and search capability of preference learning for combinatorial optimization, while demonstrating strong effectiveness and adaptability across multiple combinatorial optimization tasks.

title: Universal Loop Statistics from Active Extrusion with Kinetic Barriers
text:
Title: Universal Loop Statistics from Active Extrusion with Kinetic Barriers
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

We develop a kinetic theory of cohesin-driven loop extrusion on a disordered chromatin track with transient barriers. In the stationary state, the mean loop size is shown to obey a universal law determined by the bare processivity and a renormalized obstacle density. Beyond the mean, one-sided extrusion always yields a single-exponential loop-length distribution, whereas two-sided extrusion produces a finite sum of exponential modes and, generically, a peaked distribution. Experimental CTCF-anchored loop statistics exhibit such a peak, thereby providing a direct discriminator of extrusion symmetry. The theory therefore establishes a unified framework for disorder-limited loop extrusion and supports a scenario in which both cohesin arms actively operate in living cells.

title: Scaling laws for linear-elastic two-variant martensitic phase transitions in general domains
text:
Title: Scaling laws for linear-elastic two-variant martensitic phase transitions in general domains
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We consider a two-well problem within geometrically linear elasticity, on a bounded Lipschitz set in dimension $n\ge 2$. We assume that the two wells are compatible through a symmetrized rank-one connection and that the displacement matches their average on the boundary, and we include a regularization based on the total surface energy. We show that there are two distinct regimes, with the energy scaling differently in terms of the surface-energy coefficient $\eps$: it is proportional to $\eps^{2/3}$ if there are two distinct compatible twin-normal directions, and to $\eps^{4/5}$ if there is only one. This matches previous findings in rectangles and other special geometries, mostly in two dimensions, and the lower bounds obtained by a Fourier method by Raiţă, Rüland, Tissot and Tribuzio (2024). Our results are obtained by explicit constructions, which contain a self-similar refinement of oscillations close to the boundary, and by a short real-space proof of the matching lower bounds.

title: Demystifying Multimodal Biomolecular Co-design With Intrinsic Geodesic Coupling
text:
Title: Demystifying Multimodal Biomolecular Co-design With Intrinsic Geodesic Coupling
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Biomolecules such as proteins and small-molecule ligands play a central role in biological systems, arising from the tight interplay between sequence and three-dimensional structure. Recent generative models for biomolecular co-design aim to capture this interplay by jointly modeling coupled modalities. However, existing approaches largely adopt a parallel execution of marginal generative processes, implicitly enforcing fixed synchronous coupling. We argue that a critical but overlooked degree of freedom lies in how these marginal processes are temporally coupled during training and generation, where inappropriate coupling can introduce high-variance supervision and inconsistent intermediate states, affecting modality consistency. To address this, we introduce GeoCoupling, a systematic framework that optimizes for temporal couplings between heterogeneous modalities. Empirical results across structure-based drug design and unconditional protein design demonstrate the learned couplings consistently outperform synchronous and randomly coupled baselines, yielding biomolecules with improved physical validity and diversity.

title: Multireference perturbation theory with nonorthogonal determinants
text:
Title: Multireference perturbation theory with nonorthogonal determinants
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We introduce NOCI-RSPT, a framework for constructing perturb-then-diagonalize multireference perturbation theories for model spaces defined by nonorthogonal determinants. NOCI-RSPT realizes order-by-order size consistency by orthogonalizing the effective Hamiltonian before perturbatively truncating it and removes problematic internal excitations through model-space projection. The resulting second- and third-order theories, NOCI-RS2 and NOCI-RS3, recover MP2 and MP3 in the single-reference limit and exhibit the same respective cost scaling at fixed model-space size. Calculations on assemblies of multireference $\mathrm{H}_2$ fragments demonstrate size consistency, while calculations of the low-energy states of $\mathrm{H}_2$ along its dissociation curve demonstrate improved numerical stability and characterize the influence of intruder states. The latter calculations demonstrate the exceptional accuracy achieved by NOCI-RS3 and illustrate how model-space expansion and amplitude regularization can mitigate the effects of large perturbative corrections. Altogether, NOCI-RSPT provides a systematic route to low-scaling multireference perturbation theories built from single-reference methods.

title: The Price of Scale in Proactive Memory Recall
text:
Title: The Price of Scale in Proactive Memory Recall
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

A long-lived assistant that brings up memories without being asked must decide at every turn whether anything in its store is worth an interruption. We show that this decision is a multiple-testing problem whose difficulty grows with the store size N. On replays of LongMemEval, a similarity threshold tuned to 5% false alarms at N=8 reaches 84-100% at N=2048 across embedding models and cue types; LoCoMo and LLM judges show it too. We prove that a gate which thresholds the best of N independent irrelevant scores at false-alarm rate alpha operates at a per-item false-positive rate of about -ln(1-alpha)/N, which pins its hit rate to the far left of the ROC and makes it regularly varying in N under regular variation. Replayed hit rates stay within its bounds for mixed cues up to 0.3 points, and hit rates carry over to held-out questions to within 6.0 points. At matched false alarms the deployed score recalls 14-26 points more than raw cosine. A cue-swap conformal gate, which ranks the current cue among other cues on the same store, has a finite-sample false-alarm guarantee under exchangeability. With a background from the user's unfiltered history it keeps false alarms at 3-6% on LongMemEval at the hit rate of a label-tuned threshold; on LoCoMo it overshoots or turns conservative depending on the source of its reference cues. In a chronological replay with the user's own earlier messages as references, it fires on 5-8% of questions on stores without their answer and on 6-8% of session-opening turns, against 57% for the deployed gate at N=2048, at a median 0.4 s CPU per decision. A cross-encoder pays the same price of scale, and on a prospective-memory benchmark, similarity gates recall at most 9% of constraints at controlled false alarms. One human and two LLM annotators judge most false alarms unhelpful for a response. Code and data: https://github.com/RiverChenStillCompiling/price-of-scale

title: Electron Scattering with ASTRA: Helium and Molecular Hydrogen
text:
Title: Electron Scattering with ASTRA: Helium and Molecular Hydrogen
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We present an implementation of electron-impact scattering in ASTRA, a close-coupling method based on transition density matrices previously applied to molecular photoionization. The scattering states are obtained with a pole-free Galerkin method with variational surface matching, which yields the scattering matrix and the channel-resolved amplitudes for elastic and electronically inelastic integral cross sections and molecular-frame differential cross sections. For helium, ASTRA reproduces elastic and inelastic cross sections over a broad energy range, resolves the He$^-$(1s2s$^2$ $^2$S$^e$) Feshbach resonance in both energy and angle, and captures the principal interference structures in the n=2 excitation angular distributions, in selected channels matching measured differential-cross-section ratios more closely than available benchmark calculations. For molecular hydrogen, target polarization and interchannel coupling are represented through additional close-coupling channels, without a fitted polarization potential or a separately constructed (N+1)-electron correlation space. Compared with the restricted-channel description, the expanded calculations substantially improve agreement with UKRmol+ for elastic and inelastic cross sections. We further report fully orientation-resolved three-dimensional molecular-frame angular distributions for state-resolved electron-impact excitation. These reveal pronounced stereodynamic effects that vanish upon orientational averaging: at 15 eV, excitation of the b$^3Σ_u^+$ state is more than eight times stronger for incident momentum parallel rather than perpendicular to the molecular axis. These results connect conventional scattering benchmarks with orientation-resolved collision dynamics and open the way to larger molecular targets.

title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
text:
Title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Symmetry governs the organization of physical structures, while symmetry breaking reveals their transformations. In geometric deep learning, symmetry imposes rank constraints on equivariant representations, limiting the expressive capacity of equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs). Here we show that these constraints can instead be exploited: the singular-value spectra of equivariant representations provide a unified fingerprint of structural symmetry. We introduce spectral symmetry fingerprints (SymFP), which enable discrete point-group identification through rank-template matching and continuous symmetry analysis by quantifying spectral energy beyond target rank constraints. SymFP is orientation invariant and architecture agnostic, enabling a parameter-free GNN implementation. Its spectra can be reused across multiple target groups, and the resulting leakage scores satisfy subgroup monotonicity. Across synthetic structures, molecules, coordination complexes and large biological assemblies, SymFP accurately identifies point groups, tracks controlled symmetry breaking and reveals local and degree-resolved symmetry changes that can be obscured by global geometric measures. These results establish the spectral structure of equivariant representations as a general framework for characterizing symmetry across physical systems.

title: Large Language Models without QK-Normalization
text:
Title: Large Language Models without QK-Normalization
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Query-Key Normalization (QK-Norm) is widely adopted in modern large language models to control the growth of attention logits and improve training stability. However, query and key norms are not merely sources of instability. The query norm controls the sharpness of the attention distribution, while the key norm determines how strongly a token attracts different queries. These norms therefore carry token-specific information about attention selectivity and token importance. By normalizing both, QK-Norm suppresses this information. This raises a natural question: can we control query-key representations without discarding their sensitivity to magnitude? To address this question, we propose QK-MAP, a Magnitude-Aware Projection for constructing queries and keys. Rather than removing magnitude through normalization, QK-MAP transforms the input representation using multiple learnable frequencies, so that changes in magnitude are encoded as bounded phase patterns. This allows magnitude to be represented through phase and direction rather than vector length alone. Its periodic features have a fixed norm while remaining sensitive to magnitude changes, separating magnitude encoding from norm growth. Multiple frequencies further help distinguish magnitudes and reduce periodic ambiguity. Experiments across model scales from 190M to 7B parameters show that QK-MAP achieves lower training and validation loss than both Standard attention and QK-Norm. Further analyses show that QK-MAP preserves sensitivity to input scale, assigns less attention to the first token, and produces stronger attention contrast for relevant evidence in synthetic long-context tests. These results demonstrate that query-key scale can be effectively controlled without sacrificing token-specific magnitude information.

title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
text:
Title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Protein foundation models increasingly support the generation of novel biological sequences, yet their reliance on large public datasets creates opportunities for adversarial manipulation of the material they learn from and retrieve. We investigate two data-only poisoning attacks against protein design systems, targeting the pre-training corpus of autoregressive protein language models and the retrieval corpus of a text-guided protein generator. For the first, we pre-trained ProtGPT2 and ProGen2 variants of 300 million parameters, introducing poisoned protein sequences containing one of two triggers followed by one of three payloads. Across all poisoned runs, both architectures acquired highly reliable trigger-dependent generation under uniform and ramped poisoning schedules. Under ramped exposure, the earliest majority activation occurred after only 200 contaminated examples, while for the uniform schedule earliest activation occurred around 5000 poisoned samples. For the second attack, we inserted records into a retrieval corpus system without modifying its weights or decoding procedure. A single query-aware record captured a top-16 retrieval position for 58\% of templated requests and 97\% of free-text requests. Conditional on successful poisoned retrieval, 62\% of requests produced altered sequences, while 19-21% acquired the inserted domain by profile-HMM homology. A universal query-unaware attack using 1,500 records also achieved substantial retrieval capture and domain transfer. Together, these findings demonstrate that adversarial protein sequence contributions can establish persistent, sequence-specific behaviour during pre-training or redirect protein generation at inference, while leaving ordinary model behaviour largely preserved. Our work establishes the integrity and biological provenance of protein sequence data as critical safeguards for generative protein design systems.

title: The Geometry of Simulated Perspectives: Dissociating Representation and Behaviour in a Multimodal Language Model
text:
Title: The Geometry of Simulated Perspectives: Dissociating Representation and Behaviour in a Multimodal Language Model
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Multimodal language models can simulate different observers, yet it remains unclear how assigned perspectives reshape their internal representations and whether these changes govern their judgements. Here, we investigate the representational geometry of persona-conditioned visual interestingness in Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. Across 100 images and 53 prompting conditions, we systematically vary persona content and the linguistic framing used to introduce it, while recording behavioural ratings and layer-wise hidden states. We observe a systematic reorganisation of representational geometry across processing depth: early layers primarily encode image identity, whereas persona-specific structures emerge in later layers. Strikingly, prompt framing reshapes internal representations more strongly than persona identity, whereas persona content has a greater impact on behavioural judgements. This dissociation is further illustrated by minimal identity statements that alter representations even without changing responses. These findings demonstrate that representational distance does not necessarily reflect behavioural relevance. More broadly, they reveal how simulated perspectives emerge as distinct structures within the representational space of artificial cognitive systems, highlighting a fundamental distinction between the geometry of internal representations and their functional consequences.

title: Impropriety and resilience of the chromatic number
text:
Title: Impropriety and resilience of the chromatic number
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We show that, for $p$ bounded away from $1$ and $np\to\infty$, the chromatic number of the binomial random graph $G_{n,p}$ is resilient to removal of a subgraph $H$ with $o(n \log(np))$ edges. It follows that the same assertion holds with $H$ being a subgraph of maximum degree $o(\log(np))$; and both these results are best possible up to a constant factor. We also prove corresponding results for the random $r$-regular graph $G_{n,r}$, when $r\to\infty$ and $r/n$ is bounded away from $1$, where $H$ has $o(n\log r)$ edges or maximum degree $o(\log r)$. Our results rely on a natural connection between chromatic resilience to edge removal and improper graph colouring. This work provides counterpoint to the work of Sudakov and Vu (2008) and Alon and Sudakov (2010), which treated chromatic resilience for $G_{n,p}$ subject to the addition, rather than removal, of edges.

title: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
text:
Title: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The next generation of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys are designed to measure hundreds of millions of galaxy and quasar spectra, extending precision large-scale-structure cosmology to redshifts and volumes well beyond the reach of current Stage-IV facilities. Realising this potential requires revisiting the target selection strategies and designing them explicitly around the depth, multiplexing, and survey time of the new instruments, rather than a direct extrapolation of existing recipes. This work develops and characterises new strategies for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST), a proposed 12-metre, highly multiplexed facility expected to operate in the 2040s. Using deep multi-band photometry, including COSMOS-field data from CLAUDS and HSC, we revisit low-redshift $z \lesssim 1.6$ tracer selection of SDSS, BOSS/eBOSS, DESI and 4MOST-CRS -- Bright Galaxies, Luminous Red Galaxies, Emission Line Galaxies and quasars -- to photometric depth achievable in the WST era, and introduce a purely magnitude-limited sample (MagMax) exploiting three-dimensional color-color star-galaxy separation, and a set of Lyman-Break Galaxy dropout samples extending target selection to $z \gtrsim 2$. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, we showcase the constraining power of a WST-like cosmological survey on BAO distance parameters $α_\parallel$ and $α_\perp$, the growth rate $f$, the evolving dark energy equation $w_0w_a$, the local-type primordial non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}$, and the sum of the neutrino mass $Σm_ν$. The main outcome of this work is an optimisation framework that directly links instrumental capabilities and observing time to cosmological constraining power, providing a science-driven template applicable to the design of future generations of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys.

title: Detuning-Controlled Vibrational Autler--Townes Passage toward Single-Sublevel Orientation of Nonpolar Molecules
text:
Title: Detuning-Controlled Vibrational Autler--Townes Passage toward Single-Sublevel Orientation of Nonpolar Molecules
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Single-sublevel preparation would give collision and surface-scattering experiments access to oriented molecules, yet established orientation methods either require a permanent dipole moment or select only partially. We introduce all-optical Autler--Townes state-selective adiabatic passage (ASAP), in which a detuned infrared field dresses a rovibrational transition, and the selected dressed branch is mapped adiabatically onto one magnetic sublevel as the field vanishes. We resolve the magnetic-sublevel-selected rovibrational Autler--Townes doublet of the R(0) transition of $^{13}$CO$_2$ and show that the coupling strength and detuning set both its separation and the partition of the bare-state composition between its two components. The spectral selectivity of the target dressed branch reaches 97\% at a coupling detuning of $-1.2$~MHz. A density-matrix model calibrated against these spectra returns, for the dressed molecules, a target-sublevel population approaching 0.9 over a broad range of coupling powers and detunings.

title: Debate, Not Voting: Agentic Arbitration over Weak Optical Chemical Structure Recognition Models
text:
Title: Debate, Not Voting: Agentic Arbitration over Weak Optical Chemical Structure Recognition Models
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Optical chemical structure recognition (OCSR) turns a picture of a molecule into a machine-readable string, and it stands between decades of printed chemistry and any computational use. On real documents individual models remain unreliable. Over a 1000-molecule sample of MolParser, three readers score $46.0\%$, $43.4\%$ and $42.4\%$ exact match, yet at least one of them is right on $60.8\%$ of molecules. That gap is an ensembling problem, but not one voting can solve, because the readers seldom agree and seldom err together. We place the readers inside a multi-agent scaffold. Four language-model agents with cheminformatics tools argue about a candidate structure, write findings to an append-only knowledge base, and are held to render-and-compare gates that admit a correction only when it is demonstrably better. The debate reaches $61.9\%$, beating the best single reader by $15.9$ points and plurality voting by $9.2$ points ($p<10^{-9}$ for both, robust to correction for all $27$ tests we report), and is indistinguishable from the any-reader-right ceiling. That aggregate hides two opposing effects. On the $661$ molecules with no stereochemistry the debate is $3.9$ points above the ceiling ($p=0.004$), constructing structures no reader proposed, while on the $339$ stereochemical ones it falls below. We then swap the arbitrating model. A stronger arbitrator adds $2.2$ points (nominal $p=0.039$; neither this nor the $+3.9$ survives Bonferroni correction over all $27$ tests, so both are suggestive), and its mechanism is visible: it opens a correction on $423$ of $1000$ molecules against $120$, and an interaction test indicates it depends less on the readers (nominal $p=0.018$, not correction-robust). We conclude that the useful unit of progress is the arbitration policy rather than the reader, and that OCSR accuracy is better read against the union oracle than against the best single model.

title: Integrating Data Center Flexibility into Power System Operations: A Framework for Temporal Redispatch
text:
Title: Integrating Data Center Flexibility into Power System Operations: A Framework for Temporal Redispatch
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Rapid growth in data center electricity demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) training and inference, is expected to increase stress conditions for power grids. Operational flexibility from data centers offers a near-term lever to relieve such stresses. Existing models of data center flexibility tend to bundle economic incentives with physical constraints, obscuring the tradeoff between economic willingness to shift load and technical limitations to do so. This paper proposes a temporal-redispatch focused framework that decouples data center demand flexibility into two independently parameterized dimensions: (1) systematic flexibility, capturing the economic environment through penalties for temporal shifting of data centers' scheduled demand, and (2) operational flexibility, capturing the physical envelope through the demand shifting time window and the limit on shifted data center demand. The framework relies on a direct current optimal power flow (DC-OPF) linear program which enables annual parametric analysis at hourly resolution. The framework is studied using a synthetic grid mimicking the Texas transmission system populated with the 2026 Adjusted Forecast from ERCOT (Electric Reliability Council of Texas). Results show that operational flexibility imposes a physical lower bound on unsatisfied demand that no economic incentive can overcome; longer shifting windows and higher limits on shifted data center demand reduce operational cost with different impacts on grid utilization; and, temporal redispatch shaves system-wide net load peaks while partially compensating for localized transmission bottlenecks that emerge under modeled coal retirement scenarios.

title: YRC-Bench: Benchmarking Culturally Aware Machine Translation for Historical Heritage via Tri-Level Semantic Bridging
text:
Title: YRC-Bench: Benchmarking Culturally Aware Machine Translation for Historical Heritage via Tri-Level Semantic Bridging
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Translating historical cultural heritage poses profound challenges for machine translation systems due to the acute semantic asymmetry across eras and cultures, where terse classical syntax frequently obscures domain-specific cultural knowledge. While Large Language Models have demonstrated remarkable prowess in generic translation benchmarks, they struggle to negotiate Culturally-Specific Items and diachronic shifts in domain-rich historical texts, such as Yellow River cultural records. To bridge this critical gap, we introduce YRC-Bench, the first human-curated, multi-parallel benchmark dedicated to historical heritage translation across Classical Chinese, Modern Chinese, and nine target foreign languages. YRC-Bench establishes a tri-level parallel corpus incorporating modern explanatory glosses as explicit semantic bridges and operationalizes translation strategies through paired conserved versus substituted CSI variants categorized by cultural translatability. Systematic evaluations of nine leading LLMs across bidirectional translation directions reveal that leveraging modern Chinese glosses - especially human-curated ones - dramatically elevates both lexical fidelity and semantic adequacy. Furthermore, multidimensional human preference audits by native experts unveil distinct cross-cultural preferences between Sinographic-tradition and non-Sinographic language groups.

title: Exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
text:
Title: Exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

The static interaction potential of two non-spinning point masses in general relativity was previously computed through seventh post-Newtonian order using methods of effective field theory. Its probe limit, or zeroth-self-force contribution, is determined exactly by the Schwarzschild geometry. We derive a closed-form expression for the static first-self-force correction, quadratic in the light mass, and establish its weak-field expansion to all orders. Working in harmonic gauge, we construct the required Green function for the coupled linearised gravitational equations about the Schwarzschild background. We fix its homogeneous contributions and regularised coincident limit by matching to the dimensionally continued point-source theory. The result reproduces known perturbative coefficients and determines all higher static post-Newtonian coefficients in this mass sector.

title: Toward Sustainable Agentic AI: Carbon Tradeoffs Across Iterative Self-Refinement and Tool-Augmented Coding
text:
Title: Toward Sustainable Agentic AI: Carbon Tradeoffs Across Iterative Self-Refinement and Tool-Augmented Coding
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Agentic language model systems can improve performance either by iterating on their own outputs or by using external tools in grounded environments. While these strategies can reduce error rates and substitute for larger models in some settings, their environmental cost remains relatively underexplored. We present two complementary empirical studies that estimate the energy and carbon footprint of agentic AI across settings of increasing complexity. Study~1 evaluates iterative verbal self-refinement: GPT-4.1-mini at $k = 1$--$5$ steps versus a GPT-4.1 single-pass baseline on two MATH benchmark splits. Study~2 evaluates tool-augmented agentic coding: GPT-4.1-mini, Claude Opus~4.6, and GPT-5.3-codex on SWE-bench Lite, where agents operate inside Docker-isolated environments with access to code execution and file editing tools. In Study~1, $k=3$ refinements close a 16-percentage-point accuracy gap to within 1~point, but nearly triple the carbon footprint relative to the cheap single-pass baseline while remaining below the GPT-4.1 single-pass baseline under the current token-based carbon scenario. In Study~2, GPT-5.3-codex achieves the highest resolution rate in this sample (81.2\%), ahead of Claude Opus~4.6 (68.9\%) and GPT-4.1-mini (25.0\%), but resolved-task-normalized efficiency remains mixed: GPT-4.1-mini is lowest on estimated carbon and cost per resolved task, while GPT-5.3-codex delivers substantially higher task success. All carbon estimates cover output-token inference only; prompt tokens, which exceed 99\% of tokens in Study~2, and tool execution are not charged, so the figures are lower bounds on the full agentic footprint.

title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
text:
Title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Machine-learning surrogates in computational science often require not only accurate predictions but also expectations, variances, conserved integrals, and normalization constants. Conventional neural networks, including Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs), generally evaluate these quantities through Monte Carlo sampling or multidimensional quadrature, making repeated inference costly, particularly in high dimensions. We introduce KANs with Tractable Operators for Uncertainty and Constraints (TOUCKANs), whose finite-degree polynomial outer functions yield a decomposable sum--product representation. Under factorizing input measures, expectations and higher moments then reduce algebraically to deterministic recursions over one-dimensional leaf integrals. Independent and shared inner-block variants form a parameter-efficiency hierarchy, and a universal-approximation proof for its most restricted member extends to the complete class. The same deterministic operators allow conserved integrals and normalization to be imposed throughout training. Across uniform and Gaussian benchmarks through 50 dimensions, deterministic mean and variance errors remained below the median fixed-budget Monte Carlo errors in every case. TOUCKANs also conserved Cahn--Hilliard mass to machine precision and imposed normalization and orthogonality through deterministic moments, enabling joint computation of the lowest four Schrödinger eigenpairs in two, three, and five dimensions. TOUCKANs therefore connect KAN approximation with tractable probabilistic circuits, making statistical operators and integral constraints directly available within an expressive neural surrogate.

title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
text:
Title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

```text Let $β_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[β_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+θ_0})$ for an absolute $θ_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```

title: Anchored Stein Variational Gradient Descent Algorithm for Non-smooth Sampling
text:
Title: Anchored Stein Variational Gradient Descent Algorithm for Non-smooth Sampling
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We introduce a Stein variational framework for sampling from a target density $p\propto e^{-U}$ when the target potential $U$ is possibly non-smooth. The key idea is to introduce a smoother reference potential $U_0$ and the anchor weight $a=e^{U-U_0}$. The resulting anchored Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD) algorithm is able to target $p\propto e^{-U}$ without computing the gradient of $U$ and include standard SVGD as a special case. In particular, we allow the target potential $U$ to be locally Lipschitz while the reference potential $U_0$ is continuously differentiable, along with other suitable assumptions. Under this low regularity regime, we establish a Kullback-Leibler first variation formula for anchored perturbations, identify the corresponding steepest descent direction in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space and prove a nonasymptotic convergence bound for the anchored SVGD algorithm in terms of an anchored kernelized Stein discrepancy. Finally, we also provide guidance on constructing a suitable reference potential $U_0$ based on $U$.

title: On the Method of Projection onto Localized States for Describing Reactions and Clustering
text:
Title: On the Method of Projection onto Localized States for Describing Reactions and Clustering
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

The method of projection onto localized states intended for describing reactions and clustering is examined. In particular, the method offers a simple extension of the no-core shell model to continuum- and clusterized bound states. A critical analysis of a previous realization of the method is provided. A way to minimize the number of basis functions required for convergence is given. An easy way to obtain exactly unitary and symmetric $S$ matrix from calculations is pointed out. The method is tested in one- and two-channel $np$ scattering problems with the Daejeon $NN$ interaction. It is shown that excellent convergence can be reached even when only oscillator states with low number of excitation quanta are retained.

title: FusionQ: A Generic and Optimal Decoding Framework for Ultra-Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction
text:
Title: FusionQ: A Generic and Optimal Decoding Framework for Ultra-Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum error correction (QEC) decoding has traditionally been organized around fixed decoding instances: a monolithic space-time detector error model (DEM), or a predetermined temporal window, is handed to a backend decoder after enough syndrome data has arrived. This paper presents FusionQ, a fusion decoding framework that changes this paradigm by deriving local decoding tasks from the observed syndrome and then fusing their results into a single global correction. Instead of forcing every shot through the same global or windowed problem, FusionQ builds open-boundary local DEMs around fired detector clusters and expands the corresponding footprints only when a local optimum uses virtual boundary errors. FusionQ is generic in the decoder backend: the scheduler requires only a local solution and a boundary-use flag, so exact solvers, matching-style decoders on graphlike DEMs, and heuristic decoders can share the same runtime. We prove a compositional optimality theorem: with an exact minimum-weight local backend and boundary-free publication, fusing the published local decoding results yields a global most-likely error (MLE) solution of the original DEM. Our evaluation shows that, with an exact backend, FusionQ matches the monolithic MLE result on every shot. Across decoder backends, FusionQ substantially reduces decoding latency by overlapping local decoding with hardware syndrome acquisition.

title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
text:
Title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that neural networks are converging toward similar representation spaces. As language models become more capable, their representations are aligning with those of vision models. However, recent work has questioned whether this trend continues to hold for newer language models. Moreover, it has been shown that representation similarity metrics can be confounded by model depth and width, requiring appropriate baselines for interpretation. In this work, we first investigate where alignment emerges between unimodal models across model layers and representation dimensions. Next, we find that the PRH capability-alignment trend persists for newer models as long as the captions are sufficiently clean and informative. Finally, we contextualize cross-modal alignment, introducing unimodal and multimodal baselines on various datasets. Our results show that the cross-modal representational alignment of unimodal models can surpass that of explicitly aligned vision-language models, but remains substantially behind the alignment observed for models of the same modality. Code is available at https://github.com/ExplainableML/prh-closer-look.

title: GenISys: Integrated Ship Systems Design Using Subsystem-Conditional Tabular Diffussion
text:
Title: GenISys: Integrated Ship Systems Design Using Subsystem-Conditional Tabular Diffussion
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Ship design requires coordinating coupled subsystems to satisfy engineering constraints and balance competing performance and cost objectives. Generative artificial intelligence has supported component design, but integrated ship generation must also account for interactions among hull geometry, structure, propulsion, and operation. This paper presents GenISys, a framework for generating integrated systems, demonstrated through early-stage bulk-carrier design. Its dataset contains 217,999 proposed designs, including 16,247 that satisfy the formulated engineering constraints. The proposed simultaneous conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (SCDDPM) generates subsystems together, allowing each subsystem model to respond to changes elsewhere during generation. Experiments compare this approach with monolithic whole-ship generation and sequential subsystem generation across five independent training runs per architecture. In a study targeting lower cost per tonne of cargo transported, designs were generated for a required voyage range of 5,000 nautical miles. SCDDPM produced designs satisfying the formulated engineering constraints and meeting a common low-cost target in 55.70% of generation requests, compared with 51.10% for the monolithic model and 47.54% for the sequential model. These correspond to 9.0% and 17.2% more qualifying designs, respectively, while maintaining similar estimated transport costs. These results show how generative artificial intelligence can coordinate subsystems to generate feasible, high-performing integrated systems.

title: LAION-Audio-XL: A Web-Scale Corpus and Scaling Studies for Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining
text:
Title: LAION-Audio-XL: A Web-Scale Corpus and Scaling Studies for Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)
