Therefore, in this paper we adopt an economic model predictive control framework and focus on designing online algorithms to solve the control input design problems with a limited computational budget. In particular, we propose two tailored online algorithms based on projected gradient descent, with a custom projection routine, and the projected primal-dual method. We discuss the pros and cons of both algorithm designs, focusing in particular on computational efficiency. We further compare them through numerical experiments simulating the control of an HVAC system over the course of a day. The results show that computationally efficient online solvers for HVAC systems control are indeed possible. Moreover, the performance closely matches that of a baseline algorithm with unlimited computational budget, in terms of reference temperature tracking and comfort temperature range enforcement.

title: From Tool State to Scientific Action: Auditing Decision Provenance in Biomedical Research Agents
text:
Title: From Tool State to Scientific Action: Auditing Decision Provenance in Biomedical Research Agents
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

A scientific agent can give the same verdict while reading and citing different evidence. BioAgent-DF tests this separation using paired reference and candidate values saved at the same scientific computation site. It restores or transplants those values at their original coordinates, then runs the agent on healthy hardware. Across eight SciFact batches, Qwen3.5-4B shows repeatable citation changes in three capture-claim combinations, and Gemma 3 4B IT shows repeatable read and citation changes in four. These seven combinations cover two claims. Full restoration recovers the reference evidence sets while verdicts remain unchanged. Verdict changes observed under the baseline prompt did not recur under the explicit-example prompt. Complementary tool and optimizer experiments distinguish recovery of numerical state, recovery of ranked lists, and restoration of an agent's visible history. These results show that an audit should track both the evidence an agent uses and its final answer. In hERG cardiac-safety assay allocation, silent numerical faults changed testing decisions while the fixed-budget shortlist kept the same number of compounds labeled as blockers. After the agent had used faulty values, restoring its earlier execution state and supplying certified scores recovered all 39 changed decisions, whereas replacing the prediction file recovered none; no incorrect action was committed. A streaming implementation of the arithmetic checks reduced the total time for forward execution and verification by 42.4% relative to the original FP64 implementation, with identical flags and recovery outputs.

title: Correctness and Predictive Uncertainty in Bayesian TSK Fuzzy Regression: A Reproducible Evaluation on Tabular and Building-Meter Data
text:
Title: Correctness and Predictive Uncertainty in Bayesian TSK Fuzzy Regression: A Reproducible Evaluation on Tabular and Building-Meter Data
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Uncertainty estimates from fuzzy regression are informative only when the implementation is correct and the comparison protocol makes the sources of variation visible. We revisit a first-order Takagi--Sugeno--Kang (TSK) regression implementation and rebuild its dense, conjugate Bayesian, BIC-based, and rule-level spike-and-slab estimators using corrected code. The corrected pipeline freezes the Gaussian membership partition at training time, uses a scaled conjugate prior, evaluates firing strengths in the log domain, and reports direct posterior-predictive quantiles for Bayesian methods. Across 30 outer 80/20 splits on three targets from two UCI regression datasets, corrected TSK-LS obtains $R^2=0.957$, $0.923$, and $0.786$ on Energy-Heating, Energy-Cooling, and Concrete, respectively; rule-level Gibbs sampling with Bayesian model averaging obtains $0.957$, $0.922$, and $0.784$. We then evaluate the same workflow on a bounded chronological sample of the Building Data Genome 2 meter data that covers 158 buildings across 17 sites. In a common-unit evaluation, every method is scored on the same 47,400 test rows and every trained model uses 94,800 train--validation rows. Persistence has RMSE $27.710$, compared with $29.083$ for both TSK-LS and Bayesian TSK; the pre-specified building-level mean RMSE difference between Bayesian TSK and persistence is $+0.0447$ with a 95% site-cluster bootstrap interval of $[-1.5536,1.5665]$. The Bayesian TSK 90% intervals have PICP $0.980$ and MPIW $116.469$. Taken together, the evidence supports a narrower conclusion: spike-and-slab model averaging is a reproducible implementation option, but it does not provide a demonstrated accuracy or calibration advantage across the tested tabular and building-meter settings.

title: Pohlmeyer reduction of Newton-Cartan strings
text:
Title: Pohlmeyer reduction of Newton-Cartan strings
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We develop a Pohlmeyer-type reduction for classical non-relativistic strings on string Newton-Cartan backgrounds. For strings on a two-sphere, we identify the invariant reduced field, show that its dynamics is integrable, and construct a Lax representation. We relate this intrinsic formulation to the non-relativistic expansion of relativistic strings and obtain a dictionary between non-relativistic string solutions and their reduced counterparts. The construction explicitly determines which relativistic solitonic configurations survive the non-relativistic limit and which decouple. Moreover, it provides a framework for applying integrability methods to Newton-Cartan string dynamics.

title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
text:
Title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

AI coding harnesses couple language models to shells, filesystems, and network sockets, turning the harness into an automated Living-off-the-Land (LotL) platform: once an adversary injects instructions into retrieved content, dual-use binaries such as bash, curl, and find become the payload. We argue that security in agentic systems is a structural property of the cognitive architecture and permission composition rather than an emergent property of individual models. Static regex blacklists miss structural evasions, whereas LLM-as-a-Judge guardrails incur high latency while over-blocking benign work. We present ActiveSecHarness, a neurosymbolic reference-monitor architecture built around Separation of Intelligence and Authority. It combines (1) Macaroon-inspired HMAC capability tokens across four Trust and Authority Rings, (2) a 2D product taint lattice $\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{trust}} \times \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{sens}}$ and a workspace provenance ledger that prevents secret laundering across disk, (3) deterministic Ring-0 OS/tool guards, and (4) bytecode certificates, split-horizon audit logs, self-healing security test synthesis, and an adaptive UserWikiManager. Across $N=252$ fixtures ($120$ attack, $120$ benign, $12$ kill chains), a live local LLM judge (qwen3:4b) refuses $98.3\%$ of benign work at $142.3\,\mathrm{ms}$ latency, whereas Ring 0 achieves $\mathrm{ABR}=1.000$ and $\mathrm{FPR}=0.000$ in $12.7\,μ\mathrm{s}$ ($11{,}200\times$ faster). In a multi-step trajectory ablation, an oracle Conseca-style stateless policy misses $4/12$ kill chains ($\mathrm{ABR}=0.667$) and coarse Boolean taint blocks $83.3\%$ of benign workflows, while our 2D product lattice achieves $\mathrm{ABR}=1.000$ and $\mathrm{FPR}=0.000$ at $\approx 20\,μ\mathrm{s}$ per step.

title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection
text:
Title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization remains a central challenge in materials property prediction, where models must extrapolate to novel chemistries beyond the training distribution. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong scientific reasoning, their direct use for quantitative prediction remains limited. To address this, we systematically evaluate multiple roles for LLM assistance, finding that only taxonomy-based grouping consistently improves OOD generalization over a strong kNN+GBT baseline. Building on this, we here propose MOTIF, a framework that leverages LLMs not as predictors, but as generators of candidate taxonomies that partition materials into chemically meaningful environments. These taxonomies are evaluated via training-only pseudo-OOD validation, and only those that improve generalization are retained. Invariant feature selection is then applied within each accepted taxonomy, followed by gated aggregation across taxonomies. We evaluate on 2D halide perovskites, where bandgap prediction must generalize across distinct organic spacer families. On this benchmark, MOTIF reduces mean OOD MAE from 0.122 to 0.111 eV. Under a frozen dev/test protocol, the deployable configuration further improves errors from 0.123 to 0.117 eV (electronic bandgap) and from 0.181 to 0.173 eV (optical bandgap). Beyond this primary task, we validate transferability across additional materials datasets, including 3D perovskite solar cell efficiencies and Matbench benchmarks with structure-based splits. Across domains, MOTIF consistently improves robustness under distribution shift, outperforming expert-defined groupings, rule-based heuristics, and clustering baselines, while remaining competitive with strong classical selection methods. These results demonstrate that LLMs are most effective not as predictors, but as tools for discovering structure in data.

title: Geometry-Dependent Approximation and Stability Properties of Shallow ReLU$^k$ Networks on Bounded Euclidean Domains
text:
Title: Geometry-Dependent Approximation and Stability Properties of Shallow ReLU$^k$ Networks on Bounded Euclidean Domains
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

On bounded Euclidean domains, we study how hidden-parameter geometry affects shallow ReLU$^k$ networks through results on approximation rates, saturation-type lower bounds, Gram and stiffness matrix spectra, Bernstein and Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund inequalities, discrete least-squares recovery, and inverse approximation. Our analysis uses smooth localization and dyadic Fourier estimates. We quantify parameter geometry by the fill distance $h$ and antipodal separation distance $\underline h$. For the prescribed network space $L_n^k$, representative approximation estimates take the form \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \inf_{g_n\in L_n^k}\|f-g_n\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω')}&\lesssim h^r\|f\|_{\mathcal H^r(Ω)},\\ \inf_{g_n\in L_n^k}\|f-g_n\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω)}&\gtrsim \underline h^{\frac{d+2k+1}{2}}\|f\|_{\mathcal L^2(Ω')}. \end{aligned} \end{equation*} The upper bound exploits target regularity up to the critical order $\frac{d+2k+1}{2}$, while the lower bound applies asymptotically to fixed targets smoother than this order. The upper estimate holds on an interior subdomain $Ω'$, whereas the lower estimate concerns the larger domain $Ω$. We also obtain geometry-dependent spectral estimates that quantify conditioning and coefficient stability. Further results establish norm discretization and regularized recovery from function values, and infer target regularity from approximation rates under coefficient or separation conditions. Altogether, these results describe how parameter geometry governs approximation accuracy, the stability of coefficient representations, discrete recovery, and the regularity information contained in convergence rates.

title: FireGate: Bounding Behaviour Change Before Training in Continual RL Fine-Tuning
text:
Title: FireGate: Bounding Behaviour Change Before Training in Continual RL Fine-Tuning
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Fine-tuning a deployed language model on one task after another can change behaviour that should stay fixed, such as earlier skills, general chat or refusals. Today, such forgetting is found only after training, on the benchmarks someone chose to run. This work bounds, before training, how often its outputs change on chosen prompt distributions. FireGate places each task's update, such as a new LoRA, behind a gate, which is a classifier on the model's frozen lower layers that decides for each prompt whether the update is used. Where no gate fires, the model computes exactly what the old one computes. As a result, on any prompt distribution, every bounded behaviour score changes by at most the gates' firing rate there over a whole task stream. Calibrating each gate on unlabeled prompts of what must not change fixes that rate before training, with a PAC guarantee, whatever weights training produces. Forgetting is thus bounded by the gate's false-alarm rate, and its price is the gate's power: no update, gated or not, that changes as few protected outputs can change new-task outputs more often than the best test of that level tells new-task prompts from protected ones. On reinforcement-learning streams of up to five tasks, gated training keeps the earlier tasks and changes 3.3% of held-out chat responses, whereas ungated training changes 91.8%. Across seven models, the gain kept behind the gate follows its firing rate on new-task prompts, measured before training. The certificate covers the gated model as deployed, on the prompt distributions sampled for calibration, not against an adversary who searches for prompts that fire the gate.

title: Transport, Entropy, and the Cost of Dependence: Maximum Conditional Entropy under Transport Constraints
text:
Title: Transport, Entropy, and the Cost of Dependence: Maximum Conditional Entropy under Transport Constraints
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Maximum-entropy inference under Wasserstein constraints can be computationally challenging due to the underlying optimization over transport couplings. We investigate a tractable alternative based on maximizing conditional entropy under an average transport constraint. On Euclidean spaces, this formulation admits an explicit generalized-Gaussian additive-noise solution, providing a feasible approximation to the Wasserstein-constrained problem without solving an optimal transport problem. We establish quantitative bounds on the resulting optimality gap by showing that the two formulations admit a common feasible-marginal representation, with their discrepancy characterized by the mutual information retained between the nominal and perturbed variables. For discretely supported nominal distributions, we further obtain an exact decomposition of the gap into a marginal-entropy gain and a weighted Jensen-Shannon divergence.

title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
text:
Title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Self-distillation methods for large language models with an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher already retain a history of student updates. Muon nevertheless stores a separate momentum buffer, increasing persistent training memory. We propose Muon with Reused Teacher (Muon-RT), which reuses the teacher-student displacement to eliminate momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices. We show that this displacement encodes an exponentially weighted history of applied updates and smooths temporally uncorrelated noise under a local model. Muon-RT removes its radial component, normalizes it spectrally, and mixes it with the current gradient after Newton-Schulz (NS) orthogonalization. Under explicit regularity and alignment assumptions, we establish linear contraction of an expected objective-gap bound toward a residual error level. With Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Muon-RT improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.6 points with 42% less persistent memory, and over momentum Muon by 5.4 points with 27% less persistent memory. With Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, it improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.0 points.

title: The polar discontinuity picture in nickelate superlattices: comparison of the insulating and metallic phases
text:
Title: The polar discontinuity picture in nickelate superlattices: comparison of the insulating and metallic phases
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We present a first-principles study of the formal-charge polar discontinuity in superlattices of BaTiO$_3$ interfaced with SmNiO$_3$ or BiNiO$_3$, comparing the results for the insulating and metallic nickelate phases. Polar discontinuities arising from differently charged layers in perovskites are well-studied in heterostructures such as LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$, and recently, signatures consistent with such a polar discontinuity have been observed in systems where the formally charged layers would reside in a metal. We first identify signatures of the polar discontinuity in the structure and the density of states of superlattices with BaTiO$_3$ and insulating BiNiO$_3$, and find partial screening by modification of the BiNiO$_3$ charge disproportionation pattern analogous to our previous study on BaTiO$_3$/SmNiO$_3$. We then examine superlattices constructed from the corresponding metallic nickelate phases and find that, despite the presence of screening charges, the qualitative interfacial response is remarkably similar to that of the insulating counterparts. We show that the metallic screening charges have little influence on the apparent formal-charge polar discontinuity and discuss practical limitations of the polar-discontinuity picture when interpreting and quantifying screening at metallic nickelate/ferroelectric interfaces.

title: The Prodigal Elephant Returns: Last-Return Laws in the Superdiffusive Regime
text:
Title: The Prodigal Elephant Returns: Last-Return Laws in the Superdiffusive Regime
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Let $(S_n)$ be the one-dimensional elephant random walk with memory parameter $p\in(3/4,1)$ and first-step probability $q=\mathbb{P}(S_1=1)\in[0,1]$. Set $a=2p-1$, and let $f_{q,a}$ denote the density of the almost-sure limit of $S_n/n^a$. We prove that the last return time $T_0=\sup\{m\geq0:S_m=0\}$ satisfies: $\mathbb{P}(T_0\geq n)\sim f_{q,a}(0)\sqrt{\frac{8}{π(2a-1)}}n^{-(a-1/2)}$. Reflection gives $f_{q,a}(0)=f_{1,a}(0)$, so the constant is independent of $q$. For future walks started from admissible states $(n,x_n)$ with $x_n/\sqrt n\to z$, we establish functional convergence of the centered martingale-normalized paths to a time-changed Brownian motion. Uniform control of late hitting times then gives the eventual-return kernel $2Φ(-\sqrt{2a-1}|z|)$, uniformly on bounded scaled windows, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. The same last-visit asymptotic holds uniformly for nonempty deterministic targets $F_n\subseteq[-r_n,r_n]\cap\mathbb{Z}$, $r_n=o(\sqrt n)$, held fixed during each trajectory. Conditionally on $T_0\geq n$, we identify the joint limit of $S_n/\sqrt n$, the next return divided by $n$, and the last return divided by the next return. The last ratio converges to $A^{-1/(2a-1)}$, independently of the other two limiting coordinates, where $A$ has the arcsine distribution on $(0,1)$.

title: Accelerated search for global extrema in structured quantum signals
text:
Title: Accelerated search for global extrema in structured quantum signals
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Extreme values of a physical system are rare by definition, yet they can govern some of its most consequential and anomalous behavior. Their sparsity makes them particularly costly to identify in large data sets. Quantum computation offers a potential way to reduce this cost. The challenge is that quantum amplitudes cannot simply be read, copied, compared, or marked using conventional search oracles. Here we introduce an algorithm for searching amplitude-encoded quantum signals that exploits their underlying structure. Through a nonlinear amplitude transformation, the algorithm identifies and certifies a global extremum while exponentially reducing the effective search space for structured signals. We establish a polylogarithmic query complexity in the data size $N$, together with global completeness, efficient classical verification, and a measurable criterion for quantifying exploitable structure. We demonstrate the framework using computational turbulence data. Applied to line cuts of velocity gradients from a $1024^3$ simulation containing more than one billion grid points, the algorithm consistently isolates the extreme tail and reduces the median search space to $O(\log N)$. The clustered structure characteristic of turbulence further accelerates the search. These results establish a direct connection between physical structure and quantum advantage in extreme-value search. For accessibility, the main text emphasizes the central ideas and results, while the theoretical derivations are provided in the Appendices.

title: Can cosmic neutrinos induce a cosmic birefringence signal?
text:
Title: Can cosmic neutrinos induce a cosmic birefringence signal?
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

A coupling of photons to the cosmic neutrino asymmetry current has been proposed to explain the hinted isotropic rotation of CMB polarization. Gauge invariant UV completions require a Kalb-Ramond field that is exactly dual to a massless axion. We show that, in this case, the product of the axion-photon coupling and the axion-neutrino current coupling is fixed by the signal, $g_{aγ}/f_\ell=1/Λ_*^2$ with $Λ_*\simeq10$ TeV. Using $SU(2)_L$ gauge invariance we show that the dual axion couples to electrons as $g_{aγ}g_{ae}=m_e/Λ_*^2\simeq5\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. This value is excluded by the measured electron magnetic moment combined with light-shining-through-a-wall searches, as well as by stellar evolution. Conserved anomaly-free currents may evade these bounds, but then either a contact interaction among SM fermions excludes the model, or the relic neutrinos decouple from the signal. We conclude that cosmic neutrinos cannot induce a birefringence signal.

title: CryoNet.Refine: A One-step Diffusion Model for Rapid Refinement of Structural Models with Cryo-EM Density Map Restraints
text:
Title: CryoNet.Refine: A One-step Diffusion Model for Rapid Refinement of Structural Models with Cryo-EM Density Map Restraints
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

High-resolution structure determination by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) requires the accurate fitting of an atomic model into an experimental density map. Traditional refinement pipelines such as Phenix.real_space_refine and Rosetta are computationally expensive, demand extensive manual tuning, and present a significant bottleneck for researchers. We present CryoNet.Refine, an end-to-end deep learning framework that automates and accelerates molecular structure refinement. Our approach utilizes a one-step diffusion model that integrates a density-aware loss function with robust stereochemical restraints, enabling rapid optimization of a structure against experimental data. CryoNet.Refine provides a unified and versatile solution capable of refining protein complexes as well as DNA/RNA-protein complexes. In benchmarks against Phenix.real_space_refine, CryoNet.Refine consistently achieves substantial improvements in both model-map correlation and overall geometric quality metrics. By offering a scalable, automated, and powerful alternative, CryoNet.Refine aims to serve as an essential tool for next-generation cryo-EM structure refinement. Web server: https://cryonet.ai/refine; Source code: https://github.com/kuixu/cryonet.refine.

title: Training a force field for proteins and small molecules from scratch
text:
Title: Training a force field for proteins and small molecules from scratch
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Force fields for molecular dynamics are usually developed manually, limiting their transferability and making systematic exploration of functional forms challenging. We developed a graph neural network that assigns all force field parameters for diverse molecules using continuous atom typing. The freely-available model, called Garnet, was trained on quantum mechanical, condensed phase and protein nuclear magnetic resonance data without the use of existing parameters. The resulting force field shows comparable performance to current force fields on small molecules, folded proteins, protein complexes and disordered proteins. It shows similar results to popular approaches for relative binding free energy predictions across a range of targets. Assessing different functional forms shows that the double exponential potential is a flexible and accurate alternative to the Lennard-Jones potential. Garnet provides a platform for automated, reproducible force field discovery that brings the benefits of machine learning to classical force fields.

title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
text:
Title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.

title: CMB Bounds on Primordial Black Holes via Radiation Capture: Linear Perturbations
text:
Title: CMB Bounds on Primordial Black Holes via Radiation Capture: Linear Perturbations
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We investigate the gravitational interaction between primordial radiation, consisting of photons and ultra-relativistic neutrinos, and primordial black holes (PBHs), and study its imprint on the anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Assuming that PBHs are immersed in the cosmic radiation background, we introduce a covariant energy-momentum transfer four-vector to describe the gravitational capture of radiation by PBHs. We extend the background-level framework of M. Farhang and S. M. S. Movahed [Phys. Rev. D 114, 083533 (2026)] to an inhomogeneous Universe at linear order by consistently modifying the perturbed continuity and Euler equations to account for both energy and momentum transfer. We use the imprint of this interaction on the CMB to place novel constraints on the PBH abundance, $f_{\rm pbh}$. We show that these constraints are up to two orders of magnitude tighter than those obtained from background-only analyses and exhibit a strong dependence on the PBH mass. Using Planck temperature and polarization data, we constrain the PBH fraction to $f_{\rm pbh} \lesssim 0.05-0.002$ for $M$ in the range $10^{15}-10^{17} M_\odot$. Furthermore, sensitivity forecasts for a cosmic-variance-limited survey with $\ell_{\rm max}=7000$, assuming a fiducial $f_{\rm pbh}=0$, yield projected bounds of $f_{\rm pbh} \lesssim 10^{-2}-2\times 10^{-4}$ over the mass range $10^{13}-10^{17} M_\odot$.

title: Empirical approximation of $L^p$ norms for $p\in (1, 2)$
text:
Title: Empirical approximation of $L^p$ norms for $p\in (1, 2)$
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

For $p\in[1,2]$, we prove uniform moment estimates for weighted sums \[ \sum_{j=1}^mζ_jw_j|\langle{\bf v}_j,y\rangle|^p \] of independent subgaussian random variables $ζ_j$, where the unit vectors $\{{\bf v}_j\}_{j=1}^m$ and nonnegative weights $\{w_j\}_{j=1}^m$ form an isotropic frame. This allows us to obtain optimal sampling discretization of $L_p$ norms for each fixed $p\in[1,2]$. Namely, for an $N$-dimensional space $X_N$ of bounded functions satisfying $\|f\|_\infty\le\sqrt {KN}\,\|f\|_{L_2}$ for every $f\in X_N$, we show that $m\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}KN\log(2N)$ independent samples $ξ^1,\ldots,ξ^m$ provide the discretization \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(ξ^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p}^p \quad\forall f\in X_N \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This implies a corresponding weighted discretization result that, for $1<p<2$, improves Talagrand's bound on the dimension $m$ needed to embed $N$-dimensional subspaces of $L_p$ into $\ell_p^m$ with distortion at most $1+\varepsilon$, giving $m\le C\varepsilon^{-2}N\log(2N)$.

title: Distributional Limits of Empirical Codegree Processes in Sampled Networks
text:
Title: Distributional Limits of Empirical Codegree Processes in Sampled Networks
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study fluctuations of empirical distributions of normalized codegrees under independent vertex sampling from deterministic or random weighted parent networks. We establish a quantitative multivariate normal approximation for sampled biclique counts. Under additional graph-limit and sparsity assumptions, we establish convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the empirical codegree process indexed by smooth test functions. We further establish functional convergence on Hölder balls, with a smoothness threshold depending on network sparsity and vertex sampling probabilities. We verify our assumptions for classes of graphon-generated random graphs and give counterexamples showing that the smoothness conditions cannot in general be weakened.

title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
text:
Title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Learning-based safety certification offers a promising route for verifying complex dynamical systems when explicit models are unavailable, but existing data-driven methods often scale poorly: they treat the system as a black box, rely on dense discretizations or Lipschitz bounds, and consequently suffer from sample complexity that grows exponentially with dimension. This paper shows that a common structural property of dynamical systems--monotonicity--can be used to break this curse of dimensionality. We develop a data-driven framework for robust safety verification and safe controller synthesis for unknown monotone systems using only simulator queries. Our main theoretical result proves that, for monotone systems with upper-closed unsafe sets, safety is completely characterized by the existence of monotone inductive barrier certificates. This structure reduces certificate verification over continuous state spaces to localized boundary checks over finitely many cells. To learn such certificates, we introduce Max-Monotone Networks, a monotone neural architecture with universal approximation guarantees for monotone functions. We then propose a training and refinement algorithm that, upon successful termination, returns formally valid neural barrier certificates and, under mild partition assumptions, requires only $O(n)$ simulator queries. Across high-dimensional benchmarks, including oscillator networks with up to $13{,}659$ states and traffic networks with $1{,}000$ states, our method certifies safety in regimes where prior approaches either do not converge or exceed memory limits. These results demonstrate that exploiting order structure can make neural safety certification both scalable and formally sound.

title: BioKERN: Biological Kernel Regularization for Histology-to-Transcriptomics Neighborhood Retrieval
text:
Title: BioKERN: Biological Kernel Regularization for Histology-to-Transcriptomics Neighborhood Retrieval
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Spatially resolved biology requires representations that preserve biological neighborhood structure rather than only exact cross-modal correspondences. Existing histology--transcriptomics objectives can emphasize instance-level matching even when non-paired spots share molecular or spatial context. We introduce BioKERN, a multimodal spatial representation-learning framework that incorporates biological structure as an explicit, learnable inductive bias. BioKERN constructs a training-time biological kernel by combining transcriptomic similarity and spatial proximity, then uses it to provide graded neighborhood supervision and regularize embedding geometry. Evaluation uses a fixed, model-independent biological neighborhood definition shared by all methods. Across Mouse Brain Visium and Human Liver GSE240429, BioKERN consistently improves biological-neighborhood retrieval over BLEEP in both single- and multi-scale settings. Controlled shared-architecture experiments show that most of the improvement arises from biological-kernel regularization rather than increased model capacity. These results support explicit biological geometry as an interpretable inductive bias for multimodal learning in spatial biology.

title: Scan-Coil Delay Causes Anisotropic Signal Loss in Fast 4D-STEM
text:
Title: Scan-Coil Delay Causes Anisotropic Signal Loss in Fast 4D-STEM
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Fast pixelated detectors are driving 4D-STEM toward microsecond dwell times, a regime in which the finite response of the scan deflection coils becomes comparable to the dwell time itself. Using direct probe imaging and sub-frame diffraction analysis, we document a significant intra-dwell scan-coil delay that systematically smears the recorded signal anisotropically along the fast scan direction, with a settling timescale of several tens of microseconds. We present a phase-correlation-based sub-frame alignment procedure that measures and corrects this smearing, and we assess its impact on focused and defocused 4D-STEM reconstructions over a range of scan step sizes. The correction restores signal across a broad range of spatial frequencies, with the largest gains at the large step sizes required for low-dose biological imaging. Because it operates on existing data with no modification to the microscope, the method offers a practical route to recovering signal that would otherwise be lost to scan-coil delay.

title: Simulating closed- and open-system dynamics of Tavis--Cummings lattices on fault-tolerant quantum computers
text:
Title: Simulating closed- and open-system dynamics of Tavis--Cummings lattices on fault-tolerant quantum computers
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Tavis--Cummings lattices couple cavities containing several emitters and host polaritonic many-body dynamics whose real-time correlations are costly to compute classically in two dimensions, especially when unequal emitter relaxation or dephasing rates break permutation symmetry. We analyze logical resources for fault-tolerant closed- and open-system simulation of an atom-resolved lattice with $L$ cavities, $N$ emitters per cavity, and photon cutoff $n\_{\max}$, including target observable estimation. Building on ladder-operator block encoding, we construct circuits for photon hopping and local light--matter exchange and combine them to encode the lattice Hamiltonian. By updating source and destination photon occupations in place, the hopping circuit eliminates the auxiliary $L\lceil\log_2(n\_{\max}+1)\rceil$-qubit photon register used by two-register implementations. Across three uniform-coefficient examples with $16$ to $256$ cavities, the controlled walk uses $4.75$--$8.11%$ fewer Toffoli gates than the paired two-register implementation under matched shared preparation, precision, control, and workspace conventions. For closed systems, we implement real-time evolution with generalized quantum signal processing and bound the cost of estimating retarded cavity spectral functions. For open systems with photon loss, emitter relaxation, and dephasing, we use a sampled first-order dilation and bound the runs and timesteps needed to estimate transient photon statistics such as $g^{(2)}(0)$. With state-preparation and measurement costs explicit, these estimates provide a reference for assessing fault-tolerant light--matter lattice simulation costs.

title: Kinematic Quantum Geometry
text:
Title: Kinematic Quantum Geometry
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Kinematic quantum geometry describes fast degrees of freedom (DOFs) that adiabatically follow states parametrized by both the coordinates and the velocities of slow DOFs. It extends Born-Oppenheimer geometry, which depends on coordinates alone, introduces mixed Berry curvatures, and modifies the effective theory governing the slow DOFs. We test its predictions in two setups: spinful particles moving in magnetic textures, and Dirac electrons in graphene coupled to an LC circuit. In the first, kinematic quantum geometry produces a velocity-dependent effective mass tensor and generates a Lorentz-like force nonlinear in velocity that can arise even in coplanar textures. In the second, it renormalizes the circuit capacitance and generates a Hall current nonlinear in the electric field. For small velocities, it reproduces recent results for electronic dynamics in external electromagnetic fields and in pseudospin textures. However, the framework can remain valid at large velocities beyond the perturbative regime, provided the kinematic states are sufficiently slowly varying.

title: Th$^{4+}$ ion cluster structures and electric field gradients in $^{229}$Th:CaF$_2$
text:
Title: Th$^{4+}$ ion cluster structures and electric field gradients in $^{229}$Th:CaF$_2$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

The low-energy nuclear isomeric transition of $^{229}$Th is a promising frequency reference for a solid-state nuclear optical clock. Wide-band-gap fluoride crystals such as CaF$_2$ offer transparent hosts for embedding Th nuclei at high density. Substitution of Th$^{4+}$ for Ca$^{2+}$ requires charge compensation, linking the local defect structure to nuclear quadrupole splitting. We use first-principles calculations to examine neutral Th dimers compensated by four interstitial F ions ($\mathrm{F}_{i}^{-}$). Screening different compensation geometries by their relative formation energies identifies a family of low-energy configurations with closely similar local structures. These configurations share large electric field gradients and small asymmetry parameters, consistent with the experimental high-EFG site 3. Their calculated quadrupole splittings are further compared with the measured C13 spectra. Together, the energetic and spectroscopic results support $\mathrm{F}_{i}^{-}$-compensated Th dimers as candidate microscopic structures for site 3 in Th:CaF$_2$.

title: Statistical Analysis of Synthetic Data with Verification: A Linear Regression Framework
text:
Title: Statistical Analysis of Synthetic Data with Verification: A Linear Regression Framework
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Synthetic data are widely used for training modern AI systems. However, their statistical understanding remains limited. It is well recognized in statistics that repeated self-training on synthetic data can amplify errors inherited from pre-trained models, leading to model collapse. Verification plays a crucial role in selecting high-quality synthetic data to help prevent model collapse and improve model performance. We study verified self-training in a linear regression framework, where a pre-trained estimator generates synthetic data with injected generation noise and a verifier selects samples according to a verification threshold. Post-training on the accepted samples updates either all coordinates (full fine-tuning) or only an active subset (partial fine-tuning). Our analysis reveals three potentially counterintuitive effects. We establish that tighter verification does not always lead to lower prediction risk. We also find that a suitable level of injected generation noise can reduce prediction risk, while excessive noise can increase it. Moreover, full and partial fine-tuning can respond differently to the same verification rule, since pre-training error in the frozen coordinates affects both sample selection and post-training risk. We analyze these effects by deriving finite sample risk bounds for four separate regimes determined by the relative scales of the verification threshold, generation noise, and pre-training error. The bounds precisely characterize how verification affects prediction risk across these regimes. In particular, we quantify how the generation noise, the effective accepted sample size, and the covariance of the accepted covariates affect prediction risk. The analysis extends to iterative verified full fine-tuning, where sufficiently tight verification reduces the initial error contribution at a geometric rate.

title: Piezogyration and elastogyration in ternary chalcopyrites from first principles
text:
Title: Piezogyration and elastogyration in ternary chalcopyrites from first principles
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Natural optical activity arises from the spatial dispersion of the optical response and is described by the rank-two gyration pseudotensor. Its dependence on mechanical stress and strain, quantified by the piezogyration and elastogyration tensors, respectively, has been investigated experimentally for decades. However, a systematic first-principles description of these effects remains largely unexplored. Here we present a first-principles methodology to compute the full piezogyration and elastogyration tensors, and apply it to a set of representative ternary chalcopyrite crystals. The gyration of the unstrained crystal turns out to be a poor predictor of the magnitude of the elastogyration response, which we find to be a property inherited from their parent zinc-blende structures. The elastic compliance tensor further shapes the piezogyration response, with particularly pronounced effects in AgGaS$_2$, a well-known achiral yet optically active crystal. Finally, we explore strain-induced chirality through the trace of the gyration tensor, the only pseudoscalar contribution to the natural optical activity that is linear in the tensor components and encodes information about chirality.

title: Agnostic Marginal-Nonuniform Learning
text:
Title: Agnostic Marginal-Nonuniform Learning
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

We study the problem of binary classification in the marginal-nonuniform learning framework in the agnostic setting. In this model, the constants in the learning rate may depend on the marginal distribution of the unlabeled data, but the guarantee must hold uniformly over all conditional distributions of the labels. We also study fine-grained rates. We consider two criteria. (1) The standard agnostic setting, where the learner competes with the best concept in the class. In this setting, an immediate consequence of standard agnostic PAC learning results gives us the optimal rate of $\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$ for every class $\mathcal{H}$ with finite $\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal{H})$ and shows that arbitrarily slow rates are necessary otherwise. This also gives us the optimal fine-grained rate of $\sqrt{\tfrac{\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal{H})}{n}}$. Therefore, the dependence on the marginal distribution does not help, which is in contrast to the realizable setting. (2) In the relaxed agnostic setting, where the learner competes with $(1+λ)$ times the error of the best concept for a fixed $λ\in (0,1]$, the picture from the realizable setting reappears. We obtain a trichotomy of the achievable optimal rates: exponential rates of the form $e^{-n}$ arise precisely when the class is finite; linear rates of the form $\tfrac{1}{n}$ arise when the class is infinite but $\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal{H})$ is finite; and arbitrarily slow rates occur when $\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal{H})=\infty$. We also obtain the optimal fine-grained rate of $\tfrac{\mathrm{uVCE}(\mathcal{H})}{λn}$, where $\mathrm{uVCE}(\mathcal{H})$ is a recently introduced combinatorial complexity dimension called the uncentered $\mathrm{VC}$-eluder dimension.

title: Thermochemically Constrained Multiscale Laplace Neural Operator to Learn Stiff Chemical Kinetics with Conditional Diffusion Model Sampling
text:
Title: Thermochemically Constrained Multiscale Laplace Neural Operator to Learn Stiff Chemical Kinetics with Conditional Diffusion Model Sampling
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Stiff chemical kinetics is a major computational bottleneck in reacting-flow simulations, while data-driven solvers remain sensitive to training-state coverage and chemical dynamics. This work combines conditional diffusion sampling with a thermochemically constrained multiscale Laplace neural operator (TC-MLNO) for chemistry ODE integration. The diffusion model learns the equivalence-ratio-conditioned joint distribution of temperature and species from low-dimensional flame data, augmenting the state space without independent perturbations. TC-MLNO represents transient, non-periodic responses through pole-residue Laplace layers and assigns fast, medium, and slow species to separate branches. Thermochemical constraints are imposed through losses for mass and elemental conservation and heat release rate. The framework is evaluated in 1D premixed flames, a 2D developing jet, and a 3D turbulent burner flame. With equal-sized datasets, diffusion sampling reduces the 95th-percentile distance to the base flame manifold by up to 37.5% and the a posteriori full-species macro-average error by up to 92.7% versus random sampling, especially for minor species and radicals. TC-LNO yields smaller errors than the DeepONet baseline for 84.9% of retained modes and reduces the 95th-percentile error for the most attenuated modes from 0.372 to 0.081. In multidimensional flames, TC-MLNO better preserves reaction-zone locations, heat-release structures, and chemically sensitive species than DeepONet. Errors of representative radical and nitrogen-containing species in the 3D flame decrease by 88.0%-88.9%. Compared with direct CVODE integration, TC-MLNO reduces mean chemistry and total solution times by 90.1% and 62.6%, respectively. These results show that distribution-aware sampling and Laplace neural operator learning provide an accurate and efficient alternative for stiff chemical ODE integration.

title: Fresh Look at Shift Symmetric Modified Gravity
text:
Title: Fresh Look at Shift Symmetric Modified Gravity
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Shift symmetric Horndeski gravity can be a simple, well posed theory with protection against quantum corrections. Overturning conventional thought that such a theory cannot cross the phantom divide ($w=-1$) we present both analytic and numerical proof that it can. We carry out a detailed dynamical systems analysis showing the evolution of ghost free and stable regions within the model family, identify the fixed point and dynamical attractor structure, and derive the interaction of the $w=-1$ curve with these phase space structures. This reveals two mechanisms for cosmologies crossing the phantom divide while preserving shift symmetry.

title: The geometric case of the Erdős Similarity Conjecture. A human exposition of the OpenAI proof
text:
Title: The geometric case of the Erdős Similarity Conjecture. A human exposition of the OpenAI proof
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

For a fixed $q\in(0,1)$, can a set of positive Lebesgue measure avoid every translated and dilated copy of $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$? OpenAI's release of October 6, 2026 shows that it can, with a compact subset of $[0,1]$ whose measure is arbitrarily close to one. We give a detailed exposition of the proof, using only finite probability and basic measure theory. The proof removes a small open set intersecting every copy, obtained from a random construction: fair random choices, attached to the cells of nested grids, route each point down a finite tree, and at the leaf reached a further random choice removes the point with probability $p$. The removed set therefore has expected density $p$, however large the tree, while the branching gives each copy many independent chances to intersect it. Each chance depends on only part of the tree, so its outcome changes at only a controlled number of dilations, and a union bound over finitely many representative dilations then covers every dilation. We also relate the proof to the earlier random-cell arguments going back to Kolountzakis (Bull. London Math. Soc. 29 (1997), 415--424) and to recent work on two-fold sumsets (arXiv:2607.03584) and on Rajchman measures (arXiv:2609.04456), and we show how the method of conditional expectations makes the construction deterministic.

title: Spherization of the velocity field of cosmological perturbations near density extrema
text:
Title: Spherization of the velocity field of cosmological perturbations near density extrema
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

In this work, we consider a mechanism that tends to make the velocity field of linear cosmological perturbations near density extremum points (maxima or minima) spherically symmetric. It is shown that this mechanism begins to operate from the moment the Universe enters the stage of nonrelativistic matter domination ($z<z_{eq}\simeq 3600$) and rather quickly makes the velocity distribution near the density extremum practically isotropic. However, if the density profile of the initial perturbation is noticeably aspherical, its gravitational field subsequently destroys this isotropy.

title: Towards 3D fully randomized frequency-domain reconstruction of the speed of sound in breast ultrasound computed tomography
text:
Title: Towards 3D fully randomized frequency-domain reconstruction of the speed of sound in breast ultrasound computed tomography
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Ultrasound computed tomography is emerging as a promising diagnostic imaging tool. 2D geometries suffer from notorious out-of-plane scattering artifacts. Image reconstruction can be achieved with frequency-domain full waveform inversion and it can be further accelerated by randomly phase-encoding the elementary sources. In this manuscript, we extend our previous results for the 2D geometry of a ring-array to the 3D cylindrical geometry of multiple rings. In particular, we consider the cases of an elementary source described by a single array element (quasi-omni-directional transmission), a line source and a focused transmission respectively. With differences in image quality, we prove that a fully randomized frequency-domain inversion in 3D is capable to reconstruct portions of a human breast surrounded by the cylindrical geometry and detect mm-size masses of varying contrast in dense breast, in reasonable computing times, thus opening the concrete possibility to the design of 3D imaging devices with high sensitivity levels. The methods are applicable to multiple tomographic geometries in 3D and, in principle, can be integrated into next generation medical ultrasound scanners.

title: ProteinJEPA: Latent prediction improves protein language model pretraining
text:
Title: ProteinJEPA: Latent prediction improves protein language model pretraining
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Protein language models are trained primarily with masked language modeling (MLM), which predicts masked amino-acid identities. Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPA) instead predict latent representations, but have not been applied to proteins. ProteinJEPA supplements MLM with a cosine loss for predicting the half-depth hidden states of a teacher given the unmasked sequence. On 19 tasks, with ESM2 at 35M and 150M parameters and three pretraining seeds, MLM+JEPA outperforms compute-matched and step-matched MLM-only continued training in 78 and 76 of 114 comparisons (14 losses, 22 ties). The median compute-matched gain is $+0.0106$ on structure- and homology-sensitive tasks versus $+0.0041$ elsewhere, led by SCOPe-40 retrieval and remote homology with improvements of 6.1 percentage points in Recall@1 and 2.7 points in accuracy, respectively. Gains on these tasks increase with model size from 8M to 150M. Against the off-the-shelf checkpoint, MLM+JEPA wins 81 of 114 comparisons (median $+0.0068$) without improving MLM loss. In random initialization the gain is smaller and replicates inconsistently across seeds ($p{=}0.059$). The same recipe improves the causal ProGen3 model, beating a compute-matched next-token-prediction control on 12 of 16 tasks. Ablations show that cosine loss beats mean squared error, while adding shallower targets removes most of the task gain. JEPA-only training collapses downstream performance: latent prediction complements MLM rather than replacing it. Code: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/protJepa-FF24

title: High-frequency water megamasers as precision probes of black holes, galaxies and cosmology: A case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer
text:
Title: High-frequency water megamasers as precision probes of black holes, galaxies and cosmology: A case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Water megamasers in the circumnuclear disks of active galactic nuclei are among the most precise probes of supermassive black holes. VLBI imaging of 22 GHz disk masers has provided geometric distances to independently constrain $H_0$, accurate black hole mass measurements, and sub-parsec views of accretion disk geometry. ALMA has opened a new window into water maser transitions in the sub-mm/mm regime, which trace temperatures, densities and disk regions that are inaccessible at 22 GHz, and can be observed at higher spatial resolution and with less free-free absorption. However, current detections are limited to a few bright extragalactic masers in nearby galaxies. We present the case for a next-generation sub-mm/mm interferometer - ALMA2040 - that would open a new parameter space for maser studies. We show that a 10-fold increase in line sensitivity and three times longer baselines compared to ALMA would transform sub-mm maser studies from a few bright detections into a population-level probe, delivering black hole masses and geometric distances from sub-mm masers alone, independent of and complementary to 22 GHz measurements. Integrated into a VLBI array, ALMA2040 would resolve maser disks out to $>$160 Mpc, extend maser black hole masses into the largely untested intermediate-mass regime, reveal magnetic field structure in accretion disks through polarization studies, and test systematics in $H_0$ measurements.

title: Identifiable alignment of unpaired representations
text:
Title: Identifiable alignment of unpaired representations
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Aligning two models without paired data requires a distance that both share, yet existing methods use Euclidean or spherical geometry. This is either an arbitrary choice or imposed by their loss function. We show that, under a precise form of the manifold hypothesis, the pullback of the data metric gives such a distance for any two models of one data-generating process. This holds whether the models are encoders, decoders or both, and whatever their architecture, loss, prior or training data. The alignment map preserves this distance and the distribution of representations, and is identifiable if and only if the data distribution breaks every symmetry of the data manifold. We show that this symmetry breaking holds generically. Identifiability makes the alignment coupling the unique optimum of Gromov--Wasserstein and of its weighted combinations with a linear program. The linear program alone has the same optimum if almost every data point has a distinct distribution of distances. The coupling, and with it the alignment map, is recovered exactly from permuted samples, even without identifiability, and consistently from independent ones. Our method, Neural Gromov--Monge Alignment (NGMA), uses no pairs or labels and outperforms every unpaired and label-informed baseline. It relies on pullback distances to align image models with different priors and single-cell models trained on disjoint cells, where Euclidean distances fail.

title: Sufficient Dimension Reduction with Multimodal Predictor Objects
text:
Title: Sufficient Dimension Reduction with Multimodal Predictor Objects
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We study the regression of a scalar response $Y$ on a Euclidean predictor $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and a random predictor object $\mathcal{Z}$ in a general metric space under arbitrary structural dependence. We introduce a joint sufficient dimension reduction $(\mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{X}, \mathcal{G}_Z)$ constructed via a sequential conditional independence framework, which differs fundamentally from the ordinary central subspace of $Y \mid \mathbf{X}$. Methodologically, $\mathcal{Z}$ is embedded into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and a regularized kernel-response envelope model extracts a finite-dimensional reduction of the feature map. Partial adaptive estimation then recovers the Euclidean reduction conditional on the first-stage coordinates. We establish root-$n$ consistency rates for the first-stage envelope subspace under a shrinking regularizer, alongside large-sample consistency for the second-stage Euclidean subspace estimator. Simulations and two real-data applications illustrate the utility and flexibility of the proposed method.

title: From Granger causality to causal structure in dynamical systems
text:
Title: From Granger causality to causal structure in dynamical systems
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

The idea of testing whether the past of one signal improves the prediction of another can be traced back to Wiener. It was Granger who formalized the concept. Granger causality has become one of the most widely used tools to infer directed interactions between the components of a system. The name however can be misleading: it detects predictive relations among the measured signals, not causal relations among the mechanisms that generate them. This article starts by reviewing recent advances in observation-space Granger analysis. It then follows a path to directed structure in latent dynamical models, and asks under which conditions that structure can be read causally.

title: Lessons from double-plane lenses for galaxy profiles, the Hubble tension, and the mass-sheet degeneracy
text:
Title: Lessons from double-plane lenses for galaxy profiles, the Hubble tension, and the mass-sheet degeneracy
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Double-plane lenses, like single-plane lenses, are subject to the mass-sheet degeneracy, a fundamental limit to our knowledge of the deflector mass profiles from lensing. However, with a prior on the relative expansion history, unlike in the single-plane case, this degeneracy can be constrained with the modelling of lens images, without the need for time delays, velocity dispersion measurements or a prior on the Hubble constant $H_0$. We show that double-plane lenses are sensitive to a specific combination of the mass-sheet components of the two lens planes. Using literature values of the cosmological scaling factor from the double-plane lenses J0946 and AGEL0353, a measurement from the point-source images of J1721 (the ``Einstein zig-zag'' lens), and a reference value of $Ω_\mathrm{m}$, we show the constraints that can be placed on the mass-sheet component of each of these systems. We show that the additional information brought by images of a second source can improve measurements of $H_0$ from individual time-delay lenses by up to $\sim50\%$, depending on certain key assumptions. Using forecasted Euclid and LSST double-plane lens samples, we show that these samples will enable strong constraints on the population of mass sheets in lens galaxies. Such population constraints will have implications for a range of strong-lensing science applications, in particular in constraining $H_0$, dark energy, and the dark matter profiles of galaxies.

title: Boundary-controlled irreversible port--Hamiltonian modeling and structure-preserving discretization of tubular reactors
text:
Title: Boundary-controlled irreversible port--Hamiltonian modeling and structure-preserving discretization of tubular reactors
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This paper presents a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model and a structure-preserving spatial discretization for a non-isothermal tubular reactor with axial convection, variable-density momentum dynamics, chemical reaction, mass diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Reaction, diffusion, and heat conduction are described by irreversible port-Hamiltonian channels, whereas convection and momentum are represented by a weighted Eulerian interconnection. The boundary ports recover the axial energy flux and the corresponding entropy flux. A partitioned finite-element method is then formulated in conservative coordinates using a power-preserving change of variables. The semi-discrete model satisfies the Hamiltonian balance and a discrete entropy balance with non-negative entropy production due to reaction, diffusion, heat conduction, and jacket heat transfer. Numerical results for an open tubular reactor are validated against independently computed continuous steady boundary-value solutions and show the transient temperature, composition, and velocity profiles in the very-low-Mach regime. The same discretization is also tested with reciprocal Soret--Dufour coupling, for which the discrete entropy production remains non-negative.

title: Data-Driven Discovery of a Hyperelastic Strain-Energy Function for Veins Using Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks
text:
Title: Data-Driven Discovery of a Hyperelastic Strain-Energy Function for Veins Using Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Veins are commonly subjected to altered mechanical loading in clinical settings such as vein grafting, arteriovenous fistula creation, and tissue-engineered vascular graft implantation, making accurate constitutive models of venous tissue clinically important. Venous mechanical behavior differs characteristically from that of arteries, and existing constitutive models struggle to simultaneously fit the circumferential and axial stress-stretch responses across vein types. Here, we present a constitutive artificial neural network (CANN) framework that discovers a compact, interpretable hyperelastic constitutive model from biaxial mechanical data across three types of veins (saphenous, jugular, and inferior vena cava). The framework incorporates an expanded candidate function library with structurally motivated terms representing progressive fiber recruitment and fiber-family interactions. Sobol sensitivity analysis, correlation-based pruning, and response-level family collapse were then used to reduce the discovered basis to a compact strain-energy density function (SEF). The resulting eight-term SEF achieved significantly higher fitting accuracy than established venous constitutive models across all three types of veins $(R^2>0.9, p<0.01)$. These findings establish a framework for constitutive model discovery in veins and propose a candidate constitutive form for further validation across larger, independent cohorts.

title: Well-posedness and Quantitative Stability for Degenerate Fokker--Planck Equations with Rough Coefficients
text:
Title: Well-posedness and Quantitative Stability for Degenerate Fokker--Planck Equations with Rough Coefficients
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We establish quantitative stability and well-posedness for degenerate Fokker--Planck equations with Sobolev-regular and possibly fully degenerate diffusion coefficient. For two classes of rough drifts, stability estimates imply uniqueness, and existence is proved under suitable conditions. First, for anisotropic drifts with partial fractional Sobolev regularity, we prove both existence (as probability densities, essential for the probabilistic interpretation via superposition) and quantitative stability without imposing any growth conditions, covering the full range of fractional exponents and extending previous Lagrangian-flow results. Second, for drifts whose distributional gradients are given by singular integrals (e.g., Biot--Savart velocity fields from $L^1$ vorticity), we obtain stability estimates that allow the diffusion matrix to be time-space dependent and possibly degenerate, removing the prior restrictions of identity diffusion or bounded coefficients. Our results also recover the pure transport regime as a limiting case.

title: Chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in flavor branes
text:
Title: Chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in flavor branes
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We investigate the chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in the chiral symmetry broken phase of the holographic D3/D7 model with massless quarks, where the axial charge in the flavor sector can relax through transfer to the adjoint sector in the probe limit. We find that the dispersion relations of the quasi-normal modes are well described by the phenomenological expression for the chiral magnetic wave when the relaxation rate is small. We then determine how this rate depends on vector charge density and the chiral condensate. At higher temperatures, it increases with charge density and decreases with increasing condensate, while these dependences become non-monotonic at lower temperatures. These results show that the phenomenological description of the chiral magnetic wave also applies in the chiral symmetry broken phase in the quasi-hydrodynamic regime.

title: Science sandboxes measure the scientific capability of AI agents
text:
Title: Science sandboxes measure the scientific capability of AI agents
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Scientific progress depends not only on finding solutions, but on learning the rules that explain why they work and using that understanding to design better experiments. We introduce science sandboxes, a framework for studying this capability in AI agents through repeated cycles of experimentation, feedback, and hypothesis revision. Science sandboxes invite an agent to query the natural world in different ways, ranging from "wet" physical experiments, to "damp" predictive models trained on empirical data, to "dry" invented rules. By establishing a common experimental loop and a protocol for evaluating agents within it, science sandboxes allow assessment of both quantitative performance on specific metrics and qualitative scientific reasoning, across a spectrum of empirical verifiability. Here, we instantiate this framework in two biological settings, models of regulatory genomics and protein fitness prediction, and examine the capabilities of frontier agents. Across these settings, we could see when agents successfully optimized a quantitative metric without understanding the rules underlying the system. In particular, their scientific reasoning deteriorated when they encountered systems whose rules fell outside familiar biological priors. By highlighting such failure modes, science sandboxes make the frontier of scientific capability measurable and provide a controlled setting in which to study and ultimately expand it.

title: Weak Quasi-Convexity: First- and Second-Order Conditions, Monotonicity, and Quadratic Functions
text:
Title: Weak Quasi-Convexity: First- and Second-Order Conditions, Monotonicity, and Quadratic Functions
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

In this paper we introduce weakly quasi-convex functions, which are a generalization of weakly convex functions. We study the behavior of weakly quasi-convex functions in Euclidean spaces. We provide several illustrative examples that demonstrate the scope and distinctive features of this new class of generalized convex functions. We derive a necessary condition for weak quasi-convexity under certain assumptions and provide an example showing that its converse is not true for discontinuous functions. Under the continuity assumption on the function involved, a sufficient condition is provided with an adjusted weak quasi-convexity modulus. Also, we bring out various kinds of monotonicity in connection with weakly quasi-convex functions through the gradient mapping. We provide several illustrative examples that interpret and emphasize the newly introduced notions. We establish a first-order necessary condition for the class of differentiable weakly quasi-convex functions. Conversely, we show that a differentiable function satisfying this first-order condition is weakly quasi-convex with an adjusted modulus. We provide a second-order necessary condition under appropriate assumptions using second-order Dini derivatives. As a consequence, we derive a Hessian-based necessary condition for the class of twice continuously differentiable weakly quasi-convex functions. We provide an example to show that the converse of the second-order characterization does not hold. Furthermore, we establish various kinds of necessary conditions concerning general quadratic functions and provide many counterexamples for the failure of their sufficiency. Finally, we derive several consequences of weak quasi-convexity for optimization problems.

title: Putting a Temperature on Electron Correlation
text:
Title: Putting a Temperature on Electron Correlation
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

It is common wisdom that a better understanding of how to quantify electron correlation should lead to more efficient treatments of the correlation problem. Here, we not only substantiate this view but turn it into a concrete, systematic framework for ground states. Since prominent correlation measures such as the nonfreeness depend only on the one-particle reduced density matrix, modeling the correlation energy as a function of such a measure naturally places the framework within reduced density matrix functional theory, while keeping the cost at mean-field level. Strikingly, the variable conjugate to the measure emerges as a ``correlation temperature'', thereby connecting correlation measures, functional theory, and effective temperatures. The framework rationalizes methods such as i-DMFT, and we illustrate its key concepts analytically for the Hubbard dimer and numerically for small molecular systems. This brings a fundamental question within reach: how much of the correlation problem can be solved at mean-field cost?

title: Thouless pumping and Haldane-model topology in a driven extended SSH chain
text:
Title: Thouless pumping and Haldane-model topology in a driven extended SSH chain
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Thouless pumping provides a powerful route for probing Chern topology through quantized motion in one-dimensional lattices. We investigate such a topological pump in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. A graphical representation in Bloch space is used to construct pumping schemes. In this framework, the Bloch vector traces a closed loop that evolves in time. The Chern number of the synthetic band is then determined by the motion of this loop. Quantum pumping phenomena are demonstrated for a filled band and for a bosonic wave packet driven by Bloch oscillations. We further show that the Haldane model can be mapped to the driven extended SSH chain by replacing a quasimomentum by the pumping time. The quantized charge pump indicates that the Chern number of a two-dimensional model can be read out from a one-dimensional pumping protocol, offering an accessible route for detecting higher-dimensional topology, such as in photonic and cold-atom platforms.

title: CIR-DDG: backbone-agnostic residual correction of antibody-antigen affinity changes with explicit cross-chain geometry
text:
Title: CIR-DDG: backbone-agnostic residual correction of antibody-antigen affinity changes with explicit cross-chain geometry
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Motivation: Accurate prediction of mutation-induced protein--protein binding free-energy changes is important for antibody affinity maturation, yet scarce labels and complex interface geometry limit generalization. Heterogeneous predictors may process three-dimensional complexes without preserving the cross-chain signals most relevant to a mutation in their final scalar output. Results: We introduce CIR-DDG, a lightweight residual adapter that combines a fixed base prediction with 22 interpretable descriptors of cross-chain distance, contact density and site--partner context. In complex-level five-fold evaluation on SKEMPI 2.0 measurements from 343 complexes, CIR-DDG improved all six tested backbones on antibody--antigen interface mutations: Spearman correlation increased by 0.0346--0.1296, while RMSE decreased by 0.0074--0.0408\kcalmol. Cross-validated probing, equal-capacity controls and feature ablations support the complementarity of explicit geometry. On an independent SARS-CoV-2 RBD--ACE2 deep-mutational-scan benchmark of 3669 substitutions, the fold-specific adapters transferred without any retraining: the absolute interface Spearman correlation increased by 0.026--0.081 for all four evaluable backbones, showing that the learned geometric correction generalizes beyond SKEMPI thermodynamic measurements. Availability and implementation: CIR-DDG is available at https://github.com/ecnuabmlab/CIR-ddG.

title: Is there a density-gradient expansion for the electronic exchange energy?
text:
Title: Is there a density-gradient expansion for the electronic exchange energy?
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

An old but recurring question in ground-state density functional theory, relevant to the construction of density functional approximations, is the existence of a second-order gradient expansion for the exchange energy that is exact for densities that vary slowly over space. Here we will argue that there is such an expansion, with a gradient coefficient 10/7 of Sham's, as suggested by theoretical/mathematical derivations and by numerical calculations on model slowly-varying metallic densities, although some standard derivations do not quite capture the correct gradient coefficient. We also discuss long-range anomalies in the gradient expansions for the exchange and correlation holes around an electron. It is plausible that, as suggested earlier and recently, standard derivations are still correct for the coefficient of the second-order gradient expansion for exchange and correlation together, in which case the correct gradient coefficient for correlation is $C_{\mathrm{c}}$ = $C_{\mathrm{xc}}$ - $C_{\mathrm{x}}$. We propose possible numerical evaluations of $C_{\mathrm{xc}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{x}}$ that are free from long-range anomalies, and discuss implications for density functional approximations. Axel Becke's 1988 generalized gradient approximation (the B88 GGA) for the exchange energy brought density functional theory into chemistry, with a gradient coefficient for exchange that is optimal at the GGA level for atoms and molecules but too large for solids. Meta-GGAs seem to work as well for molecules as for solids, but may not be perfected yet. The article concludes with a few memories that the first author has of discussions with Axel Becke.

title: Perils and opportunities of AI for public climate services
text:
Title: Perils and opportunities of AI for public climate services
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative and machine-learning systems, in climate services development and provision is transforming how climate information is produced, accessed, and interpreted. AI-enabled climate services offer significant opportunities for process automation, optimisation, tailoring, and the translation of complex climate data into actionable knowledge for diverse users. However, the growing reliance on privately controlled algorithms, data infrastructures, and computing facilities raises critical concerns related to governance, transparency, equity and economic sustainability, among others. While the technical architecture of climate services increasingly relies on advanced machine learning and large-scale climate models, their legitimacy as public services may be weakened in the absence of arrangements that prioritise public value and long-lasting societal benefit over profit maximisation. The tension between the public mandate of climate services and the private nature of AI infrastructure challenges traditional notions of openness. Using a consensus-based elicitation method coupled with the PESTLE framework, we analyse the political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental risks and opportunities shaping the co-production value chain of AI-enabled climate services. We draw policy-relevant conclusions for data, model and infrastructure supporting the next generation of upstream and downstream climate services as critical applications for society. Our work presents potential and plausible challenges and benefits for a pan-European, decentralised public climate service built on sovereign AI infrastructure and open governance principles.

title: A Scientific Claim Stability Framework for Evaluating MRI Morphometry Pipelines
text:
Title: A Scientific Claim Stability Framework for Evaluating MRI Morphometry Pipelines
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

MRI morphometry pipelines are often evaluated by measurement agreement or downstream accuracy, yet their scientific value depends on the conclusions they support. Two pipelines can produce similar feature-level results yet support different conclusions about aging, cognitive decline, or neurodegeneration. We introduce Scientific Claim Stability (SCS), a claim-centric evaluation framework that converts region-of-interest (ROI) morphometry tables into auditable claim cards and evaluates their support under changes in dataset, processing pipeline, atlas, feature family, and target. Across 10,370 MRI scans from three datasets and five cohorts, SCS generates 2,783 claim cards and evaluates 89 claim-family pairs. The evaluation distinguishes stable, transferable, and fragile claims. FreeSurfer 8-FastSurfer comparisons show high evidence concordance and low anatomical-support overlap under the primary covariate specification. Acquisition-adjusted analyses show that the magnitude of support disagreement depends on the model specification. Structured review by specialists in geriatrics, neuroscience, and radiology, alongside auxiliary ChatGPT and Gemini reviewers, assesses claim plausibility, clarity, faithfulness, usefulness, and caution. SCS provides a reproducible way to audit the evidential stability of morphometry claims without assuming a universal gold standard.

title: Simulating and Characterizing Non-Gaussian Small-Scale Polarized Emission
text:
Title: Simulating and Characterizing Non-Gaussian Small-Scale Polarized Emission
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Galactic foregrounds present a major challenge for cosmic microwave background (CMB) cosmology as their amplitudes exceed the target primordial $B$-mode signal.
