While small-scale interstellar medium (ISM) emission is expected to be highly complex, current foreground simulations cannot reproduce the filamentary, non-Gaussian features of ISM structure in a stochastic way. To address this gap, we introduce a framework for generating stochastic small-scale foreground emission, using polarized synchrotron observations as an example use case. This method is capable of producing many independent realizations that additionally inherit morphological information from large angular scales. The underlying structural complexity incorporates anisotropic, multifractal, and advected non-Gaussian features that are tunable with a small number of parameters that carry physical interpretations. Because standard power spectra do not describe the complex phase coherence required for the structural complexity, we evaluate the synthetic fields using higher-order statistics, demonstrating that the Minkowski functionals and structure functions partially capture varying degrees of non-Gaussianity. This work lays the necessary foundation for new foreground simulation suites with stochastic realizations of possible non-Gaussian structure.

title: A Review of Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control Algorithms: State of the Art and Research Opportunities
text:
Title: A Review of Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control Algorithms: State of the Art and Research Opportunities
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Max-Pressure (MP) has emerged as a widely studied decentralized traffic signal control framework, thanks to its desirable theoretical properties and strong control performance. Early research on MP focused on improving control performance by exploring different variables of the traffic state for the definition of pressure. Subsequent studies expanded MP to incorporate the complexity of real-world transportation systems and emerging technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive review of these developments. The review first introduces the theoretical foundations of MP and examines early developments in movement weight definition. It then synthesizes major extensions for multimodal and multiscale network control, followed by recent developments in connected and automated vehicle (CAV) environments and the integration of MP with artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven methods. Beyond summarizing existing approaches, this review examines their underlying assumptions, data requirements, implementation considerations, and practical limitations. Based on this comprehensive review, key research gaps and future directions are identified, including remaining limitations in the theoretical foundations of MP and the underexplored integration of autonomous vehicle control with the MP framework. Overall, this review provides a structured perspective on the evolution and current state of MP control and highlights opportunities for developing more proactive, robust, and practically deployable MP-based traffic control methods.

title: Regret without Optimal-Arm Feedback under Reward-Dependent Delays
text:
Title: Regret without Optimal-Arm Feedback under Reward-Dependent Delays
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

We study stochastic bandits with reward-dependent delays, possibly infinite, whose reports omit the originating round. For each $c\in[0,1)$, Balanced Historical Optimism (BHO) has a delay term controlled by the largest suboptimal-arm quantile at level $1-cΔ_i$, without requiring optimal-arm reports. Lower bounds give an inverse-square slack cost in the logarithmic statistical regime and linear minimax regret at $c=1$. A family with growing $K$ forces worst-case regret $Ω(G\log K)$ for every learner, where $G=\max_iΔ_i h_i$ is the largest gap-weighted suboptimal cutoff. Pending-triggered balance preserves BHO's weighted-cutoff bound for $c<1$ and attains the historical-greedy exploration coefficient with deterministic rewards, a unique optimum and fixed bounded delays. Gap-weighted comparisons and experiments show when shared waiting helps and what balanced exploration costs.

title: Agents Propose, Code Verifies, Humans Decide: Verified Agentic Ingestion of Heterogeneous Scientific Tables into Relational Databases
text:
Title: Agents Propose, Code Verifies, Humans Decide: Verified Agentic Ingestion of Heterogeneous Scientific Tables into Relational Databases
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Public scientific datasets rarely arrive analysis-ready. They arrive as messy folders of wide matrices, long tables, spreadsheets, and per-cohort files whose keys and encodings differ, and every reanalysis must reconnect them first. A coding agent can automate this, but its mistakes can look plausible, and without an audit trail, a mistake that corrupts data can go uncaught. We present an AI-assisted ingestion pipeline built on one rule: LLM agents propose, deterministic code verifies, and humans decide. Narrow agents see compact, citable evidence about the files, never the data, and return typed proposals. A verifier with 39 check types tests each proposal against that evidence in two loops, one for the schema's structure and one for its meaning, and a human reviewer approves the schema and the load. Code compiles PostgreSQL DDL, reshapes the data, quarantines rows it cannot place, records provenance, and reconciles every staged row against the database. On four public biomedical datasets, one held out from development, 9 of 20 first proposals failed a check and every failure was caught: the loops repaired eight, and a one-line reviewer edit fixed the ninth. All 45.1 million values loaded with zero reconciliation gap. Discovering a dataset's structure took 4-7 LLM calls and preparing its data at most one more, costing under $0.50 per dataset. In a separate test, each of nine planted data errors was quarantined with a reason or recorded in an audit log.

title: FlowLOT: Linearized Optimal Transport for Flow Cytometry Analysis
text:
Title: FlowLOT: Linearized Optimal Transport for Flow Cytometry Analysis
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Multiparameter flow cytometry generates high-dimensional, unordered single-cell mea- surement data for disease diagnosis and monitoring, yet analysis often remains dependent on manual gating, limiting scalability and reproducibility. Existing machine-learning ap- proaches can reduce annotation burden but frequently require large training cohorts and offer limited interpretability. To address these challenges, we introduce FlowLOT , an optimal-transport-based framework that models the single-cell measurement data of a pa- tient sample as an empirical cellular distribution and maps it directly into a fixed-length feature vector. Within a single transparent architecture, FlowLOT unifies high-dimensional classification, interpretable visualization, and continuous quantitative inference. In few-shot regimes, using as few as 16 patients per class on FlowCAP-II and 8 patients per class on BLAST110, it accurately distinguishes healthy from acute myeloid leukemia (AML) sam- ples, reaching 94.3% and 98.0% balanced accuracy, respectively. The underlying embedding exposes marker-level variation driving disease-associated population shifts and enables quantitative measurable residual disease (MRD) estimation, achieving a Pearson correlation of 0.82 on held-out samples and 0.79 under cross-dataset transfer. Furthermore, at the clinically relevant 0.1% threshold for leukemia-associated immunophenotype (LAIP) residual disease, FlowLOT detects positivity with 72% sensitivity at 100% specificity. By replacing subjective manual gating and black-box deep learning with a distribution-aware framework, FlowLOT offers a sample-efficient, scalable, and interpretable solution for high- dimensional cytometry under realistic clinical and experimental constraints.

title: A Momentum-weighted Interface Stabilization Approach for Fluid-Structure Interaction with Strong Added-Mass Effects
text:
Title: A Momentum-weighted Interface Stabilization Approach for Fluid-Structure Interaction with Strong Added-Mass Effects
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Partitioned fluid-structure interaction (FSI) schemes permit the reuse of optimized standalone solvers but can become unstable under strong fluid added-mass effects, particularly when structural inertia is small relative to fluid inertia. This work traces the instability to the discrepancy between the interface pressure Schur complements of the monolithic and Dirichlet- Neumann partitioned systems, as revealed by a fixed-point analysis of the linearized FSI problem. Motivated by this analysis, a momentum-weighted interface stabilization (MWIS) is proposed, in which the interface pressure block of the fluid subproblem is augmented by an operator constructed from the fluid and structural interface momentum operators. The augmentation is consistent by construction, vanishing at convergence so that the monolithic solution is recovered. A sparse diagonal approximation of the operator, derived from element metrics, limits intersolver data exchange to quantities comparable in size to standard interface coupling data while requiring minimal modifications to the standalone solvers. Numerical experiments, spanning a linear model and established nonlinear FSI benchmarks, demonstrate improved coupling robustness in regimes of strong added-mass where the standard Dirichlet-Neumann scheme diverges.

title: Entanglement percolation enhanced by the power of choice
text:
Title: Entanglement percolation enhanced by the power of choice
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum communication networks are best supported by maximally entangled states, but imperfections in entanglement generation and distribution generally limit the distributed states to being only partially entangled. Therefore, protocols typically consisting of local operations and classical communication are required to create suitably entangled networks. Here, we introduce a power-of-choice (PoC) protocol based on reversing the selection criteria in the Achlioptas process previously considered in classical explosive percolation. The resulting PoC protocol anticipates the entanglement percolation transition, thereby reducing the entanglement resources needed to establish quantum communication. Notably, in contrast to explosive percolation, the PoC protocol admits an implementation using local information with no appreciable loss of performance.

title: The logarithm construction and (super) Weyl anomalies
text:
Title: The logarithm construction and (super) Weyl anomalies
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We apply the logarithm construction of higher-derivative conformal primary (super) fields proposed by Butter et al. to derive simple Wess-Zumino actions for: (i) Weyl anomalies in arbitrary even dimensions; (ii) $\mathcal{N} =1$ and $\mathcal{N}=2$ super-Weyl anomalies in four dimensions; and (iii) $(p,q)$ super-Weyl anomalies in two dimensions, with $p,q \leq 2$.

title: A meta-algorithm for ab initio reconstruction of complex mixtures in cryo-EM
text:
Title: A meta-algorithm for ab initio reconstruction of complex mixtures in cryo-EM
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

We describe a systematic approach for spawning and aggregating multi-class cryo-EM reconstruction jobs. This approach formalizes standard ad hoc strategies of iterative classification and filtering typically used by practitioners to sort impure, heterogeneous samples. To our knowledge, this is the first method that can successfully perform ab initio reconstruction on datasets containing dozens of distinct species. We obtain 97% accuracy on ab initio reconstruction of a 45-class subset of Tomotwin-100, 75% accuracy on the full Tomotwin-100 dataset, and demonstrate recovery of ribosomal assembly states from an unfiltered experimental cryo-EM dataset. Our approach's capability scales with compute and lays the foundation for automated cryo-EM workflows in modern experimental settings.

title: Robust paths to primordial $B$ modes in the presence of polarised point source contamination
text:
Title: Robust paths to primordial $B$ modes in the presence of polarised point source contamination
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

A detection of primordial $B$ modes in the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarisation relies on a robust control and removal of contamination from astrophysical polarised foreground emission. We examine how much polarised extragalactic point sources may contaminate the cosmological signal in ground-based CMB experiments, propagating their impact through component separation to the final parameter constraints. We discuss masking and modelling strategies to ensure that the resulting constraints remain both accurate and precise under this source of contamination. We produce synthetic data containing polarised emission from extragalactic radio sources (ERSs) and dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) following state-of-the-art models for both samples. We find that, while the DSFG contribution is likely too small to cause any significant bias to the cosmological or foreground parameters, the ERS contribution instead, if left unmasked, leads to a bias in the parameters describing the Galactic synchrotron and lensing $B$-mode components. For experiments targeting noise levels of order $σ_P\simeq 1\,μK\,{\rm arcmin}$, we find that masking all ERSs with fluxes above $\sim$0.1 Jy, coupled with a relatively simple model to marginalise over residual point-source contamination, achieves a suitable balance that allows for the robust recovery of unbiased cosmological and foreground parameters at a negligible cost in parameter uncertainties.

title: Evolutionary Informed Translation from Protein to Nucleic Acid Sequence
text:
Title: Evolutionary Informed Translation from Protein to Nucleic Acid Sequence
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The choice of nucleic acid sequence for a given protein strongly impacts function and is species-specific. Current protein-to-nucleic-acid translation models treat sequences in isolation, often over-favoring frequently used codons. To generate more natural nucleic acid sequences, we introduce PINATA (Phylogenetically Informed protein to Nucleic Acid Translation with sequence Alignment), a model that leverages sequences from related species encoded in multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) to guide prediction. Our architecture leverages evolutionary context and learns species-and protein specific context to make biologically-informed predictions. Evaluated across 61,934 gene trees and 882 species, PINATA generates sequences that mirror the naturally-occurring sequence substantially better than existing language models. PINATA leverages MSA data to improve exact native codon recovery by 17.95 percentage points over existing language models, effectively preserves natural rare-codon nuances, and more closely matches native sequence properties. PINATA maintains strong predictive performance even with limited evolutionary data. While previous methods largely treated sequences from different species in isolation, our method leverages the evolutionary relationships between nucleic acids and proteins across species to create a more biologically-informed translation. We demonstrate that leveraging rich evolutionary data through an biologically-designed method strongly aids in translating protein sequences to nucleic acid sequences across species. We will make data and code publicly available upon publication.

title: Uniform Central Limit Theorems for Degree Distributions of Sparse Graphon Models
text:
Title: Uniform Central Limit Theorems for Degree Distributions of Sparse Graphon Models
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

The degree distribution is among the most basic summaries of a network, yet no functional limit theorem for the empirical degree distribution of graphon models has been available, even for dense, bounded graphons, for which only finite-dimensional results were known. We study the empirical degree distribution of sparse $L^p$ graphon models, allowing unbounded kernels and hence heavy-tailed degrees. For graphons whose latent expected degrees have a density, we prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem whenever $nρ_n/\log n\to\infty$ and $nρ_n^{2+β}\to0$, where $ρ_n$ is the sparsity level and the kernel has $2+β$ moments for some $β>0$; the limiting covariance coincides with that of the dense case. Under additional local regularity, we establish a functional central limit theorem on compact intervals in the interior of the support. Under tail regularity and a stronger sparsity condition, we prove that uniformity extends to unbounded intervals. We also show that uniform limits fail at atoms of the degree distribution, for instance in stochastic block models. The analysis rests on an exact multilinear representation of the conditional degree distribution, which identifies its Hoeffding decomposition without Edgeworth expansions, combined with a lattice version of Billingsley's tightness criterion and moment inequalities of Efron-Stein type.

title: Interacting scalar-fermion two-component dark matter in a gauged $\boldsymbol{U(1)_{B-L}}$ model
text:
Title: Interacting scalar-fermion two-component dark matter in a gauged $\boldsymbol{U(1)_{B-L}}$ model
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We propose an interacting two-component dark matter model based on a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model, which also accommodates neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism. The dark sector consists of a Dirac fermion $χ$ and a complex scalar $S$, which can both be stable without imposing an additional discrete symmetry and are directly coupled by a gauge-invariant Yukawa interaction. The resulting conversion, semi-conversion, and semi-annihilation processes lead to a genuinely coupled freeze-out. After imposing collider and dark matter constraints, we identify viable solutions away from the $Z'$ resonance for both mass hierarchies, $m_S > m_χ$ and $m_S < m_χ$. Despite the strong direct-detection constraints, part of the surviving parameter space remains within the reach of next-generation experiments.

title: Dwarf Galaxy Reticulum II's MeerKAT L-Band Observation: Constraining WIMP Dark Matter
text:
Title: Dwarf Galaxy Reticulum II's MeerKAT L-Band Observation: Constraining WIMP Dark Matter
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The nature of dark matter remains one of the most profound open questions in modern physics, with weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) among the leading candidates proposed to account for the observed anomalies across cosmic scales. If WIMPs annihilate or decay in the dense dark matter haloes of nearby galaxies, the resulting high-energy electrons/positrons can produce synchrotron radiation in the presence of ambient magnetic fields, yielding a potentially detectable radio signature. Dwarf spheroidal galaxies are particularly promising targets for indirect dark matter searches due to their high mass-to-light ratios and low astrophysical foreground contamination. While radio observations have been widely used to constrain WIMP properties in these systems, the resulting limits remain highly sensitive to poorly constrained magnetic field assumptions. Here we utilize L-band ($1.3$--$1.5$ GHz) observations from the MeerKAT array directed towards dwarf galaxy Reticulum II and measure the surface brightness profile across the dwarf galaxy. Combining these measurements with theoretical models of WIMP annihilation and yield 95% confidence level upper limits on the WIMP annihilation cross-section $\langleσv\rangle \lesssim 10^{-26}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ for masses $m_χ\sim 10$-$200$ GeV (with the assumed uniform magnetic field model and diffusion constant). As next-generation radio facilities such as the Square Kilometre Array come online, robust characterisation of magnetic environments in dwarf galaxies will be essential to fully exploit their sensitivity to the particle nature of dark matter.

title: A physics-based-preconditioned quasi-Newton solver for energy- and momentum-conserving implicit hybrid particle-in-cell simulations
text:
Title: A physics-based-preconditioned quasi-Newton solver for energy- and momentum-conserving implicit hybrid particle-in-cell simulations
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Explicit hybrid particle-in-cell (PIC) schemes, with kinetic ions and fluid electrons, accumulate numerical heating over long simulations and are unstable to finite-grid instabilities. Energy-conserving implicit integration removes heating and instabilities, but may be inefficient due to the need of nonlinear iteration. We present a fast quasi-Newton solver for an implicit hybrid-PIC formulation. The nonlinear residual employs the electric field and electron pressure as nonlinear unknowns, and nonlinearly eliminates particles. The formulation is strictly energy conserving and, on Cartesian meshes, also momentum conserving. The nonlinear iteration is efficiently performed with a quasi-Newton solver that replaces the true Jacobian with an approximate one without spoiling conservation properties upon convergence. The approximate Jacobian replaces the particle ion linear response with an analytical mass matrix that is local and requires minimal storage. This approximate Jacobian is efficiently inverted with a physics-based multigrid preconditioner, adapted from Hall MHD. We verify the scheme linearly with whistler, kinetic Alfvén, and cylindrical normal modes, and nonlinearly with the GEM reconnection challenge. On GEM, explicit integration needs a forty-times-smaller time step, and nine times the wall-clock time, to reach an energy conservation comparable to that of the implicit solver. We apply the method to the simulation of a three-dimensional field-reversed configuration formation by external coils.

title: On the Minimal Controllability of Boolean Networks With $k$-Regular Dependency Graphs
text:
Title: On the Minimal Controllability of Boolean Networks With $k$-Regular Dependency Graphs
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Boolean networks (BNs) are widely used to model gene regulatory networks and other biological systems. In this paper, we investigate the minimal controllability problem for BNs subject to degree constraints. We first establish three new best-case upper bounds for XOR-BNs whose dependency graphs are $k$-regular. We then introduce classes of BNs that are invariant under cyclically partite transformation (CPT-invariant) and prove theorems connecting BN controllability with the surjectivity of vector-valued Boolean functions. Finally, by combining an analysis of this surjectivity with a probabilistic argument, we derive a new general lower bound on the minimum number of control nodes required for majority-type threshold BNs with $(2k+1)$-regular dependency graphs.

title: Electrically tunable superconducting dimensionality in stripe-ordered monolayer MoTe$_2$
text:
Title: Electrically tunable superconducting dimensionality in stripe-ordered monolayer MoTe$_2$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Dimensionality governs the stability of collective quantum states, including whether Cooper pairs can establish the phase coherence required for superconductivity. In solids, however, electronic dimensionality is usually encoded in the crystal structure and is difficult to control reversibly. Here we show evidence that monolayer 1$T^{\prime}$-MoTe$_2$ develops a stripe charge-density wave that reorganizes its low-energy electronic states into quasi-one-dimensional channels. Raman spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy identify the stripe order, whereas directional transport and tunneling spectroscopy reveal superconducting correlations confined to the stripe direction and insulating behavior perpendicular to it. Electrostatic doping weakens the transverse insulating response and drives the system into phase-coherent two-dimensional superconductivity. These results show that stripe charge order can reconfigure superconducting dimensionality and make it electrically tunable within a single crystalline layer.

title: Knowledge-Enriched Structured EHR Features for 30-Day Hospital Readmission Prediction on MIMIC-IV
text:
Title: Knowledge-Enriched Structured EHR Features for 30-Day Hospital Readmission Prediction on MIMIC-IV
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Recent approaches to 30-day hospital readmission prediction rely on pre-trained language models applied to discharge summaries. Although these methods achieve strong performance, they depend on the availability of clinical notes, incur substantial computational costs, and yield representations that lack interpretability. We propose a knowledge-enriched feature representation that augments structured Electronic Health Record (EHR) data with four medical knowledge sources: disease ontology mapping, procedure classification, drug ingredient vocabulary, and organ system laboratory aggregation, without using clinical notes. Each feature dimension corresponds to a named clinical concept, yielding a sparse and interpretable patient representation. The approach is evaluated with six classifiers on a MIMIC-IV v2.2 cohort. Under 20-fold cross-validation, the best configuration achieves an AUROC of 0.743. This performance is comparable to that of previously reported methods on this dataset, including both those using only structured data and those incorporating clinical notes, while requiring considerably less computational cost. Interpretability analysis shows that demographics, organ system labs, drug ingredient features, and first-level ontology disease categories drive prediction, while deeper hierarchy levels contribute negligibly. These findings indicate that knowledge-enriched structured features offer a competitive and efficient alternative to embeddings from clinical notes for 30-day readmission prediction.

title: Spectral properties of the Riemann zeta function and their physical applications
text:
Title: Spectral properties of the Riemann zeta function and their physical applications
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

This work studies the Riemann $ζ$ numerically with emphasis on its physical manifestations. Three areas are examined: (i) the spectral statistics of the non-trivial zeros, which we compare with the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble predictions, obtaining $χ^2/\text{dof} = 1.2$; (ii) the role of $ζ(\frac{3}{2})$ in determining the critical temperature for Bose-Einstein condensation, where we find $T_c = 0.13$ K for an ideal gas; and (iii) the application of $ζ$-function regularisation to the Casimir effect, yielding the standard Casimir energy density $-\frac{π^2 \hbar c}{720 a^3}$, which for $a=1\,\mathrm{nm}$ gives $\sim -4.33\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-2}}$. The numerical results are consistent with the Montgomery-Odlyzko conjecture and with spectral approaches motivated by the Hilbert-Pólya conjecture, within the statistical limitations of the analysis.

title: Axiomatic Learning and Probabilistic Structures with first applications to variants of Arithmetic Machine Learning and beyond
text:
Title: Axiomatic Learning and Probabilistic Structures with first applications to variants of Arithmetic Machine Learning and beyond
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We introduce the Axiomatic Learning Structures (ALS) and Axiomatic Probabilistic Structure (APS) in order to study the interactions of Machine Learning, Optimization, with research frameworks- which, we take the view, can be characterized at the core by the corresponding axioms. The ALS explores the interplays between structures that one is interested in Learning Theory such as Loss functions and the axioms of the objects and transformations involved in these functions. The APS studies the interaction between structures of interest in Probability Theory such as Gibbs distributions, equations with noise, etc. and the axioms of the corresponding objects and transformations. We also introduce in Section 6 Transformations-Axiomatic Based Learning (TABLe) on Mathematical data-sets. One feature of this approach is the ranking of transformations from a table for a certain task based on scores which reflect which transformations work better than others, similarly to when human investigators try various methods on a task. We also study structure recovery from noisy data. In particular, to exemplify the ideas, we consider loss functions which contain derivations and derivations-like transformations. As a first application we study recovery in the context of polynomials with integer coefficients using standard derivatives along with other types of derivations which appear in Arithmetic: the p-derivations which satisfy \textit{different axioms} from the usual derivatives. As a first application of the APS we study a class of noisy (partial/mixed) derivations equations. In the last sections, to provide further potential applications of this framework, we give an overview of an initial simplified Opinion Dynamics model and its (simultaneous) study of rules of updates.

title: Molecular architecture of TE-seeded chromosome-naive initiation networks of protein-protein interactions delineates the Human Protein Map of the assembly of multiprotein complexes
text:
Title: Molecular architecture of TE-seeded chromosome-naive initiation networks of protein-protein interactions delineates the Human Protein Map of the assembly of multiprotein complexes
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Upon binding to transposable elements seeded DNA, initiator transcription factors are poised to activate the hybrid assembly pathways (HAP) of endogenous multiprotein complexes (EMC) by iteratively engaging protein-protein interaction (PPI) cascade and creating cell type-specific pools of protein dimers. Here, molecular features and inferred biological functions of PPI cascade constituents were elucidated within the context of cell type-specific intracellular protein monomer pools documented in the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) of 154 human cell types. The following key features of the molecular architecture and functional performance of the 4 families of PPI cascade constituents were documented within the HPA contexts of intracellular proteomes: a) the ubiquitous expression and balanced representation; c) the universal availability and engagements; d) constitutive {invariant) and cell type-specific assembly profiles of EMCs. The biological relevance of the PPI cascades is demonstrated by cell-type-resolved multiprotein complex-engagement analysis across the HPA of human body, which faithfully recovers without supervision the intrinsic lineage structures of EMCs and lineage-specific master-regulator multiprotein assemblies. PPI cascade constituents have the capacity to generate 51,830 protein dimers within the proteome availability contexts of 154 types of human cells. Present analyses revealed critical impacts of the persistence of proteinopathy proteins that may cause the damage to the PPI cascade performance by sequestering 44 synaptic proteins. The sequestration of synaptic proteins withdraws structural-functional components of synapses suggesting a mechanism contributing to the pathogenesis of neurodegeneration. Conversely, reconstitution of availability of defined synaptic structural proteins appears to restore stoichiometry and recovers the lost assembly of synaptic protein dimers.

title: Hilbert space in the flat limit of AdS/CFT. II. Massless particles
text:
Title: Hilbert space in the flat limit of AdS/CFT. II. Massless particles
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Building on Part I of this series, where we described the emergence of massive scattering states, we demonstrate how unitary lowest-weight representations $\mathcal D(Δ,s)$ of the conformal group with fixed dimension $Δ$ and arbitrary integer spin $s$ contract to massless Poincaré particle representations. This requires combining the Inönü--Wigner contraction $\mathfrak{so}(2,3) \to \mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$ with an infinite boost, in which case massless scattering states naturally emerge in a carrollian basis. For $Δ>s+1$, we find that $\mathcal D(Δ,s)$ contracts to the direct sum of massless particles of all spins $s'\leq s$. At the unitarity bound, lower-spin states become null so that $\mathcal D(s+1,s)$ contracts to a single massless particle representation carrying the two maximal helicities $J=\pm s$. In both cases, the inner product converges to the Poincaré-invariant one after a single helicity-independent rescaling, so that unitarity is preserved throughout the contraction.

title: An electromechanically coupled multiphase-field model with generalized kinetic relations for ferroelectrics
text:
Title: An electromechanically coupled multiphase-field model with generalized kinetic relations for ferroelectrics
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Classical phase-field models typically use the Allen--Cahn evolution law to model interface motion as a consequence of energy-gradient descent. This implies a linear kinetic relation between the velocity of an interface (e.g., a domain wall in a ferroelectric) and its driving force. When nonlinear kinetic relations are to be modeled, as commonly found in ferroelectric ceramics, an alternative evolution law and hence an alternative model is needed. Here, we propose an electromechanically (stress-driven) coupled multiphase-field framework with a general kinetic formulation, which integrates a prescribed kinetic relation directly into the evolution law. We show that this model correctly evolves domain walls with the assigned nonlinear kinetics, e.g., of mixed exponential-power law type, following the so-called Merz--Stadler law. The multiphase formulation further enables distinct kinetic relations and interfacial energies to be assigned to different order-parameter pairs, which reflects the distinguishable properties of the different types of ferroelectric domain walls. The proposed framework is broadly applicable for simulating kinetic relations in materials with applications beyond ferroelectrics.

title: From Quantum Field Fluctuations to High-Redshift AGN: Semiclassical Origins of Halo Mass Function Constraints in the JWST Era
text:
Title: From Quantum Field Fluctuations to High-Redshift AGN: Semiclassical Origins of Halo Mass Function Constraints in the JWST Era
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We develop a continuous framework connecting quantum field fluctuations in the early Universe to the abundance and observable properties of galaxies and active galactic nuclei (AGN) at cosmic dawn. Beginning with quantum fields in curved Friedmann Lemaitre Robertson Walker spacetime, we follow inflationary vacuum fluctuations into the primordial curvature spectrum, linear matter power spectrum, mass variance $σ(M,z)$, mass peak height $ν(M,z)$, and the statistics of nonlinear halo formation. The Press-Schechter and Sheth-Tormen formalisms provide an analytic description of halo abundance and its dependence on peak rarity. A complementary high redshift halo mass function calibrated with the GUREFT simulations of Yung et al. (2024) provides a numerical description specifically constructed for the cosmic dawn regime probed by JWST. The comparison between these analytic and simulation calibrated prescriptions provides a direct measure of the sensitivity of predicted halo populations to the observations. We separate this cosmological supply of halos from the astrophysical and observational mappings that produce stars, ultraviolet luminosities, and active galactic nuclei. Controlled numerical experiments show that a percent level perturbation in the primordial fluctuation amplitude produces only a modest change in $σ$ and $ν$, but can strongly amplify the exponentially suppressed high $ν$ tail of the Halo Mass Function. This sensitivity increases toward high halo mass and high redshift, identifying rare cosmic dawn populations as potentially powerful probes of primordial statistics while simultaneously exposing the importance of uncertainties in halo abundance. High redshift AGN population statistics and the Ultraviolet Luminosity Function provide additional constraints on the primordial power spectrum and dynamics of primordial inflation theory.

title: Resource-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neighborhood Selection for Large-Scale Molecular Diversity Optimization
text:
Title: Resource-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neighborhood Selection for Large-Scale Molecular Diversity Optimization
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Large-scale combinatorial optimization remains demanding for classical heuristics, particularly when dense Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulations induce large memory footprints, high CPU utilization, and long execution times. While near-term quantum processors cannot yet deliver unconditional quantum advantage, hybrid architectures can provide practical value by reducing the resource burden. This paper presents a resource-efficiency study of Hybrid Quantum Neighborhood Selection (HQNS), a framework that decomposes large dense QUBO instances into bounded-width quantum subproblems via stochastic frontier selection. We evaluate HQNS on the Maximum Diversity Subset Selection Problem (MDSSP), focusing on the trade-off between solution quality retention and resource consumption. Benchmarks up to N=1000 candidates show that HQNS preserves 99.9908% of the mean diversity score of an 11-restart parallel Simulated Annealing baseline, while reducing wall-clock time by 94.91%, peak CPU utilization by 64.68%, and peak memory usage by 88.61%. The QPU execution time remains bounded within a 6-7 second envelope across scales, indicating that the quantum component is decoupled from the global QUBO dimension when the frontier size is fixed. These results suggest that HQNS provides a resource-aware pathway for deploying hybrid quantum optimization in practical large-scale settings, serving as an efficient architecture for incorporating near-term quantum processors into classical optimization pipelines.

title: Mutual Information Estimation via Triangular Transport Maps: Finite Sample Guarantees and Sample Allocation
text:
Title: Mutual Information Estimation via Triangular Transport Maps: Finite Sample Guarantees and Sample Allocation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We study finite sample guarantees for transport based mutual information estimation. Mutual information can be estimated by first learning the conditional and marginal densities and then evaluating their log-density ratio by Monte Carlo. Given training samples, we use triangular transport maps to learn these densities and then compute the mutual information estimate on an independent batch of evaluation samples. For conditional density estimation using triangular transport maps, we establish non-asymptotic guarantees over realizable Hölder classes by viewing the conditional density as an ordinary density with respect to the product of the law of the conditioning variable and Lebesgue measure. This allows standard density estimation techniques to be applied directly to the conditional density estimation. These results yield finite sample guarantees for the resulting mutual information estimator and characterize how a fixed sample budget should be allocated between training and evaluation in order to minimize the mean squared error. Numerical experiments support the predicted training and evaluation error rates and illustrate the resulting sample allocation tradeoff.

title: On Emergent Geometry of the Generalized BGW Theory
text:
Title: On Emergent Geometry of the Generalized BGW Theory
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We present a systematic study of the mathematical theory of the generalized Brézin-Gross-Witten (BGW) theory using methods from statistical physics. We prove the multidifferentials of the generalized BGW theory are given by the Eynard-Orantin topological recursion in a generic background with general coupling constants. Furthermore, we characterize the transition between the Witten-Kontsevich model and the generalized BGW theory. This approach yields a new proof of the Okuyama-Sakai conjecture, further elucidating the deep structural connections between these two fundamental models.

title: BQP-Complete Susceptibilities Observable at Ballistic Times in Local Quantum Dynamics
text:
Title: BQP-Complete Susceptibilities Observable at Ballistic Times in Local Quantum Dynamics
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Local response measurements track how perturbations spread in quantum simulators and nonequilibrium many-body systems. Locality bounds constrain the propagation speed, but do not determine whether the response can distinguish computational outcomes at fixed measurement precision as the distance increases. Here we construct time-independent dynamics with bounded nearest-neighbor interactions in which a fixed single-site detector responds to a remote bond phase after a time proportional to their separation. The susceptibility has a positive lower bound independent of distance. With product-state preparations, estimating this susceptibility to constant additive accuracy is complete for bounded-error quantum polynomial time (BQP), with a decision gap independent of distance. Two source-phase settings give the susceptibility with a distance-independent shot count at fixed accuracy and confidence. Inverse-polynomially weak local couplings between the computational register and the chain carrying the excitation preserve the gap. The leading correction vanishes when exchanging the two internal states of the excitation reverses the interaction. Varying the source and observation time makes all bond phases locally identifiable near the zero-phase reference setting. We also prove a conditional quantum advantage for distribution-free response prediction.

title: Fidelity Determines the Minimum Error of Quantum Recovery
text:
Title: Fidelity Determines the Minimum Error of Quantum Recovery
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Even a recovery that maximizes worst-input entanglement fidelity can retain avoidable errors in subsequent measurements. Entanglement fidelity is the probability of passing a test of whether the state and its entanglement were preserved; infidelity is the probability of failing it. Operational error is the largest possible change in any measurement probability, quantified by the normalized diamond distance. For every finite-dimensional noise channel and fixed encoding, we prove that operational error and worst-input entanglement infidelity have the same minimum over all recovery operations. The proof constructs one final unitary (a reversible quantum operation) that makes any recovery's operational error no greater than its original worst-input entanglement infidelity. With a retained noise record, we determine the optimal error and characterize all optimal decoders subject to a Kraus-rank limit for each outcome. For a fixed decoded channel, a semidefinite program finds the optimal final unitary in the low-error regime. We characterize all optimal final corrections and show that, at a fixed error floor $0<ε<1$, the operational optimizers' sensitivity to residual unitary errors of size $s$ is at worst of order $s^{4/3}$, while the canonical polar correction has quadratic sensitivity.

title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
text:
Title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We introduce a modular framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations for driven systems subject to temporally correlated classical noise. The construction combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov relation with the Magnus expansion: Functional response closes the noise average, while nested commutators retain the noncommuting chronological action of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, we derive the resulting Novikov-Magnus quantum master equation through fourth order in the noise strength. The same response hierarchy suggests a natural extension beyond Gaussian noise, with connected higher-order noise correlations weighting higher functional derivatives of the stochastic map. For a driven qubit under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited $1/f$ noise, the second- and fourth-order maps remain CPTP throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations. Their diamond-norm errors are comparable to those of the cumulant-based pseudo-Lindblad master equation, with a modest fourth-order improvement for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.

title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
text:
Title: Spin entanglement in $pp$ and $pA$ collisions: high-energy TMD effects and fragmentation probes
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Spin-spin correlations of a quark-antiquark pair produced in proton-proton or proton-Ion collisions are investigated in $k_T$-factorization within the shockwave formalism. We construct the full spin-density matrix of both inclusive and diffractive channels in the limit in which the two quarks are back-to-back. In the inclusive channel, due to linearly polarized gluons, we show that a $\cos (2 φ)$-modulation of the concurrence, stabilizer Rényi entropy, and quantum discord emerges and depends on the interplay between six small-$x$ gluon TMDs. The modulation is predicted to be maximally strong and independent of the transverse momentum imbalance, $q$, from a dilute (BFKL) perspective, while it is considerably suppressed by saturation effects. In diffraction, we observe that the pair is always entangled and exhibits the same properties found in diffractive DIS. We explain how these properties follow directly from the exclusive and eikonal nature of the Pomeron exchange. We trace this behavior to a spin-density matrix of rank at most two with maximally mixed marginals. For this class of states, entanglement and Bell nonlocality coincide even when the state is mixed, while the explicit form of the light-front helicity amplitudes ensures that both persist in the whole phase space. We suggest accessing the spin correlations in unpolarized hadron collisions through the Collins and dihadron fragmentation functions. We point out that, in inclusive production, for massless quarks, suitably chosen double-Collins asymmetries provide promising entanglement witnesses.

title: Radial dependence of galaxy and halo properties in cosmic voids: SDSS DR7 and the ELUCID constrained simulation
text:
Title: Radial dependence of galaxy and halo properties in cosmic voids: SDSS DR7 and the ELUCID constrained simulation
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Cosmic voids provide a setting for examining the interplay between mass and environment in shaping galaxy and halo properties. Using the SDSS DR7 volume-limited galaxy sample and the ELUCID constrained simulation of the local large-scale structure, we investigate the radial profiles of galaxy and subhalo properties across different mass ranges, identifying voids independently in the observed galaxy and simulated subhalo distributions. Both stellar mass and subhalo mass increase from void interiors toward the void boundary, indicating that lower-mass galaxies and subhaloes preferentially reside in void interiors. The satellite fraction of subhaloes also increases systematically toward the void boundary. Galaxy colour and specific star formation rate exhibit radial variations that are weaker than their dependence on stellar mass, while the spiral fraction shows little radial dependence at fixed stellar mass. For dark-matter haloes, the apparent radial increase in size within a broad high-mass bin largely disappears when narrower mass ranges are considered. Halo concentration and spin show radial variations at fixed mass, with higher concentrations and lower spins toward void interiors, although the concentration trend is less pronounced in the extended low-mass sample. The formation redshift of low-mass subhaloes also increases toward the void boundary, whereas this dependence weakens and eventually disappears at higher masses. Overall, the radial trends in galaxy properties are generally weaker than their mass dependence, while several subhalo properties retain measurable radial variations at fixed mass.

title: Pinpointing Pivot Points: The DECIDE Framework for Data Analysis Decision Importances
text:
Title: Pinpointing Pivot Points: The DECIDE Framework for Data Analysis Decision Importances
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Human judgment calls made throughout the data science life cycle can change the conclusions drawn from data. Independent analysts often make different choices when given the same data, leading to often unacceptable variations in results and contributing to the ongoing reproducibility crisis across scientific disciplines. The rapid adoption of agentic tools threatens to amplify this crisis. Several approaches have been developed to address this variation by following the same strategy: repeating an analysis under different combinations of analytical decisions and inspecting the distribution of outcomes. Examples include multiverse analysis, specification curve analysis, and vibration of effects. More broadly, the Predictability-Computability-Stability (PCS) framework assesses how documented judgment calls across the data science life cycle affect conclusions, with predictability serving as a reality-check that a model captures signal. Each of these approaches results in a "multiverse" object. While the distribution of outcomes reflects the overall variability of conclusions, estimating the influence of each individual decision requires additional tools. A common heuristic is to train a model to predict the outcome from these decisions and treat its coefficients or feature importances as proxies for each decision's influence. Although this strategy may work in certain cases, it assumes the model is correctly specified and accurately predicts the outcome, which we show is not always the case. In this work, we introduce DECIDE, a model-free framework that quantifies each decision's importance from the actual outcomes across the plausible decision space, avoiding issues of predictability by design. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DECIDE by applying it to real-world multiverse analyses. We further provide what is, to our knowledge, the first formal definition of the multiverse.

title: Autonomous Quantum Measurement with Agentic AI
text:
Title: Autonomous Quantum Measurement with Agentic AI
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Quantum materials exhibit diverse electronic and functional phenomena, but their characterization requires extensive experimental expertise, iterative decision-making and accumulated laboratory knowledge that is difficult to document and transfer. Here we introduce Quantum Agent (QUANTA), an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for autonomous quantum-materials characterization. Using a widely adopted Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS) as an experimental platform, QUANTA combines retrieval augmentation using scientific literature, experimental protocols and prior measurements with specialized agents for experimental planning, troubleshooting, and data interpretation. A separate deterministic control layer validates instrument actions. Guided by incoming data, QUANTA evaluates measurement quality, revises experimental plans and selects subsequent measurements. We demonstrate these capabilities through transport measurements of the topological Weyl semimetal TaP, as well as investigations of nonlinear responses in magnetic material Co2MnGa. These results establish QUANTA as a generalizable framework for evidence-driven, safeguarded and closed-loop quantum-materials characterization.

title: A Black-Box Reduction from Regret to Multi-Level Coverage
text:
Title: A Black-Box Reduction from Regret to Multi-Level Coverage
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Online Conformal Prediction (OCP) sequentially constructs prediction sets whose average empirical coverage converges to a target level over time, for arbitrary, potentially adversarial datasets. In the multi-level setting, prediction sets are produced at $d$ coverage levels at once. Prior work argued for the use of online gradient descent with isotonic projections, which produces sets nested across levels, but with a $\sqrt{d}$ dependence in the per-level coverage convergence rate. Here, we both generalize and improve prior work. First, we show that isotonic projections can be used for the construction of multi-level online conformal prediction sets from \emph{any} online learning algorithm (not just gradient descent). Then, through a black-box reduction, we show that the linearized regret of the online algorithm itself automatically gives control over both per-level coverage and distributional consistency of multi-level predictions via Fenchel duality. Finally, by using the Weighted Interval Score, a standard scoring rule for assessing multi-level interval forecasts, we prove that these projections reduce both the size of the sets and their under-coverage. We study two instantiations of our theory, $p$-norm Online Mirror Descent and coordinate-wise Universal Portfolio methods, both improving the dependence on the number of levels to $\sqrt{\log d}$ for the multi-level OCP problem. Experiments on several datasets show favorable performance compared to baselines.

title: Loop Extrusion Reversal by Condensin Motor is Mediated by Catch Bonds
text:
Title: Loop Extrusion Reversal by Condensin Motor is Mediated by Catch Bonds
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Structural Maintenance Complexes (SMC) are energy consuming motors that are important in folding the genome by loop extrusion (LE) in all stages of the cell cycle. Single molecule magnetic tweezer pulling experiments have revealed that condensin, a member of the SMC family involved in mitosis, takes occasional backward steps, thus coughing up the gains in the length of the extruded loop. To reveal the mechanism of the forward and backward steps simultaneously, we developed a theory using the stochastic kinetic model and the scrunching mechanism for LE. The calculations quantitatively account for the measured force-dependent step size and dwell time distributions in both the directions. By postulating the existence of an intermediate state in the ATP-driven cycle that is poised to take a forward or a backward step, we predict that its lifetime increases as the external mechanical force increases till a critical value and subsequently decreases at higher forces. The surprising finding of lifetime increase in an active motor, at sub-piconewton forces, is the characteristic of catch bonds, known in force-induced rupture of several passive protein complexes. The identification of catch bond-like states in condensin not only expands our understanding of LE but also highlights the significance of mechanical forces in regulating genome organization.

title: Enhancing Repository-Level Code Completion with Reinforcement Learning in Real-World Scenarios
text:
Title: Enhancing Repository-Level Code Completion with Reinforcement Learning in Real-World Scenarios
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) for code, which closely aligns with the practical needs of real-world software development, has sparked growing attention in repository-level code completion. However, existing Code LLMs present challenges in focusing on suitable contexts from the repository and in deeply reasoning about cross-file dependencies. To address these challenges, we propose a novel reinforcement learning framework for repository-level code completion. To better understand both in-file and cross-file contexts, we employ identifier-driven intent recognition to capture completion intent, thereby improving the model's performance in real-world scenarios. To enhance cross-file reasoning, we propose a reward-driven completion learning to effectively reward in complex repository completion scenarios. To guide LLMs in completing code that aligns with intended functionality and repository context, we introduce a selective-exploration strategy that directs the model to focus on low-confidence, high-reward tokens, promoting the exploration of valuable, underexplored completion patterns. Experimental results show that our approach significantly improves the performance of Code LLMs. The code and the dataset are available at https://github.com/zhenlongDai/RepoCompletion.

title: Balance-Guided Forest for Causal Effect Estimation
text:
Title: Balance-Guided Forest for Causal Effect Estimation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Covariate balancing is widely used for estimating causal effects in observational studies. A central challenge is determining which covariate features should be balanced. Forest-kernel balancing provides a data-driven way to learn informative balancing features. Existing forest-kernel balancing methods first learn a tree-based representation and then construct balancing weights. However, this procedure creates a mismatch, as limited tree capacity may be spent on features that are already well represented. We propose Balance-Guided Forest (BGF), which uses the current balancing weights to guide subsequent tree construction. BGF grows trees using a novel splitting score that combines residual imbalance with an outcome contrast, favoring splits that separate outcome-relevant regions where imbalance remains. This couples representation learning with covariate balancing rather than treating balancing as a downstream step. We establish an oracle-type bound that links the iterative construction to weighting error and causal bias. Simulations exhibit improvements in causal estimation relative to existing forest-kernel approaches. Real-data applications illustrate the practical behavior of BGF across observational studies.

title: Simple Test-Time Refinement for Plot-to-Code Generation via Visual-Code Diagnostics
text:
Title: Simple Test-Time Refinement for Plot-to-Code Generation via Visual-Code Diagnostics
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Plot-to-code generation has been greatly advanced by recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing studies mainly focus on one-pass generation or iterative sampling guided by verifier-based filtering, which does not align with the typical human programming workflow of generate first, then iteratively error-location and fix. This naturally motivates a test-time refinement paradigm for plot-to-code generation. In this work, we present the first study on plot-to-code generation via iterative test-time refinement. We propose a Visual-Code Diagnostics framework that enables refinement through visual feedback from source code. Specifically, we first categorize generation errors into four coarse-grained types, and then train lightweight discriminators to recognize and localize these errors based on the rendered visual outputs and corresponding code. Unlike traditional compiler- or debugger-based verification, our approach performs iterative refinement guided by one diagnostics system, enabling more effective semantic and visual correction during test time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method consistently improves generation quality across diverse generators and significantly outperforms strong test-time scaling baselines.

title: Solution Size Growth as an Obstacle to Iterative Refinement for Linear Optimization
text:
Title: Solution Size Growth as an Obstacle to Iterative Refinement for Linear Optimization
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Iterative refinement is a technique used to exponentially boost the precision of the solution to certain problems by solving a sequence of related problem instances. We study the size of the solutions arising from the sequence of problems produced by the iterative refinement algorithm when applied to linear optimization problems (LPs). We introduce a class of problems for which the size of such solutions can grow exponentially with the number of refinement iterations, and we show evidence that to avoid this undesirable behavior, a black-box LP solver would have to be \emph{lucky}---a concept introduced formally in this paper, by which we mean that the solver would have to return a solution of better quality than what is required by its termination tolerances. Furthermore, we show that the exponential scaling occurs if one uses a natural instantiation of the simplex algorithm using Bland's pivoting rule. We discuss the implications of our lower bound on the solution size for optimization algorithms whose running time depends polynomially on the solution size, such as quantum multiplicative weights update algorithms and quantum matrix games algorithms.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes
text:
Title: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The theory of turbo iterative decoding was brought into the quantum coding framework through the development of quantum serial turbo codes and quantum block turbo codes. In this paper, we present a theory for multidimensional quantum block turbo codes, a turbo decoding technique for multi layer product codes. We describe its algorithm and simulate the performance for the 3D case on a depolarizing channel.

title: Can end-to-end learning from raw electronic structure explain magnetic anisotropy?
text:
Title: Can end-to-end learning from raw electronic structure explain magnetic anisotropy?
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Machine-learning models trained directly on electronic spectra can predict spin--orbit-driven properties, yet models with comparable predictive accuracy may learn different electronic dependencies. We examine this problem using magnetic anisotropy in atomic-scale magnets and a validation strategy designed to assess the physical relevance of learned spectral relationships. We compare a bidirectional gated recurrent unit and a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, both trained to predict magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) from spin- and orbital-resolved scalar-relativistic densities of states (SR-DOS). Despite comparable in-domain (ID) accuracy, the architectures learn only partly overlapping spectral dependencies. Shapley additive explanations identify spectral features shared between the two architectures that can be associated with plausible spin--orbit-coupling pathways consistent with second-order perturbation theory (PT2). Adding PT2-derived MAE contributions to the model inputs has little effect on ID performance but can improve transfer beyond the training domain, with gains differing between architectures. Controlled spectral perturbations further demonstrate that similar attribution patterns do not imply the same functional dependence of the predicted MAE on spectral weight. The contrasting responses provide a functional context for architecture-dependent out-of-domain transfer. End-to-end learning can identify candidate electronic signatures of magnetic anisotropy. Their credible microscopic interpretation, however, rests on convergent evidence from predictive performance, model comparison, physical theory, controlled spectral interventions, and evaluation under distribution shift.

title: Finite temperature and pressure structural relaxations including zero-point motion and anharmonicity
text:
Title: Finite temperature and pressure structural relaxations including zero-point motion and anharmonicity
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

At finite temperature and pressure, the equilibrium structure of a crystal minimizes the Gibbs free energy rather than the static Born-Oppenheimer energy. We present WARP (Wyckoff-constrained Anharmonic Relaxations at Pressure and temperature), a symmetry-constrained, variable-cell relaxation based on the stochastic temperature-dependent effective potential method, including anharmonicity and zero-point motion. Every position update is projected onto Wyckoff positions and every strain onto symmetric strains, so a relaxation can raise the symmetry but never lower it. For aluminum, the thermal expansion follows measurements at cryogenic temperatures, including the quantum plateau below 50 K. For lanthanum hydrides at megabar pressures, equations of state agree with phonon-based and path-integral calculations, and LaH$_{10}$ relaxes from its rhombohedral static minimum to the observed cubic phase, also with a machine-learned potential fine-tuned on 150 supercells. For brucite, Mg(OD)$_2$, lattice parameters, bond distances and thermal expansion agree with neutron diffraction, and the O-D isotope effect is captured.

title: Mean Field Games in Dynamic Ticket Pricing with Overselling and Cancellations
text:
Title: Mean Field Games in Dynamic Ticket Pricing with Overselling and Cancellations
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We extend a finite-state Mean Field Game model of dynamic ticket pricing to allow overselling, stochastic cancellations, and terminal penalties for unresolved negative inventory. Cancellations generate upward inventory transitions, producing a bidirectional inventory process coupled with firms' pricing decisions. We formulate the representative-firm control problem and the population consistency conditions, and prove existence of a selected Markovian mean field equilibrium under the stated assumptions, including a compact price set and an explicit tie-breaking rule. Numerical experiments show that the quadratic terminal penalty can generate an endogenous soft-boundary mechanism that discourages progressively deeper overselling. Under a low-cancellation stress case, linear penalties more strongly reduce the prevalence of terminal overselling, whereas quadratic penalties reduce its conditional depth and lower-tail severity. A time-varying cancellation experiment suggests that anticipated future inventory recovery can support lower early prices and greater temporary overbooking exposure. Under the adopted demand normalization, stronger mean-field coupling is associated with lower equilibrium prices and slower inventory depletion. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing pricing and overbooking incentives in competitive ticket markets with cancellations.

title: Real-Space Selection Rule for Moiré Exciton-Phonon Coupling
text:
Title: Real-Space Selection Rule for Moiré Exciton-Phonon Coupling
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Exciton-phonon coupling (ExPC) governs energy relaxation and exciton dynamics in photoexcited quantum materials. Recent advances have revealed rich and tunable excitonic phenomena in moiré superlattices, yet the microscopic mechanisms underlying the coupling between moiré excitons and moiré phonons remain elusive. Here, we develop a real-space representation for moiré ExPC based on a unified theoretical framework combining the many-body Bethe-Salpeter equation with phonon perturbation theory. Furthermore, we uncover a general real-space selection rule: the spatial matching of a moiré exciton's electron and hole densities with the moiré-phonon-induced potential perturbations determines their individual coupling contributions, while coherent interference between the electron and hole contributions controls the total ExPC. We demonstrate this rule in prototypical WSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayers, revealing pronounced exciton- and phonon-mode-dependent coupling, including nearly complete suppression of ExPC through destructive electron-hole interference. These findings establish the internal electron-hole spatial configuration of moiré excitons as a key degree of freedom governing the strength and mode selectivity of their coupling to moiré phonons, opening opportunities to engineer ExPC through spatially tailored moiré potentials.

title: Transient Heat Conduction on Quantum Hardware: Replicated Temperature-Field Reconstruction and Shot-Count Sensitivity with a Variational Quantum Linear Solver
text:
Title: Transient Heat Conduction on Quantum Hardware: Replicated Temperature-Field Reconstruction and Shot-Count Sensitivity with a Variational Quantum Linear Solver
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Implicit discretizations of transient heat conduction repeatedly generate sparse linear systems, making diffusion problems a natural test bed for quantum linear solvers. This study evaluates how accurately a variational quantum linear solver (VQLS) recovers the temperature field produced by one backward-Euler step of one-dimensional conduction on IBM quantum hardware. A pre-specified confirmatory experiment compares N=4 interior temperatures encoded on two qubits with N=8 temperatures encoded on three qubits using ten paired hardware blocks; a separately defined N=16, four-qubit extension is evaluated in five independently scheduled exploratory blocks. Local VQLS optimization reduces relative temperature-field error to approximately 10^{-8} for all three cases, establishing an essentially exact ideal reference at this scale. On hardware, mean relative L2 temperature-field error is 8.07% for N=4 and 20.14% for N=8, a paired increase of 12.06 percentage points (95% CI, 10.71-13.42; exact paired sign-flip p=0.001953). The exploratory N=16 mean is 24.75+/-1.84%. A pre-specified N=16 shot-count follow-up then evaluates the same locked circuit at 2,048, 8,192, and 32,768 shots in six independently scheduled blocks. Mean field error remains 23.64%, 24.57%, and 24.37%, respectively; the 32,768-minus-2,048-shot contrast is +0.74 percentage points (95% CI, -0.65 to 2.12; p=0.281). In contrast, ideal multinomial sampling predicts a reduction from 2.68% to 0.75%. Higher shot counts reduce block-to-block variability but do not recover the mean cold-side temperature field. The results show that full-field readout of a strongly nonuniform thermal state is limited by more than ordinary finite-shot sampling under the tested hardware conditions, motivating observable-focused quantum formulations for heat flux, stored energy, and selected temperatures.

title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
text:
Title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

A recent remarkable paper by OpenAI showed that the spin-one Heisenberg chain with periodic boundary conditions has a spectral gap in the thermodynamic limit. The proof elegantly deduces this gap from the Hamiltonian's spectrum on a finite system. This basic idea is an inequality involving the purity of the original Gibbs state and a dual Gibbs state that is defined via space-time rotation. Here we consider a few generalizations of this purity bootstrap argument. We first extend it to arbitrary spatial dimensions. Our main result uses the space-time duality between symmetry generators and symmetry twists to obtain upper bounds on the splitting of nearly degenerate low-energy states, together with a nonzero gap above them, from finite-system information. As applications, we show that finite-system calculations for the 2+1-D toric code in a field and the 2+1-D transverse-field Ising model establish parameter regimes with four and two low-lying states whose splittings are bounded from above by $e^{-cL}$ and $e^{-cL^2}$ respectively for arbitrarily large system size $L$, while the gap above these states remains nonzero in the thermodynamic limit. Next, we extend it to fermionic systems and use a finite calculation to establish a symmetric mass generation phase in a $2+1$-D fermionic model. Finally, we apply the bootstrap to tensor-network states and establish exponential decay of connected correlations of all local operators in the symmetric square-lattice spin-one state introduced by Jian and Zaletel.

title: Regression with Many Generated Controls
text:
Title: Regression with Many Generated Controls
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We consider linear regression when some covariates are endogenous, a variable sufficient to control for endogeneity exists but is latent, and the practitioner can generate many proxies for the latent control. For instance, one could cheaply but imperfectly impute the latent control using different AI/ML methods, each generating a different proxy. There are several options the practitioner might consider in this scenario: including all proxies or factors computed from the proxies as controls, instrumental variables estimation, and some nonlinear variants thereof. We use a transparent model to derive the implicit estimand each approach targets, determine when these estimands recover the parameter of interest, and provide some practical recommendations. We show that with a sufficiently rich set of generated controls, practitioners can consistently estimate the parameter of interest without relying on validation data.

title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
text:
Title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Recent work has shown that a simple form of coupled dark energy with a constant coupling produces a good fit to the DESI data. In this scenario, dark matter, but not baryons, couples to a scalar field, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle (EP). We first generalize the coupled dark energy model by adding a nonminimal coupling between the scalar field and gravity, and dub the resulting model "doubly coupled dark energy". We then construct a parameter $E_P$ in this model that quantifies EP violation on cosmological scales and can be measured with large galaxy surveys in a model-independent way. Finally, we forecast constraints on the couplings for present and future spectroscopic galaxy surveys, namely DESI, Euclid, and SKA Phase 2 (SKA2). To keep the analysis as general as possible, we leave the initial power spectrum shape and the galaxy bias free to vary in several bins. Among these surveys, SKA2 could provide the tightest constraint on the coupling strength in the coupled dark energy scenario, with a relative $1σ$ uncertainty of $22\%$. The constraints weaken when both couplings are varied, but can be further improved by increasing the number of galaxies detected.

title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design
text:
Title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Generative models are increasingly used to propose molecules for drug discovery. They can produce far more candidates than can be experimentally tested, making computational selection essential. Most selection methods rely on predicted molecular properties, such as potency and toxicity, but overlook how these properties translate into drug exposure at a given dose. As a result, molecules that appear promising on paper may require impractical doses or raise safety concerns. We investigate this gap by using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations to re-evaluate molecules selected from three PARP1-targeted generative pipelines. Of 60 shortlisted molecules, seven fail to achieve sufficient target exposure, while 28% of the remaining candidates show predicted safety risks at their required dose. Moreover, 85% of candidates with an achievable dose are outperformed by molecules overlooked during static selection. These findings suggest that accounting for dose and exposure can substantially change which generated molecules are considered promising for drug development.

title: From Random Advection to Transport Noise and the LU Framework for the Navier--Stokes Equations
text:
Title: From Random Advection to Transport Noise and the LU Framework for the Navier--Stokes Equations
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We consider the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain in dimension two or three, with Dirichlet boundary conditions, when the velocity is advected by a rapidly varying stationary Markov process $\eps^{-1}m(t/\eps^2)$. The fast field may be spatially inhomogeneous. We prove that, when $\eps\to0$, the laws of the large-scale velocities are tight and that their limit points are martingale solutions of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations with transport noise in the form of the location uncertainty framework. The limiting equation contains in particular a noise which is described in terms of the covariance of the fast advection. Under a symmetry assumption on the temporal correlations of the fast field, the noise is Stratonovich and an advection by the Itô--Stokes drift appears. The proof relies on perturbed test functions, which we use both for the uniform energy bounds and for the identification of the limit. We have to adapt this method and add the Stokes operator to the Poisson equation associated to the fast advection in order to use fewer regularity assumptions and obtain correctors which satisfy the boundary conditions.

title: Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability
text:
Title: Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We prove analogues of weighted laws of iterated logarithm and laws of logarithm for non-commutative martingales and independent random variables respectively. First we obtain a weighted LIL for non-commutative martingales, extending the sharp unweighted result of arXiv:2509.22037v2 to the case for polynomial weights, then by approximation to a broader class of functions. Then we proved a weighted law of logarithm for triangular array of weights and replacing the coefficient in the denominator by regularly varying functions with index $α$. We show that the normalised sums converge to 0 for $α> 1/2$ and for the case $α=1/2$, we obtain the sharp upper bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$.

title: Topology change and the Gauss Bonnet term in causal set theory: the sign of the cosmological term and the axion decay constant
text:
Title: Topology change and the Gauss Bonnet term in causal set theory: the sign of the cosmological term and the axion decay constant
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Causal set theory permits changes of spatial topology without the metric degeneracy that forbids them in continuum Lorentzian gravity. In four dimensions such changes enter the gravitational action only through the Gauss--Bonnet term, which is the Euler density. We show that the Euler density of a discrete space is exact, local and combinatorial: it sums to the Euler characteristic at any resolution and is supported on topological defects. The Gauss--Bonnet term of a causal set is therefore fixed rather than postulated. Because it is linear in the number of elements, which is the four-volume, it acts as a cosmological constant. Its coefficient follows without forming any functional derivative, so the known obstruction in the continuum does not arise. The everpresent cosmological constant of causal set theory assumes that the mean topological charge vanishes. We show that it does not. The species of opposite sign solves the field equations only if a positive cosmological constant is already present, and, being simply connected, it cannot carry the axion charge that supports the other species.
