Only one sign survives, and the sign of the cosmological term is derived rather than assumed. We recover the surviving transition from the causal order alone in every simulated sprinkling. The action of the corresponding axion wormhole then fixes the magnitude. The observed value requires an axion decay constant near the grand unification scale, and this result is insensitive to the one-loop prefactor and to the Gauss--Bonnet coupling.

title: Neuromorphic architectures as numerical solvers for computational neuroscience
text:
Title: Neuromorphic architectures as numerical solvers for computational neuroscience
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Neuromorphic computing is closely associated with spiking neuronal networks. However, an alternative class of so-called "rate-based" models arising from computational neuroscience and machine learning forgoes spiking interactions and instead relies on continuous coupling between neurons. Existing neuromorphic implementations designed around spike-based interactions are not well-suited for emulating such models. Here view the distributed simulation of these models as message-passing algorithms on parallel hardware. Leveraging prior art in numerical algorithms and distributed simulation, we outline steps that enable the design of efficient digital neuromorphic accelerators for non-spiking neuronal models. In particular, we show that multi-bit packets, rather than spikes, are the most efficient communication strategy in packet-switched networks and that compared to basic numerical integration methods, higher-order differential equation solvers decrease both computation and communication costs while achieving lower numerical error, but that these benefits are ultimately limited by arithmetic precision. Using our proposed design principles, we convert an existing neuromorphic architecture into a distributed numerical solver - a spikeless neuromorphic system - for continuously-coupled neuronal models. We thereby demonstrate that our theoretical considerations indeed translate into practical advantages, namely reduced energy consumption and delay.

title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
text:
Title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%). These results show that obtaining decision-relevant information through interaction remains a major bottleneck for LLM planning. This is ongoing work and will be updated. The date of this version is shown on the first page.

title: Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) Semiconductors: A First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Optical, and Energy-Related Properties
text:
Title: Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) Semiconductors: A First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Optical, and Energy-Related Properties
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. The calculated dielectric functions, refractive indices, absorption coefficients, reflectivity, optical conductivities, and electron energy-loss spectra reveal systematic changes in optical response across the chalcogen series. The absorption onset shifts toward lower photon energies, from approximately 2.4 eV in Y2CdS4 to 1.7 eV in Y2CdTe4. Thermoelectric calculations indicate promising Seebeck coefficients and power factors, with Y2CdSe4 exhibiting a favorable balance of transport properties. Charge-density distributions, electron localization functions, and Bader charge analyses suggest increasing covalent bonding contributions from sulfide to telluride. These findings highlight the potential of Y2CdX4 compounds for tunable optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications.

title: Relating Dark Dimension Size with Dark Energy via 5D Quintessence Potential and Casimir Energy
text:
Title: Relating Dark Dimension Size with Dark Energy via 5D Quintessence Potential and Casimir Energy
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We explore effective field theory (EFT) realizations of the dark dimension (DD) scenario in which the size of the DD is determined by the competition between a 5D quintessence potential and the Casimir energy. When only contributions from massless fields are considered, the Casimir energy does not have a typical energy scale, and the 4D dark energy (DE) scale is set by the height of the 5D quintessence potential. The simple 5D model we first study has an attractive feature that the size of the DD is related to the 4D vacuum energy (VE), as outlined above. However, it turns out that the 4D VE thus obtained cannot work as the 4D DE in the standard cosmological setting. One of the discrepancies between the VE and the DE manifests in the radion dependence of the effective 4D Newton's gravitational constant. This leads us to explore a 5D model in which the 4D Einstein-Hilbert (EH) action is dominantly induced by quantum effects, leaving the radion dependence of the 4D Newton's constant subdominant. This model leads to an attractive cosmological model, realizing the mechanism explained in the beginning. We also explore a 6D model with the total internal volume fixed, to make the 4D Newton's constant independent of the radion. We first study a scenario in which the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions are of the same order. In this scenario, the physical origin of the size of the DD is left to its UV completion. Next, we turn to a scenario in which there is a large hierarchy between the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions. In this scenario, the energy scale of the 5D quintessence potential turns out to be much higher than the energy scale of the 4D DE as inferred from the cosmological observations, so we need to subtract a constant term in 4D to tune the 4D DE. This prevents us from obtaining the scaling relation for the DE expected in the dSDC.

title: Barlow Packings All Have Maximum Packing Fraction: Why it is so Hard to Find Barlow Structures Other than fcc or hcp?
text:
Title: Barlow Packings All Have Maximum Packing Fraction: Why it is so Hard to Find Barlow Structures Other than fcc or hcp?
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We apply lattice theory to periodic Barlow packings $(X_{1}X_{2}\dots X_{N})_{\infty}$ where $X_{i}\in\{A,B,C\}$ and $X_{i}\neq X_{i+1}$, formed by stacking two-dimensional hexagonal close-packed layers, interacting via generalized $(n,m)$-Lennard-Jones potentials. The cohesive energies of all packings lie between those of hexagonal close-packed (hcp, $(AB)$) and face-centered cubic (fcc, $(ABC)$) structure and vary almost linearly with the fcc stacking fraction. The equilibrium lattice constant, bulk modulus, Einstein frequency, and vibrational entropy show similarly near-linear trends. For the standard $(12,6)$ potential, fcc has the highest vibrational entropy and hcp the lowest, with other Barlow packings falling between them, consistent with previous sticky-hard-sphere Monte Carlo simulations and supported by phonon dispersion calculations. These trends imply an approximately linear dependence of free energy on fcc stacking fraction, with hcp and fcc as endpoints. This provides a simple thermodynamic explanation for why intermediate Barlow stackings are rare in nature: near-linearity offers little driving force to favor them. Exceptions may arise when hcp and fcc are nearly degenerate in energy or when many-body interactions, absent from the present model, favor another stacking. Density-functional calculations including dispersion forces for argon Barlow packings with periods $N=2,3,4$, and $12$ corroborate the predicted near-linear cohesive energy dependence.

title: RegimeFormer: A Large Protein Model of Global Perturbation Regimes
text:
Title: RegimeFormer: A Large Protein Model of Global Perturbation Regimes
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Protein language models organize sequence and structure at scale, but a global representation of how proteins respond to mutation remains lacking. We present RegimeFormer, a large protein perturbation model coupled to RegimeAtlas, constructed by harmonizing and indexing 202,556,313 non-redundant protein sequences across the tree of life. A diversity-preserving one-million-protein subset provides the high-resolution training and inference layer, with 995,995 proteins yielding residue-level summaries across 407,048,356 residues and substitution-specific predictions available on demand. Across experimental deep mutational scanning, molecular benchmarks, structural confidence and evolutionary constraint, RegimeFormer identifies reproducible protein-level perturbation regimes that organize residue fragility, adaptability and predictive uncertainty. Regime conditioning improves substitution-specific prediction, with the largest relative gains under unseen-protein, unseen-family and low-homology evaluation. RegimeFormer-derived molecular priors further improve downstream transcriptomic and drug-response modelling. Together, RegimeFormer and RegimeAtlas provide a scalable framework for mapping, predicting and querying protein perturbation landscapes across global sequence space.

title: Publications as benchmarks: auditing AI agents on spatial transcriptomics alignment
text:
Title: Publications as benchmarks: auditing AI agents on spatial transcriptomics alignment
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

AI agents are increasingly automating data analysis, but responsible adoption requires reliable performance evaluation, which is costly in specialized scientific domains. We introduce a framework that translates scientific publications into auditable benchmarks for AI agents and demonstrate its use on spatial transcriptomics alignment tasks. Across 121 tasks, 16 baseline methods, and six AI agents, the best agents (GPT-6-Astra and Gemini-4-Argon) matched or outperformed all baselines on 80% of tasks, often using surprisingly simple heuristics. Agent performance was robust to prompting and access to pre-installed packages. Benchmark construction also uncovered errors in prior work and shortcuts in current evaluation metrics. Finally, we show that agent-generated solutions can be distilled into a reusable program that ranks in the top 10% of baseline methods on unseen data. Our framework offers a scalable way to evaluate AI agents in specialized scientific domains by leveraging and stress-testing existing papers and metrics.

title: Euclid Bypass end-to-end simulations for spectroscopic galaxy clustering performance assessment
text:
Title: Euclid Bypass end-to-end simulations for spectroscopic galaxy clustering performance assessment
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We present a simulation framework for Euclid galaxy clustering measurements that reproduces the essential behaviour of the spectroscopic reduction chain, bypassing the computation required by full pixel-level simulations. The framework comprises two complementary tools, FastSpec, which simulates 1-dimensional slitless spectra with a simplified instrument and noise model, and Pypelid, which computes detection probabilities on input catalogues, accounting for the survey dithering sequence and spatially varying noise. We develop calibrated prescriptions for the survey selection function, redshift errors, and redshift interloper populations. Applied to the Euclid Wide Survey, the baseline selection yields a redshift purity of 74% and a sample completeness of 45%, which improves with the use of Euclid photometric colours. The redshift error distribution is found to have a Gaussian core of width $σ_z = 9.4 \times 10^{-4}$, with no significant trend over $0.9 < z < 1.8$. Emission lines [OIII]5008 and [SIII]9530 misidentified as H$α$ contribute a few to ten per cent depending on redshift, while catastrophic redshift measurement failures dominate at low signal-to-noise ratio. Simulating the Data Release 1 footprint, we find that complex survey selection effects can be corrected with a forward-modelled random catalogue, recovering the monopole and quadrupole of the galaxy 2-point correlation function. The simplified noise model does not include residual contamination from overlapping spectra, or other artefacts seen in early Euclid data; this will be revisited with DR1 data. The framework provides an efficient route for characterising the Euclid spectroscopic selection function at the precision required for galaxy clustering science, and is the basis for systematic error assessments in Euclid galaxy clustering analyses.

title: On the one-arm probability for the metric graph Gaussian free field in high dimensions
text:
Title: On the one-arm probability for the metric graph Gaussian free field in high dimensions
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We consider the sign clusters of the Gaussian free field on the cable system of a transient weighted graph with volume growth exponent $α$ and Green function decay exponent $ν$. We prove that the probability that the cluster of a vertex reaches distance $R$ is of order $R^{-β}$ when $2α 6$ and $d=6$. The upper bound combines a general entropic bound, which compares the law of the cluster under the critical loop soup and under a massive one, with a Simon-Lieb-type inequality for the massive field derived from its Markov property. The arguments are robust and require no transitivity. The lower bound follows from a competition between the capacity and the volume of the cluster. In both bounds, the key quantity is the expected exit time of the random walk from balls, which links the volume of the cluster to its radius.

title: Does DESI point towards transient cosmic acceleration?
text:
Title: Does DESI point towards transient cosmic acceleration?
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We investigate an oscillatory equation of state for dark energy that oscillates around the mean value $-1$ and includes a source term proportional to the cube of the number of e-folds. Due to this source term, the oscillation amplitude shifts towards the $w_{\rm de} -1$ regime. As the equation of state enters the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime in the future, the dark energy density dilutes, causing the Hubble parameter to decrease asymptotically towards zero, so that the present acceleration is transient: the Universe transitions to decelerated expansion and approaches a static state as $a\to\infty$, without ever contracting. We compare this equation of state with BellDE, CPL and flat $Λ$CDM. We confront the model with a combination of datasets, including Planck, DESI BAO and three different supernova compilations: Pantheon+, Union3 and DES-Dovekie. We compare the log-evidence of each model with that of $Λ$CDM. The dynamical dark energy models yield $H_0$ values in the range $66.0^{+0.80}_{-0.79}$--$67.84^{+0.69}_{-0.74}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, with matter density values in the range $Ω_{\rm m}=0.3067^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072}$--$0.3271^{+0.0083}_{-0.0080}$ across all the combinations. These values are consistent with those of the baseline model, apart from a mild upward shift in $Ω_{\rm m}$ for the Union3 combination. Among all the models, BellDE yields comparatively stronger Bayesian evidence than the other models, with weak evidence for the Pantheon+ compilation and moderate evidence for the Union3 and DES-Dovekie compilations. The sourced oscillatory model yields inconclusive evidence for Pantheon + and Union3, while weak evidence for DES-Dovekie relative to $Λ$CDM.

title: Reservoir-induced Quantum Phase Transitions in spin ensembles
text:
Title: Reservoir-induced Quantum Phase Transitions in spin ensembles
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of an open quantum system consisting of a collection of N two-level atoms in the thermodynamic limit coupled to bosonic reservoirs. Our results demonstrate that, when the system-bath interactions lacks a metastable minimum, as in the counterterm-free case, the system can undergo a quantum phase transition set by the reservoir structure rather than by coherent internal dynamics. Using exact quantum Langevin equations, valid even in the overdamped regime near criticality, where the loss rates can exceed the resonance frequency of the softening mode, we locate the critical point via the complex excitation spectrum and obtain closed-form reflection and transmission spectra that display the mode softening and an increasingly asymmetric lineshape near the transition.

title: SituRecBench: Evaluating Frontier Models as Situated Recommendation Assistants in 3D Environments
text:
Title: SituRecBench: Evaluating Frontier Models as Situated Recommendation Assistants in 3D Environments
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Recommender systems are transitioning from static retrieval engines into interactive assistants grounded in physical environments. However, current studies largely neglect the combined complexities of spatial navigation, visual grounding, and multi-turn social interaction. To bridge this gap, we introduce SituRecBench, an interactive benchmark for evaluating frontier vision-language models (VLMs) as situated recommendation assistants within high-fidelity 3D environments. We reformulate recommendation as a situated assistance process in which an assistant interacts with a user while sharing the user's egocentric view. Our benchmark simulates real-world shopping environments (e.g., supermarkets and home furnishings stores), requiring assistants to elicit preferences, ground recommendations in the environment, and guide the user to relevant locations through dialogue. The benchmark evaluates dialogue quality, recommendation utility, and navigation effectiveness through a unified interactive protocol. Extensive experiments reveal persistent challenges in spatial grounding and preference elicitation, highlighting limitations in their ability to integrate global contextual information with local observations. SituRecBench provides a rigorous foundation for advancing the development of situated assistants in the real world.

title: Is Your LLM Relay Serving What It Claims? A low-cost and high-power test for LLM Relay Auditing
text:
Title: Is Your LLM Relay Serving What It Claims? A low-cost and high-power test for LLM Relay Auditing
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Relay and reseller APIs have become a common way to access large language models (LLMs), yet users cannot directly verify whether they receive the models they request and pay for. This opacity motivates LLM relay auditing, but existing methods struggle to combine low cost, robustness to benign deployment changes, and statistically interpretable decisions under black-box access. To address these limitations, we propose distributional fingerprint auditing (DFA), a statistical method that requires only textual responses from suspect and trusted reference endpoints. DFA repeatedly queries semantically simple finite-choice probes and uses the resulting categorical response distributions to construct endpoint fingerprints. It compares the suspect and reference fingerprints probe by probe and aggregates the resulting evidence using the Cauchy combination test, yielding an approximate endpoint-level $p$-value for audit decisions at a prespecified nominal significance level. Using registered fingerprints of candidate models, a likelihood-based formulation further supports model attribution under full substitution and joint estimation of substitute identity and substitution ratio under constant-ratio mixed routing. Our benchmark includes 16 proprietary and open-weight LLMs from 10 model families. Across 240 ordered full-substitution pairs, DFA achieves high detection rates at a nominal significance level of $α=0.05$, using five probes and 250 relay requests per audit with stored reference fingerprints. Configuration overrides can lead to rejection even when the served model remains unchanged, with effects varying across models and configurations. Simulations based on stored empirical fingerprints demonstrate accurate model attribution and estimate substitution ratios, with estimation error decreasing as the audit budget increases.

title: Singularising quantum channels preserving kappa-additivity
text:
Title: Singularising quantum channels preserving kappa-additivity
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We construct quantum channels by averaging unitary shift conjugations with respect to $κ$-additive probability measures on measurable abelian groups. The channels act on the duals of operator algebras generated by shifts and bounded measurable multiplication operators. They preserve $κ$-additivity of quantum states and admit a weak-$*$ integral representation on this class. If the averaging measure vanishes on singletons, every output state is singular. In the appendix, we also establish the corresponding Fubini's theorem for $κ$-additive measures.

title: Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Reveals Grotthuss Transport in Concentrated Electrolytes
text:
Title: Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Reveals Grotthuss Transport in Concentrated Electrolytes
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Proton transfer is responsible for the anomalous high conductivity in acidic or basic aqueous solutions. Yet, the contribution of the proton transfer mechanism to the conductivity of concentrated aqueous solutions is unknown. In this work, we compute the transport properties of KOH(aq) systems with different concentrations, using Molecular Dynamics simulations with a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP), which includes proton transfer. We quantify the contribution of the proton transfer mechanism to the diffusivities of hydroxide ions and water molecules, and the ionic conductivity and transport numbers of the electrolytes. The contribution is substantial at lower concentrations, but diminishes at very high concentrations.

title: Information-Dense Synthesis for Molecular Discovery
text:
Title: Information-Dense Synthesis for Molecular Discovery
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Machine learning can accelerate molecular discovery by designing molecules and planning experiments. However, many scientific challenges demand molecules with very rare properties, and in this sparse setting, existing algorithms offer little gain over random guessing. We propose a method to efficiently search large regions of molecular space using algorithmically controlled stochastic synthesis. Rather than design, make and test individual molecules, we design and make complex mixtures, test them as a pool, then deconvolute the molecule-activity map. We optimize synthesis to encode maximal information. Theoretically, this approach can reduce the number of experiments required to find the optimal molecule among $d$ candidates from $\mathcal{O}(d)$ to $\mathcal{O}(\log d)$ or $\mathcal{O}(1)$. In simulation, on estimated protein fitness landscapes, it finds active molecules with an order of magnitude fewer experiments than existing Bayesian optimization methods.

title: PIANISTpy: A JAX-based Python package for velocity-anisotropic astrophysical equilibrium models
text:
Title: PIANISTpy: A JAX-based Python package for velocity-anisotropic astrophysical equilibrium models
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The hierarchical assembly of dark matter haloes and galaxies via mergers and anisotropic mass accretion naturally imprints non-trivial velocity anisotropy onto haloes and galaxies, an empirical fact emerging from cosmological simulations. However, dynamical studies based on idealised numerical simulations typically assume isotropic velocity distributions for the systems studied. This is mainly because no tools exist to construct anisotropic initial conditions with fully self-consistent (i.e., physical and instability-free) truncation boundary conditions for finite spatial extents. Here we present the first such analytical framework that performs truncation in phase space, with two distinct approaches to guarantee either the monotonicity of output distribution functions or identical truncated density profiles. We additionally present the open-source JAX-based GPU-accelerated Python package PIANISTpy (Particle Initial conditions with ANISoTropy) for constructing spherical, non-rotating initial conditions, supporting arbitrary double-power-law analytical radial density profiles and a library of analytical anisotropy profiles. This framework further permits the construction of systems with non-analytical anisotropy profiles via an arbitrary linear superposition of all implemented analytical anisotropy models as basis functions. PIANISTpy also outputs 3D velocity profiles and line-of-sight-integrated observables with end-to-end differentiability for rapid gradient-based Monte Carlo inference, and self-consistent local dark matter velocity distributions of anisotropic haloes beyond the unphysical Maxwell-Boltzmann simplification adopted in terrestrial detection experiments. We discuss use cases and demonstrate PIANISTpy's orders-of-magnitude higher numerical solver accuracy and superior dynamical stability of particle initial conditions relative to existing tools, including galpy and AGAMA.

title: Toward Safety-Aware AI Agents in Realistic Social Engineering Attack Scenarios
text:
Title: Toward Safety-Aware AI Agents in Realistic Social Engineering Attack Scenarios
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Personal AI agents are increasingly deployed on user devices to execute actions involving real money and sensitive data, but their security under social engineering attacks has not been systematically evaluated. We propose SEA (Social Engineering Attack Benchmark), the first interactive environment for evaluating the intrinsic security capability of AI agents in social engineering attack scenarios, covering 8 daily-life domains, 30+ simulated applications, a 4-level difficulty gradient, and a 5-dimensional evaluation framework, with 320 evaluation tasks designed in consultation with anti-fraud specialists and spanning two culturally distinct settings in Chinese and English. Evaluation on 11 frontier open-source and closed-source models, with GPT-6 evaluated only in Chinese, reveals that all models are breached to varying degrees (Chinese attack success rates ranging from 16.9% to 84.3%) proactive verification rates universally below 32%. We further propose META-SEA, a co-evolutionary framework for attack tasks and defenders. With META-SEA training, Qwen3-8B achieves defense performance comparable to closed-source models while effectively reducing ungrounded action claims.

title: Locally Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Polynomial Chaos Expansions
text:
Title: Locally Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Polynomial Chaos Expansions
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

This work develops a locally adaptive jackknife+ conformal prediction framework for polynomial chaos expansions. Therein, the non-conformity scores are normalized with an auxiliary polynomial chaos expansion trained on the log-transformed leave-one-out residuals of the base model. We show that the coverage guarantee of jackknife+ conformal prediction carries over to the adaptive intervals if the leave-one-out auxiliary models are trained on nested leave-one-out residuals. For fixed-basis polynomial chaos expansions fitted by ordinary least squares, all required quantities are derived in closed form and the guarantee-preserving adaptive intervals are obtained from a single model fit, without any model retraining. For sparse polynomial chaos expansions, where multiple model fits are necessary, we propose a heuristic simplification that limits the computational overhead of adaptivity at the cost of the formal coverage guarantee. Numerical experiments on an academic benchmark with known heteroscedastic noise and on an engineering simulation dataset show that the suggested method attains the target coverage while providing intervals that adapt to local prediction uncertainty, therefore being considerably more statistically efficient. These advantages are particularly prominent in high-uncertainty regions of the input space, where the performance of non-adaptive methods degrades substantially.

title: MNN-Pocket-0.3B Technical Report
text:
Title: MNN-Pocket-0.3B Technical Report
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

This technical report presents MNN-Pocket-0.3B, a compact 300M-parameter dense language model designed for efficient on-device deployment and supporting context lengths of up to 32K tokens. With an INT4 deployment footprint of only 173 MB and decoding throughput of up to 466 tokens/s on iPad Pro M5 (Metal), it can be seamlessly integrated into applications on edge devices such as smartphones and smart glasses. MNN-Pocket-0.3B is developed through the co-design of its architecture, data, training pipeline, and inference system. Hardware-aware architecture selection and dependency-aware vocabulary pruning balance model capability with on-device memory and compute constraints. A four-stage pre-training pipeline covering approximately 4.1 trillion high-quality Chinese and English tokens equips the model with broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities. This is followed by a three-stage post-training pipeline comprising instruction fine-tuning, multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and quantization-aware training. Finally, hardware-specific optimizations in the MNN inference engine enable fast, memory-efficient inference and long-context processing. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that MNN-Pocket-0.3B achieves frontier-level performance among models of comparable size, with particularly strong results in Chinese and English knowledge and reasoning, mathematics, coding, and instruction following. It consistently outperforms similarly sized open-source models and even surpasses several 0.5B-parameter models on instruction-following benchmarks. We release MNN-Pocket-0.3B with open weights and ready-to-use MNN deployment packages. We hope it will provide a practical foundation for capable, responsive, and memory-efficient edge applications while advancing research and development in on-device language models.

title: Origin and photoluminescence of a shallow hydrogen-related donor in silicon
text:
Title: Origin and photoluminescence of a shallow hydrogen-related donor in silicon
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Paramagnetic color centers in silicon are being investigated recently for use in quantum technologies. While the origin of most of the prominent photoluminescence (PL) lines are well understood, that is not the case for those connected to hydrogen, even though it is almost always present in silicon, e.g., shallow hydrogen-related donors (SHDs), but their atomic structure remains elusive. Recent experiments suggested connection between the SHDs and the so-called X and the B$_i$ (or X$_i$) PL-lines. An SHD, termed the MT2 center, was tentatively assigned to a bistable, negative-U defect, arising due to the interaction of hydrogen with the self-interstitial complex I$_4$. Using high-level density functional theory calculations, we investigate the interaction of hydrogen with self-interstitial complexes In. A shallow effective-mass-theory donor arises when hydrogen attacks a Si-Si bond in I$_n$, inserting itself as a bond-center interstitial (I$_n$H$_{BC}$) in an exothermic reaction. We demonstrate this in the case of a single self-interstitial and of a complex of four. The latter I$_\mathrm{4}$H$_\mathrm{BC}$ complex shows electronic, spin and PL properties remarkably close to MT2. We find that hydrogen in the presence of I$_4$ follows the same behavior as in pristine silicon, i.e., it is a negative-U bistable defect, only detectable under illumination. In the I$_4$H$_{BC}$ complex, H can hop via photo-assisted mechanism between equivalent BC sites of the I$_4$ complex, leading to a motional averaged tetragonal symmetry as experimentally observed for MT2. The zero-phonon line is distinct from the X-line (attributed to the bare I$_4$ complex), and falls well into the range of the X$_i$ lines. Our results identify the I$_4$H complex as a prototype for a class of SHDs, inferring that similar SHDs may arise, with the X$_i$ lines as their PL fingerprints, when H attacks I$_n$ clusters.

title: Learning through Capacity Awareness to Minimize Hospital Readmissions
text:
Title: Learning through Capacity Awareness to Minimize Hospital Readmissions
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Predictive algorithms are increasingly used to guide hospital discharge decisions, yet these models can exhibit censoring bias for vulnerable patients due to insufficient historical data or past discharge decisions. When biased readmission risk predictors are used to inform discharges, the training data generated by discharge decisions may perpetuate similar biases when predictors are re-trained, leading to a vicious cycle. We extend a queueing-based Markov decision process for hospital discharge to incorporate periodically retrained readmission risk predictors. Our key insight is that cost-optimal, "capacity-aware" operational decision policies can naturally diversify the lengths of stay at which patient outcomes are observed, enabling consistent estimation of readmission risk without explicit fairness constraints. We prove that repeated retraining under discharge-up-to policies converges to unbiased risk estimates under well-specification. In synthetic experiments and calibrated simulations based on patient-level data from a partner hospital, we find that where commonly used threshold-on-risk policies can remain persistently biased, discharge-up-to policies reduce learning error over status quo decision policies (such as thresholding on risk) by 24%-25%. These improvements to estimation also mitigate some forms of bias, reducing readmission cost disparities (adjusted for baseline risk differences between demographic groups) by 38%-63%. Our results demonstrate how capacity-aware decision policies can improve both predictive performance and fairness by addressing censoring bias.

title: Finite-Temperature Magnetism and Longitudinal Spin Transport in Compensated Half-Metal Ferrimagnets with Near-Zero Magnetization
text:
Title: Finite-Temperature Magnetism and Longitudinal Spin Transport in Compensated Half-Metal Ferrimagnets with Near-Zero Magnetization
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Fully compensated ferrimagnets, characterized by nearly vanishing magnetic moments at zero temperature, perfect spin-polarized electronic structures, and ultrafast spin dynamics, represent a highly promising materials platform for next-generation spintronic devices. By minimizing stray magnetic fields and reducing switching currents, FCFs enable a viable path toward high-speed, low-power spintronic devices. In this work, we present a systematic investigation of the electronic structure, finite-temperature magnetism, and spin-dependent transport properties of the Heusler-type fully compensated half-metallic ferrimagnet Mn3Al in magnetic tunnel junctions. We demonstrate that Mn3Al is a half-metallic FCF with 100% spin polarization and fully compensated magnetization at 0 K. Combining density functional theory with Monte Carlo simulations, we characterize its finite-temperature magnetic properties and show that Mn3Al exhibits a net magnetization below 11.6 emu/cc at 300 K, confirming the robustness of its nearly compensated ferrimagnetic order at room temperature. Furthermore, we predict that the Mn3Al/MgO/Mn3Al MTJ yields a giant tunneling magnetoresistance effect at 0 K, which remains as high as 232% at 300 K. Our results establish Mn3Al and related half-metallic FCFs as excellent candidates for magnetoresistance-based spintronic applications.

title: eAdS- embedded AdS, tensionless strings and contracted Carroll-Weyl symmetry
text:
Title: eAdS- embedded AdS, tensionless strings and contracted Carroll-Weyl symmetry
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We adapt the Dirac conformal $d+2$ dimensional embedding construction to define a null string in $AdS_{d+1}$. Introducing an extra Stückelberg field $\varphi$, which is a scalar under $AdS$ and shifts under local scaling of embedding space, the model acquires a local scaling invariance. We refer to this string as the embedded anti-De Sitter, $eAdS$, null string. A very useful property of this new gauged formulation is that, unlike previous gauged actions in $AdS$ background, the local scaling symmetry commutes with the $so(d,2)$ symmetry of $AdS$. Interestingly, the $eAdS$ null string is the tensionless limit of a tensile string in embedding space and the same holds for its reduction to an intrinsic description of AdS. We display the symmetries and constraint algebras both in embedding space and directly in AdS.

title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
text:
Title: Two-Component Dark Matter and Strongly First-Order Electroweak Phase Transition via a Two-Step Mechanism in the Inert Doublet plus Real Singlet Model
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We study a two-component dark matter model in which a real singlet scalar and an inert doublet scalar are simultaneously present alongside the Standard Model, each stabilized by an independent discrete symmetry. The real singlet undergoes a strong first-order transition at high temperature, establishing an intermediate phase with a non-zero singlet vacuum expectation value, which in turn generates the barrier required for the Higgs field to complete a strongly first-order electroweak transition at a lower temperature. This two-step mechanism naturally enforces the condition $v_c/T_c \geq 1$, the sphaleron washout-avoidance criterion necessary for electroweak baryogenesis. The gravitational wave spectrum from both steps is computed; the second step produces a decihertz signal, peaking near $0.08$--$0.34~\mathrm{Hz}$ across the viable parameter space and $0.14$--$0.22~\mathrm{Hz}$ at the benchmark points, that reaches the sensitivity of DECIGO for the strongest transitions and of BBO more widely, while the first remains sub-threshold for all planned detectors. At the coupling values required to drive the phase transition, the singlet is generically underabundant as a thermal relic, so the inert doublet carries the dominant fraction of the observed relic density. Confronting the model with current constraints, we find that the LUX-ZEPLIN 2024 result excludes the entire electroweak-phase-transition-viable parameter space of the singlet sector across the full mass range, even after rescaling by the singlet relic fraction, establishing a complete no-go for the singlet as a viable thermal dark matter candidate in this framework.

title: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification on Simplicial Complexes with Conformalized Simplicial Neural Networks
text:
Title: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification on Simplicial Complexes with Conformalized Simplicial Neural Networks
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Simplicial neural networks (SNNs) are powerful tools for prediction tasks on higher-order relational datasets stored on simplicial complexes (SCs), a higher-order generalization of graphs. However, SNNs usually lack rigorous uncertainty quantification (UQ), limiting their usefulness in high-stakes scenarios. We propose conformalized SNN (CF-SNN), a framework that, given a simplicial-complex entity with m prediction targets, generates prediction sets for all m targets simultaneously. Under mild assumptions, CF-SNN guarantees that, for each target, the prediction set contains the true label with a user-specified nominal coverage probability, and the realized miscoverage proportion across all m targets is guaranteed to remain close to the nominal level with high probability. Extensive experiments across a wide range of SC prediction tasks demonstrate that CF-SNN is a flexible UQ framework that achieves user-specified coverage while producing informative prediction sets of small size.

title: Getting Ready For Analysing Rubin Data : CLMM v2, The Updated LSST-DESC Cluster Weak Lensing Mass Modeling Library For Cosmology
text:
Title: Getting Ready For Analysing Rubin Data : CLMM v2, The Updated LSST-DESC Cluster Weak Lensing Mass Modeling Library For Cosmology
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The Dark Energy Science Collaboration has prepared a multitude of pipelines to process the upcoming Vera C. Rubin Observatory data and perform different scientific analyses. Here, we present the methodology to constrain the mass information of galaxy clusters from weak lensing, which is encompassed by the v2.0 release of the Cluster Lensing Mass Modeling (CLMM) code. This Python library provides the ingredients for both the modeling and data reduction of lensing observables, and the improvements in the new version were customized to handle the first WL analyses of LSST clusters, including, e.g., stacking functionalities and WL multipoles. This new version of CLMM has allowed various cluster analyses using LSST-DESC simulated data, precursor survey and Rubin commissioning and survey validation data, and is ready to be used for the first cluster cosmology analyses. CLMM is an open-source software package collaboratively written in Python, providing multiple example notebooks, including a set that can reproduce all figures in this work, and extensive documentation, publicly available at https://lsstdesc.org/CLMM/.

title: Vacuum Phase Transition and Decay to Cross the Phantom Divide
text:
Title: Vacuum Phase Transition and Decay to Cross the Phantom Divide
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We show that the vacuum metamorphosis model with decay fits current baryon acoustic oscillation and supernova distance data and cosmic microwave background measurements significantly better than $Λ$CDM and nearly as well as $w_0w_a$CDM with the same number of parameters. Vacuum metamorphosis with decay provides a physically motivated model of dark energy and an explanation of current cosmological data. In this scenario, non-perturbative quantum effects of a massive scalar field freeze the Ricci scalar curvature when it reaches a critical value proportional to the mass squared, inducing a phase transition in the scalar field, giving a phantom dark energy equation of state $w -1$, in agreement with current cosmological indications, without requiring an explicit coupling to matter.

title: Dispersion interaction between two bodies of arbitrary shape
text:
Title: Dispersion interaction between two bodies of arbitrary shape
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Based on the vacuum tensor Green's functions of electrodynamics, the Lippmann-Schwinger-type equations were derived for the correlations of electromagnetic fields. These correlations were applied within the Maxwell stress tensor and the Lorentz force formula to determine Casimir dispersion forces for two arbitrary bodies. The analysis is performed by the excitation of bodies by electric and magnetic dipoles.

title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model
text:
Title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We study the Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow of the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model, a four-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge theory with chirally invariant four-Fermi interactions, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group~(GFERG). Our gauge-invariant ansatz (truncation) for the 1PI Wilson action keeps a general photon kinetic function~$\mathcal{K}_τ(k^2)$, the fermion mass, and the scalar and vector four-Fermi couplings. For a fixed gauge coupling~$e^2$, the Gaussian and NJL (quasi-)fixed points on the critical surface merge at~$e_c^2\simeq17$, as anticipated by the ladder Schwinger--Dyson equation and the conventional Wilsonian renormalization group. We then let $e^2$ itself flow. Owing to the manifest gauge invariance of the GFERG, the flow of~$e^2$ is governed solely by the photon anomalous dimension~$γ_A$, which remains positive along both branches up to the merging point. Hence, no fixed point with~$e^2\neq0$ exists. Flows from a sufficiently large~$e^2$ in the ultraviolet (UV) reach the chirally broken phase even for vanishing four-Fermi couplings, so the gauge interaction does trigger chiral symmetry breaking. The merging point, however, is not a fixed point, and the gauge coupling vanishes in any continuum limit within our truncation.

title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
text:
Title: Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Using Routed Ensembles and Trajectory Attribution
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Multi-objective reinforcement learning is a fundamental problem for modern AI, with applications spanning post-training, reasoning models, and robotic control. A central challenge is to learn policies that balance competing objectives, such as helpfulness versus honesty in safety and alignment, or speed versus energy in robotics. The optimal policy can vary sharply with objective-weighting combinations, and the extent of this variation depends crucially on the degree of conflict among objectives, making per-preference policy learning sample-inefficient. In this paper, we introduce objective-conflict coefficients and derive near-optimal regret bounds for online settings using this measure, thereby quantifying the impact of misalignment on learning efficiency. Then, we design routed ensemble policy learning, an algorithm that maintains a small set of basis policies and dynamically routes trajectories to the policy with the highest potential reward. Finally, we consider trajectory selection as another approach to mitigate objective conflict, and design a kernel surrogate trajectory attribution algorithm that estimates how feedback signals from a set of trajectories influence policy learning on other trajectories. The kernel can capture nonlinear interactions such as synergy and antagonism between trajectories. We evaluate our approach across diverse environments and benchmarks: routed ensembles improve average performance by 4.3% over baselines for online environments from Meta-World and MO-Gymnasium, and kernel surrogate attribution improves correlation with leave-one-out analysis over existing baselines by 50%. When applied to trajectory selection, kernel-based attribution yields a 27% improvement in reward over baseline attribution methods.

title: Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals
text:
Title: Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Infrared spectroscopy is a key tool to study complex structural dynamics in molecular systems. However, resolving weak or broad vibrational modes is challenging due to their rapid decay. Here, we demonstrate a technique to significantly extend the detectable lifetime - and thereby spectral resolution - of molecular signatures by employing synchronized time-gated optical parametric amplification of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals. Utilizing a Cr:ZnS laser system and a nonlinear ZnGeP2 crystal, we achieve a 10-fold increase in the electric field strength of the infrared molecular signal, yielding a two-orders of magnitude enhancement in dynamic range and a 2-fold increase in the signal-to-noise ratio. Using isopropyl alcohol as a model system, we demonstrate that OPA-enhanced detection extends the observable window of vibrational modes up to 72 %. This approach allows for the reconstruction of high-fidelity molecular fingerprints that resolve complex vibrational relaxation pathways and weak structural dynamics, previously hidden within the background and noise, providing a pathway for new high-sensitivity and time-resolved studies of complex chemical structures.

title: Reward-Estimated Hypergradient for Bilevel Reinforcement Learning with Black-Box Follower
text:
Title: Reward-Estimated Hypergradient for Bilevel Reinforcement Learning with Black-Box Follower
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Hypergradient (HG) methods for bilevel reinforcement learning (RL) typically assume a white-box follower whose reward is known. In practice, however, the leader rarely knows the follower's reward function and can only observe its trajectories. We address this black-box setting and propose Reward-Estimated Hypergradients (RE-HG), which recovers the follower's reward from these trajectories via inverse RL (IRL). Yet IRL identifies the reward only up to potential-based shaping, a transformation that leaves the follower's behavior unchanged but biases the HG. We prove that, for linear rewards, this bias cancels when IRL estimates are aggregated across sufficiently diverse dynamics, which the leader's own updates naturally supply. To handle finite samples, RE-HG truncates small eigenvalues of the aggregated feature covariance, restoring the identifiable subspace and stabilizing the estimation. Experiments show that RE-HG estimates gradients aligned with a white-box Oracle and achieves comparable performance; empirically, the truncation also suppresses HG explosions, letting RE-HG avoid local optima that trap the Oracle in sharp reward landscapes.

title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
text:
Title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry. Quantum emitters were found in BNNTs spanning the entirety of the visible spectrum, including spectral regions where SPEs within hBN have not been reported. Furthermore, each tube was found to possess multiple SPEs at varying emission wavelengths along the length, exhibiting lifetimes as fast as 0.5 ns, which is about two-fold faster than the fastest hBN SPEs. Additionally, we demonstrate that surface passivation/coating mitigates blinking events, therefore increasing the emitter stability. Thus, BNNTs can function as a single structure supporting a variety of multiwavelength SPE sources, while maintaining a compact radius of ~25 nm, making them ideally suited for deterministic placement and integration within nanophotonic devices such as waveguides and interferometric filters.

title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
text:
Title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
text:
Title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. We present BitDecoding-FP4, an algorithm--system co-design for accurate and efficient native FP4 KV decoding. We mitigate three error sources: Dual-Residual Query Quantization splits queries into two FP4 tensors, cutting query logit error from 60% to 1%; Underflow-Aware Probability Scaling prevents E4M3 scales from rounding long-context probabilities to zero; and Outlier-Aware Key Quantization combines static smoothing, Hadamard rotation, and scale search to suppress key outliers under token-wise scaling. At the system level, we remove the softmax bottleneck via transposed softmax with fused probability quantization and stacked query MMA on paged KV caches. Across dense and MoE models with GQA and MLA, BitDecoding-FP4 stays within 0.5 points of BF16 KV accuracy with NVFP4 (1 point with MXFP4), and tracks BF16 KV in RL training rollouts. In end-to-end serving on NVIDIA B300 with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, it delivers 2.4-3.0$\times$ higher peak serving throughput than BF16 KV. The implementation is available at https://github.com/OpenBitSys/BitDecoding-FP4.

title: Spin Relaxation and Electrical Control of Spin Transport in Few-Layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$
text:
Title: Spin Relaxation and Electrical Control of Spin Transport in Few-Layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We report electrical tuning of spin relaxation in atomically thin $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, a representative low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenide. Weak antilocalization measurements reveal strong spin--orbit interaction with spin--orbit lengths of tens of nanometers, consistent with recent theoretical predictions. Despite the semimetallic nature of $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, in the ultrathin limit the spin--orbit scattering time can be tuned electrostatically by up to threefold. We further investigate vertical electric field effects on the spin--orbit length and time, and demonstrate the modulation of the Rashba parameters. Relation between spin--orbit scattering time and the diffusion coefficient indicates that spin relaxation is governed by the D'yakonov--Perel' mechanism in both monolayer and bilayer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$. These results establish few-layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$ as a platform for electrically tunable spin transport, thereby providing insight into spin relaxation in low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenides.

title: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Large Vision-Language Models
text:
Title: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Large Vision-Language Models
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Large vision-language models (LVLMs) are vulnerable to compositional harm: an image and a prompt that are benign in isolation become harmful through the model's cross-modal reasoning. Recent alignment methods report strong scores on compositional safety benchmarks, but an LLM judge only measures observed behavior and cannot reveal how robustly safety is integrated into the model. We argue that un-alignment provides a complementary audit of alignment robustness. We first show that minimal supervised fine-tuning reaches an LLM-judge score comparable to a multi-stage reinforcement-learning pipeline, so similar benchmark scores cannot establish robustness by themselves. We then show that recognition and refusal of compositional harm are decoupled: nine standard direction-finding methods detect compositional harm with up to AUC=0.99, yet ablating the recovered directions either leaves refusal intact or destroys model coherence. We therefore propose CMaG, a training-free un-alignment method for compositional safety. CMaG measures refusal intention with a refusal-versus-compliance log-probability margin, takes its gradient with respect to mid-layer activations, and contrasts it against partially benign pairs to isolate the cross-modal interaction term. A single backward pass over 80 examples yields a direction along which steering monotonically converts refusal into compliance. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA-1.5-7B, CMaG reduces compositional safety scores by up to 65 points while over 98% of outputs remain coherent, outperforming gradient-based baselines; the direction also transfers to text-explicit harm and un-aligns models hardened by defensive training. Compositional safety can thus appear behaviorally strong while remaining fragile to targeted internal intervention. Warning: this paper contains unsafe model outputs, including references to self-harm.

title: Prior-Data Fitted Networks for In-Context Off-Policy Evaluation
text:
Title: Prior-Data Fitted Networks for In-Context Off-Policy Evaluation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Off-policy evaluation (OPE) is essential for assessing decision policies before deployment when online experimentation is costly or unsafe. Accurate estimation remains difficult when behavior-policy data are limited and the target policy favors states and actions rarely observed in those data. We propose InCOPE, a prior-data fitted network that learns a shared policy-value prediction rule across synthetic OPE tasks. We construct an OPE task prior over Markov decision processes and behavior-target policy pairs, generating behavior-policy datasets and exact target-policy values for pretraining. For a new tabular decision problem, the pretrained network uses the behavior-policy dataset, target policy, and known task settings as context to predict the policy's expected return without task-specific parameter updates. Experiments across four tabular domains, including a semi-synthetic clinical setting, demonstrate InCOPE's effectiveness for policy-value estimation.

title: Mapping Instructors' Attitudes Towards Cheating with AI: An Exploratory Analysis Using Forum Analysis
text:
Title: Mapping Instructors' Attitudes Towards Cheating with AI: An Exploratory Analysis Using Forum Analysis
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

In teaching and learning environments, cheating and the violation of academic integrity have always been one of the challenges, involving different levels of concerns such as administrative, personal knowledge, learning, and equity. The introduction of large language models has brought cheating in dialogue to the forefront, given the apparent capabilities of these models to complete students' academic assignments. This study aims to leverage recent dialogues among university professors about cheating with Generative AI to better understand their beliefs about academic honesty. In doing so, we analyze a corpus of 2.01 million posts (threads and comments) in the r/Professors subreddit discussing cheating after the release of ChatGPT, providing a better understanding of teachers' motivations to discourage cheating and the strategies they use to do so. We synthesize the why and how of addressing cheating to identify caveats about the future of AI and academic integration.

title: Quantum Probability Current Guided Reduction of Coupling Control Degrees of Freedom for Excitation Transport
text:
Title: Quantum Probability Current Guided Reduction of Coupling Control Degrees of Freedom for Excitation Transport
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Time-dependent coherent control can enhance excitation transport in open quantum networks, but independently controlling every inter-site coupling creates a control space of high dimension and leads to difficult optimization problems. We introduce an edge-ranking strategy based on the control-induced change in the gradient component of the time-integrated quantum probability current, which is obtained via a graph Hodge decomposition. When our strategy is applied to the seven-site Fenna-Matthews-Olson (FMO) model, the six-edge set retains $99.83\%$ of the enhancement achieved by full control, and the four-edge set retains $97.60\%$ while reducing the pulse fluence---used here as a proxy for control effort---by $41.55\%$ relative to full control. Dephasing scans and comparisons with random edge sets and random networks provide numerical support for the relevance and potential broader utility of the ranking. These results show that edge selection guided by the quantum probability current can substantially reduce the control space while preserving high transport performance with lower control effort.

title: Bi-parameter local linearization and parameter estimation for the damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation with spatially colored noise
text:
Title: Bi-parameter local linearization and parameter estimation for the damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation with spatially colored noise
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation driven by Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space, with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$. For a globally Lipschitz diffusion coefficient, we approximate characteristic mixed increments by those of the additive equation, multiplied by the coefficient frozen at the base point. A critical-kernel reduction and localized Riesz covariance estimates control the additional kernel terms and spatial correlations. We also establish $L^p$ error bounds for normalized quadratic variations and, under a nondegeneracy condition, construct jointly strongly consistent estimators of the Hurst parameter and a positive diffusion parameter.

title: Translate, then decide: asymptotic optimality of latent-space control in bistable systems
text:
Title: Translate, then decide: asymptotic optimality of latent-space control in bistable systems
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This paper asks whether an optimal decision can be separated from the physical dynamics on which it acts. It studies this question through minimum-energy barrier crossing in scalar bistable systems. It characterizes the finite-horizon optimal feedback and shows that, as the horizon grows, it converges to a law that doubles and reverses the drift while it opposes crossing, and switches off once the barrier is passed. In physical coordinates, this law inherits the plant's nonlinearity, entangling decision and dynamics. We show that a plant-specific translation of state, input, and time maps every double well in the considered class to the same unit-rate linear world model, allowing a downstream decision stage to use a single plant-independent control primitive. This separation generally loses optimality at finite horizons because the translation does not preserve the physical control energy. Nevertheless, we prove that the excess physical energy of the layered controller vanishes as the horizon grows and that its limiting feedback reproduces the asymptotic optimum exactly. Thus, translation and optimization generally do not commute at a finite horizon, but commute in the asymptotic limit.

title: Moiré reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface
text:
Title: Moiré reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Twisted oxide double layers have emerged as a promising platform for exploring moiré physics, including polar topologies and emergent electronic phases. However, the intrinsic complexity of oxide surfaces, such as contamination, roughness, and the presence of two distinct terminations (AO and BO2), can complicate the identification of buried interfacial structures. Here, using atomically flat SrTiO3 membranes with a predominantly SrO-TiO2 interfacial configuration, we directly visualize a moiré-periodic structural reconstruction at the buried interface that is distinct from the geometric moiré of rigid stacking. The reconstructed interface hosts head-to-head-like polar distortions, moiré-modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance in otherwise paraelectric and insulating SrTiO3. Our work demonstrates that, with a well-defined termination, moiré reconstruction could serve as a route to emergent electrical behavior in twisted perovskite oxides.

title: Physical regimes of quartic quantum advantage in elastic media simulation
text:
Title: Physical regimes of quartic quantum advantage in elastic media simulation
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum algorithms for elastic media simulation have been conjectured to offer up to a quartic quantum advantage over classical methods; however, the devil is always in the details. Here, we determine key physical conditions under which this quartic separation could be achieved in the relevant parameters. For continuum elastic dynamics at fixed volume with spatial convergence order $m$, we find that the end-to-end speedup is of order $(m+4)/(m+1)$ in the simulation time, and $4/(m+1)$ in the accuracy, with exponential memory advantage. For elastic lattice systems, we define microscopically resolved bulk observables (MRBOs) as those that can be efficiently extracted from a quantum state, but cannot be resolved by a known continuum model with fewer degrees of freedom than the lattice. We then argue that the estimation of MRBOs is a candidate problem for quartic quantum advantage in problem size. We propose MRBOs for pseudorandom heterogeneous materials as an explicit end-to-end application where this occurs, while admitting efficient `quantum cheese' encodings of the material properties. We thus demonstrate how the interplay between regularity, physical scale, observable sensitivity and quantum encodability constrains the relation between classical and quantum complexity.

title: Proximal gradient method for multiobjective interval valued optimization problem with application in portfolio selection
text:
Title: Proximal gradient method for multiobjective interval valued optimization problem with application in portfolio selection
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

In this article, we consider a class of unconstrained multiobjective interval-valued optimization problems in which each objective function is a sum of a generalized Hukuhara(gH)-differentiable interval valued function and a proper, convex and gH-lower semicontinuous interval valued function, which is possibly non-gH-differentiable. Within this framework, we introduce the notion of a proximal gradient direction and characterize the Pareto critical points of the considered problem through a strongly convex auxiliary subproblem. Based on these characterizations, we develop a proximal gradient algorithm with an Armijo-type line search that ensures sufficient descent with respect to the interval partial order. We then establish the existence of an uniform lower bound on the admissible step length, the global convergence of the generated sequence to a Pareto critical point followed by a global rate of convergence in the general nonconvex setting. The theoretical findings of the proposed method are validated through some test problems and further illustrate its applicability on portfolio selection problems involving interval-valued data.

title: Learning Latent Protein Languages for Autoregressive Generation
text:
Title: Learning Latent Protein Languages for Autoregressive Generation
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Autoregressive transformers remain comparatively weak for protein sequence and structure generation. We study the role of target representation: amino acid tokens encode residue identities without explicit contextual semantics, while backbone coordinates require a discrete representation in our framework. We introduce two learned latent protein languages. Protein Latent Language (PLL) maps sequences to a 4,096-state contextual alphabet built on a frozen ESM-2 encoder, with one token per residue. Structure Latent Language (SLL) adapts GCP-VQVAE Lite with auxiliary sequence and confidence supervision while retaining decoding to backbone coordinates. We separately pretrain autoregressive transformer models on PLL and SLL tokens using next-token prediction, yielding PLLM and SLLM. Under matched downstream sequence training, PLLM has a fitted compute-scaling exponent of 0.038 versus 0.020 for the amino acid autoregressive model. In unconditional sequence generation, PLLM reduces the fraction of samples below a heuristic 1.5-bit residue-composition entropy threshold by 54% relative to the amino acid model across sampling temperatures. For sequence-to-structure prediction, replacing the original GCP-VQVAE Lite tokenizer with SLL reduces best validation perplexity by 34% under matched training. For long proteins, latent-token sampling is approximately 1,000 times faster than MSA-based AlphaFold2 in our measurements. In backbone generation, SLLM compares favorably with other generative models on diversity and novelty. We also observe early signs that using SLLM's internal token confidence for inference-time sampling can improve sequence-to-structure prediction quality beyond a single decoded sample. These results position learned latent protein languages as a promising substrate for autoregressive transformer scaling and inference-time sampling in protein generation.

title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee
text:
Title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

In recent years, singular-spectrum-based optimizers have attracted increasing attention due to their ability to preserve the matrix structure of neural network gradients, thereby enabling geometry-aware optimization. However, most singular-spectrum-based (SSB) approaches remain centralized, limiting their use in distributed learning infrastructures that exploit massive parallelism. Distributed SSB optimization is still at an early stage, with open questions about convergence guarantees and communication efficiency. To fill this gap, we propose the Distributed Momentum-based Spectral Estimator (DisMUSE), an efficient distributed SSB optimization framework for both data-center and federated settings. Using Muon-style exact orthogonalized momentum as the spectral update, DisMUSE integrates a recursive variance-reduced momentum estimator and achieves an $O((KT)^{-1/3})$ convergence rate, where $K$ and $T$ denote the number of nodes and local iterations per node, respectively. This rate matches the best-known rates for variance-reduced nonconvex distributed optimization. Building on this variance-reduced framework, we study two extensions. First, our DisMUSE method with finite Newton-Schulz (NS) iterations preserves the same convergence order under a uniform normalized support-spectrum condition, up to a multiplicative factor. Second, we develop a communication-efficient variant based on low-rank (LR) momentum transmission and quantify the error it introduces to the stationarity bound, characterizing the trade-off between accuracy and communication cost.

title: On Particle Production from Bubble Collisions in the Non-runaway Regime
text:
Title: On Particle Production from Bubble Collisions in the Non-runaway Regime
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Particle production from bubble collisions during First-Order Phase Transitions (FOPTs) has been studied as an efficient mechanism for baryogenesis and dark matter production, but existing semi-analytical treatments assume runaway bubbles with wall velocity $v_w\to 1$. We generalize this treatment to arbitrary $v_w< 1$, relevant for scenarios such as electroweak baryogenesis and transitions with significant wall friction. We first extend the analytical trapping-equation approach to finite-thickness boosted kink profiles for both elastic and inelastic collisions, then go beyond this by numerically solving the full Klein-Gordon equation without assuming $SO(1,1)$ symmetry or thin walls, across a broad grid of $v_w$ and potential shapes. We find the analytical generalization underestimates the true efficiency factor by orders of magnitude away from $v_w\to 1$, and provide new semi-analytic fit functions consisting of a power-law continuum plus a resonance peak, which reproduce the main spectral features of the numerical results across the parameter range studied. Applying these to a toy dark sector model, we show particle production is strongly suppressed as $v_w$ decreases from unity, enhanced for lighter produced particles, and that the relative contribution from the oscillatory peak differs from prior runaway-regime estimates. We also discuss limitations of the trapping equation and the off-shell effective-action truncation underlying this formalism.

title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
text:
Title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models. In this paper, we develop a framework for computation with stochastic CRNs at the level of stationary means. Specifically, we construct elementary arithmetic modules for identification, addition, and multiplication, and analyze their mean-level correctness and convergence rates. We focus on these three modules because they are simple enough to analyze explicitly while already exhibiting the new issues raised by stochastic mean-level computation. Unlike in deterministic systems, the computed value cannot be read from a single output measurement. Instead, readout requires Monte Carlo estimation, with error arising from transient bias as the system approaches stationarity and intrinsic sampling noise that persists even at stationarity. We therefore study the convergence rates of output means, variances, and autocovariances to their stationary values, as well as the stationary fluctuations governing sampling error. We also show that this readout cost can depend strongly, and sometimes unexpectedly, on the architecture of the computation. In particular, comparing linear-chain and binary-tree implementations reveals that binary trees can greatly reduce stationary variance for addition, but can instead produce exponentially larger variance for multiplication.

title: Ordered Policy Optimization
text:
Title: Ordered Policy Optimization
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) stabilizes policy updates by clipping the importance ratio between the new policy and the data-collecting policy. The standard rule uses one fixed clipping range for all samples. While this choice offers simplicity and effectiveness, it fails to distinguish statistically harmful extreme ratio values from large, yet tolerable changes. We study how to adapt the clipping radius to the reliability of the induced importance ratio distribution. Our case study demonstrates that reliable updates require controlling these extreme ratios, rather than merely verifying that individual ratios fall within a fixed interval. Motivated by this observation, we propose Ordered Policy Optimization (\textsc{OPO}). In each minibatch, \textsc{OPO} sorts the importance ratios, selects the extreme ratios that potentially have the largest effect on the update, and assigns them adaptive sample-wise radii instead of using the fixed clipping radius. These radii are derived from a prescribed tail profile, which specifies desired target values for the selected extreme ratios. The resulting objective remains first-order and requires only minibatch sorting and a modified policy loss. Experiments conducted on MuJoCo and Atari benchmarks demonstrate that this simple modification achieves strong performance relative to established baselines.

title: SCorPion: A Strategic, Controllable and Personified Conversational Companion
text:
Title: SCorPion: A Strategic, Controllable and Personified Conversational Companion
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Fixed prompt-based language models face challenges in open-domain conversations, where versatile topics require different expert advice or demonstrations to maximize their universal performance. Motivated by the dynamic prompt studies in language generation, we extract different chatting strategies from varied forms of text corpus, which steer the language model to different styles based on human principles.
