We design and deploy a conversational companion called SCorPion, which uses GraphRAG to extract and summarize the knowledge graph globally, yield community-summarized strategies, and produce query-focused optimal strategies. SCorPion has strategic thinking, yields personified and stylized responses, and can be controlled by explicit factors. Code and further results can be found in https://bachozean.github.io/scorpion-page/.

title: Bogoliubov self-consistent $GW$ and second-order Green's function methods for attractive fermionic interactions
text:
Title: Bogoliubov self-consistent $GW$ and second-order Green's function methods for attractive fermionic interactions
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Describing fermionic systems with attractive interactions, such as superconductors and atomic nuclei, beyond the mean-field level remains a central challenge. In this work, we investigate the performance of Bogoliubov fully self-consistent $GW$ (Bog.~sc$GW$) and second-order Green's function (Bog.~scGF2) methods, implemented within a unified imaginary-time and imaginary-frequency framework. Using the attractive Hubbard model as a benchmark against full configuration interaction (FCI), we find that Bog. scGF2 provides a more accurate description than Bog.~sc$GW$. In particular, Bog.~sc$GW$ systematically overestimates the correlation energy, with errors increasing rapidly as the attractive interaction strength grows. These results highlight the importance of exchange contributions in strongly correlated fermionic systems, even when exchange effects are included only at low order in perturbation theory.

title: Cosmic birefringence tomography with radio galaxies I: Testing birefringence solutions to the CMB-BAO tension
text:
Title: Cosmic birefringence tomography with radio galaxies I: Testing birefringence solutions to the CMB-BAO tension
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We present an independent test of cosmic birefringence induced by axionlike particles (ALPs) at low redshift using radio galaxies. We focus on models that can alleviate the mild tension between recent baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements and observations of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). This tension can be explained by a large cosmic birefringence rotation angle generated during the reionization epoch. Such a large rotation can arise if the recent isotropic cosmic birefringence measurements are subject to an $nπ$ phase ambiguity, with $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, or if cold dark matter injects energy into ALPs. We constrain these two scenarios by fitting the cosmic birefringence angles estimated from the jet morphologies and polarization angles of radio galaxies obtained by Battye, Jackson & Browne (2026). For the $nπ$ model, the radio-galaxy data exclude $|n|\geq 1$ at more than $2σ$ for $\log_{10}(m_φ/{\rm eV})\lesssim -30.7$. For the energy injection model, the data are consistent with no energy injection, but with a slight relative preference for a nonzero energy injection compared to the no-injection case. Since our samples are limited to $\sim 3000$ and there could still be several astrophysical uncertainties and statistical fluctuations, further exploration of tomographic cosmic birefringence using a large number of low-redshift radio galaxies is important for independent tests of cosmic birefringence.

title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
text:
Title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

During extended wakefulness, mammalian neocortical networks experience localized periods of transient neuronal silence termed off-states. Here, we examine how analogous spatiotemporally concentrated disruptions affect sequential reasoning in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). Evaluating 250 paired derivations on the GSM8K benchmark across two 8B models (Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct), we contrast clustered bursts of attention head masking against budget-matched diffuse i.i.d. dropout. Concentrated bursts induce substantial reasoning degradation: at onset parameter $\mathcal{B}=0.10$ (scheduling $\sim 5.7\%$ of vulnerable head-token volume), Qwen3-8B accuracy drops from $91.2\%$ under diffuse noise to $78.8\%$ under burst dropout ($Δ= -12.4$ percentage points [pp], exact McNemar $p = 5.5 \times 10^{-6}$), while LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct drops from $84.0\%$ to $76.8\%$ ($Δ= -7.2$ pp, $p = 0.0198$). Conversely, dispersing the identical cumulative budget uniformly across generation steps via stratified quintile matching yields substantially milder degradation (retaining $91.2\%$ in Qwen and $84.0\%$ in LLaMA). In an exploratory factorial dissociation ($N=100$), single-step dropout density is associated with an acute drop in a single schedule draw ($-10.0$ pp on Qwen, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.0425$), while multi-token continuity exhibits an inconclusive compounding trend ($-7.0$ pp, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.1892$). Error analysis reveals that Qwen failures reflect derivation errors within formatted responses (conditional accuracy drop of $-11.4$ pp), whereas in LLaMA $22.2\%$ of discordant losses lack a final answer format line (conditional gap narrows to $-5.0$ pp). These findings demonstrate that autoregressive reasoning chains are particularly vulnerable to concentrated structural disruptions, providing empirical benchmarks for fault tolerance in transformer architectures.

title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching
text:
Title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

We present BARS (Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis), a non-autoregressive rapping voice generation model based on Flow Matching, conditioned on a beat track (instrumental backing), lyrics, and a short reference voice for zero-shot timbre control. Unlike prior autoregressive rap synthesis, where rap pace and output duration are strictly determined by the beat, BARS enables independent control over the rap tempo, allowing flexible-length generation without explicit duration prediction or phoneme-level alignment. We encode lyrics using a pretrained ByT5 encoder with a lightweight Transformer adapter trained jointly with the model, without relying on speech-pretrained text encoders, enabling natural handling of non-standard orthography (e.g., slang, abbreviations) and numerals common in rap lyrics. To address alignment instabilities, such as token skipping or repetition, under strong beat conditioning, we propose Asymmetric Scaled RoPE for cross-attention, which introduces a positional structure to facilitate sequential lyric-audio alignment learning. Furthermore, the model supports partial re-generation via span masking, enabling lyric-level editing while preserving the surrounding vocal style. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high lyric fidelity, natural rap flow that is rhythmically coherent with the beat, and robust tempo control across a wide range of rapping styles and speeds.

title: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
text:
Title: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study antiferromagnetic spin systems on random regular graphs through the lens of the phase transitions characterized by the complex zeros of the partition function. Our motivating examples include the hardcore model and the antiferromagnetic Potts model (including proper $q$-colorings at $β=0$). For both models on random $d$-regular graphs, we establish, with high probability over the graph, zero-free regions throughout the interior of the replica-symmetric regime. Asymptotically, this regime extends up to tree occupation density $$α< α_{\mathrm{RSB}}(d) = (2\log d - 2\log\log d + 2 - 2\log 2 + o_d(1))/d$$ for the hardcore model and up to degree $$d < d_{\mathrm{RSB}}(q) = (2q-1)\log q - 2\log 2 + o_q(1)$$ for proper $q$-colorings. Leveraging the standard algorithmic implications of zero-freeness, we obtain deterministic polynomial-time algorithms that multiplicatively approximate the corresponding partition functions at fixed rational parameters throughout this regime, with high probability over the graph. Our algorithmic guarantees significantly improve upon prior work and extend beyond the parameter ranges reached by previously known search algorithms. As a key intermediate step, we establish the pointwise equivalence, away from the threshold, of three notions of replica symmetry: geometric (averaged pairwise correlation decay), thermodynamic (convergence to the Bethe free-energy prediction), and variational (nonpositivity of the Bethe functional). To establish zero-freeness, we develop reinforced small subgraph conditioning, lifting classical small subgraph conditioning to random holomorphic functions to control short-cycle fluctuations. We also use variational replica symmetry to obtain exponential planted overlap concentration. This enables a typical-graph truncation that controls complex second moments up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold.

title: Volcanite: Commodity-Hardware Segmentation Volume Visualization for Connectomics and Beyond
text:
Title: Volcanite: Commodity-Hardware Segmentation Volume Visualization for Connectomics and Beyond
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Modern imaging produces terabyte-scale segmentation volumes, assigning each voxel an object label. These categorical, boundary-sensitive and label-rich data underpin connectomics and other imaging-driven fields, yet their scale often forces interpretation through slices, approximate meshes or distributed workflows that obscure spatial context and voxel-level defects. Here we show that such volumes can be explored directly on commodity hardware with Volcanite, an open-source framework for dense-segmentation rendering. Combining compression-aware data handling, a Vulkan GPU backend and segmentation-specific rendering, Volcanite enables low-latency exploration without meshing or distributed infrastructure, including for unpublished, sensitive or proprietary data. Across multi-domain datasets, it preserves voxel labels, adds shadows and global illumination, and renders up to half a trillion voxels at 100 frames per second. By replacing lengthy preprocessing with direct inspection, Volcanite decouples hypothesis generation from data preparation and turns teravoxel label fields into interactive evidence for discovery, validation and cross-domain spatial analysis

title: FoldKit: A Python library for efficient storage and retrieval of co-folding predictions
text:
Title: FoldKit: A Python library for efficient storage and retrieval of co-folding predictions
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

AlphaFold 3 (AF3) enables structure prediction of biomolecular complexes through co-folding multiple interacting molecules, making it increasingly useful for de novo protein design and for large-scale studies of protein-protein, protein-peptide, and other biomolecular interactions. However, systematic co-folding experiments can produce large volumes of output data, particularly when multiple random seeds and samples are generated for each input complex. We introduce FoldKit, a Python package for efficient storage and analysis of large-scale AF3 co-folding results. FoldKit converts raw AF3 outputs into a compact, structured representation while preserving the metadata needed for downstream analysis. The FoldKit Python library provides convenient programmatic access to global, single chain, and interface confidence metrics such as pLDDT, pTM, ipTM, ipAE, and ipSAE, as well as an ensemble-level interface for accessing and aggregating these metrics for a single input across multiple seeds and samples. We benchmark FoldKit on three types of AF3 co-folding datasets: (i) a protein design campaign with 2 chains per input, (ii) a TCR-pMHC dataset with 4 chains per input, and (iii) a pooled-AF3 protein-protein interaction dataset with up to 22 chains per input. We find that FoldKit reduces storage requirements by approximately 5-15-fold compared to native AF3 outputs, depending on dataset composition, while maintaining direct programmatic access to individual predictions, ensembles, and confidence metrics. By reducing storage requirements and facilitating programmatic access to relevant outputs, FoldKit facilitates large-scale computational studies of biomolecular interactions. FoldKit is available from PyPI and can be installed using pip.

title: What Changed in Engineering Writing After Generative AI Chat Assistants: Evidence from 1.8 Million Articles
text:
Title: What Changed in Engineering Writing After Generative AI Chat Assistants: Evidence from 1.8 Million Articles
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

This study asks what changed in engineering articles after conversational language models became publicly available on November 30, 2022, and develops methods for measuring such change in a field without a uniform abstract index. It assembled 1,839,962 articles published from 2015 to 2025 in 256 engineering journals, tracked twelve measures of wording, style, and article structure, and compared each with the projection of its own pre-2023 trend. Building the monthly series showed that records dated only by year fall on January 1 and create false January peaks unless removed. In abstracts, 31 words associated with language model output appeared 82% more often than projected (55.4 against 27.0 per 10,000 words in 2025), while four control words of the same formal register fell 16%. Words that soften a claim, such as may, fell 13%, words that strengthen one, such as clearly, rose 20%, and long words rose 11%. Author counts, reference lists, page counts, and publication volume stayed within 4% of trend. The change appears in all fourteen subject categories, and false release dates, dropping any one journal or word, and word lists chosen from the data support it. A random sample of 12,866 full texts from the same corpus, including subscription articles and weighted back to it, shows the same words rising 99% in article bodies. Statements disclosing AI writing assistance, measured apart from mentions of language models, went from none to 3.7% in 2025, four in five of them at one publisher. The design is descriptive, not causal.

title: A characterization and closure property of Thorin's class
text:
Title: A characterization and closure property of Thorin's class
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Thorin's class coincides with the smallest class of probability laws on $\mathbb{R}$ that contains all gamma laws and their reflections, while being closed under convolution and weak convergence. In particular, all Thorin laws are self-decomposable. This paper proves an alternative characterization of Thorin's class in terms of what we call the hyperbolic Bochner-Bernstein property. This property corresponds to the notion of hyperbolically completely monotone Laplace transforms on the positive half line, but extended to the real-valued setting. Using the new characterization, it is shown that Thorin's class is closed under multiplication with independent random variables admitting hyperbolically completely monotone densities, which partly settles an open question raised by Bondesson and allows for proving that a large class of possibly skewed real-valued distributions is in Thorin's class. As particular examples, we apply the closure property to show that Johnson's S\textsubscript{U} distribution and the Pearson type IV distribution are in Thorin's class for all parameter choices.

title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
text:
Title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate. We classify the poles and derive the conditions on the effective couplings for poles of order $p=2$ and $p=3$, the maximal order allowed in this setting. We then proceed to study inflation. Second-order poles realize $α$-attractors with $α$ fixed by the residue and are already available in the parity-even sector of the theory. Third-order poles instead require the parity-odd sector: whenever the parity-odd quadratic couplings vanish, the kinetic function splits into two independent terms with poles of order at most $p=2$. Third-order pole-inflation, as we confirm numerically for $f(φ)\proptoφ^2$, yields $r\propto N_*^{-3/2}$ with a tunable amplitude and $n_s\simeq 1-\tfrac{3}{2N_*}$, a spectral index mildly larger than the $α$-attractor prediction and well centered in the region preferred by the current combination of ACT, SPT and DESI data. Moreover, when inflation happens far away from the pole we also find a further universal attractor, an inverse-linear plateau, with $n_s \simeq 1-\frac{4}{3N_*}$ and $r\propto N_*^{-4/3}$, testable with the forthcoming BICEP/Keck observations.

title: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls
text:
Title: Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Text encoders turn earnings calls into vectors for search, for language models that answer from retrieved passages, and for forecasting models. A live retriever can use an encoder trained once on all available text, as finance retrievers are, but a backtest needs an encoder that read no text written after the date of each vector. To address this look-ahead bias, from 412,248 calls we train vintages under four pretraining recipes, with yearly cutoffs from 2010 to 2024, and each vintage reads only text dated on or before its cutoff. We then fine-tune each vintage on the question-answer pairs of the calls themselves. The vintages we train on calls alone, with 33.8M parameters, retrieve answers on held-out calls better than the general retrievers we tested in every test quarter. Their vectors also raise by about half the rank correlation between next-day returns and forecasts built from past returns and firm size. When each vintage continues the previous one, a later vintage retrieves better on earlier quarters than the vintage available at the time, and a point-in-time language model that answers from the passages the later vintage retrieves inherits the gain. The 2024 vintage of our families also forecasts earnings surprises better, although the interval of this gain includes zero on calls that no vintage read. It forecasts returns no better, so point-in-time vintages matter most for retrieval and little for forecasts of returns.

title: Density and excess molar enthalpy of 2-butanol + glyme liquid mixtures. Application of the DISQUAC, UNIFAC (Dortmund) and ERAS models to 2-alkanol + linear ether systems
text:
Title: Density and excess molar enthalpy of 2-butanol + glyme liquid mixtures. Application of the DISQUAC, UNIFAC (Dortmund) and ERAS models to 2-alkanol + linear ether systems
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Densities and excess molar volumes ($V_{\text{m}}^{\text{E}}$) at (293.15 to 303.15) K and excess molar enthalpies ($H_{\text{m}}^{\text{E}}$) at 298.15 K are reported for the 2-butanol + 2,5-dioxahexane, or + 2,5,8-trioxanonane, or + 2,5,8,11-tetraoxadodecane, or + 2,5,8,11,14-pentaoxapentadecane systems at 95 kPa. Densities were measured using a densitometer Anton Paar DSA 5000, and excess enthalpies by means of a micro-calorimeter Tian-Calvet. $H_{\text{m}}^{\text{E}}$ and $V_{\text{m}}^{\text{E}}$ data are positive, indicating that interactions between like molecules are dominant and that the main contribution to $V_{\text{m}}^{\text{E}}$ is the interactional one. Our enthalpic data together with data from the literature have been used to evaluate the enthalpy of alcohol-glyme interactions, which are ranged between ($-$31 and $-$22) kJ mol$^{-1}$. From the comparison with $H_{\text{m}}^{\text{E}}$ results for glyme + heptane systems, and from the position of the investigated mixtures in the diagram $G_{\text{m}}^{\text{E}}$ (excess molar Gibbs energy) vs. $H_{\text{m}}^{\text{E}}$, it is shown that interactions are of dispersive type. 2-Alkanol + dipropyl ether (DPE), or + glyme systems have also been studied using the DISQUAC, UNIFAC (Dortmund) and ERAS models. According to ERAS results, physical interactions in glyme systems are dominant, while association effects are predominant in mixtures with DPE. The DISQUAC interaction parameters suggest that interactions related to the OH/O contacts are essentially dispersive. UNIFAC fails when representing thermodynamic properties of the studied solutions.

title: Controlled Oxidation of Tellurium Nanoparticles for Telecom Detection
text:
Title: Controlled Oxidation of Tellurium Nanoparticles for Telecom Detection
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Surface oxidation plays an important role in governing charge transport in semiconductor nanoparticle assemblies. Here, we investigate the optoelectronic properties of solution-processed tellurium (Te) nanoparticle ensembles prepared through gradual ambient-air exposure. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal interconnected elemental Te nanoparticles with coexisting alpha-TeO2 and hydroxyl-containing surface species, exhibiting a lower relative contribution of oxidized Te than previously investigated forced-air-oxidized ensembles. The resulting photodetectors demonstrate photoresponse at 405, 532, and 1550 nm, with maximum responsivities of 10.1, 14.4, and 8.5 mA/W, respectively. At 1550 nm, the device exhibits rise and fall times of 17.7 and 40.2 s, respectively, and an estimated shot-noise-limited specific detectivity of 1.3 * 10^6 Jones. These findings highlight the importance of controlling surface oxidation to balance interparticle charge transport and dark-current suppression, offering insights for the development of solution-processed Te-based photodetectors for short-wave infrared applications.

title: Deep Bayesian Filtering for Nonlinear Structural System Identification: A Tutorial on Structural and Physical Inductive Biases
text:
Title: Deep Bayesian Filtering for Nonlinear Structural System Identification: A Tutorial on Structural and Physical Inductive Biases
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Nonlinear structural system identification remains challenging when governing physics is only partially known and measurements are sparse. Deep Bayesian filtering addresses these challenges by combining learnable dynamical representations with probabilistic state-space models, physical inductive biases, and uncertainty-aware inference. This paper presents, for the first time, a unified tutorial treatment of deep Bayesian filtering for nonlinear structural system identification, connecting model formulation, learning, posterior inference, and evaluation. Amortized variational inference and differentiable Kalman filtering are introduced as complementary strategies within this broader framework. The Deep Markov Model (DMM) provides a data-driven reference, while the Physics-guided Deep Markov Model (PgDMM) and Neural Extended Kalman Filter (Neural EKF) serve as illustrative instances through which methodological choices and their implications are examined. Dynamic state estimation and joint state and parameter estimation are demonstrated on a three-dimensional shear-frame benchmark with hysteretic Bouc-Wen connections and sparse acceleration measurements. The comparative analysis yields new observations concerning the relationships among reconstruction accuracy, predictive fidelity, physical interpretability, and estimation robustness. Physical structure improves latent-state interpretability without necessarily ensuring faithful predictive dynamics, while comparable typical reconstruction accuracy can conceal substantial differences in estimation robustness. These findings motivate practical guidelines for model construction, training, and evaluation that distinguish reconstruction, forecasting, state recovery, and parameter identification. The tutorial concludes by outlining challenges in uncertainty calibration, identifiability, and validation on real structures.

title: Overcoming Fundamental Control Limitations in Powered Descent Flight through Robust Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion
text:
Title: Overcoming Fundamental Control Limitations in Powered Descent Flight through Robust Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This work identifies a fundamental, controller-independent limitation in reusable launch vehicle powered descent: a sudden $180^\circ$ phase transition in the open-loop transfer functions from the control inputs to the lateral drift and drift rate. The transition occurs inside the flight envelope, reverses the effective control direction, and can destabilize the closed loop system under uncertainty. An analytical condition governing this transition is derived, its physical mechanism is established, and its dependence on vehicle mass, aerodynamic properties, and geometry is characterized. An Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion (INDI)-based control architecture is then developed to inherently address this limitation and is tuned via $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ Closed Loop Shaping to provide local robustness and performance guarantees. The internal dynamics introduced by the INDI inversion are analytically derived and proven to be stable throughout the flight envelope. The proposed controller is compared against a robust gain-scheduled baseline controller through linear stability analysis and an extensive nonlinear Monte Carlo campaign. Both controllers achieve 100% success across the considered Monte Carlo campaign, though the INDI-based controller provides improved tracking performance, superior nominal and dispersed stability margins, requires fewer controller design points, and reduces controller tuning complexity.

title: BharatSynthQA: A Context-Grounded Question Answering Dataset on Indian Temples and Religious Heritage
text:
Title: BharatSynthQA: A Context-Grounded Question Answering Dataset on Indian Temples and Religious Heritage
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

India's temples and other places of worship are among its richest repositories of cultural heritage, bringing together religious tradition, history, architecture, and art. Due to the widespread curiosity, people increasingly turn to Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistants for information about them. Current models are rarely trained or evaluated on this domain. We present BharatSynthQA, a passage grounded question answering (QA) dataset focused on Indian temples, which also covers other religious sites connected to them. Our pipeline crawls Wikipedia from topics seeded by authentic heritage sources, filters articles for topical relevance, and locations in India. Further it generates Boolean, factoid, and explanatory QA pairs with a fewshot prompted LLM. An LLM judge filters the pairs on answer correctness, retaining 98,677 of 131,494 generated pairs. Additionally, 300 human-annotated pairs are released separately as a reference set. Human evaluation of the subsample of this dataset showed 89.83% of the questions were formed correctly. Benchmarking five current LLMs shows that factoid token F1 is only 0.18-0.30 without the source passage but 0.73-0.77 with it, indicating that this domain is poorly captured in model knowledge. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/theshivam7/bharatsynth-qa to support research on culturally grounded QA and retrieval-augmented generation for Indian heritage.

title: Coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes I: (3,2)-Kinematical Lie algebras with $d\geq 3$
text:
Title: Coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes I: (3,2)-Kinematical Lie algebras with $d\geq 3$
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

This is the first of several papers devoted to the classification of coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes. It is the first step in extending the classification of spatially isotropic homogeneous spacetimes of kinematical Lie groups to the much vaster context of homogeneous spacetimes that are not spatially isotropic; that is, where the rotations no longer act transitively on the space of directions in each tangent space. In this first paper we classify (up to isomorphisms preserving the rotational subalgebra) a class of the relevant transitive Lie algebras, the so-called (3,2)-kinematical Lie algebras, for the coisotropy-one case in spatial dimension at least 4. As a by-product of this classification, we classify two-dimensional real representations of Bianchi Lie algebras up to a suitable notion of equivalence.

title: Attainable and unattainable quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light--matter coupling
text:
Title: Attainable and unattainable quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light--matter coupling
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

In this paper, we study the gauge dependence of quantum precision in ultrastrongly coupled light--matter systems. The unitary between gauges carries the coupling $g$, so each truncation defines a different family. The quantum Fisher information traces an exact parabola across frames. Harmonic matter minimizes it at a universal $θ_\ast=Ω/(Ω+ω)$, set by the matter and cavity frequencies. Only the minimal-coupling bound is attainable. Frames differ by a factor $9.6$ with opposite trends. Diverging virtual-excitation gain at the Dicke point is a gauge artifact and saturates.

title: A general sharp-interface simulation framework for microstructure evolution
text:
Title: A general sharp-interface simulation framework for microstructure evolution
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Simulating microstructure evolution requires tracking many moving grain and phase boundaries coupled to thermodynamic and mechanical fields. We present Gaussian-projected kinetics (GPK), a sharp-interface framework in which every cell stores an integer grain or phase label. Near a boundary, a temporary Gaussian projection of the label map provides the interface normal and curvature and is then discarded. Capillarity, chemistry, stored energy, transport and elasticity move the boundaries through one topology-preserving update. Because the Gaussian measurement length is fixed in physical units, mesh refinement keeps a consistent capillary scale without a diffuse interface. GPK models grain growth, recrystallisation, multiphase evolution and elastic-coupled solidification in two and three dimensions. It is verified on analytical benchmarks and compared grain by grain with phase-field simulations, running 8.5 to 96 times faster at matched accuracy in our tests. An Al-Cu application with CALPHAD thermodynamic data connects it to measured recrystallisation and precipitation data.

title: FLAKE: Friction and Lattice Analysis of Kinetics and Energetics of rigid 2D clusters on crystalline substrates
text:
Title: FLAKE: Friction and Lattice Analysis of Kinetics and Energetics of rigid 2D clusters on crystalline substrates
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

When a small solid island slides across a crystalline surface, the outcome (smooth flow or stick-slip, free rotation or angular locking) is controlled almost entirely by the geometric relationship between the island and the surface: their relative orientation, size and lattice symmetry. These phenomena are central to nanoscale friction, to the interpretation of colloidal monolayer experiments and to structural superlubricity. FLAKE (Friction and Lattice Analysis of Kinetics and Energetics) is a Python package for simulating the statics and Langevin dynamics of a rigid 2D cluster sliding over a periodic or quasiperiodic substrate potential. It enables fast, systematic exploration of how geometry and substrate symmetry control the energy landscape and friction, studies that are prohibitively expensive with fully atomistic simulations. FLAKE has been the primary simulation tool for three published studies on structural superlubricity and colloidal friction.

title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
text:
Title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.

title: Row-sparse ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses with a few extra rows: local search with approximation guarantees
text:
Title: Row-sparse ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses with a few extra rows: local search with approximation guarantees
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

For a rank-$r$ matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses $H$ with few nonzero rows give least-squares solutions that are fast to evaluate and use few variables. A known determinant-based local search finds one with exactly $r$ nonzero rows and 2,1-norm within an essentially tight factor $r$ of the minimum at an exact local optimum. We let the nonzero rows of $H$ lie in a set $K$ of $k\ge r$ indices and study how to choose $K$. We bound the loss of this restriction (restricted over unrestricted minimum 2,1-norm) by a simple geometric certificate and establish that a local search maximizing the squared rank-$r$ volume of the corresponding columns of $A$ gives loss at most $\sqrt{k(r+εk)/(k-r+1)}$, where $1+ε$ is the swap tolerance. With $ε=0$ this is $r$ at $k=r$ and less than $\sqrt{2r}$ for $k\ge2r$; with $ε=1/k$ the search runs in polynomial time on rational data. The same support yields an ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverse with spectral norm within a factor $\sqrt{1+(n-k)(r+εk)/(k-r+1)}$ of that of the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. The loss guarantees hold for every norm on the rows. In general, our certificate bound is tight up to a factor depending only on $k/r$, and on some instances, for a suitable row norm, so is the loss bound; for the 2,1-norm, however, the certificate can overestimate the loss by a factor $\sqrt r$. The local search is the Fedorov exchange algorithm of 0/1 D-optimal design; this yields a fast implementation and, via the Kiefer-Wolfowitz theorem, supports of at most $r(r+1)/2+1$ rows with certificate at most $\sqrt r$, best possible in general. On instances from earlier work, the observed loss is far below the guarantee, and the method matches two ADMM heuristics when few rows are removed and otherwise gives 2,1-norms up to 27% smaller, one to two orders of magnitude faster.

title: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization
text:
Title: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization is a fundamental tool in portfolio selection, yet its nonsmooth loss structure poses a challenge for the existing theory of stochastic gradient methods including associated Langevin algorithms. In particular, the positive-part loss and the softmax portfolio parametrization lead to stochastic gradients that need not be globally Lipschitz continuous, but rather discontinuous, where available non-convex stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) guarantees often exhibit an unfavorable exponential dependence on the problem dimension. In this article, we develop a non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD for a regularized CVaR portfolio optimization problem. We exploit the geometric structure of the CVaR objective to establish linear growth, convexity-at-infinity, and one-sided Lipschitz properties of the stochastic gradient without imposing density assumptions on the asset losses that are typical in previous works. Crucially, the constants appearing in the aforementioned structural conditions are shown to be independent of the number of assets. Moreover, we establish a convergence bound in Wasserstein-2 distance with rate $\mathcal{O}(λ^{1/4})$ and a finite-time guarantee for the expected excess risk. Our analysis, together with the dimension-independent constants in the structural conditions, leads to an excess risk bound that depends linearly on the number of assets. Numerical experiments with simulated Gaussian portfolios exhibit the predicted dimension dependence. Computational comparisons with alternative stochastic optimization methods further illustrate the practical efficiency of SGLD for the optimization problem under consideration. Finally, we extend the framework to a broader class of non-convex stochastic optimization problems with discontinuous stochastic gradients.

title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
text:
Title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model. Our results establish duality defects and generalized symmetries as practical resources for preparing and probing non-local excitations on quantum hardware.

title: Learning Mechanistic Reasoning for Chemical Reactions with Large Language Models
text:
Title: Learning Mechanistic Reasoning for Chemical Reactions with Large Language Models
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Reaction mechanisms consist of the step-by-step sequences of elementary reactions that explain chemical transformations. Learning the mechanism logic is therefore essential for enhancing the fundamental chemical intelligence of large language models (LLMs). The stepwise deduction of reaction mechanism aligns naturally with the reasoning paradigms of reasoning LLMs. However, current chemical LLMs primarily emphasize coarse-grained name reactions for product prediction and retrosynthesis, often leading to physical inconsistencies and hallucinations. In contrast, specialized small-scale generative models for mechanism inference typically suffer from restricted generalization capacity across diverse chemical spaces. To overcome these limitations, we built a novel, large-scale reasoning dataset of reaction mechanisms. Furthermore, we established the FukuyamaBench, a difficult benchmark derived from Fukuyama's Advanced Organic Reaction Mechanism book, to rigorously evaluate model performance on hierarchical mechanism reasoning. Our fine-tuned Qwen3-30B-A3B achieves 8.3% exact pathway match on FukuyamaBench Set~A, surpassing the specialized FlowER model (5.1%), demonstrating that mechanism-aware training substantially enhances chemical reasoning in language models.

title: CA-DEL: An Open Multi-Target, Multi-Modal Benchmark for Learning from DNA-Encoded Library Screens
text:
Title: CA-DEL: An Open Multi-Target, Multi-Modal Benchmark for Learning from DNA-Encoded Library Screens
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The success of machine learning in drug discovery hinges on learning the relationship between a chemical structure and its biological activity. While DNA-Encoded Library (DEL) technology can generate the massive datasets required for this task, its primary signal -- sequencing read counts -- is an indirect and often noisy proxy for true molecular binding affinity. To address the scarcity of public benchmarks for developing robust models that can overcome this data challenge, we introduce CA-DEL, a multi-dimensional public benchmark featuring screens against three homologous carbonic anhydrase isoforms. While recent benchmarks like KinDEL have introduced 3D poses for kinase targets, CA-DEL distinguishes itself by focusing on the selectivity challenge among homologous Carbonic Anhydrase isoforms (CAII, CAIX, CAXII). Unlike benchmarks relying solely on noisy enrichment scores, CA-DEL integrates a rigorous validation set of experimentally determined binding affinities ($K_i$) from ChEMBL, establishing a critical Sim-to-Real evaluation paradigm: training on noisy DEL screens and testing on high-fidelity biophysical data.

title: Atomic Static Electric Quadrupole Polarizability from Relativistic Many-Body Theory With Application To Thulium $\left(6s^2\, 4f^{13}\right)$\, $^2F_{7/2}$ and $^2F_{5/2}$
text:
Title: Atomic Static Electric Quadrupole Polarizability from Relativistic Many-Body Theory With Application To Thulium $\left(6s^2\, 4f^{13}\right)$\, $^2F_{7/2}$ and $^2F_{5/2}$
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

In the present work a method for calculating atomic static electric rank-$n$ tensor quadrupole polarizabilities $α_Q^{(n)}(J)$ for arbitrary atomic electronic structure is presented. It is based on a linear-symmetry representation of atomic states using large-scale relativistic configuration interaction wavefunctions, and the quadrupole polarizabilities are obtained by a sum-over-states approach. The major result from applying this method to atomic thulium is $α_Q^{(0)}(\frac{7}{2}) = 2496^{+0}_{-231}$ \au for the electronic ground term $^2F_{7/2}$ static electric scalar quadrupole polarizability which is roughly a factor of four smaller than same property in the electronic ground state of the cesium atom. This finding adds to the favorable properties of thulium atoms in atomic-clock research.

title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
text:
Title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated specimens. On simulated data, $e_{15}$ can instead be recovered non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations using a constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN). By building exact spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers directly into the network output, the clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial state hold automatically, leaving the loss with only the interior equations of coupled electro-elastodynamics and the data misfit. Non-dimensional scaling brings all governing coefficients within one decade of O(1), and the setup removes the boundary and initial-condition penalty weights that soft-constraint methods must tune. In a six-way comparison (plane-strain PZT-5H, manufactured wavefield, 30 dB noise), a soft-penalty baseline with adaptive weights converges to an erroneous $e_{15}$ in four of the five runs (51.7% mean error), and fixed penalties reach an error of 0.85% only after a second-order optimization stage. The constrained formulations reach mean $e_{15}$ errors between 0.15% and 0.51% with held-out displacement errors below 1%. Within these variants, the spatial multiplier gives rapid first-order convergence, and the quadratic temporal multiplier lowers the early-time electrostatic residual by a factor of 6.8 versus a linear one. On finite-element data along one subsurface line, the full formulation recovers $e_{15}$ with 1.19% mean error at 30 dB and keeps it between 0.65% and 2.71% across a 40 to 0 dB noise sweep. Finally, training on displacements alone still recovers $e_{15}$ with mean errors of 0.45% on finite-element and 1.64% on manufactured data.

title: Intermolecular and Interfacial Origins of Layering in a Near-Isotropic Organic Glass Former
text:
Title: Intermolecular and Interfacial Origins of Layering in a Near-Isotropic Organic Glass Former
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Physical vapor deposition can produce organic glasses with enhanced stability and pronounced structural anisotropy (layering) even when the constituent molecules are nearly spherical. However, the microscopic origin of the layering in spherical molecular glass formers remains unclear. We investigated vapor-deposited films of 9-(3,5-di(naphthalen-1-yl)phenyl)anthracene (α,α-A) by grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering, atomistic molecular dynamics, and coarse-grained simulations. Experimentally, the layering signal varies nonmonotonically with deposition temperature and is strongest near 0.8T_g. Simulated scattering calculations reproduce the principal experimental features and show that the layering peak does not originate from shifts in single molecule degrees of freedom. In fact, the simulated deposited and bulk glasses show largely the same single-molecule conformations. Interestingly, a one-site coarse-grained liquid with isotropic interactions develops a comparable interfacial layering signature. These results indicate that layering in α,α-A arises primarily from collective density correlations generated at the free surface during deposition rather than from conformational bias or orientational ordering. The findings connect structural anisotropy in vapor-deposited molecular glasses to the generic interfacial organization of simple liquids.

title: Field-induced phase-matching in Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers
text:
Title: Field-induced phase-matching in Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Superconducting Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) enable broadband, quantum-limited amplification of weak microwave signals. JTWPAs are essential for the single-shot readout of superconducting qubits, broadband vacuum squeezing, or the generation of microwave cluster states. Phase-matching between signal and pump modes in such JTWPAs represents a major engineering challenge, which is typically solved by integrating resonators in a nonlinear medium in order to tailor electromagnetic dispersion relations and achieve a broadband, high-gain amplification. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a phase-matching approach using a homogeneous nonlinear medium based on Josephson elements by exploiting a magnetic field inhomogeneity. We show how the latter may lead to the sign reversal of the 3-wave mixing nonlinearity and stabilization of the parametric amplification. We envision this technique as a viable alternative to conventional phase-matching approaches.

title: Phylogeny.fr: the phylogenetic platform designed for non-specialists
text:
Title: Phylogeny.fr: the phylogenetic platform designed for non-specialists
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Phylogenetic analysis has become a standard approach across many areas of biology, yet the growing complexity of phylogenetic methods and software remains a major obstacle for non-specialists. Since its launch in 2008, Phylogeny.fr has provided an accessible web platform for building phylogenetic trees using widely accepted methods without requiring local software installation. Here, we present a major redesign and modernization of the service. The new version integrates state-of-the-art tools while preserving historical programs for legacy support and relies on modern web architecture and HPC infrastructure. New interactive React-based viewers, ReSeqt and Reactree, provide intuitive exploration and publication-ready visualization of alignments and trees. The Blast-Explorer companion tool has also been updated and now includes clustering options. By combining ease of use, methodological flexibility, and modern phylogenetic tools, the new Phylogeny.fr addresses the needs of researchers, teachers, and students seeking accessible and reliable phylogenetic analyses.

title: An S-matrix Formalism for the Nonclassical Optical Response of Plasmonic Nanowires
text:
Title: An S-matrix Formalism for the Nonclassical Optical Response of Plasmonic Nanowires
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

This paper reports a computational scheme which predicts the light-matter interaction in multiple mesoscopic plasmonic nanowires (NWs), each of which includes concentric or eccentric constituent wires. Lying at the core of the proposed scheme is the S-Matrix of each individual cylindrical interface. The optical response of the materials inside and outside each interface can be described by three popular mesoscopic models: the Hydrodynamic Drude model (HDM) and its diffusive variant, namely the Generalized Nonlocal Optical Response (GNOR) model, as well as the Surface Response Model (SRM). To take into account the relative displacements between the cylindrical interfaces, the addition theorem is applied to construct the main equation behind the algorithm, where the possibility of longitudinal waves intrinsic in the HDM and GNOR models is also included. The optical responses calculated by the proposed S Matrix Method are compared with an in-house developed boundary element method (BEM) toolbox for a single gold NW and an eccentric dual-material NW, and excellent agreements are seen. The algorithm is further physically checked for a sodium nanolens trimer featuring large field focusing, and the effects of the HDM and the SRM are compared.

title: Quantum Simulation of Quantum Channels and Applications
text:
Title: Quantum Simulation of Quantum Channels and Applications
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We review the basic theory of quantum channels and develop a strategy for simulating them on digital quantum computers, drawing upon the Choi-Kraus operator-sum representation and Stinespring dilation to provide a unified approach for various applications. We discuss three types of applications, offering explicit examples for each: the preparation of mixed states, measurements described by positive operator-valued measures (POVMs), and the simulation of the evolution of Markovian quantum systems. We recover fundamental concepts from quantum theory, such as the purification of a mixed state and the Naimark dilation associated with a POVM. Regarding the simulation of the evolution of a Markovian quantum system, we introduce an operator, termed the residual operator, to construct, from the system's Liouvillian, a quantum channel that serves as a first-order approximation of the quantum dynamical semigroup. This allows the simulation of quantum dynamics to be performed in a manner analogous to the Euler method for ordinary differential equations, avoiding Trotterization. We prove all the theoretical results mentioned, with the exception of the fundamental Choi-Kraus theorem concerning the operator-sum representation of quantum channels, for which we provide the appropriate references. The explicit simulations discussed were implemented using the AerSimulator from IBM's Qiskit SDK, with the corresponding code available on GitHub.

title: $\texttt{DisMorph}$: learning to disentangle technical distortions from true biological change
text:
Title: $\texttt{DisMorph}$: learning to disentangle technical distortions from true biological change
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Longitudinal MRI enables sensitive measurement of structural brain change for studying aging and neurodegenerative disease. Deformable image registration is a key tool for estimating such change by computing a dense deformation that captures geometric differences between longitudinal scans. However, MRI scanners introduce geometric distortions that vary across acquisition systems and protocols, such as gradient non-linearity (GNL) distortion. Existing registration methods estimate a single field that conflates biological and technical effects, potentially biasing downstream morphometric measurements if distortions remain (partially) uncorrected. We propose $\texttt{DisMorph}$, a registration framework trained entirely on synthetic data that explicitly decomposes longitudinal deformation into technical and anatomical transforms. It predicts two dense deformations, each encoding one effect. During training, a novel generative model synthesizes both effects separately to provide disentanglement supervision, while domain randomization promotes generalization across imaging protocols. We evaluate our method in three complementary settings. On simulated data with known ground truth, our method detects anatomical change more accurately and consistently than conventional registration. On real image pairs that differ only by GNL distortion, our method assigns most geometric change to the distortion field, demonstrating specificity in the absence of anatomical change. On longitudinal Alzheimer's disease (AD) pairs, our method detects anatomical change in AD-related brain structures while identifying residual distortion left after standard correction. By disentangling MRI-induced distortion from biological change in the longitudinal deformation, our method paves the way for more accurate longitudinal morphometry in clinical settings where maintaining acquisition consistency is challenging.

title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
text:
Title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $φ$ couples via the effective operator $φ\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. Embedding $φ$ as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory requires an anomaly coefficient $\gtrsim100$, implying a Landau pole for QCD. These tensions are relaxed for more strongly coupled dark gauge sectors.

title: Immobilisation and remobilisation of surfactant-covered drop interfaces in electric fields: Simulations
text:
Title: Immobilisation and remobilisation of surfactant-covered drop interfaces in electric fields: Simulations
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Fluid--fluid interfaces are seldom clean due to the presence of surfactants, which can strongly modify their dynamics. Interfacial flow redistributes surfactant, creating concentration gradients whose Marangoni stresses can immobilise the interface. By contrast, surface diffusion or exchange with the bulk can reduce these gradients and restore interfacial motion. We study this competition using a two-dimensional model of a surfactant-covered leaky-dielectric drop in a uniform electric field. Electric stresses drive the classical Taylor circulation, in which the drop remains non-rotating. At stronger fields, convection of interfacial charge can destabilise this state and produce the Quincke regime, characterised by spontaneous mean rotation. Using a fully nonlinear model on a fixed circular interface, we show that weak surfactant diffusion allows Marangoni stresses to suppress the Taylor circulation almost completely. Quincke rotation remobilises this nearly arrested interface and restores a substantial straining circulation, whose orientation varies with the applied field. Surfactant also shifts the critical field for rotation and can change the onset from subcritical to supercritical. Surface diffusion and exchange with a well-mixed bulk reservoir can produce similar flow responses and rotation thresholds despite different surfactant distributions. The spatial variation of surfactant concentration therefore provides additional information for distinguishing the two transport mechanisms.

title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
text:
Title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We investigate the following: do existence bounds obtained by interlacing methods describe the spectra of typical random graphs? Depending on the model, we provide both positive and negative answers. We establish a Friedman-type theorem for zig-zag products of random regular graphs $G$ with a fixed vertex-transitive gadget $H$, where $G$ is sampled from independent permutations or matchings. We prove that the new spectrum converges in Hausdorff distance to that of the zig-zag product of the infinite regular tree with $H$. In particular, the new spectral radius converges to the sharp threshold established by Cohen, Cohen, and Maor. We establish the spectral limit using strong convergence and, drawing on quantitative estimates of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, and van Handel, obtain an $O(1/n)$ upper-tail bound in the permutation model. For the irregular configuration model, we show that the interlacing bound of Cohen and Maor, asymptotically $2\sqrt{μ-1}/μ$ for limiting average degree $μ$, is atypical: for uniformly bounded degree sequences with a nonconstant limiting degree law of minimum $δ\ge 2$, a random graph exceeds the interlacing bound by a positive constant with high probability. This gap is explained by the limiting spectral distribution, whose support edge is $2\sqrt{δ-1}/δ$. Strikingly, unlike the familiar behavior of random regular graphs, our experiments reveal second eigenvalues that remain far below this limiting edge even for the largest graphs tested. For $δ\ge3$, we propose that the scarcity of minimum-degree trees explains this behavior; estimates for their size suggest spectral witnesses within $O\left((\log\log n)^{-2}\right)$ of the limiting edge, which is consistent with our numerical observations.

title: From Shape to Species: The Use of Persistent Homology in Restructuring the Taxonomy of \textit{Acropora} corals
text:
Title: From Shape to Species: The Use of Persistent Homology in Restructuring the Taxonomy of \textit{Acropora} corals
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Traditional coral taxonomy is increasingly challenged by recent advances in molecular evidence. Quantitative methods previously used to identify morphological descriptors have not been successful at detecting significant differences at the macroscale. It is of great interest to optimise methods for effectively delimiting species within the complex genus \textit{Acropora} to ensure sustainable, long-term management of these vital ecosystems. Topological Data Analysis (TDA) is designed to study the shape of data and can detect features that familiar methods overlook. This novel approach makes TDA and persistent homology a logical choice for studying coral morphology in a taxonomic context. The results show that valid topological information can be extracted from in-situ coral images and that there is great potential in further refining this method. This study is a first exploration into the potential of persistent homology in supporting the delimitation of the reef-building scleractinian corals \textit{Acropora}.

title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 4: variance under a general distribution
text:
Title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 4: variance under a general distribution
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study the variance of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf p}=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|X_{j+1}-X_j-N(p_{j+1}-p_j)|$ of $X\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ for fixed $n\ge3$ and fixed $\mathbf p$ with all $p_i>0$, as $N\to\infty$. We prove $\mathrm{Var}(d_{\mathbf p})=N\,v(\mathbf p)+O(1)$, where $v(\mathbf p)$, the variance of the sum of absolute values of the limiting Gaussian edge vector, is expressed through the exact multinomial edge variances and correlations and Nabeya's covariance formula for folded bivariate normal variables. Unlike in the uniform case, non-adjacent edge pairs generally contribute to $v(\mathbf p)$. The $O(1)$ remainder is controlled by a lattice Edgeworth expansion and Poisson summation; it oscillates with the lattice phases $\{N(p_{j+1}-p_j)\}$, and for $n=3,4$, where a pair of edges exhausts the bins, the summation runs over a sublattice coset. The formula reduces to the known uniform result (the classical Hoel--Kamat variance), gives a closed form when the reference law is a symmetric comb, and has a shape-independent large-bin limit for positive $C^1$ profiles. For the statistic $d_{\mathbf r}$ centered at a reference law $\mathbf r\ne\mathbf p$ the absolute values linearize: when every edge is mismatched the variance is that of a linear form in the counts up to an exponentially small error, and in mixed (triangular-array) regimes it is given to $o(N)$ by bivariate folded-normal covariances. The two-bin formulas are recorded from the companion preprints, and exact finite-$N$ reductions for $n\le4$ are used for validation.

title: Gendered Misclassification from Surname-Based Race Imputation
text:
Title: Gendered Misclassification from Surname-Based Race Imputation
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Researchers increasingly estimate political behavior based on race and gender from voter files, where race is imputed from surnames and geography. This only works where surnames suggest group membership, an assumption violated where surnames follow norms around marriage. Imputation is therefore biased against women who adopt their husband's surname, especially those who racially inter-marry, an outcome itself endogenous to partisanship. Using six US states recording self-reported race, I show that imputation is less accurate for Asian and Hispanic women, particularly those sharing the surname of a partner of another race, who differ politically from other women of their race. This violates assumptions behind downstream inference approaches, which nearly double the gender gap in partisanship among Asian voters. I derive an expression showing the bias is largest where a group is small. Using maiden rather than marriage-adopted surnames in North Carolina raises accuracy up to fourfold for women married across racial lines. Recovering maiden surnames, or omitting the married surname, removes much of the bias. In a national replication of a study of gender gaps in turnout, the correction more than triples the gap among Asian voters. In Lebanon, where wives register in their husband's locality, the error enters through geography.

title: Reachability Constraints and Monotones for Quantum-State Texture
text:
Title: Reachability Constraints and Monotones for Quantum-State Texture
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

How a quantum resource can be quantified depends on which operations are free. Yet two proposed quantifiers of quantum state texture can increase under free operations: the Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information relative to the unique textureless state and the squared Hilbert-Schmidt distance from that state. We show reachability from every state orthogonal to the textureless state, whether pure or mixed: each can be freely transformed into any other state. Therefore, every texture monotone must assign the same maximal value to all such states, a requirement that neither candidate satisfies. We then construct valid texture monotones by adding the population outside the textureless state to the skew information and by maximizing the squared Hilbert-Schmidt distance over free operations. We prove faithfulness, convexity, and invariance under textureless ancillas, characterize additivity properties and strong monotonicity, satisfied only in the Wigner-Yanase case, and derive tight bounds for both monotones at fixed overlap with the textureless state and characterize all saturating states. Together, these results show how allowed state transformations impose operational constraints on the quantification of quantum state texture.

title: Co--dsorption of terrylene and tetrapentacontane on hexagonal boron nitride - towards a two-dimensional Shpolskii matrix
text:
Title: Co--dsorption of terrylene and tetrapentacontane on hexagonal boron nitride - towards a two-dimensional Shpolskii matrix
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Organic molecular emitters are promising building blocks for quantum technologies, but their use at two-dimensional interfaces is limited by diffusion, aggregation, and photobleaching. We present work towards constructing an ultrathin two-dimensional Shpolskii-like host-guest matrix on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) by co-depositing terrylene fluorophores with the long-chain tetrapentacontane in a solution-phase process. We demonstrate that this approach disperses terrylene in a roughly one-nanometer-thin alkane layer without detectable phase separation and allows tuning the emitter density from ensembles to isolated emitters showing characteristic blinking behavior consistent with single-molecule fluorescence. Time-lapse confocal microscopy, autocorrelation analysis, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching show that suppressed diffusion and stable emitter positions can be achieved in several samples with a tetrapentacontane matrix. Encapsulation with hBN from the top side further improves photostability, with emitters demonstrating long lifetimes despite high photon doses. Successful co-adsorption of isolated emitters and alkane matrix is a milestone towards extending Shpolskii-type molecular isolation to hBN and provides a route towards stable, interface-integrated molecular qubits.

title: Spatially Informed and Direction Sensitive Representation Learning for Spatial Transcriptomics
text:
Title: Spatially Informed and Direction Sensitive Representation Learning for Spatial Transcriptomics
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Cellular states are shaped by both intrinsic gene expression programs and the spatial microenvironment in which cells reside. Spatial transcriptomics makes this context measurable, but effective representation learning requires capturing both spatially informative molecular signals and intercellular organization. Existing approaches address these challenges only partially: conventional gene selection can overlook spatially structured signals, while methods for encoding cell-cell relationships often either reduce a cell's microenvironment to proximity alone, discarding direction, or rely on absolute coordinates tied to an arbitrary tissue frame. Consequently, cells with similar neighbor distances but distinct spatial organization may receive overly similar representations, despite experiencing different biological contexts that shape their cellular states. We introduce Tessera, a spatial representation learning framework that addresses both molecular selection and cellular context. Tessera combines spatially informed gene selection with a geometric inductive bias that contextualizes each cell within its local tissue environment. By modeling relative cell-cell relationships, Tessera is translation-invariant while preserving direction, allowing neighboring cells to contribute differently according to their spatial context and cellular state. Across held-out tissues and technologies, Tessera outperforms existing spatial foundation models in representation quality and generalizes zero-shot to contexts up to $16\times$ larger than those seen during training.

title: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data
text:
Title: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Equation learning seeks to discover compact, interpretable equations from data using various machine-learning techniques. However, few workflows discover and interpret learned equations in sparse, high-dimensional materials datasets. We present nn-EQL, an equation-learning framework that generates candidate equations through iterative training, pruning, and retraining of a neural network with customizable, user-specified neuron-level activation functions. Candidate equations are ranked using a minimum description length (MDL)-inspired score, balancing error and sparsity, and diagnosed to assess term-wise contributions, input-scaled sensitivities, and uncertainties. We demonstrate nn-EQL on standard AI-Feynman benchmarks as well as multiscale high-dimensional materials datasets such as finite-element simulations of heterogeneous materials, and high-throughput experimental thin-film deposition data. nn-EQL integrates with tabular data and high-dimensional data via standard encoder models, learning equations and providing insight into learned terms. Looking forward, integrating physically interpretable representations, multimodal and multi-fidelity data, and adaptive data acquisition could enable equation learning to formulate and test mechanistic hypotheses.

title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
text:
Title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Grain growth during heat treatment strongly affects the microstructure of polycrystalline materials and, consequently, their mechanical properties. Although numerical methods such as front-tracking or front-capturing simulations can accurately describe grain growth, their high computational cost limits their use for long or non-isothermal thermal cycles. In previous work, grain growth was successfully predicted under isothermal conditions by treating grain size distributions as time series and forecasting their evolution using recurrent neural networks, allowing complete grain growth trajectories to be generated in seconds rather than through costly PDE-based simulations. In the present work, this forecasting framework is reformulated to handle non-isothermal conditions by explicitly incorporating thermal information into the model architecture. Grain size distributions are encoded using a convolutional neural network, thermal descriptors are embedded through a dedicated multilayer perceptron, and temporal evolution is predicted using a recurrent network. Instantaneous temperature and thermal rate are provided at each time step, allowing the model to adapt its predictions to changing thermal conditions. The framework is trained and evaluated on datasets generated from validated front-tracking simulations across a wide range of non-isothermal thermal paths. The results show that the thermally conditioned model accurately reproduces grain growth dynamics under complex thermal histories, achieving, in k-fold cross-validation over all simulations, mean relative errors of 2.99% (one-hour cycles) and 4.51% (four-hour cycles) with coefficients of determination exceeding 0.99, and mean relative errors between 1.91% and 14.66% on ten simulations following four unseen thermal histories of increasing complexity.

title: SeedFold: Scaling Biomolecular Structure Prediction
text:
Title: SeedFold: Scaling Biomolecular Structure Prediction
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Highly accurate biomolecular structure prediction is a key component of developing biomolecular foundation models, and one of the most critical aspects of building foundation models is identifying the recipes for scaling the model. In this work, we present SeedFold, a folding model that successfully scales up the model capacity. Our contributions are threefold: first, we identify an effective width-scaling strategy for the Pairformer to increase representation capacity; second, we introduce a novel linear triangular attention that reduces computational complexity to enable efficient scaling; finally, we construct a large-scale distillation dataset to substantially enlarge the training set. Experiments on FoldBench show that SeedFold outperforms AlphaFold3 on most protein-related tasks.

title: TransMem: Transition-Aware Retrieval for Evolving Personal Memory
text:
Title: TransMem: Transition-Aware Retrieval for Evolving Personal Memory
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Long-term personalized agents are increasingly expected to answer queries over user histories in which preferences, goals, and constraints evolve across interleaved conversations. Existing retrieval-based and structured-memory systems can surface relevant facts, but often return isolated memory units that do not explain which earlier preference was refined, contradicted, or superseded by later evidence. We introduce TransMem, a transition-aware memory retrieval framework that stores preference updates as explicit retrieval units alongside ordinary factual memories. During memory construction, TransMem routes user interaction history into topic-structured memory graphs, detects shift events, and grounds them as transition records. At inference time, TransMem first retrieves factual anchors and then adaptively expands over transition records, producing a compact context of factual anchors and accepted transition records. Experiments on PersonaMem and PersonaBench across two Qwen backbones show that TransMem outperforms representative retrieval-based and structured-memory baselines. Controlled analyses further show that transition records and adaptive expansion contribute beyond factual anchoring, chronological expansion, flat transition retrieval, and fixed-hop traversal. These results suggest that preference-update records are useful retrieval units for long-term personalization.

title: LinMix: Data Mixing as Linear Domain Attribution
text:
Title: LinMix: Data Mixing as Linear Domain Attribution
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Language model performance depends strongly on the mixture of domains in the pretraining data corpus. Popular data mixing methods select these domain weights by training many small proxy models on random mixes and then fitting a regression model to predict performance from the mix. We recognize this practice as a domain attribution problem, where the regression measures each domain's contribution to the target metric. Through this lens, the standard Dirichlet sampling of proxy data mixes is a poor regression design that requires tuning and cannot support a linear fit for hundreds of domains. Building on classical optimal experimental design, we introduce LinMix, which samples mixes at the vertices of the capped simplex so that each domain is at its cap or absent. This hyperparameter-free vertex sampling decorrelates domain effects, enabling an interpretable linear model whose coefficients are the domain attributions. The optimal mix given by LinMix provably keeps only domains with positive attribution values and requires no search over candidate mixes. We further establish the optimality of vertex sampling, and prove that Dirichlet sampling inflates the attribution error when its mixes concentrate around the prior data mix. Pretraining experiments with 1B-parameter OLMo2 and 4B Qwen3.5 language models show that LinMix outperforms Dirichlet-based data mixing across reasoning, code, and math benchmarks, with relative gains of 46% on MBPP and 14% on GSM8K. At 288 fine-grained domains, only vertex sampling supports a linear fit, and LinMix improves benchmark accuracy by 11% on average over the best nonlinear baseline.

title: Effective Optical Geometry and Holographic Phase Structure of a Magnetic AdS Black Hole
text:
Title: Effective Optical Geometry and Holographic Phase Structure of a Magnetic AdS Black Hole
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We study circular null orbits, thermodynamic topology, and the holographic thermodynamic description of a four-dimensional magnetically charged AdS black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics. The background orbit structure is classified using Duan s phi-mapping construction and compared with the extraordinary electromagnetic characteristics. The latter defines an effective optical metric with an additional radial factor that modifies the orbit condition and introduces explicit dependence on the AdS radius. For four representative configurations, the local indices of the five isolated orbits are unchanged while their radii shift by up to 5.187 %. The background mass thresholds vary smoothly across sigma = 1/4 when the total mass is used, whereas the fixed-m0 parametrization is singular there. Regularity at the center requires sigma > 1 and m0 = 0. The thermodynamic analysis separates local stability indices from equilibrium coexistence: stable Gibbs-free-energy branches cross only in model-dependent parameter intervals. The boundary canonical ensemble exhibits critical behavior consistent with mean-field exponents, and the examined grand-canonical ensemble has a Hawking-Page crossing. In the mixed ensemble, the free-energy branches have a finite endpoint discontinuity, but the sampled competing states do not satisfy the full local-stability criterion

title: Non-Destructive Detection of Early Drought Stress via Spectral Submanifold Analysis
text:
Title: Non-Destructive Detection of Early Drought Stress via Spectral Submanifold Analysis
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Non-destructive early detection of water stress is critical for precision agriculture, yet current detection methods are often labor-intensive or destructive. We propose a rapid, non-invasive method based on Spectral Submanifold (SSM) reduction to analyze the nonlinear vibration dynamics of soybean plants. Unlike traditional linear modal analysis, our data-driven approach reveals a distinct transition in the dominant dynamics of the plant stem as drought progresses.
