Title: When Reasoning looks like Hidden Understanding: How Chain-of-Thought Fosters Anthropomorphism, Perceptions of Epistemic Superiority, and Cognitive Deference
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

As AI-based products permeate society, specifically systems using generative models, a belief system is emerging about what these products are and what they can and cannot do. One common belief concerns the perception of the form of language as evidence of 'understanding' language. As these generative models reproduce linguistic patterns rather than understand meaning, interpreting these patterns as evidence of understanding is a misattribution. This misconception is extended by the notion that generative models can 'explain their reasoning.' Anecdotally, these misconceptions which mistake the form of language for its meaning are driving cognitive deference to AI systems in a way that displaces human agency. Such mistakes involve attributions of cognitive properties to the system, allowing them to be treated like intentional 'minds'. Importantly, perceived epistemic authority and superiority make that 'mind' worth deferring to. Anthropomorphism in tandem with epistemic authority and superiority, we argue, increases the risk that users generalise from narrow task performance to broader competencies, committing the "fallacy of composition". This paper explores misconceptions of Chain of Thought (CoT) reasoning as sufficient transparent 'explanation'. We explore how anthropomorphism acts as a vehicle for cognitive deference of decision-making and perceptions of epistemic superiority in AI systems. Finally, we explore CoT's ramifications using medicine as an example. Taken together, we conclude that explainability operationalised through CoT is highly problematic and undercuts the very ethical principles it is intended to serve. While CoT may be valuable for improving output accuracy and moderation, we suggest that the practice of asking models to provide user facing reasons for their outputs should be actively discouraged, and AI literacy training should explicitly caution against its use.

title: CryoAnomaly: Few-Shot Cryo-EM Particle Picking via Anomaly-Guided Hard Negative Suppression
text:
Title: CryoAnomaly: Few-Shot Cryo-EM Particle Picking via Anomaly-Guided Hard Negative Suppression
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is crucial for analyzing 3D biological structures, in which automated particle picking is essential for the workflow. However, fully supervised methods require extensive manual annotations. While few-shot learning offers a potential solution, existing approaches struggle to handle the diverse contaminations inherent in real micrographs owing to insufficient negative supervision, resulting in false positives that degrade the quality of the 3D reconstruction. Although synthetic data provides abundant and perfect labels, their use has primarily been restricted to validating identical proteins or augmenting full-shot training, leaving the potential for few-shot adaptation to novel proteins unexplored. In this study, we investigate the effective utilization of synthetic data for few-shot particle picking. We identify that direct transfer fails due to a ``clean-vs-contaminated'' Sim2Real gap. To overcome this, we propose CryoAnomaly, which is a framework that turns this gap into an advantage. By employing an anomaly detector trained on clean synthetic data, we identify real-world contaminants as anomalies and suppress them via a novel anomaly-guided hard negative suppression loss. On the CryoPPP benchmark, CryoAnomaly achieves the best picking accuracy and reconstruction resolution among state-of-the-art methods in the few-shot setting. The proposed anomaly-guided loss is confirmed to be effective on datasets with diverse contamination, where reliable pseudo-anomaly masks can be generated. Our code, dataset, and project page are available at: https://github.com/riku359/CryoAnomaly, https://huggingface.co/datasets/rikrikrik/CryoAnomaly, https://riku359.github.io/CryoAnomaly-page/.

title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
text:
Title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces its proposed method as the baseline; an AI-Scientist entering the environment is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. We release the first 1,000 verified environments. With the world as an evaluation, we found that frontier AI-Scientists can already surpass the human researchers 74% of the time. As a record of how AI does science, it contains 6,400 hours of research traces, with every idea, experiment, failure, and success. As a training ground, we are able to raise (+158%) a small model to match frontier models in research ideation. At last, AI-Scientists' own world has arrived, grown from and growing with science itself.

title: Quark-level CPT violation in neutral-meson systems
text:
Title: Quark-level CPT violation in neutral-meson systems
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

This work investigates CPT and Lorentz breakdown in neutral-meson interferometry within the nonminimal Standard-Model Extension. Employing methods of chiral perturbation theory for mass dimension d=5, a connection between the quark-level and the meson effective pseudoscalar Lagrangian is established. The resulting phenomenological signatures in neutral-meson oscillations with particular focus on the detector geometry are explored. This analysis permits the interpretation of such CPT tests within the d=5 quark sector of the Standard-Model Extension. Existing data are used to extract first constraints on two coefficients and to estimate achievable sensitivity gains over published bounds of up to 18 orders of magnitude.

title: Toward a theory of Evaluability
text:
Title: Toward a theory of Evaluability
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Machine learning models, particularly large foundation models, are increasingly evaluated along multiple axes that are relevant for their usage. In addition to accuracy measures appropriate for the specific task of interest, measures capturing safety, calibration and fairness properties are often of interest. The classical approach to these problems assumes that the test set has been held out from the training process, an assumption that is increasingly harder to justify for large foundation models. In this work, we formalize a notion of evaluability without this assumption, and ask if it is feasible to evaluate black-box models in settings where our test samples may have been used during training. We study this problem under different settings, capturing different levels of access to the model. We first study the natural setting, where the evaluator only looks at the output of the model on the test set. We fully characterize the class of distributions where accurate evaluation is possible, and show tight upper and lower bounds on the sample complexity of evaluation. Our results show that black-box evaluation in this setup is feasible if and only if the distribution is close to being small support. We then consider evaluation algorithms that can query the model on additional inputs and demonstrate connections to self-correctors studied in program testing. Using these, we show that a small amount of query access can increase the power of the evaluator for natural distributions and concept classes.

title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
text:
Title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Non-intrusive Model Reduction under Data Scarcity
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Many-query analyses, in which a computational model is repeatedly evaluated, play an important role in uncertainty quantification and optimization for engineering design. However, many-query analyses can be prohibitively expensive when considering high-fidelity numerical models, especially those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Surrogate modeling replaces costly simulations with cheap approximations, enabling practical uncertainty quantification and design workflows. Machine learning (ML) approaches to surrogate modeling have gained significant traction in the development of surrogate models due to their non-intrusive nature; they do not require access to the underlying simulation code. The Operator Inference (OpInf) approach, in particular, fits reduced operators to state and corresponding time derivative data. However, high-fidelity training data is scarce due to limited computational budgets, and OpInf models trained on such scarce data often exhibit high variance, a critical liability in high-risk engineering design. We propose Multifidelity Operator Inference (MF-OpInf), which reduces this variance by supplementing scarce high-fidelity snapshots with abundant low-fidelity data drawn from coarser discretizations of the same problem. MF-OpInf handles data across varying fidelity levels by utilizing a multifidelity linear regression framework to estimate the reduced operators. Numerical experiments on model PDE problems demonstrate that MF-OpInf predicts PDE solution fields with higher accuracy compared to the high-fidelity-only OpInf with the same computational budget.

title: One Curve, Different Weights: AUC, the Brier Score, Decision-Weighted AUC, and the Policy Youden Index
text:
Title: One Curve, Different Weights: AUC, the Brier Score, Decision-Weighted AUC, and the Policy Youden Index
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

AUC and the Brier score are standard summaries of a binary risk score, yet they can rank models differently. We introduce a weighted AUC, AUC$_π$, which weights each pair of observations by how differently a decision maker with probability of acting $π$ treats them. We show that all three are built on weighted averages of one curve, the Youden index $J(t) = \mathrm{TPR}(t) - \mathrm{FPR}(t)$ across cutoffs $t$, and that the averages differ in the weights they put on the cutoffs. Each weights a cutoff by how much something rises across it: for AUC, the distribution of all scores; for the Brier score, the true probability $\mathbb{E}[Y \mid S]$; for AUC$_π$, the decision maker's probability of acting. Up to normalization, AUC$_π$ is the Brier skill score of the ideal forecast with its weight moved to the cutoffs the decision maker cares about. We also show that weighting pairs by $|π(s) - π(s')|$ is, up to scale, the only pair weight fixed in advance that makes a pair-weighted AUC an average of the Youden curve for every score distribution. As a ranking measure, AUC weights every model the same way. Hand (2009) shows that it can also be read as an average over cost thresholds, and in that reading each model weights the thresholds differently. The numerator of AUC$_π$, which we call the policy Youden index, is the expected share of class 1 a fixed policy acts on minus the expected share of class 0. It judges every model by the same policy and so avoids this; the full ratio AUC$_π$ does not.

title: Anomalous thermal transport in isotope-enriched germanium carbide
text:
Title: Anomalous thermal transport in isotope-enriched germanium carbide
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Advances in modern electronics demand the dissipation of heat fluxes approaching 1000 W cm$^{-2}$, which drives an urgent need for materials with thermal conductivity ($κ$) exceeding 1000 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. Here, by solving the Boltzmann transport equation considering both three- and four-phonon interactions, we observe that isotopically pure cubic germanium carbide (GeC) exhibits a remarkable $κ$ of 1018 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is further corroborated by state-of-the-art machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations. Two unique mechanisms underlie this anomalously high $κ$: a remarkably strong isotopic enhancement effect (289%) and a surprisingly modest suppression due to four-phonon scattering (22%)-despite the presence of a wide acoustic-optical phonon gap. Moreover, we find that GeC defies the conventional Leibfried-Schlomann formula and exhibits a non-monotonic variation of $κ$ with external hydrostatic pressure at elevated temperatures. Our findings establish isotope-enriched GeC as a material of ultrahigh $κ$ and an ideal platform for exploring exotic phonon physics.

title: BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch
text:
Title: BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We study the robustness of two state-of-the-art BP-based qLDPC decoders, Relay-BP and beam search, designed for independent noise when applied to spatially correlated noise with unchanged single-mechanism error probabilities. We generate correlated errors with a hidden Gaussian Markov random field, which lets us control the strength and range of the correlation while keeping every marginal error probability exact. This setting complements correlation-aware decoding: it asks how existing decoders perform when their assumed joint error model is mismatched. Across multiple tested circuits and code instances that we simulated, we observe that correlations can change logical error rates by orders of magnitude, reduce the finite-size distance advantage, and alter the relative ranking of Relay-BP, beam search, and BP-OSD. On one of the two tested circuits, Relay-BP and beam search become worse than BP-OSD, and increasing relay memory or beam width does not compensate for the degradation. Configuration analysis indicates that correlation primarily increases the probability of trapping configurations that are known to challenge these decoders; at matched error weight, correlated errors still cause decoding failures several times more often than i.i.d. errors. Finally, supplying the decoders with the marginals conditioned on the hidden field recovers most of the lost performance in the tested settings identifying prior mismatch as a major contributor to performance degradation under correlation.

title: Irreducible Weyl Semimetals
text:
Title: Irreducible Weyl Semimetals
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

A key objective in Weyl-semimetal (WSM) research is to identify phases built from minimal configurations of Weyl points (WPs), which provide the simplest settings for investigating the intrinsic physics of chiral topological charges. Pang et al. [Phys. Rev. Res. 8, 033304 (2026)] recently established that crystallographically realizable WSMs can be decomposed into linear combinations of 16 minimal "irreducible Weyl molecules" (IWMs). A fundamental question remains unresolved: which of these non-decomposable configurations can themselves form standalone crystalline phases? Here we introduce irreducible Weyl semimetals (IWSMs), in which two bands crossing near the Fermi level form an elementary symmetry-compatible complex whose complete Weyl-node configuration is charge neutral and crystallographically indivisible. Combining all 1651 magnetic space groups with Weyl-orbit multiplicities and band-compatibility relations, we classify IWSMs formed by crystalline-symmetry-protected twofold WPs. Only ten of the sixteen primitive inventories admit one-copy realizations, comprising four Pair, four Split, and two Mixed charge-node architectures. Remarkably, this classification uncovers five unconventional and previously unrecognized topological phases: the charge-three Pair IWSM {3, -3}; the Split IWSMs {3, -1, -1, -1}, and {4, -1, -1, -1, -1}; and the Mixed IWSMs {3, 1, -2, -2} and {3, 3, -2, -2, -2}. For all ten classes, symmetry-constrained lattice models verify the complete node inventories, Chern charges, and surface chiral-flow incidence. Our results establish crystalline irreducibility as a phase-level organizing principle beyond individual Weyl nodes and provide a symmetry-resolved framework for identifying minimal Weyl complexes in electronic, phononic, and photonic systems.

title: Controlled Binary Assignment Flows
text:
Title: Controlled Binary Assignment Flows
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

This paper introduces a geometric approach to the representation and learning of time-variant parametrizations of deep assignment flows, for binary data labelings on graphs. Each edge carries an optimally controlled parameter flow in a 2-dimensional totally geodesic submanifold, based on objectives derived from a non-local linear scale space representation of the input data. The aggregation of triplets of such flows in 5-dimensional totally geodesic submanifolds is learned from data. The fusion of these flows determines the trajectory in the high-dimensional symmetric parameter space and by geometric integration the layers of binary deep assignment flows. Numerical results demonstrate the expressivity and the limitation of our highly parallel geometric local synthesis approach to high-dimensional deep assignment flow parametrizations.

title: Fixed-Dimensional Latent Flow for Generating Variable-Size 3D Molecules
text:
Title: Fixed-Dimensional Latent Flow for Generating Variable-Size 3D Molecules
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Molecular size is intrinsically linked to composition, structure, and properties, but most 3D molecular generators treat size as a predefined input rather than a quantity to be generated. We introduce Equivariant-Free Transformer-Autoencoded Latent Flow Matching, a two-stage framework that samples a fixed-dimensional latent vector using flow matching and employs an autoregressive Transformer to determine molecular size, atom types, coordinates, and chemical attributes. Canonical atom ordering and rigid-pose alignment enable Transformers without equivariant layers, while decoded attributes guide bond reconstruction. On PCQM4Mv2, unconditional generation yields 87.9\% unique and novel molecules passing sanitization and PoseBusters checks, exceeding baselines with lower end-to-end training and sampling time and higher end-to-end throughput. Across ten target HOMO-LUMO gaps, internal ranking retains 30\% of the screened candidates and increases the density functional theory-verified hit rate within 0.1 eV of the target from 25.0\% to 52.4\%, while largely preserving novelty and diversity. These results demonstrate fixed-dimensional latent generation with autoregressive decoding as a practical approach to molecular design without prespecifying size.

title: Two-point residual step size gradient methods for linear systems
text:
Title: Two-point residual step size gradient methods for linear systems
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Kaczmarz-type methods often converge slowly when the coefficient matrix is ill-conditioned. In particular, when the smallest singular value is small, every row of the coefficient matrix is nearly orthogonal to the corresponding right singular direction, so that the iteration stalls along that direction. To break this slow-convergence regime, we borrow the delayed-step-size idea of the Barzilai-Borwein (BB) method and, within the framework of the residual-based surrogate-hyperplane Kaczmarz method, propose two new step sizes for gradient-descent-type methods solving linear systems: a delayed residual step size \(α_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\) and a residual-difference step size \(α_k^{\mathrm{RD}}\), which correspond, respectively, to the BB1 and BB2 step sizes in convex quadratic optimization. We prove that \(α_k^{\mathrm{RD}}\leα_k^{\mathrm{DR}}\), and we analyze the convergence of the resulting method in a canonical model with two singular values: although the step sizes are non-monotone, the residual norm is shown to decrease after finitely many steps. Numerical experiments on some ill-conditioned linear systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

title: pCoMole: Pareto-Constrained Molecule Editing with Discrete Flows
text:
Title: pCoMole: Pareto-Constrained Molecule Editing with Discrete Flows
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Biomolecular therapeutics often start from known sequences and require targeted editing to improve multiple properties while satisfying hard biochemical and manufacturability constraints. However, existing generative methods do not jointly support multi-objective optimization, hard feasibility, and sequence editing in discrete, variable-length biological spaces. In this work, we introduce Pareto-Constrained Molecule Editing (pCoMole), a framework built on discrete flow matching that steers a pre-trained Edit Flow toward user-specified preferences while enforcing terminal feasibility. pCoMole defines a feasibility-gated terminal distribution using an augmented Tchebycheff utility and realizes the resulting preference tilt through a Doob-h transform of the underlying edit process. To make this construction practical, we approximate the required harmonic function using short Monte Carlo rollouts over candidate edits, yielding an efficient guided editor with provable preference consistency. We validate pCoMole by shrinking GFP while retaining fluorescence-related properties, shortening diverse Cas9 orthologs while preserving PAM specificity, and compressing peptide binders into short peptidomimetics that optimize seven drug-related properties under hard constraints. In wet lab testing, two 229-residue pCoMole-designed eGFP variants retained clear green fluorescence in BL21 cells after 10 deletions, with either one or two substitutions. Together, pCoMole enables constraint-aware, Pareto-aligned editing of biomolecular sequences in discrete, variable-length spaces.

title: DISSOLVR: An Interpretable and Fast Framework for Aqueous and Organic Solubility Prediction
text:
Title: DISSOLVR: An Interpretable and Fast Framework for Aqueous and Organic Solubility Prediction
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

High-fidelity solubility prediction is fundamental to pharmaceutical development and environmental partitioning, where accurate modeling must couple molecular structure with thermodynamic behavior across diverse chemical environments. However, recent advancements have been dominated by deep learning architectures that often sacrifice physical interpretability for predictive power. We challenge this trend by showing that state-of-the-art performance does not require such non-transparent architectures. To address this, we introduce DISSOLVR, a transparent framework for molecular solubility prediction. In addition, we perform a comprehensive literature review and a benchmarking study against various methods. We show that DISSOLVR approaches the aleatoric limit of experimental uncertainty and achieves OOD generalization through structural invariance, derived by mapping molecules to physically-grounded descriptors. Then, we present an LLM-assisted post-hoc explanation pipeline that bridges the gap between symbolic model artifacts and chemically grounded narratives. Finally, a comparative benchmark of a survey involving 22 expert chemists reveals that expert evaluators provide deep insights.

title: A Physical Testbed for Self-Driving Laboratories: Comparing Bayesian and Agentic Optimization in a Minimal Closed-Loop Color Formulation Task
text:
Title: A Physical Testbed for Self-Driving Laboratories: Comparing Bayesian and Agentic Optimization in a Minimal Closed-Loop Color Formulation Task
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) integrate laboratory robotics and automation with AI-driven decision-making to close the design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycle. However, physical testbeds that combine off-the-shelf hardware and AI into a functioning closed-loop workflow remain in early stages of development, and their integration with commercial laboratory automation is comparatively less developed. In this work, we develop a physical testbed that assembles and integrates commercially available laboratory automation instruments and demonstrate continuous, closed-loop, autonomous operation over 24 cumulative hours of unattended experimentation. We validate this platform on a minimal closed-loop discovery task in which the system autonomously formulates aqueous dye mixtures to match a target absorbance spectrum. The system completed six independent campaigns, each consisting of 48 closed-loop iterations over approximately four hours. In every campaign, the system autonomously selected, dispensed, and measured each mixture, with an AI-driven decision-making algorithm determining subsequent formulations without human intervention. Using this testbed, we compared the performance of two AI-driven decision-making algorithms, traditional Bayesian optimization (BO) and an agentic approach, in selecting mixtures under a fixed total-volume constraint. The agentic optimizer matched target absorbance spectra using fewer iterations than BO, with reductions up to 52%, and converged on a solution for one target that BO failed to match within 48 iterations. These results demonstrate a reference physical platform for SDLs that can evaluate both established and emerging AI strategies, including large language model (LLM)-directed optimization, before their deployment in real-world applications where experiments may be costly and time-consuming to prepare.

title: A law of the iterated logarithm for random multiplicative functions on integers with a large prime factor
text:
Title: A law of the iterated logarithm for random multiplicative functions on integers with a large prime factor
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers. We investigate the almost sure fluctuations of the restricted sum $M^{>}(x)=\sum_{n\le x;~ P(n)>x^{1/2}}f(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime factor of $n$. With $Q(x)$ being the conditional variance of $M^{>}(x)$ given the values of $f$ at primes not exceeding $x^{1/2}$, we prove that, almost surely, the upper and lower limits of $M^{>}(x)(2Q(x)\log\log Q(x))^{-1/2}$ as $x\to\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, respectively. Furthermore, it is shown that the almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$.

title: Descriptive power and predictive limits of a discrete Hasimoto--DNLS model of protein backbone structure
text:
Title: Descriptive power and predictive limits of a discrete Hasimoto--DNLS model of protein backbone structure
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Determining 3D protein structure from sequence remains a fundamental biophysical challenge. The C$_α$ backbone's discrete Frenet geometry maps, via a Hasimoto transform, to a complex scalar field $ψ=κ\,e^{i\sumτ}$ obeying a discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation (DNLS), whose solitons reproduce secondary-structure motifs. Whether this compact mapping extends to a predictive folding framework remains open. We derive an exact closed-form decomposition of the DNLS effective potential $V_{\text{eff}}=V_{\text{re}}+iV_{\text{im}}$ via curvature ratios and torsion angles, validated to machine precision across 856 non-redundant proteins. Our analysis identifies three structural barriers to forward prediction: (i)~$V_{\text{im}}$ encodes chirality via the odd symmetry of $\sinτ$; its magnitude is ${\sim}31\%$ of the real part, and neglecting it causes a $2^N$ degeneracy; (ii)~$V_{\text{re}}$ is determined mostly (${\sim}95\%$) by local geometry, leaving explicit sequence dependence below ${\sim}5\%$ of variance; and (iii)~self-consistent field iterations fail to recover native structures (mean RMSD $= 13.1$\,Å) even with hydrogen-bond terms, yielding zero torsion correlations. Conversely, the DNLS dispersion relation residual serves as a geometric order parameter for $α$-helices (ROC AUC $= 0.72$), identifying where the backbone best approximates an integrable system. Thus, the Hasimoto map functions as a kinematic identity, not a dynamical governing equation. Obstacles to \textit{ab initio} prediction stem from the purely local, real-potential reduction built upon it, rather than the lossless map itself.

title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
text:
Title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Frontier agents retrieve structural metadata well and compute geometry from coordinates less reliably. We ask how much of a benchmark score reflects that gap and how much reflects the evaluation configuration around the model. We study ProteinGeoBench, a suite of 131 protein-structure tasks, using 4,249 rollouts from four frontier models and 4,486 further trials across 26 models. Three of the four frontier models fall within 0.031 of one another (0.785 to 0.816) with no difference between them resolved, while the fourth scores 0.707 and all three gaps to it exclude zero. Three of the four do better on metadata lookup than on numeric calculation. The fourth is slightly better on numeric. Numeric tasks are 28 of the 131 but half of the twelve tasks that all four models fail. The ranking also depends on the evaluation budget: with one run per task, 23.9% of bootstrap replicates put a different model first. On a selected 15-task slice, removing network access lowers scores more than blocking eight structural-database domains, but the two contrasts were graded in different passes and cannot be cleanly decomposed. Swapping in each model's own command-line agent changes scores by -0.071 to +0.086, a comparison too small to rule out moderate harness effects. Across 26 models, numeric performance rises with non-numeric performance rather than staying flat. The experiments use different task subsets, so they cannot rank model, harness, access and task composition against one another. Evaluations should report results by task family, along with the number of runs, the harness and the access conditions.

title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
text:
Title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

title: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
text:
Title: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We give an explicit construction of all ALF and ALE toric gravitational instantons in terms of certain rational matrix functions of one complex variable on the Riemann sphere; these provide patching matrices for their corresponding twistor holomorphic vector bundles. The reconstruction of the instantons arises from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert splitting problem and we show how this can be solved via linear algebra, resembling but not equivalent to the Belinski--Zakharov ansatz. This construction gives a complete classification together with an explicit form for all toric gravitational instantons up to the resolutions of conical and orbifold singularities. We illustrate the formalism by computer--assisted numerical construction of two new ALF (but not AF) gravitational instantons with five nodes.

title: Direct and indirect operator learning strategies for parametric optimal control problems
text:
Title: Direct and indirect operator learning strategies for parametric optimal control problems
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This paper focuses on the use of learning nonlinear operators via Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) for approximating the solutions of optimal control problems. We study two operator learning strategies, namely, indirect and direct, both based on DeepONets, for parametric families of optimal control problems where the same problem must be solved many times for different initial data, different parameters, different cost function weights, and different bounds defining the set of the admissible controls. In the indirect strategy two DeepONets approximate the solution operators of the state and adjoint systems, and their predictions are used inside iterative projected gradient algorithms for finding the optimal control. In the direct strategy, a single DeepONet approximates the operator that maps directly to the optimal control generated by a reference solver; consequently, a new control is obtained through a single evaluation of the network. In order to analyze the computational cost, the efficiency, the speed and the accuracy of the learning strategies, we consider an optimal control problem related to an ordinary differential system that describes the temporal evolution of the glioblastoma growth subject to therapeutic interventions. For this specific optimal control problem we propose a discretize-then-optimize strategy, based on an implicit-explicit finite difference method, and then, we develop several numerical experiments in order to compare the two DeepONet learning strategies for this problem. The proposed operator learning DeepONet strategies can be adapted to approximate large classes of optimal control problems related to diverse differential systems.

title: Cuscuton Fifth Force: Implications of Non-Dynamical Scalars for Structure Growth
text:
Title: Cuscuton Fifth Force: Implications of Non-Dynamical Scalars for Structure Growth
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The cuscuton is a scalar field that obeys a constraint rather than an evolution equation, so it modifies gravity without adding a propagating scalar degree of freedom. We study the cosmology of effective cuscuton theory when matter is minimally coupled in the Jordan frame, and therefore conformally coupled to the cuscuton in the Einstein-frame. We derive the background and linear perturbation equations and show that the algebraic cuscuton response mediates a fifth force even though the scalar itself does not propagate. The same conformal factor also changes Einstein-frame particle masses and the friction of matter perturbations, tying the strength and sign of the force to the background evolution rather than to an independent coupling. We study a power-law family of models which contain both tracking solutions and sign-switching solutions; in the latter the effective cuscuton density runs from negative during matter domination to a positive, cosmological-constant-like value today. Using a modified version of CLASS, including the induced particle-mass dependence of recombination, we illustrate the corresponding changes to CMB temperature and linear matter power spectra for benchmark models, without fitting to data. In the strongest benchmarks the fifth force changes the effective gravitational coupling on sub-horizon scales by about one percent, smaller than the accompanying changes to the matter power spectrum and the acoustic scale. For the sign-switching solutions this change is negative over most of cosmic history, so a non-propagating field can weaken rather than strengthen gravitational attraction.

title: Small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation
text:
Title: Small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

This paper investigates the small inertia limit of the distribution-dependent stochastic Cucker--Smale equation with the full velocity alignment source term, which serves as the mean-field equation for the stochastic Cucker--Smale model. Inspired by the idea of Hottovy et al. \cite{Hottovy2015} to rearrange SDEs via integration by parts, we repeatedly perform integration by parts on independent copies of our equation. Then we define a global position correction and a quadratic remainder, both with uniformly bounded tails. Applying the Aldous criterion, we obtain tightness of the position correction, which in turn yields tightness of the position process. Subsequently, using the averaging method on the fast time scale, the quadratic functional can be decomposed into the equilibrium average, local quadratic fluctuations, and exponential transients. Then, the Poisson--Lyapunov equation is employed to prove the convergence of the time integral. Finally, under various suitable assumptions, we obtain the weak convergence of the laws of the approximating processes to the law of the solution of the small-inertia limit equation, along with the identification of the limiting process, and also the convergence rate of strong $L^1$-convergence. The extra noise-induced drift term can be expressed as the solution of a contraction-type Fredholm equation. This paper is complementary to the deterministic particle limit work of \cite{Carrillo2021,Choi2021} .

title: Spectral properties of twisted soft waveguides
text:
Title: Spectral properties of twisted soft waveguides
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We discuss a model of a soft waveguide described by Schrödinger operator whose potential is a twisted straight channel of non-circular profile. We show that a compactly supported twist makes the operator subcritical, the property being expressed in terms of a Hardy-type inequality. On the other hand, a periodic twist raises the essential spectrum and its local slowdown may give rise to isolated eigenvalues below the essential spectrum threshold.

title: Flex-DDCM: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Image Compression via Diffusion Trajectory Guidance
text:
Title: Flex-DDCM: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Image Compression via Diffusion Trajectory Guidance
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Recent zero-shot image compression methods exploit the powerful priors of pretrained diffusion models to produce perceptually pleasing reconstructions without compression-specific training. However, image compression serves not only human viewing but also machine analysis, while existing zero-shot codecs have limited flexibility in meeting the diverse reconstruction requirements of these applications. In this paper, we propose Flex-DDCM, a framework for zero-shot task-oriented image compression via diffusion trajectory guidance. Building on Turbo-DDCM, we adapt the coded diffusion trajectory through task-guided noise selection, embedding the effects of task guidance into the compressed representation. Guidance terms can be applied individually or combined, with timestep-dependent strengths controlling their influence throughout denoising. This design enables task adaptation without introducing additional decoding complexity. Experiments demonstrate flexible trade-offs among pixel fidelity, perceptual quality, and downstream task performance, with competitive performance against trained task-oriented codecs and faster decoding than Diff-ICMH.

title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole: Linear stability and strong cosmic censorship conjecture
text:
Title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole: Linear stability and strong cosmic censorship conjecture
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We present an alternative formulation of coupled gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black holes, yielding decoupled radial and angular equations with a well-defined $Λ\rightarrow 0$ limit. We compute the quasinormal mode spectra using spectral and direct integration methods, finding excellent agreement. All of these modes are consistent with the linear stability of the Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole. We investigate the photon sphere and near-extremal modes, revealing a non-trivial interplay between rotation and electric charge. We further explore the implications for the strong cosmic censorship conjecture and find that the photon sphere modes predominantly determine its validity within the parameter space considered. While increasing the rotation of the black hole generally favours the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, increasing the electric charge can promote its violation. We also find that the region of parameter space exhibiting a violation of the conjecture is comparatively smaller for gravitational perturbations than for electromagnetic perturbations. These results highlight the important role of rotation, electric charge, and the nature of perturbations in determining the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in Kerr--Newman--de Sitter spacetimes.

title: Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part I: common random numbers meet supermartingales
text:
Title: Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part I: common random numbers meet supermartingales
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We analyze adaptive sampling stochastic model-based trust-region methods that build their models in random subspaces and use common random numbers (CRN) within an iteration, and obtain, within a STORM-type analysis, the first $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ bound on the number of function evaluations needed to reach $\varepsilon$-stationarity, both almost surely and in expectation. The subspace model reduces the per-iteration computational cost, which allows scalability. The analysis relies on a general framework for the complexity of adaptive stochastic processes that carries the almost-sure analysis of ASTRO-DF into the STORM setting and adds expected bounds by a direct counting argument, without the renewal-reward argument of Blanchet et al. (2019). The bounds are obtained for two variants of a stochastic model-based trust-region method that differ in how the function evaluations used to measure progress are generated. The first algorithm, ASTRA-F, proceeds in a STORM-like manner: the trial point and the incumbent are re-evaluated on an independent set of replications, so that the estimates entering the acceptance test are independent of the model, as every existing STORM-type analysis requires their accuracy to be assessed conditionally on the model. The second, ASTRA-R, allows a practical approach: the trial point is evaluated on the replications already drawn to build the model, which avoids re-evaluating the incumbent, needs one adaptive sample size per iteration instead of two, and reduces the randomness entering the iteration. To our knowledge, no STORM-type analysis has been able to accommodate the latter approach as the accuracy of an estimate at a point chosen from the samples cannot be assessed conditionally on the model; we overcome this with a probabilistic chaining argument.

title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
text:
Title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Estimating biased finite-memory sources from a single trajectory is a fundamental problem with practical impact, for example in estimating entropy for cryptography. We study order-$d$ binary sources whose conditional probabilities have bias at most $ε$, and establish *sharp* sample complexity bounds: relative accuracy $γ$ with confidence $1-δ$ needs $γ^{-2}\,(\tfrac12-ε)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\tfrac1δ)$ samples up to constants depending on $ε$, with matching upper and lower bounds and no dependence on mixing time or spectral gap. The proof rests on a sharp bound on expected hitting times of the sliding-window (de Bruijn) chain, which stay of order $1/π(w)$ uniformly in $d$ exactly when $ε<\tfrac3{10}$, and on majorization of the window masses by those of independent biased coins. Applied to published entropy-source validations, the bounds show that their trace lengths may be underpowered: $10^6$ bits cannot resolve all transitions of an $8$-bit model to better than about $4.5\%$ relative error.

title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
text:
Title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

title: On some stochastic evolutions on Laguerre-Polya functions
text:
Title: On some stochastic evolutions on Laguerre-Polya functions
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We prove uniqueness in law for three stochastic evolutions on normalised Laguerre-Pólya functions arising as scaling limits of matrix characteristic polynomial dynamics. In particular, this implies that Ahn's universal Brownian Gibbs line ensemble arising from random matrix products has the law of the logarithms of the reciprocal zeros of the solution, unique in law, to a simple stochastic equation on entire functions started from $\mathrm{e}^{-z}$. The method of proof relies on some integrable structure of the problem in the special form of a new duality with finite-dimensional diffusions which is closely related to intertwinings.

title: The structure of the pion at large $N_c$
text:
Title: The structure of the pion at large $N_c$
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. Gauge configurations for different values of the lattice spacing are generated with the pure-gauge TEK action, while the pion correlators are computed for different quark masses with maximally twisted mass fermions. The bare matrix element corresponding to the quark momentum fraction is obtained using the Feynman-Hellmann method, and we use perturbative renormalization factors to connect to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. A global analysis at several lattice spacings, pion masses, and values of $N_c$ yields $\langle x\rangle_q^{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}(2\,\mathrm{GeV}) = 0.267(105)$ at the physical pion mass in the large-$N_c$ limit. This value is significantly smaller than existing $N_c=3$ determinations from phenomenology and lattice QCD, indicating that, in the large-$N_c$ limit, the pion's light-cone momentum is carried predominantly by gluons.

title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
text:
Title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

When an LLM agent fails part-way through a long task, the usual analysis records a symptom: a failure-mode label, or the agent and step judged responsible. It does not say where the error entered, which state carried it to the symptom, whether anything in the trajectory contradicted it, or which control could have caught it. We define an episode record that ties a candidate fault to its origin, propagation, detection, response and consequence, located by operational phase and state domain, and that names the control families whose observation and reach cover it. We turned the record into a written annotation protocol and applied it to 95 failed runs of six multi-agent systems from the public Who&When and MAD corpora, reading each trajectory in full. Faults enter early (median at 0.18 of the run), mostly as wrong decisions or fabrications over task state, and in 37 of 88 Who&When runs before the step the corpus' human labels mark as decisive. In 72% of failed runs the trajectory already contained evidence against the error before the failure; in 88% of those no agent acted on it. Something flagged a deviation in 31% of runs, but no response removed the deviated state. Independent judges reading the unused evidence, task contracts fixed at admission, and re-checking beliefs against the environment reach most episodes; restoring the agent's own state would have sufficed in 35 of 95 runs. A text scan of the raw corpus also shows that 45% of the hand-crafted Who&When failures ended with a provider content-filter crash after which the harness emitted a final answer no agent produced, a failure class that neither symptom taxonomies nor responsible-agent labels represent. Protocol, records and scripts are included.

title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
text:
Title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (35.9%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

title: Accurate representation of the continuum orbital in a Gaussian basis set: application to Auger decay rates
text:
Title: Accurate representation of the continuum orbital in a Gaussian basis set: application to Auger decay rates
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Many processes in chemistry and physics, such as autoionization, photoionization, or electron-impact collisions, involve unbound electrons. Despite their importance, theoretical methods for modeling continuum electrons remain significantly less developed than those for purely bound electronic states. Here we present a novel approach for treating continuum electrons within Gaussian-based quantum chemistry. The method represents continuum orbital in a discrete basis of standard Gaussian-type orbitals (GTOs), where the continuum wave function is obtained by solving the Lippmann-Schwinger equation with proper boundary conditions using an analytical representation of the Green's function in an auxiliary GTO basis set. The resulting continuum orbital is multicentered and multichannel, providing a rigorous description of scattering states. As an initial application of the new methodology, we compute Auger decay rates for several atomic and molecular systems, including Ne, H$_2$O, CO$_2$, and Ar. We demonstrate a consistent improvement of the results with increasing the quality of the continuum representation. We show also that higher-order electron-correlation effects in the bound domain are essential for an accurate treatment of satellite transitions. The present formalism therefore provides a systematically improvable Gaussian-based framework for continuum-electron problems that is fully compatible with standard quantum chemistry methods.

title: Field-free transverse response in altermagnet and topological insulator heterojunctions
text:
Title: Field-free transverse response in altermagnet and topological insulator heterojunctions
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We theoretically investigate the transport properties of a topological insulator (TI) connected to two-dimensional altermagnetic (AM) leads in the absence of an external magnetic field. Exploiting the intrinsic time-reversal symmetry breaking of altermagnets, we report the emergence of a field-free transverse differential conductivity in the resulting AM-TI-AM heterostructure. Our analysis reveals that this transverse response is highly sensitive to the orientation of the Néel vector: a finite transverse conductivity manifests when the Néel vector possesses an out-of-plane component, whereas it strictly vanishes for in-plane orientations ($θ= π/2$) under symmetric chemical potentials ($μ_t = μ_b$) due to the restoration of symmetry between the $k_y$ and $-k_y$ momentum channels. Conversely, when asymmetric chemical potentials are applied ($μ_t \neq μ_b$), this symmetry is broken, yielding a finite transverse response even for an in-plane Néel vector. Furthermore, we demonstrate that while the longitudinal differential conductivity exhibits Fabry-Pérot-type oscillations as a function of the TI's chemical potential, the transverse conductivity displays a distinct antisymmetric dependence. Notably, the oscillatory behavior of the longitudinal conductivity persists even at finite temperatures. Spatially, the transverse current contribution decays exponentially with position inside the TI region. We also find that both the longitudinal and transverse differential conductivities exhibit periodic oscillations with the junction parameter $χ_t=χ_b$. These findings provide a fundamental understanding of field-free transverse responses in spin-momentum locked surface states, highlighting the potential of AM-TI heterojunctions for next-generation spintronic applications.

title: Calibrated concept profiles: making the reading of a model's neurons a measurement
text:
Title: Calibrated concept profiles: making the reading of a model's neurons a measurement
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Interpretability has largely moved from reading a model's neurons directly to reading a second model trained on the first: a probe, a sparse autoencoder, a crosscoder. The move answered real faults -- mixed meanings, thresholds without a unit, readings that did not transfer from one study to the next -- but gave up what a direct reading alone provides: nothing trained in between, the neurons themselves named, and a reading that can be repeated and compared. Here the direct reading is made a measurement. A neuron's activation varies with the prompt, so its reading is a distribution over a population of stimuli. We declare that population: every factor around a target construct is drawn at its rate in a reference corpus and logged. From the declared distribution we generate a battery of prompts, and draw it twice. From the battery we compute the calibrated concept profile, one number per neuron, stated in units of the neuron's own spread on ordinary input; the two draws give every number a noise unit. Before the profile is read, a fixed set of checks licenses the battery on the model, and the smallest change the profile can resolve across training checkpoints is measured. Realised for Python on OpenCoder-1.5B and followed across checkpoints spanning two trillion training tokens, the profile gives what the alternatives do not report: a unit on every number, a chance level for every comparison, and which neurons carry a construct at every checkpoint. The battery, the code and the data behind every result are released.

title: Optimal Actuator Support Design for Infinite-Horizon Linear-Quadratic Parabolic Control Problems
text:
Title: Optimal Actuator Support Design for Infinite-Horizon Linear-Quadratic Parabolic Control Problems
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study an optimal actuator design problem for infinite-horizon LQ control problems governed by parabolic equations. The control acts only on a small measurable subregion of the spatial domain, and the objective combines the infinite-horizon control value with a cost for the actuator region. Using the Riccati representation of the value function, we derive a comparison identity for two actuator supports and obtain an exact expansion of the objective. This leads to a topological derivative with respect to local changes in the support. We prove a localized Riccati sensitivity estimate to control the remainder and show that the infinite-horizon term in the derivative can be computed by solving a Lyapunov equation. This yields a computable support-update algorithm with a measure-controlled Armijo search. Under explicit uniform remainder and admissibility assumptions, its first-order stationarity defect tends to zero. Numerical experiments illustrate these results.

title: SkillDuet: Co-Evolving Models and Skills through Response Feedback
text:
Title: SkillDuet: Co-Evolving Models and Skills through Response Feedback
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

During reinforcement learning, experience can be both internalized in LLM parameters and retained externally as reusable textual skills. Parameter updates alter the model's behavior and the interaction experience from which new skills are extracted. These skills, in turn, guide the model's subsequent interactions and parameter updates. As the model's capabilities evolve, previously beneficial skills may become redundant or detrimental. We present SkillDuet, a framework that coordinates parameter updates and skill evolution through model response feedback. Skills extracted from on-policy trajectories guide parameter updates through OPD at every step. A response-based score, Strength, ranks candidate skills by the magnitude of the shift they induce in the current model's responses, and the highest-scoring skills are periodically consolidated into a persistent global skill set (Global). The updated model and Global jointly guide subsequent interactions, generating experience for further parameter and skill updates. With Qwen3-4B, SkillDuet achieves success rates of 98.57% on ALFWorld and 92.97% on WebShop, exceeding the matched SEED-API baseline by 2.86 and 5.47 percentage points, respectively. Ablations show that response-based skill selection and Global consolidation improve task performance. Further experiments show that the benefits of retained skills depend on both their content and their compatibility with the model. SkillDuet provides a concrete mechanism for model-skill co-evolution and skill-level recursive self-improvement.

title: Small-time Wasserstein action for KPZ and $Φ^4_3$
text:
Title: Small-time Wasserstein action for KPZ and $Φ^4_3$
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We determine the leading small-time Wasserstein action of the full spatial laws of centered KPZ and dynamical $Φ^4_3$, both started from zero. The leading term is Gaussian, with an explicit heat-trace constant. A common comparison also determines the ratio of length to displacement. For KPZ, a first-chaos cancellation yields a quadratic coupling error. For $Φ^4_3$, two weighted entropies and an adjoint estimate give comparison bounds uniform in the spectral cutoff. Integrating a Gaussian rotation gives a differentiable realization of the full law; the comparison holds at every positive time.

title: Elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals for orthogonal groups and Seiberg duality on the lens space
text:
Title: Elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals for orthogonal groups and Seiberg duality on the lens space
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We derive new transformation formulas for elliptic hypergeometric sum/integrals associated with the orthogonal groups $\mathrm{SO}(N)$. The sum/integrals are written in terms of the lens elliptic gamma function, which depends on an integer $r\geq 1$ in addition to the usual complex variables, and they reduce to the elliptic hypergeometric integrals of Spiridonov and Vartanov for $r=1$. The derivation uses the $BC_n\leftrightarrow BC_{\tilde n}$ transformation formula proven in our previous paper, together with a duplication formula for the lens elliptic gamma function proven here. The duplication formula takes a different form depending on whether $r$ is even or odd. Physically, the new transformations show that the supersymmetric lens indices on $S^1\times S^3/\mathbb{Z}_r$ of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ and $\mathrm{SO}(N_f-N+4)$ gauge theories related by Seiberg duality are equal for odd $r$. For even $r$, where the lens index depends on the global form of the gauge group, they show the equality of the contributions from flat connections whose holonomies lie in a common maximal torus. The $BC_n$ formula itself gives the corresponding statement for the symplectic groups.

title: Polynomial-time classical and quantum simulation of quantum impurity models
text:
Title: Polynomial-time classical and quantum simulation of quantum impurity models
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Quantum impurity models are paradigmatic models of interacting quantum matter, as well as key computational primitives for modern electronic-structure methods. They describe a small subsystem of interacting fermions coupled to a large, noninteracting bath. We perform a comprehensive study of the computational complexity of simulating impurity models, delineating the boundary between classical and quantum tractability for this class of problems. Our main finding is that static properties of quantum impurity models can be calculated efficiently on a classical computer. Specifically, we give classical algorithms that (1) estimate the ground-state energy to additive precision $δ$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,δ^{-1})$, and (2) estimate the partition function at inverse temperature $β$ to relative precision $δ$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,β,δ^{-1})$, where $n$ is the system size. These results improve the previous best-known complexity for ground-state energy estimation from quasipolynomial to polynomial time, while establishing for the first time rigorous polynomial-time guarantees for simulating impurity models in thermal equilibrium. On the other hand, we find that simulating dynamical properties of impurity models is hard for classical computers but easy on a quantum computer. As a canonical example, we show that computing their nonequilibrium Green's functions captures the full power of quantum computation, even at finite temperature. Taken together, our results rule out superpolynomial quantum speedups for computing static properties, but provide an avenue for quantum advantage in simulating impurity physics out of equilibrium.

title: A Preconditioned Semismooth Newton Method for Box-Constrained Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Random Coefficients
text:
Title: A Preconditioned Semismooth Newton Method for Box-Constrained Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Random Coefficients
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We consider the optimal control problem of an elliptic PDE with random diffusion under pointwise box constraints on the control. The constraints make the optimality conditions nonsmooth, with an active set that is not known in advance, and the random diffusion couples the state and the adjoint across all stochastic modes. To design a solution algorithm for this problem, we rely on the Fenchel duality viewpoint. Fenchel duality absorbs the box constraint into the objective and yields an exact reduced problem in the elliptic adjoint variable alone. After a stochastic Galerkin--finite element discretization, eliminating the state leaves a strongly monotone, piecewise smooth equation, which we solve directly by a matrix-free semismooth Newton method with the box projection retained exactly and with no outer iteration, penalty or smoothing parameter. Next, we introduce and analyze a current-set preconditioner, which adds the active-set correction of the current Newton step to a mean-diffusion reference operator and is inverted exactly by a rank-1 update. For implementation, we use a cheaper preconditioner that keeps only a fraction of free control values. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence of the state, and Newton and PCG counts that stay bounded under mesh refinement and growth of the stochastic dimension.

title: MS-MLB: An Open Machine Learning Benchmark for Blood-Based MS Classification
text:
Title: MS-MLB: An Open Machine Learning Benchmark for Blood-Based MS Classification
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Multiple sclerosis (MS) is diagnosed through clinical assessment, magnetic resonance imaging, laboratory evidence when appropriate, and exclusion of better explanations. Blood RNA expression data may contain disease associated immune signal, but a blood RNA classifier cannot be treated as a replacement for clinical diagnosis. This paper presents MS-MLB (Multiple Sclerosis Machine Learning Benchmark), a reproducible open benchmark for machine learning based MS research classification from whole blood RNA expression data. MS-MLB uses the public GSE17048 cohort, converts it into an MS versus healthy control task, and evaluates multiple algorithms under a shared, leakage controlled pipeline that a researcher can rerun without reconfiguring the evaluation. The evaluation includes nested cross-validation, an untouched stratified holdout set, bootstrap confidence intervals, ROC and precision recall analysis, calibration measurement, and an exploratory MS Research Score. In the final benchmark summary, Gradient Boosting ranked first by MS Research Score on the holdout set, with an MS Research Score of 93.83, AUC-ROC of 0.989, sensitivity of 0.950, specificity of 0.778, $F_{1}$ score of 0.927, and Brier score of 0.050. Prior studies have applied machine learning to MS blood transcriptomic data, including PBMC stage classification and whole blood diagnostic signature modeling. The contribution here is different and narrower. To our knowledge, MS-MLB is the first open benchmark focused on MS versus healthy control classification from GSE17048 whole blood RNA expression data with a documented external model submission pathway built into the framework. The score is intended for research comparison only and has not been clinically validated. The benchmark is accessible here: https://github.com/duckyquang/MS-MLB.

title: ORCHID: Connecting Finite-Temperature Thermodynamic Evidence to Computational Materials Discovery
text:
Title: ORCHID: Connecting Finite-Temperature Thermodynamic Evidence to Computational Materials Discovery
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Finite-temperature phase stability is essential to materials discovery, but the evidence needed to describe it remains scattered across decades of literature. ORCHID organizes this evidence around the thermodynamic states that the observations describe, using tiered agentic extraction guided by thermodynamic rules, expert supervision and explicit validation. The collection contains 73,542 values from 1,321 papers, represented with their thermodynamic states, phase identities, provenance, evidence classes and uncertainty, together with assessed phase assemblages and calculated references. A qualified subset is released in ESPEI-compatible form for CALPHAD assessment, and machine-readable access supports both human and AI-assisted reuse. Blind expert evaluation of 48 diagram fields gives 93.8% agreement, increasing to 97.9% after accounting for notation conventions. On a common formation-enthalpy benchmark, eight MLIPs show residual spreads close to their DFT reference, motivating evaluation of finite-temperature phase stability through PhaseForge. One-shot MLIP-PhaseForge descriptions of Cu-Zr recover 0.35-0.56 of observed phase occurrences at assessed field points. ORCHID-assisted refinement through PhaseForge+ recovers 9 of 13 invariant temperatures within 2 sigma and reduces held-out activity error from 5.1 to 1.7 kJ/mol. By supplying interpreted literature evidence directly to gradient-based refinement through PhaseForge+, ORCHID connects evidence recovery to programmatic CALPHAD assessment. With the initial description and fitting datasets prepared, the final Cu-Zr refinement completes in approximately 27 minutes, providing a foundation for continuously updated thermodynamic models and their use in materials discovery.

title: Adaptive Protocol for Rényi Entropy Estimation
text:
Title: Adaptive Protocol for Rényi Entropy Estimation
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The second-order Rényi entropy is one of the most important quantities used for characterizing the entanglement structure of states prepared in quantum many-body experiments. With access to qubit projective measurement data, it can be estimated via a protocol in which repeated measurements are taken after each of a set of random local unitary operations is applied to the quantum state. To obtain accurate values for the second Rényi entropy on shot-limited devices, care must be taken when choosing the number of different unitary settings to apply, and the respective number of projective measurements to take. In this paper, we propose an adaptive protocol for estimating the Rényi entropy that iteratively optimizes the ratio of basis settings to measurements, using a gradient-based approach and starting from an initial small set of measurements. Using synthetic data, we demonstrate that for several prototypical states, our method converges to values for this ratio that are comparable to the optimal values obtained by a brute-force grid search, and it exhibits slower growth of the measurement budget required for a fixed target accuracy than fixed-ratio protocols. Our adaptive protocol therefore promotes efficient estimation of the Rényi entropy in finite-size, shot-limited quantum experiments by making effective use of the available measurement budget.

title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
text:
Title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Formal world models can support planning, verification, and safety reasoning, but constructing them from open-ended natural-language situations is difficult, particularly in multi-agent settings where several formalizations may be plausible. We study whether five LLMs can generate such world models as partially observable stochastic games and whether mechanical validity is sufficient to establish that the resulting model faithfully represents the intended decision problem. We introduce a benchmark of 44 scenarios spanning game, situational, and cultural settings and evaluate generated world models along three dimensions: mechanical validity, reference-relative structural agreement, and semantic criteria. Across three empirical tracks, we analyze 410 first-pass generations. In the reference-backed game track, 134/135 generated world models pass a strict mechanical audit, yet mean permutation-invariant structural F1 is only 0.366, with just 28/134 mechanically valid models exactly matching the authored reference. In the cultural track, explicitly naming the country changes the generated structural representation for most LLMs while producing only small changes in automated semantic scores. These results show that executability is a necessary but insufficient criterion for LLM-generated world models: models that are mechanically valid can still differ substantially in the structure used by downstream neuro-symbolic reasoning and planning.

title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
text:
Title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Real materials consist of multiple stable or metastable states under real-world conditions, existing as statistical ergodic ensembles of configurations rather than ideal crystals. Yet, data-driven computational materials discovery increasingly biases itself toward finding "new stable structures" from ground-state DFT calculations alone. This limits our long-term ability to discover materials whose properties emerge from metastable phases, to explain experimental observations, or to model thermodynamic behavior comprehensively. Predicting ergodic sets of atomic configurations of known and hypothetical solids is a fundamental challenge in theoretical crystallography, approached via many complementary methods. We discuss this conceptually and introduce crystALL, a pragmatic and powerful data-driven approach to discovering ensembles beyond the convex hull, embracing structural diversity over stability alone, enabling robust experiment matching in cases evading traditional methods. crystALL leverages 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD to rapidly generate a comprehensive candidate set by: (1) species substitutions; (2) ML feature-space analysis with pySIPFENN; (3) representative structure selection via clustering and energy-minimization or property matching; and (4) construction of the final candidate ensemble for experimental or ab initio validation. We also uniquely address the common challenge of experimental composition uncertainties spanning many integer stoichiometries by new efficient searches across anonymized compositional ranges rather than fixed formulas. Overall, crystALL's ensemble-focused philosophy provides critical advantages over the prevailing convex-hull-searching paradigm, which often fails to account for key experimental observations and increases AI/ML discovery bias over time - akin to model collapse in LLMs retrained on iteratively generated content.

title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
text:
Title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Ammonium thiocyanate (NH4SCN) has been used extensively to improve the current extraction and device performance of quasi-two-dimensional perovskite solar cells. Whilst this additive has been shown to influence quasi-2D perovskite crystallisation, a detailed understanding of its mechanism has not yet been established. Through spectroscopic and structural studies, we demonstrate that NH4SCN enables quasi-2D perovskite phases to structurally template the dominant 3D phase. Contrary to previous reports, we suggest that the benefit of this additive comes from an improvement to the 3D perovskite structure, not from charges transferring through vertically oriented 2D perovskite layers. We show that this additive provides kinetic control over the quasi-2D phase formation, suppressing the unfavourable n = 1 perovskite phase and promoting the growth of high-n 2D scaffold phases by extending the nucleation window. This promotes the in-situ templated growth of MAPbI3. We provide robust structural analysis demonstrating highly (110)-ordered 3D perovskite, with the mechanism confirmed by close lattice matching between this phase and quasi-2D phases. Furthermore, we show that this structural control is cation dependent, requiring both close lattice matching between quasi-2D and 3D perovskite phases, and successful kinetic control of the relevant quasi-2D phases.

title: PEtab SciML: an exchange format for specifying and training dynamic scientific machine learning models
text:
Title: PEtab SciML: an exchange format for specifying and training dynamic scientific machine learning models
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Summary: Dynamic scientific machine learning (SciML) models that combine mechanistic ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with machine learning (ML) components have applications ranging from learning unknown biological processes to integrating auxiliary data modalities into dynamic modelling. To enable reproducible and efficient SciML training, we introduce PEtab SciML, an interoperable data format for specifying parameter estimation problems in which mechanistic and ML model parameters are jointly estimated from time series data. PEtab SciML supports several ML ODE hybridization patterns in realistic problem setups. It is accompanied by a reference Python library and downstream modelling support in Python/JAX and Julia, provided by AMICI and PEtab$.$jl, respectively, and a collection of real data benchmarks. Availability and implementation: PEtab SciML is available on GitHub (https://github.com/PEtab-dev/petab_sciml). The reference Python package is installable from PyPI and is continuously tested and supported on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

title: SuperWIMPs in the Kination Era: Imprints on $N_{\rm eff}$ and CMB Spectral Distortions
text:
