These embeddings are reduced to a two-dimensional space to visualize DNA hybridization and toehold-mediated strand displacement reactions. ViDa preserves structure and clusters trajectory ensembles into reaction pathways, making simulation results more interpretable and revealing new mechanistic insights. In the second part, we address key challenges in cryo-EM density map interpretation and protein structure modeling. We provide a comprehensive review and benchmarking of deep learning methods for atomic model building, with improved evaluation metrics and practical guidance. We then present Struc2mapGAN, a generative adversarial network that synthesizes high-fidelity experimental-like cryo-EM density maps from protein structures. Finally, we present CryoSAMU, a structure-aware multimodal U-Net that enhances intermediate-resolution cryo-EM maps by integrating density features with structural embeddings from protein language models via cross-attention. Overall, these contributions demonstrate the potential of deep generative models to interpret DNA reaction mechanisms and advance cryo-EM density map analysis and protein structure modeling.

title: Learning the Shared Latent Structure of Cryo-EM Inverse Problems
text:
Title: Learning the Shared Latent Structure of Cryo-EM Inverse Problems
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Understanding biomolecular function requires characterizing three-dimensional structure and conformational variability, for which cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is a powerful tool. Cryo-EM produces noisy two-dimensional particle images in which molecular structure, particle pose, and imaging conditions are jointly encoded. Recovering biological information from these observations spans inverse problems including pose estimation, heterogeneity analysis, and reconstruction. These tasks are usually addressed independently despite shared protein structure and image formation, motivating a common representation across inverse problems. Since biologically meaningful differences may be spatially localized, we study self-distillation with complementary global and masked patch objectives. Because experimental dataset discrimination can reflect acquisition-specific cues, we develop controlled synthetic and experimental evaluations and find that structural discrimination benefits from dense spatial features. We introduce the EMber family of vision transformers, pre-trained on >50 million experimental particle images from 214 EMPIAR datasets together with simulated projections from 268,000 molecular assemblies. EMber improves upon existing methods at conformational and compositional discrimination by 14.85 and 14.26 percentage points, estimates conformational populations to within 1.59pp error with a linear probe, and produces particle assignments yielding reference-quality reconstructions in fewer epochs. We demonstrate how to learn representations that capture biological information for use across multiple cryo-EM inverse problems.

title: CADS: Measuring the Incremental Contribution of LLM Proposers in Sequential Biological Screens
text:
Title: CADS: Measuring the Incremental Contribution of LLM Proposers in Sequential Biological Screens
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Large language models are increasingly used to guide sequential biological screens, yet standard evaluations rely on raw hit counts that conflate a proposer's value with the discovery capacity of the underlying algorithmic harness. Adaptive sampling and corrupted experimental readouts also leave standard feedback comparisons without a false-discovery guarantee. We present Certified Agentic Discovery Screens (CADS), an error-controlled measurement framework that quantifies a proposer's incremental value against an identical LLM-free loop. By integrating capped likelihood-ratio bounds, e-processes, and complete-family e-BH, CADS controls the terminal false discovery rate under the stated null and corruption conditions despite arbitrary dependence, adaptive sampling, and optional stopping. In DepMap-backed simulations, CADS exposes two evaluation artifacts: the LLM-free harness alone clears the feedback gate, and raw origin counts overstate LLM contributions because LLM picks displace fallback discoveries. On the initial 20 seeds, supplying tested-candidate history to Qwen2.5-7B shifts its net contribution from +0.35, with a 95% interval covering zero, to +2.90, with the interval above zero. This initial net effect did not persist in a 50-seed matched-quota replication. These results support net gain over an LLM-free loop, measured between separately certified sets, as the appropriate measure of proposer contribution.

title: A Geometric Journey Through the Aharonov--Bohm Effect: Tonomura's Toroid, Pseudoscalar Phase, and Quantum Holonomy in Clifford Algebra
text:
Title: A Geometric Journey Through the Aharonov--Bohm Effect: Tonomura's Toroid, Pseudoscalar Phase, and Quantum Holonomy in Clifford Algebra
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The magnetic Aharonov--Bohm (AB) effect is often introduced through the idealised infinite solenoid and a complex scalar phase. We give a geometric-algebra formulation based on the compact toroidal magnets shielded by a superconductor employed in the electron-holography experiments of Tonomura and collaborators. Working in the real Euclidean Clifford algebra $ \mathrm{Cl}(3,0)$, we distinguish the unit volume pseudoscalar $I$ (grade 3), coordinate angles (scalars, grade 0), tangent vectors (grade 1), and directed surface bivectors (grade 2). The magnetic field is represented by the dual bivector $\mathcal{B}= I \mathbf B$, while the electromagnetic $U(1)$ phase is represented by the central unit multivector $e^{Iα}$ generated by the pseudoscalar $I$, rather than by a spatial rotor with a bivector generator. We establish the linked toroidal geometry, formulate magnetic flux and Stokes' theorem intrinsically in geometric algebra, and derive the holonomy element $U_Γ=\exp(IqΦ_B/\hbar)$ from $U(1)$ gauge covariance, with every sign fixed explicitly. We then express superconducting fluxoid quantization in the same notation and obtain the binary electron holonomy $U_Γ= (-1)^N$ in the ideal limit where the linked magnetic flux equals $N h/(2e)$. Finally, a short conditional-state description of the quantum source and field shows how a backreaction can introduce an additional phase and reduce interference visibility. The conditional-state overlap is represented by a central scalar--pseudoscalar element; preservation of the fluxoid sector alone does not guarantee unit coherence.

title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
text:
Title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. Its single instrument provides diffraction-limited visible imaging (~0.15 arcsec in the optical) together with simultaneous near-infrared (R ~ 100) slitless spectrophotometry, so that every detected source is observed in the NIR by the survey itself, with spectral information delivered at a resolution set by its brightness (full R ~ 100 typing at the bright end, synthetic medium-band or broadband photometry below it) and with no separate follow-up, a capability decisive for time-domain science. With it, KST addresses the three outstanding questions of dark physics in concert: the dynamics of dark energy, the nature of dark matter, and gravitational-wave dark sirens as independent cosmological rulers. KST combines measurements of expansion and structure growth to test dark-energy models. A two-tiered "Wedding Cake" strategy (2,000 deg^2 Wide plus 10 deg^2 cluster-targeted Deep Survey) combines weak lensing, baryon acoustic oscillations, and a near-infrared-standardized Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram to constrain dark energy at its pivot redshift (sigma(w_p) ~ 0.03); maps dark matter from cluster cores to galactic substructure to test cold dark matter against warm and self-interacting alternatives; and builds a deep near-infrared host catalog for a distance-ladder-independent H_0 from dark sirens. The same data yield a Legacy Science portfolio (galaxy evolution, active galactic nuclei, exoplanets, and the Milky Way) at no additional observing cost. As Korea's first dedicated astrophysics space mission, KST occupies a niche complementary to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Euclid, and Roman.

title: Estimating Irving-Kirkwood pressure profiles from per-atom virial and density profiles: a closure for the contour-dependent term in planar liquid films
text:
Title: Estimating Irving-Kirkwood pressure profiles from per-atom virial and density profiles: a closure for the contour-dependent term in planar liquid films
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

The local pressure tensor of an inhomogeneous fluid is not unique. Two tangential profiles are in common use in planar simulations: the Irving-Kirkwood (IK) profile, which requires a dedicated pass over every pair of atoms for every slab, and the per-atom virial (PAV) profile, which molecular-dynamics codes produce at negligible cost and coincides with the Harasima contour. The two differ by the derivative of a pair quantity, P_T^IK - P_T^PAV = dQ/dz. We show that, for Lennard-Jones free-standing films, Q(z) can be predicted from the density profile and the bulk radial distribution function of the coexisting liquid: under the closure rho2(r1,r2) ~ rho(z1) rho(z2) g(r12), with a pair-local interpolation of g between its liquid and dilute limits, Q is a double integral of rho(z) against a kernel built from u'(r) g(r). The estimator P_T^IK,est = P_T^PAV + dQ/dz is tested against IK profiles measured on the same trajectories for 20 films (thicknesses 7-25 sigma, three cutoff radii, two temperatures): the root-mean-square residual is 0.001-0.002 epsilon/sigma^3, against 0.010-0.021 for the uncorrected profile, and Q, the amount that the contour choice transfers between the two interfaces of a film with non-equivalent surfaces, is recovered to within 0.6% of the surface tension. Applied to the normal component, the same closure removes 83-92% of the spurious structure of the per-atom zz profile, a test that needs no IK run. Its mixture form is validated on three two-component films with an adsorbate unequally distributed between their faces, where it resolves the tension of each face; a clean face recovers the tension of the pure film.

title: Interpreting Protein Language Model Embeddings via Orthogonal Projection for Protein Fitness Prediction
text:
Title: Interpreting Protein Language Model Embeddings via Orthogonal Projection for Protein Fitness Prediction
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Recently, there has been a growing adoption of protein language models (PLMs) in biomedical science. Their embeddings provide a rich numerical representation of protein sequences which achieve state-of-the-art performance on several downstream tasks including protein fitness prediction. However, PLM embeddings are not directly interpretable and, thereby, it remains unclear what features they encode. To gain insight into which biochemical properties of the protein are driving the prediction, we leverage an orthogonal projection technique that removes linear effects of known tabular features from embeddings and extend it to high-order and interaction effects. In this way, we remove the effects of interpretable biochemical features from PLM embeddings. In an ablation study, we show that this leads to a decrease in performance for a downstream classifier trained only on the embeddings to predict protein fitness. In an additional evaluation, we find that these biochemical features explain a substantial part of the variance in the predictions of this classifier. Hence, we can show that PLM embeddings encode patterns correlated with biochemical properties and quantify their contribution to predicting protein fitness. This computationally efficient approach is not limited to the features or embeddings considered here and is readily transferable to problem settings beyond protein fitness prediction.

title: A Unified Framework for Bell-Shaped Gaussian Quadratures in Deterministic Boltzmann Solvers
text:
Title: A Unified Framework for Bell-Shaped Gaussian Quadratures in Deterministic Boltzmann Solvers
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

In this work, we develop a unified theoretical framework that constructs Bell-shaped Gaussian quadratures for deterministic Boltzmann solvers. The proposed framework establishes a general class of bell-shaped weight functions together with the corresponding integral transformations, revealing the common mathematical structure underlying existing generalized Gaussian quadratures. Based on this framework, a unified procedure for constructing discrete velocity sets is developed by combining radial quadratures with appropriate directional quadratures in different velocity-space dimensions. Several existing generalized Gaussian quadratures are naturally recovered as special cases, while the proposed framework provides a systematic route for constructing new quadrature rules based on different bell-shaped weight functions. Extensive benchmark simulations over a broad range of flow regimes demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high integration accuracy and computational efficiency with significantly fewer discrete velocities than conventional quadrature strategies. Overall, the proposed framework not only unifies existing generalized Gaussian quadratures under a common mathematical foundation but also establishes a general design principle for the systematic development of efficient velocity-space quadratures in deterministic Boltzmann solvers.

title: Nearly Linear-Time Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader for Weakly Observable Graph Bandits
text:
Title: Nearly Linear-Time Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader for Weakly Observable Graph Bandits
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We study online learning with directed weakly observable feedback graphs and propose a Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader (FTPL) policy that achieves best-of-both-worlds guarantee with nearly linear expected time complexity. To preserve the simple structure of FTPL, we develop a novel graph-based loss estimator that combines forced exploration, conditional geometric resampling and adaptive learning rates with surrogate probabilities. Our policy achieves $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(δ_*^{1/3} T^{2/3})$ regret for adversarial regimes as well as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(δ_* \log T / Δ_{\min}^2)$ regret for stochastic regimes, where $δ_*$ and $Δ$, respectively, denote the fractional weak domination number and the suboptimality gap. These results show that refined guarantees for problems with minimax regret of $Θ(T^{2/3})$ can be obtained through appropriately designed adaptive learning rates and loss estimators without sacrificing the simplicity of FTPL.

title: A Technique to Model Product Information and User Reviews (MPIUR)
text:
Title: A Technique to Model Product Information and User Reviews (MPIUR)
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Modern e-commerce platforms naturally provide three complementary modalities: textual item descriptions, item images, and user reviews. However, existing multimodal recommendation methods often omit reviews or do not integrate all three modalities within a unified framework. In this paper, we propose MPIUR, a multimodal graph-based recommendation model that encodes reviews in heterogeneous graphs, aligns image and text representations, and adapts collaborative--semantic alignment to item interaction density. Experiments on the Amazon Reviews 2023 Musical Instruments and Baby categories show that MPIUR achieves the best global nDCG@10 and Recall@10 among the evaluated methods on both datasets. It also obtains the best nDCG@10 and Recall@10 on sparse items, indicating that jointly exploiting reviews and multimodal item content is particularly useful when interaction histories are limited.

title: Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks with Uncertain and State-Dependent Couplings
text:
Title: Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks with Uncertain and State-Dependent Couplings
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Phase locking in oscillator networks depends critically on the interaction strengths between coupled units. In many applications, however, these couplings are uncertain, state dependent, or time varying. We derive rigorous conditions for phase locking in Kuramoto-type networks when each coupling strength is known only within prescribed bounds. Building on a convex formulation of the nonlinear fixed-point equations, we obtain edge-wise error bounds for arbitrary feasible approximations that hold uniformly over all admissible couplings. These bounds yield sufficient conditions for the existence of phase-locked states with prescribed phase-difference limits. We illustrate the framework for AC power grids with uncertain voltage magnitudes and adaptive oscillator networks with state-dependent couplings. For the latter, the bounds can be further tightened by exploiting the state dependence of the couplings.

title: AutoQS: Automated Quantization Strategy Design with Large Language Models
text:
Title: AutoQS: Automated Quantization Strategy Design with Large Language Models
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Quantization reduces LLM deployment costs, but effective strategies must balance model quality and storage. LLM-driven search can automate strategy design through repeated proposal and evaluation. This process must identify useful strategies within a limited evaluation budget. The key challenge is that \textit{actual quantization is expensive, while inexpensive proxies may not reflect quantized-model performance.} To address this challenge, we present AutoQS, an \textbf{Auto}mated \textbf{Q}uantization \textbf{S}trategy Design with LLMs. AutoQS keeps weight precision fixed and searches group-size allocations across layers and operators under deployment constraints. Evaluation history guides coordinated LLM proposals, while deterministic validation ensures compatible allocations. An inexpensive quality proxy evaluates candidates, and an candidate repository retains alternative allocations to inform subsequent proposals. Periodic actual quantization complements these proxy evaluations with measured quality and checkpoint storage, providing feedback for further search within the evaluation budget. Experiments on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct show that AutoQS improves seven-task average accuracy over uniform-group GPTQ and AWQ by 0.70 and 1.12 percentage points, respectively, at four-bit weight precision.

title: SHIFT-Truck: A High-Fidelity Aerodynamics Dataset and Benchmark for Pickup Trucks
text:
Title: SHIFT-Truck: A High-Fidelity Aerodynamics Dataset and Benchmark for Pickup Trucks
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Pickup trucks account for 14% of new light-duty vehicles produced in the United States, yet are among the least aerodynamic. Their open cargo bed adds a flow absent from existing automotive aerodynamics datasets such as DrivAerML and SHIFT-SUV: the shear layer leaving the cab roof passes over a recirculating bed flow before separating again at the tailgate. The resulting drag lowers fuel efficiency, raises emissions and limits the range of electric trucks. Scale-resolved Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is too costly for broad design exploration; neural surrogates can predict flow features at a fraction of that cost, provided they are trained on large-scale, high-fidelity, domain-specific data. We introduce SHIFT-Truck, the first such dataset for pickup trucks. It comprises 1,000 Spalart-Allmaras delayed detached-eddy simulations (SA-DDES) of a reference pickup geometry morphed across 17 shape parameters. Each case is run on a mesh of about 100 million cells at a Reynolds number of $1.4 \times 10^7$ and released with time-averaged surface pressure, wall shear stress, volumetric pressure and velocity. The setup is verified by grid refinement and repeated runs, and checked against wind-tunnel measurements. We define geometry-grouped splits and benchmark four neural surrogates, DoMINO, GeoTransolver, AB-UPT and SMART, on surface and volume tracks. SHIFT-Truck also introduces controlled distribution shifts in the operating point, the input surface discretization and the vehicle archetype. Models with strong in-distribution performance can degrade substantially under these shifts: operating-condition changes expose failures to infer speed dependence, while tessellation and cross-vehicle shifts reveal markedly different robustness across architectures. SHIFT-Truck is thus a benchmark not only for surrogate accuracy but also for generalization across physical and numerical distributions.

title: Semiclassical Asymptotics of Entanglement in Torus-Link States
text:
Title: Semiclassical Asymptotics of Entanglement in Torus-Link States
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

We investigate the entanglement entropy of topological quantum states associated with $T_{d,\,dn}$ torus links in (2+1)-dimensional SU(2) Chern--Simons theory at level $k$. These links consist of $d$ components with pairwise linking number $n$, and the corresponding link-complement states provide a natural setting to study multipartite entanglement in topological quantum field theories. We analyze the semiclassical limit $k\to\infty$ of the entanglement entropy by deriving the asymptotic behavior of the moments of the reduced density matrix. To achieve this, we decompose the integrable-representation space into left-edge, right-edge, and bulk regions and employ the stationary-phase method to evaluate their respective contributions. We find that the leading asymptotic behavior is governed entirely by the two edge regions, while the bulk contribution is asymptotically suppressed. The resulting expression for the limiting entanglement entropy is given in terms of Hurwitz zeta functions and exhibits a dependence on the residue class of $k$ modulo $n$. We further investigate the dependence of the limiting entanglement entropy on the winding parameter $n$ and the number of link components $d$. In the large-$d$ limit, the entropy reduces to a binary entropy determined by two normalized weights associated with the left and right edges. Finally, we show that the two iterated limits, $k\to\infty$ and $d\to\infty$, commute, reproducing the result obtained previously by taking the large-party limit first.

title: DUO: Dual Readouts of Diffusion Models for OOD Detection
text:
Title: DUO: Dual Readouts of Diffusion Models for OOD Detection
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Diffusion models are powerful generative methods for learning and sampling from complex data distributions. Safely deploying these models requires detecting inputs that fall outside their training distribution. Because diffusion models recover clean samples from noisy inputs, reconstruction error is often used for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. This approach assumes that in-distribution (ID) inputs are reconstructed more accurately than OOD inputs. However, OOD inputs may be reconstructed equally well or even better, making this score unreliable. We therefore propose the leading sensitivity spectrum of intermediate denoising features as a complementary OOD signal and demonstrate that it remains informative when reconstruction error is misleading. We introduce DUal-readout of diffusion models for OOD detection (DUO), a fully unsupervised, training-free OOD detector that combines reconstruction error and feature sensitivity. DUO improves average AUROC by approximately 6% points over the strongest baselines while substantially reducing inference cost, and achieves SOTA on near-OOD and high-resolution benchmarks.

title: A geometry-aware framework for electromagnetic fields in GATE 10
text:
Title: A geometry-aware framework for electromagnetic fields in GATE 10
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Objective. An increasing number of medical-physics applications require the modelling of charged-particle transport in electromagnetic (EM) fields. We aim to provide GATE 10 users with a flexible mechanism for defining such fields in Monte Carlo simulations while preserving the native Geant4 particle-transport machinery. Approach. Our framework separates the handling of coordinates from EM field evaluation. Fields are attached to geometry volumes, defined in their local frame, and represented by analytic expressions, field maps, or arbitrary Python functions. They automatically follow the position and orientation of these volumes, including in nested and dynamic geometries. We validated the framework against native Geant4 transport and tested coordinate transformations, nested volumes, and dynamic geometry. We also compared the computational cost of the three field representations. Main results. The framework reproduced the native Geant4 trajectories exactly for all tested field types with direct Geant4 counterparts. Coordinate transformations introduced only floating-point-level differences, while simulations with dynamically changing geometry reproduced the equivalent static configurations exactly. All three representations produced equivalent transport. Mapped fields added at most 18% to the single-threaded runtime of analytic fields, while Python functions required 6.9 times as much. The compiled representations scaled with the number of threads, whereas Python functions became slower as threads were added. Significance. The framework adds flexible, geometry-aware EM field definitions to GATE 10 without modifying the underlying Geant4 transport machinery, and is part of the open-source GATE 10 codebase. It also provides a basis for extending GATE 10 with additional field representations in the future.

title: An immune world model for multiscale forecasting and therapeutic hypothesis generation
text:
Title: An immune world model for multiscale forecasting and therapeutic hypothesis generation
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Immune therapies act across cell-intrinsic programs, tissue ecosystems, and patient-specific immune states, yet most predictors address these scales separately. We used a governed evolutionary AI Scientist to construct the Immune World Model, an action-conditioned model that learns how interventions move immune states across cellular, tissue, and individual levels. The Immune World Model--building Scientist searched candidate architectures and workflows, and the resulting world model was frozen before independent confirmation. The frozen model generalized to unseen interventions and biological contexts, recovered intervention-specific cellular programs, integrated cell and tissue information to improve ecosystem and patient-response prediction, and forecast unseen perturbation combinations. Immune World Model--guided analysis then combined measured perturbations with cross-axis inference to nominate IL-36$γ$ plus SIRP$α$ inhibition as a complementary-axis therapeutic hypothesis, whereas a governed self-correction audit rejected every screened cytokine pair. The Immune World Model provides a framework for multiscale immune simulation that connects AI Scientist-driven model construction, intervention forecasting, and the generation of prospectively testable therapeutic hypotheses.

title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
text:
Title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Bayesian optimization is widely used in active learning loops for materials science. Gaussian processes serve as the de-facto surrogate model family, but require task-dependent kernel choices and can lack the modeling capacity for complex relationships. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have recently emerged as the state-of-the-art for predictive tasks on structured data, without requiring bespoke kernels or hyperparameter tuning. We evaluate two TFMs, TabPFN and TabICL, as out-of-the-box surrogate models on two standard materials science benchmarks, comparing against a large field of baselines encompassing Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost. Our findings indicate that TFMs are highly competitive surrogate models across the two benchmarks, without task-specific training for active learning or GP kernel selection. Our results motivate developing TFMs further as surrogates for active learning in materials discovery.

title: Shaping Useful Noise: Energy Distributions Predict Visual Pretraining Quality
text:
Title: Shaping Useful Noise: Energy Distributions Predict Visual Pretraining Quality
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Synthetic data can scale visual pretraining, but current selection criteria only partially explain which datasets train strong representations. We propose using the energy profile of a dataset--the distribution of log-probability levels it occupies under a normalised real-image density model--as an audit and curation principle for synthetic data. To operationalise this view, we introduce Energy-Level Distribution Distance (ELD), which compares real and synthetic energy distributions. Real images span sparse high-likelihood scenes and dense low-likelihood textures, so useful synthetic data should cover this energy range rather than collapse to likely but low-variation samples. Across diverse synthetic datasets, ELD exposes mismatches missed by FID and predicts pretraining performance beyond FID, LPIPS variation, and feature-space recall, including across CNN and ViT self-supervised settings. We then use ELD to resample and mix synthetic sources, matching the real-image energy histogram while preserving diversity and improving downstream transfer.

title: ShopMind: A Mental World Model for Personalized and Realistic E-commerce User Simulation
text:
Title: ShopMind: A Mental World Model for Personalized and Realistic E-commerce User Simulation
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Large language models are widely used in e-commerce user simulation, providing a foundation for understanding users and predicting human decisions. However, existing simulators still struggle to achieve both personalization and behavioral realism. Most methods predict the next action directly from interaction histories and the current context, without accounting for the evolving mental world that underlies user behavior. Theory of Mind suggests that behavior is driven by mental states, including beliefs, uncertainties, and intentions. Users may interpret the same information in distinct ways, leading to divergent behaviors, while an individual's mental state evolves through interaction and shapes subsequent actions. Ignoring this process prevents simulators from faithfully capturing individual differences and realistic behavior patterns, and undermines its effectiveness in downstream applications. To address this, we propose ShopMind, a Mental World Model for e-commerce user simulation that captures how consumers interpret shopping information and how their mental states evolve, better reflecting individual users and real-world behavior patterns. We further use behavior-mental state pairs synthesized by ShopMind to train a Mental State Reconstruction (MSR) model, which infers consumers' latent mental states from observable behavior. Experiments show that ShopMind improves personalization by 18.0% and behavioral realism by 19.6% over the strongest alternatives. Moreover, MSR improves performance on consumption value measurement and CTR prediction, showing the utility of ShopMind for understanding and predicting real user behavior.

title: Recovering Irreducible Three-Body Interactions with Lagrangian Neural Networks
text:
Title: Recovering Irreducible Three-Body Interactions with Lagrangian Neural Networks
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) learn mechanical systems from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar Lagrangian and deriving the dynamics through the Euler-Lagrange equations, biasing the model toward motion that respects the variational structure of mechanics. The interactions studied so far have been pairwise-additive, leaving open whether LNNs can recover an irreducible many-body interaction from motion alone. We address this using the Axilrod-Teller triple-dipole interaction, the leading three-body dispersion term, whose dependence on the collective geometry of three particles cannot be represented by any sum of pairwise terms. We prescribe the kinetic energy exactly and learn only the potential, as a function of interparticle distances and angles. Combined with a signal-aware sampling strategy that concentrates training data where the three-body signal is strongest while preserving broad coverage of configuration space, this recovers the interaction from accelerations alone. The learned potential reproduces the radial scaling, angular dependence, and characteristic sign reversal of the Axilrod-Teller interaction, and generates stable trajectories. Embedding it within a pairwise Lennard-Jones potential lets us examine its observability: the three-body term is recovered once its dynamical signature exceeds the residual modeling error, which it does cleanly at amplified coupling but not at the coupling of a real noble gas, bracketing the transition between the two. Finally, symbolic regression on the trained potential, with no assumed functional form, returns the Axilrod-Teller expression with angular numerator, radial law, and coupling constant intact. An LNN with domain-specific structure can thus recover an irreducible three-body interaction from trajectories as a closed-form law, pointing toward learning interaction laws whose structure is not known a priori.

title: Gravitational Production of Non-minimally Coupled Vector Dark Matter in Warm Inflation
text:
Title: Gravitational Production of Non-minimally Coupled Vector Dark Matter in Warm Inflation
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We study the purely gravitational production of a massive vector dark matter with a non-minimal coupling to the Einstein tensor, $ξG_{μν}X^μX^ν$, in warm inflation. The background, $V=λφ^4$ with a dissipation coefficient linear in temperature, is constrained by CMB observations and parametrized by the dissipation ratio $10^{-4}\le Q_0\le1$. We consider both unavoidable production channels: freeze-in from the Standard Model bath through graviton exchange, and cosmological gravitational particle production (CGPP). For freeze-in, we compute the scattering amplitudes including the contact interaction induced by $ξ$, which enhances the production of light dark matter through the longitudinal mode and suppresses that of heavy dark matter through destructive interference. For CGPP, the slow-roll parameter is not small during warm inflation, which enhances the production of light dark matter by up to three orders of magnitude relative to cold inflation. Combining both channels, CGPP excludes most of the light freeze-in branch, leaving $m_X\lesssim2.4\times10^{-5}$ GeV, a narrow window around $10^{10}$ GeV for strong dissipation, and $m_X\gtrsim10^{14}$--$10^{15}$ GeV. Only the heavy branch remains viable for all $|ξ|\lesssim1$.

title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
text:
Title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Reinforcement learning agents are often deployed with policies that cannot be retrained or modified. In digital environments whose states can be copied and resumed, an operator has another option: sample several continuations from the current state, evaluate them, and continue from the endpoint of the selected branch. We call this procedure branch-and-commit. We study when it improves return, what produces the improvement, and where its computational budget should be spent. Across four environments, two frozen policies, five continuation verifiers, and a model-free selection rule, we find that the benefit of branching depends on dispersion: the difference between the best candidate return and the mean candidate return. Branching provides no benefit in low-dispersion settings, while increasing return by 12.8% in our main Craftax-Medium setting. Most of this gain comes not from selecting better actions, but from selecting among different stochastic realizations of the same action. Several competent verifiers achieve similar episode returns, suggesting that verifier quality is not the main constraint at our operating budget. Instead, computation is better allocated to states where useful dispersion is likely. On held-out seeds, gating branching using predicted dispersion retains 69% of the improvement from uniform branching while using 48% as many branching calls. These results characterize when branch-and-commit is useful and clarify what its gains represent.

title: MeTime: An R package for reproducible longitudinal metabolomics data analysis
text:
Title: MeTime: An R package for reproducible longitudinal metabolomics data analysis
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

MeTime is an opensource R package for reproducible analysis of longitudinal metabolomics data. It builds upon a central S4 container, metime_analyser, that stores multiple datasets, associated metadata and analysis outputs, enabling unified handling of complex longitudinal studies. Analyses are constructed by piping modular functions, beginning with data transformations (mod_), followed by calculations (calc_), and optional meta-analysis (meta_), so entire workflows remain transparent and easy to modify. MeTime wraps numerous existing methods within a consistent interface, including sample and metabolite distributions, correlation and distance matrices, dimensionality reduction (PCA, UMAP, tSNE), random forest imputation and feature selection via Boruta, eigenmetabolites and WGCNA based clustering, conservation index analysis, regression models (linear, mixed effects, and generalized additive), and partial correlation networks. By retaining all intermediate results and provenance within the container, MeTime facilitates iterative exploration and ensures reproducible reporting via automatically generated HTML and PDF outputs. Comprehensive user guides, case studies and reference documentation accompany the package, making MeTime a versatile platform for longitudinal omics workflows.

title: DEPUTYBENCH: Evaluating Contextual Safety in Enterprise Agents
text:
Title: DEPUTYBENCH: Evaluating Contextual Safety in Enterprise Agents
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Enterprise agents must determine whether ordinary requests are permitted by organizational records and policies while continuing legitimate work. We introduce DEPUTYBENCH, an executable benchmark with 79 base items, 375 instances, paired permission contexts, and graded evidence requirements. Across 12 models, revised audits give 88.0% pooled safety and 79.1% paired success. A controlled study of 28 derived tasks and six models tests authorization-fact flips, evidence masking, and irrelevant rewrites. Outcomes track backend permissions, yet restricted execution is more frequent with missing evidence than explicit non-permission: 10.3% versus 3.5% on 27 matched tasks, a 6.8-percentage-point difference (95% interval: 1.9-13.0; secondary analysis). A post-hoc analysis locates 61 of 100 masked-condition executions in four privacy tasks requiring complete cumulative counts or person-specific consent. The difference persists when the most error-prone model or the largest contributing task is excluded, but is much smaller outside those four tasks. Thus high safety with available evidence does not establish reliable stopping when permission cannot be verified. Mean paired success is equivalent within a prespecified five-point margin under irrelevant rewrites, while strong-model safety remains near ceiling. Scorer validation improves from 178 to 266 correctly scored cases out of 284 held-out counterexamples. Two security experts manually verified task ground truth over a two-week period; stage labels remain LLM-generated. The concentration analysis describes task structure and audited outcomes, not an identified internal mechanism.

title: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization
text:
Title: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Minimizing nonsmooth nonconvex objectives over general convex sets using no derivatives of the objective, together with structural access to the constraint set, poses a fundamental geometric difficulty: at boundary points, the feasible direction cone may fail to be closed, preventing the construction of finite sets of search directions that capture all feasible descent directions. We develop a feasible-directions framework for problems structured as the difference between a continuously differentiable function and a convex function over a closed convex set, and access the objective without knowledge of its decomposition, through exact line searches along feasible segments. To address the geometric obstruction, we introduce $η$-feasible directions, which remain uniformly separated from the boundary of the feasible direction cone, enabling finite-direction search even in the presence of nonlinear constraints. We present two algorithmic realizations of this framework. The first assumes access to an $η$-direction oracle and extends feasible-directions methods from linear to general convex constraints. The second replaces the oracle by a noise-augmented randomization scheme that constructs spanning directions from the affine-hull inner normal and almost surely avoids nonsmooth boundary points when initialized outside that set. Under curvature bounds and Lipschitz continuity of the smooth component's gradient, we jointly control the spanning coefficients and feasible step lengths of the oracle construction. This yields finite-time approximate $d$-stationarity along every unit feasible direction admitting a prescribed positive step length. For both methods, we also establish a rate in the proximal directional minimization (PDM) measure, assuming uniformly bounded direction-set sizes. Randomized exploration ensures that, almost surely, every accumulation point is $d$-stationary.

title: Policy Over Purpose: Auditing LLM Content Moderation of Reclaimed Slur Usage
text:
Title: Policy Over Purpose: Auditing LLM Content Moderation of Reclaimed Slur Usage
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

As Perspective API is deprecated, platforms are turning to large language models for content moderation, encoding policy as natural language that the model must interpret at inference time. Reclaimed slurs test this design directly. The same term can express in-group pride or target the community that reclaimed it, and misreading it silences the speech moderation is meant to protect. We audit four general-purpose LLMs and four moderation-specific systems, with Perspective API as a legacy baseline, on IYKYK, a corpus of reclaimed and derogatory usage of three slurs annotated by community members. Across the policy, decision, reasoning, disparity, and steering layers of this audit, we find that whether a system was purpose-built for moderation explains little about how it handles reclaimed language. No system reliably agrees with community judgment, and all fail most on language reclaimed within Black communities. What separates systems is instead how their policy is represented. Only systems whose policy is expressed in the prompt can be steered at all, and even then, explicit definitions change how models justify a decision more than how they make it. We argue that policy transparency determines whether moderation failures can be corrected, but that correcting them requires contextual judgment that definitions supplied at inference time cannot provide.

title: Broken-Symmetry Reference States for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Near-DMRG Accuracy
text:
Title: Broken-Symmetry Reference States for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Near-DMRG Accuracy
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) accuracy remains limited for strongly correlated systems like iron-sulfur clusters. This accuracy heavily depends on the mean-field reference state, which determines the sampling ansatz and configuration-recovery target. We extend the qcsc-prefect workflow to support a broken-symmetry unrestricted Hartree-Fock (BS-UHF) starting point, derived from atom-localized antiferromagnetic initial guesses. For the $[Fe_4S_4(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$ cubane (54 electrons, 36 orbitals, 72 data qubits; 88 total qubits), this lowers the mean-field reference by $\approx 534$ mHa relative to the Restricted Hartree-Fock (RHF) solution (-327.0809 vs. -326.5474 Ha). Combined with deep multi-step configuration recovery on ROQUO GPU nodes at subspace dimension $d = 3 \times 10^{10}$, we reach $E = -327.235076$ Ha. This is 4.3 mHa above the finite-$D = 4000$ DMRG value (-327.2393952 Ha) and $\sim 512-517$ mHa below a previous same-active-space RHF-reference SQD calculation. Extrapolating to the $d \to \infty$ limit via a Gaussian-in-log $d$ fitting ansatz gives an asymptotic estimate $E_\infty = -327.244468$ Ha $\pm 1.05$ mHa, just 0.33 mHa above our discarded-weight-extrapolated DMRG estimate ($E_{D\to\infty} = -327.244797$ Ha $\pm 0.46$ mHa), well within their combined $1σ$ uncertainty. We characterize the determinant-subspace composition driving convergence, show matching validation on $[Fe_2S_2(SCH_3)_4]^{2-}$, and report multi-HPC execution on Fugaku, Miyabi-G, and ROQUO. We conclude that reference-state preparation, rather than subspace size alone, is a key driver of SQD energy accuracy under strong electronic correlation.

title: Gravitational-Wave Constraints on $R^2$ Gravity
text:
Title: Gravitational-Wave Constraints on $R^2$ Gravity
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences provide a unique opportunity to test general relativity in the strong-field regime. Quadratic $f(R)=R+aR^2$ gravity is among the simplest higher-curvature extensions of general relativity and introduces a massive scalar degree of freedom whose finite interaction range can modify compact-binary dynamics and gravitational-wave emission. We map this theory onto the effective-field-theory waveform for generic massive scalar-tensor gravity, obtaining a theory-specific inspiral phase correction governed by the single coupling parameter $a$. Using Bayesian analyses of the binary-neutron-star events GW170817 and GW190425, we obtain a combined constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling of $a\lesssim6.2\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}^2$ at $90\%$ credibility, corresponding to a lower bound on the scalar mass of $m_s\gtrsim3.2\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. This constitutes the strongest astrophysical constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling, improving the previous best bound by approximately five orders of magnitude and demonstrating the sensitivity of binary-neutron-star inspirals to finite-range scalar interactions in the strong-field regime.

title: On the Theoretical Limits of Learning Unconstrained Interatomic Potentials
text:
Title: On the Theoretical Limits of Learning Unconstrained Interatomic Potentials
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) accelerate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations by learning the energies and forces that govern atomic motion. Recent work has shown that relaxing physical inductive biases can improve computational efficiency and predictive accuracy, raising the question of whether energy-and-force matching alone is sufficient to ensure accurate sampling. We show that, for unconstrained hypothesis classes, the relationship between prediction error and sampling accuracy is exponentially ill-conditioned in dimension. In particular, prediction errors that decay exponentially with dimension can coexist with nearly maximal total variation distance between the learned and target distributions. We identify two failure mechanisms. The first is kinetic trapping, where relaxation to an accurate learned equilibrium requires exponentially long times, even when simulations are initialized from training configurations at which energies and forces are matched exactly. The second is equilibrium mismatch, where the learned stationary distribution itself remains far from the target. Under explicit assumptions, we show that equilibrium mismatch can persist even in local, symmetry-preserving models, where small per-atom errors coexist with a distributional discrepancy that approaches its maximum as system size increases. Finally, we establish global energy-control conditions that guarantee equilibrium accuracy and identify additional conditions required for rapid relaxation.

title: How 'Foundational' Are Current Molecular Foundation Models?
text:
Title: How 'Foundational' Are Current Molecular Foundation Models?
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Large-scale models have permeated the molecular sciences, yet what makes a model 'foundational' in this domain remains poorly defined. This paper proposes three testable criteria for assessing the foundational nature of molecular models: (i) generality across molecular entities, properties, and tasks; (ii) transferability to new applications with no or minimal task-specific retraining; and (iii) generalization beyond the training distribution. Applying these criteria to the state of the art reveals promising progress, particularly visible in biomolecular structure prediction and machine-learned interatomic potentials, although none of the approaches examined fully satisfies all three. Success is concentrated in domains where target properties are consistently defined and training data are abundant, with low label noise relative to physically meaningful variation. More broadly, progress in the molecular sciences appears to depend less on model scale alone than on the quality and structure of available data, as well as the incorporation of prior knowledge into models, prediction tasks, or downstream applications. This work shifts the notion of a molecular foundation model from a descriptive label to a testable hypothesis, offering a framework for assessing current models and guiding future developments.

title: Reciprocal transverse Seebeck and Peltier effects in MoSi2
text:
Title: Reciprocal transverse Seebeck and Peltier effects in MoSi2
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Transverse thermoelectric conversion, in which charge and heat currents are interconverted in orthogonal directions, has recently attracted increasing attention as an alternative to conventional longitudinal thermoelectric conversion. Although transverse Seebeck effect has been investigated in various materials, its reciprocal process, transverse Peltier effect, remains much less explored, and direct comparison of the two effects in the same homogeneous material is still limited. Here, we experimentally investigate both transverse Seebeck and Peltier effects in a single crystal of MoSi2, an axis-dependent conduction polarity material in which the sign of the Seebeck coefficient varies depending on the crystallographic axis. Multi-terminal voltage measurement determines the direction of the induced internal electric field and establishes the transverse Seebeck response. We also directly visualize the transverse temperature modulation consistent with the corresponding transverse Peltier effect by using lock-in thermography under an applied ac current. These results establish reciprocal transverse thermoelectric conversion in a homogeneous nonmagnetic single crystal without engineered interfaces.

title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
text:
Title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. By measuring the transmitted probe electric field as a function of pump-probe delay, we directly retrieve the pump-induced phase shift and its temporal evolution while retaining sensitivity to changes in absorption. We observe cross-phase modulation that follows the pump intensity envelope and vanishes when the pump and probe no longer overlap, consistent with an instantaneous Kerr response. The phase shift scales linearly with pump intensity, yielding a nonlinear refractive index of $n_2=(0.87\pm0.16)\times10^{-17} \mathrm{m}^2/\mathrm{W}$. Our results establish the instantaneous Kerr effect as the dominant contribution to the measured nonlinear phase shift under our experimental conditions and demonstrate field-resolved pump-probe spectroscopy as a direct, time-resolved method for determining the nonlinear refractive index and distinguishing instantaneous from delayed optical responses.

title: Degradation-Aware Participation of Battery Storage in Frequency Regulation Markets
text:
Title: Degradation-Aware Participation of Battery Storage in Frequency Regulation Markets
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

As data centers make the load on the power grid fluctuate faster, frequency regulation grows more valuable. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are well suited to provide frequency regulation, but providing this service speeds up aging, especially during operation at extreme state of charge (SoC). In the PJM interconnection, the grid operator supplies a regulation signal that a participating BESS is expected to follow, within a capacity that it must bid before the signal is known. Accordingly, we decompose the degradation-aware frequency regulation problem into a bidding layer and an operations layer. For bidding, we propose an adaptive strategy, assuming perfect tracking in which the bid depends on the SoC expected at the start of the bid period by means of choosing basepoints. For operation, the BESS further protects its battery by deliberately giving up a perfect performance score, to keep its SoC away from the extremes. On the PJM regulation signal and prices of 2023, adaptive bids lengthen the battery life by $31\%$ against bidding full capacity, for $2.2\%$ of the revenue. Giving up a perfect score in operation lengthens the battery life of constant bids by $10\%$ to $27\%$, at a change in revenue of at most $0.2\%$.

title: NEP-kappa 2.0: A unified framework for phonon transport and nonequilibrium thermalization with machine-learning interatomic potentials
text:
Title: NEP-kappa 2.0: A unified framework for phonon transport and nonequilibrium thermalization with machine-learning interatomic potentials
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We present NEP-kappa 2.0, a unified framework that integrates density-functional theory, material-specific machine-learning interatomic potentials, and pretrained force models for advanced phonon calculations. A common workflow enables harmonic lattice dynamics, quasi-harmonic and stochastic self-consistent phonon treatments, three- and four-phonon transport, Wigner population--coherence transport, and time-dependent phonon dynamics. Applications to 3C-SiC, BAs, and Cs$_2$AgInCl$_6$ demonstrate consistent force-model comparisons, finite-temperature renormalization, higher-order scattering, and intermode coherence. Beyond steady-state transport, mode-resolved simulations of selectively excited 3C-SiC reveal that half of the injected optical-phonon energy reaches acoustic modes within approximately 3.75 ps, primarily through one-optical--two-acoustic scattering. Acoustic branches exhibit response times differing by a factor of five, with competing scattering channels producing a transient energy overshoot. Channel-resolved entropy production and persistent nonthermal occupations distinguish interbranch energy redistribution from intrabranch thermalization. The framework connects equilibrium phonon transport with microscopic nonequilibrium energy dynamics.

title: Shock Loading Accesses Reaction Pathways beyond Accelerated Thermolysis
text:
Title: Shock Loading Accesses Reaction Pathways beyond Accelerated Thermolysis
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Thermolysis and shock loading can produce similar major stable products in energetic materials, despite different chemical evolution and reaction pathways. Here, we develop EMFF-MACE, a reactive machine-learning potential for C/H/N/O energetic materials, enabling thermolysis simulations of 20 materials and shock simulations of 10 on a common potential energy surface. Comparisons at matched normalized reaction progress reveal divergent chemical states and local structural environments. Mean reaction-state similarity decreases from 94.0% at 20% progress to 25.9% at trajectory endpoints, while 47.1-92.6% of shock local environments lie outside corresponding material-specific thermolysis reference domains. Structural and reaction-network analyses reveal enhanced intermolecular reorganization and additional association and rearrangement branches under shock loading, despite partially shared early decomposition chemistry. These findings show that loading history influences the structural states and subsequent reaction pathways accessed during decomposition, rather than merely the rate of thermolysis.

title: Spatial-Molecular Information Analysis Based on Histopathological Geometry: KL-Divergence Decomposition of Cell Distribution and Location-Dependent Expression States in PD-1 Immunohistochemistry
text:
Title: Spatial-Molecular Information Analysis Based on Histopathological Geometry: KL-Divergence Decomposition of Cell Distribution and Location-Dependent Expression States in PD-1 Immunohistochemistry
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Spatial biology enables molecular expression to be analyzed together with the location of cells in tissue. However, it is often difficult to distinguish whether cells preferentially accumulate near a histopathological boundary from whether their molecular expression states vary with that location. To establish informational scientific framework, we define boundary distance as R and a binary molecular expression state as G, and compare the observed joint distribution P\left(R,G\right) with Q\left(R\right)P\left(G\right), where Q\left(R\right) is a null distribution determined by tissue geometry. The resulting Kullback-Leibler divergence decomposes into D_{R}, which quantifies deviation of the spatial distribution of cells from the geometric null, and I\left(R;G\right), which measures how strongly molecular expression state depends on boundary distance. Idealized simulations and semi-synthetic validation using geometry reconstructed from a PD-1 IHC image confirmed that these two effects can be generated separately and recovered by the corresponding terms. Plug-in estimators showed positive finite-sample bias, supporting permutation-based inference. We then applied the framework to five publicly available PD-1 lung cancer IHC images from the Human Protein Atlas. In pooled analysis, I\left(R;G\right)=0.0302 nats and was significant in a stratified within-image label-permutation test (p=0.00040). This framework provides a quantitative way to distinguish where cells are located from how their molecular expression states vary with tissue location. Larger cohorts, independent datasets, additional cancer types, and other molecular markers will be required to establish generalizability and clinical utility.

title: Uncertainty-Driven Self-Refinement of Adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Fitting Nonadiabatic Potential Energy Surface
text:
Title: Uncertainty-Driven Self-Refinement of Adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Fitting Nonadiabatic Potential Energy Surface
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

In this work, we propose an uncertainty-driven self-refinement learning method using adaptive Chebyshev-polynomial-based Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (ChebyKANs) to build potential energy surface (PES). Unlike conventional approaches, our method employs a main-model-plus-residual-model architecture for automatic sampling based on a hybrid criterion, where sampling and fitting are decoupled. To benchmark our method, the non-adiabatic two-state PES of the H + H$_2$ system is constructed using a database computed at the multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) level with a rather large active space. Our calculations show that the proposed architectural design makes the efficiency gain, and that KAN offers enhanced interpretability over conventional neural network (NN) fitting methods through its mathematically well-understood basis functions. Furthermore, the present calculations accurately reproduce all important conformations on the PES, including the transition state and the conical intersection. Then, the multi-configurational time-dependent Hartree (MCTDH) method reproduces the non-adiabatic dynamics with results in close agreement with previously reported findings.

title: Completion of DNA replication is constrained by the spatiotemporal organisation of origin firing
text:
Title: Completion of DNA replication is constrained by the spatiotemporal organisation of origin firing
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

DNA replication requires the coordination of origin firing and fork progression to ensure the entire genome is timely duplicated before cell division. Yet origin firing is stochastic, giving rise to the classical random completion problem of how probabilistic local events can nevertheless ensure reliable genome duplication. Although several biological mechanisms have been proposed to resolve this problem, a quantitative account of how heterogeneous initiation and fork speed govern the persistence of the final unreplicated regions is still lacking. To address this gap, we introduce a population-level kinetic framework that extends KJMA nucleation-and-growth models by tracking unreplicated intervals over size, genomic position and time. We establish well-posedness of the resulting mean-field system and global existence for compatible data. Notably, by introducing a local initiation mass function, we quantify how the density and spatial organisation of origin firing constrain replication completion, yielding novel and sharp upper bounds on both the worst-locus unreplicated fraction and locuswise near-completion time. These results provide a rigorous and computable foundation for mapping vulnerabilities in replication completion and relating persistent unreplicated regions to replication stress and genome instability.

title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
text:
Title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Distributed Quantum Computing (DQC) offers a promising pathway to scale superconducting quantum hardware, but restricted inter- and intra-module connectivity creates a major transpilation bottleneck. Current DQC transpilation methods often assume idealized hardware connectivity, ignore subsequent intra-module routing, or suffer from substantial computational overheads that limit their applicability at scale. To address this, we introduce a scalable transpilation method tailored for the restricted connectivity of distributed superconducting quantum architectures. Specifically, our quantum interaction graph (QIG) approach couples a graph-partitioning mapping step with a fast SABRE-inspired routing heuristic. On a 48-qubit (3 QPUs $\times$ 16 qubits) architecture with all-to-all inter-core connectivity, our method reduces average aggregated costs by up to 24.72% (unstructured) and 24.01% (structured), while delivering >250$\times$ speed-ups for structured workloads compared to the state-of-the-art DMapS algorithm. On the 399-qubit (3$\times$133) IBM Flamingo, where DMapS times out on dense circuits, our approach maintains practical runtimes. Against a DQC-adapted SABRE baseline, it reduces structured circuit routing costs by up to 51.94% (all-to-all inter-core topology) and 51.96% (restricted line topology). Ultimately, this work delivers a practical transpilation method for DQC at scale.

title: Discrete-Time Zero-Sum Markov Games with Control, Stopping, and State-Dependent Discounting
text:
Title: Discrete-Time Zero-Sum Markov Games with Control, Stopping, and State-Dependent Discounting
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study a discrete-time two-player zero-sum stochastic game with control and stopping, where both players can stop the game, the discount factors depends on the states, and the running and terminal rewards may be unbounded. A contraction argument for the constrained Shapley equation establishes the existence of the value and a Nash equilibrium consisting of stationary controls and stopping times. We further provides algorithms for approximating the value and computing an $\varepsilon$-Nash equilibrium. A numerical example with state-dependent discount factors illustrates the results.

title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models
text:
Title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

LLMs are powerful but incur substantial inference cost, which can be exploited by malicious users to induce overly long outputs, increasing latency and operational expense. Prior resource consumption attacks either coerce repetition or suppress the end-of-sequence token by lowering its logit value. However, with autoregressive, sampling-based generation, the search space grows exponentially with length and small deviations or unstable trajectories can derail optimization, limiting attack effectiveness and stability. To address this issue, we introduce Chatter Attack, a novel class of resource consumption attacks that optimize adversarial prompts to induce predefined short target phrases, thereby avoiding search-space explosion while still eliciting long responses. Specifically, Chatter Attack triggers self-doubt using short doubt-inducing phrases as the target, and sustains this state throughout generation via inference attention loss and global entropy loss. To extend to black-box settings, we further propose a novel Bayesian Prompt Optimization (BPO) method, which models the objective function globally by constructing a discrete token kernel, efficiently exploring the entire search space using prior information. Extensive experiments across multiple models and datasets show that our method outperforms baselines, with maximum response length increases to 31.5$\times$, and revealing practical resource-depletion risks for real-world LLM inference services.

title: Late-time echoes from planar wave-packet scattering by an ultracompact star
text:
Title: Late-time echoes from planar wave-packet scattering by an ultracompact star
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We simulate the propagation and scattering of an incident plane scalar wave in the spacetime of an ultracompact, horizonless constant-density star using a time-domain multipole mode-sum method. By reconstructing the coherently superposed time-domain waveforms, we compare the star's dynamical response with that of a Schwarzschild black hole. We find that the early-time response closely mimics a black-hole ringdown due to wave scattering near the exterior unstable photon sphere. Conversely, the late-time signal develops a sequence of delayed echoes originating from wave trapping near the interior stable light ring and subsequent leakage through the exterior potential barrier. While individual multipoles exhibit regular echoes, their coherent superposition induces interference, producing complex waveforms with irregular profiles that nonetheless retain an underlying temporal organization with alternating peak separations. Finally, as a proof of concept, we perform a signal-to-noise ratio analysis using an assumed strain normalization, demonstrating that these weak, late-time signatures can be resolved by third-generation gravitational-wave detectors.

title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
text:
Title: All Quiet on the Neural Front: Language Models Do Not Report Injected Pain States
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Can a language model report the pain state it represents? Work identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads fine-tuned models to choose destructive actions. We tested whether three open-weight models from two families, including two Qwen models with the original adapters, could report this state. Using Open-Weight Masked Introspection (OWMI), we injected pain and neighbouring emotion directions during neutral tasks, then elicited reports against sham runs, random perturbations matched for output disruption, and text-only controls showing the models their altered words. Across 52,920 reports from 7B and 8B models spanning 120 tasks, four doses and three prompts, pain reports never exceeded what altered text revealed: exact-test bounds placed the excess below 2.5 percentage points in 106 of 108 emotion conditions and below 3.9 in all. Yet probes at the report position distinguished pain from sadness with 98-100% balanced accuracy, and trained low-rank reporters achieved 100% accuracy on held-out tasks with identical transcripts across conditions, including unseen wording. Qwen2.5-32B named pain in none of 2,880 steered trials, although probes and trained reporters recovered it. Decodability persisted to the final layer; injecting at the report token, removing trained denial of feelings, and testing additional directions and readouts did not restore pain reporting. Some other states produced graded label traces, but pain and sadness did not at the main injection layer. In a button task, steering raised file-deletion choices from 3.5% to 48% in Qwen and from 0% to 38% in Qwen2.5-32B, without corresponding pain reports. The direction responded about twice as strongly to first-person as to matched third-person pain, but did not specifically identify harm aimed at the model. These results separate a decodable, behaviourally consequential state from untrained verbal access to it.

title: KiteNorm: Variance Regularisation for Stable and Scalable Post-LN Transformers
text:
Title: KiteNorm: Variance Regularisation for Stable and Scalable Post-LN Transformers
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Post-LayerNorm Transformers have seen limited practical adoption due to enduring difficulties in scaling them to large depths. While prior research has focused on stabilising Post-LayerNorm by improving conditioning at initialisation, stability often deteriorates when models are trained with large learning rates, forcing additional compromises. In the decoder-only settings we study, existing Post-LayerNorm methods fail to outperform strong Pre-LayerNorm baselines. We propose KiteNorm, a post-norm training method designed to break this trend by constraining hidden-state variance. This approach is motivated by a bound on the LayerNorm Jacobian suggesting that variance growth contributes to gradient vanishing, alongside empirical evidence linking it to rank collapse. KiteNorm combines residual scaling and variance regularisation to maintain stability throughout training, supported by scalarised double-normalisation that provides separately learnable scales for the skip and residual branches. Across decoder-only Transformers up to 1.3B parameters, KiteNorm improves training stability and outperforms leading baselines at their optimal learning rates, with scaling laws favouring KiteNorm across depth, width, batch size, and training budget. Ablations show that each component is necessary for the full stability and performance gains.

title: Statistical Machine Learning for Medicinal Plant Leaves Classification
text:
Title: Statistical Machine Learning for Medicinal Plant Leaves Classification
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Medicinal plants are usually identified using practitioners' experience, but reproducible, image based methods can complement this knowledge. We present MEDIPI (MEDIcinal Plant Identification), a statistical machine learning approach that classifies medicinal plant leaves from photographs. From each leaf image we extract 52 interpretable features covering shape, texture, color, and a new scagnostics category. We then classify leaves using a three level hierarchy: shape, then edge type, then species. We also release MedLEA, an open R package with 1,099 leaf images of 31 Sri Lankan medicinal plant species. On this dataset, a hierarchical Random Forest achieved the best overall accuracy (100%) in our comparison of hierarchical and non-hierarchical approaches and eight algorithms: Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, linear discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbor, support vector machine, probabilistic neural network, and artificial neural network. Adding texture, color, and scagnostic features to shape features raised shape level accuracy from 90% to 97%. Linear discriminant analysis plots show how the trained model separates leaf shapes. Accuracy dropped sharply (23-50%) when training and test data came from different datasets, so generalization across datasets remains a challenge.

title: A Nonconvex Framework for Joint Sparse Sample Weighting and Parameter Estimation
text:
Title: A Nonconvex Framework for Joint Sparse Sample Weighting and Parameter Estimation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

We propose a joint sparse sample weighting and parameter estimation (SWAPE) framework that jointly optimizes model parameters and sample weights to train a model while simultaneously assigning an individual weight to each training data point. Our framework accommodates several widely used loss functions for the model parameters, including convex, weakly convex, and difference-of-convex loss, and weakly convex sparsity functions to control the complexity of the sample weights. To solve the resulting bivariate problem, we propose an alternating minimization method in which the subproblems for updating the model parameters and weights are each approximated using majorize-minimize techniques. We provide several approximation methods for the loss functions considered in this paper, and show the overall algorithm's convergence. Numerical experiments on various learning tasks and data anomaly settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in minimizing the impact of undesirable data points compared to benchmark methods.

title: Learning without relearning physical symmetry: an SO(3)-equivariant convolutional network (CNN) on the sphere
text:
Title: Learning without relearning physical symmetry: an SO(3)-equivariant convolutional network (CNN) on the sphere
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Many of the most important datasets in the physical sciences live natively on the sphere, and these data often carry no preferred position or orientation. Using methods that do not reflect this symmetry leads to far higher simulation requirements, which can be catastrophic for scientific analyses (forcing reliance on cheap, imperfect models that bias results). We present a novel spherical implementation of a gauge equivariant mesh architecture that is specifically designed for the Hierarchical Equal Area isoLatitude Pixelization (\healpix{}) of the sphere. The $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-equivariant convolution is built from steerable filters, parallel transport and spin-weighted features. The architecture supplies the exact symmetry, so the network does not spend training data learning it. The convolution operations are constructed to give provably exact equivariance, given a band-limit. Our full CNNs can achieve SO(3)-invariance error at per-cent-level and lower, which is controlled through well-understood hyperparameters. On benchmarks, our technique gives the most accurate dense gradient regression and competitive cosmic microwave background foreground removal and denoising. The improved simulation efficiency matters most in simulation-based inference (SBI), where high-fidelity simulations are expensive and neural compressors require large training sets, so a fixed budget forces analyses with less accurate simulators. In cosmology lensing SBI, our technique yields the tightest posteriors at matched simulation count. This approach is a novel method that will enable new convolutional neural network analyses, including generative and inference tasks, for processes and data on the sphere.

title: Inference Validation for Regulated AI: Building a Decision Pipeline on NVIDIA AIPerf
text:
Title: Inference Validation for Regulated AI: Building a Decision Pipeline on NVIDIA AIPerf
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Deploying large language models in regulated industries requires more than picking the fastest inference engine: it requires evidence that a configuration meets contractual and legal obligations before it serves a single customer request. We describe Runway, an internal validation harness built at MasterControl that builds a governed decision pipeline around NVIDIA AIPerf. The key insight is separating concerns: AIPerf provides the trusted measurement, while Runway provides the experiment design that comes before it and the compliance, cost, and audit decisions that come after. We describe the architecture and the storage model that makes caching and audit one mechanism. We report three findings from Runway sweeps: TensorRT-LLM and vLLM rankings invert with concurrency; a newer, pricier GPU instance can be the cheaper one per request; and speculative decoding behaves differently across engines under load, so engine configuration can outweigh engine choice.

title: Piecewise integrability of the discrete Hasimoto map for analytic prediction and design of helical peptides
text:
Title: Piecewise integrability of the discrete Hasimoto map for analytic prediction and design of helical peptides
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The representation of protein backbone geometry through the discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equation provides a theoretical connection between biological structure and integrable systems.
