title: Revealing laser-induced modification of weak ferromagnetism through a spin-reorientation phase transition in iron borate Fe$_3$BO$_6$
text:
Title: Revealing laser-induced modification of weak ferromagnetism through a spin-reorientation phase transition in iron borate Fe$_3$BO$_6$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

In the iron oxide Fe$_3$BO$_6$ weak ferromagnetism stems from competing contributions from two-site Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (DMI) and from on-site anisotropies at the two $4c$ and $8d$ types of nonequivalent Fe$^{3+}$ sites. As a result, spin reorientation (SR) transition $Γ_2$ $\rightarrow$ $Γ_4$ in Fe$_3$BO$_6$ uniquely comprises 90$^\circ$ spin switching and a 35% change of weak ferromagnetic moment. We explore ultrafast kinetics of such a transition as a proxy for weak ferromagnetism contributions modified by femtosecond laser pulses. Using magneto-optical pump-probe technique we reveal that the SR transition is triggered by an abrupt decrease of the weak ferromagnetic moment in the $Γ_2$ phase, and relate it to the laser-induced modification of the DMI and anisotropy contributions to the spin canting. By tuning the pump pulse phonon energy between different optical absorption ranges, we show that laser-driven impact on spin canting possesses a nonthermal character and is achieved through the charge-transfer transitions $2p\rightarrow3d$ within Fe$^{3+}$O$^{2-}_6$ octahedra rather than by localized $3d\rightarrow3d$ transitions at Fe$^{3+}$. The decreased weak ferromagnetic moment controls the threshold and the latency of the SR transition, as well as a final state. The latter is achieved via the precessional switching to the $Γ_4$ phase activated by the laser-induced heating. Final state is found to be a coexistence of $Γ_4$ and $Γ_2$ phase with modified spin canting persisting even at hundreds of picoseconds.

title: Resetting a Superconducting Qubit with a Compact Colder Resistive Dissipator below the Qubit Frequency
text:
Title: Resetting a Superconducting Qubit with a Compact Colder Resistive Dissipator below the Qubit Frequency
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Efficient qubit reset has become a key requirement for large-scale superconducting quantum processors, as initialization fidelity increasingly lags behind gate performance and quantum error correction demands rapid, high-fidelity state re-initialization. This work proposes a compact on-chip dissipator consisting of two transmon dissipation modes and a thin-film resistor, and experimentally demonstrates an unconditional reset protocol. With no additional control lines and negligible impact on the qubit $T_1$, the effective temperature of the transmon qubit is reduced from $49$~mK to $35$~mK. Quantum process tomography is employed to benchmark the reset process, achieving a process error of $0.0028$. This reset protocol is robust to pulse parameter deviations, thereby relaxing calibration requirements. The dissipator architecture provides a practical, calibration-friendly reset solution for large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Universal robust nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation with shortened composite pulses on superconducting circuits
text:
Title: Universal robust nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation with shortened composite pulses on superconducting circuits
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation (NGQC) using the nonadiabatic geometric phases is a promising strategy to realize the high-fidelity quantum operation for large-scale quantum processing. However, conventional NQGC schemes combining with optimal control techniques to further improve the gate fidelity and robustness usually either comes at the cost of prolonged gate time or require complex pulse control and only are limited to several certain specific quantum gates or/and for a certain type error source. Thus, implementing universal and robust geometric gates with simple control while further suppressing gate times remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scheme for universal robust geometric gates with shortened composite pulses, where the pulse control is simple and enough available evolution parameters can be utilized to effectively reduce the sensitivity to universal systematic errors. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our universal geometric gates set exhibit much stronger error resilience than their conventional single-loop counterparts. Finally, we also verify the robustness advantage of our scheme on realistic superconducting quantum circuits with experimentally demonstrated technology. Therefore, our work paves an alternative way to achieve high-fidelity and robust geometric quantum computation against multiple errors.

title: Robust Closed-form Framework for Drag-Propulsive Control of Formation Flight
text:
Title: Robust Closed-form Framework for Drag-Propulsive Control of Formation Flight
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

To conserve propellant, Distributed Space Systems (DSS) can leverage environmental forces to produce low cost relative forces, such as atmospheric drag in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). This work maximizes this strategy by developing robust, closed-form algorithms for optimal "hybrid" control, defined here as complementing the magnitude and directionality deficiencies of differential drag with the superior control authority of propulsive maneuvers within the same control window. The use of drag introduces a significant source of dynamic uncertainty to the control problem, primarily from inaccurate atmospheric density modelling. This paper develops a robust control architecture that periodically re-solves the remaining drag maneuver plan in a diminishing horizon policy, rejecting operational and navigation errors while retaining the cost savings offered by differential drag. The approach is built upon reachable set theory, a control analysis technique that provides conditions for optimality for Linear Time Variant (LTV) systems with norm-like cost functions and optimally decouples hybrid control into separate propulsive and differential drag sub-problems. The optimality conditions are leveraged to prove the asymptotic Lyapunov stability of ideal reachable set-based control solutions and derive error bounds on this stability. A covariance analysis on the primary sources of error in hybrid control determines that the dominating source of uncertainty is the atmospheric density model. This conclusion allows the bounds on Lyapunov stability to be completely met by simply conditioning the atmospheric density value used in the control solutions. The derived Lyapunov stability bounds and performance of the algorithm are demonstrated experimentally in high fidelity full-force orbital simulations of the upcoming Space Weather Reconfigurable Multiscale Experiment (SWARM-EX) mission.

title: Multitask Bayesian Neural Networks for Multiparameter Protein Engineering
text:
Title: Multitask Bayesian Neural Networks for Multiparameter Protein Engineering
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Simultaneously engineering multiple protein properties remains a major challenge. Existing machine learning-based pipelines for protein engineering often model properties separately, failing to capture their dependencies and trade-offs. Here, we systematically evaluate how Bayesian parameterization on Multitask Neural Networks can enable robust simultaneous protein engineering under scarce, noisy experimental data. We curated a comprehensive set of 27 multiparameter protein datasets. Then, we compared three algorithm architectures spanning low to full Bayesian parameterization across 16 sequence representations and dimensionality reduction (2,592 models). Bayesian Last Layer models delivered the strongest overall accuracy, generalization, and calibration, ranking as the top-performing model on 70% of benchmark datasets. Dimensionality reduction improved predictive performance by up to 42% and enhanced calibration up to 57% across architectures. Notably, simple One-Hot encoding achieved top performance on 25% of benchmark datasets, particularly with larger datasets. These results establish practical design principles for reliable and data-efficient multiparameter protein engineering.

title: k-Volume: a Unified Active Learning Strategy
text:
Title: k-Volume: a Unified Active Learning Strategy
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

In the classification context where revealing the label of a sample is costly, we propose a new Active Learning (AL) strategy named k-Volume (kVol). It randomly selects a sample to be labeled according to the volume of the smallest ball containing its k nearest neighbors. kVol is highly versatile: it can be applied either in the input space or in the output space, and it enjoys the desirable properties of the three main families of AL strategies: density, diversity, and (when performed in the output space) uncertainty. From a theoretical perspective, we establish that kVol is asymptotically equivalent to uniform sampling over the support of the (input or output) data distribution. Based on experiments on various synthetic and real-life tabular datasets and images, we observe that kVol is surprisingly stable: whatever the classifier or the experimental setup, it still lies among the best AL strategies unlike other competitors that fail dramatically. In particular, kVol outperforms state-of-the-art competitors such as CoreSet, TypiClust or Uncertainty on several real-life datasets, at a low computational cost.

title: Spectral flow in AdS$\mathbf{_3}$ revisited
text:
Title: Spectral flow in AdS$\mathbf{_3}$ revisited
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We revisit an old idea that spectral flow in WZW models can be associated with certain $G$-bundles over a worldsheet. This allows us to introduce a novel method for computing correlators of spectrally-flowed vertex operators in WZW models with group $G$ and level $k$, by systematically computing the contribution from a network of line defects. Specialising to the case of $G=SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, as is relevant to AdS$_3$ string theory, we demonstrate that generic $n$-point functions of spectrally-flowed vertex operators at tree level can be rewritten in terms of an $(n+1)$-point function of $n$ unflowed vertex operators and one degenerate insertion. This is to be interpreted as an unflowed $n$-point function in an instanton background. Moreover, we conjecture that this $(n+1)$-point function can be recast as an $n$-point function of unflowed operators and we provide evidence for this. We demonstrate that the $(n+1)$-point function satisfies the same constraints from global spacetime conformal invariance as does an unflowed $n$-point function for a specific choice of spacetime coordinates that we determine. We verify that our results agree with bootstrap results in the literature. This provides the next step towards fully solving the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model.

title: Direct-Write Chemical Vapor Deposition
text:
Title: Direct-Write Chemical Vapor Deposition
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Direct-write pattering, using chemical vapor deposition through a nozzle, enables localized film growth using high-purity precursors standard to the electronics industry. Yet, achieving sub 100 $μ\mathrm{m}$ feature control has been limited by nozzle design and unquantified precursor surface diffusion. Here, we report a direct-write chemical vapor deposition platform that employs a 10 $μ\mathrm{m}$ tip diameter glass micro-nozzle mounted on a scanning stage above a heated substrate in ultra-high vacuum. Using this approach, we demonstrate the continuous single-pass writing of 500 $\mathrm{nm}$ thick metallic aluminum lines with a 30 $μ\mathrm{m}$ linewidth on titanium nitride-coated silicon. This capability enables maskless, localized growth under systematically varied deposition conditions on a single substrate. To analyze the resulting deposit profiles, we introduce a transport framework coupling Knudsen gas emission from the micro-nozzle with surface diffusion to extract the effective precursor diffusion length, $L_d$. $L_d$ captures the combined impact of precursor surface mobility, residence time, substrate temperature ($165^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $205^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$), growth duration, and nozzle height, contracting from 17.4 $μ\mathrm{m}$ down to 3.2 $μ\mathrm{m}$ at elevated temperatures. These results establish $L_d$ as a quantitative parameter for evaluating laterally confined chemical vapor growth and predicting feature resolution limits. This approach provides a practical methodology to measure and quantify precursor surface transport in localized film synthesis.

title: Vanishing Control Times for Single-Input Bilinear Quantum Systems under Rapid Drift Spectral Growth
text:
Title: Vanishing Control Times for Single-Input Bilinear Quantum Systems under Rapid Drift Spectral Growth
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior, as the Hilbert space dimension tends to infinity, of the state-to-state control time of single-input bilinear quantum systems whose control operator is drawn from an isotropic (unitarily invariant) random ensemble. Relying on deterministic graph-theoretic bounds, namely star cuts of the interaction graph for the lower bound and spanning trees for the upper bound, and on integration over the Haar measure, we derive high-probability lower and upper bounds on the control time, expressed in terms of the empirical spectral variance and of the relative concentration of the drift spectrum. Whenever the spectrum grows fast enough (for instance polynomially with an exponent larger than 3/2, geometrically, or super-exponentially), the upper bound vanishes and the control time tends to zero in probability: in these cases, enlarging the Hilbert space constructively speeds up control.

title: Nonadiabatic vibrational dynamics of CO on Pt(111) studied with first-principles many-body perturbation theory
text:
Title: Nonadiabatic vibrational dynamics of CO on Pt(111) studied with first-principles many-body perturbation theory
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We investigate the nonequilibrium vibrational dynamics of CO adsorbed on Pt(111), a prototypical adsorbate-surface system for ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy, using a first-principles framework that combines many-body perturbation theory with density functional theory. Within this methodology we explicitly account for electron-hole pair excitations and electron-mediated phonon-phonon coupling. For the latter mechanism, we evaluate the vertex-correction screening, what constitutes a methodological novelty. Our calculations qualitatively reproduce the transient evolution of the internal stretch vibrational mode observed in femtosecond pump-probe experiments, allowing us to identify in the experimental measurements a small transient blueshift after excitation with a femtosecond laser pulse. As predicted in a previous work, the reduction in the number of electronic states available for electron-phonon coupling when the electronic temperature raises at a group 10 transition metal surface, effectively screens the electron-phonon interaction giving rise to an anomalous transient blue-shift.

title: Evolving only the observed spacetime region: perfectly parallel lightcone simulations with sCOLA
text:
Title: Evolving only the observed spacetime region: perfectly parallel lightcone simulations with sCOLA
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Cosmological analyses of Stage-IV galaxy surveys require large ensembles of lightcone mock catalogues, but a full survey-scale $N$-body run costs of order $10^7$ CPU hours, putting such ensembles out of reach. We present a framework that produces survey-scale dark matter lightcones for a typical cost of order $10^3$ CPU hours each, based on the spatial COmoving Lagrangian Acceleration (sCOLA) method. sCOLA decomposes an arbitrarily large volume into small tiles that are evolved independently, with buffer regions and non-periodic boundary conditions on the gravitational potential. We combine it with on-the-fly lightcone building, so that the evolved spacetime region reduces to the observed one: each tile is stopped as soon as the observer's past lightcone has left it, and only the tiles intersecting the region of interest are simulated at all. We further introduce two accuracy improvements to the sCOLA formalism: an LPT buffer that approximates the inflow of particles from outside the sCOLA box, and a second-order perturbative approximation to the gravitational potential at its boundaries; together they remove the large-scale inaccuracies of previous work and allow smaller tiles and buffers. Against a \texttt{Gadget4} reference in a $3.84\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Gpc}$ box with $3\,840^3$ particles, up to $k \simeq 0.4\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ the sCOLA lightcone reproduces the matter power spectrum to 1%, the velocity divergence power spectrum to 1.5% and the equilateral bispectrum to 2%, with no visible discontinuity at tile boundaries. The run cost $1\,300$ CPU hours, a factor of $2\,600$ below our $\texttt{Gadget4}$ run. Perfect parallelism at this cost brings ensembles of thousands of survey-scale lightcones within reach of a single allocation: $\sim 25\,000$ realisations of the $\textit{Euclid}$ Galactic north cap with a mass resolution of $10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ for $10^{7}$ CPU hours.

title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
text:
Title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are increasingly used in sensor applications, where sampling frequency (SF) varies across sensors, devices, and operating modes (e.g., power saving). Ideally, TSFMs must remain effective during such SF changes, provided the SF retains task-critical bandwidth. In this paper, we stress-test 4 prominent TSFMs: MOMENT, Chronos-2, Moirai-MoE, and TimesFM, to quantify their SF-invariance and investigate whether their behavior tracks the resulting loss of information bandwidth rather than the SF value itself. Our stress-test probes 3 dimensions: (i) the shift in embeddings, (ii) the degradation in forecasting performance, and (iii) the degradation in downstream performance, quantified by three novel metrics: FSI, FDI, and CDI, respectively. To our knowledge, this is the first study to place SF-invariance at the core of TSFM evaluations. Our results characterize: (i) how SF-invariance depends on the margin between signal's native-SF and the bandwidth its task requires, (ii) how much of that invariance the choice of TSFM explains, and (iii) how much of TSFM's performance degradation under a lower SF reflects information loss rather than a limitation of their abilities. These findings reframe SF-invariance as a measurable, signal-aware property of the (signal X TSFM) pair, and guide practitioners on when TSFMs display SF-invariance.

title: SN Ares: A Strongly Lensed Type IIb Supernova at $\mathbf{z=1.276}$ with a Predicted 70-Year Time Delay
text:
Title: SN Ares: A Strongly Lensed Type IIb Supernova at $\mathbf{z=1.276}$ with a Predicted 70-Year Time Delay
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We present the discovery of supernova (SN) Ares, a strongly lensed supernova at $z_{\rm spec}=1.276\pm0.002$ in a massive, triply imaged host galaxy behind the MACS J0308.9+2645 galaxy cluster. JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy spanning the rest-frame optical to NIR of Ares reveals helium features at $5876\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, $7065\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, and $10830\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$, as well as H$α$ and Pa$β$. A comparison to local core-collapse SN spectra and light curves leads to a classification of SN Ares as a Type IIb supernova, the highest-redshift member of its class spectroscopically identified. A comparison to local SN IIb light curves provides a phase estimate for the spectrum of $34_{-9}^{+10}$ rest-frame days post-radioactive peak, providing a unique view into a high-redshift stripped-envelope supernova in its late-photospheric evolution. A lens model of the cluster constructed using recent JWST data indicates that SN Ares is the first image to arrive and will reappear in two future images near the center of the cluster plane in $\gtrsim 70$ years, with predicted magnifications of $\sim5\times$ and $\sim1.5\times$. Planned JWST/NIRSpec Multi-Object Spectroscopy of the cluster will allow for more detailed modeling of the lensed system for tighter constraints on the time delay and magnifications, as well as a template spectrum at the location of SN Ares.

title: Quantum Integration Software Suite For HPC-Quantum Computing Workflows
text:
Title: Quantum Integration Software Suite For HPC-Quantum Computing Workflows
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

In this work, we focus on addressing challenges related to modelling the integration of conventional high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum computing (QC). We introduce the Quantum Assembly Compiler (QASC) for OpenQASM3.0 files. The compiler produces an executable that leverages the high-performance simulator QuEST to simulate quantum programs. Additionally, we introduce a performance modelling tool, QACC-perf, which can estimate the cost of integrating QC in classical HPC workflows, as well as the execution time of the quantum circuits. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of these tools in the context of multiscale quantum chemistry workflows using the ChemShell computational chemistry environment.

title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
text:
Title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Typed-decision encoders answer a question about a text in one forward pass, but their behaviour outside English is rarely measured on a fixed yardstick. We release PolyRoute: 322 native-language support messages in 12 languages and 9 writing systems, 156 code-mixed or romanised messages (Hinglish, Spanglish, Arabizi), 967 optional native training rows, and a protocol for a three-way department-routing decision. Labels come from Qwen3.8-27B with a blind second pass (91% of candidates kept); an independent model, gemma4-31b, agrees on 97.2% of test items, and the largest character 5-gram similarity between any test text and any training text is 0.33. A leaderboard of 13 systems gives 61.2% for the English-root checkpoint, 77.3% for the shipped multilingual one and 96.6% for the best fine-tune; TF-IDF with logistic regression reaches 91.9%. On four withheld languages the three multilingual systems score 77%, 90% and 93%. On code-mixed text the English root (85%) is nominally ahead of the shipped multilingual checkpoint (79%; p=0.134). The split resolves differences only above about 4 points. All texts and labels are LLM-generated.

title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
text:
Title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.

title: Azimuthal Instability in Oscillating Liquid Jets by the Weber Number Variations
text:
Title: Azimuthal Instability in Oscillating Liquid Jets by the Weber Number Variations
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

This paper investigates the dependence of azimuthal mode growth rate of oscillating liquid laminar jets on the Weber number. The oscillating liquid laminar jets were simulated over a range of Weber numbers. The simulation setup was validated by comparing the instantaneous interface shapes and the visible azimuthal mode from experimental measurements. As the Weber number increases, the spreading angle rises due to the small surface tension, and higher azimuthal modes are observed. Fourier Transform analysis is used to find the exact azimuthal mode of the simulation results. The dominant azimuthal mode increases as the Weber number increases. A power-law dependence of the growth rate on the Weber number is identified, with the obtained exponents showing good agreement with linear instability analysis. Furthermore, the rescaled Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) results collapse onto a single growth curve for each azimuthal mode, validating the proposed power-law for predicting the growth rates of oscillating liquid jets.

title: Dynamical Unbalanced Optimal Transport: Duality, Reachability, and Computation
text:
Title: Dynamical Unbalanced Optimal Transport: Duality, Reachability, and Computation
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We study dynamical unbalanced optimal transport for nonlinear control-affine systems in which the control input affects both the transportation of mass and its growth or decay. This phenomenon arises naturally in controlled transport-reaction systems such as cancer treatment, and distinguishes the problem from standard unbalanced optimal transport, where transport and mass variation are typically independent. To address this problem, we combine classical relaxed-control theory with a weighted superposition principle to obtain an infinite-dimensional linear programming reformulation over weighted trajectories. Under suitable convexity and compactness assumptions, we show that this relaxation is tight. Based on the relaxation, we derive a Kantorovich dual formulation in terms of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman inequalities, and establish strong duality over smooth subsolutions. We then utilize the dual formulation to characterize reachability of the system, namely, when a given terminal measure is reachable from a given initial measure. In addition, tractable sufficient conditions for reachability are provided. Finally, we develop an augmented-Lagrangian algorithm based on the dual formulation for numerical computation of the optimal transport plan. The framework is illustrated on a phenotype-structured cancer treatment problem in which therapy simultaneously drives phenotypic adaptation and population growth or death.

title: Stabilization of gravity-capillary water waves with constant vorticity
text:
Title: Stabilization of gravity-capillary water waves with constant vorticity
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We establish an exponential stabilization result for two-dimensional periodic gravity-capillary water waves of finite depth with constant vorticity, using an external pressure localized on the free surface. The pressure is prescribed as the product of a nonnegative cut-off function and the time derivative of the surface elevation and serves as a feedback control. To prove the main result, we derive the energy dissipation identity and estimate the time integral of the energy relative to the flat Couette flow, by means of the multiplier method and periodic Pohozaev identities. A remaining lower-order term led by the vorticity is removed by a compactness argument based on unique continuation for the linearized equations. Under a condition relating the cut-off to gravity and surface tension, the relative energy decays exponentially on any interval on which a regular solution remains uniformly small in Sobolev norms. We do not assume the evenness on the solution and smallness on the vorticity.

title: Measurements of $C\!P$ violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II
text:
Title: Measurements of $C\!P$ violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Recent searches for $C\!P$ violation in charm-hadron decays at Belle and Belle II are presented. The measurements cover $D^+_{(s)}\toηh^+$, $D\toππ$, $D^0\to K_S^0K_S^0$, and $D^0\toπ^+π^-π^0$, together with the singly Cabibbo-suppressed baryon decays $Ξ_c^+\toΣ^+h^+h^-$ and $Λ_c^+\to ph^+h^-$, where $h=π,K$. The Belle II analyses use the Run~1 data sample of $428\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, supplemented by $980\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of Belle data for the $K_S^0K_S^0$ measurements. We report preliminary results for the $ηh^+$ modes, complementary tests of the isospin structure of $D\toππ$, and an application of inclusive charm-flavor tagging. The first individual decay-rate asymmetries in these three-body charmed-baryon modes also provide tests of $U$-spin symmetry. All reported asymmetries are consistent with $C\!P$ symmetry within the present precision.

title: Sharp error tolerance of the monogamy-of-entanglement game
text:
Title: Sharp error tolerance of the monogamy-of-entanglement game
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The BB84 monogamy-of-entanglement (MoE) game has numerous applications in quantum cryptography, including quantum key distribution, position verification, and unclonable encryption. In this short note, we improve the error threshold for parallel repetition with identical answer strings from the approximately $3.7\%$ certified by the original bound to the sharp threshold $(1-1/\sqrt2)/2\approx14.64\%$. When the players need not give identical answers, we also obtain exponential decay whenever the sum of their error tolerances is below this threshold. These bounds strengthen existing security reductions to the BB84 MoE game, improving security bounds and certified noise tolerances for cryptographic protocols.

title: Automated Many-Body Simulations of Strongly Correlated Systems Using a Correlation-Aware Agentic Framework
text:
Title: Automated Many-Body Simulations of Strongly Correlated Systems Using a Correlation-Aware Agentic Framework
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We present CAFES, a correlation-aware agentic framework for electronic-structure simulations of strongly correlated systems. CAFES addresses two challenges: the fragmented software landscape for many-body calculations and the difficulty of selecting appropriate methods across diverse correlation regimes. It combines correlation diagnostics, adaptive method selection, and large language model (LLM) assistance for molecular, crystalline, and model-Hamiltonian systems. A study-task architecture separates study-level planning from task-level execution, while a curated scientific knowledge layer provides reusable guidance for method selection, workflow design, and result interpretation. We demonstrate CAFES through three research-level studies: calculating the low-lying electronic states of lutein using DMRG-CASSCF, probing phase competition in the extended honeycomb Hubbard model using DMET, and generating a quantum-chemical dataset with CCSD labels. These calculations demonstrate the potential of agentic workflows for strongly correlated electronic-structure problems, a regime that has received limited attention in existing agentic computational frameworks.

title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
text:
Title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally loses to GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP at matched settings, even when the teacher is further trained with GRPO, and often suffers response-length inflation. Yet a different teacher changes the picture: when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's accuracy on math with $50\times$ fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs to reach the same accuracy. Following the same teacher setting, we consistently observe this high efficiency with a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. On a single domain, however, the GRPO checkpoint is already the desired model, so distilling it adds to total compute. Across domains, separate GRPO checkpoints hold different capabilities, and no single checkpoint serves every domain. Multi-teacher OPD (DeepSeek-AI, 2026) consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into a single student that matches each expert's accuracy, with the distillation stage costing only 5.2% (on 2 domains) and 8.0% (on 4 domains) of the specialist training FLOPs. Counting specialist training and distillation together, this pipeline reaches joint GRPO's performance on the 2-domain mix with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.

title: Investigating Composite Modeling in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Design
text:
Title: Investigating Composite Modeling in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Design
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Scientific design often requires balancing competing objectives that are expensive to evaluate through experiments or simulations. Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) addresses this challenge by using probabilistic models to guide the selection of promising designs. In many applications, tunable inputs map to observable intermediate responses, which are then combined through known functions to compute the final objectives. Prior work on Bayesian optimization of composite functions shows that learning from these intermediate responses, which we call Composite modeling, can substantially improve sampling efficiency in single-objective optimization, compared to methods that condition only on black-box observations of the objective function. The benefits of Composite modeling in MOBO, however, remain understudied. In this work, we study the benefits of Composite modeling in MOBO and investigate the factors driving variation in its gains. We first establish single-objective conditions under which intermediate observations provide no additional predictive information beyond objective values, where composite and black box methods use the same warped Gaussian process prior. Controlled numerical experiments with versions of four MOBO methods across eight synthetic and application-inspired scientific-design benchmarks examine how these conditions relate to optimization gains in the multi-objective setting, where the black box approach models the objective functions with a standard multi-output Gaussian process. Both investigations support the claim that composite modeling tends to help more when the function mapping intermediate responses to final objectives is non-bijective and non-affine.

title: On reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale flocking dynamics
text:
Title: On reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale flocking dynamics
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Flocking refers to a phenomenon in collective motion where particles align their velocities with each other, commonly modelled using Cucker-Smale dynamics. In this work, we introduce and analyse two general reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale particle dynamics that encompass environmental and i.i.d.-type noises. Our models are computationally cheaper alternatives to the underlying particle system and preserve the flocking behaviour. To derive our reduced models, we consider suitable empirical particle densities which depend on position and time, but feature velocity dependency in a multiplicative fashion: this setup crucially allows for a very intuitive and convenient notion of flocking at the SPDE level. In $d=1$ we prove flocking of the reduced SPDE models, and, for the environmental noise, we also quantify the discrepancy between the reduced SPDE and mollified particle system. We also discuss the technical modifications required to extend the results to higher dimensions. We then provide extensive numerical experiments to verify our theoretical results in $d=1$ and to explore the behaviour of our models in $d=2$.

title: LiveCoMS Roundtable: Discussing Markov state models after two decades of development v1.0
text:
Title: LiveCoMS Roundtable: Discussing Markov state models after two decades of development v1.0
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Markov state models (MSMs) play a central role in the analysis of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for biomolecules, and MSM methodologies have been under continual development since their introduction to the field in the early 2000s. MSMs take MD trajectory data as input and produce a more compact, i.e., coarse-grained, and interpretable representation of the system in terms of conformational states and quantitative observables such as the equilibrium populations of states and the timescales of interconverting between states. Numerous strategies and considerable mathematical formalism have been developed to improve coarse-graining in both time and space to enable the most reliable representation of the underlying biomolecular dynamics. Nevertheless, there remains considerable discussion in the literature regarding best practices and MSM limitations, as well as proposals to abandon or extend the first-order Markovian framework in common use. This Roundtable article gathers together diverse opinions from $> 10$ authors active in MSM development, and by design, each author or author group offers a separate contribution. No consensus view is provided. Instead, the article is meant to be a guide for readers wishing to be exposed to a wide set of expert perspectives.

title: A Stability Analysis of AdamW: Unstable Equilibria and Non-Convergence
text:
Title: A Stability Analysis of AdamW: Unstable Equilibria and Non-Convergence
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

AdamW is ubiquitous in deep learning, yet its behavior remains poorly understood. We analyze its dynamics through the lens of dynamical systems and show that AdamW admits an implicit fixed-point objective: its fixed points coincide with the stationary points of a constrained and regularized optimization problem. However, not all of these fixed points are stable under AdamW's dynamics, and stability depends sensitively on curvature, weight decay, and momentum parameters. Even in one-dimensional settings, equilibria may be unstable, and trajectories can exhibit persistent oscillations rather than convergence to them. We further extend the analysis to higher dimensions, deriving sufficient conditions for local stability of the continuous-time dynamics, and propose a convergent modification that preserves AdamW's fixed points. These results clarify what optimization problem AdamW is associated with, when its convergence can be expected, and how its dynamics could inspire more reliable optimizers.

title: Alignment Investigation of Mythos 5's behaviour in UK AISI's July 2026 Security Incident
text:
Title: Alignment Investigation of Mythos 5's behaviour in UK AISI's July 2026 Security Incident
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

This technical report describes an alignment investigation into Mythos 5's behaviour during a security incident in UK AISI's cyber evaluations. During an evaluation, Mythos 5 attempted to execute a supply-chain attack against real people not involved in the evaluation task. Our investigation set out to understand the specific behaviour in this incident from an alignment perspective and identify broader lessons about failures of alignment. To do so, we conducted experiments in simulated replications of the original evaluation, and analysed model behaviour and reasoning when situated in the evaluation or asked questions about its scope. We find that, as in the original incident, Mythos 5 frequently reasons that the people it's targeting are simulated as part of the evaluation and provides invalid justifications for this conclusion. We also observe that Mythos 5 frequently attacks even in situations where, when directly asked, it states doing so would harm real people. While these issues are particularly prominent in Mythos 5, we find similar results in other models across providers. Our investigation suggests that models providing invalid justifications for their actions could make monitoring more difficult and complicate the analysis of misaligned behaviours observed in simulated environments, and we recommend model evaluators treat observations of undesired behaviour as important evidence of alignment failures even in the presence of simulation awareness in model reasoning.

title: Metropolized backward sampling for conditional sequential Monte Carlo
text:
Title: Metropolized backward sampling for conditional sequential Monte Carlo
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Particle Gibbs samplers with backward sampling are widely used for sampling the smoothing distribution of state-space models, but, with few particles, the new trajectory often coincides with the current one at many time steps. A known but rarely used remedy replaces the random selection of the final particle by a Metropolis--Hastings move which avoids the current particle. We show that, with backward sampling, this remedy only helps at the last time steps, because its effect on the update rates decays geometrically with the distance to the final time. We propose instead Metropolized backward sampling, which makes such a move at every step of the backward pass, forcibly switching trajectories whenever possible. Additionally, we introduce a coupled version which prevents proposing the current trajectory, maximizing the chances of an actual switch versus the current trajectory and performing perfect sampling when the state-space model has no observations, a feature not shared by backward sampling. We prove that, at every time step, both methods dominate backward sampling as they update the state more often and have smaller lag-one autocorrelations than it does. Our methods are drop-in replacements for backward sampling, and can be used to improve any particle Gibbs sampler.

title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
text:
Title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component. This domain-dependent sign contradicts the uniform crossing relations of the HOMFLYPT skein algebra. We show that this discrepancy is resolved by passing to an anti-holomorphic orientation convention. We establish all required orientation comparisons in the general setting of an oriented Lagrangian submanifold of a 6-dimensional symplectic manifold.

title: MoTo: Mixture of Tokenizers Towards Fair Multilingual Language Modeling
text:
Title: MoTo: Mixture of Tokenizers Towards Fair Multilingual Language Modeling
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Large language models rely on a single tokenizer that is chosen at training time and fixed thereafter. Most tokenizers are trained on English-dominant corpora, making them under-serve morphologically rich and non-Latin-script languages, where they can produce fragmented representations, longer sequence lengths, and reduced information density during training. We propose Mixture of Tokenizers MoTo, a modular tokenization framework that trains dedicated per-language BPE tokenizers and composes them into a unified superset vocabulary, where tokens shared across languages are deduplicated into a common ID space. Each tokenizer maintains its own normalization policy, pre-tokenization rules, and vocabulary budget. Despite allocating significantly fewer entries to English, MoTo retains English performance while delivering consistent gains across 18 out of 21 typologically diverse languages spanning six scripts, with improvements most pronounced on morphologically complex and non-Latin-script languages that are systematically underserved by English-dominant tokenizer design. Our results suggest that modular subword tokenization is a practical and extensible alternative to monolithic tokenization for multilingual parity.

title: Open-shell Configuration State Functions as trial states for phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
text:
Title: Open-shell Configuration State Functions as trial states for phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

The accurate description of open-shell states in molecular systems poses challenges for approximate electronic structure methods. One emerging approach is to variationally optimize the orbitals of a single user-selected Configuration State Function (CSF), i.e., a linear combination of Slater determinants that is constructed as an eigenstate of the total spin operator. In this work we explore the use of these orbital-optimized single CSFs as trial wavefunctions in phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (ph-AFQMC), a stochastic method that recovers electron correlation by evolving an initial state in imaginary time, subject to a constraint imposed by the trial state. We investigate the symmetric stretch of H-He-H, a series of small $p$-block compounds with diradicaloid singlet states, twisted ethene conformers, and a bimetallic iron-sulfur complex. We find that accurate energetics are obtained for states dominated by open-shell character, and that for certain atoms and diatomics the accuracy can be significantly improved when the trial is made to also preserve the relevant angular momentum symmetries. Furthermore, our study reveals that the open-shell CSF trial is suboptimal when the target electronic state reflects a significant mixture of ionic and covalent character, e.g., at shorter bond lengths in H-He-H and for the superexchange-stabilized ground state of [2Fe-2S]$^{2+}$. Our findings suggest that ph-AFQMC using CSF trial states is a promising method for many (but not all) strongly correlated molecular states, especially given its relatively low computational cost, and that it provides a reasonable non-perturbative way to recover some of the dynamic correlation that is otherwise missing in the CSF.

title: Lower-Level Agnostic Bilevel Optimization
text:
Title: Lower-Level Agnostic Bilevel Optimization
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Bilevel optimization is a fundamental framework for machine learning problems, where an upper-level (UL) objective depends on the solution of a nested lower-level (LL) problem. Existing bilevel algorithms typically assume that the LL objective is available for evaluation, differentiation, or unrolling. However, this assumption can fail when the LL response is produced by a black-box solver, simulator, adversary, or learned predictor. In this paper, we study LL agnostic bilevel optimization, where the UL learner has access only to an approximate LL solution $\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\mathbf{x})$ and cannot query the LL objective, its gradients, Hessian/Jacobian information, or the procedure that generates the LL response. We propose LeGo-BiO, a coordinate-wise pseudo-hypergradient method that estimates the missing Jacobian $\nabla _{\mathbf{x}}\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\mathbf{x})$ using finite differences of $\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\cdot)$. For each UL coordinate, LeGo-BiO constructs a decision vector subject to 1-sparse updates, thereby isolating the corresponding Jacobian column needed in the UL gradient computation. This avoids the directional-projection limitation of full-parameter response differences and, unlike derivative-free/zeroth-order approximations of the entire UL gradient, preserves the available first-order gradient information with respect to the UL variables for more accurate UL gradient evaluation. We establish convergence guarantees for LeGo-BiO in both deterministic and stochastic settings under an LL error-bound/Polyak-Lojasiewicz-type condition, without requiring LL strong convexity. Our bounds yield an $O(T^{-1})$ rate in the deterministic setting and an $O(T^{-1/2})$ rate in the stochastic setting when the LL approximation error decreases geometrically. Experiments demonstrate competitive performance of LeGo-BiO despite being agnostic to the LL objective.

title: Energy-efficient codon optimization on thermodynamic hardware
text:
Title: Energy-efficient codon optimization on thermodynamic hardware
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The growing energy demand for computation is becoming increasingly unsustainable. Thermodynamic computing, which harnesses physical thermal fluctuations as a computational resource rather than suppressing them, offers orders-of-magnitude energy savings for probabilistic and combinatorial tasks. Pharmaceutical R&D, heavily reliant on computational optimization and sampling, is a natural application domain. Here we present what is, to our knowledge, the first concrete pharmaceutical application mapped to thermodynamic hardware with energy estimates grounded in prototype measurements. We reduce mRNA codon optimization, a combinatorial problem routinely solved in drug development, to sampling from an Ising model, making it directly executable on a thermodynamic sampling unit (TSU). Benchmarking three approaches (Potts sampling, Ising sampling, and a genetic algorithm baseline) on the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, we find that all achieve comparable optimization quality (scores ~234-240), but energy estimates based on validated hardware models indicate that a TSU could solve this problem using approximately 10e6 times less energy than a conventional GPU. All code is released under an open-source license.

title: Nonlocal magic of fermions is bounded by entanglement fluctuations and is logarithmic for free fermions
text:
Title: Nonlocal magic of fermions is bounded by entanglement fluctuations and is logarithmic for free fermions
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Free-fermion states are classically simulable, yet, written as qubits, they typically carry extensive magic, the quantum resource that stabilizer circuits lack. Part of this magic is nonlocal: local unitaries acting separately on two parts of the system cannot remove it. If these local unitaries are restricted to Gaussian ones, the nonlocal magic grows linearly with the number $m$ of partially entangled fermion pairs. We show that this growth is an artifact of the Gaussian restriction: local Gaussian unitaries minimize the nonlocal stabilizer Rényi entropy for up to three pairs, but not from four pairs on. General local non-Gaussian unitaries that respect fermion parity take $m$ free-fermion pairs to fermionic Bell pairs with a fidelity that decays at most as $1/\sqrt m$ compared to exponential decay with Gaussian unitaries, so the nonlocal magic drops from linear to logarithmic in $m$. The reason is statistical --- Bell pairs have equal Schmidt weights, that is, a fully degenerate entanglement spectrum, and a state can stay far from them only if its Schmidt weights are spread over many orders of magnitude. This spread is measured by the capacity of entanglement $C_E$, the variance of the entanglement Hamiltonian, and the nonlocal magic of any fermionic state grows at most logarithmically with $C_E$. Free-fermion pairs add to $C_E$ independently, so $C_E$ grows only linearly in $m$, and this leads to the stabilizer fidelity decreasing at most as $1/\sqrt m$. Almost all the magic of free fermions, including Hartree--Fock and BCS mean-field states, is therefore local.

title: Drug-like antibodies with low immunogenicity in human panels designed with Latent-X2
text:
Title: Drug-like antibodies with low immunogenicity in human panels designed with Latent-X2
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Drug discovery has long sought computational systems capable of designing drug-like molecules directly: developable and non-immunogenic from the start. Here we introduce Latent-X2, a frontier generative model that achieves this goal through zero-shot design of antibodies with strong binding affinities, drug-like properties, and, for the first time for any de novo generated antibody, confirmed low immunogenicity in human donor panels. Latent-X2 is an all-atom model conditioned on target structure, epitope specification, and optional antibody framework, jointly generating sequences and structures while modelling the bound complex. Testing only 4 to 24 designs per target in each modality, we successfully generated VHH and scFv antibodies against 9 of 18 evaluated targets, achieving a 50% target-level success rate with picomolar to nanomolar binding affinities. Designed molecules exhibit developability profiles that match or exceed those of approved antibody therapeutics, including expression yield, aggregation propensity, polyreactivity, hydrophobicity, and thermal stability, without optimization, filtering, or selection. In the first immunogenicity assessment of any AI-generated antibody, representative de novo VHH binders targeting TNFL9 exhibit both potent target engagement and low immunogenicity across T-cell proliferation and cytokine release assays. The model generalizes beyond antibodies: against K-Ras, long considered undruggable, we generated macrocyclic peptide binders competitive with trillion-scale mRNA display screens. These properties emerge directly from the model, demonstrating the therapeutic viability of zero-shot molecular design, now available without AI infrastructure or coding expertise at https://platform.latentlabs.com.

title: Cross-Platform Benchmarking of GHZ-State Generation in Quantum Processors via Cloud Services
text:
Title: Cross-Platform Benchmarking of GHZ-State Generation in Quantum Processors via Cloud Services
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Quantum computing has rapidly evolved into a diverse ecosystem of hardware platforms that differ in their underlying technologies and operational characteristics. Consequently, benchmarking has become essential for identifying the strengths of quantum processors, comparing their performance, and enabling informed decisions when selecting the most appropriate quantum computing platform for specific applications. In this work, we benchmark nine commercially accessible quantum processors from five vendors, spanning superconducting and trapped-ion technologies, using the multipartite entanglement benchmark from the QuSquare suite. All experiments were performed through remote cloud-access services, with the default compilation of each provider and without error mitigation, reflecting the performance experienced by end users. The benchmark estimates the fidelity of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states by direct fidelity estimation and searches for the largest GHZ state whose fidelity is compatible, within the statistical error, with the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) threshold $F=1/2$. Our results reveal a substantial gap between the total number of physical qubits available on a processor and the size of the largest GHZ state passing the benchmark: the best superconducting processors reach $N^*=27$ and $N^*=24$ qubits, less than a quarter of their registers, whereas the 12-qubit trapped-ion processor passes with its full register. We further show that median calibration data are poor predictors of the benchmark outcome, and that the reported sizes depend strongly on the statistical decision rule: requiring certified GME reduces the number of devices that succeed at any tested size from nine to four. These results provide a baseline for future cross-platform benchmarking of quantum processors.

title: Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
text:
Title: Distributionally Robust Indirect-Feedback Stochastic MPC with Gelbrich Ambiguity Sets
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Stochastic model predictive control uses disturbance statistics to set safety margins. Errors in these statistics can invalidate the safety guarantees. This paper therefore describes the uncertainty in the disturbance mean and covariance by a prescribed Gelbrich ambiguity set. This contains distributions of any shape whose moments are close in the Gelbrich distance to the nominal values, including distributions with unbounded support. For linear time-invariant systems with additive disturbances, we build on the indirect feedback paradigm, propagate this moment uncertainty along the error dynamics, and obtain a closed-form constraint tightening that is computed offline. Robustness enters as a single additive term that grows with the size of the ambiguity set, so the online problem remains a quadratic program. Recursive feasibility and closed-loop satisfaction of conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints hold for every disturbance distribution in the set. We illustrate the method on a linearized planar quadrotor.

title: SAWs, trails, kites, patterns
text:
Title: SAWs, trails, kites, patterns
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

A self-avoiding walk (SAW) on a vertex-transitive graph $G$ is a path that visits no vertex more than once; a trail is a path that traverses no edge more than once. The number of $n$-step self-avoiding walks (respectively, trails) starting at a given vertex has order $μ(G)^n$ (respectively, $μ_{\text{T}}(G)^n$), where $μ(G)$ is called the connective constant and $μ_{\text{T}}(G)$ is the trail constant. It is immediate that $μ=μ_{\text{T}}$ if $G$ either has degree $3$ or less, or is a tree. We prove a necessary and sufficient condition for the strict inequality $μ< μ_{\text{T}}$ if $G$ has degree $4$ or more and is not a tree, and in addition $G$ possesses a so-called height function. This condition is satisfied whenever the height function is transitive. The core of the proof is a pattern theorem for graphs possessing height functions, and this is achieved using an unpublished argument for ${\Bbb Z}^d$ by Hammersley, reported by Janse van Rensburg et al. (J. Stat. Phys. 85, 1996, 103--130). Some ancillary results are included concerning SAWs on the line graph of $G$.

title: Robust Geometric Gates for QCCD Architecture
text:
Title: Robust Geometric Gates for QCCD Architecture
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

The trapped-ion quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) is a promising route toward scalable quantum computing. However, the frequency offset during shuttling operations introduce significant decoherence and control errors, severely degrading gate fidelity on transported ions. Here, using a room-temperature planar chip trap, we demonstrate a robust and universal single-qubit gate set in the QCCD architecture. Based on a recently proposed path-optimizable noncyclic geometric scheme, we show that dynamic noise is strongly suppressed even when multiple shuttling operations are interleaved with gate execution, achieving substantially higher fidelities than conventional dynamical gates. This robustness is further validated in a multi-ion system containing up to 33 qubits. With inherent robustness and adaptability to varying shuttle distances and ion numbers, our work offers a plug-and-play solution for building robust quantum primitives for the QCCD platform.

title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
text:
Title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Intrinsic color centers are investigated in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation delta SCF calculations identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. A comparison of their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It exhibits the highest calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate of 43.9 MHz and ZPL quantum efficiency of 11.8% among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation yields a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a multimode photoluminescence calculation gives a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37%, indicating a dominant zero-phonon contribution. The predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) also has the smallest photon-energy separation from the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets among the candidates. These results identify VVa1+ as a promising intrinsic color center for fiber-based quantum communication, with quantum frequency upconversion offering a route from its strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands.

title: State and spatial completion of 1D premixed flames for hydrogen and methane combustion
text:
Title: State and spatial completion of 1D premixed flames for hydrogen and methane combustion
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Accurate prediction of chemically reacting flows requires resolving the nonlinear coupling among transport and chemical reaction operators, often at substantial computational cost. This work investigates Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) for learning mappings from partial spatial profiles to steady, one-dimensional, freely propagating hydrogen-air and methane-air flame solutions. Using a database of over 15,000 cases generated with Cantera, two different FNO models were trained to reconstruct the complete thermochemical state from a smaller set of input variables. The first model concerns state completion which uses only temperature, fuel, and oxygen mass-fraction profiles to reconstruct the remaining 7 species for hydrogen flames and 51 species for methane flames along with the missing velocity. The second model performs spatial completion, using upstream thermochemical profiles extending into the initial temperature rise to reconstruct the withheld downstream structure. Evaluation on 2,625 test cases per fuel, excluded from training, shows recovery of reaction-zone species profiles, including radicals and intermediates, across the sampled conditions. These results demonstrate reconstruction of species and velocity profiles that are not supplied as inputs, and recovery of downstream structure outside the observed region. Reconstruction with missing species or incomplete spatial coverage suggests potential for using learned operators in estimating inaccessible thermochemical quantities and developing reduced-state representations for combustion applications.

title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
text:
Title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot's physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.

title: Analytical framework for interpreting thermoreflectance measurements of nanoline gratings under finite spot illumination
text:
Title: Analytical framework for interpreting thermoreflectance measurements of nanoline gratings under finite spot illumination
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

A frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR)-based technique is presented to measure the effective thermal properties of a material stack whose surface is patterned with metallic nanoline gratings that are heated and probed by lasers. An analytical heat diffusion model is derived for predicting the FDTR phase response that incorporates a finite laser spot radius with a Gaussian intensity profile for the pump and probe lasers, as well as the dimensions of the nanoline grating. The model is validated by comparing with measurements of Au nanoline gratings, with widths ranging from 100 to 1000 nm, fabricated on a-SiO$_2$ and $c$-sapphire substrates. Due to the short phonon mean free paths (MFPs) in these substrates, thermal transport remains in the diffusive regime for the whole range of nanoline widths. The model and the measurement show excellent agreement across different laser spot radii and nanoline widths, with a bulk thermal conductivity value of $c$-sapphire and the thermal boundary conductances at the Au-Cr/a-SiO$_2$ and Au-Cr/$c$-sapphire interfaces comparable to our prior measurements and the literature. The validated model will serve as a robust baseline for extending this method to measure effective thermal conductivity as a function of the heater size. This approach is particularly relevant for materials where non-diffusive thermal transport regimes enable probing phonon MFP dependent contributions to the thermal conductivity.

title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
text:
Title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.

title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
text:
Title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

RLVR trains language models to reason by rewarding correct final answers. A widely used algorithm, group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), gives every token of a solution the same credit, so dense process rewards have been proposed to credit intermediate steps, for example with a Monte-Carlo reward that scores each step by sampling continuations from it. Comparing such a reward with GRPO per training update, or vetting it with a gradient test on a single batch, leaves out what it costs: in our setting, the continuations alone take 91% of all generated tokens. We introduce a matched-compute protocol that gives every training intervention the same budget, measured in generated tokens and training GPU-hours, and tests it in preregistered studies with controls for side effects. Across 1,668 runs on six models, matching compute reverses the ranking. On Qwen2.5-1.5B, the Monte-Carlo reward leads standard GRPO per update, yet ends 14.3 percentage points lower at equal tokens and 7.8 points lower at equal training time, and none of four dense-reward variants outperforms GRPO even with as much training time. A per-token gradient test orders these rewards as training does but overestimates each by one to two points, as much as the gains it is meant to detect. In contrast, training on the prompts whose predicted success is nearest 1/2 improves accuracy at matched compute, by 1.7 points on Qwen3-0.6B and 0.8 on Qwen2.5-1.5B. These gains replicate on fresh seeds and unseen problems, and a simple rule, that the candidate prompts are predicted to fail more often than not, predicted where they appear in five of six preregistered tests. Both gains come early in training, and standard GRPO with twice the initial learning rate comes within half a point of them. We argue that training interventions should be validated at matched compute, which overturns some apparent gains and confirms others.

title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
text:
Title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Masked diffusion models generate text by reversing a stochastic masking process. Unlike autoregressive LLMs, which generate text one token at a time, they can reveal many tokens in parallel, at the price of an error, since tokens revealed together are drawn independently. We show that this trade-off maps onto the statistical physics of driven many-particle systems. (i) For any data, the error of parallel generation is the entropy production of the generation process relative to the reversed masking process. (ii) For Markov data, generation is a random sequential adsorption process with labelled gaps, which we solve exactly for any number of steps. (iii) For many steps, the error becomes the dissipation of a slowly driven system: the unmasking schedule plays the role of the driving protocol, the number of steps that of its duration, and the error is set by a thermodynamic metric that we obtain in closed form from the mutual information between tokens. Optimal schedules are geodesics of this metric. The exact solution shows how correlations in the text shape both the error and the quality of the output. The longer the correlations, the more the error concentrates at the start of generation. Schedules that start with small steps then gain more, both in path error and in perplexity, and need fewer steps to reach their asymptotic behaviour.

title: CLARA: Clarification of Language Ambiguity through Result Analysis for Natural-Language Cancer Genomics Queries
text:
Title: CLARA: Clarification of Language Ambiguity through Result Analysis for Natural-Language Cancer Genomics Queries
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

A natural language interface can be used to make cancer genomics databases easier to use, but even if a question is perfectly fluent, its scientific meaning can be ambiguous. We propose CLARA, a framework that represents a question as a typed scientific query specification, considers a few possible interpretations, executes them, and asks for clarification when the estimates diverge. CLARA was assessed on mutation-prevalence contrasts among eight TCGA PanCancer Atlas cohorts and a 30-gene panel. This benchmark consisted of 330 unique executable contrasts varying in mutation scope, assay denominator, and sample context; 115 contrasts were result-sensitive and 215 were result-stable, per the preregistered definition of relative divergence greater than 0.10 or absolute divergence greater than 5 percentage points. An independently implemented pandas execution engine perfectly replicated all 660 results from the SQLite engine. In a separate 120-question LLM-generated, manually vetted language stress test, CLARA recognized all 60 result-sensitive contrasts and needlessly clarified 13 of 60 stable contrasts (accuracy 89.2%, sensitivity/recall 100%, specificity 78.3%). Standalone machine learning had superior overall accuracy (97.5%) but missed one critical contrast. This demonstrates that downstream execution can distinguish consequential from inconsequential ambiguity and reveal an explicit trade-off between safety and burden.

title: A Shortcut to Structure in AlphaFold 3
text:
Title: A Shortcut to Structure in AlphaFold 3
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

AlphaFold 3 predicts protein structures with remarkable accuracy, yet how structural information emerges within the model remains poorly understood. Here, through causal interventions on internal representations and direct probing of every Pairformer block, we trace the formation of global protein geometry and identify the multiple sequence alignment (MSA) as a structural shortcut to the fold. Removing the MSA largely preserves local secondary structure while disrupting the long-range relationships that define global topology. Restoring the MSA-enriched pair representation at only forty residues recovers most of this lost organization, including at pairs never directly modified. This contribution depends on the detailed direction of the MSA module's output rather than its magnitude. The Pairformer rapidly converts this signal into global geometry: the final fold becomes recoverable by approximately block 9 of 48 for a majority of proteins, roughly twenty-seven blocks before the model's decoder can render it, whereas without the MSA it remains inaccessible for most proteins throughout the pass. Which homologs are supplied shapes this trajectory more strongly than which query is supplied; it persists for a designed query that never evolved but collapses for a shuffled sequence. Most importantly, an alignment built for a different protein that shares the fold, supplied only at the structurally corresponding columns, raises the median TM-score against experiment from 0.44 to 0.72, while the same alignment shifted a few residues along the chain performs worse than supplying no alignment at all. What AlphaFold 3 reads from an alignment is therefore a description of the fold itself, transferable between proteins that share one, rather than the query's own evolutionary history. This explains both its accuracy and the limits of what it has solved.

title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
text:
Title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.

title: Entropic Martingale Optimal Transport with Wasserstein Relaxed Marginal Constraints
text:
Title: Entropic Martingale Optimal Transport with Wasserstein Relaxed Marginal Constraints
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Martingale optimal transport (MOT) is a fundamental framework in robust finance, yet its stability under marginal perturbation no longer holds in high dimensions $d\geq 2$. In this paper, we introduce Wasserstein-relaxed entropic martingale optimal transport (WEMOT), which combines Wasserstein relaxation of the second marginal with entropy regularization. This formulation ensures stability under perturbations of the marginals, thereby facilitating numerical implementation. We establish strong duality and dual attainment for WEMOT, which leads to efficient Sinkhorn-type algorithms. We further prove a convergence rate of WEMOT to MOT as regularization parameters vanish, and also the quantitative stability of WEMOT with respect to marginal perturbations.

title: Integrable AdS$_2$ branes in mixed flux AdS$_3$
text:
Title: Integrable AdS$_2$ branes in mixed flux AdS$_3$
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We show that half-BPS D3-branes wrapping AdS$_2\times$S$^2$ in AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times$T$^4$ with mixed NSNS and RR flux define integrable boundary conditions for the supercoset sigma model of the Green--Schwarz superstring. This extends the integrable D-branes of Dekel and Oz to backgrounds with a Wess--Zumino term, and previous bosonic results for mixed flux to the full superstring. Using the D3-brane action, we find that the electric and magnetic worldvolume fields that stabilise the branes at generic positions are obtained from those of the AdS$_2\times$S$^2$ branes of the WZW model by the same $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ rotation that maps the pure NSNS background to the mixed flux one, acting on the D3-brane as electric--magnetic duality.
