We integrate the diarization conditioning into a longform Parakeet backbone (DiCoP) and add cross-speaker attention, which lets the model attend across the speaker dimension so that speakers are no longer decoded in isolation, and an STNO mask refiner that re-estimates the diarization-derived conditioning. As conversational data with genuine multi-speaker interaction is scarce, we scale training with a pseudo-labeling pipeline that mines 5.4k hours of in-the-wild multi-speaker audio from YODAS2. Combining these with synthetic and real data yields state-of-the-art results across several meeting benchmarks. We open-source the resulting models, DiCoP and Pandemonium, and the pseudo-labeled data.

title: Constraining the Inner Dark Matter Profiles of Strong-Lensing Galaxy Clusters
text:
Title: Constraining the Inner Dark Matter Profiles of Strong-Lensing Galaxy Clusters
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

We present mass modeling of three strong lensing galaxy clusters found in the Dark Energy Survey utilizing Hubble Space Telescope imaging for lens modeling, and complementary constraints from Chandra X-ray observations. All three clusters are relaxed and have giant arc or ring lens structures ideal for constraints on the dark matter distribution. The strong lens modeling and X-ray temperatures yield consistent total cluster mass estimates. We find these clusters have best-fit X-ray temperatures of $2.7 - 6.2$ keV and total masses of M$_{200} = (1-6) \times 10^{14} M_{\odot}$. Our lens models parameterize dark matter distribution with a generalized Navarro-Frenk-White (GNFW) density profile. While the GNFW profile allows the inner dark matter slope to vary, we find in all cases that the inner slopes are consistent with the standard NFW density profile $γ^{DM} = 1$. The X-ray surface brightness distributions for all three clusters are generally symmetric with no significant substructure, supporting the conclusion that these are relaxed clusters. In addition, we find generally low values of the external shear magnitude with median values ranging $|γ^{ext}| = 0.04-0.09$ and consistent with zero for two of the clusters.

title: From Fluent Text to Ontology-Compatible Definitions: A Quality-Control Agentic Workflow
text:
Title: From Fluent Text to Ontology-Compatible Definitions: A Quality-Control Agentic Workflow
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Biomedical ontologies are structured knowledge systems that must evolve continuously to represent newly emerging knowledge, but their manual maintenance remains time-consuming and laborintensive. Textual definitions are especially costly because they must be readable to humans and compatible with controlled entities, relations, and logical constraints. Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising way to assist ontology engineering tasks, including definition generation. However, textual plausibility does not guarantee knowledge-system compatibility. A generated definition may be fluent and close to a reference definition, yet still fail to ground its implied entities or violate ontology-level constraints. Directly inserting such definitions into ontology libraries may therefore introduce entity-level hallucinations and logical inconsistencies. To address this problem, we propose two structured-knowledge incompatibility metrics, Entity Error Rate (EER) and Logical Inconsistency Rate (LIR), to quantify entity grounding and logical consistency for LLM-generated ontology definitions. We further develop an agentic quality-control (QC) workflow that treats definition generation as an iterative process rather than a direct decoding step: it generates definitions, extracts axioms, checks entity existence and logical consistency, and uses the resulting diagnostics to drive repair loops. Comprehensive experiments on Disease Ontology, Uberon Ontology, and Uberon-ConstraintStress demonstrate that EER and LIR complement conventional reference-based metrics by evaluating whether generated content can be grounded and checked inside the target ontology. The workflow effectively decreases EER while maintaining strong conventional text-generation performance. LIR further exposes sparse ontology-level logical failures that are invisible to text similarity metrics, although their repair remains limited.

title: The Self-repelling Burglar
text:
Title: The Self-repelling Burglar
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

In this paper, we study the conditional location of $X_T$ given the local time profile $L_T(\cdot)$ for two non-Markovian self-interacting processes: the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM) and the true self-repelling motion (TSRM). For TSRM, our novel approach yields a new proof of Dumaz's clever burglar result [Dumaz 2012].

title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
text:
Title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.

title: Scaling Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks with Agent Swarms
text:
Title: Scaling Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks with Agent Swarms
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Prompt injections have emerged as one of the top security risks faced by AI agents today. Early work in prompt injection attacks looked at simple tool-call agents and static attack payloads, and were saturated since mid-2025. As of Fall 2026, human red-teaming may be nearing saturation, especially on the Gemini family of models. In this work, we argue that despite this apparent plateau, prompt injection attacks are still possible and continued effort into prompt injection defense is needed. We design a new synthetic evaluation dataset which uses random non-malicious actions as adversarial goals. Such dataset design helps us to evaluate prompt injection robustness as a model ability to respect instruction hierarchy, and disentangle this ability from model knowledge of security practices. We show that an agentic attacker of increased capabilities can reliably trick model to follow instructions in tool output in our evaluation, even for models previously considered robust on public prompt injection benchmarks such as GraySwan Arena. This shows that current frontier defenses may require proactive, automated red-teaming to remain resilient to increasingly capable adversaries.

title: PULSES: multi-agent AI for autonomous excited-state model building and dynamics
text:
Title: PULSES: multi-agent AI for autonomous excited-state model building and dynamics
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Simulating molecular excited-state processes requires resolving electronic and nuclear dynamics, but the cost of direct quantum-chemical calculations limits accessible system sizes and timescales. Machine-learning models can extend these simulations, yet they often need to be tailored to specific molecular systems and scientific objectives. Building and deploying such models requires coordinated decisions across conformational sampling, quantum-chemical labelling, model training, validation and dynamics. Here we introduce Paired agents for Unified Learning and Simulation of Excited States (PULSES), a multi-agent system that automates this workflow within expert-approved boundaries. A human expert and planner define the scientific objective, methods and decision boundaries, while an orchestrator coordinates domain agents and artifact-specific scientific assurance during execution. We evaluate PULSES on 15 computational chemistry tasks and demonstrate end-to-end applications to perylene exciton Hamiltonians, solvent-dependent biphenyl relaxation, and excited-state proton transfer in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline. These results demonstrate traceable, expert-bounded construction and deployment of specialized excited-state models, while retaining scientific validation as a requirement rather than assuming that successful execution establishes correctness.

title: Learning Epidemic Threshold Equations from Simulation: REEBLRA, an Interpretable Bayesian Classification Framework for Reproduction Numbers
text:
Title: Learning Epidemic Threshold Equations from Simulation: REEBLRA, an Interpretable Bayesian Classification Framework for Reproduction Numbers
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

The basic reproduction number, $R_0$, is central to infectious-disease modelling, yet analytic expressions can be difficult to derive for high-dimensional, nonlinear, or structurally complex models. We introduce REEBLRA ($R_0$ Equation Estimation using Bayesian Logistic Regression Algorithm), an interpretable framework that learns explicit surrogate equations for epidemic thresholds from parameter--response data. Rather than directly regressing $R_0$, REEBLRA estimates $\Pr\{R_0(\boldsymbolθ)>c\}$ for parameter vector $\boldsymbolθ$ and threshold $c$. It provides a binary equation for classifying epidemic invasion ($R_0>1$) and successive threshold equations defining ordered brackets that approximate $R_0$, the expected number of secondary infections caused by a typical case in a fully susceptible population. The resulting equations support parameter screening, sensitivity interpretation, threshold classification, and exploratory analysis when analytic derivation is cumbersome. Bayesian logistic regression using standardized polynomial-like features and proper weakly informative priors yields regularized estimates, posterior uncertainty, and finite coefficients under complete or quasi-complete separation. We establish a mechanistic--surrogate concordance principle linking the full fitted-score gradient to the local gradient of $\log R_0$ under explicit regularity and tangency assumptions, allowing conditional interpretation of threshold directions. Across seven analytic-label benchmarks associated with ODE models, including a 15-compartment five-group SIR system, five-fold binary AUC was 0.999--1.000 and ordered-bracket accuracy was 0.951--0.998. REEBLRA complements rather than replaces mechanistic derivations, bridging simulation, machine learning, and reproduction-number analysis. An accompanying Shiny app supports implementation.

title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
text:
Title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

title: A full chemical network treatment of supermassive black hole seed formation from dark matter annihilation or decay
text:
Title: A full chemical network treatment of supermassive black hole seed formation from dark matter annihilation or decay
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The recent discoveries of high-redshift quasars at $z\sim6-10.1$ present a challenge to conventional supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenarios: their central SMBHs are too large to have grown from early stellar remnants, even under efficient super-Eddington accretion. An alternative approach is the direct collapse of primordial, dust- and metal-free gas clouds into black hole seeds as early as $z\sim20$. To prevent fragmentation from highly efficient molecular hydrogen cooling and allow such a collapse, a strong flux of UV photons is required to photodissociate molecular hydrogen, suppressing star formation. We investigate whether the decay or annihilation of dark matter with masses below $\sim200$ eV can produce sufficient UV radiation, both from the cosmological background and within early dark matter halos. Using thermal simulations of a one-zone primordial gas cloud model with the Grackle chemistry and cooling library, we map the resulting gas behavior across a range of dark matter lifetimes, cross sections, and masses. From this, we determine regions of parameter space where direct collapse into an SMBH is possible and the corresponding maximum halo mass required.

title: Compression Through a Context Lens: Evaluating Adaptation, Quantization, and Distillation in Arabic Legal LLMs
text:
Title: Compression Through a Context Lens: Evaluating Adaptation, Quantization, and Distillation in Arabic Legal LLMs
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Model compression can facilitate the deployment of large language models in resource-constrained legal settings, but its effects on domain-specific performance may depend on the evaluation protocol. We investigate this issue using ArabLegalEval, a Saudi Arabic legal benchmark, under both with-context and no-context evaluation. The former provides supporting legal passages, while the latter assesses performance without external context. Removing the context produces accuracy gaps of up to 27 percentage points for the base model. We examine three stages: domain adaptation, quantization, and knowledge distillation across FANAR-9B, JAIS-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B. Four-bit quantization reduces model memory by 64-71%, with changes in no-context MCQ accuracy ranging from -3.2 to +1.6 percentage points. Distillation produces more variable results, with accuracy generally declining as student size decreases. A Qwen2.5-7B student distilled from FANAR achieves 76.6% no-context accuracy, compared with 77.2% for its teacher. Our findings suggest that no-context evaluation provides a useful complement to context-supported testing when assessing the effects of adaptation and compression on Arabic legal language models.

title: Luminosity-weighted galaxy and gravitational wave cross-correlations
text:
Title: Luminosity-weighted galaxy and gravitational wave cross-correlations
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Cross-correlations of galaxies and gravitational waves (GW) can be used to extract cosmological parameters and the gravitational wave bias. In this work, we study how to include galaxy luminosities in these spatial cross-correlations, inspired by the standard approach of dark sirens line-of-sight redshift priors. We present a formalism to include luminosity information in galaxy-GW simulations and study the effects of assigning a hosting probability that depends on luminosity through a simple power law $p_{\rm{host}} \propto L^β$ with $β\in \{0,1,2\}$ corresponding to uniformly, linear and quadratically weighted in luminosity. This effectively changes the GW linear bias with respect to dark matter and, in principle, allows to gain signal-to-noise and a sharper measurement of cosmological parameters. For a realistic luminosity dependence of the galaxy bias taken from DESI data, the gain is marginal, making the method robust to different luminosity weighting prescriptions. We show that the cross-correlation inference is able to recover the injected GW bias within $10\%$ if there is a mismatch between the injected linear bias of host galaxies and observed galaxies, provided that one sticks to relatively large scales. We also show that the Hubble constant and matter energy density can be recovered to $0.5\%$ and $5\%$ respectively with a third generation network of GW detectors, regardless of the modeling of the GW bias.

title: Turkish Multimodal Video Fact-Checking: A New Dataset and a Comparison of Zero-Shot Agentic and Fine-Tuned Systems
text:
Title: Turkish Multimodal Video Fact-Checking: A New Dataset and a Comparison of Zero-Shot Agentic and Fine-Tuned Systems
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Video-based misinformation spreads rapidly on social media, but almost all existing fact-checking systems focus exclusively on English text. Tools for low-resource languages such as Turkish are severely limited. In this work, we present TeViD (Turkish Video Fact-checking Dataset), to the best of our knowledge the first multimodal video fact-checking dataset for Turkish. We compiled the dataset from articles published by Teyit.org, an IFCN-certified organisation, and enriched it with translated Snopes articles and synthetic examples to reduce class imbalance. Building on TeViD, we develop two verification pipelines that share the same open-source base model. First, in 3MFact-TR (Pipeline 1), we adapt the multi-role 3MFact framework to Turkish with the Qwen2.5-7B large language model and the Qwen2-VL-7B vision-language model, and add three modules of our own: a semantic inconsistency checker, a 5W1H question manager, and a bilingual evidence retriever that excludes fact-checking sites to prevent leakage. Second, as our Fine-Tuned Model (Pipeline 2), we fine-tune a single Qwen2.5-7B with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to produce closed-book verdicts from the claim and the video's textual description. We report accuracy, macro F1, True class F1, and True class recall for both systems, together with ablation studies.

title: Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models
text:
Title: Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have become an increasingly popular means of translating Large Language Model (LLM) hidden state vectors into a human-comprehensible list of features or symbols. As such, SAEs may provide insight into an LLM's knowledge representation and internal ``mental'' grammar - topics of pragmatic interest for mechanistic interpretation of AI behavior and of theoretical interest for the study of in silico representations of human language. Language models with fewer than 100M parameters, trained on small corpora, nonetheless exhibit strong grammatical competence and discourse coherence, despite producing content of limited reliability. We use SAEs that we trained on one such model (Pythia-70M) to conduct an in-depth examination of how a single grammatical phenomenon, number agreement, is represented and processed in an LLM. We demonstrate the mechanism and the methodology by which SAEs can be used to find and propagate ``plural noun'', ``plural matrix subject'', and ``generate a plural verb'' features which cause the LLM to produce plural verb forms such as ``are'', ``do'', or ``have'' instead of ``is'', ``does'', and ``has'' in response to prompts such as ``the men in the park''. We show that intervening to remove these features from the hidden states of plural subject noun tokens causes the model to produce singular verbs instead, and vice versa. We also show that corresponding ``singular noun'' and ``generate a singular verb'' features are not as effective for this task. This asymmetry suggests that Pythia-70m makes use of a privative representation of grammatical number in English. These findings replicated with larger LLMs Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.1-8b yielded similar results. Our main contribution is a novel approach to the use of SAEs to understanding how LLMs encode human language that addresses a number of technical and methodological challenges.

title: Learning Between the Lines: Interaction Interpolation in a Multi Element Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
text:
Title: Learning Between the Lines: Interaction Interpolation in a Multi Element Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

The continuous development of machine learning inter-atomic potentials (MLIAPs)has greatly accelerated materials research in recent years. However, the need to con- struct custom MLIAPs for each unique problem remains a bottleneck which raises the question of the transferability of MLIAPs. While foundation MLIAPs can achieve transferability due to the broad coverage of chemical space represented in their training sets, their size and computational cost limits their routine use. We address this gap by developing a lightweight general-purpose MLIAP for metal alloys spanning twelve elements (Al, Sc, Ti, V, Cu, Zn, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta, W). Here, we utilize a step-wise active learning (AL) approach to develop a compact yet diverse dataset and model that generalizes well by interpolating from previously seen interactions. The resulting potentials transfer effectively to unseen, higher body-order alloys systems, requiring only unary and binary training data to capture ternary and quaternary systems. The model also transfers well to new elements via an alchemical extrapolation within the network, requiring only unary data for the new element and its alloys. These findings suggest that MLIAPs trained on targeted, diversity-driven datasets provide transferability at a relatively low computational cost, offering a practical path toward general-purpose, resource-efficient MLIAPs for materials modeling.

title: Algebraic coefficients of fractional parentage for three particles in the oscillator Jacobi basis
text:
Title: Algebraic coefficients of fractional parentage for three particles in the oscillator Jacobi basis
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We present a closed-form construction of the orbital coefficients of fractional parentage (CFP) of three identical particles in the translationally invariant harmonic oscillator (HO) Jacobi basis. These are usually obtained by numerically diagonalizing a permutation operator in every energy-angular-momentum block. We show this diagonalization is unnecessary. Dressing the class operator $P_{13} + P_{23}$ with the single unitary $W = H^1 Φ$ -- a fixed complexification followed by the HO bracket with mass parameter $d=1$ -- turns it into the label swap times an integer. Every CFP is then the single ket $|K_{i,s}\rangle = 2Q^s W^\dagger|i\rangle$ -- a 2-scaled, sign-decorated column of the $d=1$ bracket restricted to one $e_2$-parity of the labels -- whose norm, $1 + s\langle i | J | i \rangle$, is itself a single matrix element. The same $W$ carries label parity into swap symmetry, $W Q^s W^\dagger = R^s$, making the bookkeeping collapse. The eigenvalues are exact integers $\pm 2$ and $\pm 1$ labeling the $S(3)$ symmetry classes. The construction is uniform in $E$, $L$ and symmetry class, reducing CFP-specific work from $O(n^3)$ to $O(n^2)$ in block dimension. An eigensolver remains only inside the bracket engine supplying $H^1$, where all residual numerical error originates. We implement this on an SU(3)-basis bracket engine, checking all 1301 blocks up to $E=50$ (912 366 CFPs, largest block $2907 \times 2907$): the $S(3)$ class assignment is exact everywhere. The residual numerical error (entirely the bracket engine's) stays below $10^{-8}$ for $E \leq 35$, restoring to $\leq 10^{-22}$ via a quadruple-precision build beyond that. We further validate against independently generated antisymmetrization data of a production three-nucleon code, including the $^3$He ground-state energy.

title: What an Observer Reads off a Holographic Screen
text:
Title: What an Observer Reads off a Holographic Screen
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

What does an observer read off a holographic screen that is an array of qubits rather than a surface? In the generalized holographic principle the interaction between two separable systems acts on such a screen as a weighted sum, up to an overall prefactor, of commuting observables with values plus and minus one. When the weights are nonnegative and the prefactor is one and the joint eigenspaces are lines, everything a probe reads off the spectrum depends only on the list of weights, which we call the profile. On the screen with equal weights summing to one the running dimension read by a diffusion probe falls short of two at unit time by at most twice the reciprocal of the number of qubits; a geometric profile gives instead, through its level count, a plateau of any positive height. An observer correlates sets of qubits; its readout carries a profile at a given weighting when the levels it reads, counted with multiplicity, are those of a screen with one weight per set. We prove that a readout carries a profile at every weighting exactly when the distinct nonzero traces of its qubits are linearly independent over the field with two elements, the trace of a qubit being the list of sets that contain it; such a readout is a partition of the qubits it covers up to an invertible recoding, and a dependent one carries a profile only on finitely many proper linear subspaces of weightings. Refining a grouping without end builds a tower whose boundary is a profinite set and hence a condensed set, on which a strictly positive compatible profile separates the locally constant functions by a distance. Applications certify probabilistic and strong contextuality and give the leading shortfall of the distance between the poles of the fuzzy sphere; in a model of monogamous entanglement the pairs that weight-one threads representing operational ER=EPR can occupy at once are exactly the partial matchings.

title: The RAS-CCSD model, with applications for open-shell molecules
text:
Title: The RAS-CCSD model, with applications for open-shell molecules
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

The restricted active space coupled cluster singles and doubles (RAS-CCSD) model, and its pilot implementation is detailed. The approach offers a simple, pragmatic way to formulate a coupled cluster theory for open-shell and multireference systems. For ground state energies, errors (compared to FCI) are shown to be similar to those of unrestricted (spin-orbital) CCSD. For excited states, the errors of RAS-CCSD are generally larger, and adaptations to the methodology are needed to achieve an approach which is balanced for both ground and excited states. However, unlike unrestricted CCSD, the approach is spin-adapted and can be used to add dynamical correlation to a multideterminantal reference state.

title: Unconventional SOC-activated Altermagnetic Spin Splitting and Half-Angle Locking of Spin Transport
text:
Title: Unconventional SOC-activated Altermagnetic Spin Splitting and Half-Angle Locking of Spin Transport
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Conventional altermagnetic spin splitting arises from staggered exchange and sublattice-dependent anisotropic hopping without requiring spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Here we derive a low-energy effective model showing that SOC and staggered exchange can jointly activate additional spin splitting on momentum planes where the nonrelativistic contribution vanishes. In hexagonal $α$-MnTe, this SOC-activated contribution produces d-wave spin splitting near $Γ$ with out-of-plane spin polarization. Its leading angular pattern counter-rotates by half the in-plane Néel-vector rotation angle. First-principles spin-transport calculations reveal a corresponding approximate half-angle locking between the Néel-vector orientation and the electric-field directions maximizing the signed longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Analytical transport calculations based on the effective model trace this locking to the same angular coupling between momentum and the Néel vector that governs the spin-splitting pattern. Our findings connect the microscopic mechanism of SOC-activated altermagnetic spin splitting to directional spin transport, providing a theoretical basis for probing Néel-vector orientation and controlling spin-current generation.

title: Higher Integrability, Generalized Symmetries, and Partially Topological Field Theories
text:
Title: Higher Integrability, Generalized Symmetries, and Partially Topological Field Theories
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We exhibit a classical link between higher Lax integrability and generalized symmetries in a non-Lorentzian higher semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory on $M\times\mathbb CP^1$. The equations of motion determine a spectrally dependent flat higher connection on $M$ whose Laurent coefficients organise an infinite hierarchy of conserved quantities. We construct a spectral family of classical $(d_M-2)$-form symmetry line defects associated with the Lax connection, establish an action-preserving deformation law, and exhibit suitable gauge-invariant probes on which the induced transformations act nontrivially.

title: Initialization masks overcome decoding obstructions in compressed QAOA
text:
Title: Initialization masks overcome decoding obstructions in compressed QAOA
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

In compressed quantum optimization, a variational state is converted into a classical assignment by decoding noncommuting observables. We show that this step creates structural restrictions that changing the initialization can remove, even when increasing circuit depth cannot. For an explicit infinite family of connected cubic graphs on $n=3r$ vertices, with a fixed Pauli encoding and deterministic sign decoder, every all-plus QAOA circuit has cut at most $2r$, at every finite depth and every real angle sequence. A uniform signed product-state mask at fixed depth-one angles has expected cut $13r/4$, an additive advantage $5n/12$; an infinite subfamily admits an optimal mask. A second construction retains a linear depth-one separation under weak weighted couplings, a bounded cost-angle domain and a specified production-encoder ordering. Noiseless simulations then test classical mask selection before energy optimization. On 1,699 random cubic MaxCut instances, one selected mask achieves mean ratio $0.9100$, versus $0.7067$ for the all-plus $X$ baseline and $0.9125$ for the best of $r^2$ separately optimized random masks. On complete cohorts of weighted MaxCut, sparse Ising, Max-2-XOR and Max-2-SAT, the selected mask also improves on the baseline at every size, but it trails the pool at small sizes and leads it significantly only at the larger MaxCut and Ising sizes. Finite-pool order statistics separate the effect of selection from that of drawing a random mask. The results distinguish decoded expressivity from optimized energy and empirical performance; they do not establish a quantum computational advantage.

title: Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic: Adaptive Switching Costs for Robust Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
text:
Title: Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic: Adaptive Switching Costs for Robust Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Deliberation costs are commonly used in hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) to prevent options from collapsing to primitive actions. Existing approaches rely on fixed penalties or duration-based adaptations, both of which are indirect proxies for an option's utility. This paper argues that option persistence should instead depend on the opportunity cost of abandoning the current behavior. We propose the Opportunity-Cost Option-Critic ($OC^2$) framework, which defines a state-dependent deliberation cost using the positive value gap between the active option and its best alternative. This encourages persistence when the current option is clearly preferable and allows rapid switching when a better option emerges. We show that directly learning such costs leads to a degenerate zero-cost solution and introduces an auxiliary objective that aligns the learned cost with the value-gap target. The approach is evaluated in Four Rooms and Pinball domains under stationary, goal-shift, and geometry-shift conditions. In the Pinball goal-shift task, the $OC^2$ framework achieves a 52\% first-ten-episode success rate compared with 18\% for a fixed-cost baseline. The results suggest that opportunity-cost-based persistence improves adaptation in non-stationary environments.

title: Tersoff-NN: Hybrid Machine-Learned Bond-Order Extension of the Tersoff Potential
text:
Title: Tersoff-NN: Hybrid Machine-Learned Bond-Order Extension of the Tersoff Potential
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Accurate, robust, and efficient interatomic potentials are highly desirable for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Although machine-learning interatomic potentials can reproduce first-principles potential-energy surfaces with high accuracy, they typically incur higher computational costs than conventional empirical potentials and may be less reliable outside their training domains. We developed Tersoff-NN, a hybrid machine-learning potential for Si, which retains the analytical radial interactions and cutoff structure of the Tersoff potential while representing its environment-dependent bond-order factor using compact neural networks (NNs). Benchmarks for 32,768-atom systems show that Tersoff-NN is 4-12 times faster than the Behler-Parrinello-type NN potentials tested in this study. Tersoff-NN improves the short-range structure of liquid Si relative to the conventional Tersoff potential, closely reproduces the ab initio radial and angular distributions, and reproduces the equilibrium structure of diamond Si and qualitative energetic trends among several crystalline phases. Furthermore, melt-quench simulations reveal a disordered solid with predominantly four-coordinated, tetrahedral-like local environments. Additionally, characteristic reconstruction motifs are retained on Si surfaces despite their exclusion from the training dataset. A direct comparison with an alternative atom-centered bond-order NN highlights the critical role of physical constraints in ensuring dynamic stability. Despite exhibiting comparable validation errors, the selected triplet-based architecture remains stable, while an alternative model exhibits unphysical bond-order growth and atomic collapse. These results confirm that learning only the bond-order term improves the description of diverse Si environments while retaining substantial computational efficiency and enhancing dynamical stability.

title: When Does Data Value Reduce to Class Balance? A Coverage View of Per-Point Data Valuation
text:
Title: When Does Data Value Reduce to Class Balance? A Coverage View of Per-Point Data Valuation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Per-point data-valuation scores -- Data Shapley, influence, leverage -- are routinely used to select training data: keep the points with the top $k$ scores. We argue that top-$k$ by a fixed, mode-blind per-point score is the wrong selection rule precisely in the regime where data selection matters. The reason is that a point's value is not a fixed number but depends on what else has been selected -- a near-duplicate of an already-chosen point adds almost nothing, however high its score -- and a per-point scalar cannot express this interaction. The theory quantifies this failure exactly: in an equal latent-mode model, fixed top-$k$ selection incurs a closed-form excess risk over adaptive coverage because it repeatedly spends budget on already-covered modes. The gap is largest when the budget is tight, the learner representation is redundant, and missing a mode is costly. The practical rule is simple: use balance when the labels available at selection identify the learner's modes, and use explicit coverage when they do not. On standard classification tasks with strong pretrained features, class-balancing the same per-point scores recovers the missing coverage and matches or outperforms generic set coverage across our datasets. Without labels, label-free coverage improves accuracy by up to +0.20 while raw top-$k$ can fall below random; when labels are coarser than the modes, coverage within coarse strata performs best. We turn this distinction into a pre-specified diagnostic and validate it across both favorable and stress-test settings. The limits are part of the claim: the advantage is representation-relative. Coverage fails when the relevant modes are not expressed in the learner geometry, as with spurious subgroups, or when data quality varies independently of coverage -- exactly as the theory predicts.

title: An Accelerated Dynamic Stochastic Primal-Dual Method for Multi-stage Stochastic Optimization
text:
Title: An Accelerated Dynamic Stochastic Primal-Dual Method for Multi-stage Stochastic Optimization
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

We consider multi-stage stochastic optimization problems with smooth convex stage costs and linear linking constraints. Dynamic stochastic approximation (DSA), a stochastic first-order method, uses a recursive structure whose memory requirement grows only linearly with the number of stages. Its implementation, however, requires an exact solution of the proximal subproblem associated with the stage cost, and this subproblem often admits no closed-form solution. To resolve this issue, we develop an accelerated dynamic stochastic primal-dual (A-DSPD) framework that retains the recursive value-function structure and only requires the gradient of the stage cost. Within this framework, each stagewise saddle-point subproblem is solved by an inexact accelerated stochastic primal-dual method (iASPD), which applies Nesterov acceleration to the smooth stage cost and uses recursively generated stochastic $ε$-subgradients for the nonsmooth downstream value function. For the stochastic composite saddle-point problem, after $N$ primal-dual updates, iASPD yields optimality and feasibility bounds in which the contribution of the smooth stage cost decays at a faster rate $O(1/N^2)$, while the terms associated with stochastic $ε$-subgradients of the nonsmooth value function decay as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$, up to the prescribed oracle inexactness. We also develop bounds for the stochastic $ε$-subgradient estimators and the dual iterates, which yield complexity guarantees for A-DSPD. Specifically, A-DSPD computes an $ε$-solution using $O(1/ε^4)$ sampled scenarios and $O(1/ε^5)$ primal-dual updates for three-stage problems. We further extend the method and its convergence analysis to problems with an arbitrary finite number of stages. Numerical experiments on three-stage stochastic portfolio models illustrate the empirical advantage of the proposed method.

title: First-fracture kinetics in periodic chains: from free-energy landscapes and dynamical recrossing to absolute rates
text:
Title: First-fracture kinetics in periodic chains: from free-energy landscapes and dynamical recrossing to absolute rates
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

The nearly collinear configuration of highly stretched polymer chains before fracture motivates one-dimensional models. At fixed extension, stretching one bond redistributes length among the others, coupling rupture to the whole chain. In this work, I develop a framework for fracture-healing rates in periodic Morse chains, combining deterministic theories, equilibrium simulations and a quasi-deterministic approach using equilibrium fluxes and barrier-top trajectories. Constrained-partition calculations closely reproduce simulated populations and intact-state tensions. An intact-reservoir potential of mean force (PMF) supplies the first-fracture surface probability, while recrossing corrects the attempt flux without a rate-fitted prefactor. Independent rate tests identify an operational chain-length boundary for accurate two-state kinetics; failed-return durations decrease relative to population relaxation as chains grow. Kramers-Grote-Hynes (KGH), nonlinear reactive-flux and equilibrium rates show excellent agreement in this regime. KGH predicts rates away from coexistence and a chain-dependent local activation length dominated by the barrier response. Rates decrease approximately exponentially before declining more gently for longer chains: barrier growth dominates, additional fracture sites partly compensate, and transmission varies more weakly. Beyond coexistence, long chains can fracture practically irreversibly because healing becomes too rare to observe. Projected committor crossings, where the configuration-averaged probability of reaching the fractured core first is one half, lie near site-PMF maxima, although configurations at equal bond length retain different fracture probabilities. Multiple fractures remain negligible near coexistence through at least $N=50$. The framework could supply state-dependent rates to mesoscopic fracture models of polymer networks.

title: Instantons from geometry in M2-brane sphere partition functions
text:
Title: Instantons from geometry in M2-brane sphere partition functions
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Can the geometry transverse to M2-branes capture effects that are exponentially small in their three-sphere ($S^3$) partition function? We investigate this question by extending beyond constant maps the proposal that M2-brane observables are encoded by equivariant topological strings on the transverse Calabi-Yau fourfold (CY$_4$). Our central object is the disk partition function of the CY$_4$ gauged linear sigma model, a quantum generalization of the equivariant volume. After a Gamma-function normalization and a Mellin transform, it reproduces the complete leading WKB grand potential in the examples admitting a suitable Fermi-gas description, including the R-charge and mass deformations compatible with that description. In particular, the transform recovers membrane-instanton series even for $\mathbb{C}^4$, which has no compact curves. For resolved CY$_4$ cones with compact curves, the match requires a quantum refinement of the classical mesonic constraint. We establish the exact equalities of the corresponding dressed disk partition functions with the classical spectral traces for ABJM, ADHM and a representative set of flavored M2-brane quiver theories. Away from the deformation loci where this match can be established, the same construction yields geometric predictions for the membrane-instanton sector that remain to be tested.

title: Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits for the total edge-length of random directional nearest-neighbour graphs
text:
Title: Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits for the total edge-length of random directional nearest-neighbour graphs
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study planar random spatial graphs defined by inserting an edge between every point of a homogeneous Poisson process on the unit square and a nearest-neighbour within a fixed cone of directions (if there is such a point). We prove large-sample distributional limit theorems for the total Euclidean edge length of the graph, where the limit distribution is either Gaussian (due to contributions from the bulk) or, when one or both of the boundaries of the cone of directions align with the edges of the square, a convolution of Gaussian with a non-Gaussian law arising from boundary effects due to long edges near a boundary. This work extends previously known cases, including the ordinary nearest-neighbour graph (full cone of directions), where the Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Bickel & Breiman and Avram & Bertsimas, and Bhatt & Roy's minimal directed spanning forest (with 'south-west' directions), where the non-Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Penrose & Wade.

title: D2ML: Models for Direct-to-Biology Small Molecule Screening
text:
Title: D2ML: Models for Direct-to-Biology Small Molecule Screening
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Direct-to-biology (D2B) screening enables rapid testing of newly synthesized molecules without purification. However, uncertain concentrations in crude mixtures and limited purified-compound measurements complicate the use of these data in machine learning. Here we show that models tailored to the structure of D2B data can improve prediction and guide the discovery of more potent and selective compounds. Our assay-aware models predict activity from single-point screens, relative potency across targets from crude dose-response assays, and absolute potency from purified-compound measurements. For crude assays, potency ratios between targets tested from the same well can retain selectivity information despite uncertain concentrations. A joint model that shares information across stages and balances their contributions to training improved predictions over separate neural networks. The largest gain was in crude dose-response selectivity prediction, where rank correlation increased from 0.27 to 0.40. In a separate experiment, independently trained models guided the selection of 84 new compounds to improve ROS1 potency while limiting activity against the anti-target TRKB. Synthesis and testing identified compounds that extended the measured Pareto front, achieving better combinations of potency and selectivity than those in the training data. The most selective new compound achieved a ROS1 IC50 of 14.7 nM and 233-fold selectivity over TRKB. By comparison, the most selective training compound had a ROS1 IC50 of 20.3 nM and 79-fold selectivity. ATLAS provides the experimental setting for this approach, supporting synthesis and screening of 1,000-10,000 model-selected compounds in two- to three-week cycles. Together, these results show how assay-aware learning can use the full D2B assay sequence to guide multi-objective molecular optimization.

title: Quantum HHL Algorithm for Solving 1D Linear Advection Equation Using Explicit and Implicit Finite Difference Schemes
text:
Title: Quantum HHL Algorithm for Solving 1D Linear Advection Equation Using Explicit and Implicit Finite Difference Schemes
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

This study develops and implements a Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) quantum algorithm for solving a one-dimensional linear advection equation with periodic boundary conditions. The governing equation is first discretized using a classical finite difference (FD) scheme to obtain a linear system suitable for quantum solution. We present a newly designed, circuit-level implementation of HHL assembled from Qiskit circuit components and exploit the circulant structure of the periodic discretization matrices through Fourier-based matrix evolution. The HHL algorithm is benchmarked with three explicit schemes and one implicit scheme. The implicit scheme requires a nontrivial linear solve arising from the discretized PDE on progressively finer grids, whereas the explicit schemes provide different input fields for testing state preparation and reconstruction with identity coefficient matrices. HHL solution states are validated against direct classical solves in noiseless simulation. For hardware execution, the periodic matrix structure permits a Fourier implementation that applies reciprocal eigenvalues without phase estimation. Results on the IBM Rensselaer Nighthawk processor are compared at a shared final time. Noiseless reconstructed fields approach the transported profile on resolved grids, while substantial hardware errors remain for both explicit and implicit schemes. Crank-Nicolson remains exceptionally well-conditioned and utilizes similar circuit re sources to the explicit controls, proving that hardware degradation in our tests was not driven by poor matrix conditioning. Ultimately, this study shows new means for HHL algorithms to study quantum CFD problems involving advection equations with implicit time integrations, while demonstrating how state preparation and measurement affect the practical performance of quantum solvers on current devices.

title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
text:
Title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with PDC, close to the 0.88 obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
text:
Title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a workhorse algorithm for continuous optimization. It is a folk belief among deep learning practitioners that learning rate decay in SGD substantially improves performance. However, it has remained unclear whether learning rate decay offers an asymptotic advantage for global nonconvex optimization. We answer this question in the affirmative by demonstrating a natural class of nonconvex functions for which, we prove that SGD with learning rate decay requires exponentially fewer gradient queries for global optimization than SGD with any fixed learning rate in the small-step size regime. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first exponential advantage that has been demonstrated for learning rate decay. The class of functions we consider includes many popular benchmark nonconvex functions. Our results provide a robust explanatory theory for the empirically observed benefits of learning rate decay for global optimization. We show that annealing performs the non-logconcave sampling task associated to the optimization problem in polynomial time, via a novel application of weak Poincaré inequalities.

title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
text:
Title: Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Structure predictors like ESMFold fold proteins using neural network computation and have transformed structural biology. However, the driving mechanism from amino-acid (AA) sequence to 3D structure is insufficiently understood, and biological meaning remains locked in the dense network. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have shown promising results in obtaining interpretable concept features over an overcomplete basis of intermediate protein sequence-model representations. Yet folding models, which predict physical shape from AA sequence semantics, have no such account. We hypothesize that the features carrying the folding computation evolve in the 3D structural regression process. In this paper, we interpret the folding trunk in three steps. First, a pilot analysis on the representation distribution across modules and recycles locates distinct spatial computation in the trunk. Second, the dictionaries expose a division of labor: the single representation carries inherited semantics, and the pair representation computes the pairwise geometry. Third, we interpret the dictionary at scale with a reasoning language model, trace how the concepts compose across blocks by gradient-based attribution, and follow the interpreted code to the model's folding output, verifying where the computation aligns with, or departs from, known biochemistry. Together, the sparse dictionaries we train capture the relational geometry the trunk computes beyond the sequence model, and their concept activations forecast the model's own fold quality, turning the black-box folding trunk into a sparse, interpretable, and scientifically verifiable circuit.

title: Singular parabolic Anderson models - From flat space to geometric contexts
text:
Title: Singular parabolic Anderson models - From flat space to geometric contexts
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

These notes (which grew out of some lecture notes prepared for the first Aarhus Summer School in Analysis and Probability) are an introduction to the parabolic Anderson model (PAM), or otherwise stated the stochastic heat equation $\partial_{t} u \,=\, \tfrac{1}{2}Δ\, u \,+\, β\, u\,\dot{W}$. In this system, a multiplicative random potential $\dot{W}$ drives the solution away from the smooth spreading of the classical heat flow and toward intermittency. Namely one observes that mass concentrates, as time grows, on a few tall and widely separated peaks. Through the Feynman-Kac representation this analytic phenomenon has an equivalent probabilistic reading as the localization of a directed polymer in a random environment. We first develop this picture on the flat space $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, covering the construction of the driving noise, well-posedness of the equation, and two-sided bounds on the moment Lyapunov exponents that quantify intermittency. We then turn to the more original goal of the monograph: understanding how these phenomena, and the exponents attached to them, change when $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is replaced by a genuinely geometric background, such as a sub-Riemannian manifold or a fractal set. Throughout, the emphasis is on concepts, main results, and the intuition behind their proofs, rather than on exhaustive technical detail.

title: On finite elements for geometrically-exact planar beams with hyperelastic material models
text:
Title: On finite elements for geometrically-exact planar beams with hyperelastic material models
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

A geometrically-exact planar beam finite-element framework is developed for the analysis of beams with hyperelastic constitutive models. A conventional three-field beam model is first formulated with full geometrical nonlinearity and a linear elastic material law. The kinematics are then enriched by an additional global field that permits deformation through the in-plane thickness. The out-of-plane direction is incorporated separately through plane-strain and plane-stress constitutive reductions, allowing the cross-sectional deformation assumptions and constitutive behaviour to be formulated independently. Numerical results for the present benchmarks show that the plane-stress condition gives essentially coincident centreline deformations for the Poisson's ratio values considered. In contrast, the plane-strain condition, which is widely employed in the literature, makes the formulation sensitive to Poisson's ratio coupling, with the beam becoming significantly stiffer at higher Poisson's ratios. Comparisons between Saint Venant-Kirchhoff and Neo-Hookean hyperelastic models further demonstrate close agreement in the global deformation and in-plane thickness response, with small constitutive differences becoming more apparent in the local out-of-plane stretch. The proposed approach offers a simple and consistent framework to integrate hyperelastic material models into planar geometrically-exact beam models.

title: Colossal Spin--Lattice--Charge Coupling in Noncollinear Ferrimagnetic NbMnX$_2$ ($X$ = S, Se, Te) Monolayers
text:
Title: Colossal Spin--Lattice--Charge Coupling in Noncollinear Ferrimagnetic NbMnX$_2$ ($X$ = S, Se, Te) Monolayers
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Noncollinear ferrimagnets combine a net magnetic moment with internal spin degrees of freedom, creating opportunities to couple magnetic, mechanical, thermal, and electronic responses. Using first-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomistic spin simulations, and transport modeling, we identify stable NbMnX$_2$ ($X$ = S, Se, Te) monolayers with noncollinear ferrimagnetic ground states and Curie temperatures up to 313 K. Competing exchange, Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions, and magnetic anisotropy produce field-responsive canted states that couple strongly to the lattice and charge carriers. Magnetization rotation changes the elastic modulus of NbMnTe$_2$ by up to 36\%, while lattice entropy substantially enhances the near-room-temperature magnetocaloric response of NbMnS$_2$ and NbMnSe$_2$. In NbMnSe$_2$, rotation restores a mirror-protected crossing, continuously closes an approximately 0.13 eV gap, and produces a conductivity-based anisotropic magnetoresistance ratio up to 10,000\% at 100 K. The combined results establish noncollinear NbMnX$_2$ monolayers as a multifunctional platform for two-dimensional spintronics, nanomechanics, and thermal control.

title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
text:
Title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes. We examine the errors of five memory systems on longitudinal medical dialogue and find three recurring causes: the retrieved evidence gives an outdated state, includes another person's health facts, or lacks a safety fact the answer depends on. We present MedGraph, a graph memory built for these three cases. Construction extracts dated facts from each session, attributes each fact to the person it describes, and links medication, diagnosis, and measurement records into chains that keep earlier states. Retrieval ranks the patient's chains as units, reads each chain at the time the question asks about, and adds the original dialogue text; a patient profile lists every recorded safety fact with every question. On MedMemoryBench, MedGraph has the highest overall accuracy with both a GPT and a Qwen backbone, 10.5 and 10.4 points above the strongest of five baselines, with efficient memory construction and answering in the GPT setting.

title: TRACE: Adaptive Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization for Open-Ended Molecular Design
text:
Title: TRACE: Adaptive Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization for Open-Ended Molecular Design
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Optimizing molecules under small evaluation budgets requires deciding both where in chemical space to search and which candidate within that region to evaluate. We introduce Trust Region Adaptive Chemical Exploration (TRACE), a framework for open-ended molecular Bayesian optimization (BO), where candidates are generated on demand rather than selected from a fixed library. TRACE combines an objective-free graph-perturbation mechanism with a fixed, chemistry-aware Gaussian process (GP) surrogate using fragprints, a representation combining molecular fingerprints and fragment descriptors. Rather than learning the search geometry itself, TRACE makes the scale of chemical exploration explicit through a Tanimoto-similarity threshold controlling chemical extent and a cardinality budget controlling candidate-search breadth. A simple success/failure controller expands or contracts both quantities during optimization, while the GP and acquisition function select which admissible molecules to evaluate. Across six challenging molecular optimization benchmarks under matched 1,000-evaluation budgets, TRACE achieves the strongest overall sample efficiency as measured by the best molecule found as evaluations accumulate. Crossed ablations on two objectives further show that adaptive region control contributes beyond the proposal mechanism, while its benefit depends on the proposal distribution. We further apply TRACE to the stability of iron phthalocyanine (FePc), a non-precious molecular electrocatalyst whose degradation can involve loss of the Fe center. Using a first-principles density functional theory (DFT) workflow designed for accurate energy evaluation, TRACE increases the computed thermodynamic resistance to Fe dissolution from 0.42 to 2.59 eV over 80 designed evaluations.

title: Pricing Symbolic Rules by What GNNs Leave Unlearned
text:
Title: Pricing Symbolic Rules by What GNNs Leave Unlearned
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Symbolic knowledge (motif counts, ring counts, label constraints) is routinely added to graph neural networks (GNNs) and justified by their limited expressivity. We replace this yardstick with an exact one. The largest log-loss reduction a rule $S$ can give a model family is $I(Y;S\midσ)$ given what the family computes; every realised gain splits exactly into this term plus repaid neural debt; and for a trained network with representation $T$ the value is $I(Y;S\mid T)$, the label information training failed to extract. Rule design thus becomes rule discovery: we score candidates on the network's out-of-fold residual against calibrated permutation nulls with family-wise error control. On ZINC, discovery recovers the hidden ring term $\max(0,\ell_{\max}-6)$ of the target in three independent runs ($p_{\mathrm{adj}}=0.001$) and beats expert cycle counts; frozen and applied to five unseen datasets it is never significantly worse than the plain network or the expert rule, and on BBBP it significantly beats both.

title: Exact Splitting of Amplitudes and One-Loop Integrands: A Classical Origin of Zeros
text:
Title: Exact Splitting of Amplitudes and One-Loop Integrands: A Classical Origin of Zeros
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We introduce a recursion based on hidden zeros that reconstructs complete tree level scattering amplitudes and one-loop integrands at generic kinematics. The recursion takes a universal exact-splitting form: both tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands are expressed as sums of products of complete tree functions, with the chosen zero conditions manifest in every term. We establish this structure for cubic scalar theory, the nonlinear sigma model, and inverse string Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) functions. We derive the tree splitting formula from the equations of motion, showing that hidden zeros arise when the product of two currents solves the equations of motion, while corrections away from the zero reconstruct the full amplitude. We further show that inverse KLT is the unique extension of $\mathrm{Tr}(φ^3)$ with higher-point non-derivative interactions that preserves hidden zeros.

title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models
text:
Title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Broad classes of deep generative models (DGMs) operate by learning to map a simple source distribution, such as a standard Gaussian, to a complex high-dimensional target distribution. Despite their success, DGMs often empirically struggle to accurately represent distributions with heavy tails or well-separated modes. In this work, we show that these difficulties reflect intrinsic properties of the underlying transport problem rather than particular neural network architectures or training procedures. We establish quantitative lower bounds on the gradients and Jacobians of pushforward mappings that transport log-concave source distributions to such targets. For heavy-tailed target distributions, the required gradient magnitude grows as the target develops increasingly large moments. For multimodal target distributions, the low-probability regions between well-separated modes similarly force large gradients in the transport map. We discuss how such large derivatives relate to trade-offs between expressivity and numerical stability. Our results hold under substantially weaker regularity conditions than previous analyses and remain stable under perturbations of the target distribution. Finally, we show that these obstructions can be mitigated when the goal is approximation of a given density rather than generative modeling. Specifically, we propose simple classes of bijective reparametrizations that can alleviate the difficult geometric structure and reduce the gradient burden placed on the learned generative map. Numerical experiments support our theoretical analysis.

title: Asymmetric Correspondence Learning for Lexical and Style Embeddings: Interpreting Latent Space via Acoustic Features
text:
Title: Asymmetric Correspondence Learning for Lexical and Style Embeddings: Interpreting Latent Space via Acoustic Features
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Self-supervised speech embeddings jointly encode lexical, speaker, and prosodic information, complicating feature isolation. We introduce Asymmetric Correspondence Learning (ACL), distilling HuBERT features into separate Acoustic Word Embeddings (AWEs) and Acoustic Style Embeddings (ASEs) via a split-latent correspondence bottleneck. Through probing and clustering evaluations on single-word utterances, we demonstrate that substantial variance from extrinsic sources remains encoded within each latent space, despite linear probing indicating the information has been stripped. Whilst the AWE space exhibits cohesive lexical clustering (AP$\approx$0.90, Fisher$\approx$6.28), linear probing on the ASE space achieves 97.9\% speaker accuracy across a diffuse topology (Fisher$\approx$1.01), yet preserves substantial lexical variance (Fisher$\approx$0.86) that remains linearly unrecoverable (0.17\%). To explain these findings, we apply group-level permutation feature importance over eGeMAPS acoustic features, finding that AWEs partition by vocal tract filters and ASEs by $F_0$ dynamics. These findings suggest that standard diagnostic benchmarks may be insufficient for verifying feature isolation, as substantial speech structure can be retained even when it remains entirely hidden from probes.

title: A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials
text:
Title: A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

Let $π_n$ be a uniform parking function of size $n$. We determine the scale at which its first $k$ coordinates cease to be close in total variation to $k$ independent uniform variables on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The distance is comparable to $1\wedge \sqrt{k\log(k+1)/n}$, uniformly for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and tends to one above the scale $n/\log n$. At the critical scale $k\simλn/\log n$, it converges to $2Φ(\sqrt{λ/π})-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. A key ingredient is the Lorentzian property of the occupation generating polynomial of parking functions. Together with a strengthened Han inequality, this yields a relative entropy estimate for approximation by the product of the one-coordinate marginals.

title: Detection of residual native state entropy changes upon mutation in Fyn SH3
text:
Title: Detection of residual native state entropy changes upon mutation in Fyn SH3
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

NMR relaxation experiments have shown that there are small but measurable changes in the native state dynamics of the Fyn SH3 domain associated with the substitution by other amino acids of a phenylalanine residue (F20) in the hydrophobic core. We have here used experimental values of NMR order parameters for the wild type protein and two mutational variants (F20L and F20V) as restraints in molecular dynamics simulations. This approach is highly sensitive and provides an atomistic description of the subtle perturbations in native state fluctuations accompanying the mutations. The structural ensembles that we have determined using this method allow the changes in the native state entropy of the protein caused by each of the mutations to be estimated. These entropy changes correspond to free energy variations of several kcal/mol and therefore represent sizable contributions to the overall changes in stability that are associated with the amino acid mutations.

title: How Much Skill Orchestration Can LLM Agents Compile Away? Execution-Grounded Specialization for Token-Efficient Skill Use
text:
Title: How Much Skill Orchestration Can LLM Agents Compile Away? Execution-Grounded Specialization for Token-Efficient Skill Use
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Reusable skills guide large language model (LLM) agents through recurring requests, but each invocation still requires the model to interpret the skill and reconstruct its orchestration. Can agents automatically compile this orchestration into an executable fast path without human intervention? We first study zero-shot skill specialization, which compiles without execution evidence, and find that despite the skill's procedural guidance, incorrect assumptions about runtime bindings can make generated plans brittle and recovery costly. This motivates SkillCache, a one-trace skill specialization method that compiles a completed invocation into a parameterized capsule of programs and natural-language steps, replays it before reuse, and drives it with a plan executor that returns control to the model only when needed, keeping the source skill for recovery. With the Claude Code harness, warm execution of the same request reduces tokens on 87 SkillsBench tasks by 81% with Claude Sonnet 4.6 and by 74% with Claude Opus 4.8 at comparable reward, and capsules stay effective under controlled request changes. Capsules also transfer across models, raising three open-weight models' mean reward by 12-25 percentage points while reducing their tokens by 72-81%, suggesting that execution-grounded compilation is a promising approach to efficient repeated skill use and cross-model transfer.

title: Quantum-Enhanced QSAR for DYRK1A: Evaluating Complementary and Utility QPU-Derived Molecular Representations
text:
Title: Quantum-Enhanced QSAR for DYRK1A: Evaluating Complementary and Utility QPU-Derived Molecular Representations
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

In drug discovery, hit identification selects a limited set of compounds for experimental evaluation from a larger collection of candidates. Because laboratory screening capacity is limited, that choice determines which chemical series continue into further investigation. A hit that is not assayed does not enter confirmation or the analog series, and that chemical series is not opened. For the DYRK1A kinase, the same test molecules were scored from a tabular representation of molecular descriptors and from a vector measured on a quantum processor, with the same RBF-SVM. The question is whether the two models propose the same set for experimental evaluation: they propose different compounds. The model on the vector measured on the quantum processor includes compounds that the tabular representation leaves out, and among them are already-labeled actives. The tabular representation includes actives that the vector measured on the quantum processor leaves out. What is reported is that set: who enters, with what label, and whether published chemistry already mentions it. No formal quantum advantage is claimed, nor a mechanism for why the two vectors separate differently. Those compounds fall within the neighborhood that both representations already cover; what changes is which model marks them active. From that follows the cost of predictive disagreement: each model would send a different chemical series to experimental evaluation.

title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
text:
Title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Experiments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions determine centrality from final-state quantities, usually the charged-particle multiplicity. Performing the same in hydrodynamic simulations requires millions of events, which is impractical for state-of-the-art hybrid models, and centrality is therefore commonly approximated by the initial entropy or energy. We show that neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict the event-by-event multiplicity and mean transverse momentum $[p_T]$ with relative errors of 1--2\%, which makes it possible to generate millions of collisions at a small fraction of the cost of the full simulation. For Pb--Pb collisions at $2.76$~TeV and Au--Au collisions at $200$~GeV, the initial-state and final-state definitions select nearly the same events in 10\%-wide classes, but up to 20\% of the events change class when the classes are 1\% wide. We then compute the fluctuations of $[p_T]$ and its Pearson correlations with a proxy of the elliptic flow, estimated from the initial eccentricity, and with multiplicity. The first correlation is insensitive to how centrality is defined, while the second changes substantially. The approach can be applied at every design point of Bayesian analyses at modest additional cost.

title: A parallel solver for vortex-induced vibrations at zero mass ratio
text:
Title: A parallel solver for vortex-induced vibrations at zero mass ratio
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

We present a parallel strategy for the study of the vortex-induced vibrations (VIV) of a rigid, massless cylinder mounted on translational springs, in two and three dimensions. Without mass or damping, its motion is governed solely by the fluid forces and the spring restoring force, and is an immediate response to the flow. We focus on low spring stiffness, yielding high reduced velocity and maximal oscillation amplitude. A monolithic finite element method in an arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework with implicit time stepping is proposed, solving the fluid flow, cylinder dynamics, and mesh motion simultaneously. Mesh movement is modelled with a linear elastic pseudo-solid with variable Lamé coefficients, and the no-slip condition on the cylinder is enforced with a Lagrange multiplier coupled to the position degrees of freedom; three strategies are explored to enforce this force-position coupling in a distributed framework. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to propose a distributed solver for three-dimensional fluid-structure interaction at zero mass ratio. The solver is verified with manufactured solutions, and exhibits second-order accuracy in time. A numerical study of two- and three-dimensional VIV for Reynolds numbers from 100 to 300 reproduces the VIV responses obtained in previous two-dimensional studies, and predicts nonperiodic 3D oscillations starting at $Re = 300$. Using the direct solver MUMPS, the proposed method scales to up to 768 compute cores.

title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
text:
Title: Dual-Resonator Organic Microcavities for Triplet-Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion offers a compelling route to harvest sub-bandgap photons to increase the efficiency of photovoltaics, but low sensitizer doping required to suppress non-radiative aggregation quenching severely restricts light absorption. Here, we present a dual-resonator planar silver microcavity housing a thermally co-evaporated rubrene:palladium phthalocyanine (PdPC) active layer designed to simultaneously enhance triplet-sensitizer absorption and out-couple upconverted emission. By aligning a dispersive cavity mode with the PdPC absorption peak at $32^\circ$, we achieve a 12-fold enhancement in absorptance at 665 nm. This absorption boost, combined with directional outcoupling through a second cavity mode, outweighs cavity-induced reabsorption losses to yield a 22-fold peak and 4.5-fold integrated enhancement in detected upconversion emission. Overall, this work highlights the potential of microcavity integration to substantially enhance solid-state upconversion performance across low-intensity optoelectronic applications.

title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels
text:
Title: Adaptive Quantization Preserves Fast Rates for TD Learning over Rate-Limited Channels
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Motivated by reinforcement learning subject to communication constraints, we study a policy evaluation problem with linear function approximation over a rate-limited channel. In our setup, an agent interacting with an unknown environment (modeled as a Markov Decision Process) transmits quantized estimates of a temporal-difference (TD) learning update direction to a server over a finite-capacity channel. Our goal is to investigate to what extent one can preserve the statistical convergence rates achievable when the channel has infinite capacity. To that end, we propose a new algorithm called Batched Adaptively Quantized TD (BAQ-TD), which uses batching to reduce the variance of the transmitted information, and adaptive quantization to encode innovations. We prove a high-probability finite-time error bound for BAQ-TD, and show that, above a certain finite channel capacity, BAQ-TD preserves the convergence rate of unquantized TD up to logarithmic factors. Specifically, for a $d$-dimensional value function parameter, we establish that transmitting a total of $\mathcal{O}(d \log(T))$ bits over a horizon of length $T$ suffices to achieve the order-optimal rate of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/T)$, marking an exponential improvement in communication-complexity over prior work.

title: AURA: Auditory Spatial Intelligence via a Unified Representation from a General-Audio Encoder through Complete Alignment
text:
Title: AURA: Auditory Spatial Intelligence via a Unified Representation from a General-Audio Encoder through Complete Alignment
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Answering spatial questions about multi-source scenes requires a model both to identify each sound and to locate it. Existing spatial audio-language models obtain spatial information from a dedicated encoder, which separates spatial and semantic processing into distinct feature spaces. We study whether a general-audio codec trained without spatial supervision can serve both purposes. A controlled layer-wise analysis shows that the frozen codec retains spatial information, with lateral cues carried by the difference between the two ear channels. This information, however, is not readily accessible: in dual-source scenes, a model trained on these features predicts left/right at chance and, on the remaining axes, assigns the detected direction to the queried and the non-queried source equally often. We attribute this failure to an audio--text information asymmetry, in which the audio contains both sources while the answer describes only the queried one. A controlled $2\times2$ experiment shows that either completing the scene description or exposing the inter-channel difference lifts left/right accuracy above chance, whereas binding directions to the queried source requires both. Building on these findings, AURA keeps the codec and the language model frozen and exceeds the strongest dedicated system on SpatialSoundQA by 10.31 points in dual-source direction accuracy, with about 40\% of its trainable parameters.

title: Unsupervised Learning of Cell Instances with Generative Routing Pyramids
text:
Title: Unsupervised Learning of Cell Instances with Generative Routing Pyramids
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Identifying and representing object instances such as cells or nuclei is a common task in microscopy image analysis. Established machine learning workflows typically use supervised detection or segmentation followed by feature extraction or classification, which requires manual annotations and treats instance segmentation and cell representation as separate stages. We describe a new unsupervised method for cell instance segmentation and phenotypic classification from unlabeled microscopy images. Our method is based on reconstructing each image using a coarse-to-fine routing pyramid that associates pixels with spatially sparse latent sources. The resulting pixel-to-latent associations yield instance masks, while the source latents encode cell morphology. We demonstrate competitive performance in instance segmentation across diverse cell morphologies and imaging modalities, as well as generative modeling of cellular phenotypes under perturbations. Source code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/weigertlab/routing-pyramids.
